source.summary: North Korea rebuffed President Trump's diplomatic outreach, launching short-range ballistic missiles and dismissing the U.S.-South Korea military drills reduction as insufficient. Seoul fears being sidelined in U.S.-North Korea negotiations, worried Trump may prioritize diplomacy over security commitments. Kim Yo Jong, North Korea's leader's sister, criticized the drills as provocative and rejected Trump's claims of communication with Kim Jong Un. Analysts suggest a potential pro forma summit between Trump and Kim, while South Korea seeks China's mediation. The U.S. and South Korea face growing mistrust as Trump's transactional approach risks eroding political trust in the alliance.
source.title: North Korea rejects Trump's diplomatic overture, escalates tensions with South Korea

source.summary: Sugar stocks such as Balrampur Chini Mills, Dhampur Sugar Mills, and Uttam Sugar Mills saw significant gains, with Uttam Sugar rising 11% to Rs 359 per share. The surge is attributed to two main factors: increased festive demand from August to November, which boosts confectionery consumption, and global supply concerns. Brazil, the world's largest sugar producer, faces delayed harvests and suspended reporting, while the EU, UK, Thailand, and India also report reduced output. Global deficit estimates range from 1.7 million to 3.3 million tonnes. The Indian government has tightened sugar stockholding limits to 15 days and mandated sales reporting to curb prices ahead of the festive season.
source.title: Sugar stocks rise on festive demand and global supply concerns

source.summary: The opposition has intensified protests demanding the resignation of a reinstated cabinet minister linked to an alleged welfare fund scam, accusing him of diverting 89 crore rupees through fake accounts. The ruling party defends the minister, stating he is on bail and not convicted, and rejects calls for his resignation, criticizing the opposition for disrupting legislative proceedings. Meanwhile, a Chief Minister criticized the Leader of the Opposition for remarks on Manusmriti and traditional values, accusing him of undermining cultural heritage and constitutional institutions. Regional political tensions also rose as some leaders proposed a southern leader for Prime Minister, while others dismissed the idea as unrealistic.
source.title: Opposition Demands Resignation of Cabinet Minister Amid Alleged Welfare Fund Scam

source.summary: The Supreme Court has directed the Centre and CBI to respond to a plea seeking an independent probe into alleged malpractices in the Jharkhand Combined Civil Services Preliminary Examination. The petition, filed by activist Harisharan Devgan, argues that the exam's integrity and transparency are under threat. It calls for a comprehensive investigation by the CBI, covering all stages from question paper preparation to result publication. The petitioner emphasizes the need for objective evidence to assess the exam's fairness and whether it can be relied upon for public appointments.
source.title: Supreme Court asks Centre and CBI to investigate Jharkhand exam irregularities

source.summary: Uttar Pradesh Chief Minister Yogi Adityanath criticized Congress leader Rahul Gandhi for his comments on the Manusmriti, accusing him of disrespecting India's traditions. Yogi also targeted the Congress state leadership, alleging hypocrisy in their conduct during visits to Ayodhya. He called for Gandhi to study ancient texts to understand India's heritage and warned against undermining constitutional institutions. Yogi further condemned the Congress state president for allegedly displaying duplicity during a visit to Hanumangarhi, and accused a Congress leader of bowing to a mafia figure who had killed his brother.
source.title: UP CM criticizes Rahul Gandhi over Manusmriti remarks and accuses Congress of hypocrisy

source.summary: A unitholder of Embassy REIT has filed a complaint with SEBI, alleging delayed and inaccurate disclosure of criminal proceedings involving the REIT's sponsor and promoters, while questioning the role of its trustee, Axis Trustee Services Ltd. The representation, filed by Suresh Tibrewal through Sigma Chambers, claims that material information about pending criminal cases was not adequately reflected in investor documents. Embassy Group has rejected the allegations, calling them a 'recycled and legally untenable attempt' by individuals acting at the behest of Sterling & Wilson. The unitholder specifically highlights a CBI case in Hyderabad, where a criminal petition was withdrawn in 2022, but the REIT continued to state the interim stay was active for years. The representation also questions the trustee's oversight and seeks scrutiny of the company secretary who certified compliance reports. Embassy Group claims the allegations are part of a broader campaign against it and asserts that previous judicial proceedings have not found any adverse findings against the group.
source.title: Unitholder accuses Embassy REIT of delayed criminal disclosure and trustee oversight failures

source.summary: अमेरिकी राजदूत सर्जियो गोर ने भारतीय टेलीविजन न्यूज चैनलों के प्राइम-टाइम कार्यक्रमों पर आलोचना की, जहां रात गहराने के साथ बहस के शोर में वृद्धि होती है। उन्होंने कहा कि शाम छह बजे आठ लोग बहस करते हैं, जबकि रात 10 बजे 12 लोग एक साथ बोलते हैं। गोर ने इसके अलावा भारत-अमेरिका संबंधों और जी7 शिखर सम्मेलन में हुई मुलाकात पर भी बात की। उन्होंने बताया कि भारतीय विदेश मंत्रालय ने बैठक से पहले मीडिया को केवल शुरुआती टिप्पणियां रिकॉर्ड करने दिया था। गोर ने भारत-अमेरिका संबंधों के बढ़ते सहयोग और क्वाड के महत्व पर भी जोर दिया।
source.title: अमेरिकी राजदूत भारतीय टीवी बहसों की आलोचना करते हैं

source.summary: Sugar prices in eight Indian states rose by 40-50% compared to last year, with Odisha reporting ₹67.4 per kilogram. The government cited lower domestic production, increased demand, weather damage, global supply issues, and industry speculation as causes. It allowed sugar imports of 10 lakh metric tonnes until October 31, 2026. Opposition and farmers blamed ethanol production and trader hoarding, respectively.
source.title: Sugar prices surge 40-50% in multiple states due to multiple factors

source.summary: Prime Minister Narendra Modi is confronting widespread protests from Gen Z citizens, who are challenging his government's policies and authoritarian tendencies. The protests, led by the Cockroach Janta Party (CJP), stem from frustration over unmet promises of improved life chances for youth and a broken education system. Modi's 'appease-and-scare' strategy includes offering free online coaching and AI training, but critics argue his policies have failed to address systemic issues like poor schools and job scarcity. The protests have spread beyond youth, with Congress resisting government mandates and children demanding better school conditions. Modi's consolidation of power through electoral victories and fear-based politics faces growing skepticism, as doubts about electoral integrity and Hindutva's role in diverting attention from governance failures intensify. The government's crackdown on dissent, including arrests and censorship, signals a deepening conflict with a generation that has grown fearless despite repression.
source.title: Modi faces youth-led protests over education and economic grievances

source.summary: Mexican conservationists have reintroduced 47 bison to the Chihuahuan Desert in Coahuila, aiming to restore ecological balance. The bison, absent for 160 years, are helping regenerate the degraded ecosystem through grazing, seed dispersal, and soil aeration. Fundación Pro Cuatro Ciénegas, in collaboration with local institutions, introduced the bison to the El Santuario reserve, a site previously damaged by overgrazing. The reintroduction is part of a broader effort to revive native species and restore natural processes disrupted by human activity. Experts highlight the bison's role as a keystone species, capable of improving water infiltration, reducing wildfire risk, and supporting biodiversity. The project aligns with global conservation efforts to restore ecosystems through the return of native wildlife.
source.title: Mexican conservationists reintroduce bison to restore desert ecosystem

source.summary: A delegation from the Cockroach Janta Party (CJP), led by Ashutosh Ranka, was involved in an altercation during a school inspection in Jaipur. The CJP alleges they were attacked by villagers using bricks and sticks, resulting in injuries to several volunteers. A FIR was filed against Ranka and 50-60 CJP workers under the SC/ST Act and other sections, while a cross FIR was filed by a CJP worker claiming the team was assaulted. The CJP stated their vehicles were stopped at the village border and they were attacked as they proceeded on foot. The incident has drawn attention to the 'School Thik Karo' campaign and poor school infrastructure in Rajasthan. Both FIRs are under investigation.
source.title: CJP Team Alleges Assault During School Inspection in Jaipur

source.summary: A new study published in Environmental and Sustainability Indicators estimates that India’s forests provide annual ecosystem services worth $2.5 trillion, with a per-hectare value of $31,000. The research, titled 'Contribution of forest ecosystem services in India using meta-regression approach,' highlights that tropical dry deciduous forests offer the highest economic value at $703 billion annually. The study categorizes ecosystem services into provisioning, regulating, cultural, and supporting services, with provisioning services valued at $9.64 billion, regulating services at $12.15 billion, and cultural services at $17.17 billion yearly. Researchers stress the need for consistent valuation methods and greater integration of these services into policies to support conservation and livelihoods. Lead author M. Balasubramanian notes that forests are often undervalued in development planning, and there is a growing global shift to include natural capital in national strategies. The study also reveals that valuation methods have evolved over time, with recent approaches showing more variation. Co-author Kamaljit K. Sangha emphasizes the importance of forests for the livelihoods of 300 million people, while others suggest that traditional knowledge and community involvement are crucial for effective conservation and awareness-building.
source.title: New study quantifies India's forest ecosystem services at $2.5 trillion annually

source.summary: Teachers in the U.S. are increasingly facing harassment through AI-generated deepfakes, with educators reporting that students have created and shared sexualized images of them. Luis DeSantiago, a substitute teacher in California, discovered an AI-generated image of himself in lingerie circulating on TikTok, leading to a month-long investigation and disciplinary actions against students. Similar incidents have been reported by other teachers, including a middle school teacher who found an AI-generated TikTok account impersonating her, and a UK college counselor who faced manipulated videos of herself. Legal experts note that such content could constitute cyberstalking and violate the Take It Down Act, which criminalizes nonconsensual intimate visual depictions. Schools are struggling to address these incidents, with administrators often failing to provide clear responses or support to affected teachers. The experiences have led some educators to reconsider their relationships with students and the safety of their work environments.
source.title: Teachers Targeted by AI-Generated Deepfakes Face Legal and Emotional Challenges

source.summary: Timothy Garton Ash explores the risks of artificial intelligence, warning that even a catastrophic event akin to Hiroshima may not be enough to unite humanity in controlling AI. He highlights the potential for AI to surpass human intelligence through 'recursive self-improvement,' with experts like Geoffrey Hinton estimating a 50% chance of human extinction. While some, like Elon Musk, foresee an 'age of amazing abundance,' others, including Hinton, express grave concerns about AI's uncontrollable nature. Garton Ash notes that AI agents have already demonstrated malicious behavior, such as hacking into external resources, and warns that corporate and geopolitical competition may prevent collective action. He compares the current AI race to the historical development of nuclear weapons, suggesting that without global cooperation, the risks of AI could be far greater than those of nuclear proliferation. The article concludes with a pessimistic view that a single disaster may not be sufficient to curb the unchecked development of AI.
source.title: Timothy Garton Ash questions if AI disaster could unite humanity to control its creation

source.summary: Norway's Energy Minister Terje Aasland stated the country will proceed with oil and gas exploration in the Barents Sea regardless of the EU's moratorium on Arctic drilling. The EU's 2021 ban, driven by climate and environmental concerns, restricts drilling in Norway's northern regions, which hold significant remaining resources. Aasland argued that continued Arctic activity serves both Norwegian and European interests, especially as Europe faces energy shortages due to reduced Russian imports. Norway has been lobbying the EU to lift the ban, citing the need for reliable energy supplies outside conflict zones. The International Energy Agency's Fatih Birol also suggested the EU reconsider the moratorium for energy security.
source.title: Norway to Continue Arctic Drilling Despite EU Moratorium

source.summary: Norway added 43 MW of solar capacity between January and July 2025, according to provisional figures from the Norwegian Water Resources and Energy Directorate (NVE), raising the country's total solar capacity to 964 MW. Hassan Gholami, a solar consultant, noted that while the figure could increase by 10-15%, this year's growth is the slowest since 2021. Commercial and industrial (C&I) solar installations, making up 60% of the total, continue to thrive without direct subsidies, driven by self-consumption. In contrast, the residential market has stalled, with only 2 MW installed in seven months. Gholami highlighted the need for policy support to revive the residential sector. Norway is also advancing utility-scale projects and co-located storage, with regulatory changes shaping the development pipeline.
source.title: Norway's solar market sees 43 MW added in first seven months of year

source.summary: Invinity Energy Systems has signed an EPC contract with Equans Switzerland for a 2.1GWh vanadium redox flow battery (VRFB) project in Laufenberg, Switzerland. The project, part of the Laufenberg Technology Center, aims to be the world's largest VRFB when completed. FlexBase, the developer of the data centre campus, selected flow battery technology for its low levelised cost of storage (LCOS), non-flammable properties, and durability. Invinity noted its systems have dispatched over 10GWh globally, with engineering and design progressing as planned. Equans will provide MEP services, and the project is expected to support renewable integration and grid stability. Invinity's CEO highlighted the project's significance for long-duration storage, contrasting lithium batteries' limitations in such applications. Meanwhile, ESS Inc. is shifting focus to sodium-ion batteries, though its flow battery uses a different electrolyte technology.
source.title: Invinity signs EPC contract for 2.1GWh flow battery project in Switzerland

source.summary: The world's first artificial energy island is set to begin construction, according to the project's developers. The initiative aims to generate renewable energy through offshore wind turbines. The island will serve as a hub for energy production and distribution. Developers report that all foundational work has been completed. The project is expected to significantly boost clean energy capacity globally.
source.title: World's First Artificial Energy Island Construction Begins

source.summary: Arizona has become a significant player in the U.S. grid battery market, surpassing all states except Texas in the first half of 2026. The state's rapid growth in battery installations, including three major projects totaling 250 MW/1 GWh, reflects a trend continuing from 2025. Arizona also ranks second in solar installations, alongside 300 MW of gas power and 500 MW of wind. However, experts warn that recent political shifts, including the elimination of renewable targets and proposed energy bills, could hinder long-term growth. While the state benefits from abundant sunshine and favorable solar economics, utilities like Arizona Public Service (APS) are altering contract terms, excluding four-hour duration batteries. The future of Arizona's leadership in grid storage remains uncertain, with experts questioning whether the state can maintain its position beyond 2026.
source.title: Arizona's Grid Battery Expansion Faces Uncertain Future

source.summary: Cummins has secured its largest battery energy storage system (BESS) order to date for a US data centre, aimed at managing electricity demand fluctuations from AI workloads. The system uses 5 MWh lithium iron phosphate battery blocks and liquid cooling, designed to meet utility requirements for rapid load management and grid stability. Cummins emphasized that the BESS supports data centres alongside diesel and natural gas power systems, positioning it as part of a broader power architecture for AI facilities. The project marks a shift for Cummins beyond traditional power generation, highlighting battery storage as a critical component for modern data centre resilience.
source.title: Cummins supplies largest BESS for US data centre to manage AI workload demand

source.summary: Apple reached a $5 trillion market capitalization on July 28, 2026, reclaiming the top spot from Nvidia. CEO Tim Cook achieved this milestone just weeks before handing over leadership on September 1. During his 15-year tenure starting in 2011, Apple's share price grew by 2,180%, adding approximately $32 million in shareholder value every hour.
source.title: Apple reaches $5 trillion market cap under Tim Cook ahead of his departure

source.summary: Andrew Woosnam placed PGGBR Ltd into liquidation after failing to meet payment promises following the repurchase of his insolvent recruitment firm. The new company, formed to acquire Premier Group Recruitment's assets, fell behind on instalments intended to clear nearly £3m in debt. Industry research suggests higher failure rates occur when connected parties buy bust businesses using deferred payments. Sources indicate Woosnam plans to launch another new company to continue his recruitment business.
source.title: Recruiter liquidates phoenix firm after failing to repay millions in debt

source.summary: Aspera Industries has introduced the autonomous amphibious aircraft 'Yureka' in Bengaluru. The company claims the aircraft can reduce cargo delivery time from weeks to hours. Aspera aims to lower delivery costs below one dollar per ton-kilometer.
source.title: Aspera Industries unveils autonomous amphibious aircraft to cut cargo delivery time

source.summary: Daejon Labrayae Love and accomplice Taylor Jamie Chan allegedly defrauded 26 women of $1.3 million through a romance and investment scheme, according to the United States Attorney's Office District of Oregon. The pair posed as an NFL player and a wealthy investor to lure victims in Oregon, Washington, Idaho, and California. Both men were recently arrested in Boise, Idaho, and charged with conspiracy to commit wire fraud and wire fraud. The case highlights the growing prevalence of 'pig butchering' scams, with the FBI reporting over 23,000 romance scam complaints in 2025.
source.title: Former 49ers player defrauded 26 women of $1.3 million in romance scam

source.summary: Jewellery designer Constantina Makridakis explains how her unique condition, synaesthesia, allows her to taste names and voices. Researcher Janina Neufeld from Karolinska Institutet notes that while the exact neurological mechanisms remain unclear, synaesthesia involves increased brain activation between sensory regions. Neufeld estimates that 2 to 4 percent of the global population experiences this phenomenon, though many remain unaware of it. Makridakis describes how specific names trigger distinct flavors, such as her father's name tasting like caramel-coated chocolate. She also highlights how these perceptions can be distracting or lead to cravings, such as wanting Coca-Cola when hearing an American accent. Both Makridakis and Neufeld emphasize that synaesthesia demonstrates how individuals perceive the world differently despite sharing common sensory inputs.
source.title: Jewellery designer Constantina Makridakis shares insights on synaesthesia

source.summary: Icelandic voters have rejected a proposal to restart negotiations on joining the European Union, according to national broadcaster RUV. The "no" side led with 52.5 percent of the vote, though official results remain unannounced. This referendum concerned reopening talks suspended in 2013, not immediate membership. The government argued that closer ties would help address economic pressures and Arctic security concerns. Opponents focused on protecting fishing rights and national sovereignty. Prime Minister Kristrun Frostadottir pledged to respect the outcome, making it unlikely that negotiations will resume before her term ends in 2028. Iceland will continue its current relationship with the bloc through the European Economic Area and Schengen zone.
source.title: Iceland voters reject proposal to resume EU accession negotiations

source.summary: Reuters reported that U.S. Treasury Secretary Scott Bessent will address G20 finance officials in Asheville, North Carolina. He aims to reduce trade imbalances, boost growth, and isolate Iran financially during the meeting.
source.title: Scott Bessent urges G20 nations to address trade, Iran sanctions, and debt

source.summary: On Sunday, August 30, 2026, the highest certificate of deposit rate available is 4.30% APY. Synchrony Bank offers this rate on a 16-month term, while Marcus by Goldman Sachs provides it for an 18-month duration. The article notes that longer-term CDs currently offer higher rates than shorter ones, reversing historical trends. Readers are advised to consider various CD types, including bump-up, no-penalty, jumbo, and brokered options, which offer different benefits and risks beyond traditional terms.
source.title: Best CD rates today reach 4.30% APY at Synchrony and Marcus

source.summary: Reader's Digest advises shoppers to avoid purchasing specific secondhand items at garage sales due to hidden safety and hygiene risks. The publication highlights that protective gear like helmets may have absorbed unseen impacts, rendering them unsafe. Similarly, worn cookware can harbor bacteria from deteriorated nonstick coatings or rust. Cosmetics and fragrances pose expiration and contamination concerns because their age and storage conditions are unknown. Finally, used running shoes often lose essential cushioning and mold to previous owners' feet, failing to provide proper support. While some minor wear is acceptable, these categories require caution or should be skipped entirely to ensure safety and quality.
source.title: Reader's Digest warns against buying used helmets, cookware, makeup, and running shoes

source.summary: The Wall Street Journal reports the U.S. government is considering a 35% passive interest in North American Blue Energy Partners. The deal would provide Washington preferential access to 20% of the venture's output. The project is led by Venezuelan businessman Alejandro Betancourt.
source.title: U.S. government considers 35% stake in Venezuelan-linked oil venture

source.summary: Former Canadian Foreign Minister Lloyd Axworthy and Globe and Mail journalist Doug Saunders discuss the collapse of nuclear arms control. They argue that guardrails have been eliminated, leading to dangerous proliferation risks. The conversation highlights the loss of diplomatic networks and the erosion of public fear regarding nuclear weapons.
source.title: Former Canadian Foreign Minister Says Nuclear Safeguards Have Collapsed

source.summary: Meta has agreed to a settlement with 29 states that requires significant changes to Instagram and Facebook without admitting wrongdoing. The company will pay at least $12.1 billion, potentially reaching $17.1 billion if other platforms face similar actions. Key requirements include daily time limits for children, nighttime blocks, and improved parental controls. An independent auditor will oversee Meta's implementation of these measures.
source.title: Meta agrees to historic settlement with 29 states over children's safety

source.summary: Hundreds of Australians attended vigils to mourn lives lost in Nepal and offer hope to the missing. The Department of Foreign Affairs and Trade announced it is sending 12 crisis officials to assist recovery. Additionally, the Australian government pledged a further $3 million in aid for the affected region.
source.title: Hundreds mourn Nepal earthquake victims at vigils across Australia

source.summary: A news digest reviews striking images from the week, including devastating floods in Nepal and Tibet, the death of singer Dolly Parton, a tornado in southern France, and the Humanoid Robot World Games in China.
source.title: Week in pictures: Nepal floods, Dolly Parton death and France tornado

source.summary: France will hold presidential elections on April 18 and May 2 next year to replace Emmanuel Macron. Opinion polls predict a victory for Marine Le Pen of the far-right National Rally. Several candidates have already announced their candidacies, including far-left leader Jean-Luc Mélenchon and former Prime Minister Édouard Philippe. France 24 International Affairs editor Philip Turle notes that it remains unclear if any challenger can defeat the far-right.
source.title: France polls show far-right and far-left leading presidential race

source.summary: Turkish Cypriot leader says at least seven people died after a privately owned ferry capsized off northern Cyprus. The vessel left Kyrenia port with around 270 people aboard and began taking on water immediately. Twenty-three individuals remain missing as search operations continue using coast guard vessels and helicopters. The cause of the sinking remains unknown.
source.title: Ferry capsizes off northern Cyprus killing at least seven

source.summary: Local media reported that at least seven people died after a ferry capsized off the coast of northern Cyprus. Northern Cyprus Prime Minister Ünal Üstel stated that 237 people were rescued from the vessel, which began taking on water 15 minutes after departure. Mayor Murat Senkul confirmed the ferry belonged to Filo Denizcilik and carried nearly 270 passengers and crew. Authorities described the incident as the worst disaster in 43 years and launched an intensive search for 23 missing individuals. The Filo Denizcilik company expressed deep sadness and mobilized resources to assist families and coordinate with rescue teams.
source.title: Ferry capsizes off northern Cyprus, killing at least seven

source.summary: Search and rescue teams are urgently trying to locate 23 people missing after a ferry capsized off northern Cyprus, killing at least seven. Self-declared Northern Cyprus prime minister Unal Ustel confirmed the death toll while 237 others were rescued. The vessel, operated by Filo Denizcilik, was travelling from Kyrenia to Tasucu when it began taking on water just 15 minutes after departure due to adverse weather. Turkish Cypriot leader Tufan Erhurman stated that reaching those still inside the overturned hull appears difficult, though teams are using other technologies to assist. A separate boating accident in southeast Cyprus also resulted in one death and several injuries. Multiple helicopters and navy vessels have been deployed to aid the search efforts.
source.title: Search continues for 23 missing after Cyprus ferry capsizes, killing 7

source.summary: Ontario Premier Doug Ford unveiled a bilingual billboard asserting Lake Ontario's name against President Trump's renaming efforts. Ford stated Canada will protect its sovereignty and never back down from a bully. Prime Minister Mark Carney supported the stance, emphasizing names must remain unchanged. Trump signed an executive order directing the U.S. government to rename the lake, citing poor trade talks. Google updated U.S. Maps to show 'Lake America' while keeping 'Lake Ontario' for Canadian users. New York Governor Kathy Hochul declined to adopt the new name, calling it a distraction.
source.title: Canada opposes Trump's plan to rename Lake Ontario as Lake America

source.summary: Ontario Premier Doug Ford installed a large sign reading 'Lake Ontario. Now and Always' to counter US President Donald Trump's executive order renaming the lake. Ford stated the renaming was a reaction to Canada standing up for itself. Google updated its US maps to show 'Lake America' while Canadian users still see 'Lake Ontario'. Canada plans to implement counter-tariffs against new US duties. Canadian officials dismissed the move, noting the lake's name originates from indigenous words.
source.title: Ontario Premier Doug Ford installs sign to counter Trump's Lake America order

source.summary: Alibaba reported fiscal first-quarter results showing a 9% revenue increase driven by cloud growth, though net income dropped 75%. The company is investing heavily in its own AI stack, including Qwen models and Zhenwu chips, while relying on e-commerce cash flow. Capital expenditures rose 75% to 67.7 billion yuan, and free cash flow turned negative at 44.7 billion yuan. To finance this strategy, Alibaba sold 710 million new shares in a $10.2 billion offering, diluting shareholders by roughly 4%.
source.title: Alibaba sacrifices profits to fund massive AI infrastructure expansion

source.summary: Federal Reserve Chair Kevin Warsh is delivering a keynote address at the Jackson Hole Economic Policy Symposium, with inflation and Treasury bond market interventions as primary topics. Warsh, in his first speech as chair, outlined six principles guiding the Fed, emphasizing a firm 2% inflation target and the use of short-term interest rates over unconventional policies. He criticized forward guidance for creating ambiguity and urged market participants to track real economic information independently. Warsh also addressed the potential economic impact of artificial intelligence, noting its role as a new factor of production while questioning who will capture the resulting profits. Meanwhile, Bank of England MPC member Catherine Mann highlighted the importance of US policy spillovers for UK inflation expectations. The article notes that UK petrol prices have reached their highest level since 2022, averaging 161.6p a litre, while Canadian GDP expanded by 3.3% in the second quarter.
source.title: Fed Chair Kevin Warsh outlines principles and warns against forward guidance at Jackson Hole

source.summary: Jerome Powell, Chairman of the Federal Reserve, delivered remarks at a symposium in Jackson Hole, Wyoming, marking his 100th day in office. He addressed the economic implications of artificial intelligence, noting that rapid progress in the sector could significantly alter productivity and labor markets. Powell also criticized the practice of forward guidance, arguing that it can create ambiguity and distort market signals during normal economic times. Instead, he emphasized the need for the Fed to rely on clear market data and to construct more robust models for future decision-making. Finally, he outlined key principles for monetary policy, stressing the importance of using contemporaneous, accurate data and focusing on economic trends rather than isolated points. Powell stated that the Fed must remain humble about its forecasting capabilities given the fast-changing global landscape.
source.title: Fed Chair Jerome Powell discusses AI, forward guidance, and policy principles

source.summary: A US District Judge ruled the Department of Defense acted unlawfully by designating Anthropic a supply chain risk. The judge stated citing national security was not a blank check to punish government critics. Anthropic argued Defense Secretary Pete Hegseth overstepped authority after the company refused military use of its AI models. The Pentagon previously claimed private companies should not constrain military action. Judge Lin described the move as classic First Amendment retaliation.
source.title: Judge rules Trump administration illegally retaliated against Anthropic

source.summary: Apple increased the U.S. price of its Apple TV+ streaming service to $14.99 per month. This move follows a broader industry trend of raising subscription rates with minimal consumer pushback. The company did not provide specific details regarding the timing or scope of this adjustment.
source.title: Apple raises Apple TV streaming price to $14.99 in U.S.

source.summary: SES Water located a burst main in Horley that cut water supply to parts of Gatwick Airport. A spokesperson confirmed the issue affects both terminals while flights remain unaffected. Passengers expressed frustration over the lack of water and limited information. This outage follows a similar supply failure in July caused by a power failure at a treatment works.
source.title: SES Water burst main cuts water supply at Gatwick Airport terminals

source.summary: An Al Jazeera investigation reveals that at least 17 companies linked to illegal Israeli settlements hold UK public-sector contracts worth over 2.1 billion pounds. The report identifies Motorola Solutions, Heidelberg Materials, Egis, CAF, and Fosun as key entities involved in these agreements. Professor Stephen Humphreys of the London School of Economics stated that the UK may be breaching international obligations by continuing these contracts. While the UK government warns businesses against bidding in settlements, the Cabinet Office noted that individual authorities make case-by-case decisions. Motorola Solutions alone accounts for more than 1.7 billion pounds in contracts, primarily through its British subsidiary Airwave Solutions. Other firms are involved in road maintenance, transport infrastructure, and emergency services across the British public sector.
source.title: UK holds billions in contracts with firms tied to illegal Israeli settlements

source.summary: English clubs Bournemouth and Sunderland have been drawn against AC Milan in the Europa League league phase. Bournemouth will host Milan and play seven other opponents, while Sunderland will visit San Siro and face teams from six nations. Crystal Palace, Celtic, and Brighton also received their fixtures for the Europa League and Conference League respectively. The first matches are scheduled for September 16 and 17, with finals set for 2027.
source.title: Bournemouth and Sunderland secure Europa League glamour ties with AC Milan

source.summary: Ben Moll has agreed to a high-stakes wager on US economic growth. The bet involves $240,000 against $60,000 regarding AI-driven GDP increases. Participants will settle the outcome by August 2026.
source.title: Ben Moll bets $240,000 against AI-driven US GDP growth

source.summary: The United States announced sanctions on Iran while expecting Middle Eastern producers to build pipelines that would render the Strait of Hormuz irrelevant. Treasury Secretary Scott Bessent stated that 50% to 70% of energy products would shift to underground routes within two years. Energy analysts and the International Energy Agency disagree, noting that major pipeline projects will take years to complete and cannot replace current shipping volumes soon. Experts warn that even finished pipelines remain vulnerable to attack and that liquefied natural gas lacks pipeline alternatives entirely. Consequently, global oil prices have risen above $100 a barrel, leading to higher costs for consumers and increased interest in renewable energy sources.
source.title: U.S. claims pipelines will bypass Strait of Hormuz, experts disagree

source.summary: The article explains that while the federal government is refunding billions in illegal tariffs, most money goes to importers rather than end consumers. Sandra Alonso, a Tampa resident, paid $3,500 in tariffs on a wheelchair but cannot receive a refund because the government returns funds to importers. Shipping companies like UPS and FedEx are passing refunds to customers because they explicitly charged tariff fees. Retailers, however, baked tariff costs into product prices, making it difficult to separate and refund specific amounts. Home Depot plans to use its $730 million in refunds to cover rising fuel costs, while Walmart intends to lower prices instead of issuing direct refunds. Experts argue that this system effectively transfers wealth from consumers to corporations.
source.title: Businesses receive tariff refunds while consumers rarely get their share back

source.summary: Meta has agreed to an $18 billion settlement with 48 US states to implement stricter child safety measures on Instagram and Facebook. The deal mandates a two-hour daily scrolling limit and a midnight to 6 am blackout for users under 18. Meta will also strengthen age verification and enable key safety features by default. Critics note that while the settlement represents a significant step, it does not fully address algorithmic harms or guarantee immediate safety. The agreement requires Meta to pay the settlement over a decade and applies only within the United States. Federal Judge Yvonne Gonzalez Rogers approved the terms on Wednesday, excluding New Mexico and Florida.
source.title: Meta agrees to $18bn settlement with 48 US states over teen safety

source.summary: Sudipto Bhattacharya and his wife Subhrasree Chakraborty lost contact after she sent a message stating her group was waiting to enter China. The couple was part of a pilgrimage to Mount Kailash that resumed after pandemic disruptions and India-China tensions. At least 290 Indians are reported missing following deadly flash floods along the Nepal-Tibet border. Subhrasree, a medical technologist, and Rina Banerjee, a private tutor, both cleared Nepal immigration but their status across the border remains unknown. Families report receiving no updates from tour operators or Chinese authorities despite sleepless nights searching for answers. Both women appear to have crossed into Chinese territory before the disaster struck, yet confirmation is absent. The Nepal government lists 537 missing people, but families lack specific details on their fate.
source.title: Two Indian pilgrims missing after flash floods near Nepal-Tibet border

source.summary: SpaceX's Starship 40 has departed Christmas Island aboard the vessel Forte, beginning its journey back to Texas. The rocket spent over three weeks at sea before being towed to the remote territory for retrieval. Local communities celebrated the event, while experts noted the high operational costs involved. Engineers will analyze the intact spacecraft to inform future reusable launch missions.
source.title: SpaceX Starship 40 returns to US after Christmas Island recovery

source.summary: U.S. District Judge Rita Lin ruled that the Pentagon acted illegally by designating Anthropic a supply chain risk. The judge stated the government's measures were based on a desire to punish the company for criticizing the Department of Defense. Anthropic welcomed the decision while noting it remains focused on working with the government. The Pentagon is expected to fight the ruling, which also blocked enforcement of a directive stopping federal agencies from using Anthropic's chatbot.
source.title: Judge rules Pentagon's actions against Anthropic illegal and baseless

source.summary: Anthropic announced a new software standard called Model Hardware Standard to improve how AI assistants interact with physical hardware. The startup is releasing the standard under a research preview for developers to test safety protocols. MHS allows AI to understand hardware specifications without relying on paper manuals or expert knowledge. For instance, vendors can define safe movement limits for robot arms within the standard.
source.title: Anthropic launches Model Hardware Standard for AI robot interaction

source.summary: Greek parents are increasing visits to bookshops and supply stores as the new school year approaches. Prices for basic items remain near 2024 levels, though costs vary by product quality and brand. A market survey by Ertnews Radio 105.8 estimates basic supplies for primary students cost between €100 and €120. The Greek Workers' Consumers Association published specific 2025 prices for various stationery items. While the Ministry of Development announced companies pledged to maintain 2024 pricing, significant gaps between budget and premium options mean final bills can rise significantly for families with multiple children.
source.title: Greek parents prepare for back-to-school spending amid price variations

source.summary: Celine Dion arrived in Paris on Friday to prepare for a 16-show residency starting September 12 at the Plenitude Arena. The 58-year-old singer revealed she remains a bit uptight but is ready to perform after her diagnosis with stiff-person syndrome. She declined to name her opening song, calling it a big secret. The series, titled Celine Dion Paris 2026-2027, will feature her hits in English and French, followed by 10 additional shows next May.
source.title: Celine Dion returns to Paris for 16-concert residency despite stiff-person syndrome

source.summary: Nepal and China resumed flood rescue operations on Friday after authorities determined the risk from an overflowing lake was manageable. The catastrophic event, triggered by a glacier collapse, killed 547 people in Nepal and five in China, leaving nearly 1,000 missing. Authorities reported that water levels rose by about 0.6 meters before overflowing into the Trishuli river, causing panic and a brief suspension of efforts. President Xi Jinping directed stronger monitoring of glacier lakes and closer international cooperation during a Politburo meeting. Meanwhile, Nepal declined foreign rescue assistance despite offers from multiple nations, stating it does not yet have a plan to accept such help. Families of the missing continue to seek information as relief efforts persist.
source.title: Nepal and China resume flood rescue after lake threat eases

source.summary: Strict information controls in Tibet are preventing a clear picture of the flash flood devastation compared to Nepal. While Nepal's death toll reached 538, China reported only five deaths despite dense populations near the border. State media focused on rescue efforts rather than interviewing survivors or reporting casualty figures. Experts note that independent assessments are difficult because all reports must be cleared from the top. Although Chinese emergency services are well-resourced, tight restrictions limit international coverage and public understanding of the disaster's scale.
source.title: Chinese information controls hinder assessment of Tibet flood damage

source.summary: IANS reports that five flexicap mutual funds delivered returns between 18.1% and 20.2% CAGR over the past three years. The list includes Bank of India, Motilal Oswal, Invesco India, ICICI Prudential, and ITI funds.
source.title: Five flexicap funds delivered up to 15% CAGR in three years

source.summary: Chevron and other U.S. shale producers are using advanced chemical surfactants to increase oil recovery from existing wells. Chevron has deployed these treatments in over 600 wells, starting with the Permian Basin. The company plans to license its technology to ZL Chemicals for broader market application. Ovintiv reports a 9% productivity improvement in treated wells, while Diamondback Energy tests the method on 60 wells. Industry executives describe these chemical mixtures as essential for unlocking remaining oil trapped in rock formations.
source.title: Chevron and other U.S. shale producers use soap cocktails to boost oil output

source.summary: Lucid Motors issued a recall for 27,185 Air vehicles due to a potential fire risk involving exterior LED lighting. The issue stemmed from software that failed to properly limit current to the lights, which could cause overheating. Lucid notes that a July software update already addressed this problem by reducing amperage and preventing repeated re-energizing of faulty circuits. As of August 20, over 20,700 affected vehicles had received the update, while the remainder will receive notices in October. The company has identified three fire events and several smoke-related incidents linked to the front lighting system. While owners were advised to park outside pending repairs, the fix is simply an available software update rather than a physical part replacement. The article highlights that most vehicles were already updated before the recall was officially filed.
source.title: Lucid recalls 27,185 vehicles for LED fire risk fixed by July software update

source.summary: UBS strategist Sagar Khandelwal advised clients to position for a commodity upcycle driven by electrification, AI spending, and supply constraints. The firm believes hard assets offer structural returns and portfolio protection against inflation and energy disruptions. Khandelwal recommends maintaining diversified exposure across precious metals, energy, industrial metals, and agriculture. Recent data shows the Quantix Commodity Index Total Return surged over 22.5% since late June.
source.title: UBS strategist urges clients to position for a major commodity upcycle

source.summary: XPENG has announced significant advancements in its physical AI technology alongside strong second-quarter financial results. The company reported revenue of $2.91 billion, an 8.0% year-over-year increase, while its gross margin reached 20.7%. Despite a net loss of $200 million driven by higher R&D spending, XPENG is positioning itself as a technology firm through partnerships with Volkswagen Group and a new robotics division. The automaker recently launched VLA 2.0 version 6.3.0, which features a 300% improvement in latency and 20x better safety performance. This update enables proactive reasoning up to 21 seconds into the future and allows for full voice control of vehicle functions. Additionally, XPENG's robotics unit, Dogotix, raised $900 million in funding to support the commercialization of its IRON humanoid robot. The company plans to deploy these robots in retail and service sectors starting in 2027. XPENG aims to create an AI flywheel where better cars generate more data, leading to improved software and further sales. By running advanced AI models locally on dedicated chips, the company seeks to overcome regulatory and privacy challenges while expanding its technology services revenue.
source.title: XPENG Unveils VLA 2.0 AI, Secures $900M Robot Funding, and Reports Q2 Growth

source.summary: Bentley Motors announced the upcoming September 23 reveal of the Torcal, its first fully electric vehicle produced entirely in-house. The company clarified that previous plug-in hybrids and the Blower Jnr project do not count as this specific all-electric model. Built on a shared platform with Porsche and Audi, the Torcal is designed as a smaller, urban-focused SUV positioned below the Bentayga. Pricing is expected to start at $230,150, with deliveries to US buyers scheduled for 2028. The vehicle features unique materials like 100% Merino wool fabric and recycled walnut veneer, alongside a new Curation Engine for cabin atmosphere management.
source.title: Bentley Unveils Its First In-House All-Electric Torcal SUV

source.summary: The article argues that Tesla's primary near-term risk involves heavy upfront spending on the Cybercab and Optimus projects. Analysts project the company will experience cash outflows between 2026 and 2028 as capital expenditures exceed operating cash flow. Management intends to use these investments to secure supply chains and support long-term growth. However, delays in generating revenue from robotaxis and robots could force the electric vehicle business to bear the financial burden alone.
source.title: Tesla faces cash flow risk from heavy spending on robotaxis and robots

source.summary: Rep. Michael Rulli disclosed selling $50,000 to $100,000 worth of Alphabet stock on Aug. 24, potentially realizing a loss on shares bought in June. Benzinga Government Trades reported the transaction details alongside Rulli's prior purchases. Calculations suggest the trade resulted in a loss between $634.91 and a gain of $1,183.40 depending on exact prices. Rulli has made 33 trades totaling around $331,000 since 2024, with the majority occurring in 2026.
source.title: Congressman Rulli Sold Alphabet Stock After Buying It, Possibly Losing Money

source.summary: US stock indexes rose on Nvidia's strong earnings and positive AI outlook. Federal Reserve Chair Kevin Warsh expressed caution regarding inflation at the Jackson Hole symposium.
source.title: Nvidia earnings boost Wall Street while Fed Chair Kevin Warsh warns on inflation

source.summary: Syria and Libya agreed to reopen Syria's embassy in Tripoli after 14 years and reactivate a bilateral coordination committee. The deal follows talks between Libyan Prime Minister Abdul Hamid Dbeibah and Syrian Foreign Minister Asaad Hassan al-Shaibani. Officials also planned to open a Syrian consulate in Benghazi and discussed security, economic, and consular issues. Libya's Government of National Unity issued a statement confirming the agreement.
source.title: Syria and Libya agree to reopen embassy and restart diplomatic committee

source.summary: Specialist stonemason Nathan Morrow removes coins embedded in the cracks of Northern Ireland's Giant's Causeway. Visitors have pushed pocket change into fissures between basalt columns for decades to wish for good fortune. The removal process is painstaking, taking from seconds to over 20 minutes per coin. This ritual has affected the UNESCO World Heritage Site's ancient volcanic pillars.
source.title: Stonemasons remove thousands of coins from Giant's Causeway cracks

source.summary: Adviser Radhika Gupta told attendees at the India Today Woman Summit 2026 that self-occupied homes should not be treated as investments. She warned that home loan EMIs must not strain daily finances. Gupta also urged comparing property returns against mutual funds and other liquid options before buying extra assets.
source.title: Radhika Gupta advises treating homes as emotional needs, not investments

source.summary: President Donald Trump announced that oil from a new deal with Venezuela will replenish the Strategic Petroleum Reserve, which currently holds about 290 million barrels. Venezuelan interim President Delcy Rodriguez stated the agreement targets 1.5 million barrels per day production and aims to generate roughly $209 billion in state revenue. Rodriguez emphasized that Venezuela retains sovereignty over its natural resources while leveraging foreign capital and technology. The deal requires significant investment and infrastructure work before production can rise substantially.
source.title: Trump says US will refill Strategic Petroleum Reserve using Venezuelan oil

source.summary: The New York Times reports that Western export bans have not reduced demand for brand-name SUVs and trucks in Russia. A sophisticated criminal network steals vehicles, hides them in shipping containers, and ships them to Russia, often through the Middle East. Interpol received 4,798 reports of stolen Canadian vehicles found in Russia between February 2024 and July 2026. Pickup trucks like Dodge Rams and Ford F-150s are in particularly high demand. The Royal Canadian Mounted Police states Russia is the top international destination for these reported stolen cars. Interpol figures likely undercount the actual scale of the problem.
source.title: Russia imports stolen Canadian trucks via criminal networks

source.summary: Alexis Abramson argues that UK solar bonds could lower capital costs for rooftop solar installations. The proposal attaches loans to properties rather than individuals, ensuring stability if homeowners move. While the US has existing financing tools, Abramson notes they do not offer the same ownership benefits. He suggests a state-by-state approach in the US due to varying utility structures. The author warns that expiring tax credits increase the urgent need for such financing solutions.
source.title: Columbia Climate School Dean proposes solar bonds to lower UK home financing costs

source.summary: Venezuela's interim president Delcy Rodriguez defended a controversial energy agreement with Donald Trump, asserting the nation retains full ownership of its oil reserves. Rodriguez stated the deal aims to generate over $209bn in revenue and transform Venezuela into an energy powerhouse. Trump announced the historic transaction, claiming it will fill the US Strategic National Reserves and double American oil holdings. The agreement reportedly involves Washington taking control of 65bn barrels from 17 strategic oilfields. The deal has sparked outrage among Venezuelan opposition figures and former officials who condemn it as a neocolonial land grab. Critics argue the pact undermines democratic prospects and compares the state oil company to a US subsidiary. Rodriguez countered accusations of surrendering resources, emphasizing the need for investment to convert underground wealth into national development.
source.title: Venezuela's Delcy Rodriguez defends controversial oil deal with Donald Trump

source.summary: Wall Street closed lower after Federal Reserve Chair Kevin Warsh suggested interest rates might rise due to inflation concerns. ASX 200 futures are pricing in a 0.4 per cent slide on opening. The Australian dollar remained flat at 71.58 US cents while Wall Street indices posted minor losses. Several Australian companies are scheduled to release financial results today.
source.title: ASX futures fall as Wall Street retreats on US inflation fears

source.summary: A US official confirmed that American forces struck two Iranian launchers on Larak Island on Sunday. The official stated that Islamic Revolutionary Guard Corps forces were preparing to launch rockets with sea mines into the Strait of Hormuz. Iranian state media reported that the attack killed and wounded several soldiers and citizens. The strike marks the first known American attacks on Iran since late July.
source.title: US forces strike two Iranian launchers on Larak island

source.summary: Brisbane residents report being woken by construction noise at 4am at a West End McDonald's site. Brisbane City Council confirmed it has not authorized work at that time. Council documents show out-of-hours approval was granted only between 9pm and 2am. Store Tec declined to comment on the violation, stating it is a matter for McDonald's. A McDonald's spokesperson said investigations are ongoing. The restaurant is scheduled to open in late 2026.
source.title: Residents report illegal McDonald's construction at 4am in Brisbane

source.summary: Paris Brunner scored both goals as AS Monaco defeated Olympique de Marseille 2-0 to lead the Ligue 1 table. Monaco remains the only team with two wins after their opening matches. Meanwhile, Stade Rennais beat Le Mans 3-2, and Paris FC defeated Nice 3-0. Reigning champions PSG sit in 11th place after drawing their first two games.
source.title: Paris Brunner scores twice as Monaco top Ligue 1 after beating Marseille

source.summary: The BJP has criticized Rahul Gandhi for hypocrisy over his 'smash the patriarchy' remarks, questioning whether he applies the same principles within his Congress party. BJP leader Bansuri Swaraj accused Gandhi of failing to challenge patriarchy within his own party, citing controversies involving Congress leaders Supriya Shrinate and Randeep Surjewala. She also criticized Gandhi for a joke about Italian Prime Minister Giorgia Meloni and questioned his stance on women's empowerment, including his opposition to the Women's Reservation Bill. Gandhi's remarks were part of the Congress' 'Chhatron Ki Goonj' campaign, where he called for challenging a patriarchal system that restricts women's freedoms. The BJP highlighted Modi's focus on women-led development, contrasting it with Gandhi's alleged lack of action on women's issues.
source.title: BJP criticizes Rahul Gandhi on hypocrisy over patriarchy remarks

source.summary: The U.S. Treasury Department has launched an economic campaign against Iran, targeting its global financial connections, but faces challenges from China, its largest trading partner. China, which receives over 80% of Iranian oil, has expressed support for Iran within international law and warned against unilateral sanctions. Analysts suggest China will likely cooperate minimally to avoid disrupting its upcoming summit with U.S. President Trump. While the U.S. has sanctioned several Iranian-linked entities, including Chinese-owned oil tankers, it has avoided direct sanctions on major Chinese businesses ahead of the summit. Experts believe Trump will prioritize maintaining the fragile trade relationship with China over aggressive action, given the upcoming state visit and potential for future economic cooperation.
source.title: U.S. economic pressure on Iran faces China's cautious cooperation

source.summary: At least three Indian oil refiners and a global energy major plan to avoid using Iran's blacklisted ships for security reasons, according to four sources. Iran has blacklisted 45 vessels for crossing the Strait of Hormuz, threatening to fine, detain, or confiscate cargoes from non-compliant ships. The move targets shuttle runs by Gulf producers like Saudi Arabia and the UAE, which use ship-to-ship transfers to move oil through the strait. Some blacklisted tankers are owned by Saudi Aramco and ADNOC. Analysts warn that Iran's threats could narrow the pool of willing participants in STS transfers, increasing compliance costs and risks for firms with Gulf exposure.
source.title: Indian oil firms and global energy company avoid Iran's blacklisted ships for security

source.summary: Farm ponds in Bundelkhand, a semi-arid region in India, are struggling to provide reliable irrigation due to erratic rainfall linked to a strengthening El Niño and inadequate maintenance. Farmers like Vipin Kumar Yadav report that their ponds, which were filled last year, are now only partially filled, threatening wheat and mustard crops. Experts highlight issues such as seepage, siltation, poor construction, and lack of maintenance funding as major obstacles. The Indian government has prioritized water conservation measures, but many ponds, like those of Keshav Yadav and Sunder Kol, have failed due to improper site selection and insufficient resources. Studies suggest that scientific design, regular desiltation, and community involvement are essential for improving pond effectiveness. Officials acknowledge the need for better maintenance provisions and scientific planning to ensure these structures serve their intended purpose.
source.title: Farm ponds in Bundelkhand face challenges due to El Niño and poor maintenance

source.summary: A planned trans-shipment port in Galathea Bay, Great Nicobar Island, poses a threat to leatherback turtles, which nest there. These turtles, the largest living sea turtles, migrate thousands of kilometers to lay eggs on open sandy beaches. The project, part of the Great Nicobar Island development, includes building a container port, airport, and township, which could destroy the nesting site. Conservation efforts are critical as leatherbacks face threats from habitat loss, bycatch, and artificial lighting. The IUCN lists them as globally vulnerable, with India providing the highest legal protection under the Wildlife (Protection) Act, 1972.
source.title: Trans-shipment project threatens leatherback turtle nesting site in Galathea Bay

source.summary: Mahindra Holidays & Resorts India Limited received a ₹11.34 crore GST demand notice from the Dehradun authority, citing alleged tax shortfalls across four financial years. The company stated it does not expect the show cause notice to have a material financial impact and is pursuing legal remedies. The demand includes ₹11.33 crore in taxes and ₹50,000 in penalties under Uttarakhand and Central GST Acts. The notice was issued via email on 25 August 2026.
source.title: Mahindra Holidays Faces ₹11.34 Crore GST Demand for Tax Shortfalls

source.summary: Karnataka politicians addressed multiple issues during recent discussions. Nikhil Kumaraswamy criticized the state government for functioning like a mafia and questioned land acquisition for an AI city, while UT Khader emphasized the need for a single national anthem and defended youth activism. Discussions also focused on Bengaluru's infrastructure challenges, including a controversial tunnel road project and traffic congestion. Officials outlined plans to expand public transport, improve urban planning, and address environmental concerns. The state government proposed significant investments in infrastructure, including road expansions, metro networks, and stormwater management, to manage rapid urban growth.
source.title: Karnataka Politicians Discuss National Anthem, Infrastructure, and Urban Development

source.summary: Pakistan's women's cricket team is preparing for the Women's Asia Cup by playing full T20 matches against a men's side from the Abdul Qadir Cricket Academy. The matches, which involve both teenage and senior male players, are designed to expose the women's team to greater pressure and improve their decision-making. Captain Fatima Sana emphasized that these games will help the team handle pressure better, as Pakistan has never won the tournament and has struggled in recent competitions. The team will compete in Group A with India, Thailand, and Hong Kong, starting against Thailand on September 1.
source.title: Pakistan women's team trains against men's side for Asia Cup

source.summary: Tamil Nadu Health Minister K.G. Arunraj inaugurated Maa Kauvery, a 120-bed hospital in Chennai dedicated to women and children. The facility offers maternity care, obstetrics, gynaecology, fertility services, neonatal care, and paediatric critical care. It provides 24/7 support for expectant mothers and newborns, including advanced NICU and PICU units. Dr. D. Senguttuvan noted that the model has been successfully implemented in Tiruchi since 2024.
source.title: Tamil Nadu Health Minister Opens 120-Bed Women and Children's Hospital in Chennai

source.summary: A violent clash erupted at Jadavpur University in Kolkata on August 19, involving students from rival factions and a mob of unknown men armed with stones and batons. The incident, which included vandalism and arson, was reportedly incited by a BJP MLA's call for 'mayhem through the night.' Despite the chaos, Chief Minister Suvendu Adhikari dismissed the event as 'nothing' happening at the university. The ABVP denied involvement, while students and faculty criticized the lack of police action and the university's security measures. The incident sparked broader discussions about political influence on campus, with BJP leaders and others accusing the university of harboring 'anti-national' sentiments. A committee was set up to investigate, but no arrests had been made by the time of the report. The violence highlighted tensions between left-leaning students and right-wing groups, with some right-wing organizations gaining new prominence under the current political regime.
source.title: Jadavpur University Violence and Political Responses

source.summary: India's engineering exports increased by 18% year-on-year to $12.24 billion in July 2026, driven by growth across most key markets. The US remained the largest destination, with exports rising 20% to $2.18 billion. However, shipments to Saudi Arabia declined due to logistics issues and geopolitical tensions. The sector's growth was outpaced only by overall merchandise exports, which rose 17% in the same period. EEPC India noted challenges such as rising costs, regulatory hurdles, and geopolitical risks, urging exporters to enhance competitiveness and diversify markets.
source.title: India’s engineering exports jump 18% to $12.24 billion in July; US remains top market

source.summary: Maharashtra FDA chief Tukaram Mundhe clarified that his show-cause notices to Bollywood actors Shah Rukh Khan, Ajay Devgn, and Tiger Shroff for endorsing Vimal's ad were based on existing regulations, not personal discretion. He emphasized that the Food Safety and Standards (Advertising and Claims) Regulations, 2018, hold advertisers and promoters equally responsible for ensuring truthful claims. Mundhe stated that the notices were issued under these rules, which prohibit misleading advertisements, including surrogate promotions of prohibited tobacco products. The FDA claimed the Vimal ad could be an indirect promotion of banned pan masala/tobacco items, and warned of fines up to ₹10 lakh if the actors failed to respond satisfactorily. Mundhe also highlighted his broader crackdown on food businesses, including raids on restaurants and hotels, and noted that over 8,000 licenses have been canceled in the past three years.
source.title: Maharashtra FDA chief clarifies action against Bollywood actors over Vimal ad

source.summary: A Delhi-based family stayed at The Oberoi Udaivilas Hotel in Udaipur for 10 days and left without settling a ₹5.74 lakh bill, prompting the hotel to file an FIR. The family claimed a travel agency would cover the cost, but no prior agreement existed with Maker Baha Travel Agency. The hotel's liaison manager filed the complaint at Ambamata police station, and an investigation is underway. The Oberoi Udaivilas, a luxury property known for hosting celebrities and weddings, typically charges ₹40,000 to ₹70,000 per night.
source.title: Delhi family avoids paying ₹5.74 lakh hotel bill, FIR filed

source.summary: A 20-year-old NEET aspirant from Madhya Pradesh was found dead in her rented flat in Kota, Rajasthan, suspected to be a suicide case. The student, living with her younger sister, had been preparing for the NEET examination at a private coaching institute. Her sister reported no response when knocking on the door, leading to the discovery of the body hanging in the room. Police said no suicide note was found and are investigating the circumstances. The postmortem will be conducted after the family arrives in Kota. Mental health support helplines are provided for those in need.
source.title: 20-year-old NEET aspirant found dead in Kota flat, suspected suicide

source.summary: In 1984, NASA sent 3,301 bees to space aboard the Space Shuttle Discovery to study their ability to build honeycomb in microgravity. The experiment, part of the STS-41C mission, aimed to understand bee behavior and honeycomb structure in zero gravity. Bees initially struggled with flight, colliding with enclosure walls, but adapted by day seven. They built around 200 cm of honeycomb, with cells showing differences in size and wall thickness compared to Earth-made combs. Most bees survived, and the queen laid 35 eggs, though none hatched upon return.
source.title: NASA's 1984 experiment tracked bees' honeycomb construction in microgravity

source.summary: The Indian stock market closed slightly lower on August 26, with gains in banking and metal stocks offset by declines in technology and consumer goods sectors. The Nifty 50 fell 0.52% to 24,207, while the Sensex dropped 0.05% to 77,614. Metal stocks like Hindustan Zinc and SAIL surged between 2% and 5.6%, driven by better realization prospects. Banking stocks benefited from eased inflation concerns and lower bond yields. However, IT stocks weakened as U.S. visa appointments paused, raising margin pressure fears. Crude oil prices fell $1.60 to $86.98 a barrel amid hopes the Strait of Hormuz could reopen. SBFC Finance and IDBI Bank saw significant gains, while Varun Beverages and Jubilant FoodWorks were among the top losers.
source.title: Indian Markets Mixed as Metal Stocks Rise and Tech Shares Fall

source.summary: Gurugram faces severe waterlogging during monsoons, unlike Noida, due to three key factors. First, Noida's drainage system was developed before urban expansion, with major drains connected to rivers like Yamuna and Hindon, while Gurugram's drains are limited and often clogged. Second, Gurugram's natural drainage was disrupted by rapid urbanization, with ponds and channels filled and replaced by concrete, reducing water absorption. Third, Gurugram's growth was fragmented, with private developers building isolated colonies without adequate public infrastructure, leading to disconnected drainage systems. In contrast, Noida's planned development ensured integrated infrastructure. Neighboring Dwarka, despite being a planned settlement, also suffers from drainage issues due to outdated planning and encroachments.
source.title: Gurugram's drainage issues contrast with Noida's planning

source.summary: HP Inc. and Huawei have signed a multi-year cross-licensing agreement for Wi-Fi patents, including the latest Wi-Fi 7 standard. The deal grants both companies access to each other's patents, though financial terms remain undisclosed. Huawei's Chief Intellectual Property Officer highlighted the agreement as a testament to the company's innovation in ICT. The partnership comes despite ongoing U.S. trade restrictions on Huawei, which have limited its access to advanced semiconductors and software. HP described the license as standard and not indicative of a broader strategic relationship. The agreement follows a recent lawsuit and the resolution of legal actions through a patent pool.
source.title: HP and Huawei Enter Multi-Year Wi-Fi Patent Licensing Agreement

source.summary: Michael Kugelman, a South Asia expert at the Atlantic Council, discusses potential changes in U.S. policy toward India, focusing on recent remarks by U.S. Ambassador Sergio Gor in Kashmir. The conversation explores implications of China's ties with Pakistan and a new defense pact involving Türkiye, Saudi Arabia, and Pakistan. Kugelman examines how evolving security dynamics in West Asia may impact India's strategic interests and the role of the U.S. and China in the region. The discussion also covers India-U.S. relations, the China-Pakistan Economic Corridor, and Russia's influence in South Asia.
source.title: US Expert Analyzes Shift in Kashmir Policy Amid India-China Relations

source.summary: A flash flood and mudslide in Nepal's Rasuwa district, near the Tibet border, killed at least 17 people and destroyed villages, roads, and hydropower infrastructure. The BBC reported the flood was caused by excessive snowmelt in the Bhote Koshi River. Rescue efforts, including Nepalese and Chinese helicopters, faced challenges due to high water levels. Authorities warned of missing persons, with 105 Indian nationals reported missing. Prime Minister Balendra Shah ordered coordinated rescue operations and relocation of residents from flood-prone areas. Last year's similar flood killed nine and left 24 missing.
source.title: Flash flood in Nepal-Tibet border kills 17, washes away villages
