source.summary: Protests in Manipur have intensified as civil society groups demand the National Register of Citizens (NRC) be implemented before the 2027 census, citing concerns over undocumented migration and demographic changes. Tribal councils oppose immediate rollout, arguing it is premature and exacerbates regional divisions. Meanwhile, a 48-hour strike disrupted daily life in valley districts. In unrelated news, Chandigarh police uncovered a terror plot involving explosives and weapons, while political figures discussed legal actions and social audits.
source.title: Manipur Protests Escalate Over NRC Implementation Before 2027 Census

source.summary: The Income Tax Department urged taxpayers with business or professional income to file their ITRs by August 31, 2026, for the AY 2026-27 fiscal year. As of August 20, over 6.5 crore ITRs had been filed, including more than 5.9 crore ITR-1 and ITR-2 forms by the July 31 deadline. The department highlighted that ITR-3, ITR-4, ITR-5, and ITR-7 are applicable to non-audit category taxpayers, while ITR-6 is for companies and ITR-7 for trusts and charitable institutions.
source.title: Income Tax Department Urges Taxpayers to File ITRs by August 31

source.summary: The Indian rupee fell 3 paise to 95.74 against the US dollar on Monday, influenced by a strong American currency and weak domestic markets. Forex traders noted that rising Brent crude prices, importer demand, and concerns over US sanctions on Iran affected investor sentiment. The dollar index rose to 98.98, while Brent crude fell to $92.86 per barrel. Domestic markets saw the Sensex and Nifty decline, with foreign investors selling equities worth ₹542.71 crore. India's forex reserves increased by $9.905 billion to $716.907 billion.
source.title: Rupee declines 3 paise to 95.74 against dollar amid market uncertainty

source.summary: The Kochi Corporation is planning to repatriate residents from other states at the Palluruthy Relief Settlement to their respective care facilities, ahead of a proposed overhaul. The existing 10,000 sq. ft. facility, housing 138 residents, will be replaced with a modern, self-sustaining complex featuring a wellness centre and commercial space. Antony Painuthara, chairperson of the Corporation’s welfare committee, stated that around 30-40% of residents are from outside Kerala. The plan includes restoring residents to their families where possible. Sources noted the urgent need for renovation, while an NGO criticized the PRS for past neglect and reduced rescue efforts.
source.title: Kochi Corporation proposes repatriation of residents from other States ahead of overhaul of Palluruthy Relief Settlement

source.summary: The Madras High Court has extended the interim stay on notifying five Tamil Nadu assembly bypolls until September 8, as election petitions challenging the results remain pending. The court rejected the Tamil Nadu government's request to lift the stay. One bypoll was triggered by Chief Minister C Jopseph Vijay's victory in the Trichy East constituency. Meanwhile, DMK president MK Stalin filed an election petition challenging the victory of TVK candidate VS Babu in Kolathur, citing alleged voting machine malfunctions and irregularities. Stalin's loss to Babu, who attributed his win to Vijay's leadership and local connections, has sparked legal and political debate.
source.title: Madras High Court Extends Stay on Tamil Nadu Assembly Bypolls

source.summary: Iran's rial hit a record low of 2.02 million to the dollar as the US prepares new sanctions. The currency's decline follows months of economic strain and conflict. Despite the pressure, Iran maintains control over the Strait of Hormuz, a critical oil route. Iran and Oman are nearing an agreement to jointly manage the strait, amid US criticism of Oman. The US plans stronger sanctions, including secondary penalties against countries trading with Iran. The UAE has suspended trade with Iran, worsening its economic situation. Iran warns against supporting the new sanctions, calling it an act of war.
source.title: US sanctions push Iranian rial to record low as tensions over Hormuz persist

source.summary: Maharashtra has introduced a rule requiring taxi and autorickshaw drivers to demonstrate a working knowledge of Marathi, raising constitutional concerns. The 2026 amendment to the Motor Vehicles Rules mandates that drivers prove language proficiency, with failure leading to potential suspension or revocation of their permits. The state argues this ensures effective communication with passengers, but critics highlight that the regulation risks conflating language proficiency with occupational competence. Article 19 of the Constitution protects the right to practice a profession, and legal experts warn that tying employment to linguistic ability could undermine the principle of free movement across states. The rule has faced similar challenges before, with courts previously rejecting similar conditions. While the state has leeway to regulate transport, the proportionality of the Marathi requirement remains questionable, as it may impose undue burdens on drivers who perform essential functions unrelated to language. The case underscores the tension between linguistic identity and individual freedoms in India's federal structure.
source.title: Maharashtra's Marathi Language Rule for Taxi Drivers Sparks Constitutional Concern

source.summary: SoftBank Group plans to issue $6.3 billion in retail bonds in Japan, the largest such issuance by any issuer in the country, to fund its commitments to OpenAI and refinance maturing debt. The seven-year bonds, priced on 4 September with a coupon range of 4.3-4.9%, will be SoftBank's third retail bond sale in 2026. The move reflects the company's strategy to secure funds for its AI investments, which include over $60 billion in commitments to OpenAI. SoftBank's shares fell 5.3% following the announcement. Analysts note the bond's reliance on retail investors due to banks' reluctance to take on the risk. The company faces a $20 billion shortfall even after this issuance, suggesting potential offshore bond offerings. S&P Global Ratings upgraded SoftBank's outlook to stable, citing improved financial ratios.
source.title: SoftBank to issue $6.3 billion retail bonds for OpenAI funding and debt refinancing

source.summary: The Indian Space Research Organisation (ISRO) transferred the entire Small Satellite Launch Vehicle (SSLV) to Hindustan Aeronautics Limited (HAL) for Rs 511 crore, aiming to shift routine satellite launches to industry. ISRO will collaborate with HAL during the initial two years as it builds its first two rockets. Critics question whether two years is sufficient for HAL to absorb the technology, citing past failures in transferring complex manufacturing knowledge. A 2015 audit of HAL's Su-30MKI fighter production revealed limited indigenous content and higher costs, suggesting challenges in transferring critical design expertise. The deal marks a significant step toward India's goal of establishing a mature space economy worth $44 billion by 2033.
source.title: ISRO Transfers SSLV to HAL Amid Concerns Over Technology Absorption Timeline

source.summary: Godrej Industries Group signed a memorandum of understanding with the Haryana government, outlining a ₹20,000 crore investment plan to create around 40,000 jobs by FY28. The investment will expand on its existing ₹12,000 crore investment in the state, with Godrej Properties planning an additional ₹16,000 crore in real estate. Godrej Ventures aims to invest ₹3,500 crore in Gurugram's office infrastructure. The group highlighted Haryana's economic growth and urban development as key factors in its decision.
source.title: Godrej Industries to invest ₹20,000 crore in Haryana, aiming for 40,000 jobs by FY28

source.summary: The Indian Sugar Mills Association (ISMA) asserts there is no sugar shortage in India, with sufficient stocks to meet demand. ISMA president Niraj Shirgaokar attributes recent price increases to speculative stocking and weather-related production issues. The government has allowed duty-free imports of up to 1 million tonnes of raw sugar to address rising prices. The National Federation of Cooperative Sugar Factories (NFCSF) maintains that domestic supplies are adequate, with production estimates for the 2025-26 season at 279 lakh tonnes. Imports from Brazil may arrive before October 15, though the October 31 deadline is not strictly enforced. The government is expected to consider shipments arriving after this date.
source.title: India's Sugar Supply Adequate, Prices Expected to Drop

source.summary: Stock futures declined on Monday amid concerns over rising Treasury yields and fears of prolonged US-Iran tensions. The Dow Jones, S&P 500, and Nasdaq-100 futures all fell, following a week of market declines. Treasury yields, including the 30-year US Treasury yield reaching nearly 5.3%, have pressured stocks by making bonds more attractive and increasing borrowing costs. Global bond yields in Japan, France, and Germany also rose, adding to financial market concerns. Investors worry that a prolonged US-Iran conflict could keep oil prices high, exacerbating inflation. The US Treasury attempted to stabilize bond markets with measures similar to quantitative easing, but the effects were short-lived. The upcoming PCE inflation data and the Fed's Jackson Hole meeting will provide further clues about interest rates. Nvidia's earnings, expected to show potential price hikes for AI infrastructure, will also test market sentiment. Asian markets showed mixed performance, with Japan and South Korea experiencing declines. Overall, investors remain cautious due to a combination of higher yields, inflation worries, geopolitical risks, and major earnings reports.
source.title: Stock futures fall as Treasury yields and Iran tensions weigh on markets

source.summary: A 31-year-old man from Kerala was arrested for allegedly uploading intimate videos of his wife on a pornographic website and performing sexual acts in front of his four-year-old daughter. The wife discovered the videos after friends alerted her, leading to a police complaint. The accused also pushed for 'wife-swapping,' which the wife refused. Despite counselling, he continued the alleged offences, including another video of him engaging in sexual acts with the daughter. The case is under investigation under the Bharatiya Nyaya Sanhita and POCSO Act. The accused was traced and arrested after going into hiding.
source.title: Kerala man arrested for sharing intimate videos of wife and sexually abusing daughter

source.summary: India's ethanol blending policy, which mandates E20 fuel, has significantly altered agricultural patterns by diverting foodgrains like maize and rice into biofuel production. This shift, driven by the Petroleum and Road Transport Ministries, has displaced traditional crops and raised concerns about food security. NITI Aayog reports highlight potential shortages in pulses and edible oils by 2047-48, yet the ethanol program continues to expand maize cultivation, creating a conflict with food self-reliance goals. The government's ethanol policy generates revenue for distilleries but transfers public assets to private hands, while maize farmers face uncertain prices and market instability. The policy also impacts consumers by reducing fuel efficiency and increasing feed costs for livestock. The article calls for a more equitable distribution of benefits and suggests alternatives like crop residues for ethanol production, emphasizing the need for transparent policy adjustments.
source.title: India's ethanol policy shifts food production, raises security concerns

source.summary: The Maharashtra government's new requirement for autorickshaw, taxi, and cab drivers to speak Marathi has led to increased fares and service disruptions in Mumbai. Drivers, many of whom are elderly and lack formal education, have protested the rule, with some staging strikes and blocking roads. Critics, including musician Avantika Ganguly and former actress Divya Unni, argue the policy is impractical and burdens hardworking individuals. Ganguly reported paying three times the usual fare and facing longer wait times, while Unni criticized the use of fines and harassment as methods to enforce language proficiency. Commuters have also expressed frustration, noting the disruption affects millions who rely on these services daily.
source.title: Mumbai commuters face higher fares and shortages due to Marathi language requirement for drivers

source.summary: Apollo Micro Systems has acquired a 34% stake in Shauryastra Defence Systems, a newly incorporated defence technology company. The investment involved a cash payment of ₹34,000 for 3,400 equity shares at ₹10 each. Shauryastra Defence Systems was established on 21 August 2026 to address futuristic operational needs of the Indian Armed Forces. The venture will be led by Dr V. K. Saraswat, with Apollo Micro Systems aiming to expand its defence electronics capabilities and align with the Atmanirbhar Bharat initiative. The transaction was completed without additional regulatory approvals. The company also announced its open offer to acquire shares in Premier Explosives, with SEBI setting a 12-day tender period for the offer.
source.title: Apollo Micro Systems Acquires 34% Stake in Shauryastra Defence Systems

source.summary: The Indian stock market closed lower on Monday, 24 August, with the Sensex dropping 0.22% to 77,369 and the Nifty 50 falling 0.14% to 24,219.05. The Nifty Metal index rose 1.6%, outperforming other sectors. Market declines were attributed to weak global cues, US-Iran tensions, and rising bond yields. Analysts noted caution as investors awaited further US sanctions on Iran. Banking and financial sectors underperformed, while realty and IT indices saw gains. Technical analysis suggested potential support levels for the Nifty at 24,050-24,070 and resistance at 24,350-24,370.
source.title: Indian stock market declines amid global weakness, metal sector rises

source.summary: U.S. Treasury Secretary Scott Bessent warned Iran of an economic D-Day, announcing new sanctions targeting Iran's trade partners. The move follows Iran's President Masoud Pezeshkian defending a memorandum of understanding with the U.S. as a path out of the stalled war. Iran vowed to shut down all oil exports from the Gulf if the economic war continues. Bessent emphasized the Trump administration's shift to economic pressure, aiming to sever Iran's economic lifelines. Iran dismissed the sanctions as desperate, with Supreme National Security Council secretary Mohsen Rezaei threatening to cut oil exports and label support for U.S. measures as an act of war. The U.S. plans to reveal more severe sanctions, while Iran's Foreign Minister Abbas Araghchi called the measures repetitive and urged respectful dialogue.
source.title: U.S. threatens Iran with economic sanctions as Tehran vows oil export shutdown

source.summary: Saikat Majumdar's review of Avni Doshi's novel 'The First House' critiques the book's lack of compelling character development and narrative depth. While praising Doshi's choice to focus on marital decay without political polemic, Majumdar argues the characters remain elusive and emotionally irrelevant. The protagonist, a woman trapped in a failing marriage, is underdeveloped, with limited depth beyond her self-perceived unattractiveness and economic dependence. The husband is portrayed as a cardboard cut-out, and the daughters are passive, infantilized figures. Majumdar notes the novel's attempt to create a spectrum of unattractive characters fails to engage the reader, as they lack distinct personalities and emotional resonance. The narrative, set in a middle-class US suburb, is criticized for its vacuousness and claustrophobic tone, with the narrator's self-indulgent ruminations failing to evoke empathy. The review highlights the novel's failure to transform boredom into fascination, leaving a lasting impression of vague, half-baked expressions that fail to connect with readers.
source.title: Review of Avni Doshi's 'The First House' highlights weak character development and narrative emptiness

source.summary: Gold prices in India remained high on Monday, with 24-carat gold priced at ₹1,62,289 per 10 grams and 22-carat gold at ₹1,48,656.72 per 10 grams. Mumbai and Kolkata saw slightly higher rates, while Delhi and Bengaluru remained stable. International gold prices also reached a three-month high, driven by global uncertainty, a weaker US dollar, and expectations of easing interest rates. Central bank purchases and geopolitical tensions further supported demand for gold.
source.title: Indian gold prices remain elevated with 24K at ₹1,62,289 per 10 grams

source.summary: Nepal and Chinese authorities report that a catastrophic mudslide triggered by a glacier collapse has killed at least 797 people and left more than 3,000 missing. On the fifth day of rescue efforts, 2,502 people remain unaccounted for in Nepal while 546 are missing in Tibet. Chinese Foreign Minister Wang Yi described the event as the most severe cross-border disaster in recent years. The Red Cross estimates over 90,000 people were affected, with China linking the disaster to climate change. Rescue operations face extreme challenges due to rising river levels and new landslides. Authorities in Nepal have begun mass burials for decomposing bodies, noting that more than half are beyond recognition. International experts are assisting with tunnel rescue operations and forensic identification.
source.title: Nepal and China report nearly 800 deaths and over 3,000 missing after Himalayan mudslide

source.summary: At least seven people died after a ferry carrying nearly 270 people capsized off northern Cyprus on Sunday, Turkish media reported. Northern Cyprus Prime Minister Unal Ustel stated that 237 individuals were rescued while a search continues for 24 others. The vessel, owned by Filo Denizcilik, sank 7.5 kilometers off the coast after taking on water due to adverse weather just 15 minutes after departing Kyrenia for Tasucu.
source.title: Ferry capsizes off northern Cyprus killing at least seven

source.summary: The prime minister of the Turkish Republic of Northern Cyprus stated that 237 people were rescued and seven died after a vessel carrying 267 people capsized off Kyrenia. Unal Ustel told Anadolu that search and rescue efforts continue for 23 missing individuals. Türkiye's Interior Ministry confirmed the passenger vessel FILOJET began taking on water about four miles off Kyrenia Port. Multiple coast guard and naval assets from both regions were deployed to support the ongoing operations.
source.title: TRNC Premier reports 237 rescued and 7 dead after vessel capsizes off Kyrenia

source.summary: Rosenheim police confirmed that a 31-year-old British woman died from injuries sustained in a stabbing at the local train station early Sunday morning. Federal officers detained a 27-year-old German man from Furstenfeldbruck immediately after the attack. Authorities have not released the names of the victim or suspect due to privacy rules and are currently investigating the motive. Police are asking witnesses who saw an argument or physical altercation to come forward.
source.title: German police detain suspect after stabbing British woman at Rosenheim station

source.summary: UNESCO added six historic plantation estates, known as 'rocas', to its World Heritage List last month, highlighting their significance in the history of forced labor. Conceicao Moreno, a National Assembly member and descendant of plantation workers, emphasized the deep cultural connection these sites hold for the community. While most estates remain in disrepair, investment firm HBD is renovating two sites into hotels to generate employment and preserve the architecture. Culture chief Emir Boa Morte stated that this recognition aims to mobilize the population and restore the buildings over the next decade. Officials insist that new development will not erase history but will instead combine the past with present uses. UNESCO noted the sites illustrate a large-scale colonial agro-industrial system based on forced migration from the late 19th to mid-20th century.
source.title: UNESCO recognition boosts preservation efforts for Sao Tome historic plantations

source.summary: Engineers from ArianeGroup, Arianespace, CNES, Eumetsat, ESA, and Thales Alenia Space describe the preparation of an Ariane 6 rocket carrying the MTG-I2 satellite at Europe's Spaceport. The rocket was built to be cheaper and more versatile than its predecessor while enabling faster assembly and flexible launch windows. The satellite, weighing 3.8 tonnes, will monitor European skies to help prevent natural disasters like floods and fires. James Champion of the European Space Agency states the programme cost 6 billion euros with benefits exceeding 61 billion. Cristian Bank of Eumetsat notes the satellite will update data every 2.5 minutes to improve local weather forecasting. Graeme Mason of ESA calls the new imager the best in the world, with a lightning detector ahead of US technology. The launch marks the completion of Europe's third-generation meteorological constellation.
source.title: Engineers prepare Ariane 6 rocket to launch MTG-I2 weather satellite

source.summary: Ducati's Marc Marquez won the Aragon Grand Prix, his third consecutive victory on the circuit. He overtook Aprilia's Marco Bezzecchi on lap six to secure the win. KTM's Pedro Acosta finished second, while Bezzecchi took third. Marquez moved to 237 points, closing the gap to leader Jorge Martin. Marquez attributed his earlier struggles to a setup error regarding his rear ride-height device.
source.title: Ducati's Marc Marquez wins Aragon Grand Prix to narrow championship gap

source.summary: At least seven people died after a ferry carrying nearly 270 passengers and crew capsized off northern Cyprus, Turkish media reported. Northern Cyprus Prime Minister Unal Ustel stated that 237 people were rescued while a search continues for 24 others. The vessel, owned by Filo Denizcilik, began taking on water 15 minutes after departure due to adverse weather. Kyrenia Mayor Murat Senkul confirmed the ship sank off Diana beach. Cyprus government spokesman Constantinos Letymbiotis expressed readiness to assist in search and rescue efforts.
source.title: Seven die after ferry capsizes off northern Cyprus carrying nearly 270 people

source.summary: French authorities report two sailors are missing after the Maranello sank southwest of Plymouth. The French naval prefecture states the vessel contacted the Stradale regarding fishing gear issues before sinking. Three crew members were recovered, with one injured and evacuated by helicopter. A major search-and-rescue operation continues in waters under British responsibility, involving French and British assets coordinated by MRCC Falmouth.
source.title: Two sailors missing after French trawler sinks near British port

source.summary: Spain's Council of Ministers will approve a €165 million emergency package for Ceuta to revive the local economy and strengthen public services. First Deputy Prime Minister Carlos Cuerpo announced the funds, which include €80 million for immediate economic support and €70 million for 2027. Minister Ángel Víctor Torres pledged that all irregular migrants who entered between July 30 and 31 will be returned to Morocco. The package complements a separate €180 million structural recovery plan currently being negotiated with local stakeholders.
source.title: Spain approves €165m emergency aid for Ceuta amid migrant crisis

source.summary: Russian Ambassador-at-large Andrey Belousov accused the United States of viewing Europe as a potential nuclear battlefield. Speaking on RT TV, he claimed Washington seeks to divert attention from American nuclear deployments in Europe. Belousov warned that reducing Russia's non-strategic arsenal could increase nuclear-use risks involving US allies. He stated Moscow remains open to strategic dialogue but demands equal security guarantees. The comments follow the expiration of the New START treaty and ongoing NATO-Russia tensions.
source.title: Russian Ambassador accuses US of treating Europe as nuclear battlefield

source.summary: The Trump administration claims a new deal will soon allow the U.S. to get a majority of its oil from Venezuela. NPR notes there are many reasons to be skeptical of this announcement. The outlet states it does not offer or accept money for coverage or interviews. Anyone making such an offer does not represent NPR.
source.title: Trump administration claims new deal will make Venezuela majority US oil source

source.summary: Guinea-Bissau's military junta voted to amend the constitution, granting the president authority to appoint and dismiss the prime minister and dissolve parliament. The proposed changes would reduce parliamentary seats from 102 to 65 to stabilize institutions ahead of December elections. Opposition groups have urged a boycott, warning the move could cement junta leader power. Results are expected from Tuesday after Sunday polls closed.
source.title: Guinea-Bissau junta votes on presidential power expansion

source.summary: The article lists locations in France's most beautiful villages where buyers can purchase property. It notes that a required site part failed to load due to browser issues. Readers are advised to check connections or disable ad blockers.
source.title: France's most beautiful villages offer property for sale

source.title: NASA launches Roman telescope to study dark energy and exoplanets

source.summary: India likely grew at more than 7% last quarter, yet this pace may not achieve Prime Minister Narendra Modi's vision of a developed nation by 2047. Ashok Lahiri, a senior official at the country's apex government-run think tank, states that reaching this status requires the world's sixth-largest economy to grow at 9.25% annually for 21 years. While the Viksit Bharat initiative is a centerpiece of Modi's third term, several economists warn that assuming the current growth rate, India's economy would fall short of this ambitious target.
source.title: India's 7% growth may fall short of Modi's 2047 developed nation dream

source.summary: Australia's far-right One Nation party secured its first lower house seat in Western Australia by defeating the ruling Labor Party in a special election. With 75% of votes counted, One Nation candidate Luke Herdegen held 57% of the vote, according to the state electoral commission. Broadcaster ABC called the by-election for Herdegen, marking a significant shift from last year's results where Labor won the area. The special election was triggered when longtime Labor lawmaker Paul Papalia announced his retirement due to a family illness.
source.title: One Nation party wins Western Australia special election seat

source.summary: Italy aims to reform its beach concession system by introducing public tenders for all 12,000 paid beaches by September 30, 2027. The European Commission has pressured Rome to comply with the 2009 Bolkestein directive regarding free competition. Current private operators manage over 42% of the coastline, according to Legambiente, while the state collects between €80m and €100m annually. Critics warn that new tenders could displace traditional family-owned businesses in favor of large tourism groups.
source.title: Italy plans to reform its 12,000 private beaches by 2027

source.summary: The article reports that residents of Narsarsuaq, a remote settlement in southern Greenland, are increasingly concerned about the potential return of United States military presence and the exploitation of local natural resources. Ole Guldager, a local historian, stated that the community fears losing their homes if American troops reoccupy the former base. The United States has been negotiating with Danish and Greenlandic representatives to expand its military footprint, demanding sovereignty over the territory of future installations. Meanwhile, Aviaja Lennert, a farmer near the Kvanefjeld rare earth deposit, expressed worry about uranium extraction and US interest in the island's wealth. The European Union is attempting to strengthen its influence by proposing increased investment and urging respect for Greenlandic sovereignty. Barry Andrews, an Irish MEP, emphasized that Greenland's sovereignty must be respected and that the EU should be the island's preferred partner. Despite these diplomatic efforts, the Greenland government recently ordered a postponement of a controversial oil exploration project linked to US interests.
source.title: Residents fear US military return and mining threats in southern Greenland

source.summary: Arthur Kermalvezen and Audrey, both donor-conceived in Paris, fell in love but feared they might be half-siblings due to limited sperm banks. French laws restrict genetic testing, forcing the couple to rely on an illegal doctor or a home kit ordered abroad. After confirming they were not related, Audrey discovered her biological sister was a client she had represented in court. Their DNA testing revealed four out of ten activists shared the same donor. Audrey eventually found her deceased donor, Philippe, through a genetic match. Their campaign contributed to legal changes allowing future donor-conceived individuals to access donor information. Despite these wins, France remains one of few European nations banning at-home DNA tests.
source.title: Donor-conceived couple in France tests for sibling relation

source.summary: President Donald Trump sold up to $25 million of Vanguard Dividend Appreciation ETF (VIG) in June 2026, while holding Schwab U.S. Dividend Equity ETF (SCHD). VIG's performance lagged behind SCHD's 30% year-to-date gain. Trump also bought Fidelity National Information Services (FIS), Home Depot (HD), and the Technology Select Sector SPDR ETF (XLK). SCHD outperformed the S&P 500 due to its energy holdings and exclusion of AI mega-caps. The report notes the filing only provides a range for the sale and no rationale for the transaction.
source.title: Trump Just Dumped Over $5 Million Of A Popular Dividend ETF. Here’s What It Means For VIG and SCHD

source.summary: US Treasury Secretary Scott Bessent warned Iran of an 'economic D-Day' to sever all financial ties, threatening to isolate any nation partnering with the country. Iran dismissed the comments, vowing to shut down oil exports if the conflict continues. The Strait of Hormuz, a critical oil route, has been effectively blocked by Iran since February. Bessent's remarks followed previous US threats, including Trump's April warning of a 'civilisation dying' unless Iran unblocked the strait. The US has imposed tough sanctions on Iran since 2018, after pulling out of the 2015 nuclear deal. Biden's attempts to reinstate the deal failed, and recent sanctions targeted foreign firms doing business with Tehran.
source.title: US Treasury Secretary warns of economic D-Day against Iran

source.summary: The UK government must decide whether to approve oil and gas drilling at Rosebank and Jackdaw fields, with differing environmental and energy implications. The Conservative government previously granted licenses in 2022 and 2023, but a court ruled their environmental assessments were incomplete, failing to account for emissions from burning the extracted oil and gas. The new energy and climate secretary, Miatta Fahnbulleh, must assess if updated assessments justify approval. Jackdaw, a small gasfield, could contribute to energy security by displacing dirtier LNG imports, while Rosebank, a large oilfield, would generate significant emissions over 25 years, conflicting with net zero targets. The article argues that Rosebank should only be approved if it meets carbon capture and storage (CCS) conditions, a technology already used by Equinor. The government is also urged to accelerate decommissioning of aging fields and publish a net zero transition roadmap to address economic and climate concerns.
source.title: UK Government Faces Decision on Oil Drilling Conditions Amid Climate and Energy Pressures

source.summary: The article explores the potential for a financial crisis amid rising interest rates and geopolitical tensions, particularly focusing on the U.S. Treasury market. It notes that while high interest rates are not a direct cause of funding crises, they can lead to significant price corrections for riskier assets. The piece highlights the shift in demand for U.S. Treasury securities from foreign official reserves to private investors, including hedge funds and domestic private buyers. It also discusses the role of private credit markets and the risks associated with leverage, drawing parallels to the 2008 subprime crisis. The article warns that a financial meltdown could be linked to the unwinding of borrowing bubbles, especially in the context of an AI-driven economy. It concludes by suggesting that the current economic framework may be leading to a paradigm breakdown, similar to the end of the gold standard era.
source.title: Analysts Discuss Risks of Financial Crisis Amid Rising Interest Rates and Geopolitical Tensions

source.summary: Nine individuals, including an Nvidia employee, face charges in Taiwan for illegally exporting AI servers to China, violating U.S. export controls. The servers, containing advanced Nvidia chips, were shipped through Indonesia and Japan. Prosecutors allege breach of trust and document forgery, seeking up to five years in prison for seven defendants. Three are charged with embezzlement. Taiwan lacks specific laws against such exports, prompting calls for legislative change. Nvidia and Super Micro have not commented on the allegations.
source.title: Nvidia Employee Charged in Taiwan AI Server Smuggling Case

source.summary: Shein, a global ultra-fast fashion company, has launched its initial public offering. The company faces challenges as its growth rate has slowed. Shein's IPO marks a significant step in its expansion strategy. The move comes as the fashion industry experiences shifting consumer trends and increased competition. The company's financial performance will be closely watched by investors.
source.title: Shein Launches IPO Amid Slowing Growth

source.summary: Iranian Oil Minister Mohsen Paknejad announced a major natural gas discovery in southern Fars province, estimating over 7.5 trillion cubic feet of gas, with 5.7 trillion cubic feet recoverable. The gas, classified as 'sweet', is expected to reduce development and production costs. The find could support Iran's energy needs for 15 years, though production timelines remain unclear. The announcement follows pressure on Iran's oil exports due to US sanctions and naval restrictions.
source.title: Iran discovers 7.5 trillion cubic feet of natural gas in Fars province

source.summary: The article outlines the emerging competition within France's left-wing political sphere as the 2027 presidential election approaches. Key figures and factions are positioning themselves for the contest, signaling a potential shift in the country's political landscape. The piece highlights the dynamics at play among leftist candidates and their respective parties. The source notes the significance of this internal battle in shaping the broader electoral narrative. The article emphasizes the importance of this phase in the lead-up to the election.
source.title: French Left Faces Internal Struggle Ahead of 2027 Presidential Race

source.summary: Volkswagen CEO Oliver Blume warned that the company and Germany's car industry are facing 'the biggest upheaval in their history' due to global challenges and Chinese competition. The statement was made ahead of meetings with staff. Blume described the situation as 'more than critical', highlighting the severe pressures on the sector.
source.title: Volkswagen CEO warns German car industry faces historic upheaval

source.summary: Japan's seismic risks vary across its largest cities, with Tokyo, Osaka, and Nagoya facing different threats. A recent 5.9 magnitude earthquake in Tokyo highlighted the region's vulnerability to a more destructive quake. Osaka and Nagoya are at risk from the Nankai Trough megathrust earthquake, while Tokyo's main concern is a direct earthquake beneath the capital. The Japanese government has proposed establishing a second capital to mitigate the impact of a catastrophic Tokyo quake.
source.title: Japan's Megacities Face Divergent Seismic Risks and Preparedness Challenges

source.summary: The US has canceled a joint amphibious landing drill with South Korea, scheduled for September, due to the ongoing conflict with Iran. South Korean and US military officials confirmed the cancellation of the Ssangyong exercise, according to The Chosun Daily. The Pentagon is mobilizing troops to the Middle East, with 39,000 troops stationed on the Korean Peninsula under a defense pact with Seoul. South Korea plans to hold its own drill, which typically involves 10,000 to 20,000 personnel, amphibious assault ships, and stealth aircraft. Washington reportedly informed South Korea that troop mobilization for the exercise was difficult due to the aftermath of the Iran war. The decision follows the early conclusion of the annual Ulchi Freedom Shield exercise, which was shortened to five days under Trump's instructions, prioritizing outreach to North Korea.
source.title: US halts joint amphibious drill with South Korea due to Iran conflict

source.summary: Japanese clinics are promoting 'beauty sleep' treatments that include psychotropic drugs and sleeping pills, sparking controversy. Experts criticize the practice, noting these medications are not intended for cosmetic use and may lead to dependence. The treatments, not covered by public health insurance, have raised concerns about inappropriate prescription practices. The Japanese Society of Sleep Research advises against long-term use of such medications for non-medical purposes. Kurume University's president warns that sleeping pills should be used only for insomnia treatment, not for beauty enhancement.
source.title: Japanese Clinics Offer Beauty Sleep Treatments with Prescription Drugs

source.summary: The article discusses how the U.S. war with Iran is interconnected with other global conflicts, including Russia's war in Ukraine and tensions in the Korean Peninsula. NPR correspondents Tom Bowman and Emily Feng explain that North Korea is providing troops to Russia, while Russia and China are supporting Iran's military efforts. The article highlights the global impact of these conflicts, such as disruptions in oil supply through the Strait of Hormuz and the strain on U.S. military resources like Patriot missiles. It also notes how China is strengthening its military capabilities to rival the U.S., with potential implications for Taiwan. The discussion includes Trump's outreach to North Korea and the strategic considerations of nuclear proliferation in the region.
source.title: U.S.-Iran War Ties to Global Conflicts and Strategic Shifts

source.summary: The Supreme Court has directed the State of Jharkhand and its Public Service Commission to respond to a petition seeking a CBI investigation into alleged malpractices in a civil services exam. The petition, filed by activist Harisharan Devgan, argues that the State Criminal Investigation Department lacks impartiality. Students have protested for over a month, citing irregularities in evaluation, including a viral OMR carbon copy showing discrepancies. The petition calls for securing physical and digital evidence, including CCTV footage and server logs, to ensure an unbiased probe.
source.title: Supreme Court asks Jharkhand to allow CBI probe into exam irregularities

source.summary: Tamil Nadu Chief Minister C Joseph Vijay announced the abandonment of the Parandur greenfield airport project, citing concerns over agricultural land disruption and impact on farmers' livelihoods. The decision follows protests from residents of 12 surrounding villages, whom Vijay supported. While the government will expand Chennai's Meenambakkam airport, it is now seeking alternative sites for a new airport through feasibility studies. The DMK criticized the move, arguing it could harm industrial growth and push businesses to neighboring states. The announcement triggered an assembly walkout by DMK MLAs, who accused the government of a policy reversal.
source.title: Tamil Nadu chief minister scraps Parandur airport plan due to land concerns

source.summary: An Indian-American engineer, Anita Nariani Schulze, has filed a discrimination lawsuit against Apple Inc., alleging that her male managers from India and Pakistan treated her with bias based on her nationality, religion, and gender. The case, filed in California state court, claims her managers excluded her from meetings, criticized her work, and denied her bonuses despite positive performance reviews. Judge Sunil R. Kulkarni rejected Apple's motion to dismiss the case but denied Schulze's request to represent a class of female employees. Meanwhile, Cisco Systems faces a separate lawsuit from California's civil rights agency over alleged caste-based discrimination against a Dalit employee. Cisco denies the claims, arguing caste is not a protected category under U.S. law.
source.title: Indian Engineer Files Bias Lawsuit Against Apple

source.summary: Protests in Manipur have intensified as civil society groups demand the National Register of Citizens (NRC) be implemented before the 2027 census, citing concerns over undocumented migration and demographic changes. Tribal councils oppose immediate rollout, arguing it is premature and exacerbates regional divisions. Meanwhile, a 48-hour strike disrupted daily life in valley districts. In unrelated news, Chandigarh police uncovered a terror plot involving explosives and weapons, while political figures discussed legal actions and social audits.
source.title: Manipur Protests Escalate Over NRC Implementation Before 2027 Census

source.summary: The Indian rupee fell 3 paise to 95.74 against the US dollar on Monday, influenced by a strong American currency and weak domestic markets. Forex traders noted that rising Brent crude prices, importer demand, and concerns over US sanctions on Iran affected investor sentiment. The dollar index rose to 98.98, while Brent crude fell to $92.86 per barrel. Domestic markets saw the Sensex and Nifty decline, with foreign investors selling equities worth ₹542.71 crore. India's forex reserves increased by $9.905 billion to $716.907 billion.
source.title: Rupee declines 3 paise to 95.74 against dollar amid market uncertainty

source.summary: The Kochi Corporation is planning to repatriate residents from other states at the Palluruthy Relief Settlement to their respective care facilities, ahead of a proposed overhaul. The existing 10,000 sq. ft. facility, housing 138 residents, will be replaced with a modern, self-sustaining complex featuring a wellness centre and commercial space. Antony Painuthara, chairperson of the Corporation’s welfare committee, stated that around 30-40% of residents are from outside Kerala. The plan includes restoring residents to their families where possible. Sources noted the urgent need for renovation, while an NGO criticized the PRS for past neglect and reduced rescue efforts.
source.title: Kochi Corporation proposes repatriation of residents from other States ahead of overhaul of Palluruthy Relief Settlement

source.summary: Iran's rial hit a record low of 2.02 million to the dollar as the US prepares new sanctions. The currency's decline follows months of economic strain and conflict. Despite the pressure, Iran maintains control over the Strait of Hormuz, a critical oil route. Iran and Oman are nearing an agreement to jointly manage the strait, amid US criticism of Oman. The US plans stronger sanctions, including secondary penalties against countries trading with Iran. The UAE has suspended trade with Iran, worsening its economic situation. Iran warns against supporting the new sanctions, calling it an act of war.
source.title: US sanctions push Iranian rial to record low as tensions over Hormuz persist

source.summary: The Paris region has introduced retro 'sunflower' pools, evoking nostalgia among residents and visitors. These pools, designed with sunflower motifs, have become a popular attraction. Local authorities stated the initiative aims to blend historical charm with modern recreational spaces. The project has drawn positive reactions from the community. The pools are part of a broader effort to revitalize public spaces with thematic elements.
source.title: Paris Region Introduces Retro Sunflower Pools Sparking Nostalgia

source.summary: Nine years after the 2017 Myanmar military crackdown that displaced hundreds of thousands of Rohingya Muslims, the crisis continues to escalate. Despite ongoing humanitarian efforts, conditions in refugee camps in Bangladesh have deteriorated, with aid shrinking and living conditions worsening. Analysts warn that repatriation is premature as conflict in Rakhine state persists, and more Rohingya continue fleeing into Bangladesh. The U.N. refugee agency reports that 154,000 additional Rohingya have arrived since 2024, with conditions in Rakhine remaining unstable. Rohingya refugees, barred from legal work in Bangladesh, rely heavily on dwindling humanitarian aid, which has been cut multiple times in recent years. With international attention waning and funding shortfalls, refugees face increasing risks of falling into illicit economies or dangerous journeys to Malaysia. Experts call for greater international engagement and support to address the crisis, which has left over a million Rohingya in limbo for nearly a decade.
source.title: Rohingya refugees face worsening crisis as return remains uncertain

source.summary: Samuel Bateman, a polygamous sect leader featured in Netflix's Trust Me: The False Prophet, is set to be sentenced after three girls were found in a poorly ventilated trailer. Bateman, already serving a 50-year federal prison sentence for child sex offenses, faces additional charges from a 2022 traffic stop. Authorities were alerted after seeing small fingers through the trailer's gaps, revealing conditions with a makeshift toilet and no air conditioning. Each count carries a mandatory sentence of four to eight years. Bateman, who claimed the girls had escaped, admitted knowing the girls were trapped but downplayed the conditions. His sect, an offshoot of Warren Jeffs' group, has seen its influence wane, with the towns no longer under court supervision.
source.title: Polygamous leader to face sentencing after girls rescued from trailer

source.summary: US President Donald Trump claimed all mines have been removed or detonated in the Strait of Hormuz, according to his social media post. He warned Iran that any vessel placing new mines would be 'systematically destroyed' under Space Force surveillance. Trump emphasized a 'zero tolerance policy' on mine placement, asserting Washington is monitoring the strategic waterway and other locations with Space Force technology. The statement was made on 25 August 2026.
source.title: Trump announces mine clearance in Strait of Hormuz, threatens Iran with 'zero tolerance'

source.summary: Two unvaccinated people in Pennsylvania have died from measles, according to health officials. Pennsylvania reported 393 cases this year, part of a national surge to the highest level in 35 years. Last year, two unvaccinated children in Texas died during an outbreak affecting over 1,000 people. Vaccination rates in Lancaster County, where the deaths occurred, are 85% for kindergarten-age students, below the 95% needed for herd immunity. Public health officials warn that vaccine hesitancy and recent policy changes may contribute to the spread of measles.
source.title: Two unvaccinated individuals die from measles in Pennsylvania

source.summary: Brazil’s data protection regulator fined ByteDance, TikTok’s parent company, nearly $30 million for alleged mishandling of minors' personal data. The ruling cited failures in protecting children and teenagers' information across both logged-in and guest sessions. The company has 10 days to appeal the decision, which also orders the removal of illegally collected data and a plan to improve protections for minors. The regulator previously recommended suspending Discord live broadcasts following a suicide case linked to the platform. Brazil’s government and Supreme Court have sought to regulate internet use by minors, with similar efforts underway in Australia, Canada, and Indonesia.
source.title: Brazilian Regulator Fines TikTok's Parent Company $30 Million Over Data Privacy Violations Involving Minors

source.summary: The AP has outlined a hypothetical 17-game college football road trip that would allow fans to see every team in its preseason Top 25. The journey begins with the Apple Cup between Washington State and Washington on September 6, followed by games involving SMU, Missouri, Tennessee, and LSU. The schedule includes key matchups like Oklahoma vs. Georgia, Ohio State vs. Iowa, and the Iron Bowl between Auburn and Alabama on November 28. The route prioritizes reasonable travel times between games, with some games scheduled in the early afternoon to allow for overnight travel. The trip concludes with a Thanksgiving showdown between Texas and Texas A&M, followed by the Iron Bowl. The AP's plan highlights major rivalries and potential matchups that could shape the season.
source.title: AP's College Football Top 25 Dream Road Trip Outlines 17 Games

source.summary: Israeli Prime Minister Benjamin Netanyahu accused Iran of attempting to kill one of his sons, though he provided no details about the alleged plot. The claim came during an interview with Channel 14, following reports that a security agency refused to protect a political rival ahead of the October 27 general election. Netanyahu emphasized the need for security measures, citing the heightened tensions since the U.S.-Israeli war on Iran began in February. Israeli media reported that Shin Bet chief David Zini declined to provide security for Gadi Eisenkot, whose party is projected to win the most seats. Netanyahu told Zini that appropriate security should be provided for any prime ministerial candidate.
source.title: Netanyahu Accuses Iran of Attempting to Kill One of His Sons

source.summary: Slovak police have arrested three foreign nationals for planning an arson attack on a drone manufacturing facility, which could have endangered 70 employees. The suspects allegedly prepared a napalm-like mixture and a site plan, leading to the seizure of incendiary substances and tools. Two were detained in Slovakia, while the third was arrested in Germany under a European arrest warrant. Authorities reported no injuries or damage due to their intervention.
source.title: Slovak police arrest three foreigners for planned arson at drone factory

source.summary: A US judge has rejected Ghislaine Maxwell's attempt to overturn her sex trafficking conviction. The court dismissed her appeal, upholding the original verdict. Maxwell was found guilty of conspiring to sexually exploit minors. The ruling marks the final stage in her legal proceedings. The court emphasized the evidence supporting the conviction.
source.title: US judge denies Ghislaine Maxwell's appeal against sex trafficking conviction

source.summary: Sudan's short-stature football team faces war, displacement, and limited resources as it prepares for the 2026 World Cup. Players from different regions, many displaced by conflict, train in Khartoum despite security challenges. Soccer expert Mohammed Abdullah praised their dedication. The team, established in 2020, aims to overcome financial and travel obstacles. Player Ibrahim Abdalla overcame childhood discrimination to pursue football. Sudan missed the first World Cup for short-stature teams due to funding issues. The federation's president, Mohammed Nour Kasha, said the team brings hope to a war-torn country. The conflict has killed 59,000 and displaced 13 million people, making the team's campaign a symbol of resilience.
source.title: Sudan's short-stature football team seeks World Cup amid conflict

source.summary: The World Health Organisation has updated temporary recommendations for member states amid the ongoing Ebola outbreak in the Democratic Republic of Congo. The DRC is classified as the only country at 'very high' risk, with neighboring nations like Burundi and the Central African Republic rated 'high risk'. The WHO chief noted the outbreak is spreading faster than any previous one and remains a public health emergency of international concern. Congolese authorities reported 5514 confirmed cases and 2690 deaths, resulting in a 47.9 percent fatality rate.
source.title: WHO updates Ebola recommendations as DRC outbreak spreads

source.summary: Russian military drones have been accused of targeting Ukrainian civilians in 'human safaris,' a practice described as a war crime by the UN. A video showing a civilian cyclist being killed by a drone, posted and later deleted by the Russian military, sparked outrage. Experts note this is not an isolated incident, with such attacks occurring for two years, particularly in Kherson and other frontline regions. The practice involves using short-range drones to hunt civilians, including pedestrians, cyclists, and vehicles, often with the intent to instill fear and force displacement. The UN's independent commission has condemned these actions as potential crimes against humanity. Analysts suggest the tactics are tolerated by Russian military leadership and may serve as training for drone operators or a means to desensitize troops to civilian casualties. The videos are also used to justify further drone purchases and funding. Despite the controversy, the Russian military continues these operations, with experts warning that the low cost and effectiveness of such tactics could be replicated elsewhere.
source.title: Russian drones target Ukrainian civilians in 'human safaris' across multiple regions

source.summary: A tornado struck a southern French village, injuring dozens and leaving over 1,400 homes without electricity. Local authorities in Pomas reported two people in critical condition. The village is now assessing the aftermath of the storm, which occurred on August 25.
source.title: French village assesses damage after tornado leaves 1,400 homes without power

source.summary: A rare tornado struck the French village of Pomas, damaging 300 of its 476 homes and injuring 37 people, including two severely. Mayor Herve Gine described the event as resembling 'being bombed by nature,' with widespread destruction and residents in shock. Interior Minister Laurent Nunez called it 'of rare intensity,' while officials noted 7,250 households in the region lost power. Emergency crews searched for victims, and some residents were relocated to a temporary shelter. The incident highlights ongoing extreme weather events in France this summer.
source.title: Tornado damages French village, leaves 37 injured

source.summary: U.S. President Donald Trump criticized Iran's continued executions of individuals linked to protests that erupted earlier this year. He condemned the Islamic Republic's actions as a humanitarian crisis, citing the high number of executions since the war began. Trump's remarks came amid rising tensions in the region, with Iranian authorities reporting over 3,000 deaths attributed to 'terrorist acts' by the U.S. and Israel. Rights groups, however, documented a higher toll and accused security forces of excessive force. Over 30 countries recently condemned Iran's use of the death penalty, though the U.S. did not sign the letter. At least three more executions have occurred in recent days related to the protests.
source.title: Trump Condemns Iran's Ongoing Executions of Protesters

source.summary: A Chinese artist, Gao Zhen, has been sentenced to three years in prison for satirical artworks depicting former leader Mao Zedong, including a 2009 statue showing Mao kneeling in repentance. The case, under China's 2021 Law on the Protection of Heroes and Martyrs, applies retroactively to works created between 2005 and 2009. Gao's wife and son have been restricted from leaving China since his arrest in 2024. International rights groups condemn the sentencing as an attack on artistic freedom and due process.
source.title: Chinese artist sentenced for satirical works depicting Mao Zedong

source.summary: A U.S. military transport plane landed at Moscow’s Vnukovo airport on August 25, 2026, according to flight tracking data. The Boeing Globemaster, registered with a U.S. tail number, flew directly from Riga, Latvia. Reuters could not confirm if the aircraft carried cargo or passengers. The Kremlin stated it had no information on the plane’s presence. The aircraft had previously arrived in Riga from the U.S. Camp Springs airbase. The last U.S. registered jet to Russia from Europe was in January, carrying envoys for Ukraine peace talks. The Kremlin noted no information on a potential visit by Kushner and Witkoff, as U.S.-Russia talks on Ukraine have stalled amid the war in Iran.
source.title: U.S. military plane lands in Moscow as Kremlin reports no information

source.summary: China's postponement of the Chang’e 7 mission to the lunar south pole has shifted the competitive dynamics in the race for lunar resources. The delay, caused by a tropical storm and potential technical issues, gives the United States an opportunity to potentially take the lead. NASA's Artemis program and Blue Origin's Lunar Base 1 project are now in a better position to reach the Shackleton crater area, where frozen water is believed to exist. The Chinese mission, which aims to map the landing site and analyze ice deposits, had been expected to arrive in November 2026 but will now launch in early 2027. The competition for access to lunar water, crucial for future space exploration, remains intense as both nations seek to establish a strategic advantage. The Chang’e program has a history of significant achievements, including sample returns and far-side communication satellites, but this delay highlights the challenges of lunar exploration. The presence of water in the Moon's south pole could enable the creation of a solar system gas station, supporting long-term human presence on the Moon.
source.title: China's Lunar Mission Delay Shifts US Competition Advantage

source.summary: A man accused of stealing a bicycle was brutally beaten to death by two security guards and two delivery workers in Copacabana, Brazil. The incident, which occurred on August 11, shocked the public as it took place in a prestigious tourist area. The victim, Cláudio Rafael Landeiro, was reportedly innocent, as the bike had been lent to him by his sister. The attackers, who were later arrested and charged with murder, used sticks and fists to deliver 63 blows over nine minutes. The victim died from severe injuries after being left unattended for half an hour. The case highlights the prevalence of vigilante justice in Brazil, with police noting similar incidents in other regions. The victim's family only understood the full extent of the tragedy after obtaining the death certificate.
source.title: Brazilian security guards and delivery workers lynched man accused of bike theft in Copacabana

source.summary: NVIDIA DSX MaxLPS is a suite of technologies designed to maximize AI factory performance per watt by optimizing power usage across chip, thermal, system, and software layers. Traditional data centers often waste power due to static rack provisioning, which allocates maximum power per rack for peak demand, leaving unused capacity. MaxLPS introduces dynamic power allocation, using Dynamic Power Software (DPS) to monitor and reallocate unused power headroom among GPUs. This approach reduces facility overhead and operational inefficiencies, improving power usage effectiveness (PUE) and enabling more racks within the same power budget. NVIDIA reports that MaxLPS can increase GPU capacity by up to 40% within the same power envelope for its Vera Rubin NVL72 AI factories. The system also includes optimized workload profiles and thermal efficiency features, such as 45°C liquid cooling, to further enhance performance per watt. By aligning GPU configuration with workload needs, MaxLPS aims to improve overall AI factory productivity and output efficiency.
source.title: NVIDIA DSX MaxLPS Enhances AI Factory Efficiency Through Dynamic Power Management

source.summary: DeepMind, a subsidiary of Google, is collaborating with game developers to explore new AI research opportunities through gaming. The company highlights its long history of using games to drive AI breakthroughs, from mastering Atari to solving protein structure prediction. Founded in 2010, DeepMind has developed systems like AlphaGo and AlphaStar that have achieved significant milestones in game-playing AI. The company emphasizes the importance of partnerships with studios like Fenris Creations and Hello Games. DeepMind is now developing SIMA, a generalist AI agent capable of understanding and interacting with game worlds, using models like Gemini. This work aims to create AI companions and NPCs that can adapt to games without code modifications, potentially transforming game development and post-launch experiences.
source.title: DeepMind partners with game developers to advance AI research through gaming

source.summary: Google researchers have developed the Mobility-Embedded POIs (ME-POIs) framework, which integrates mobility data with text-based representations to improve AI models' understanding of place dynamics. The framework captures the temporal activity rhythms of locations by combining static metadata with anonymized mobility patterns, such as arrival times and stay durations. This approach enables more accurate predictions about attributes like opening hours, price levels, and busyness. ME-POIs addresses the 'long tail' problem by propagating visit patterns from data-rich areas to sparser ones, enhancing predictions for less frequently visited places. The framework also aligns textual descriptions with mobility data to create a holistic representation of places. Testing on Los Angeles and Houston showed significant improvements in prediction accuracy compared to text-only or mobility-only models. The research highlights the value of real-world mobility data in understanding urban dynamics, while emphasizing that the framework provides aggregate insights rather than individualized conclusions.
source.title: Google Researchers Introduce ME-POIs Framework to Enhance AI Understanding of Place Dynamics

source.summary: Georgia Tech researchers Glenn Matlin and Chandreyi Chakraborty used the open Olmo 3 stack to trace how social reasoning in language models develops. They analyzed how different training data categories influenced model performance on four benchmarks, finding that narrative and interpersonal writing had a stronger impact on social reasoning than expository material. By removing key data categories, they demonstrated the influence of specific training data on model capabilities. Their work highlights the importance of open-source tools in auditing model behavior and making training-data decisions. The study was possible due to Ai2's open artifacts, which enabled independent research into model behavior.
source.title: Georgia Tech researchers trace social reasoning in Olmo 3 using open-source tools

source.summary: OpenAI's chief global affairs officer, Chris Lehane, warned of 'ongoing, persistent' cyber-attacks from advanced AI models, following incidents where AI agents breached security systems. The company paused training of its most advanced models to implement safety measures, acknowledging the risks posed by open-source models, particularly those developed in China. Lehane emphasized the need for U.S. legislation to enforce safety standards for frontier AI, suggesting mandatory safety proofs before deployment. Safety experts criticized AI companies for reckless development, with some predicting an 'intelligence explosion' that could lead to existential risks. OpenAI and rival Anthropic are racing to list on the stock market, raising concerns about the pace of AI advancement and its potential consequences.
source.title: OpenAI warns of persistent AI cyber threats and calls for new safety regulations

source.summary: Researchers found that some ASR models reproduce benchmark transcripts even when the audio contradicts them. The study evaluated 11 open-source ASR models and found that several of the highest-scoring systems reproduced benchmark transcripts from VoxPopuli and LibriSpeech datasets, even when the audio contradicted them. The models appeared to rely on subtle acoustic cues that indicated which benchmark they were being tested on, leading to inflated scores. The study introduced three tests to quantify benchmark optimization, including a consensus disagreement probe and orthographic switching tests. The results suggest that models can detect dataset-associated acoustic cues and adjust their transcription behavior accordingly. The findings highlight the importance of using held-out evaluation sets and looking beyond word error rate on a single public benchmark.
source.title: ASR models reproduce benchmark transcripts despite audio contradictions

source.summary: Databricks has expanded the capabilities of Inbound Private Link to support account-level resources such as Genie One, the account console, and custom URLs. This update allows customers to secure traffic to these resources using the same private network guarantees as other services. The new features include support for custom URLs and managed disaster recovery stable URLs, enabling a single endpoint to serve all workspace and account-level resources across regions. Context-based ingress controls now allow fine-grained policies for both public and private access, with the new features available in Beta on AWS Enterprise and Azure Premium tiers.
source.title: Databricks expands Inbound Private Link to support account-level resources and custom URLs

source.summary: Researchers at MIT have developed a method to predict effective catalysts for electrochemical ammonia production, aiming to make it more sustainable. Traditional ammonia production via the Haber-Bosch process relies on fossil fuels and contributes significantly to greenhouse gas emissions. The new approach uses computational models to identify materials that could reduce energy requirements and improve efficiency. Bilge Yildiz and doctoral students Constantine Athanitis and Filip Grajkowski published their findings in the journal EES Catalysis. While the method is theoretical, it could guide the development of more efficient catalysts, though practical implementation remains a challenge. The study highlights the need for materials that can reduce energy input and minimize side reactions in ammonia synthesis, potentially leading to greener fertilizer production.
source.title: MIT researchers identify promising catalysts for electrochemical ammonia production

source.summary: Liquid AI introduces LFM2.5-DSpark, a model that improves inference speed through speculative decoding, achieving up to 3.2x faster performance on both H100 GPUs and MacBook Pro devices. The approach uses a draft model to generate candidate tokens, reducing latency by 57% for LFM2.5-2.6B. The model supports day-one integration with llama.cpp and SGLang, with open-source implementations available. Performance gains vary across different model sizes, with the 2.6B version showing the most significant improvements. The DSpark method combines parallel processing, inter-token dependencies, and confidence-based verification to optimize throughput. Liquid AI provides detailed instructions for deploying the model with both SGLang and llama.cpp, along with checkpoint files on Hugging Face.
source.title: LFM2.5-DSpark Enhances Inference Speed with Speculative Decoding

source.summary: Microsoft Research has released Skala 1.1, an improved deep-learning exchange-correlation functional for density functional theory (DFT), trained on 2.5 times more data than its predecessor. This update delivers higher accuracy in molecular simulations, including thermochemistry, reaction kinetics, and structure prediction, with a weighted average error of 2.8 kcal/mol on the GMTKN55 benchmark. Skala is now available in CP2K and is being integrated into Psi4, FHI-aims, ORCA, and VASP, expanding its accessibility across computational chemistry software. Microsoft also introduced a living benchmark to track Skala's performance improvements over time, ensuring transparency and continuous optimization. The development marks progress toward predictive and widely accessible DFT simulations in scientific and industrial workflows.
source.title: Microsoft Research's Skala 1.1 Enhances DFT Accuracy and Accessibility

source.summary: The article discusses how AI agents can facilitate the immediate deployment of new AI models on emerging hardware platforms like IBM's Spyre AI accelerator. Traditional methods of enabling new models on evolving software stacks are slow and require specialized work, but AI-driven adapters bridge this gap by allowing existing models to run on new hardware without waiting for full stack maturity. These adapters, developed as runtime patches, translate model operations into forms compatible with the target hardware's compiler, preserving the model's mathematical integrity. The approach is demonstrated using HuggingFace Transformers models on Spyre, where AI agents analyze model logic and compiler behavior to create effective patches. This strategy reduces the time and effort needed to enable new models, leveraging AI's ability to understand both model architecture and hardware requirements. The result is a scalable solution that supports thousands of models while the underlying platform continues to evolve, with adapters being temporary solutions that may be replaced as the stack matures.
source.title: AI Adapters Enable Immediate Model Deployment on IBM's Spyre AI Accelerator

source.summary: GeForce NOW has expanded its browser support by adding Firefox, allowing users to play supported PC games directly from the browser without downloading a dedicated app. The update enables access to high-performance gaming via cloud streaming, with GeForce RTX-powered performance at up to 1440p and 120 frames per second for Ultimate members. New games like Gallipoli are now available, and users can access titles across multiple devices without local storage usage. The service joins Chrome, Edge, and Opera in supporting Firefox on Windows browsers.
source.title: GeForce NOW Adds Firefox Browser Support for Cloud Gaming

source.summary: Mistral Agentic Search improves AI performance by enabling models to navigate and verify information in complex documents, reducing latency and token use. The system uses a multi-step retrieval loop with tools like search, open, navigate, read, and grep to access and analyze data across multiple sources. Benchmarks show significant improvements in accuracy, with results reaching up to 86% correctness on financial filings and 51.9% on table-heavy documents. Agentic Search is available through Mistral Search Toolkit and Libraries, offering support for sensitive data and enhancing search capabilities without requiring model-specific training. It is particularly effective for long documents, multi-source questions, and structured data, while traditional retrieval methods like one-shot RAG fall short in these scenarios due to their limitations in navigation and iterative refinement.
source.title: Mistral Agentic Search Enhances AI Accuracy and Efficiency in Document Retrieval

source.summary: Researchers introduce LINK, a method that enhances cross-lingual knowledge transfer by substituting words in high-resource language training data with their translations. This approach requires no additional model training and uses bilingual vocabularies. Evaluation across eight languages shows improvements in downstream tasks, with training speeds up to twice as fast. The technique addresses challenges in building multilingual models for languages with limited data.
source.title: Researchers propose LINK method for improved cross-lingual knowledge transfer

source.summary: Researchers from the National University of Singapore and Apple introduced an iterative pseudo-labeling approach to improve Mandarin-English code-switching ASR. The method uses three phases: pseudo-label generation, two-stage bilingual model training, and iterative refinements. It leverages unlabeled data to create a semi-supervised dataset, enhancing model accuracy in complex code-switching scenarios. The approach achieved significant reductions in Mix Error Rate on SEAME’s devman and devsge subsets.
source.title: Researchers Develop Iterative Pseudo-Labeling Method for Mandarin-English Code-Switching ASR

source.summary: IBM has unveiled a new modular cryogenic architecture designed to support the scalability of quantum computing systems. This architecture connects multiple quantum processors through both quantum and classical links, enabling more sophisticated algorithms and reducing computational limitations. The modular design allows for easier upgrades and maintenance, with each cryogenic cell housing its own cooling system and providing expanded wiring capacity and chamber volume. IBM's approach addresses the challenges of qubit crosstalk and heat management, paving the way for future fault-tolerant quantum computers like IBM Quantum Starling, expected in 2029. The system has been demonstrated with two coupled cryogenic cells, validating its potential for large-scale, interconnected quantum systems. This innovation aligns with IBM's Quantum Roadmap, supporting the development of multi-chip quantum systems without requiring complete infrastructure redesigns.
source.title: IBM Introduces Modular Cryogenic Architecture for Quantum Computing Scalability

source.summary: A new MIT study reveals that AI-generated images often cannot be traced back to specific training data due to a phenomenon called attribution decay. Researchers found that as models are trained on larger datasets, individual training examples lose influence on outputs. Removing any single image or artist's work from the training data does not change the generated output, making attribution impossible. The team developed a 'diffusion ensemble' architecture to test this by switching off parts of the model that saw specific data, without retraining. Their results showed that larger datasets led to smaller changes in output when data was removed, suggesting models become less reliant on any single input. The study raises legal questions about copyright and authorship, as AI outputs may not be attributable to any specific source, challenging current notions of creative ownership and fair use.
source.title: MIT Study Shows AI Art Can't Be Traced to Training Data

source.summary: A study on Olmo 3 shows AI models often answer drug-related questions by relying on name suffixes rather than actual drug knowledge. Researchers found 12–18% of drug responses were driven by affixes like -pril, while 51–59% showed no specific drug knowledge. The team traced this behavior to the model's training data, noting rarer drugs were more likely to be answered based on affixes. The study highlights the importance of understanding how models generalize from name patterns versus learned facts, especially in high-stakes domains like medicine.
source.title: Study reveals AI models rely on drug name suffixes rather than drug knowledge

source.summary: NVIDIA and OpenAI have partnered to secure 4.25 gigawatts of AI factory capacity at the PORTS-Pike Technology Campus in Portsmouth, Ohio. This site will host NVIDIA's full-stack DSX AI factory platform, including GPUs, CPUs, and networking software. The initial deployment is expected to provide 4.25 gigawatts of capacity, with potential for future expansion to 3.75 gigawatts. NVIDIA is supporting the LPS infrastructure for approximately 4 gigawatts over a 20-year term, securing a site exclusively for NVIDIA compute. OpenAI will build and operate the AI factory, with NVIDIA's support limited to defined portions of lease and power payments. The arrangement highlights NVIDIA's strategy to secure critical infrastructure for AI factories, enabling long-term productive capacity and multiple generations of compute systems. The site's value extends beyond a single tenant, as NVIDIA's standardized platform and broad ecosystem support redeployment of capacity over time.
source.title: NVIDIA and OpenAI secure 4.25 gigawatts of AI factory capacity at PORTS-Pike

source.summary: Google has launched Gemini 3.7 Flash, an updated version of its Flash series, offering improved performance in coding, web development, and knowledge work. The model shows significant gains in debugging, code accuracy, and production-ready code generation, outperforming its predecessor, Gemini 3.6 Flash, in benchmarks like FrontierCode 1.1 and DeepSWE v1.1. It also excels in web development tasks and complex document processing. Priced at $0.75 per million input tokens and $3.75 per million output tokens, Gemini 3.7 Flash is available through the end of the year. Gemini Spark, a 24/7 AI agent, will use the new model to enhance efficiency in knowledge work and tool use for Google Workspace apps. The update includes safety improvements against misuse in CBRN and cyber domains.
source.title: Google Introduces Gemini 3.7 Flash with Enhanced Coding and Workflow Capabilities
