source.summary: Selena Gomez is contesting allegations that she defrauded investors of nearly $1.2m by failing to support her mental health platform, Wondermind. Her lawyer argues the claims are threadbare and that Gomez never agreed to manage the company. While the dispute puts her mother in a difficult position, experts warn that family-run businesses often lack proper governance. Commentators suggest that celebrities should carefully consider how a business might impact their reputation before lending their name to it.
source.title: Selena Gomez denies fraud claims regarding Wondermind investment

source.summary: Haiti's national police faced intense scrutiny following a deadly gang attack in Kenscoff that killed 47 people and kidnapped over 50. Police spokesperson Garry Desrosiers stated at a news conference that authorities could not discuss specific plans to respond to the incident. The attack underscores the continued influence of armed groups, with one leader threatening to execute hostages if any gang members are killed. While violence in the area had previously dropped by 66 percent, the UN warns that gang-related violence is spreading geographically. Currently, an estimated 70 percent of Port-au-Prince remains under gang control, displacing more than 1.5 million people. A UN-backed Gang Suppression Force has arrived to help dismantle organized violence, though critics question the success of such international efforts. Police head Vladimir Paraison indicated an investigation is underway to probe potential complicity or negligence within the force.
source.title: Haiti police face scrutiny after deadly gang attack kills 47

source.summary: Andy Burnham announced new measures to protect consumers from aggressive bailiffs and unscrupulous builders. The government will require private bailiffs in England and Wales to be accredited by the Enforcement Conduct Board. A government-backed scheme will help people identify trusted builders starting next month. Additionally, a new app service will allow consumers to release payment to builders in stages linked to project milestones.
source.title: Andy Burnham announces crackdown on rogue bailiffs and cowboy builders

source.summary: Bloomberg News reports that the US Federal Trade Commission is preparing a potential lawsuit against YouTube regarding consumer protection violations. The investigation, led by the Bureau of Consumer Protection, examines whether users were misled by content policies before having accounts suspended. While the probe is in its final stages, it remains unclear which specific accounts were covered. Some career staff within the agency have privately expressed disagreement with filing the case. YouTube declined to comment on the matter.
source.title: US FTC investigates YouTube over consumer protection and account suspensions

source.summary: The Wall Street Journal reports that Nvidia has paused revenue-sharing deals with AI cloud companies. The chip giant stepped back from the program last week, though it could revamp the initiative later. An Nvidia spokesperson stated the business model remains in place and continues to evolve. The move comes amid investor scrutiny over Nvidia's role in circular deals that could inflate demand. Some employees expressed concerns about potential antitrust scrutiny regarding the initiative's control over customer business practices.
source.title: Nvidia pauses revenue-sharing deals with AI cloud companies

source.summary: Australian shares are expected to edge higher following gains in the US market, where Nvidia helped fuel a technology sector rally. The ASX 200 futures are currently trading up 0.1% to 9,000 points. Nvidia shares surged 8.7% after the company exceeded analyst expectations and provided strong revenue guidance for fiscal 2028. Meanwhile, three major Australian banks have revised their forecasts, predicting the Reserve Bank of Australia will lift interest rates at least once more in 2026. CBA economist Belinda Allen stated that broad-based economic strength keeps a rate hike firmly on the table despite signs of a potential slowdown. Morningstar reported that the August corporate reporting season has improved modestly, with analysts raising fair value estimates for roughly one-third of companies. Additionally, Wesfarmers CEO Rob Scott highlighted how the Anko brand's design capabilities are expanding beyond Kmart into other group businesses like Officeworks and K Homes.
source.title: ASX poised to rise after Nvidia drives Wall Street tech rally

source.summary: Nvidia is preparing to launch an employee-funded political action committee named NVPAC, according to a person familiar with the decision. The move follows similar initiatives by Meta and Google to direct donations toward candidates supporting business objectives. Nvidia executives previously contributed $443,000 to the Republican National Committee. CEO Jensen Huang has cultivated close ties with President Trump regarding AI regulation. Anthropic established a comparable group that raised over $350,000 from staff.
source.title: Nvidia launches employee-funded PAC to influence U.S. policy

source.summary: Police in Perth have charged a 38-year-old man with the murder of a 28-year-old woman found dead in St James. Authorities allege the victim suffered extensive injuries from an assault by the man in the days before her death. Homicide Squad detectives investigated the case and questioned the suspect in custody. The accused is scheduled to appear in Perth Magistrates Court today.
source.title: Man charged with alleged domestic violence murder of woman in Perth

source.summary: Three Stars and Stripes staff members filed a lawsuit against the Pentagon alleging First Amendment violations following their terminations. Publisher Max Lederer, editor-in-chief Erik Slavin, and reporter Lara Korte claim the Trump administration breached their rights to oppose state interference in reporting. The suit argues the dismissals were retaliation for publishing a report on conditions aboard the U.S.S. Abraham Lincoln and opposing potential censorship. Lederer stated the Pentagon installed a new deputy publisher without his knowledge, signaling a shift toward greater editorial control. The plaintiffs are represented by multiple legal groups, with Defense Secretary Pete Hegseth named as a defendant.
source.title: Stars and Stripes staff sue Pentagon over firings citing First Amendment

source.summary: One Nation has appointed investment banker Mike Newman as its New South Wales leader and first lower-house candidate for the March 2027 state election. Newman, who previously worked as a trade bureaucrat in Asia, will contest the seat of Cessnock. During an interview, he outlined policy proposals including halving payroll tax, freezing public servant numbers, and implementing performance metrics in the public service. He also addressed concerns about the party's stance on migrants and social cohesion. Current polling data from the Sydney Morning Herald Resolve poll in July shows One Nation at 25% in NSW, ahead of the Coalition at 23% and Labor at 29%. Meanwhile, the Greens criticized the government's refugee intake adjustment as a lack of principle, while the Coalition expressed support for the government's humanitarian response to the Nepal floods. Additionally, NSW has launched a bird flu vaccination program for vulnerable native species.
source.title: One Nation names Mike Newman as NSW leader ahead of 2027 election

source.summary: Three journalists sued the Department of Defense on Thursday, claiming their firings from Stars and Stripes violated their First Amendment rights. The complaint alleges the dismissals were retaliation for reporting on deteriorating conditions aboard the USS Abraham Lincoln and for public statements supporting press freedom. Former publisher Max Lederer refused to fire two colleagues, leading to his own dismissal and subsequent retirement. The lawsuit argues the Pentagon's actions undermined the news outlet's historical editorial independence.
source.title: Three journalists sue Pentagon over dismissals from Stars and Stripes

source.summary: The article states that TotalEnergies is reducing its reliance on Russian gas while maintaining partial exposure. The text notes the company has not fully withdrawn from Russian energy sources. No specific figures or dates are provided in the source.
source.title: TotalEnergies cuts Russian gas exposure but keeps some supply

source.summary: US President Donald Trump signed an executive order renaming Lake Ontario to Lake America, effective immediately. The move follows collapsed trade talks and new tariffs between the US and Canada. Trump stated the change reflects American greatness, while Interior Secretary Doug Burgum pledged to implement it. Canadian officials, including Prime Minister Mark Carney and Premier Doug Ford, dismissed the proposal, noting the lake's 400-year history and international status. US lawmakers also criticized the order, with some proposing bills to nullify it. The White House claims the US Department of the Interior has 30 days to update the name with the Geographic Names Information Service. Canada is not required to recognize the change, as no international body governs such names for shared waters.
source.title: Trump signs order to rename Lake Ontario to Lake America

source.summary: Hundreds gathered in Oslo to support King Harald V, who is in an extremely serious condition at Oslo University Hospital. Queen Sonja and Crown Prince Haakon cancelled engagements to visit the King. Prime Minister Jonas Gahr Støre and Parliament Speaker Masud Gharahkhani also returned to Norway from abroad. The King has ruled out abdication despite recent health issues.
source.title: Hundreds gather in Oslo to support Norway's King Harald V

source.summary: Hundreds gathered in Oslo to support King Harald V, who is in an extremely serious condition at Oslo University Hospital. Queen Sonja and Crown Prince Haakon cancelled engagements to visit the King. Prime Minister Jonas Gahr Støre and Parliament Speaker Masud Gharahkhani also altered their travel plans to express solidarity. The King has ruled out abdication despite recent health issues.
source.title: Hundreds gather in Oslo to support Norway's King Harald V

source.summary: Regional governor Oleksandr Prokudin urged Kherson residents to leave after Russian attacks damaged a district heating plant. Prokudin warned of prolonged power and heating outages due to the severe infrastructure damage. He stated there is currently no way to destroy the glide bombs used in the strikes. The city, which had about 280,000 inhabitants before the 2022 invasion, faces an extremely difficult security situation.
source.title: Kherson governor urges residents to flee as Russian strikes damage heating plant

source.summary: The provided text contains a headline stating Trump's claim but includes a technical error message preventing the article body from loading. Consequently, no further details or attribution are available to summarize.
source.title: Trump claims Putin will not attack NATO territory

source.summary: Catastrophic flash floods and landslides struck Nuwakot district in central Nepal on 26 August, following a glacial collapse near the Nepal-Tibet border. Communities along the Trishuli River basin suffered widespread destruction, with hundreds of residents, tourists, and security personnel still unaccounted for. The Nepal Army deployed MI-17 helicopters to evacuate injured survivors and support search-and-rescue teams. Authorities have placed communities along the Trishuli and Narayani rivers on high alert due to the risk of further flooding and landslides. Several bridges and key roads linking Nuwakot with neighbouring districts and Kathmandu have been swept away or severely damaged.
source.title: Nepal floods and landslides in Nuwakot leave hundreds missing

source.summary: Catastrophic flash floods and landslides struck Nuwakot district in central Nepal on 26 August, following a glacial collapse near the Nepal-Tibet border. Communities along the Trishuli River basin suffered severe damage to infrastructure and buildings. Hundreds of residents, tourists, and security personnel remain unaccounted for as rescue operations continue. The Nepal Army deployed MI-17 helicopters to evacuate injured survivors and support search teams. Authorities have placed communities on high alert due to the risk of further flooding and landslides.
source.title: Catastrophic floods and landslides in Nepal's Nuwakot leave hundreds missing

source.summary: Britain welcomed the dissolution of the Syrian Democratic Forces and their integration into state institutions. UK Deputy UN Representative Kate Foster stated that this move supports Syria's territorial integrity and sovereignty. The group's leader, Mazloum Abdi, announced the dissolution following a January agreement. Foster also praised recent Israel-Syria talks while warning against further strikes in Idlib.
source.title: UK welcomes dissolution of SDF terror group in Syria

source.summary: Tesla has begun delivering its Semi electric trucks to Europe, with Einride placing the largest order to date for 500 units. The order, for use in U.S. routes, marks the start of high-volume production at Gigafactory 1 in Nevada. Pricing details for the Semi were not disclosed but are set to be announced at the IAA Transportation conference. Einride CEO Roozbeh Charli highlighted the partnership's role in advancing sustainable freight, while Tesla's Dan Priestley emphasized the cost savings and operational efficiency of electric trucks. Other long-term partners like PepsiCo and DHL may follow with large orders.
source.title: Tesla Semi Begins European Deliveries with 500-Unit Order from Einride

source.summary: GeoPura demonstrated hydrogen-powered charging for an electric ship at Tilbury Port, using a 300 kW system with five Ballard fuel cells. The vessel, battery electric, was charged through hydrogen conversion to electricity. While hydrogen's role in the energy chain is questioned, the demonstration highlights port infrastructure challenges. Ports often face electrical limitations, making battery storage a more efficient solution for high-power charging. Hydrogen's efficiency penalty, at about 3.1 MWh to 1 MWh, makes it less suitable for routine port operations. The article emphasizes the importance of repeat deployment and commercial viability over demonstration success. True commercial significance will depend on metrics like vessel usage, energy supplied, and cost efficiency. The maritime transition is expected to focus on reliable operations rather than technological firsts.
source.title: GeoPura Demonstrates Hydrogen Charging for Electric Ship at Tilbury Port

source.summary: The Trump administration has redirected a $500 million Biden-era grant intended for decarbonizing steelmaking to upgrade a coal-fueled blast furnace at Cleveland-Cliffs' Middletown steel mill. The Department of Energy changed the scope of the funding, which was originally meant to replace the aging furnace with cleaner technology, to instead refurbish and optimize the coal-fired system. Cleveland-Cliffs CEO Lourenco Goncalves stated the decision aligns with the Trump administration's priorities, emphasizing the use of 'beautiful coal.' The move has drawn criticism from environmental advocates and residents, who argue it undermines efforts to reduce emissions. The grant, part of a $6.3 billion program under the Inflation Reduction Act, was initially meant to support net-zero emissions, but the revised plan shifts focus to improving efficiency of the existing coal furnace, with the company investing $500 million of its own funds.
source.title: Trump administration redirects $500M steel grant to coal furnace upgrades

source.summary: Hyundai has started taking pre-orders for its Ioniq V electric vehicle in China, with the base model priced at $17,700 (119,900 yuan). The car, unveiled at the Chengdu Auto Show, offers three trim levels with varying battery sizes and power outputs. It is built on Hyundai’s E-GMP platform with 800V charging, though specific charging speeds have not been announced. The vehicle features a 27-inch display, Chinese AI models, and a driver assistance system from Momenta. While pre-orders are open in China, the model is not available elsewhere yet. Hyundai plans to expand to markets like Australia but has not set a timeline for global availability. The article notes that China leads in EV adoption and that Hyundai’s entry may influence its global strategy.
source.title: Hyundai begins Ioniq V pre-orders in China with $17,700 base price

source.summary: Arevon Energy has completed its 300-MW Nighthawk Energy Storage Project in Poway, California, using lithium iron phosphate battery technology. The facility, which Arevon developed, built, and will operate, supports grid reliability and has a long-term agreement with PG&E. The project is expected to generate over $30 million in property tax revenue for local services. Arevon's CEO highlighted the importance of energy storage for meeting rising demand, while local officials praised the project's economic and infrastructural benefits. The company also partners with local organizations in Poway, supporting community programs and initiatives. Arevon operates over 6.3 GW of solar and storage projects across 18 states, with ongoing developments in California.
source.title: Arevon Energy Launches 300-MW Nighthawk Storage Project in California

source.summary: A new federal initiative to establish nuclear 'lifecycle' campuses has led to states competing for roles in managing used nuclear fuel, marking a shift from past political resistance. The initiative proposes integrating advanced reactors, fuel production, and recycling with responsible waste management. However, opposition in Idaho and Tennessee highlights concerns about the volume, duration, and safety of waste storage, as well as the risk of facilities becoming permanent federal waste sites. The article argues that states should be consenting partners with enforceable rights, defined benefits, and binding plans for waste disposal. It emphasizes the potential of recycling to recover valuable materials and reduce long-term disposal needs, while stressing the necessity of transparent partnerships and durable economic benefits for host communities. The piece calls for a national strategy that avoids past failures by ensuring accountability and public confidence in nuclear development efforts.
source.title: Federal Initiative Sparks State Competition for Nuclear Waste Management Roles

source.summary: The U.S. faces growing hydropower challenges due to worsening droughts, particularly in the West. Lake Mead and Lake Powell, two major reservoirs, have reached record-low levels, threatening power generation capacity. The Bureau of Reclamation warns there's a risk these reservoirs could fall below operational thresholds. While these dams provide only a small portion of the Southwest's electricity, drought conditions are impacting dozens of hydropower plants across North America. Canada, which relies heavily on hydropower, is also experiencing a prolonged drought, affecting its ability to supply clean energy to the U.S. through new transmission lines. Meanwhile, the Trump administration is supporting battery projects, with LG Energy Solution opening a facility in Michigan and Form Energy advancing grid-scale storage. In Pennsylvania, Governor Josh Shapiro is imposing new requirements on data centers to manage rising energy demand.
source.title: Hydropower shortages threaten U.S. and Canadian energy supply

source.summary: The TM EDISON consortium, comprising Jan De Nul and DEME, completed the installation of all 23 caissons for the 3.5 GW Princess Elisabeth Energy Island project, 45km off Belgium's coast. This marks the end of foundation works, enabling the project to move to the next phase. The artificial island, developed for Elia Transmission Belgium, will serve as a hub for transmitting offshore wind energy to Belgium's grid and connect to UK and Danish networks. Caissons, each weighing around 22,000t, were built in Vlissingen and transported to sea. The project, scheduled for completion in 2031, received a €99m EU subsidy for this phase.
source.title: TM EDISON consortium completes caisson installation for Princess Elisabeth Energy Island

source.summary: PowerChina Jiangxi Electric Power Construction has won a EUR 12 million contract to build a 30 MW solar power plant in North Macedonia, managed by state utility ESM. The project will use two sites: 10 MW at the Oslomej coal mine and 20 MW near the Bitola thermal power plant. EBRD financed the tender, which selected PowerChina for the public-private partnership. ESM previously built a 10 MW solar plant at Oslomej, highlighting the site's suitability for solar projects. PowerChina is active in Southeast Europe, with recent projects in Serbia.
source.title: PowerChina to build 30 MW solar plant in North Macedonia

source.summary: Croatia has adopted amendments to its electricity market law, streamlining procedures for renewable energy projects and enhancing consumer protections. The changes align with EU standards, ensuring energy independence and stability. Key provisions include extended energy approvals for investors, risk management systems for suppliers, and measures to support consumers facing high energy costs. The law also allows temporary power cuts for non-vulnerable users failing to pay grid fees, as stated by the Ministry of Economy.
source.title: Croatia updates rules for constructing new power plants

source.summary: The Austrian government plans to overhaul its solar subsidy framework, prioritizing energy storage over direct photovoltaic support. The Ministry of Economy and Energy announced a new strategy to accelerate battery storage permits and fund intelligent energy management systems. Under the proposed reforms, small solar systems will be phased out, while storage and EMS will receive financial support to increase self-consumption and reduce grid strain. The government aims to achieve 8 GW of storage capacity by 2030, which could lower wholesale power prices. Industry groups welcome the shift but urge concrete implementation, emphasizing the need for clear funding mechanisms and regulatory support. PV&B Austria's Vera Immitzer stressed that policy must translate into action, while local installer Hansesun criticized the plans as inadequate, calling for tax relief measures to ensure investment certainty.
source.title: Austria shifts solar subsidy focus to energy storage

source.summary: LONGi and JinkoSolar are advancing solar-storage solutions for commercial and industrial applications. LONGi deployed Hi-MO X10 modules in a 200 kWp rooftop project in Saudi Arabia, demonstrating high-efficiency PV for C&I facilities. The company also supplied Hi-MO 9 modules for a 71 MWp solar portfolio in Italy, highlighting next-gen module technology. JinkoSolar extended its Sunny 365 platform to retail and AI data centers, integrating Tiger Neo 3.0 modules with SunGiga G2 storage. The solutions aim to reduce energy costs, improve efficiency, and address grid constraints through advanced PV and storage technologies.
source.title: LONGi and JinkoSolar Expand Solar-Storage Solutions for Commercial and Industrial Use

source.summary: ESS Inc CEO Drew Buckley discusses the company's challenges with its iron flow battery technology, which failed to meet commercial expectations since its 2021 SPAC listing. The company's share price has plummeted, and it faces doubts about its ability to continue as a going concern. Buckley explains that the iron flow battery worked in the lab but struggled with commercial deployment, leading to a strategic shift toward sodium-ion battery technology. He highlights the need for a longer development timeline for iron flow and positions sodium-ion as a lower-risk, faster-to-market option. The Bridge sodium-ion BESS, developed with Alsym, is designed to be a turnkey solution for utility-scale applications, particularly in data centers and AI workloads. Buckley emphasizes leveraging ESS's existing engineering and software capabilities to accelerate the sodium-ion product's commercialization.
source.title: ESS Inc CEO outlines pivot to sodium-ion batteries after iron flow battery struggles

source.summary: The S&P 500's CAPE ratio has hit 42.2, its highest since the dot-com bubble in 1999, signaling extreme market valuation. The metric, which adjusts earnings for inflation and removes anomalies, suggests the current market is significantly overpriced compared to historical averages of around 27. While the dot-com era saw speculative investing in unprofitable tech firms, today's high valuations are driven by AI advancements and big tech growth. Analysts warn of potential market corrections, though current earnings fundamentals differ from the bubble period.
source.title: CAPE Ratio Reaches Dot-Com Bubble Levels as AI Drives Market Valuations

source.summary: Analysts at 24/7 Wall St. suggest Amazon (AMZN) is undervalued, with a $343.50 price target and 32.8% upside, citing AWS's 36.7% growth in Q2 FY2026 as its fastest in 18 quarters. The stock trades at a forward P/E of 17, lower than Alphabet and Microsoft. Bulls argue AWS's operating leverage and AI monetization could push shares to $393.98, while risks include high capital intensity and inflated net income due to Anthropic's $53.40 billion mark.
source.title: Analysts Highlight Amazon's Undervalued Position Amid AWS Growth

source.summary: Nancy Kassebaum Baker, a centrist Republican senator from Kansas who died at 94, called for Donald Trump's impeachment in 2021 following the Capitol attack. She was the first woman elected to the U.S. Senate without following a spouse, serving three terms from 1978 to 1997. Known for her moderate politics, she supported progressive measures like an assault weapons ban and worked across party lines. Despite her popularity in Kansas, she frustrated conservative activists. After leaving the Senate, she continued public service roles, including as a member of a bipartisan campaign finance commission. She married former Senator Howard Baker in 1996, and later became an ambassador to Japan with her husband. Her son reported her death from natural causes.
source.title: Nancy Kassebaum Baker, centrist Republican senator, calls for Trump's impeachment

source.summary: Iran-linked hackers are blamed for a cyber-attack that temporarily shut down a UK power plant, according to the government. The incident involved a small-scale energy generator, with no risk to the wider energy system. The UK government emphasized its resilient energy infrastructure and collaboration with the sector to ensure security. The National Cyber Security Centre reported no outages from major power stations. The attack follows warnings about increasing threats from hostile states like Iran, which has been accused of cyber-attacks on Turkey and Israel. The US has warned of ongoing threats from Iran-affiliated groups like CyberAv3ngers, which targeted critical infrastructure in 2023.
source.title: Iran-linked hackers caused UK power plant shutdown, government says

source.summary: A self-taught painter and remodeling contractor, Alan Mootnick, founded the Gibbon Conservation Center in California 50 years ago, transforming it into a globally recognized sanctuary for gibbons. The center now cares for 40 gibbons across five species, known for their distinctive vocalizations. Director Gabi Skollar, who joined Mootnick in 2005, continues his mission after his death in 2011, living on-site with caretakers and dedicating her life to the gibbons. The sanctuary contributes to gibbon research and conservation efforts, facing threats from habitat destruction and wildlife trade. Skollar aims to expand the facility and create an education center, honoring Mootnick's legacy through ongoing care and research.
source.title: Self-taught painter turned gibbon expert runs world-leading sanctuary

source.summary: A federal judge has ruled that Michael Jeffries, former CEO of Abercrombie & Fitch, is mentally competent to stand trial for sex-trafficking charges. Jeffries, 82, was hospitalized for months due to dementia and Alzheimer’s symptoms. Judge Nusrat Choudhury reviewed medical reports and phone calls to determine his competency. Jeffries and two co-defendants face charges related to luring men to sex parties through modeling job offers. The case follows previous sexual misconduct allegations.
source.title: Judge rules former Abercrombie CEO mentally fit for sex-trafficking trial

source.summary: Bangladesh's Prime Minister Tarique Rahman has postponed his first visit to India, straining bilateral relations. The delay follows a press conference by exiled Prime Minister Sheikh Hasina, which Dhaka criticized as interfering in its internal affairs. India had invited Rahman for a visit ahead of the BRICS summit, but tensions persist over Hasina's extradition request and her political speeches from India. Bangladesh's Foreign Ministry stated that a conducive environment is needed for the visit, while India's officials remain noncommittal. Analysts note that domestic politics in Bangladesh, particularly the July 2024 uprising, influence its foreign policy, shifting its focus from India to other nations. India's border fencing and deportation policies further strain ties, with Dhaka accusing New Delhi of extrajudicial actions. Experts suggest dialogue is essential to mend relations, as both nations face challenges in maintaining a productive partnership.
source.title: Bangladesh's PM delays India visit amid diplomatic tensions

source.summary: The government has exercised the full greenshoe option in the Hindustan Copper Offer for Sale (OFS), increasing the stake sale from 3% to 6%. This follows strong subscription of 3.41 times by non-retail investors on the first day of bidding. The OFS, open to retail investors on Wednesday, allows bids between 9:15 am and 3:30 pm on BSE and NSE. At least 10% of the OFS size is reserved for retail investors, with an additional 25,000 shares set aside for employees. The floor price of ₹514 per share, a discount to recent market prices, may not reflect the actual price retail investors face due to institutional demand. Analyst Vaqarjaved Khan notes the discount could disappear if institutional investors clear the OFS at higher prices. While the company's Q1 profit surged 163% year-on-year, improved margins are attributed to higher copper prices rather than operational improvements. Khan advises investors to consider the OFS for long-term copper exposure rather than short-term gains.
source.title: Government Exercises Greenshoe Option in Hindustan Copper OFS, Expanding Stake Sale to 6%

source.summary: The Foundation for India and Indian Diaspora Studies (FIIDS) warns that proposed $103,265 additional H1-B visa fees could make hiring economically impractical, potentially shifting high-value jobs overseas. Khanderao Kand, FIIDS' Chief of Policy and Strategy, said the fee could burden startups and companies with hundreds of millions in extra costs. Combined with a potential $100,000 OPT fee, the policy risks making the student-to-work pathway unaffordable. FIIDS also cited a 17 per cent drop in international student enrolment and projected losses of up to $3.4 billion due to reduced international student numbers.
source.title: FIIDS warns H1-B fee hike may push high-value jobs overseas

source.summary: Civil society organisations in Bengaluru, including Eddelu Karnataka and Muslim Muttahida Mahaz, plan a September 1 campaign to highlight alleged flaws in the SIR process. Actor Prakash Raj endorsed the 'Election Commission Chalo' initiative, which aims to flag issues with the electoral roll data. Activists argue that high numbers under the ADDSO category suggest improper conduct, with some genuine voters being incorrectly removed. Jagruta Karnataka called for more time to file objections, while BJP spokesperson S Prakash defended the process, citing voter non-compliance.
source.title: Civil society groups plan September 1 campaign to highlight SIR flaws

source.summary: Five family members were discovered dead in a lodge room in Srisailam, Andhra Pradesh, with police suspecting a suicide pact linked to financial struggles. The deceased included a 36-year-old man, his three sisters, and a 15-year-old nephew. Authorities noted the family had overstayed their rented room, which was not permitted, and had reportedly claimed to be unwell. The lodge staff noticed a foul smell before alerting police, who registered a case of suspicious death. Temple authorities criticized the lodge for violating accommodation rules, which limit stays to 48 hours for devotees.
source.title: 5 of family found dead in Srisailam; suicide suspected

source.summary: Indian equities are expected to open higher on Wednesday, with the GIFT Nifty indicating a gap-up after the benchmark indices closed strongly. Vaishali Parekh of Prabhudas Lilladher noted the index is trading over 200 points above Tuesday's Nifty 50 close of 24,334. She identified a bullish engulfing pattern on the daily chart, suggesting potential for further gains. The Nifty 50 faces a key resistance at 24,400 and support at 24,000, while the Bank Nifty remains near its 200-period MA at 57,450. Parekh recommended buying Astral, Sai Life Sciences, and ICICI Bank with specific price targets and stop-loss levels.
source.title: Indian equities poised for gap-up opening as GIFT Nifty signals higher start

source.summary: The United States has paused all visa applications and appointments worldwide as part of an immigration crackdown, according to the Financial Times. The move aims to limit access to those who may rely on state assistance, as stated by an official. The State Department announced a global training program for embassies, with visa appointments to be rescheduled. Applicants received emails informing them of cancellations and were promised new dates later.
source.title: US halts global visa appointments amid immigration crackdown

source.summary: Rajasthan Agriculture and Rural Development Minister Dr. Kirori Lal Meena was admitted to the ICU at Jaipur SMS Hospital after testing positive for swine flu. Meanwhile, protests erupted at IIT Delhi following the suicide of a physics student, with students demanding financial compensation, resignations, and an independent inquiry. The institute formed an external panel to investigate the incident. In another case, a family in Andhra Pradesh died by suicide after alleging harassment and forced conversion by a rifle shooting coach. Additionally, an Indian loitering munition accidentally struck a sensitive Pakistani nuclear site during Operation Sindoor, raising concerns about military infrastructure vulnerabilities.
source.title: Rajasthan Minister Admits to Swine Flu ICU, Campus Protests Over Student Suicide

source.summary: The Indian men's hockey team's underwhelming performance at the World Cup has raised concerns, with critics pointing to defensive lapses, poor decision-making, and an ineffective attack. Despite moments of promise, the team conceded 16 goals in five matches, scoring 14, including five field goals. Former player and coach Jagbir Singh criticized the team's lack of consistency and questioned the coaching staff's strategies, particularly the midfield's inability to adapt. With less than three weeks until the Asian Games, the team faces pressure to improve ahead of the LA Olympics.
source.title: India's hockey team struggles in World Cup, faces criticism for poor performance

source.summary: The US has paused visa appointments worldwide as the Trump administration initiates a global training program for consular officers. The State Department said the training will adjust visa schedules, though details remain unclear. The initiative aims to ensure thorough screening of applicants for potential reliance on public benefits. This follows broader immigration crackdowns, including visa and green-card revocations, and legal challenges to some policies. The administration also plans to increase H-1B visa fees and tighten screening for applicants, while considering revoking business and tourism visas for those seeking asylum.
source.title: US halts global visa appointments amid Trump administration training push

source.summary: Coimbatore's Onam sadya experiences showcase regional Kerala culinary traditions and local adaptations. Karthiyayini Kovai offers a 24-item takeaway sadya with Kerala-style dishes and North Kerala influences, priced at ₹799, available until August 27. Rasanai presents a 28-dish sadya with regional variations, including Thiruvananthapuram and Thrissur specialties, priced at ₹1205 for dine-in. Friends Catering, with a 30-year history, serves a 20-dish sadya featuring traditional dishes like kaalan and aviyal, with a focus on handmade desserts. All venues emphasize family traditions, with preparations starting days in advance and special arrangements for the final day of the festival.
source.title: Coimbatore Onam sadya offerings highlight regional diversity and festive traditions

source.summary: SpaceX, led by Elon Musk, announced plans to build a $100 billion spaceport in Louisiana, which will be its largest launch site. The project, named Starbase Louisiana, will feature over a dozen launch towers, enabling more than 30 Starship flights per day. The site, spanning 125,000 acres in Vermilion Parish, will include facilities for propellant production, power generation, and deep-water shipping. Construction is set to begin in 2027, with the first Starship launch expected in 2029. The project is expected to create over 3,000 jobs. Louisiana Governor Jeff Landry praised the investment, highlighting its potential for new jobs and economic growth. SpaceX aims to significantly increase rocket launches, including deploying space-based data centres by the end of next year.
source.title: SpaceX to develop $100 billion Louisiana spaceport with over a dozen launch towers

source.summary: An independent director, Anil Khandelwal, resigned from Rashi Peripherals Ltd, citing governance concerns related to the company's professional engagements with firms linked to two of its independent directors. Khandelwal alleged that director appointments and management compensation were handled by company management rather than the board's nomination committee, and that due diligence for an acquisition was conducted by firms associated with the directors. The company's chairperson, Krishna Kumar Choudary, denied any governance lapses, stating the engagements were at arm's length and within legal limits. Rashi Peripherals' stock fell 10% following the resignation, with the company's market cap at ₹5,200 crore. The resignation marks the second such instance this year, following a similar exit by Atanu Chakraborty from HDFC Bank.
source.title: Independent director resigns over governance concerns at Rashi Peripherals

source.summary: Sir Demis Hassabis, Chief Scientist of Alphabet and founder of DeepMind, emphasizes his scientific approach to AI, aiming to understand nature and the universe. His work at DeepMind focused on AI applications in medicine and agriculture rather than chasing user metrics. The book 'The Infinity Machine' explores his career, from his origins in North London to his role in developing breakthroughs like AlphaGo and AlphaFold. Hassabis's philosophy of deep reinforcement learning contrasts with early symbolic AI, allowing machines to learn through observation. The book also examines DeepMind's competitive landscape, including its response to OpenAI and the rise of Chinese AI labs like DeepSeek. It raises questions about the ethical implications of AI development and the challenges of managing its rapid growth.
source.title: Demis Hassabis's journey in AI and science

source.summary: NITI Aayog's report flags a structural imbalance in India's higher education system, where millions of students pursue generic degrees with weak job links. Only 8.25% of graduates are employed in roles aligned with their qualifications, and 13% of all graduates are unemployed. The report notes that 1.86 crore students apply for just 55,000 government jobs, highlighting the mismatch between education and employment. It calls for reimagining higher education through industry participation and Public-Private Partnership (PPP) models to align curricula with industry needs. The report suggests moving toward specialised, job-linked programmes and expanding work-integrated learning to improve employability.
source.title: NITI Aayog highlights job mismatch in India's higher education system

source.summary: Tamil Nadu Chief Minister C Joseph Vijay has scrapped the Parandur site for Chennai's second airport, sending the project back to the drawing board. The decision, which the DMK's MK Stalin called an 'irreversible setback,' was made after protests from local communities concerned about displacement and environmental impact. While the existing Chennai International Airport has not yet reached its capacity threshold, experts warn that the long lead time for developing a new airport could delay necessary infrastructure. The airport's current capacity is expected to rise to 55 million passengers by 2026 with planned expansions, but industry bodies stress the urgency of finding an alternative site to avoid losing investment and talent to other regional hubs. The Parandur project, which would have handled 100 million passengers annually, was seen as long-term infrastructure rather than an immediate solution to congestion.
source.title: Chennai's Second Airport Project Back to Site Selection After Parandur Scrapped

source.summary: Crude oil prices fell 6% over two days, with Brent crude at $86 and U.S. West Texas Intermediate at $80.42, reacting to developments around the Strait of Hormuz and Iran-Oman negotiations. JPMorgan estimates prolonged disruption could push Brent prices up by $7-$8 per barrel, while Goldman Sachs warns of potential $120 per barrel if disruptions continue. However, the bank forecasts Brent to average $80 in Q4 and $75 next year, with risks tilted to the upside due to ongoing tensions.
source.title: Oil prices drop 6% amid Strait of Hormuz tensions and Iran-Oman talks

source.summary: Banks in multiple Indian states and Union Territories will close on August 26 due to Eid-e-Milad-un-Nabi. The Reserve Bank of India lists this day as a holiday under the Negotiable Instruments Act. Branches in cities like Mumbai, Delhi, and Chennai will remain shut, while others in areas like Ahmedabad and Jaipur will operate normally. Online banking and UPI services will remain functional. The next major holidays are August 28 and August 30.
source.title: Banks in several states close on Eid-e-Milad, August 26

source.summary: Hindustan Copper has opened its offer for retail investors, with a 10% discount on the floor price of Rs 514. The government plans to sell a 3% equity stake as part of the base offer, with an additional 3% available as a green shoe option. The OFS, valued at nearly Rs 2,982 crore, received strong demand from non-retail investors, leading to the exercise of the greenshoe option. A minimum of 10% of the offer size is reserved for retail investors. Analysts note that the discount is already stale, and the stock has sharply crashed more than 7% on the opening day. The government's divestment efforts continue with this OFS, following recent stake sales in other PSUs.
source.title: Hindustan Copper OFS opens for retail investors with 10% discount

source.summary: सोशल मीडिया पर वायरल हो रहे बयान में रामदेव के कांग्रेस की आलोचना करने पर माफी मांगने का दावा नकली है। नवभारत टाइम्स और अन्य स्रोतों के अनुसार, रामदेव के कोई ऐसा सार्वजनिक बयान उपलब्ध नहीं है। उनके हालिया बयानों में कांग्रेस या विपक्ष की आलोचना ही है। एक इंटरव्यू में रामदेव ने 'मोहब्बत की दुकान' के नारे को समाज में घृणा के कारण नकार लिया। निष्कर्ष यह है कि वायरल बयान गलत है।
source.title: रामदेव के बयान के वायरल दावे नकली हैं, न्यूज चैनल ने खंडन किया

source.summary: NASSCOM responded to the U.S. Department of Homeland Security’s proposal to set the H-1B visa fee at $103,265, emphasizing the program’s role in addressing U.S. skill gaps. The agency argued that the fee increase should be viewed in light of the program’s original purpose and highlighted that Indian tech companies have reduced H-1B employee numbers while investing over $1.1 billion in U.S. STEM education. NASSCOM also noted a significant drop in H-1B employees from Indian firms over five years and pledged continued engagement with stakeholders on the issue.
source.title: NASSCOM urges context for H-1B fee hike amid industry investment

source.summary: The article discusses the challenges of implementing AI agents in production environments, identifying a 'prototyping tax' that slows down development. This tax arises from the inefficiencies in traditional R&D processes, which are not well-suited for AI agents. The key issue is the gap between conceptualizing an AI project and delivering a working prototype, leading to lost momentum and failed initiatives. The article highlights that the problem is not with the AI agents themselves but with the organizational setup. Teams that succeed are those that provide agents with a strong foundation in business semantics, enabling faster development cycles. By integrating governance and context into the development process, these teams reduce the time-to-prototype and increase the rate of production-ready solutions. The article also presents case studies showing how platforms like Databricks' Genie Code improve efficiency by understanding data schemas and governance models. The conclusion emphasizes that addressing the prototyping tax is essential for successful AI implementation, with measurable benefits in productivity and compliance.
source.title: AI Prototyping Tax Hinders Roadmaps, Solutions Found

source.summary: Databricks introduces AI Functions to integrate AI capabilities directly into data warehouses, enabling seamless processing of both structured and unstructured data. These functions allow analysts to perform tasks like sentiment analysis, classification, and translation within SQL queries, eliminating the need to move data to external AI environments. By embedding AI within the data warehouse, organizations can maintain governance and security while scaling AI workloads efficiently. Key functions include ai_parse_document for converting binary files to text, ai_extract for extracting specific data, ai_classify for categorizing text, and ai_query for general-purpose AI tasks. The integration streamlines workflows, reduces complexity, and enables real-time insights without disrupting existing data pipelines.
source.title: AI Functions Enhance Data Warehouse Integration for Structured and Unstructured Data

source.summary: Researchers challenge traditional unlearning methods by identifying data points with negligible impact on model outputs. They propose an efficient framework that reduces dataset size before unlearning, achieving up to 50% computational savings in real-world examples. The study compares influence functions across language and vision tasks to determine which data can be safely removed. This approach addresses growing data privacy concerns in machine learning.
source.title: Researchers Propose Efficient Unlearning Framework by Identifying Low Influence Data Points

source.summary: OlmoEarth Studio now allows users to generate and export custom embedding vectors from Earth observation data, supporting a range of downstream tasks. These embeddings, derived from open-source foundation models, are lightweight and shareable as Cloud-Optimized GeoTIFFs. Users can configure parameters like area of interest, time span, and encoder variant to tailor embeddings for specific applications. The embeddings capture surface characteristics, enabling similarity search, segmentation, and unsupervised exploration. A simple linear classifier trained on a few labeled pixels can produce detailed land-cover maps, demonstrating the embeddings' rich representation. The platform also supports supervised fine-tuning for higher performance. The embeddings are computed on demand, reflecting current conditions, and can be used for change detection across time periods. The article includes examples of using embeddings for land-cover classification and visualization through principal component analysis.
source.title: OlmoEarth Studio enables custom embedding exports for Earth observation analysis

source.summary: Two agentic memory systems, ACE and ALTK-Evolve, avoid compressing an agent's learned lessons into summaries. Both store lessons as individual guidelines, but differ in how they deliver them. ACE provides a comprehensive playbook on every step, while ALTK-Evolve delivers a curated subset based on the model's capacity. On the AppWorld benchmark, ALTK-Evolve achieves comparable or better accuracy at lower token costs, especially for weaker models. ACE excels on easier tasks with its full playbook, while ALTK-Evolve outperforms on harder tasks through selective retrieval. The difference lies in delivery calibration, with ALTK-Evolve optimizing for model efficiency. Both systems emphasize retaining detailed lessons rather than distilling them into generic rules.
source.title: ALTK-Evolve and ACE Compare Agentic Memory Approaches Without Compression

source.summary: NVIDIA and the open source community are driving progress in local AI by releasing new models and tools that enable developers to build and run advanced agents on personal and edge systems. The company highlights several recent developments, including the Qwen3.8-27B model optimized for NVIDIA RTX GPUs, which supports fast local inference for coding tasks. Other models like Cosmos 3 Edge, MiniMax-H3, and DeepSeek-V4-Flash are also being made available, with support for NVIDIA hardware. NVIDIA is also enhancing its DGX Spark systems with new features like the Sync Cluster Assistant, which allows developers to cluster multiple systems for running larger models. Additionally, the release of Muse Glimmer, a 30-billion-parameter model optimized for local agentic workflows, is enabling always-on AI assistants for coding and data processing. These advancements are part of NVIDIA's ongoing efforts to support the open source ecosystem and empower developers with high-performance, local AI solutions.
source.title: NVIDIA and Open Source Community Advance Local AI with New Models and Tools

source.summary: NVIDIA has introduced Nemotron 3.5 Lightning, a 30-billion-parameter mixture-of-experts model designed for high-volume, specialized tasks in agentic AI systems. The model offers up to 4x faster output speed and 30% faster task completion compared to similar models. It is open and customizable, allowing organizations to post-train it with their domain-specific data. Additionally, NVIDIA released NeMo Switchyard, an open-source library for intelligent model routing, enabling developers to direct requests to the most suitable model for each task. This reduces costs and improves efficiency across various industries. Partners like Boomi, Cadence, and LangChain have tested NeMo Switchyard, reporting significant cost reductions and performance improvements. Both tools are available on multiple platforms, enhancing deployment flexibility for enterprises.
source.title: NVIDIA Releases Nemotron 3.5 Lightning and NeMo Switchyard for Enhanced Agentic AI Systems

source.summary: Researchers trained a 1.7B-parameter flow model on 2.1T tokens and self-distilled it into a Categorical Flow Map (CFM) capable of generating high-quality text in just 4 inference steps. The model maintains near-data-level token entropy and achieves results comparable to discrete diffusion methods on standard language benchmarks. The study also introduces a likelihood bound for CFMs in the semi-discrete setting and identifies challenges in scaling these models, offering insights on loss weighting and time scheduling.
source.title: Researchers train 1.7B-parameter flow model for efficient text generation

source.summary: MIT students and postdocs participated in Congressional Visit Days, meeting with 62 congressional offices to advocate for sustained federal investment in scientific research. The event, organized by the MIT Science Policy Initiative, aimed to connect researchers with policymakers and demonstrate how scientists can engage in policy advocacy. Participants discussed both general science funding and specific policies related to their research areas, including AI, environmental science, and energy. The experience highlighted the importance of bipartisanship in supporting science and emphasized the need for researchers to engage with policymakers to shape future decisions.
source.title: MIT Researchers Advocate for Federal Science Funding During Congressional Visit

source.summary: In 1975, MIT researchers and Boston’s Beth Israel Hospital began creating a medical database to store and share electrocardiogram recordings, aiming to facilitate collaboration in arrhythmia research. The project, which took years to complete, eventually became the foundation for PhysioNet, a global platform for clinical data sharing. By 1999, PhysioNet had evolved into a comprehensive repository hosting hundreds of databases, with over 15,000 scientific publications citing it and users from 180 countries. The platform's open-access model and emphasis on data sharing have influenced the development of similar systems like MIMIC and Health Data Nexus. As artificial intelligence advances, PhysioNet has expanded to include electronic health records, imaging data, and AI models, becoming a cornerstone for health-care AI research. Researchers and platform stewards envision further growth, including new tools for user contributions and interdisciplinary collaboration.
source.title: MIT's PhysioNet database transformed from local research tool to global health data standard

source.summary: The PyTorch Foundation has announced a design contest for the 2026 PyTorch Conference North America flare pin. The winning design will be produced as a 1-inch die-cut soft enamel pin and the entrant will receive a complimentary conference ticket. Submissions must include the official PyTorch Foundation symbol, the year 2026, and be suitable for a professional event. Entries must be original, use official assets, and follow brand guidelines. The contest requires participants to submit designs via social media platforms with specific hashtags, and includes rules about AI use, copyright, and eligibility. The winning design will be selected by the PyTorch Foundation Marketing Committee based on originality, legibility, and brand compliance.
source.title: PyTorch Foundation Launches 2026 Flare Pin Design Contest

source.summary: Helion, a PyTorch DSL for ML kernels, now supports TPU v7 with a backend that compiles kernels to Pallas. The system autotunes pipelining strategies to optimize performance across different input shapes. On flash attention workloads, Helion achieves 838 TFLOPs, utilizing TPU's VMEM and compute units effectively. The approach allows non-experts to write kernels with PyTorch-style code, while maintaining performance comparable to Pallas. Helion's autotuner selects between pipelining and unrolling strategies based on input size, balancing VMEM usage and compute efficiency.
source.title: Helion enables efficient TPU kernel authoring with autotuned pipelining

source.summary: IBM has signed a definitive agreement to acquire HRL Laboratories, a research institution with a 80-year history of scientific innovation. The acquisition aims to accelerate IBM's quantum computing goals by leveraging HRL's expertise in silicon-spin qubit engineering. HRL is renowned for pioneering the laser, advancing semiconductor technology, and contributing to fields like ion propulsion and artificial intelligence. The lab has also developed key technologies such as memristors and quantum dot systems. Today, HRL continues research in quantum computing, materials science, and sensing technology, complementing IBM's own 80-year legacy in computing innovation.
source.title: IBM Acquires HRL Laboratories to Advance Quantum Computing

source.summary: Google has introduced three new Gemini models: 3.6 Flash, 3.5 Flash-Lite, and 3.5 Flash Cyber. The 3.6 Flash model offers 17% better token efficiency and improved performance in coding, knowledge work, and multimodal tasks, with a lower cost per token. 3.5 Flash-Lite is the fastest in the 3.5 series, delivering 350 output tokens per second and a strong price-to-performance ratio for high-throughput workflows. The 3.5 Flash Cyber model is designed for cybersecurity applications, combining a specialized model with CodeMender to detect and fix vulnerabilities efficiently. These models are available now through various platforms, with Gemini 3.5 Pro in testing and Gemini 4 in development.
source.title: Gemini 3.6 Flash and 3.5 Flash-Lite models introduced for improved efficiency and performance

source.summary: Google introduced Gemini 3.5 Flash Cyber, a lightweight cybersecurity model designed to detect and fix software vulnerabilities more efficiently than previous models. Built on 3.5 Flash, it is optimized for speed and affordability, making it suitable for large-scale code analysis. The model will be available through CodeMender to governments and trusted partners in a limited-access pilot program. Google claims it can handle complex codebases by analyzing multiple code paths, and benchmark tests show it performs competitively against larger models on the CyberGym benchmark.
source.title: Google Launches Gemini 3.5 Flash Cyber for Cybersecurity

source.summary: Researchers from Google Research explain that the creativity of diffusion models stems from the 'score smoothing' effect in neural networks, which allows them to interpolate between training data points rather than merely memorizing them. The study, presented at ICLR 2026, shows that diffusion models generate novel data by learning a smoothed version of the score function, which drives the denoising process to create new samples. This phenomenon occurs because neural networks, due to regularization effects like weight decay, naturally learn smoother approximations of the perfect score function. The research demonstrates that this score smoothing enables diffusion models to explore the data manifold, producing realistic yet novel outputs. The findings suggest that the 'creativity' of these models is a predictable mathematical outcome of their learning process, offering insights into how to design more effective generative models that balance quality and innovation.
source.title: Diffusion Models' Creativity Arises from Score Smoothing in Neural Networks

source.summary: Researchers introduce Turnstile, a proxy tool that records exact token-level histories during agent interactions to improve reinforcement learning. By capturing token IDs at the moment of generation, Turnstile ensures accurate training signals for models. The tool works with existing agent harnesses without requiring changes, providing a framework-neutral trajectory for RL training. It addresses issues like retokenization drift and context mismatches, enabling stable learning for both text-only and multimodal agents.
source.title: Turnstile captures token IDs for accurate reinforcement learning in agent interactions

source.summary: Google Research introduces SensorFM, a foundation model trained on over one trillion minutes of sensor data from five million people. The model learns a general-purpose representation of human physiology, enabling transfer to 35 health prediction tasks. SensorFM addresses challenges in wearable health data by using self-supervised learning to handle missing and fragmented data, improving performance on both classification and regression tasks. The model's ability to generalize across multiple health domains and support label-efficient adaptation is demonstrated through extensive experiments. Additionally, SensorFM is integrated into a Personal Health Agent, showing significant improvements in generating personalized health summaries compared to baseline methods.
source.title: SensorFM: Towards a general intelligence and interface for wearable health data

source.summary: Flint is a visualization language designed to let AI agents create expressive, visually polished charts from simple, human-editable specifications. It leverages semantic data types to guide design choices like scales, formatting, and color schemes, reducing the need for detailed, error-prone manual configurations. The system automatically adjusts layouts and adapts to data changes, ensuring readability without explicit user input. Flint specifications can compile to multiple backends, including Vega-Lite, Apache ECharts, and Chart.js, enabling flexibility across visualization tools. The project includes the flint-chart library and a flint-chart-mcp server, allowing agents to create, validate, and render charts in chat or coding environments. In testing, Flint outperformed direct Vega-Lite generation methods, achieving higher scores with various LLMs. It is now used in Microsoft Research's Data Formulator project for AI-assisted data analysis.
source.title: Flint enables AI agents to generate polished charts from simple specifications

source.summary: Binh Pham, a robotics software engineer, demonstrated MolmoAct 2's capabilities at a hackathon, showcasing its ability to perform tasks without specific training. The model, available open-source, allows users to inspect, adapt, and customize it with provided artifacts. Pham noted its strong spatial awareness and generalization, comparing it to the GPT-2 moment for robotics. The release includes model weights, data, training code, and fine-tuning scripts, enhancing reproducibility and development in the field.
source.title: MolmoAct 2 enables general-purpose robotic tasks through open-source model

source.summary: Prime Minister Andy Burnham made his first appearance in the House of Commons on Tuesday. He outlined plans to restart the economy and redistribute power from London to regions. Wars in Europe and the Middle East currently weigh on his economic promises. FRANCE 24's Mark Owen spoke with Dr Martin Farr about the situation.
source.title: Andy Burnham addresses House of Commons on economy and regional power

source.summary: Two new studies reveal that federal judges are installing panic buttons and hiring private security due to a surge in threats. Researchers from NYU, UC Berkeley, and the Brennan Center interviewed dozens of judges who reported feeling overwhelmed by harassment. One judge considered altering a ruling to protect their family from vitriol. Judge Esther Salas stated that recent attacks have made her more worried than after her son's death in 2020. The reports recommend increased funding for judicial security and more prosecutions of those making threats.
source.title: Federal judges install panic buttons and hire security amid rising threats

source.summary: Monterey County police are searching for a 14-year-old girl and her father after a newborn was found dead on a roadside. The sheriff's office stated the infant had signs of traumatic injury and the girl is charged with murder. Authorities believe the father is hiding the teen. Sheriff Tina Nieto called for the father to turn himself in, noting he faces multiple sex crime charges. The investigation utilized automated license plate readers to identify suspects within 53 hours.
source.title: Police seek 14-year-old girl and father after newborn found dead

source.summary: Treasury Secretary Scott Bessent announced US support for the Financial Literacy Solutions Sprint at a G20 ministers meeting. The contest will select winners from innovative technology solutions developed within G20 member states to improve financial understanding. Bessent also highlighted the Trump Accounts initiative, which deposits $1,000 into investment accounts for infants born during Trump's second term. Critics argue that financial struggles stem from a lack of disposable income rather than ignorance, citing recent survey data showing widespread dissatisfaction with economic conditions.
source.title: Scott Bessent promotes financial literacy contest and Trump-era investment plan at G20

source.summary: Milo Yiannopoulos appeared on Piers Morgan Uncensored to discuss his recent deportation by ICE. He described the experience as terrifying and expressed shame regarding his previous support for Donald Trump. The Department of Homeland Security stated Yiannopoulos overstayed his visa, though he disputed this claim during the interview. Yiannopoulos also criticized the brutality of US immigration enforcement.
source.title: Deported Milo Yiannopoulos expresses shame over past support for Trump

source.summary: The authors of a new op-ed argue that integrating Indigenous and local community knowledge into seed propagation strengthens forest restoration outcomes. They state that these communities are indispensable partners due to their familiarity with local species and ecological rhythms. The commentary highlights that focusing on seed quality rather than planting numbers is essential for long-term resilience. Evidence from Indonesia shows local communities developed four propagation techniques to produce tens of thousands of seedlings. The authors suggest that engaging these groups fosters ownership and empowers communities. They recommend incorporating traditional ecological knowledge into technical designs and providing sustainable finance models. The text notes that current efforts remain fragmented in Southeast Asia despite global restoration initiatives.
source.title: Indigenous knowledge improves forest restoration seed production in Southeast Asia

source.summary: Democratic Senate candidate Abdul El-Sayed responded to Vice President JD Vance's attacks by defining evil as policies that harm working people. Vance described El-Sayed as representative of terrible evil during a speech in Michigan. El-Sayed accused the vice president of using dog whistles regarding Islamophobia and ethnic division. The exchange also involved comments about Vance's family and El-Sayed's previous remarks on a synagogue attack. Vance urged voters to reject El-Sayed, while El-Sayed called his opponents sock puppets. Both candidates are campaigning for the November election in Michigan.
source.title: Abdul El-Sayed accuses JD Vance of evil rhetoric and dog whistles

source.summary: The Starmus Festival board created the Jane Goodall Earth Medal to honor the late conservationist, with former UN climate chief Christiana Figueres selected as the inaugural recipient. Festival co-founder Garik Israelian explained that advisory members Brian May and Peter Gabriel inspired the award, which aims to celebrate Goodall's legacy of uncompromising advocacy. Figueres expressed deep gratitude, describing Goodall as an absolute giant whose leadership continued until her final day. The festival's eighth edition, titled 'The Search for Truth,' features discussions on combating disinformation in the age of social media. Both guests argue that algorithms prioritizing engagement over facts create a post-truth environment where negative emotions dominate public discourse. They suggest that regulating tech companies and improving education are necessary steps to counteract the spread of misinformation. Figueres noted that humans are evolutionarily drawn to bad news, but society must consciously choose to surround itself with accurate information rather than fear-based content.
source.title: Christiana Figueres receives inaugural Jane Goodall Earth Medal at Starmus Festival

source.summary: Ukrainian President Volodymyr Zelenskyy warned airlines and insurers that Russian airspace is becoming unsafe due to escalating drone operations. He stated that the war started by Russia is effectively closing its own skies. Zelenskyy emphasized that Ukraine does not threaten civilian aircraft but noted the sheer scale of drones in Russian airspace. This warning follows a week of sustained Russian attacks on Kyiv using jet-powered drones and missiles.
source.title: Zelenskyy warns Russian airspace will effectively close due to drone operations

source.summary: Jurors in the Lindsay Clancy trial reached a deadlock after four days of deliberations, prompting Judge William Sullivan to ask them to keep trying. Clancy faces three counts of first-degree murder for killing her three children in Massachusetts in 2023. Her lawyer argues she suffered from postpartum psychosis and could not distinguish right from wrong. The jury, consisting of nine women and three men, has heard weeks of testimony. If found guilty, Clancy could face a mandatory life sentence without parole. Alternatively, she could be found not guilty by reason of insanity and sent to a psychiatric hospital.
source.title: Jurors deadlocked in Lindsay Clancy murder trial but judge urges continued deliberation

source.summary: Israeli Prime Minister Benjamin Netanyahu stated that forces captured Hamas internal security chief Muein al-Arabid during a Tuesday operation. Hamas officials claimed the officer was wounded and his wife killed during the raid. The operation involved an Israeli-allied militia and resulted in multiple civilian deaths. Palestinian health officials reported four people killed in the initial assault, while separate strikes later killed at least six more individuals. Israeli forces transferred the captured target to Israel for questioning.
source.title: Netanyahu says Israel captured Hamas security chief in Gaza

source.summary: Spain's Council of Ministers approved a 309 million euro extraordinary funding package for Ceuta to address the ongoing migrant crisis. Economy Minister Carlos Cuerpo described the measures as a shock response intended to safeguard jobs and support businesses. The funds are divided into healthcare, security, humanitarian care for minors, and direct business support. President Juan Jesús Vivas called for national unity, stating the city would never be abandoned despite the challenges. The announcement coincided with political demonstrations in the city highlighting internal divisions.
source.title: Spain approves 309 million euro aid package for Ceuta amid migrant crisis

source.summary: Bank of America confirmed that vice president Erin Piacenti was fatally stabbed in Times Square. New York Mayor Zohran Mamdani stated a woman stabbed two people before police shot her. NYPD identified the attacker as Pamela Cisneros, noting she had a history of mental health problems. Piacenti died from abdominal wounds while the second victim remains in stable condition.
source.title: Bank of America VP killed in Times Square stabbing by woman with knives

source.summary: The International Monetary Fund and Senegal agreed to a new $2.2 billion loan programme. The 36-month arrangement supports reforms for 2026–2029 and requires corrective measures for past data misreporting. The deal needs executive board approval. Senegal's fiscal deficit narrowed to 6.4 percent of GDP in 2025. Political tensions remain between President Faye and Speaker Sonko regarding debt restructuring.
source.title: Senegal and IMF agree new $2.2 billion loan programme

source.summary: Several victims' associations filed a complaint with UEFA against FC Borac Banja Luka regarding the glorification of Ratko Mladic during matches. The groups stated supporters displayed symbols and banners honoring Mladic, a convicted war criminal sentenced to life imprisonment. They called for disciplinary measures if UEFA finds violations of its regulations. FENA news agency reported the complaint was filed Tuesday in Brussels.
source.title: Bosnian associations urge UEFA to sanction FC Borac over war criminal glorification

source.summary: A Kremlin aide reported that Russian President Vladimir Putin and Chinese President Xi Jinping discussed a potential trilateral meeting with US President Donald Trump. Yuri Ushakov stated the leaders spoke about this possibility during talks in Bishkek. The Asia-Pacific Economic Cooperation summit is scheduled for November in Shenzhen. Ushakov also mentioned separate discussions regarding humanitarian issues in the Ukraine war.
source.title: Kremlin aide says Putin, Trump, Xi may meet at APEC

source.summary: The Democratic Republic of Congo government reports that confirmed Ebola infections have surpassed 6,000, with 2,911 deaths recorded so far. UN Secretary-General Antonio Guterres stated the epidemic is the fastest-growing on record and warned that international resources are lagging behind the reality on the ground. Health Minister Samuel Roger Kamba announced a vaccination campaign for over 50,000 front-line workers using doses originally developed for a different variant. Conflict and insecurity in eastern provinces continue to obstruct response teams, who reported attacks while handling Ebola-related deaths. Education Minister Raissa Malu proposed radio-based learning to maintain schooling, though teachers note a lack of necessary infrastructure. Despite these challenges, authorities highlight that more than 1,360 people have recovered from the virus.
source.title: Congo Ebola cases exceed 6,000 as violence hampers response

source.summary: Cuban theater group El Ciervo Encantado announced it will no longer operate under state supervision after more than a decade of conflicts with the Ministry of Culture. The group stated on social media that it would cease using its Vedado headquarters while continuing to create art in alternative spaces. Founded by Nelda Castillo thirty years ago, the ensemble has long challenged institutional control over Cuban performance art. Their recent decision marks a significant political gesture against censorship and bureaucratic oversight in the country. The group plans to present works in private homes and other venues to maintain their critical voice. This move highlights ongoing tensions between independent artists and state regulators in Cuba's cultural sector.
source.title: Cuban theater group El Ciervo Encantado defies censorship by leaving state headquarters

source.summary: The article reports that accelerated melting of Arctic ice has opened a new commercial shipping route. It notes that this development is due to changing climate conditions in the region. The text mentions potential impacts on global trade and navigation.
source.title: Accelerated Arctic ice melting opens new commercial shipping route

source.summary: Germany blames Russia for a drone incident at an airport and has announced new sanctions against the country. The German government stated that the attack was a deliberate act by Russian forces. Officials said the measures target individuals and entities linked to the aggression.
source.title: Germany blames Russia for drone incident and imposes sanctions
