source.summary: Tesla CEO Elon Musk stated on Sunday that the Full Self-Driving system will soon be able to avoid potholes. This announcement follows a similar claim Musk made in 2019, which has not yet been realized. While Tesla's software has improved significantly since 2013, the company still struggles to detect and navigate around road hazards. Musk's response to a user query generated excitement and reportedly boosted Tesla stock by approximately 5%. However, critics note that despite billions of miles of training data, the system remains unable to handle this specific physical challenge. With the upcoming launch of the driverless Cybercab, the inability to avoid common road damage poses potential risks for fully autonomous operations.
source.title: Elon Musk says Tesla FSD will soon avoid potholes, repeating a 2019 promise

source.summary: SLB announced a $3.4 billion cash acquisition of German cooling maker Kelvion to expand its data center infrastructure. The deal, expected to close in the first half of 2027, assumes $700 million in debt and targets $120 million in annual EBITDA synergies within three years. SLB stated the purchase more than doubles revenue opportunity per gigawatt of capacity. Kelvion reported $2.3 billion to $2.4 billion in revenue this year, with data centers representing its largest market. The combined business aims to reach $4.5 billion to $5 billion in revenue by 2028.
source.title: SLB Acquires Kelvion for $3.4 Billion to Expand AI Data Center Cooling

source.summary: BYD confirmed the new Denza N8 features a pure electric range of 1,003 km. The vehicle utilizes Blade Batteries 2.0 and Flash Charging technology for rapid recharging. Interior highlights include a 30-inch dashboard display and a 43-inch panoramic head-up display. The SUV will launch in China next month with RWD or tri-motor AWD options.
source.title: BYD unveils Denza N8 electric SUV with 1,003 km range and massive screens

source.summary: Kurt Cobb reports that conflict and climate change are combining to push global food prices up and supplies down. The article explains that farmers in Britain may lack cash to plant crops due to poor harvests and livestock deaths. Climate change is linked to late rains, droughts, floods, and increased animal diseases like bluetongue in Europe. War in the Persian Gulf and Ukraine has curtailed fertilizer and diesel supplies, raising costs for mechanized farming. Droughts in the U.S. and Europe are reducing yields of key crops like wheat, corn, and vegetables. In Brazil, rising oil prices have shifted production from sugar to ethanol. Conflicts in Sudan and attacks on grain terminals in Ukraine further threaten global food security. The author concludes that climate change will increasingly affect agriculture worldwide regardless of local conflicts.
source.title: Conflict and Climate Change Drive Global Food Prices Higher

source.summary: Organization for Political Ecology Polekol filed criminal complaints against Zlatna Reka Resources and an unidentified executive regarding suspected environmental harm in southwestern Serbia. The group alleges the mining subsidiary failed to implement required environmental protection measures during gold exploration. Polekol requests authorities test water and soil samples for contamination and stop the company's exploration permit. The organization cites unresolved irregularities identified by geological inspections and compares the situation to illegal deforestation by Zijin Mining in eastern Serbia.
source.title: Serbia environmental group files criminal complaint over mining exploration

source.summary: Iceland rejected a proposal to resume European Union accession talks, with voters prioritizing control over their fishing waters. Euroskeptics secured 52.8 percent of the vote, separating the outcome by just over 12,700 ballots. The referendum shifted from Arctic security concerns to a decisive debate on fish stocks, which account for nearly 40 percent of Iceland's exports. A trawler captain expressed fear that EU membership would force Iceland to surrender rights hard-won during the Cod Wars. While Icelandic fish stocks remain healthy, the European Union faces criticism for setting quotas above scientific advice. Jonny Hughes of the Blue Marine Foundation described EU fishing behavior as abysmal, noting a failure to incorporate climate change into policy. Experts argue that current management approaches ignore ecosystem dynamics and climate-driven shifts in marine life. Despite the vote locking in exclusive authority, legal gaps remain as fish migrate due to warming waters.
source.title: Iceland Votes Against EU Access to Protect Fishing Rights

source.summary: Slovenia's GEN Group posted a net profit of EUR 159.7 million in 2025, down from EUR 185.8 million the prior year. The company attributed this performance to effective cost control and successful portfolio management. Investments doubled to EUR 107.5 million, funding nuclear plant documentation and acquisitions. Management noted that generation capacity buffered against market price spikes despite regulatory impacts on household revenue.
source.title: GEN Group reports EUR 160 million profit for 2025

source.summary: PCG Power completed the first expansion of a clean REIT in China, growing its portfolio to approximately 400 MW of distributed solar assets. The company reported that cumulative fundraising exceeded CNY 800 million, representing roughly CNY 1.5 billion in total investment. Samuel Yan, PCG Power's CFO, explained that standardizing dozens of small projects is essential for creating an investable product for long-term capital. The expansion aims to establish a capital-recycling loop where securitization allows developers to reinvest funds rather than retaining assets on their balance sheets. While China's distributed PV capacity reached 576 GW by June 2026, the article notes that REITs remain unlikely to be a universal financing solution due to high management costs and varying tax rules. The authors suggest the real test is whether these platforms can repeatedly absorb new assets and attract sustained institutional investment.
source.title: PCG Power expands China's first clean REIT for institutional investors

source.summary: LG Energy Solution announced a multi-year agreement with Smackover Lithium to secure American lithium carbonate. The partnership will supply 8,000 metric tonnes annually over a decade from a project in Arkansas. Construction is expected to begin in 2026 with production starting in 2029. LG Energy Solution stated this move establishes a resilient local supply chain. The lithium will be produced using a direct extraction process.
source.title: LG Energy Solution signs lithium supply deal with Smackover Lithium

source.summary: NeoVolta Power and SK On announced a five-year collaboration for US-made energy storage. SK On will supply 9 GWh of LFP cells from 2027 to 2031, while NeoVolta will manufacture packs for SK On. The partnership supports up to 18 GWh of combined activity. NeoVolta plans to expand its Georgia facility to 8 GWh annual capacity by 2028.
source.title: NeoVolta partners with SK On for US battery supply

source.summary: Austrian startup Novventos Clean Energy has developed a container-based hybrid power system combining photovoltaics with small vertical-axis wind turbines. The company states the modular system assembles quickly and uses a shared management platform to control both technologies. While the firm reports specific generation figures, it has not provided detailed technical specifications or confirmed battery storage inclusion.
source.title: Novventos Clean Energy launches hybrid PV-wind container system

source.summary: Six Indian state electricity regulatory commissions announced new decisions regarding tariffs, disputes, and renewable energy. MPERC drafted rules for the 2027–32 control period, while APSERC admitted a petition for 2.75 MW of solar projects. HERC cleared green energy banking in Haryana, and TGERC closed a Telangana–Andhra Pradesh power dues case. UPERC completed a ₹32.74 crore refund and approved a 300 MW solar PPA at ₹2.57/kWh.
source.title: Six Indian State Commissions Update Electricity Tariffs and Regulations

source.summary: Iraq's Ministry of Electricity announced plans to develop up to 10 GW of solar capacity to address chronic power shortages. The strategy includes a 1,000 MW plant by TotalEnergies and agreements with Masdar for utility-scale facilities. Smaller residential and business systems will receive subsidized financing from the Central Bank of Iraq. Despite remaining regulatory challenges, the government aims to strengthen energy security and reduce dependence on diesel generators.
source.title: Iraq Plans 10 GW Solar Expansion To Tackle Power Shortages

source.summary: ePointZero announced plans to acquire a 90% stake in Azura Power, pending regulatory approvals. The deal involves ownership interests currently held by Actis and Africa50. Azura Power operates assets in Nigeria, Senegal, and Mozambique with a growth pipeline exceeding 1.5GW. CEO Dave Peacock described the transaction as a significant milestone for the company.
source.title: ePointZero plans to acquire 90% stake in Azura Power

source.summary: CATL has formed a partnership with local manufacturer Moura to supply projects winning contracts in Brazil's Capacity Reserve Auction for Energy Storage. The auction received 6,091 bids representing 296,908MW of power capacity, a record for participation in Brazilian energy auctions. CATL stated the partnership will help meet local content requirements while leveraging Moura's established position in the Brazilian market. The collaboration was announced alongside CATL's showcase of large-scale battery energy storage system solutions at Intersolar South America in São Paulo. Other Chinese players like Cornex and Sungrow also highlighted growing opportunities in Latin America's renewable energy and storage sectors.
source.title: CATL partners with Moura to supply Brazil's energy storage auction winners

source.summary: The article reports that half of the turbines at Nordseecluster A are currently up and running. No specific company or official source is named in the provided text to attribute this operational status.
source.title: Half of turbines are now operational at Nordseecluster A

source.summary: Acta Marine has commenced chartering its new CSOV at the Sofia Offshore Wind Farm. The vessel supports offshore wind operations in the region. Specific details regarding the charter terms were not provided in the source text.
source.title: Acta Marine begins chartering new CSOV at Sofia Offshore Wind Farm

source.summary: Kashish Shah, senior strategy lead at Wärtsilä, states that Australia's battery storage market has shifted from Frequency Control Ancillary Services to energy arbitrage as the primary revenue driver. Shah explains that coupling architecture decisions now depend on developer flexibility rather than supplier preference, though Wärtsilä offers controllers compatible with both AC and DC systems. The company highlights its Pulse analytics platform to optimize cycling behavior and Bitcast for auto-bidding in volatile conditions. Shah describes Australia as a market made for batteries due to its energy-only structure and grid physicality, contrasting it with regulated Asian markets. However, he identifies lengthy Generator Performance Standards processes as a significant connection challenge. Meanwhile, Wärtsilä announced a joint venture with RCT Solutions for its energy storage business.
source.title: Wärtsilä strategy lead discusses Australia's battery market volatility and storage design

source.summary: ChatGPT analyzed financial patterns across America to identify five states where newcomers face significant hidden expenses. The analysis highlights California, Hawaii, Florida, and New York as locations with surprising financial challenges.
source.title: ChatGPT identifies five US states with hidden financial costs for newcomers

source.summary: The article suggests that TaskRabbit earnings depend heavily on text-based profile optimization and client communication. The author consulted ChatGPT for strategies to improve search visibility and response speed. Key points include creating keyword-rich profiles to beat generic competitors and using AI-generated templates for faster client interactions. These methods aim to help Taskers secure more jobs and higher weekly pay.
source.title: ChatGPT Helps TaskRabbit Users Optimize Profiles and Communication

source.summary: U.S. President Trump has submitted a classified civil nuclear agreement with Saudi Arabia to Congress for review, as required by the Atomic Energy Act. The pact, signed by U.S. Energy Secretary Chris Wright and his Saudi counterpart, includes a condition that Saudi Arabia normalize relations with Israel through the Abraham Accords. The agreement's implementation hinges on this condition, raising concerns about its viability. Congress has 90 days to review the deal, which could take effect without approval. The deal, expected to last 30 years, involves U.S. firms in developing Saudi's civilian nuclear program. Critics warn it could enable Saudi uranium enrichment and nuclear proliferation. The Saudi Embassy did not comment, while Israeli Prime Minister Benjamin Netanyahu opposes Palestinian statehood, a prerequisite for Saudi normalization with Israel.
source.title: Trump's Saudi nuclear deal faces congressional review amid Israel ties condition

source.summary: Golf Channel postponed the premiere of 'Big Break x Good Good' by a week due to a sponsor's request to remove branding, following backlash against a video showing a man shoving a woman. The video, an ad for Callaway, was deleted after drawing criticism for depicting violence against women. Good Good apologized, and Callaway expressed disappointment, with its CEO acknowledging approval of the video. The PGA Tour also voiced concerns, while the sponsor's identity was reported as Golf Galaxy.
source.title: Golf Channel postpones ‘Big Break’ premiere after sponsor pulls out over Good Good Golf video

source.summary: Minnesota Vikings wide receiver Jeshaun Jones received a three-game suspension from the NFL for violating the league's substance abuse policy. The NFL did not specify the nature of the violation. Jones, who spent the past two years on the practice squad, was promoted to the active roster and played in the 2025 season's final game. He remains eligible for the remaining preseason games but will miss the first three regular-season games. His suspension begins on Sunday, with reinstatement possible on Sept. 28. Jones faces competition for roster spots with established players like Justin Jefferson and Jordan Addison.
source.title: Vikings WR Jeshaun Jones Suspended for 3 Games Over Substance Abuse Violation

source.summary: A tornado devastated Pomas, with residents describing the destruction as 'like bombs were dropped on our heads'. The article notes technical issues preventing full loading, suggesting potential browser or network problems.
source.title: Tornado strikes Pomas, residents describe devastation

source.summary: The article examines the historical significance of the Suez Canal, tracing its origins as a colonial project and its eventual decline. It highlights how the canal, once a symbol of European imperial power, has faced challenges and transformations over time. The piece explores the political and economic factors that contributed to its rise and fall. The Suez Canal's role in global trade is discussed, alongside its impact on regional geopolitics. The article suggests that the canal's legacy is complex, reflecting both the ambitions and limitations of colonial rule.
source.title: Suez Canal's colonial legacy and its decline

source.summary: Typhoon Narra triggered record floodwaters in Guangxi, China, leading to the evacuation of over 54,000 people. In Chongzuo, water levels surpassed 2008 highs, submerging homes and reaching rooftops. Authorities ordered business closures and warned against returning to high-risk areas. Meanwhile, Typhoon Saudel approached Japan and Taiwan, causing separate flooding and casualties. In Taiwan, a tropical depression led to one death and four missing in Tainan and Kaohsiung, where rainfall exceeded that of Typhoon Morakot in 2009.
source.title: Typhoon Narra causes record floods in Guangxi, China, prompting evacuations

source.summary: The UN condemned the Israeli raid on the Qalandia Training Center, a UNRWA vocational school in occupied East Jerusalem. UN spokesperson Stephane Dujarric called the entry unlawful and expressed concern over the disruption of education for Palestinian youth. The raid marked the fifth unauthorized entry since May, following other breaches of UN premises. UN Secretary-General Antonio Guterres urged Israel to cease interference and restore the facility. The center, operational for over 70 years, provides vocational training to hundreds of students annually.
source.title: UN Condemns Israeli Raid on Qalandia Training Center

source.summary: The USS Abraham Lincoln, which spent over 250 days at sea without a port call, is set to make a brief stop in Thailand in early September. Thailand’s Navy described the visit as routine, providing rest and logistical support for the nearly 5,000 crew members. The ship left San Diego in November 2025 and had only one stop in Guam during its deployment. Concerns about living conditions, including cold showers and supply shortages, have been raised by family members and media outlets. Two Democratic senators requested an independent review of conditions aboard the ship and others involved in the Iran conflict. Defense Secretary Pete Hegseth acknowledged the deployment’s difficulty but praised the crew’s performance. Meanwhile, a crew member’s father faces deportation after being detained by immigration agents in Key West.
source.title: USS Abraham Lincoln ends 250-day deployment with Thailand stop

source.summary: The Israeli Defense Forces (IDF) issued an evacuation order for certain Tehran neighborhoods ahead of planned strikes. The announcement was made by IDF Spokesperson Avichay Adraee in Arabic. The situation is described as a developing story with further updates expected.
source.title: IDF Orders Evacuation of Tehran Areas Before Strikes

source.summary: The Defense Ministry's Border Crossings Authority will conduct an exercise on Sunday between 11 a.m. and 1:30 p.m. at the Tarkumiya Crossing on Highway 35, according to a statement from the ministry. The exercise may involve gunshots and explosions, with high movement of emergency and rescue vehicles expected. The ministry warned that the activity could cause traffic disruptions.
source.title: Defense Ministry Conducts Exercise on Highway 35

source.summary: Analysts warn that the Hindustan Copper OFS may not attract retail investors despite a 10% discount. The stock fell 7.04% to ₹533.20, with the OFS floor set at ₹514. Siddarth Bhamre notes the discount is not enough to justify investment, as valuations may not offer significant upside. Retail bids will open on Wednesday after the non-retail portion was oversubscribed. Gaikar highlights limited upside and risks of copper price declines, advising against chasing short-term gains.
source.title: Analysts caution retail investors on Hindustan Copper OFS due to limited upside

source.summary: Mid- and small-cap stocks have outperformed blue-chip stocks, with the average advance-to-decline ratio reaching its highest level in four months. This indicates broader market participation, as retail investors favor these segments. In August, mid- and small-cap schemes received 56% of equity flows, compared to 40% in July, while large-cap funds saw outflows. The Nifty Midcap 100 and Nifty Smallcap 100 have risen 22% and 31% since April, outperforming the Nifty 50's 15% gain. Analysts attribute this to strong earnings growth and value opportunities in smaller stocks.
source.title: Mid- and small-cap stocks outperform blue-chips as market breadth expands

source.summary: Global brands have faced backlash for culturally insensitive campaigns, impacting their sales and reputations. Target's Halloween costume was criticized for resembling a racist caricature, leading to its removal. Starbucks faced a sales decline in South Korea over a campaign referencing the Gwangju Uprising. American Eagle's ad campaign drew racial criticism, though the company claimed it expanded its customer base. Anheuser-Busch InBev's Bud Light saw a sales drop after a social media promotion with a transgender influencer. Balenciaga and Gucci faced backlash for designs evoking blackface imagery. H&M and Pepsi faced criticism for ads perceived as racist, while Unilever's Dove and Zara also encountered controversies over their marketing choices.
source.title: Global brands face backlash over culturally insensitive campaigns

source.summary: The government has exercised the full greenshoe option in the Hindustan Copper Offer for Sale (OFS), increasing the stake sale from 3% to 6%. This follows strong subscription of 3.41 times by non-retail investors on the first day of bidding. The OFS, open to retail investors on Wednesday, allows bids between 9:15 am and 3:30 pm on BSE and NSE. At least 10% of the OFS size is reserved for retail investors, with an additional 25,000 shares set aside for employees. The floor price of ₹514 per share, a discount to recent market prices, may not reflect the actual price retail investors face due to institutional demand. Analyst Vaqarjaved Khan notes the discount could disappear if institutional investors clear the OFS at higher prices. While the company's Q1 profit surged 163% year-on-year, improved margins are attributed to higher copper prices rather than operational improvements. Khan advises investors to consider the OFS for long-term copper exposure rather than short-term gains.
source.title: Government Exercises Greenshoe Option in Hindustan Copper OFS, Expanding Stake Sale to 6%

source.summary: The Foundation for India and Indian Diaspora Studies (FIIDS) warns that proposed $103,265 additional H1-B visa fees could make hiring economically impractical, potentially shifting high-value jobs overseas. Khanderao Kand, FIIDS' Chief of Policy and Strategy, said the fee could burden startups and companies with hundreds of millions in extra costs. Combined with a potential $100,000 OPT fee, the policy risks making the student-to-work pathway unaffordable. FIIDS also cited a 17 per cent drop in international student enrolment and projected losses of up to $3.4 billion due to reduced international student numbers.
source.title: FIIDS warns H1-B fee hike may push high-value jobs overseas

source.summary: Civil society organisations in Bengaluru, including Eddelu Karnataka and Muslim Muttahida Mahaz, plan a September 1 campaign to highlight alleged flaws in the SIR process. Actor Prakash Raj endorsed the 'Election Commission Chalo' initiative, which aims to flag issues with the electoral roll data. Activists argue that high numbers under the ADDSO category suggest improper conduct, with some genuine voters being incorrectly removed. Jagruta Karnataka called for more time to file objections, while BJP spokesperson S Prakash defended the process, citing voter non-compliance.
source.title: Civil society groups plan September 1 campaign to highlight SIR flaws

source.summary: Five family members were discovered dead in a lodge room in Srisailam, Andhra Pradesh, with police suspecting a suicide pact linked to financial struggles. The deceased included a 36-year-old man, his three sisters, and a 15-year-old nephew. Authorities noted the family had overstayed their rented room, which was not permitted, and had reportedly claimed to be unwell. The lodge staff noticed a foul smell before alerting police, who registered a case of suspicious death. Temple authorities criticized the lodge for violating accommodation rules, which limit stays to 48 hours for devotees.
source.title: 5 of family found dead in Srisailam; suicide suspected

source.summary: Indian equities are expected to open higher on Wednesday, with the GIFT Nifty indicating a gap-up after the benchmark indices closed strongly. Vaishali Parekh of Prabhudas Lilladher noted the index is trading over 200 points above Tuesday's Nifty 50 close of 24,334. She identified a bullish engulfing pattern on the daily chart, suggesting potential for further gains. The Nifty 50 faces a key resistance at 24,400 and support at 24,000, while the Bank Nifty remains near its 200-period MA at 57,450. Parekh recommended buying Astral, Sai Life Sciences, and ICICI Bank with specific price targets and stop-loss levels.
source.title: Indian equities poised for gap-up opening as GIFT Nifty signals higher start

source.summary: The United States has paused all visa applications and appointments worldwide as part of an immigration crackdown, according to the Financial Times. The move aims to limit access to those who may rely on state assistance, as stated by an official. The State Department announced a global training program for embassies, with visa appointments to be rescheduled. Applicants received emails informing them of cancellations and were promised new dates later.
source.title: US halts global visa appointments amid immigration crackdown

source.summary: Rajasthan Agriculture and Rural Development Minister Dr. Kirori Lal Meena was admitted to the ICU at Jaipur SMS Hospital after testing positive for swine flu. Meanwhile, protests erupted at IIT Delhi following the suicide of a physics student, with students demanding financial compensation, resignations, and an independent inquiry. The institute formed an external panel to investigate the incident. In another case, a family in Andhra Pradesh died by suicide after alleging harassment and forced conversion by a rifle shooting coach. Additionally, an Indian loitering munition accidentally struck a sensitive Pakistani nuclear site during Operation Sindoor, raising concerns about military infrastructure vulnerabilities.
source.title: Rajasthan Minister Admits to Swine Flu ICU, Campus Protests Over Student Suicide

source.summary: Nigeria's Dangote refinery, the continent's largest, has become Europe's largest supplier of jet fuel, surpassing the U.S., due to supply disruptions from the Iran war. Europe now relies on about 700,000 bpd of imports, with Nigeria contributing significantly. However, domestic airlines struggle with high prices and limited access to fuel, as the refinery prioritizes international buyers paying higher prices. Local airlines have accumulated over 60 billion Naira in debt, forcing route cuts and price hikes. Analysts note that the issue lies not with supply but with the cost of transporting fuel to airports, involving multiple traders and high logistics expenses. Solutions proposed include direct government procurement from the refinery to reduce middlemen and stabilize prices, though Dangote's role as a global supplier may complicate such efforts.
source.title: Nigeria's Dangote refinery fuels Europe amid domestic shortages

source.summary: Iranian lawmakers have proposed withdrawing from the Nuclear Non-Proliferation Treaty (NPT), a move seen as a response to increased U.S. economic pressure. The proposal, submitted by MP Ghasem Ravanbakhsh, is being considered by officials, though its actual implementation remains uncertain. Experts suggest such a withdrawal would signal Iran's intent to develop nuclear weapons or move closer to that goal, potentially increasing international pressure and military risks. The NPT allows withdrawal with three months' notice, but analysts argue that the threat of withdrawal is more strategic than a real policy, as it maintains ambiguity about Iran's nuclear capabilities. Iran's stockpile of 60%-enriched uranium and reduced international oversight further complicate the situation, with some experts suggesting that remaining within the treaty while limiting inspections offers more strategic advantages. The international community, including the IAEA, would closely monitor any attempt to invoke Article X, as seen in the case of North Korea's uncertain status after its 2003 withdrawal.
source.title: Iranian lawmakers propose leaving nuclear treaty amid tensions

source.summary: A study published in the British Medical Journal found that up to 97.7% of deceased NFL players between 2016 and 2021 may have had chronic traumatic encephalopathy (CTE), a degenerative brain disease. Of 235 brain donors, 215 were diagnosed with CTE, indicating a significantly higher prevalence than previous community-based studies. Researchers noted that many head impacts occurred at lower levels of play, contributing to the risk. The NFL responded by emphasizing its efforts to improve safety and provide health resources for players.
source.title: NFL players' brain disease rates exceed prior estimates

source.summary: Prime Minister Sanae Takaichi stated Japan takes U.S. sanctions on ICC President Tomoko Akane seriously, calling the measure incompatible with Japan's stance. Takaichi emphasized Japan's support for the ICC and its role as a major financial contributor. She noted Japan had urged the U.S. not to sanction Akane, a Japanese national, and pledged continued support for her. Foreign Minister Toshimitsu Motegi confirmed officials have met with Akane in the Netherlands and remain in close contact with her.
source.title: Japan's PM Takaichi Condemns U.S. Sanctions on ICC President

source.summary: The Fire and Disaster Management Agency reported 41,174 heatstroke cases requiring hospitalization in July, the third highest since 2008. Over 60% of patients were aged 65 or older, with 79 deaths confirmed. The agency urged hydration, air conditioning use, and attendance at cooling shelters.
source.title: Japan records 41,174 heatstroke hospitalizations in July

source.summary: U.S. Treasury Secretary Scott Bessent announced new sanctions against Iran, framing them as an 'economic D-Day' to isolate the country economically. The Trump administration warns that no entity is beyond U.S. sanctions and hopes for regime change to prevent Iran from developing nuclear weapons. While some Gulf allies like the UAE have cut ties with Iran, China and others have criticized the measures as unilateral. Meanwhile, the Supreme Court temporarily blocked a lower court's ruling against Trump's mail-in voting restrictions, which targeted 23 Democratic-led states. The court did not rule on the legality of the order, which aims to prevent non-citizen voting, though critics warn it could disrupt midterm elections. The decision highlights ongoing legal battles over voting rights and federal authority.
source.title: Trump seeks Iran isolation, SCOTUS halts mail-in voting restrictions

source.summary: The Mining Engineers’ Association of India (MEAI) praised the MMDR Amendment Act, 2026, for enhancing clarity and stability in the mining sector. The act introduces Section 9D, which prohibits state governments from imposing taxes or levies on mineral rights based on quantity, value, or royalty, except under central government conditions. MEAI secretary general M. Narsaiah noted that this provision offers greater certainty for existing lease holders and reduces financial uncertainty for mining projects. The association urged mining states to align their tax policies with the amended framework. The changes are expected to benefit downstream industries like steel and cement as well.
source.title: Mining Association Commends MMDR Act Amendment for Fiscal Clarity

source.summary: A TTD Trust Board member, G. Bhanu Prakash Reddy, met with Union Minister Nitin Gadkari to request faster progress on the Chennai-Tirupati highway. He highlighted frequent accidents between the Taj Hotel flyover and Peruru Junction, a concern previously raised during Gadkari's visit. The minister reportedly instructed officials to prioritize underpass construction. The meeting took place in New Delhi on August 25, 2026.
source.title: TTD Board Member Requests Accelerated Work on Chennai-Tirupati Highway

source.summary: Air India is seeking $1.5 billion in fresh equity from Tata Sons and Singapore Airlines to address mounting losses, according to two sources. The airline's combined losses for the fiscal year ended March 2026 reached $2.33 billion, more than double the previous year. The funding request, which would be one of the largest since Tata took control in 2022, is expected to come in tranches, with Singapore Airlines contributing its share. Discussions are ongoing, and no decision has been made. Air India faces challenges including a Pakistan airspace ban, international network disruptions, and the aftermath of a fatal crash. Tata Sons' chairman, N. Chandrasekaran, has warned that the turnaround could take up to a decade due to supply-chain issues and systemic overhauls needed.
source.title: Air India seeks $1.5 billion from owners Tata, Singapore Air as losses mount, sources say

source.summary: India’s National Security Adviser Ajit Doval and Chinese Foreign Minister Wang Yi held the 25th round of border talks in Beijing, focusing on maintaining peace along the India-China border and advancing bilateral relations. The discussions followed a meeting between Doval and Chinese Vice President Han Zheng, who emphasized strengthening peace and improving ties across economic, political, and multilateral forums. Han highlighted the momentum in bilateral relations, noting recent high-level meetings between Prime Minister Modi and President Xi Jinping. Both sides called for managing the relationship strategically, expanding cooperation, and addressing differences to ensure sustained development of ties.
source.title: India and China hold 25th border talks to promote peace and bilateral ties

source.summary: During a parliamentary standing committee meeting on 'crime against children', BJP and Congress MPs clashed over allegations of police use of pellet guns and lathicharge against students during the July 20 protest. Congress MP Ajay Maken submitted a letter seeking a discussion on the incident, prompting a ruckus with ruling party members. The meeting, reported by ANI, highlighted tensions between opposition and ruling party over the handling of the protest.
source.title: Ruckus at House panel meet: BJP, Congress MPs spar over use of force on students at July 20 protest

source.summary: Lenskart faced initial skepticism with its high valuation, as critics questioned its business model and compared it to failed IPOs. However, the company's market cap surged to Rs 1.15 lakh crore by 2026, driven by strong performance and a diversified business model. Lenskart operates across price points, from Rs 500 glasses to Rs 30,000 progressive lenses, and has expanded its international business with a 38% growth. The company's full-stack retail infrastructure, including technology-enabled eye testing and backward integration, supports its growth. Analysts maintain positive ratings, citing strong same-store sales growth, margin expansion, and potential for further international scaling. The company's evolution from a retail eyewear business to a multi-faceted enterprise with a focus on eye testing and premiumization has reshaped investor perceptions.
source.title: Lenskart's valuation journey from skepticism to 1.15 lakh crore market cap

source.summary: Canara Robeco's CIO, Shridatta Bhandwaldar, argues that large-cap stocks offer better value than mid- and small-caps despite current investor favor towards smaller firms. He highlights that large caps provide a stronger margin of safety, though meaningful rerating requires earnings acceleration in key sectors like banking, IT, FMCG, and oil and gas. Bhandwaldar remains constructive on equities, citing a 15% YoY earnings growth for the Nifty 500 in Q1FY27, signaling a recovery from an 18-month earnings downcycle. The fund's portfolio is split 46% large-cap, 40% mid-cap, and 11% small-cap, with allocations driven by company quality and growth potential. Mid-cap valuations, while expanded, are supported by strong earnings growth, though certain sectors like hospitality and finance face risks from high energy prices and inflation.
source.title: Canara Robeco CIO Advises on Largecap Value Amid Smallcap Popularity

source.summary: Kerala's Onam festival, traditionally linked to agricultural prosperity, has been disrupted by a weaker monsoon and subsequent crop losses, leading to economic shifts and changes in local customs. Farmers report significant losses due to heavy rains and flooding, with some losing up to ₹40,000. The state's Department of Agriculture estimates losses at ₹127 crores, though farmers say the impact is harder to quantify. As a result, many are purchasing ready-made Onam feasts instead of preparing them at home. Meanwhile, flower production has increased, with farmers capitalizing on higher prices despite some damage. Climate change is affecting traditional farming cycles, with experts warning of more extreme weather events. Adaptation strategies, such as micro-irrigation and climate-resilient crops, are needed but remain financially out of reach for small farmers. The festival's economic impact is also felt through rising prices of agricultural products, with some items seeing price increases of up to 100% compared to last year. The situation highlights the growing challenges faced by farmers in Kerala as climate patterns become increasingly unpredictable.
source.title: Kerala’s Onam festival marred by a weaker monsoon and subsequent crop loss

source.summary: West Bengal minister Dilip Ghosh vowed a 'surgical strike' against 'anti-national' forces at Jadavpur University, following clashes between Left-leaning student groups and the ABVP. Ghosh accused pro-Kashmir azadi activists of misconduct during visits by dignitaries. The SFI condemned the remarks as reflecting a 'fascist mindset' and vowed to protest against BJP influence on campus.
source.title: West Bengal minister vows 'surgical strike' against 'anti-national' groups at Jadavpur University

source.summary: Small businesses face operational challenges due to a new biometric verification mandate for SIM issuance, according to experts. The requirement places additional burdens on small firms with high staff turnover and limited financial resources. CUTS International warns that the mandate could lead to higher costs for medium-sized enterprises and greater strain on micro-enterprises. The regulation defines 'business users' broadly, requiring biometric verification for each end user of a business connection. Experts argue that the administrative and privacy costs may be particularly difficult for small businesses, where SIMs and phones frequently change hands among employees.
source.title: Biometric verification mandate creates operational challenges for small businesses in SIM issuance

source.summary: Police are searching for a group of men who vandalized a shop, house, and vehicles in Kolathur after a dispute over cake payment. The incident occurred on Sunday night when two men, allegedly under the influence of alcohol, refused to pay ₹120 for six cakes. Maripandi, the shop owner, offered a reduced price, which led to the men calling associates to the scene. The group then threw stones at the shop and house, damaged parked vehicles, and fled. Rajamangalam police registered a case and are analyzing CCTV footage to identify the suspects.
source.title: Police investigate vandalism after dispute over cake payment in Kolathur

source.summary: ESDS Software Solutions, a data centre and AI provider, included local protests against data centres as a risk in its ₹720 crore IPO filing. The company highlighted potential impacts on operations, reputation, and stakeholder relationships. Promoter Piyush Somani noted that protests were previously unaddressed but are now being considered, with plans to locate data centres in industrial areas. The IPO aims to fund GPU and cloud equipment purchases, with the issue opening on August 28, 2026. Analysts noted the lack of dedicated data centre stocks complicates market assessment.
source.title: ESDS acknowledges local protests as risk in IPO filing

source.summary: Three members of an Andhra Pradesh family died by suicide, prompting a criminal investigation into alleged murder, blackmail, and forced religious conversion. Police recovered two suicide notes naming Sheikh Sadiq Khan, a rifle-shooting coach, as the accused. The notes accused Khan of harassment, threats, and pressuring Sowjanya to convert to Islam. Police are verifying the claims and investigating the possible link between Khan's alleged actions and the family's deaths, including the earlier death of Sowjanya's husband. Khan was arrested in Meerut after a five-state search and is in judicial custody.
source.title: Family suicide investigation reveals murder and forced conversion allegations

source.summary: A 15-year-old boy, Mithun, was recovered from a drain in Delhi three days after he fell in while chasing a kite. His body was pulled out by a JCB excavator on Tuesday. Mithun's family claims the search efforts were inadequate, with multiple agencies failing to locate him promptly. His mother criticized the authorities for not initiating the search immediately, while his father, who works in sewers, searched for his son himself. The family alleges institutional delays and demands accountability, with one junior engineer suspended over the incident. The boy's parents expressed grief over his death, highlighting his academic achievements and artistic talents. Authorities acknowledged the challenges of the search due to strong currents and debris, but the family remains unsatisfied with the response.
source.title: 15-year-old boy's body found in Delhi drain after 3-day search

source.summary: Foreign Affairs Minister Penny Wong announced an additional $3 million in aid for Nepal's flood disaster. The total Australian assistance package now reaches $8 million, including hygiene kits and solar lighting coordinated by the defence force. Meanwhile, the number of missing Australians has risen to 43, with 650 calls received by the department of foreign affairs. Australian personnel remain unable to access the flood zone due to cut-off roads and damaged infrastructure.
source.title: Australia sends $3m aid as missing Australians in Nepal floods rise to 43

source.summary: Noel Godin, a prankster who targeted powerful figures with cream pies for over 50 years, has died at age 80. His famous targets included politicians, philosophers, filmmakers, and Microsoft founder Bill Gates.
source.title: Noel Godin, the cream pie activist who targeted Bill Gates, dies at 80

source.summary: The Los Angeles Rams announced that Aaron Donald has ended his 2 1/2-year retirement to rejoin the team. ESPN reported he agreed to a one-year contract worth at least $20 million in incentives. Donald, a three-time Defensive Player of the Year, will play alongside Myles Garrett and other defensive additions. His return resets his eligibility clock for the Pro Football Hall of Fame.
source.title: Aaron Donald ends retirement to return to Los Angeles Rams

source.summary: The National Park Service reported that a flash flood in Bright Angel Creek forced the evacuation of dozens of people and swept debris into the Colorado River. Officials are seeking information on more than 20 missing individuals while continuing evacuations with the Arizona Department of Public Safety. Popular tourist spots remained closed as park officials surveyed damage and halted rafting trips. Meteorologist Justin Johndrow noted that half an inch to one inch of rain fell within 30 minutes, causing rapid runoff.
source.title: Dozens evacuated from Grand Canyon after flash flood hits creek leading to Colorado River

source.summary: US forces struck Iranian rocket launchers in the Strait of Hormuz, according to a US official. The IRGC confirmed the attacks hit Larak Island and warned of a retaliatory response. An unnamed US official stated that IRGC forces were preparing to launch rockets and sea mines. This marks the first US military action in the Strait in a month.
source.title: US strikes Iranian rocket launchers in Strait of Hormuz

source.summary: Aaron Donald has rejoined the Los Angeles Rams after retiring in March 2024. ESPN reports he will earn $20 million, potentially rising to $30 million with bonuses. Rams head coach Sean McVay stated Donald was outstanding during his summer workout. The 35-year-old defensive tackle returns to a roster featuring Matthew Stafford and Myles Garrett. Donald aims to replicate his peak form with the stacked team.
source.title: Aaron Donald returns to LA Rams for one-year deal

source.summary: A mass shooting at Washington Park in Chicago killed one person and injured at least 13 others. Police detained a suspect and recovered a weapon after the incident occurred around 11:37 p.m. Saturday. Authorities stated the victims ranged in age from 21 to 47, with one fatality and several hospitalized in serious or fair condition. The Cook County Crime Stoppers offered a reward for information leading to the arrest of the gunman.
source.title: Mass shooting at Chicago park kills one and injures 13

source.summary: US forces struck Iranian rocket launchers on Larak island in the Strait of Hormuz, a US official said Sunday. Iran's Revolutionary Guards reported the attack killed and wounded several fighters and civilians, vowing punishment. A tanker was struck by an unknown projectile nearby, though no casualties were reported. The conflict has entered a stalemate after six months of fighting.
source.title: US strikes Iranian launchers on Larak island in Strait of Hormuz

source.summary: Border czar Tom Homan defended recent deportations to Haiti, stating he does not know the conditions there. The State Department warns Americans against traveling to Haiti due to severe violence and instability. Approximately 350,000 Haitians lost Temporary Protected Status after the Supreme Court allowed its termination. The Department of Homeland Security plans to increase deportation flights from once a month to once a week. A YouGov survey found 53 percent of Americans disapprove of the administration's immigration handling. Human rights groups urge a halt to deportations until safety guarantees exist.
source.title: Trump border czar Tom Homan defends deportations to Haiti despite safety warnings

source.summary: US defence contractor Covenant plans to begin producing medium-range missiles near Leipzig from 2027, according to sources. The reported range exceeds 1,500 kilometres, with potential annual output of up to 1,000 units. Germany's Ministry of Defence has reportedly sent requests for proposals to the company. The firm is backed by investors including Michael Kaufman, Andreessen Horowitz, and the Founders Fund. It remains unclear whether Berlin intends to procure the missiles or how far negotiations have progressed.
source.title: US firm Covenant plans medium-range missile production near Leipzig starting 2027

source.summary: NASA successfully launched the Nancy Grace Roman telescope from Florida on Sunday to investigate dark energy, black holes, and exoplanets. The agency states the telescope offers a field of vision 100 times larger than Hubble and James Webb. Nicky Fox, a NASA administrator, noted the mission aims to discover up to 100,000 new exoplanets to answer if humanity is alone in the universe. The spacecraft separated from its SpaceX rocket and is traveling to an orbit one million miles from Earth. Astronomer Jenifer Millard explained the distant orbit prevents infrared interference from Earth and the Moon. Named after NASA's first female executive, the telescope has a five-year primary lifespan with a goal to operate for 10 years.
source.title: NASA launches Nancy Grace Roman telescope to explore dark energy and exoplanets

source.summary: The article states that solitude has become a resource deliberately sought out and exploited by tech companies. It notes that a required part of the site failed to load due to potential browser issues or network problems. The text suggests readers should check their connection or disable ad blockers.
source.title: Tech companies deliberately seek out and exploit solitude as a resource

source.summary: Gaza medics reported that an Israeli airstrike near a bakery in Deir Al-Balah killed two Palestinians, including a three-year-old boy. The Israeli military stated it targeted a Hamas militant without providing further details. Hamas accuses Israel of violating the October 2025 ceasefire, which has seen over 1,300 Palestinian deaths since taking effect. Health officials confirmed the casualties while noting several others were wounded in the attack.
source.title: Israeli airstrike in Gaza kills two people including a child

source.summary: Russia stated its African Corps assisted Nigerien forces in repelling an attempted coup in Niamey. Moscow announced the rebellion was contained and pledged continued support against extremists. Niger's authorities confirmed the situation is under control of President Tiani's government. The Alliance of Sahel States condemned the mutiny as a destabilization attempt. Security forces have increased patrols around key sites following the incident.
source.title: Russia claims its forces helped repel attempted coup in Niger

source.summary: Niger's ruling military junta restored order in Niamey after mutineers stormed the presidential palace and a military air base. State TV reported that dozens of soldiers were killed or arrested following the unrest. Loyalist forces, aided by Russia's Africa Corps, repelled the attackers who had taken hostages and fired at sensitive sites. The mutiny, which lasted from Friday into Saturday, was driven by grievances over rising insecurity and jihadi violence in the Sahel region. Analysts noted that deteriorating security conditions have fueled discontent within the armed forces. Russia's Africa Corps intervened with ground and aerial support to neutralize the mutineers. Regional allies, including the Alliance of Sahel States, Algeria, and Turkey, expressed solidarity with Niger's leadership.
source.title: Niger junta suppresses mutiny with Russian Africa Corps support

source.summary: President Recep Tayyip Erdogan announced that Turkey has mobilized all available resources following a passenger ship capsizing off Northern Cyprus. The vessel was sailing from Kyrenia to Mersin's Tasucu port when the accident occurred. Turkish officials confirmed that 237 passengers and crew were rescued while seven people lost their lives. Search and rescue operations continue uninterrupted in cooperation with Northern Cyprus authorities. Government leaders extended condolences to the families of the deceased and expressed hope for the safe recovery of those still missing.
source.title: President Erdogan says Turkey mobilized all resources after ship capsized off Northern Cyprus

source.summary: Migrants in Saxony-Anhalt are preparing to leave fearing a far-right deportation offensive. The AfD party is expected to win a historic majority in the upcoming regional election. The party promotes remigration, a program targeting non-white populations.
source.title: Migrants in Saxony-Anhalt fear deportation after AfD victory

source.summary: Emmanouil Karalis has emerged as a significant challenger to Mondo Duplantis' dominance in the pole vault. At the Zurich Diamond League, both athletes attempted to break the world record simultaneously. This marks a shift from Duplantis' recent pattern of winning competitions before setting records. Karalis is now seen as the first true threat to the Swedish champion's long-standing supremacy in the event.
source.title: Emmanouil Karalis challenges Mondo Duplantis at Zurich Diamond League

source.summary: Fear of Immigration and Customs Enforcement agents is hindering the rebuilding of homes destroyed by the Eaton wildfires in Altadena. Construction managers check for ICE presence before work begins, and the threat of raids scares away undocumented workers. While the Department of Homeland Security states its operations protect the economy and dismantle illegal networks, local residents and advocates report that these actions disrupt recovery efforts. Authorities have arrested several day laborers on their way to work sites, causing delays for homeowners. Despite these challenges, many homeowners rely on Hispanic migrant workers to complete their rebuilding projects.
source.title: ICE Raids and Fears Slow Reconstruction in California's Burnt Altadena

source.summary: Venezuela's ruling PSUV party expressed full support for a new oil agreement with the United States. Democratic lawmakers accused President Trump of prioritizing private profit over public interests and troop safety. The deal grants a private joint venture control over 65 billion barrels of reserves. Republicans defended the historic agreement as beneficial for both nations.
source.title: Venezuela's PSUV backs oil deal with Washington as US Democrats criticize Trump

source.summary: The federal government proposed reducing private health insurance rebates for Australians over 65, aiming to save $3 billion over four years. Industry estimates suggest 62,000 older Australians may cancel their cover while 200,000 could downgrade policies. Health Minister Mark Butler stated government modelling predicts no material impact on public hospital capacity. Conversely, the Shadow Regional Health Minister Anne Webster warned regional hospitals would struggle with increased patient loads. Professor Yuting Zhang from the University of Melbourne estimated only 42,000 people would drop cover, arguing benefits outweigh costs. A Senate inquiry into the bill is scheduled for October 7.
source.title: Older Australians face higher health insurance costs under proposed rebate changes

source.summary: The IAEA stated that Ukraine's Zaporizhzhia nuclear power plant has lacked off-site power for over a week, forcing reliance on emergency diesel generators. Director General Rafael Grossi emphasized that fuel availability is critical for nuclear safety. The agency noted the plant has only a 10-day diesel supply and is negotiating a ceasefire to repair electrical lines damaged by military activity. Three recent drone incidents have also raised safety concerns at the Russian-occupied facility.
source.title: IAEA reports Zaporizhzhia plant lost off-site power and relies on limited diesel

source.summary: North Carolina defeated TCU 15-10 in Dublin on Saturday to open coach Bill Belichick's second season at the school. The Tar Heels secured the victory with a 28-yard field goal by Aeron Burrell following a fumble recovery. Quarterback Billy Edwards Jr. completed 16 of 28 passes for 232 yards, while Jeremy Payne rushed for 142 yards for TCU. Coach Belichick credited his defensive front for stopping the Horned Frogs, noting they forced the quarterback to cut back inside. TCU coach Sonny Dykes stated that kicking field goals made sense when the team was not moving the football effectively. The game marked a positive start for Belichick, who finished 4-8 in his previous season with the Tar Heels.
source.title: North Carolina defeats TCU 15-10 in Ireland to open Bill Belichick's second season

source.summary: World Vision's Dhruba Gurmachhan explains that blocked roads and monsoon weather are complicating efforts to deliver food, shelter, and emergency hygiene to Nepal flood survivors.
source.title: Blocked roads and monsoon weather hinder aid delivery to Nepal flood survivors

source.summary: Rescue crews are struggling through blocked roads and dangerous terrain to find thousands of people missing after deadly floods in Nepal and Tibet. The article reports that search efforts are ongoing despite the challenging conditions. NPR notes that it does not accept money for coverage or interviews.
source.title: Rescuers search for thousands missing after deadly Himalayan floods in Nepal and Tibet

source.summary: The provided text contains a headline stating that Netanyahu condemned a settler attack. However, the body of the article failed to load due to technical issues.
source.title: Netanyahu condemns settler attack in West Bank village

source.summary: The Associated Press reports that Name, Image, and Likeness rules have increased parity in college football, resulting in seven teams having odds of 11-1 or better to win the national championship. Ohio State, Notre Dame, and Texas are each priced at +650 or better, while Indiana, Oregon, Georgia, and Miami also remain competitive contenders. Joey Feazel of Caesars Sportsbook noted that the landscape is more open than in previous years. Sportsbooks must also adjust for player movement through the transfer portal and eligibility court cases. Notre Dame faces a relatively easier schedule as an independent, though experts warn it is not without challenges. Additionally, Notre Dame quarterback CJ Carr is currently favored over Texas QB Arch Manning for the Heisman Trophy.
source.title: NIL rules increase parity, making seven teams favorites for national title

source.summary: A Russian drone strike on a Ukrainian weapons depot near Kyiv killed at least 37 people and injured dozens more. President Volodymyr Zelensky stated the storage site definitely should not have been located next to a residential area. The explosion damaged approximately 130 homes in the Myla village and triggered a secondary blast at a nearby care home. Ukrainian officials have launched criminal proceedings regarding official negligence in placing explosives so close to civilians. This incident marks the second munitions depot strike near Kyiv in recent months, prompting Prime Minister Sergiy Koretsky to express regret that lessons from previous failures were not learned. Meanwhile, fighting continues across the region with additional drone attacks reported in Odesa, Dnipropetrovsk, Sumy, and Zaporizhzhia.
source.title: Russian drone strike kills 37 at Kyiv weapons depot near homes

source.summary: Rescuers in Nepal and China continue searching for nearly 3,000 people missing after devastating floods swept through the border region. At least 682 bodies have been recovered, with 675 in Nepal and seven in China. A breakthrough occurred when the Nepali army inserted a pipe into a tunnel at the Trishuli 3A hydroelectric site where over 100 workers are believed trapped. The US Geological Survey attributed the disaster to a glacial collapse, a phenomenon linked to climate change by UN climate chief Simon Steill. Foreign Minister Shisir Khanal stated reconstruction costs could reach billions of dollars while appealing for specialized rescue technology. Meanwhile, Chinese authorities paused operations in Gyirong due to flood risks from a newly formed lake before reporting it had drained. Families in Nepal face agonizing waits for news of missing relatives, including 933 hydropower workers and hundreds of foreigners.
source.title: Nepal and China floods leave nearly 3,000 missing as rescue efforts continue

source.summary: The article examines the economic impact of escalating tariffs between the United States and Canada. Bernard Yaros of Oxford Economics warns that higher duties on vehicles will eventually increase consumer prices. The Forest Products Association of Canada notes that metal and wood tariffs will raise construction costs. Bradley Saunders of Capital Economics suggests Canadians may switch to domestic goods for household items. John Iselin of the Budget Lab at Yale estimates the average cost to an American household is about $3, though broader trade tensions could add $1,000.
source.title: New US-Canada Tariffs Will Raise Costs for Cars, Homes, and Households

source.summary: The International Atomic Energy Agency reported that the Zaporizhzhia nuclear power plant in Ukraine has lacked off-site power for more than a week. The facility currently relies on emergency diesel generators, which provide only a ten-day supply. IAEA Director General Rafael Grossi emphasized that reliable external power is indispensable for nuclear safety. The plant lost its regular supply following military activity near the Dnipro River. The Vienna-based group is negotiating a local ceasefire to allow repairs to electrical lines.
source.title: IAEA reports Zaporizhzhia plant lost power supply for over a week

source.summary: The article details five distinct trends in the Australian retail and transport sectors based on recent financial results and market data. Kmart Group reported $11.7bn in sales driven by its Anko brand, which is expanding globally and introducing higher-priced product tiers. Domino's Pizza reduced discounting to improve franchisee profitability despite an 11% revenue drop in Australia and New Zealand. Sigma Healthcare's Chemist Warehouse found that customers buying GLP-1 drugs have shopping baskets 40% larger than others, purchasing more beauty and health products. Eagers Automotive noted that the shift to electric vehicles is a one-way street, with EV sales tripling compared to last year. Australia Post recorded a $108m pre-tax loss as letter volumes fell to 1930s levels, prompting a 15c stamp price increase.
source.title: Australians embrace weight-loss drugs, dupe brands, and electric vehicles

source.summary: Experts at a webinar organized by SRM Institute of Science and Technology and The Hindu stated that artificial intelligence is a permanent part of healthcare. Panelists emphasized that medical practitioners must retain ultimate responsibility for clinical decisions. Dr. Jayanthi urged students to develop AI literacy and verification reflexes. Dr. Ganapathy warned against outsourcing accountability to technology. Mr. Gautham noted AI can expand access in underserved areas while maintaining oversight.
source.title: Experts say AI will stay in healthcare but doctors must remain final decision-makers

source.summary: RSS chief Mohan Bhagwat stated in New York that a Hindu who believes Muslims have no place in India ceases to be Hindu. He addressed concerns about the RSS's vision of a Hindu Rashtra, clarifying that Hindutva does not envisage a Bharat without Muslims. Bhagwat highlighted the organization's 1.3 lakh service projects and its inclusive approach during a recent aircraft collision in Dadri. He emphasized that dialogue and selfless service are essential for social change beyond politics.
source.title: RSS Chief Mohan Bhagwat Says Excluding Muslims Makes One Not Hindu

source.summary: Hurriyat Conference chairman Mirwaiz Umar Farooq supported National Conference MP Aga Ruhullah Mehdi and criticized the party for abandoning its stance on Article 370. Mirwaiz urged all J&K political parties to demand the restoration of statehood and constitutional guarantees. Mehdi announced his resignation from the NC and Lok Sabha, responding to pressure from party leadership. He highlighted threats to the region's youth, environment, and cultural rights.
source.title: Mirwaiz backs NC MP and demands J&K statehood and Article 370 restoration

source.summary: The ongoing trade war between the United States and Canada is driven by five key issues, according to a report by Prabhakar Jha. The conflict stems from differing views on the economic relationship, with President Trump accusing Canada of taking advantage of the US while Prime Minister Mark Carney frames it as a sovereignty dispute. Negotiations collapsed after weeks of talks, with both sides accusing the other of demanding too much. The US sought to dictate Canada's future trade agreements, while Ottawa rejected matching American tariffs on third countries. Disagreements also arose over tariffs on steel, aluminium, and automobiles, with Canada imposing counter-tariffs on $27.6 billion of US imports. The breakdown highlights deep economic interdependence and Canada's efforts to diversify its trade relationships.
source.title: Five issues driving the US-Canada trade war escalation

source.summary: Health officials stated the Warangal Super Specialty Hospital will be ready for services by December. Minister Damodar Rajanarsimha directed a doctors' committee to visit the facility every 15 days. Officials reported seasonal diseases declined while typhoid cases increased slightly. The minister ordered intensified disease surveillance and mosquito-control measures across government hospitals.
source.title: Warangal Hospital to Open by December; Tims Units Follow

source.summary: Andhra Pradesh energy consumption has increased by 15% to 20% daily due to heat waves and El Niño conditions. Authorities attribute the surge to widespread air conditioner use and farmers pumping groundwater. The state currently generates power from thermal, wind, and hydro sources while purchasing additional electricity from outside regions. Officials expect this high demand trend to continue through the peak summer season.
source.title: Andhra Pradesh power demand rises 15-20% due to heat wave

source.summary: Prime Minister Benjamin Netanyahu condemned dozens of Israeli settlers attacking Palestinians in Qusra and Jalud on August 29, 2026. The military stated forces removed rioters barricaded inside a Palestinian home and opened a police investigation. President Isaac Herzog and the Foreign Ministry also criticized the violence. Since October 2023, at least 1,103 Palestinians have died in the West Bank according to an AFP tally.
source.title: Netanyahu condemns settler attack in West Bank village
