source.summary: Researchers at Varonis discovered a vulnerability in Microsoft 365 Copilot by asking the AI assistant about its guardrails, leading to the exposure of an undocumented parameter that bypassed user consent. The parameter ?autorun=1, when combined with ?q=, allowed silent execution of prompts upon clicking a malicious link. Microsoft mitigated the issue in February by blocking ?q= from injecting text, and introduced further fixes on Tuesday.
source.title: Researchers exploit Microsoft Copilot's undocumented parameter to bypass consent requirements

source.summary: Ofer Mendelevitch, head of developer relations at BAND, discussed transitioning from step-by-step prompting to loop engineering in coding workflows. He used a package version resolver as an example, showing how agents can work autonomously by verifying goals and iterating without constant human input. The approach involves defining verifiable goals, allowing agents to test and refine code independently. Mendelevitch also introduced multi-agent collaboration, with one agent writing code and another reviewing it, including adversarial checks. This method aims to reduce human intervention and improve code quality.
source.title: Ofer Mendelevitch Demonstrates Transition from Prompting to Multi-Agent Coding Workflows

source.summary: Flock, a police-tech company with 120,000 license plate readers, introduced updates to prevent misuse by officers, including stalking. The Washington Post found 50 cases of misuse, such as a Wisconsin officer searching for a woman 179 times. Flock's new measures require case numbers for searches but do not verify them, allowing fake entries. Critics argue these changes fail to address broader concerns about mass surveillance, with some cities canceling contracts and states considering bans. The article questions whether Flock's systems truly solve crime or enable overreach, suggesting alternatives like limiting data retention and access to only emergency cases. Flock's business model relies on collecting extensive data, but growing backlash may force changes in how its technology is used.
source.title: Flock's surveillance system faces criticism over loopholes and civil liberties concerns

source.summary: Axiom Math's AI system, AxiomProver, has verified the correctness of the 246 theorem, which states there are infinitely many prime pairs separated by 246. This marks a significant milestone in AI-assisted mathematical research, demonstrating the potential of automated verification in number theory. The theorem, part of ongoing efforts to solve the twin prime conjecture, was formalized using AxiomProver's multi-agent system, which has also been used to verify other proofs and solve mathematical problems. The achievement highlights the growing role of AI in ensuring the reliability of mathematical proofs and, potentially, in verifying AI-generated code for critical systems. Axiom Math's founder, Ken Ono, emphasizes the importance of formalization as a stepping stone toward safer AI-driven technologies.
source.title: Axiom Math's AI Verifies 246 Theorem on Prime Gaps

source.summary: The article explores the relationship between 10-year-old neurodivergent Xander and his robot companion Moxie, highlighting both the potential and limitations of social robots in therapy. Moxie, a 15-inch AI-powered robot designed to assist children with autism, engages Xander in conversations and helps him practice social skills. However, the article notes that Moxie's initial purpose—to provide therapeutic support—was not fully realized, as Xander's interactions with her were more recreational than therapeutic. The piece also discusses the broader implications of social robots in autism therapy, citing research by experts like Brian Scassellati and Maja Mataric, who argue that robots can offer consistent, engaging support for children. Despite positive reviews and media attention, the article raises concerns about the practical challenges of implementing such technology, including delays in responses and the inability to adapt to the unpredictable behavior of children. The story of Moxie's eventual failure underscores the complexities and risks of relying on robots for emotional and social development, especially for vulnerable communities.
source.title: A neurodivergent child's robot companion and the challenges of social robotics

source.summary: Z.ai has released its GLM-5.3 model, which outperforms several U.S. models like Kimi K3 and Claude Fable 5 on coding benchmarks. The model, with 750B parameters, is available in the coding plan and will soon be accessible via API and Hugging Face. The article suggests that Z.ai's success stems from rapid release cycles and efficient post-training techniques, allowing them to keep pace with U.S. labs despite having a smaller model size. The piece also explores the broader implications of China's growing data industry and the dual-use risks of advanced cybersecurity capabilities in GLM-5.3. Z.ai emphasizes safety measures but acknowledges the need for industry-wide governance as open-weight models become more prevalent.
source.title: Z.ai's GLM-5.3 Model Challenges U.S. Competitors in Coding Benchmarks

source.summary: A study by the University of Jaén in Spain found that semi-transparent photovoltaic modules can reduce greenhouse temperatures by up to 5°C and lower water losses by up to 60%. The research compared cadmium telluride (CdTe) and amorphous silicon (a-Si) modules installed on experimental greenhouses, revealing that both technologies created cooler, more humid environments. CdTe modules transmitted 50% of solar radiation, while a-Si modules transmitted 20%. The study also noted that CdTe allowed more beneficial wavelengths for photosynthesis to pass through, suggesting spectral quality is as important as transparency. The findings highlight potential economic benefits for greenhouse operators through reduced energy costs and irrigation needs.
source.title: Semi-transparent PV reduces greenhouse temperatures by up to 5 C

source.summary: Sun Drops Energia, a subsidiary of KPI Green Energy, has agreed to acquire up to 100% of DMGEL for ₹55.80 crore through a share-swap deal. The transaction involves purchasing 1,70,84,853 shares at ₹32.66 each, with Sun Drops issuing CCPS as consideration. Completion is targeted by September 30, 2026, pending shareholder approvals. DMGEL, a renewable energy firm based in Ahmedabad, reported ₹213.98 crore revenue in FY 2025-26. The deal is classified as a related-party transaction due to Dr. Faruk G. Patel's 8.95% stake in DMGEL. An independent valuation report supports the arm’s-length nature of the transaction.
source.title: KPI Green Energy Subsidiary Acquires Stake in DMGEL for ₹55.80 Crore

source.summary: Iran-backed hackers caused a UK power plant to shut down for four days in July, according to reports in The Sunday Telegraph and The Guardian. The UK government stated the incident involved a small-scale generator and posed no risk to the national energy system. Cyber experts warned the attack highlights growing threats to critical infrastructure and signals an escalation in the Iran conflict. The UK government emphasized its resilient energy system and collaboration with the sector to enhance security.
source.title: Iran-linked hackers disrupt UK power plant for four days

source.summary: Oman's Nama Power and Water Procurement Company (PWP) has issued an RFP to select a consultancy for a renewable energy feasibility study in Musandam Governorate. The study will evaluate solar PV, wind, hybrid systems, and energy storage technologies to support the region's future energy needs. Tender documents are available from August 24 to September 3, 2026, with a submission deadline of September 24, 2026. SMEs with a Riyada card can access documents for free. Bidders must provide a bank guarantee or certified cheque equivalent to 1% of the tender value.
source.title: Oman's PWP seeks consultancy for Musandam renewable energy study

source.summary: Low Carbon's Beacon Fen Energy Park has received planning approval for a 400 MW solar plant paired with a 600 MW battery storage system in England. The project, located near Sleaford, is expected to start construction in 2027 and reach full operation in the early 2030s. It will connect to the same substation as a nearby solar project approved in 2025. The approval marks a significant step for Low Carbon and reflects continued government support for large-scale solar projects. The Department for Energy Security and Net Zero granted the consent, following a review process for projects exceeding 100 MW capacity.
source.title: Low Carbon's 400 MW solar project with 600 MW battery gets UK approval

source.summary: Iran's economy minister warned of a strong response to U.S. sanctions, stating Tehran is 'fully prepared' for the measures. The U.S. Treasury announced 'Operation Economic Outcast,' targeting Iran's trade partners and sanctioning 60 entities, including oil-related assets. Analysts noted the U.S. avoided targeting major Chinese financial institutions to prevent retaliation. China remains Iran's largest crude buyer, though exports have dropped due to the Strait of Hormuz crisis. Oil prices fell slightly but stayed above pre-war levels.
source.title: Iran Warns of Retaliation Amid U.S. Sanctions Expansion

source.summary: Battery storage developers in Australia are experiencing declining revenues as arbitrage spreads narrow, according to experts at the Battery Asset Management Summit Australia 2026. Matt Grover of Fluence noted that many business cases built on assumptions of rapid coal plant closures are now feeling the financial strain. He described the current situation as a short-term market cycle rather than a structural issue. Thomas Schmitz of Aquila Clean Energy APAC highlighted that battery storage systems function similarly to peaker plants, which operate at low capacity factors. He warned against overreliance on projected FCAS revenue in financial models. The panel criticized the federal government's Capacity Investment Scheme, arguing it introduces unnecessary complexity and risks. Experts also discussed shifting contract structures and the challenges of aligning investor expectations with battery operational realities. AI's role in trading was downplayed, with a focus on established operations research methods for optimization.
source.title: Battery storage developers face revenue decline as coal plant closures delay

source.summary: The Federation of Bosnia and Herzegovina (FBiH) has signed an agreement with European Energy Exchange AG (EEX) to use a registry for issuing guarantees of origin (GOs) for electricity. This marks a key step toward establishing a modern GO system. The Operator za OIEiEK stated next steps will involve preparing the registry for use and creating conditions for full operational implementation. GOs verify electricity generation from renewable sources. EEX reported that total traded volume of GO Futures exceeded 100 TWh since launch, with over 60 TWh traded in 2026 alone. The agreement follows 12 years of preparations, aiming to enhance transparency and align FBiH with the European energy market amid decarbonization efforts.
source.title: FBiH signs agreement to implement guarantees of origin registry

source.summary: The U.S. is advancing its critical minerals strategy with significant investments and international partnerships, while the EU faces criticism for its slow pace and bureaucratic hurdles. Bernd Schaefer, a European industry representative, praised the U.S. for its decisive approach, contrasting it with the EU's hesitancy and over-administration. The EU has attempted to fast-track key projects but faces challenges like lengthy approval times and local opposition, exemplified by the Serbian Jadar lithium project. Meanwhile, the U.S. has secured supply deals globally, outpacing the EU's regulatory focus on methane reduction and packaging. Analysts note the EU risks becoming as reliant on the U.S. for critical minerals as it is on China, highlighting the need for faster action in Brussels to remain competitive.
source.title: U.S. Outpaces EU in Critical Minerals Investments

source.summary: Tesla's Robotaxi service has drawn complaints from users, including Tesla ambassadors and owners, over routing errors and missed pickups. Reggie Overton, a self-described Tesla Ambassador, reported a 2.3-mile trip estimated at 66 minutes that ended with him needing to call an Uber. A four-time Tesla owner documented multiple incidents, including being dropped off miles from his destination and a Robotaxi getting stuck in the middle of the road. Tesla's support was unable to reroute vehicles or provide refunds, prompting users to criticize the service. The article highlights ongoing issues with Tesla's autonomous driving technology, noting that human intervention is still required for many tasks. The service's limited geofences and low mileage suggest it is not yet ready for widespread use. The article also notes that Tesla's response to complaints appears to be reactive, with refunds only provided after public attention.
source.title: Tesla ‘Robotaxi’ sold a 66-minute 2.3-mile ride and left a rider 3 miles from his destination

source.summary: Hutchison Ports Pakistan is investing $76 million to deploy over 70 electric terminal tractors and additional electric equipment at its Karachi container terminal. The initiative includes 20 new e-trucks by October 2024 and 50 more by the end of 2027. The investment also covers electric material handlers, cranes, and trailers. The Westwell E-Truck, built in China, features a powerful electric motor and a 282 kWh battery, offering a range of 150 km and fast charging capabilities. The company reported positive performance from its initial electric trucks, driving the expansion of its decarbonization plan.
source.title: Hutchison Ports Pakistan invests $76M to deploy 70 electric trucks and equipment

source.summary: Crude oil inventories in Cushing, Oklahoma, dropped below 20 million barrels from June 19 to July 10, approaching tank bottom levels. Tank bottoms refer to the minimum volume needed for storage facilities to operate, distinguishing working storage capacity from shell capacity. The EIA is reviewing a pilot study to better understand these minimum levels. The WTI-Cushing price spread turned negative in mid-June, indicating tight market conditions. Storage facilities cannot fully deplete inventories due to operational limits, making some barrels inaccessible even when not empty.
source.title: Crude Oil Storage Levels Near Tank Bottoms in Cushing

source.summary: Petroleum markets in the second quarter of 2026 were marked by volatility due to disruptions through the Strait of Hormuz, leading to higher crude oil prices and increased U.S. refinery activity. Brent crude prices fluctuated between $72 and $118 per barrel, influenced by geopolitical tensions and the signing of a U.S.-Iran MOU. U.S. refinery margins and production rose, with distillate and jet fuel exports reaching record highs. The disruptions prompted global buyers to seek alternative supply sources, boosting U.S. exports and refinery runs.
source.title: Strait of Hormuz disruptions drive volatile oil prices and increased U.S. exports

source.summary: Van Oord has finished installing all 111 monopiles for the 1.5GW Baltica 2 offshore wind farm in Poland, a project developed by a PGE and Ørsted joint venture. The phase involved placing 107 turbine foundations and four substation foundations, completed safely and on schedule. The monopiles, up to 100m long and weighing 1,900t, were installed using Van Oord’s specialist vessels. The project aims to supply renewable energy to 2.5 million Polish homes and support the country’s energy security. Work continues on secondary structures, with full commercial operation expected by 2027.
source.title: Van Oord completes monopile installation for Baltica 2 wind farm in Poland

source.summary: Pakistani Field Marshal Asim Munir met with Iranian officials in Tehran, including President Masoud Pezeshkian and Supreme National Security Council Secretary Mohsen Rezaei, amid stalled peace negotiations with the United States. Analysts suggest Munir's success hinges on persuading Iran's military leadership, which includes General Ali Abdollahi and IRGC commander Ahmad Vahidi, to return to talks. While Iranian officials expressed skepticism toward the U.S., they did not offer new concessions. The visit coincided with U.S. threats of economic sanctions and potential military action against Iran. Munir's role is seen as critical due to his direct access to Iran's top military decision-makers, a key advantage over other mediators like Oman. Analysts note the growing influence of Iran's security establishment in shaping war and peace decisions, with Rezaei and Vahidi seen as central to any political resolution.
source.title: Pakistani General Asim Munir Mediates Talks with Iranian Military Leaders Amid War Deadlock

source.summary: Sliman Mansour, a leading Palestinian artist known for his resistance-themed works, has died at 79 after a long illness, his family announced. Born in 1947 in Birzeit, Mansour became a key figure in Palestinian art, using symbols of land and memory to depict the Palestinian narrative. His work blended ancient regional influences with Arab and Islamic art, while reflecting everyday life in Palestinian villages. During the first Intifada, he co-founded the New Vision group, using locally sourced materials after boycotting Israeli supplies. Mansour's art was seen as a visual archive of the Palestinian cause, capturing the homeland's essence through his brushwork.
source.title: Palestinian artist Sliman Mansour, giant of resistance art, dies aged 79

source.summary: Leonid Radvinsky, the late owner of OnlyFans, received more than $700m in dividends before his death from cancer in March 2026. Fenix International Ltd, which owns OnlyFans, reported $714m in pre-tax profit for the year ending November 2025. The company paid $535m in dividends for that period and an additional $174m by March 2026. Radvinsky, who bought the platform in 2018, died at 43. OnlyFans, known for its adult content, has 132 million paying subscribers and 2.5 million active creators. The platform faces regulatory scrutiny over content and age verification issues, with a £1m fine from Ofcom. OnlyFans CEO Keily Blair stated the company has paid over $30bn to creators since its launch.
source.title: OnlyFans owner received over $700m in dividends before death

source.summary: The Guardian investigates the sardine industry's profitability as demand surges due to viral trends, despite a collapse in Morocco's sardine stock. Influencers promoted sardines as a health trend, while sardinecore became a fashion trend. This has led to shortages in supermarkets. The article explores who benefits from the boom, its impact on local fishermen, and sustainability challenges amid global heating.
source.title: Sardine industry profits as demand rises amid stock collapse

source.summary: Global Energy Monitor reports the US is building twice as much gas-fired power capacity as China, driven by AI datacenter demand. This surge, with 76% more under-construction projects in the first half of the year, has increased US gas power capacity by 50% to 378GW. Around half of this new capacity is linked to datacenters requiring significant electricity for AI operations. The shift to gas, rather than renewables, could increase US power emissions by up to 20%. Analysts warn this locks in decades of pollution and volatile fuel costs. Meanwhile, the Trump administration has supported datacenter construction, reducing environmental reviews to expedite projects, despite growing local opposition and climate concerns.
source.title: US Expands Gas-Fired Power for AI Datacenters, Outpacing China

source.summary: The U.S. Treasury Secretary Scott Bessent has launched a new sanctions campaign against Iran, aiming to cut off all economic lifelines to the regime. This follows a protracted conflict with Iran that has damaged the global economy and weakened Trump's leverage. Analysts suggest that while sanctions may pressure Iran, the regime has historically bypassed them through smuggling. The Trump administration's strategy faces challenges, particularly with China, which remains a major buyer of Iranian oil. China's cooperation is critical, but it has resisted unilateral sanctions. Meanwhile, Iran's economy is suffering under the U.S. naval blockade, with citizens reporting severe shortages and financial strain. Iranian officials argue that the economic pressure is more damaging than the war itself, and they threaten retaliation against countries joining the U.S. sanctions.
source.title: U.S. Economic Sanctions on Iran Aim to Weaken Regime Amid Regional Tensions

source.summary: A study by David Neumark and Emma Wohl finds minimum wages negatively affect employment, hours, and earnings of low-wage workers in poor and low-income families. Using data from the Survey of Income and Program Participation, the researchers report adverse effects rather than benefits. The findings suggest minimum wages do not reduce poverty, as they harm employment outcomes for these workers. The study does not show a stronger impact on the poorest workers, but the overall effects contribute to the lack of poverty reduction from minimum wage policies.
source.title: Minimum Wages Linked to Lower Employment for Low-Income Workers

source.summary: Indumati Thapa, a 87-year-old widow, and other Gurkha families in Reading face financial hardship due to pensions based on Nepalese living costs, which are significantly lower than those in the UK. The government acknowledges their service but has not adjusted pensions to reflect British living standards. Labour MPs are pushing for reforms, while many elderly Gurkhas rely on family for support. Some, like Devisara Rana, wish to return to Nepal but fear they cannot afford the trip. The Ministry of Defence reaffirms its commitment to supporting Gurkha veterans and their families.
source.title: Gurkha families seek pension reform after decades of service

source.summary: The Federal Reserve Board has issued a prohibition order against James Burns, former chief lending officer of Heritage State Bank in Lawrenceville, Illinois, due to appraisal-related lending misconduct. The enforcement action was announced on July 16, 2026. The board did not provide further details on the specifics of the misconduct or the consequences of the prohibition order.
source.title: Federal Reserve Prohibits Former Bank Lending Officer Over Appraisal Misconduct

source.summary: The Federal Reserve Board released minutes from its discount rate meetings on June 8 and June 17, 2026. The documents detail the process used to determine discount rates for depository institutions through the discount window. The Board emphasized that this process differs from the Federal Open Market Committee's approach to setting the federal funds rate target range. The minutes were made public for release on July 14, 2026.
source.title: Federal Reserve Releases Discount Rate Meeting Minutes for June 2026

source.summary: Citi Trends reported GAAP EPS of -$0.11, beating expectations by $0.21, and revenue of $211.63M, exceeding forecasts by $3.26M. The company raised its 2026 comparable store sales growth forecast to 9%-11% and total sales growth to 10%-12%. It also increased its gross margin expansion outlook to 50–70 basis points and adjusted EBITDA to $38M–$42M. Citi Trends reduced new store openings from 25 to 20 but increased remodels to 60–65 from 50.
source.title: Citi Trends Raises 2026 Sales and EBITDA Forecasts, Reduces New Store Openings

source.summary: A failed assassination attempt on Bolivian lawyer Nadia Beller, orchestrated by her ex-boyfriend Fernando Cerimedo, has revealed the extent of US influence in Latin American politics. Cerimedo, a key advisor to Bolivian President Rodrigo Paz and linked to Trump-aligned leaders, was arrested after the attack. Beller accused him of domestic violence and corruption, claiming he was a CIA agent. Cerimedo faces charges of attempted femicide and money laundering. His role in political campaigns and disinformation operations, including bot farms, highlights the US's covert strategies in the region. The incident underscores the broader US strategy, dubbed the Donroe Doctrine, which seeks to reshape Latin American politics through influence and manipulation.
source.title: Bolivian Lawyer's Attack Exposes US Influence in Latin America

source.summary: A gang coalition in Haiti carried out a violent attack overnight, resulting in at least 47 deaths and 22 injuries in a neighborhood near Port-au-Prince, according to the UN. The attack has sparked anger over the lack of protection from repeated deadly incidents.
source.title: Haiti Gang Coalition Launches Violent Attack

source.summary: Professor Ronita Bardhan from the University of Cambridge emphasizes that thermal safety is a critical issue involving biology, physiology, and urban design. She highlights the importance of immediate cooling solutions during extreme heat events, stressing the need for both adaptation and mitigation strategies. Bardhan argues that protecting human life should be the priority, with access to shade, hydration, and cooling centers being essential. She also notes the interconnected nature of thermal safety with public health, energy security, and inequality.
source.title: Professor Discusses Thermal Safety and Its Implications for Public Health

source.summary: One month after a megafire destroyed much of a French town, residents have come together in unprecedented solidarity. Local authorities reported widespread community support, with neighbors helping each other rebuild. Volunteers organized efforts to clear debris and assist affected families. The town's mayor praised the collective spirit as a testament to resilience. Despite the destruction, the community remains focused on recovery and unity.
source.title: French town shows solidarity one month after devastating megafire

source.summary: Australia's music industry has banned AI-generated songs from its official charts, requiring tracks to be 'substantially human made'. The Australian Recording Industry Association (ARIA) argues this move protects the human nature of artistry as AI-generated music becomes more prevalent. The decision follows controversy over an AI-assisted cover of Madonna's 'Like A Prayer' that reached No. 1 on the ARIA dance chart. Under new rules, artists can use AI tools but must have written the song and performed the lead vocal. ARIA chief Annabelle Herd emphasized that unlicensed AI output would undermine the recorded music industry. Meanwhile, a study found 38.5% of global music released in July 2026 involved AI, with 23.2% fully AI-generated. Spotify plans to label AI-generated artists with an 'AI Persona' badge starting in September 2026. The Velvet Sundown, an AI-generated band, gained over a million monthly listeners on Spotify, highlighting the growing influence of AI in music.
source.title: Australia bans AI-generated music from official charts

source.summary: The UK government has announced a £10bn initial investment in a mix of subsidised housing in England, with 60% allocated to social renting. This aligns with the Starmer government's policy and marks a shift from Andy Burnham's earlier proposal to dedicate the entire £39bn Affordable Homes Programme to council housing. The plan includes building 70,000 homes outside London, with the remaining £6bn for London to be allocated later. The government aims to construct 300,000 affordable homes over the next decade through 33 strategic partners, including three local councils for the first time. Critics, including the Greens, accuse Burnham of backtracking on his commitment to council housing. Meanwhile, Burnham plans a trip to the US to lobby for Ukraine's access to Patriot missiles, and Reform UK has proposed evicting social housing tenants who fail to maintain their properties.
source.title: UK government announces housing plan with 60% social renting, Burnham revises earlier pledge

source.summary: The USS Abraham Lincoln, a US Navy aircraft carrier, will dock in Thailand next week after a 200-day deployment in the Middle East during the Iran war, according to a Thai official. The ship, which has 5,000 sailors and marines, set a record for consecutive days at sea, with reports of deteriorating conditions, mental health concerns, and logistical issues aboard. A sailor's wife told the Guardian that her husband's messages showed less hope and exhaustion. Democratic lawmakers have criticized the Pentagon over these conditions. Meanwhile, Trump defended the ship's maintenance, dismissing reports of poor conditions as fake news. Canada announced it would retaliate against US tariffs, while political developments in South Carolina and Oklahoma unfolded.
source.title: USS Abraham Lincoln docks in Thailand after 200-day Middle East deployment

source.summary: Israeli Defense Minister Israel Katz has declared that kites and balloons from Gaza will be treated as security threats, comparable to drones, despite no evidence of explosives. The move follows recent sightings of kites crossing into Israeli territory, raising concerns in communities affected by the October 7 attack. Netanyahu warned of targeted assassinations against those responsible, while Hamas accused Israel of using the issue to justify further aggression. Military inspections found no dangerous material on recovered kites, but Israeli officials continue to view them as potential threats. Gazans see kite flying as a rare form of recreation amid ongoing conflict and displacement.
source.title: Israeli defense minister labels Gaza kites as security threats akin to drones

source.summary: Pediatricians recommend resetting children's sleep schedules before the school year begins to improve focus and learning. Dr. Gabrina Dixon emphasizes the importance of adequate sleep for cognitive function, noting varying sleep needs by age. Experts suggest gradually shifting bedtimes earlier, avoiding heavy meals and screens before bed, and incorporating relaxing activities. Parents are advised to adjust routines based on their child's needs, with examples of practical strategies. Sleep anxiety is addressed through open communication and gradual exposure to school-related activities. Experts stress the importance of starting the new routine with patience and reassurance.
source.title: Pediatricians advise adjusting children's sleep schedules for back-to-school transition

source.summary: The TVK government in Tamil Nadu has canceled the proposed SIPCOT industrial park at Valapatti following strong opposition from local farmers. Minister Lokesh Tamilselvan announced the project will be relocated to Lathuwadi within the same district. This move marks the third major infrastructure initiative from the previous DMK regime to be scrapped or altered by the current administration. The decision highlights a recurring political pattern where incoming regimes review projects launched by preceding governments amidst local protests.
source.title: TVK Cancels Namakkal SIPCOT Project After Farmer Protests

source.summary: Prime Minister Narendra Modi received Uzbekistan's 'Oliy Darajali Do'stlik' Order, marking his 36th international award since 2016. During talks with Uzbek President Shavkat Mirziyoyev, the leaders elevated bilateral ties to a comprehensive strategic partnership. They agreed to an annual trade target of $5 billion by 2030, up from the current volume of over $1 billion. The two nations also signed 11 agreements covering mining, tourism, and a long-term uranium supply framework.
source.title: PM Modi receives 36th international honour as India-Uzbekistan trade targets $5B

source.summary: Former Wrestling Federation of India president Brij Bhushan Singh stated that sexual harassment allegations against him have elevated his status. Speaking at a felicitation ceremony in Mahendragarh, he compared the situation to the story of Kaikeyi and Ram. Singh noted that while some wrestlers received significant farewells, their current value is negligible. He defended his past decisions to protect junior wrestlers, arguing that reversing them would have harmed those without influence.
source.title: Brij Bhushan Singh claims harassment allegations made him a hero

source.summary: Indian Army Aviation pilots performed a daring casualty evacuation at 18,600 feet in Ladakh's Zanskar range. The Fire & Fury Corps stated that the team stripped the helicopter of non-essential gear to fly in severe winds with no landing space. Pilots maintained a perilous hover, touching down on one skid on a steep, snow-covered slope. This mission highlights the corps' unique capability to operate mechanized forces in extreme high-altitude environments.
source.title: Indian Army pilots execute high-altitude helicopter rescue in Ladakh

source.summary: The Worli Police Camp Sarvajanik Ganeshotsav Mandal began its 77th Ganeshotsav celebrations today with a grand procession. Police personnel and traffic cops enthusiastically welcomed the 'Mumbai Polisancha Raja' idol from Gansankul to the camp. The event featured traditional dhol-tasha beats and devotional chants, creating a festive atmosphere of devotion.
source.title: Worli Police Camp Begins 77th Ganeshotsav With Grand Idol Procession

source.summary: India Women defeated Thailand Women by 94 runs in the T20 Asia Cup after setting a target of 160. Shafali Verma scored 64 off 36 balls to help India reach 159/9. Indian spinners Deepti Sharma and Shree Charani took three and two wickets respectively, while Nandani Sharma claimed three wickets for Thailand. Thailand collapsed to 65/16.1 in their chase.
source.title: India Women defeat Thailand Women by 94 runs in T20 Asia Cup

source.summary: The Mumbai Suburban Collector issued a notification allowing sarvajanik Ganeshotsav mandals to use loudspeakers until midnight on four specific days in 2026. The permitted dates are September 15, 18, 19, and 25, covering the period from 6 am to 12 midnight. This exception applies only to these four days, while other festival days remain subject to standard noise pollution rules. The permission is conditional on maintaining noise limits and adhering to Bombay High Court orders.
source.title: Mumbai mandals granted midnight loudspeaker permission on four 2026 Ganpati visarjan days

source.summary: The Uttarakhand Pradesh Congress Committee will lodge FIRs across all districts on Monday regarding a purification ritual at Haldwani's Ramlila Ground. Congress president Mallikarjun Kharge alleged the act violated the SC/ST Act after his August 8 rally. Rahul Gandhi demanded immediate legal action, while BJP MP Sudhanshu Trivedi denied any caste angle. Senior leaders, including Kumari Selja, are expected to participate in a major protest in Dehradun on September 7.
source.title: Uttarakhand Congress files police complaints over purification ritual row

source.summary: Police in Mumbai arrested a 45-year-old woman after she allegedly ran over an eight-year-old boy while talking on her phone. The victim died at Holy Family Hospital following severe injuries from the collision. Authorities registered a case against the driver, identified as Megha Rawal, under multiple sections of the Bharatiya Nyaya Sanhita and the Motor Vehicles Act. Further investigation is currently underway.
source.title: Mumbai police arrest woman who killed boy while driving distracted

source.summary: Retired schoolteachers Anukul Poddar and Reba Roy Poddar returned from Nepal on Sunday after narrowly avoiding a flash flood. Their tour manager received disaster news and reversed the vehicle just before reaching the affected area. The couple chose to return by train rather than fly due to fear of traveling through the disaster zone. Another retired couple from the same district remains untraced.
source.title: Retired Bengal couple recounts narrow escape from Nepal flood

source.summary: Bengaluru's commercial real estate market is experiencing significant delays between securing statutory clearances and starting construction. Developers attribute these bottlenecks to the administrative transition from BBMP to the Greater Bengaluru Authority, which has slowed approval processes. Mid-stream rule changes and idle contractors have increased costs and uncertainty for projects. While office demand remains strong with vacancy rates declining, the approval stage continues to lock up capital before construction begins. Experts suggest that better coordination between authorities and digital scrutiny could improve predictability and execution timelines.
source.title: Bengaluru commercial projects face approval delays squeezing new supply

source.summary: The article argues that microfinance has failed to deliver promised economic independence for many low-income households in Asia. Experts state that flawed assumptions about capital access and entrepreneurial potential often lead to ineffective policy interventions. Evidence from India suggests loans frequently boost existing businesses instead of creating new ones, while high interest rates in places like Bangladesh strain borrowers. Research indicates that multiple loans often result in debt juggling rather than productive investment, leaving families financially vulnerable. Additionally, the sector's shift toward using land as collateral risks putting farmers' primary assets at risk. The authors conclude that broader support for skills and infrastructure is essential, noting that debt is inappropriate for households lacking sustainable returns.
source.title: Microfinance loans often increase debt rather than creating economic freedom for the poor

source.summary: NSE cash market volumes fell to a five-month low in August amid uncertainty over the new Closing Auction Session mechanism. Average daily turnover dropped 3 per cent to ₹1,16,579 crore as sharp index swings and profit-booking dampened investor appetite. SEBI introduced the CAS framework on August 3 to determine official closing prices for 208 stocks. Former SEBI Chairman UK Sinha suggested better preparation was needed but expects the system to stabilize. Analysts noted that while the BSE saw a recovery, the NSE remains more affected by the disruption.
source.title: NSE cash volumes hit five-month low as CAS swings unsettle investors

source.summary: Prime Minister Narendra Modi departed Tashkent for Bishkek to attend the 26th SCO Summit following a two-day state visit to Uzbekistan. He thanked President Mirziyoyev for strengthening India-Uzbekistan ties and elevated the relationship to a Comprehensive Strategic Partnership. The leaders agreed to increase bilateral trade to USD 5 billion by 2030 and cooperate on critical minerals and digital infrastructure. Modi also paid tribute to former PM Lal Bahadur Shastri and received Uzbekistan's highest honour, the Oliy Darajali Do'stlik Order.
source.title: PM Modi leaves Uzbekistan for SCO Summit after bilateral talks

source.summary: Essel Group Chairman Subhash Chandra addressed social media concerns regarding his personal insolvency by detailing repayment figures and guarantee amounts. He stated that borrowers repaid ₹3,803 crore of the ₹4,808 crore they received, leaving a balance of ₹998 crore. Chandra explained that while total personal guarantees signed amounted to ₹22,000 crore, the current claims filed by lenders stood at ₹5,311 crore. He noted that some lenders had already received full repayment but still submitted claims to the National Company Law Tribunal. The chairman clarified that the repayment plan was prepared by a court-appointed Resolution Professional and highlighted that his family sold assets to assist with repayments. Chandra expressed hope that lenders would reconcile outstanding accounts with borrowers to recover the remaining dues.
source.title: Subhash Chandra clarifies personal guarantee repayments in NCLT insolvency case

source.summary: The government will meet industry and exporters to discuss India-US trade trends. Additional Secretary Darpan Jain will chair the session. Minister Piyush Goyal will visit the US in late September for G-20 talks. India's exports to the US grew marginally to USD 87.31 billion in 2025-26. The US imposed a 10 per cent tariff on India from July 24.
source.title: Govt meets industry on India-US trade ahead of minister visit

source.summary: A review of Pratyaksha's new collection, The Mistress of Phoolpur, notes that while some stories offer interesting ideas, the overall execution falls short. The author reports that two stories, 'The Hunt' and 'Ma, Let's Fly', successfully explore themes of desire and family dynamics. However, the reviewer argues that other tales rely on clichés or fail to deliver dramatic impact. The book maps fault lines between restraint and transgression but remains highly uneven. Ultimately, the collection provides a few sparks of inspiration alongside several forgettable tales.
source.title: Review finds uneven quality in Pratyaksha's short story collection

source.summary: Northern Railway rescued more than 400 passengers and crew after incessant rain caused a hill slip between Koti and Ghumman stations. The incident exposed part of a bridge and short-terminated four incoming trains. Officials evacuated travelers using buses and a specially rescheduled train. The railway stated the operation was seamless with no complaints or refund requests.
source.title: Northern Railway rescues over 400 passengers after hill slip halts Kalka-Shimla train

source.summary: A six-year-old boy in Patna, Bihar, initiated a sit-in protest alleging police beat his parents during custody. The child, who previously joined student demonstrations, demands a meeting with Prime Minister Narendra Modi to address his grievances. Police officials stated the boy was handed to his mother for safety and advised the family to be more careful. The boy vowed to continue the protest until the Prime Minister meets him.
source.title: Six-year-old Bihar boy stages dharna over 'police excesses' against parents

source.summary: Indian equity markets closed cautiously on August 31, 2026, with the Nifty slipping 0.31% to 24,175.65 amid global concerns and volatility from the new Closing Auction Session. Sumeet Bagadia, Executive Director at Choice Broking, noted that the Nifty trades below key moving averages with a sideways bias, expecting a trading range of 24,000–24,300. He also observed that Bank Nifty remained range-bound between 57,000 and 58,000. Bagadia recommended three specific stocks for purchase on Monday: Jindal Worldwide, Manali Petrochemicals, and Andhra Sugars. He provided specific entry prices, target prices, and stop-loss levels for each pick. The article states these views are those of the analyst and not Mint, advising investors to consult certified experts before making decisions.
source.title: Sumeet Bagadia recommends three stocks under Rs 100 for Monday

source.summary: Databricks has launched Precision Mode for its Document Intelligence API, ai_extract, to improve accuracy in complex document extraction. The feature combines custom-trained models with an agentic harness, achieving state-of-the-art results across 9,000 benchmark documents. It outperforms leading frontier models like GPT-5.6 Sol by seven percentage points in accuracy. Intercontinental Exchange highlights the tool's ability to transform complex financial documents into structured data, enabling faster analysis and decision-making. The solution addresses challenges such as long documents, dense tables, and nested schemas through a chunk-and-merge approach, demonstrating robustness against common failure modes in existing models.
source.title: Databricks Introduces Precision Mode for Enhanced Document Extraction Accuracy

source.summary: Retailers are increasingly adopting AI to enhance operations, but face challenges in governing sensitive customer data and ensuring consistent AI performance. The article highlights the need for a control plane that provides a unified layer for AI systems, enabling trusted data access, cost control, and governance across the enterprise. Databricks offers such a solution through its Unity Catalog, Unity AI Gateway, Foundation Model APIs, and Genie, allowing retailers to manage AI use cases without creating new data silos. The shift from isolated AI experiments to enterprise-wide adoption requires a governance framework that supports model flexibility, data integrity, and auditability. Retailers must balance innovation with control, ensuring AI systems are grounded in trusted enterprise context while enabling teams to work efficiently.
source.title: Retailers Need AI Control Plane for Trusted Context and Governance

source.summary: A large-scale study examines Group Relative Policy Optimization (GRPO) in non-English and multilingual settings, finding that training in native languages often achieves results close to English reasoning. The research highlights strong crosslingual transfer but warns of language-specific regressions in some models. The study emphasizes the need for broad evaluation when applying RLVR beyond English, as outcomes vary significantly by model and language.
source.title: GRPO Study Shows Crosslingual Gains and Language-Specific Risks in Multilingual Training

source.summary: A constraint-aware GPU allocator improved utilization and priority-weighted output by up to 33 percentage points and 105%, respectively, compared to a FIFO scheduler on identical hardware and workloads. The improvement stemmed from reordering allocation decisions to prioritize jobs based on their value and resource needs. Real-time inference, which requires elastic allocation, and batch-like jobs, which need contiguous GPU blocks, were managed through a formal model that enforces constraints such as GPU exclusivity, demand ranges, and non-preemption. The allocator treated real-time demand as a dynamic curve rather than a fixed reservation, reclaiming idle GPUs for batch work during troughs. It also prioritized jobs across the scheduling horizon, avoiding the inefficiencies of FIFO, which left high-priority tasks waiting behind earlier arrivals. The system, which runs in 1 to 2 milliseconds on contended scenarios, demonstrated gains across five benchmark scenarios, with the strongest improvement in a training-heavy workload. The results highlight the importance of prioritizing value over simple occupancy metrics in GPU scheduling.
source.title: Constraint-aware GPU Allocator Boosts Utilization and Priority Output by 33 Percentage Points

source.summary: The open model ecosystem on Hugging Face's Hub has expanded significantly, with Qwen emerging as a dominant force. Qwen-based models now account for 151,448 derivatives, surpassing Meta's and Llama's totals. This growth is attributed to Qwen's consistent release schedule, broad model coverage, and permissive Apache 2.0 licensing. While Chinese labs like Moonshot and MiniMax focus on large, frontier models, U.S. labs such as NVIDIA and AMD emphasize hardware compatibility and optimization. The rise of local inference tools like llama.cpp has enabled developers to run large models on consumer hardware, with Qwen's GGUF downloads reaching 39.6 million monthly. Despite the dominance of small models in downloads, the frontier models are increasingly accessible through community-driven quantization and conversion efforts.
source.title: Qwen's Open Model Ecosystem Dominates with 151,448 Derivatives

source.summary: GeForce NOW has released its native Linux app, ending its beta phase, and introduced cloud optimizations to enhance gaming performance. The update supports Ubuntu 24.04 and later, with a new Flatpack repository for easier updates. The service also improved DLSS Frame Generation, reducing latency and boosting frame rates for Performance members. Additionally, Chromebook users can access GeForce RTX gaming through cloud streaming, with new owners eligible for a free year of service via Chromebook Fast Pass. Nine new games were added to the library this week.
source.title: GeForce NOW Launches Native Linux App and Optimizes Cloud Gaming for Chromebooks

source.summary: NVIDIA founder and CEO Jensen Huang is ranked No. 1 on Glassdoor’s 2026 Best CEOs list, with 99% employee approval. The ranking, based on employee feedback, highlights leaders who foster trust and culture. Glassdoor reintroduced the list after a five-year hiatus, emphasizing CEO impact on employee experience. Tech companies dominate the list, with nine tech CEOs included. NVIDIA also ranked No. 1 in Glassdoor’s Best Places to Work in Technology and AI. Employee reviews praised Huang’s leadership and the company’s collaborative culture, noting opportunities in AI innovation.
source.title: NVIDIA CEO Ranked Top CEO in 2026 by Glassdoor

source.summary: Google's AMIE (Video) system, an advanced medical AI, demonstrates expert-level performance in real-time video consultations through a randomized study with 300 live sessions and 30 board-certified physicians. The system integrates visual and auditory cues, guides patients through virtual exams, and performs diagnostic reasoning in real time. AMIE (Video) uses an asynchronous multi-agent architecture to balance conversational speed with clinical analysis. It outperformed both text-based AMIE (Text) and human physicians in physical examination and communication skills, with patient actors preferring the video interface. However, the study used professional actors in simulated settings, and real-world validation remains essential before broader clinical adoption.
source.title: Google's AMIE (Video) achieves expert-level performance in real-time clinical consultations

source.summary: Meta has introduced Muse Glimmer, a 30-billion-parameter model derived from Muse Spark, designed for on-device agentic workflows. The model is supported by ExecuTorch, which provides end-to-end execution on NVIDIA GPUs and Apple silicon. ExecuTorch allows developers to implement models in PyTorch and export them for optimized deployment across different backends. Key features include support for text and image inputs, DFlash speculative decoding, and 128K+ token context. Prebuilt PTE artifacts are available for download, and users can build their own by selecting backend, modality, and other parameters. The system enables efficient execution with performance improvements through speculative decoding, as demonstrated in benchmark results. Meta also highlights ongoing work to enhance features like cross-session prefix sharing and continuous batching for better agentic capabilities.
source.title: Meta Launches Muse Glimmer AI Model with ExecuTorch for On-Device Agentic Workflows

source.summary: PyTorch Conference North America will take place in San Jose, California, on October 20–21, 2026. Keynote speakers include leaders from Meta, NVIDIA, Google Cloud, and the PyTorch Foundation. The event will feature technical sessions and community collaboration. The PyTorch Foundation is accepting design submissions for a conference pin until August 14, with the winner receiving a complimentary ticket. Companies can also explore sponsorship opportunities to engage with the AI ecosystem.
source.title: PyTorch Conference North America Announces 2026 Keynote Speakers

source.summary: MIT researchers, led by Ju Li, have developed a stable electrolyte for sodium-metal batteries by identifying a suitable solvent. Sodium-metal batteries offer advantages over lithium-ion batteries, including greater abundance and lower cost, but face challenges with stability and fast charging. The team discovered that a small solvent molecule, DMFSA, enables both rapid ion transport and electrolyte stability. This breakthrough addresses the trade-off between speed and stability in battery performance. The research, published in Joule, introduces a new design strategy for electrolytes based on solvent size and molecular similarity, with potential applications beyond sodium batteries.
source.title: MIT Researchers Develop Stable Electrolyte for Sodium-Metal Batteries

source.summary: The U.S. Department of Commerce’s National Institute of Standards and Technology (NIST) and the Department of Energy (DOE) have signed a memorandum of understanding to collaborate on AI-driven innovation to tackle national science and technology challenges under the Genesis Mission. The initiative, led by the White House Office of Science and Technology Policy, aims to double American scientific productivity within a decade. NIST will focus on two areas: advancing AI in manufacturing productivity and securing critical infrastructure from cyberthreats. Both efforts are designed as two-year projects to deliver scalable, high-impact solutions for commercial and industrial use.
source.title: NIST and DOE Launch AI Collaboration to Address National Science Challenges

source.summary: A study by MIT and other institutions found that explainable AI methods affect non-experts and clinicians differently in skin disease diagnosis. Non-experts saw improved accuracy with AI assistance, largely due to deference to the system, while clinicians performed best without explanations. The research highlights the risks of overreliance on AI explanations, especially for less experienced users. The study suggests that explainable AI can lead to automation bias, where users follow incorrect AI recommendations. Researchers recommend approaches that encourage critical thinking rather than blind trust in AI outputs. The findings emphasize the need to tailor AI systems to user expertise to avoid errors and ensure effective healthcare outcomes.
source.title: Explainable AI impacts vary with user expertise in skin disease diagnosis

source.summary: IBM researchers led by Hari Krovi are investigating how quantum computing can offer significant speedups in solving complex differential equations. These equations, which describe phenomena ranging from fluid dynamics to financial modeling, are challenging for classical computers as systems grow in size and complexity. Krovi's team is developing quantum algorithms that map differential equations to linear systems, leveraging techniques like the HHL algorithm to achieve exponential speedups. Their work includes applications to differential algebraic equations (DAEs) in electrical circuits and integral differential equations with memory, showing potential for quantum advantage in areas like RLC circuit simulations. While current quantum methods can handle simple cases, challenges remain in solving turbulent regimes like those described by the Navier-Stokes equation. The team is also exploring future directions, including quantum SPICE-like tools and applications in materials science and epidemiology.
source.title: IBM Researchers Explore Quantum Computing's Potential in Solving Differential Equations

source.summary: The article presents a puzzle titled 'The Wheel of Buttons' from the Ponder This challenge, August 2026. The puzzle involves a game show with a wheel of buttons that can be in 'on' or 'off' states. Contestants must press a subset of buttons in each round to ensure all buttons are 'on' by the end, regardless of the wheel's random spins. The goal is to find an optimal strategy that guarantees a win in the fewest rounds. The solution is described as a sequence of natural numbers, with rounds separated by zeros. The article lists solvers who submitted correct answers, including several with asterisks indicating they solved the bonus part of the puzzle. The optimal solution sum for the puzzle is the focus, with a bonus challenge for a more complex version.
source.title: Contestants Solve Puzzle Involving Button States and Optimal Strategy

source.summary: Tuhin Chakrabarty and his team used the infini-gram tool to analyze AI-generated books and found they contain more rare expressions from existing literature compared to human-written works. Among top-selling self-published books on Amazon, those with substantial AI text had 43.2% of their text matching rare expressions from existing books, compared to 37.6% in books without AI detection. The overlap was even greater when compared to award-winning literature, with AI-heavy books showing 41.6% of text matching rare expressions. Chakrabarty's research highlights how AI models draw on distinctive language from training data, raising copyright concerns. The study also suggests that AI-generated texts may more heavily rely on unique phrasing from published works than human authors, challenging assumptions about originality in writing.
source.title: AI-generated books draw more from existing literature than human-written ones

source.summary: The Science One Framework, developed by Google Cloud researchers Rui Meng and Tomas Pfister, introduces a new verifiability system called Chain-of-Evidence (CoE) to address hallucinations in AI-generated scientific research. Current autonomous research systems often produce non-existent citations, misaligned code-text, and unverifiable results. The Science One Framework, which builds evidence chains during research, achieves zero phantom references and fully verifiable scores. It outperforms existing systems like Sakana AI's AI Scientist v2 and DeepScientist on benchmark tasks such as MLE-Bench and Parameter-Golf. The CoE Audit, an automated protocol, evaluates AI-generated papers against their code and evidence, revealing that baselines hallucinate up to 21% of references. The framework maintains method-code alignment and achieves state-of-the-art performance without compromising scientific rigor. The Science One Framework is presented as an experimental prototype, not a production-ready tool.
source.title: Science One Framework Achieves Zero Hallucinations in AI-Generated Research

source.summary: A new framework called ControlG addresses the challenge of training machine learning models to handle multiple objectives simultaneously in graph self-supervised learning. The method, inspired by industrial control systems, uses a proportional-integral-derivative (PID) controller to allocate computational resources to different objectives over time, rather than blending gradients at each step. This approach avoids conflicts between objectives and improves performance on various graph benchmarks. ControlG outperforms existing multitask methods across node classification, link prediction, and node clustering tasks, with notable gains on both homophilic and heterophilic graphs. The framework also provides interpretability, allowing users to track how computational resources are allocated during training. The work was developed by Amazon researchers and presented at the International Conference on Machine Learning (ICML).
source.title: ControlG framework improves multitask machine learning by coordinating objectives through PID control

source.summary: Microsoft's Echoverse project develops high-fidelity synthetic environments to train computer-use agents more effectively. The initiative includes twelve training worlds, ten deep domain worlds and two capability worlds, each focusing on specific UI elements like date pickers and nested filters. These environments replicate real application behavior with coherent state across screens and users, enabling agents to learn from real consequences rather than static screenshots. Trained on these worlds, a 9B model improved its performance from 36.5% to 67.1%, nearing GPT-5.4's results. The project emphasizes co-evolving the model, the world, and the verifier to iteratively improve all components. Echoverse also provides four worlds with code, data, and graders for further research.
source.title: Echoverse creates deep synthetic environments to improve computer-use agents

source.summary: EvoLib is a framework that allows AI systems to learn from their experiences by transforming raw data into an evolving library of reusable knowledge. Unlike traditional memory systems that store static experiences, EvoLib continuously refines and consolidates knowledge as new experiences arrive. The framework extracts skills from successful solutions and insights from mistakes, making them more general and applicable across tasks. Key mechanisms include consolidation, which merges similar knowledge, and a weighting system that prioritizes knowledge based on its long-term utility. Testing across mathematical reasoning, coding, and environment exploration tasks showed EvoLib outperforms existing memory approaches with more efficient token usage. The system also maintains stable performance regardless of task order, demonstrating its robustness in real-world scenarios. EvoLib represents a step toward AI systems that can continually improve and adapt after deployment, much like humans.
source.title: EvoLib enables AI to learn from evolving knowledge

source.summary: Polish prosecutors have opened a terrorism investigation into a deliberate fire at WB Electronics factory in Skarżysko-Kamienna. Authorities state the blaze, which destroyed warehouse facilities valued at least 15 million PLN, resulted from an explosive device. CCTV footage reportedly shows an individual in a balaclava entering the site. WB Group claims production will resume without delaying deliveries to the Polish armed forces. This incident follows a similar fire at an aircraft parts warehouse in Lublin within 24 hours.
source.title: Polish prosecutors launch terrorism probe after drone factory fire

source.summary: Rescuers in Nepal are using explosives to blast into a hillside near the Trishuli River, searching for over 600 workers trapped in mud-filled tunnels. The country's disaster management authority reports 939 deaths and 3,925 missing people, with roughly one in seven believed to be hydropower employees. An international team including Chinese and Nepalese military personnel is leading the operation, which experts describe as extraordinary due to massive boulders blocking access. Families express anxiety as the search continues, while authorities in Chitwan conduct temporary burials for unidentified bodies. Meanwhile, Chinese officials report 16 deaths and 546 missing in Tibet, imposing penalties on those speculating about higher casualty figures.
source.title: Nepal rescuers blast hillside to find trapped hydropower workers

source.summary: Flash floods killed at least two people and left 15 missing in Arizona's Grand Canyon National Park after torrential rains saturated the ground. The National Park Service reported that debris flows overwhelmed hikers and damaged the canyon's only water pipeline. Meteorologist Ben Knoll stated that a super El Niño pattern and human-caused climate change increased atmospheric moisture levels by 5 to 15 percent. The National Weather Service maintains a flood watch for northern and central Arizona through Monday evening.
source.title: Deadly flash floods in Grand Canyon kill two, leave 15 missing

source.summary: Donald Trump told American voters they would be to blame if they stop data centre development. He stated that China could not be happier about increased opposition to these projects. The issue is gaining traction ahead of the US midterms as energy bills rise and communities are disturbed. Trump emphasized the US is locked in an AI race with China.
source.title: Trump warns voters against halting US data centre development

source.summary: Gen. Dan Caine, chairman of the Joint Chiefs of Staff, wrote Sen. Elissa Slotkin to confirm the military has no plans to send troops to polling places during the 2026 midterm elections. The general stated the Joint Force will not use personnel to seize ballots or voting machines. Caine noted he has not received nor anticipates receiving any unlawful orders regarding the military's role in the upcoming November 2026 elections. While anxiety about potential interference remains, federal law prohibits armed federal force deployment at election locations unless necessary to repel armed enemies.
source.title: US military has no plans to send troops to the polls in November, top general says

source.summary: Novak Djokovic lost his first-round match at the US Open to Mariano Navone, marking his earliest Grand Slam exit in two decades. The 39-year-old Serbian player has now gone three consecutive years without winning a major title. Djokovic attributed his painful performance to consistent physical issues, including vomiting, cramping, and back pain exacerbated by heat and humidity. He admitted to swallowing pills and receiving medical treatment during the match before collapsing. While he has not announced retirement, his recent form raises questions about his future on the court. Fellow former top players Roger Federer and Rafael Nadal also retired after battling similar physical ailments. Djokovic remains the record holder with 24 Grand Slam singles titles.
source.title: Novak Djokovic exits US Open early amid physical struggles and three-year title drought

source.summary: Ethiopia's national dialogue concluded with delegates overwhelmingly supporting constitutional changes to create a powerful executive presidency. Critics warn the move could allow Prime Minister Abiy Ahmed to consolidate control, drawing comparisons to Turkey's system. While supporters argue the role would unify the nation, opposition parties boycotted the process, and armed groups remain excluded. The recommendations may be presented to parliament in October, though unresolved conflicts and ethnic tensions persist.
source.title: Ethiopia delegates endorse executive presidency plan amid power grab fears

source.summary: The US and Iran exchanged fire for the first time in a month, with missiles striking Iranian launchers on Larak Island and Iran retaliating against bases in Jordan and the UAE. US Central Command said it acted after detecting plans to deploy fresh mines in the Strait of Hormuz. In response, the Islamic Revolutionary Guard Corps claimed to have targeted US airbases in Jordan, causing heavy damage, while the UAE intercepted a drone. President Trump threatened further action, calling Iran a failed nation. Iranian President Masoud Pezeshkian stated that continuing the war is not in Iran's interest and remains ready to implement a mediated memorandum of understanding. Independent tracking agency Tanker Trackers reported Iranian crude exports have been at zero for some time. US Treasury Secretary Scott Bessent claimed Iran is lashing out kinetically because it is losing economically due to fresh sanctions.
source.title: Trump threatens further action after US and Iran exchange fire in Hormuz

source.summary: Federal officials from the Fraud Detection and National Security Directorate are interviewing witnesses regarding Alexandra Lozano, who faces two class-action lawsuits over immigration fraud. Agents in Seattle aim to present a case to a grand jury for potential criminal charges, though Lozano has not yet been charged. The investigation follows allegations that Lozano misled clients, used false information in applications, and enriched herself through fees ranging from $10,000 to $25,000 per case. When she surrendered her law license in May, approximately 54,000 immigration cases were left in limbo. One lawsuit details how a client named Severo López Contreras was detained by ICE after Lozano failed to file his T visa application despite collecting $17,500. Attorneys representing 34 plaintiffs state that Lozano remains silent while her clients face deportation risks.
source.title: Federal agents investigate Alexandra Lozano after 54,000 immigration cases remain unresolved

source.title: Messi announces retirement from international football

source.summary: Frank Furedi resigned as executive director of MCC Brussels on Monday due to persistent failures to pay contractually agreed funds. A spokesperson confirmed no staff in the EU capital received wages in July or August. The thinktank, an offshoot of the Mathias Corvinus Collegium Foundation, launched in late 2022 to influence political debate. Furedi stated the organization effectively ceased operations and could not pay suppliers or meet Belgian insolvency law conditions. He plans to ensure the institution's intellectual legacy continues in another form with like-minded individuals.
source.title: Frank Furedi resigns as head of Viktor Orbán's MCC Brussels over unpaid wages

source.summary: Prime Minister Benjamin Netanyahu and right-wing ministers celebrated the discovery of the Altalena shipwreck, a 1948 vessel sunk during a confrontation between the Israeli army and the Irgun militia. The event has become a focal point for political debate ahead of legislative elections in October. While Netanyahu described the find as an emotional moment, critics argue the timing serves to incite against his political opponents. Historians note the incident nearly sparked a civil war, with Menachem Begin preventing further violence. Experts question the feasibility of raising the 18,000-ton ship, calling the recovery promise a publicity stunt. The discovery has reignited historical tensions between Israel's left and right factions.
source.title: Netanyahu uses Altalena wreck discovery to target left before elections

source.summary: Hungarian Prime Minister Péter Magyar told the Bled Strategic Forum that the European Union faces a leadership crisis and must decide whether to survive or win. He criticized Brussels' bureaucracy for stifling initiatives and highlighted unfair daily migration fines against Hungary. Magyar noted that while the EU focuses on internal questions, China is investing in European infrastructure. He also mentioned his government's recent agreement to release frozen funds after meeting Recovery Fund milestones.
source.title: Hungarian PM Magyar urges EU to choose survival or victory amid leadership crisis

source.summary: The Grand Canyon faces renewed storm threats after a flash flood killed one person and left 15 missing. The National Weather Service warns dangerous conditions persist through Monday due to saturated soils. Authorities suspended overnight stays and tightened water conservation measures after the Transcanyon Waterline was destroyed. More than 60 people were evacuated by helicopter while crews assess damage to trails and infrastructure.
source.title: Grand Canyon braces for more storms after deadly flash flood

source.summary: India's Ministry of External Affairs rejected a Permanent Court of Arbitration ruling regarding the Indus Waters Treaty, citing a lack of jurisdiction. The MEA stated the court was illegally constituted and its award has no effect on India's sovereign decisions. India maintains its decision to hold the treaty in abeyance remains in force. The court ordered India to observe treaty obligations and imposed measures on the Ratle Hydro-Electric Plant until July 2027.
source.title: India rejects Permanent Court of Arbitration ruling on Indus Waters Treaty

source.summary: Singapore is advancing a national climate adaptation plan while simultaneously approving the clearing of secondary forests for housing. Residents and scientists argue that environmental impact assessments fail to account for the climate and health benefits of these forests. The government plans to proceed with development at Maju Forest and Gillman Barracks, though it will retain more greenery than originally proposed. Experts warn that forest loss could increase urban heat and flood risks, contradicting the city's "city in nature" vision. While Singapore has committed billions to engineered defenses like seawalls, conservationists contend that planting saplings cannot replace the ecosystem services of mature forests.
source.title: Singapore clears forests for housing despite climate adaptation spending

source.summary: The provided text contains an error message regarding a failed site load and does not include the article body or headline details. Consequently, no summary of the reported event can be generated from the available source text.
source.title: Sweden signs €4.3 billion deal to acquire four French frigates

source.summary: Lionel Messi announced his retirement from international soccer on Monday after 20 years representing Argentina. The 39-year-old stated the decision hurt deeply but felt the time had come. He concluded his career as Argentina's all-time leading scorer with 125 goals. Messi explained he delayed publishing his letter due to his father's recent death. He will continue playing for Inter Miami while supporting Argentina from the sidelines.
source.title: Lionel Messi announces retirement from international soccer for Argentina

source.summary: Health authorities in the Democratic Republic of Congo reported 6,041 confirmed Ebola cases and 2,911 deaths as of August 31. The World Health Organization describes this outbreak as the largest in the country's history, driven by the rare Bundibugyo strain. Insecurity and a health worker strike hinder response efforts across six provinces. The case fatality ratio stands at approximately 48 percent, though more than 1,360 people have recovered.
source.title: DRC Ebola cases exceed 6,000 as death toll approaches 3,000

source.summary: Gerard A. Akindes argues that FIFA's financial support has increased African football's dependency rather than fostering sustainable autonomy. The author notes that while Gianni Infantino's programs have injected over one billion dollars since 2016, they often prioritize elite structures over grassroots development. Akindes highlights governance distortions and a lack of transparency in how funds are managed by national federations. He also points out that lucrative broadcasting rights have shifted the sport away from its role as a people's game. Ultimately, the article asserts that African football leaders must demonstrate greater independence to prioritize local needs over the global FIFA agenda.
source.title: Gerard A. Akindes questions FIFA's impact on African football development
