source.summary: Antonina Kulhava works as a humanitarian deminer for the Mines Advisory Group in Ukraine, clearing over 139,000 square kilometres of land from Russian explosives. She transitioned from finance and pastry cooking to this dangerous role, noting that women comprise only 12% of operational field deminers. Kulhava guides teams using mechanical, manual, and canine methods to remove seven types of ordnance, including drones and cluster munitions. Her work allows farmers to cultivate fields again, with sunflowers now growing where mines once lay. She attributes her confidence to experience and says the work helps people return to their homes.
source.title: Antonina Kulhava clears Russian mines in Ukraine to restore farmland

source.summary: A recent survey indicates that nearly 60% of South Koreans now support mandatory military service for women, marking a significant shift from previous taboos. The Reform Institute conducted the study, which found strong backing among both men and women across various age groups. Experts attribute this change to declining birth rates, shrinking male recruitment numbers, and growing demands for gender equality. However, Professor Hyobin Lee warns that requiring women to serve could exacerbate existing burdens related to childcare and career interruptions. Conversely, activist Song Young-Chae opposes the idea, arguing resources should instead focus on advanced technologies like drones. The government plans to revise its defense plan this autumn, addressing these personnel shortages and modernization needs.
source.title: South Korea sees rising support for mandatory military service for women

source.summary: The CFTC ordered Gabriel Perez, a former White House teleprompter operator, to pay $172,000 for betting on President Trump's speeches using inside information. Perez must surrender $107,539 in profits and pay a $65,000 penalty, with his fine reduced due to cooperation. Kalshi identified the federal employee through unusual betting patterns and reported the activity to regulators. Perez is banned from trading for three years, while the White House has not yet commented on the settlement.
source.title: Ex-White House teleprompter operator ordered to pay $172,000 for Trump speech bets

source.summary: Jai Arrow returned to the field for South Sydney in a cameo appearance against the Gold Coast Titans. The player was substituted in the opening seconds to a standing ovation. Arrow will appear again next week against the Sydney Roosters to reach his 100th NRL match.
source.title: Jai Arrow makes emotional cameo return for South Sydney against Gold Coast

source.summary: The provided text contains an error message regarding a failed site load rather than property information. No specific locations or buying advice were included in the available content.
source.title: France property buyers seek festive atmosphere locations

source.summary: Vibeke Andersen, a 53-year-old woman with paranoid schizophrenia, used virtual reality therapy to confront voices she heard for 27 years. Researchers at Copenhagen University Hospital’s VIRTU group created an avatar representing her dominant voice, allowing her to confront it directly in a controlled environment. The study, published in The Lancet Psychiatry in 2025, found that VR therapy significantly reduced hallucination severity and frequency compared to standard care. Andersen reported the voices disappeared by her final session and remained silent five years later. The treatment is considered safe and tolerable, though it may be overwhelming for some patients. Researchers plan to incorporate AI to create virtual therapists and generate personalized scenarios for broader mental health applications.
source.title: VR therapy helps schizophrenia patient silence 27 years of voices

source.summary: Funerals were held on Friday for 12 victims of wildfires in Algeria's Jijel province, with Prime Minister Sifi Ghrieb attending the services. President Abdelmajid Tebboune declared three days of national mourning following the tragedy. The death toll includes 54 injured people, as authorities noted nearly 2,000 fires occurred across the country in July alone.
source.title: Funerals held for 12 victims of Algeria's deadly wildfires

source.summary: GiveDirectly is running a $198 million trial in Malawi where 230,000 adults receive approximately $700 each. The program allows recipients to spend the funds freely, aiming to demonstrate the potential of unconditional cash transfers. Beneficiaries like 19-year-old Yonas Fote are using the money to start small businesses, such as a cinema in Kamala. The experiment seeks to show how direct cash aid can thrive local economies.
source.title: GiveDirectly tests $700 cash transfers in Malawi to boost local economies

source.summary: Billie Jean King continues her advocacy for women's sports equity 54 years after helping pass Title IX. She attributes the growth of professional women's leagues to increased visibility for young athletes. King warns that current threats to Title IX, including administrative changes and new reports, could harm girls' access to sports. She emphasizes the need to keep girls involved at the grassroots level. Despite challenges, King remains undaunted, noting that inclusion is a significant investment for society.
source.title: Billie Jean King Advocates for Women's Sports Equity Amid Title IX Challenges

source.summary: Anadolu Agency reports on major international developments including a US-Venezuela oil agreement and rising flood deaths in Nepal. The article details Russia's ICBM launch, US sanctions on Iran-linked entities, and various sports and political updates from around the world.
source.title: Trump finalizes oil deal with Venezuela amid global news roundup

source.summary: EL PAÍS reports on an interview with Edi Rama, Albania's prime minister, who identifies primarily as an artist. Rama, who has served four consecutive terms since 2013, recently exhibited new bronze sculptures in Berlin. He explained that he uses artificial intelligence to create digital models for his sculptures before refining them by hand. During his tenure as mayor of Tirana, Rama oversaw a project to paint public buildings with bright colors, a move he says improved tax collection and public safety. Now in office, he creates colorful drawings on his desk to "detoxify" the stress of politics. Rama stated that art should not change the world or pass judgment, but rather shift perspectives. He also noted that he vet all potential buyers of his work to ensure no connection to his government position.
source.title: Albanian Prime Minister Edi Rama discusses his art and political career

source.summary: Mexico is adjusting to the absence of Nemesio Oseguera Cervantes, known as El Mencho, who was killed in a military operation six months ago. Historian Enrique Guerra Manzo explains that Oseguera rose from a marijuana-growing background in Michoacán to lead the Jalisco New Generation Cartel. Authorities have arrested several key figures since his death, yet the group remains watchful and potentially led by his stepson. The article notes that the cartel's future reorganization remains uncertain as the state offensive continues. Experts describe the current situation as a volatile limbo where the old leadership has not fully died and the new has not yet emerged.
source.title: Mexico Adapts to Life Without El Mencho After Six Months

source.summary: South Africa formally accused Israel of failing to comply with three International Court of Justice orders regarding the Gaza conflict. The Department of International Relations and Cooperation submitted a dossier claiming over 10% of Gaza's population has been killed or injured. Pretoria stated it will pursue all available avenues to ensure Israel's adherence to the Genocide Convention. The submission highlighted rising casualty numbers and increased miscarriage rates since the alleged ceasefire announcement.
source.title: South Africa accuses Israel of defying ICJ orders as Gaza toll rises

source.summary: The article explores how Egypt repurposed the Suez Canal from a symbol of exploitation into a tool for emancipation. It details the historical context and strategic shifts that enabled this transformation. The narrative highlights key moments in the canal's evolution under Egyptian leadership.
source.title: Egypt transforms Suez Canal from exploitation symbol to emancipation tool

source.summary: President Donald Trump announced a new agreement with Venezuela that could grant the United States access to 65 billion barrels of oil reserves. Secretary of State Marco Rubio and Defense Secretary Pete Hegseth negotiated the deal with Venezuela's acting President Delcy Rodríguez. The arrangement allows a private company to develop 17 oil fields, giving the U.S. a 55% effective output stake and rights to purchase oil at cost. Rodríguez stated the agreement could attract $100 billion in investment and generate over $209 billion in taxes. The oil produced would fill the U.S. strategic petroleum reserve and support military use. Experts caution that significant production increases will not occur immediately due to damaged infrastructure and the time required for repairs.
source.title: Trump Announces Deal With Venezuela For 65 Billion Barrels Of Oil

source.summary: The Cockroach Janta Party (CJP) has launched a campaign to audit 100 rural government schools over two months, aiming to document facility conditions and pressure authorities for improvements. The activist group, which previously forced the resignation of Education Minister Dharmendra Pradhan, now seeks to shift from street protests to sustained local activism involving parents and volunteers. Authorities in states like Maharashtra and Rajasthan have restricted access or taken police action against volunteers, citing concerns over student safety and unauthorized inspections. While the CJP argues citizens have a right to inspect publicly funded institutions, critics question whether activists possess the expertise to assess infrastructure safely. The campaign faces legal and logistical challenges as it navigates India's complex administrative structure and varying state responses to public scrutiny.
source.title: India's CJP launches school audits to test government accountability limits

source.summary: A massive glacier collapse triggered deadly floods in Nepal and Tibet, killing at least 400 people and leaving over a thousand missing. Scientists attribute the event to climate change, which is destabilizing glaciers and permafrost globally. Experts warn that such glacier hazards will become more frequent as temperatures rise. Additionally, preliminary reports suggest Nepal's flood warning systems were ill-equipped to handle the disaster despite previous government investments.
source.title: Melting glacier caused deadly Nepal floods as climate change increases similar hazards

source.summary: Sandhya Devanathan is leaving Meta after more than a decade to join OpenAI as Vice President for Southeast Asia and Australia. OpenAI confirmed she will be based in Singapore and report to Kiran Mani. Devanathan, who brings over 25 years of experience, did not immediately disclose her joining date. She described the departure as bittersweet and expressed pride in her work at Meta.
source.title: Sandhya Devanathan leaves Meta to join OpenAI as VP for Southeast Asia and Australia

source.summary: The Students Federation of India Kerala unit criticized a Samastha circular restricting women's presence at religious events. SFI State secretary P.S. Sanjeev called the directive anti-women and out of tune with modern society. He highlighted Justice M. Fathima Beevi's 1989 appointment as evidence of Muslim women's progress. Sanjeev urged the organization to reconsider its position in 2026.
source.title: SFI Kerala unit condemns Samastha circular as anti-women

source.summary: AAP Delhi chief Saurabh Bharadwaj challenged the BJP regarding three of its Delhi Lok Sabha MPs attending a condolence meeting for Sajjan Kumar. The party asked if they would suspend the MPs for allegedly backstabbing Sikhs. This incident occurs as SAD leaders suggest a potential alliance with the BJP for upcoming Punjab assembly elections. The Times of India reported these developments on Saturday.
source.title: AAP Delhi chief questions BJP over MPs visiting Sajjan Kumar home

source.summary: U.S. Treasury Secretary Scott Bessent warned Iran of an economic D-Day, announcing new sanctions targeting Iran's trade partners. The move follows Iran's President Masoud Pezeshkian defending a memorandum of understanding with the U.S. as a path out of the stalled war. Iran vowed to shut down all oil exports from the Gulf if the economic war continues. Bessent emphasized the Trump administration's shift to economic pressure, aiming to sever Iran's economic lifelines. Iran dismissed the sanctions as desperate, with Supreme National Security Council secretary Mohsen Rezaei threatening to cut oil exports and label support for U.S. measures as an act of war. The U.S. plans to reveal more severe sanctions, while Iran's Foreign Minister Abbas Araghchi called the measures repetitive and urged respectful dialogue.
source.title: U.S. threatens Iran with economic sanctions as Tehran vows oil export shutdown

source.summary: A photo of BJP national president Nitin Navneet showing an inverted national flag has been shared on social media, but it is edited. The claim that he does not know the correct order of the flag's colors is false. The image was verified using Google Lens, matching it with official BJP website and social media accounts, confirming the flag was held correctly. A Deccan Herald report mentions BJP Delhi unit filed a complaint against the viral fake image. The conclusion is that the edited photo is being shared with misleading claims.
source.title: BJP National President's Edited Photo Showing Inverted Flag Shared on Social Media

source.summary: Young people in Beni organized a caravan to raise awareness about Ebola and address violence against response teams. The event, supported by NGOs and the WHO, followed attacks on burial teams and treatment centers. Beni, previously an Ebola epicenter, now faces a rapidly spreading outbreak that has surpassed the 2018 epidemic in deaths. Organizers linked the violence to regional insecurity and called for government support. They emphasized the need for community engagement to combat misinformation and mistrust of health workers.
source.title: Youth organize caravan to counter Ebola response violence in Beni

source.summary: Iranian Deputy Foreign Minister Mohsen Rezaei stated that the Strait of Hormuz remains closed and will not reopen until the United States changes its behavior. Meanwhile, US President Donald Trump claimed the strait as 'new American territory' on Truth Social, a claim he has made before. The strait, a critical shipping lane, has been closed since the war began, with both sides disputing control. Rezaei also warned Gulf states against joining US sanctions and threatened retaliation against those that do. Talks between Iran and Oman on regulating Hormuz traffic have stalled.
source.title: Trump claims Hormuz on Truth Social, Rezaei says 'shut until US changes'

source.summary: Australia is developing new rare earth refineries to reduce reliance on Chinese imports. The initiative aims to boost domestic processing capabilities. The government is supporting infrastructure projects in key regions. Industry experts highlight strategic importance of securing supply chains. The move is part of broader efforts to enhance mineral processing independence.
source.title: Australia expands rare earth refining capacity to challenge China

source.summary: Crude oil prices fell over 1% on Monday as investors anticipated new US sanctions against Iran, which could disrupt Middle East oil supplies. Brent crude dropped $1.22 to $93.17 per barrel, while WTI crude fell $1.20 to $85.86 per barrel. The decline followed a week of gains after US-Iran peace talks stalled, limiting oil shipments through the Strait of Hormuz. US Treasury Secretary Scott Bessent warned of 'toughest sanctions in history' against Iran, while President Trump threatened sanctions on countries trading with Tehran. A firm raised its Brent price forecast for the quarter to $86 per barrel, citing continued production disruptions and increased Chinese demand.
source.title: Oil prices drop as US prepares new sanctions against Iran

source.summary: US Ambassador Sergio Gor remarked on the chaotic nature of Indian prime-time TV news, noting that shows grow more intense as the evening progresses. He described the 10-person simultaneous speech format as unique. Gor also shared details about a planned no-questions arrangement for Modi-Trump talks at the G7 summit, which was disregarded when Trump unexpectedly invited media questions, leading to a 45-minute press session. The Indian government has not commented on the no-questions request. Gor highlighted strengthening India-US ties across trade, defense, and space, while also touching on the sensitive issue of Jammu and Kashmir, which sparked diplomatic tension with Pakistan.
source.title: US Ambassador Comments on Indian TV News Chaos and Modi-Trump Meeting

source.summary: Norway has extended the deadline for submitting licence applications for its first commercial offshore wind farm. The extension aims to provide more time for stakeholders to prepare. The original deadline was set for early 2024. The move reflects the government's commitment to renewable energy development. The wind farm is expected to contribute significantly to Norway's energy goals.
source.title: Norway extends deadline for first commercial offshore wind farm licence application

source.summary: The National Institute of Standards and Technology (NIST) has been granted a patent for a water heater system that kills Legionella pneumophila, a bacterium linked to Legionnaires’ disease. The system heats water to 70°C (160°F) to eliminate nearly all Legionella, then cools it to a safe temperature using a heat exchanger. This approach addresses the risk of bacterial growth in plumbing systems, where warm water creates ideal conditions for the bacteria to thrive. The design is energy-efficient and prevents scalding, with potential applications in larger facilities like nursing homes and hotels. NIST engineer Dave Yashar noted the system could offer a cost-effective, passive solution for preventing Legionella outbreaks.
source.title: NIST Patent Develops Water Heater to Kill Legionella Bacteria

source.summary: Kathi Zellweger, a Swiss aid worker, documented her efforts to provide relief during North Korea's severe famine in the 1990s. In Sinuiju, she visited families struggling with hunger, including Mrs. Kim and Mr. Lee, who relied on bartering for survival. The Public Distribution System had collapsed, leaving urban residents without food. Zellweger noted that markets emerged as a crucial survival mechanism, though they were tolerated only grudgingly by the government. These markets, often hidden, became a lifeline for many, despite rising prices and limited access. Zellweger's work highlighted the 'hidden famine' in North Korea, where suffering was less visible but no less real.
source.title: Kathi Zellweger's Humanitarian Work in North Korea's Famine

source.summary: Tanker traffic through the Strait of Hormuz dropped below 20 vessels over the weekend, with only four crossing on Sunday, according to Kpler data. The U.S. Treasury Secretary warned of an economic D-Day against Iran, while Iran threatened to halt all oil exports from the Persian Gulf. UK Maritime Trade Operations reported 45% of vessels passing through the strait were tankers, with oil tankers making up 56% of that total. Oil prices fell as markets anticipated U.S. economic pressure on Tehran.
source.title: Strait of Hormuz sees reduced tanker traffic amid U.S.-Iran tensions

source.summary: Kazakhstan will hold parliamentary elections on August 23, transforming its legislative body from a two-chamber to a single-chamber system. Experts suggest the ruling party, Adilet, will likely win, consolidating President Tokayev's power and weakening the legacy of former president Nursultan Nazarbayev. The new constitution allows Tokayev to seek another term in 2029 and replaces the two-chamber parliament with a single-chamber assembly. Independent candidates are barred, limiting political choice. European Union officials and experts note a lack of reaction to the political changes, citing pragmatic economic interests. Kazakhstan remains neutral in the Russia-Europe conflict, balancing relations with multiple powers while seeking to avoid over-dependence on any single nation.
source.title: Kazakhstan's parliamentary elections and political consolidation under Tokayev

source.summary: Pakistan's Army Chief, Asim Munir, met with Iranian leaders in Tehran to discuss measures to prevent conflict escalation and reopen the Strait of Hormuz, according to the army's media wing. The visit aimed to support peace efforts and de-escalate tensions in the U.S.-Iran conflict. Discussions focused on regional stability, a permanent end to instability, and ways to achieve lasting peace. The Strait of Hormuz, a critical shipping route, has been disrupted by the ongoing conflict, affecting global oil supplies. Pakistan has been a key mediator in stalled peace talks, but efforts to revive negotiations have so far failed. The U.S. continues to impose sanctions on Iran, intensifying regional pressures.
source.title: Pakistan and Iran discuss reopening Strait of Hormuz to ease West Asia tensions

source.summary: Kazatomprom's CEO, Meirzhan Yussupov, highlighted the growing demand for nuclear energy, driven by a pledge from 38 countries representing 70% of global GDP to triple nuclear power by 2050. He noted that uranium prices have reached an 18-year high and are stable, creating a strong foundation for long-term contracts. The company reported a 9% year-on-year revenue increase to KZT718 billion, attributing it to financial discipline and favorable market conditions. Yussupov emphasized the end of the 'cheap uranium' era and the need for secure, emission-free power. Kazatomprom has signed agreements with SNURDC and Uranium One for uranium sales, with details kept confidential. The company also announced amendments to Kazakhstan's Subsoil Use Code, affecting uranium mining licenses and exploration frameworks. Meanwhile, the TQZ sulphuric acid plant faces delays due to paleontological findings, pushing its commissioning date to 2027-2028 and potentially impacting production plans.
source.title: Kazatomprom Sees Shift in Uranium Market as Demand Grows

source.summary: One Nation MP David Farley incorrectly stated the party's migration policy would include an additional 100,000 annual migrants, surpassing Labor's forecast of 225,000. Party leader Pauline Hanson corrected the claim, reaffirming the policy aims to reduce net overseas migration to 130,000 annually. Barnaby Joyce acknowledged Farley's mistake, noting it was a common occurrence in political careers. Meanwhile, KPMG Australia announced plans to cut 360 employees and 27 partners following an audit scandal, citing weak demand for consulting services and a 1% revenue decline to $2.26 billion. The firm's CEO, John Sams, emphasized the need to rebuild trust and adapt to changing client expectations. In other news, Leah Stewart, a shark bite survivor, expressed gratitude for community support during her recovery, while ACOSS highlighted the disparity between jobseeker payments and the pension, calling for policy reform. Apartment rents in Australian capital cities now exceed half of a typical worker's take-home pay, prompting calls for rent protections. A man was found with critical injuries on a Melbourne walking trail, and the Alan Jones trial continued with new witness testimony.
source.title: One Nation MP's migration policy misstatement corrected; KPMG cuts staff amid audit scandal

source.summary: The family of Ann Marie Smith, an Adelaide woman who died in 2020 from severe neglect, has shared their grief in victim impact statements during a court case against her former NDIS provider. Amy June Collins, a former co-director of Integrity Care SA, pleaded guilty to reckless conduct under the Work Health and Safety Act. The court heard statements from Smith's brother and uncle, who described her suffering and the preventable nature of her death. Collins' lawyer claimed her actions were not the cause of Smith's death, blaming her carer instead. The case highlights concerns about oversight in disability care, with the family urging stronger protections for vulnerable individuals.
source.title: Family of NDIS client recounts neglect leading to death in court

source.summary: Tesla is recalling 2,740,642 Model 3 and Model Y vehicles in China to enhance driver monitoring. The recall follows Chinese regulators' findings that steering-wheel torque monitoring alone is insufficient for ensuring driver attention during assisted-driving mode. The update introduces cabin-camera monitoring to track eye contact with the road, a system previously circumvented by drivers using plastic doll heads. This recall mirrors similar actions in the U.S., where Tesla faced a 2023 recall for similar driver engagement issues. The move aligns with China's tightening regulations on automated driving features. Tesla also filed another recall for 3 million vehicles over an emergency door release mechanism, making this its largest recall in China to date.
source.title: Tesla expands driver monitoring in China with 2.7 million recall

source.summary: The PyTorch Foundation has announced a design contest for the 2026 PyTorch Conference North America flare pin. The winning design will be produced as a 1-inch die-cut soft enamel pin and the entrant will receive a complimentary conference ticket. Submissions must include the official PyTorch Foundation symbol, the year 2026, and be suitable for a professional event. Entries must be original, use official assets, and follow brand guidelines. The contest requires participants to submit designs via social media platforms with specific hashtags, and includes rules about AI use, copyright, and eligibility. The winning design will be selected by the PyTorch Foundation Marketing Committee based on originality, legibility, and brand compliance.
source.title: PyTorch Foundation Launches 2026 Flare Pin Design Contest

source.summary: UK Prime Minister Andy Burnham visited Ukraine's capital Kyiv on Independence Day, accompanied by European leaders. He plans to announce that the UK will allow MBDA, a European defense company, to share declassified information about UK-made components of the Storm Shadow/Scalp missiles. This move aims to help Ukraine develop its own long-range missile capabilities. Burnham also intends to meet with Ukrainian President Zelenskyy and chair the first meeting of the Coalition of the Willing. Ukrainian Foreign Minister Sybiha emphasized the importance of international support for Ukraine's independence.
source.title: UK PM Announces Missile Component Sharing with Ukraine During Independence Day Visit

source.summary: The Trump administration is intensifying economic pressure on Iran to push for negotiations over the Strait of Hormuz, with Treasury Secretary Scott Bessent set to outline new measures. The U.S. has already imposed extensive sanctions, which are expected to deepen Iran's distrust of the U.S. Meanwhile, the Supreme Court will decide whether Trump can continue construction on his ballroom, with the National Trust for Historic Preservation arguing that congressional approval is required. The Trump administration claims the ballroom is essential to an integrated military complex. Investors dumped stocks and bonds after government debt yields reached their highest level in nearly two decades, with the Treasury Department buying back bonds to reassure investors. The U.S. also manages wild horse populations through helicopter captures in Colorado, and new research shows positive experiences from Oregon's psychedelic industry.
source.title: Trump escalates economic pressure on Iran as SCOTUS rules on White House ballroom

source.summary: The She's Birdie is a personal safety alarm that emits a 130db siren and strobe light for up to 40 minutes when activated. The device, priced under $30, is recommended for college students, parents with young children, and older adults. The Hearing Health Foundation compares the sound level to a jackhammer. The author has used the gadget on their keychain for nearly seven years.
source.title: Personal safety alarm offers loud siren for under $30

source.summary: Teachers in the U.S. are increasingly facing harassment through AI-generated deepfakes, with educators reporting that students have created and shared sexualized images of them. Luis DeSantiago, a substitute teacher in California, discovered an AI-generated image of himself in lingerie circulating on TikTok, leading to a month-long investigation and disciplinary actions against students. Similar incidents have been reported by other teachers, including a middle school teacher who found an AI-generated TikTok account impersonating her, and a UK college counselor who faced manipulated videos of herself. Legal experts note that such content could constitute cyberstalking and violate the Take It Down Act, which criminalizes nonconsensual intimate visual depictions. Schools are struggling to address these incidents, with administrators often failing to provide clear responses or support to affected teachers. The experiences have led some educators to reconsider their relationships with students and the safety of their work environments.
source.title: Teachers Targeted by AI-Generated Deepfakes Face Legal and Emotional Challenges

source.summary: The article explores the data efficiency gap between human children and large language models (LLMs), highlighting how children can achieve fluency in language with far less data than required to train AI systems. Researchers note that while LLMs like GPT-3.1 and Llama 3.1 require trillions of words for training, a child may only need around 100 million words. This discrepancy raises questions about how children learn language so efficiently. Cognitive scientists like Michael C. Frank and Ethan Gotlieb Wilcox argue that understanding this process could lead to more data-efficient AI models, which could benefit applications like minority language chatbots. The article also discusses the debate between innate linguistic abilities and environmental learning, referencing theories from Noam Chomsky and B.F. Skinner. Competitions like BabyLM aim to test hypotheses about language acquisition by training models on smaller datasets, mimicking the learning environment of young children.
source.title: Kids outlearn AI—and we still don’t know why

source.summary: NVIDIA FLARE, an open-source framework for federated learning, addresses challenges in training vision-language models (VLMs) across distributed data sites. The system enables efficient coordination of training and aggregation of model updates, particularly for large multimodal models. FedUMM, a collaboration between William & Mary and NVIDIA, demonstrates federated lightweight adapter training over a frozen multimodal backbone, reducing communication costs. Key design decisions include what model state to federate and how to transfer and aggregate updates efficiently. NVIDIA FLARE supports both parameter-efficient and full-model communication patterns through features like tensor streaming, disk-backed aggregation, and externalization. Experiments show that adapter-only federation significantly reduces per-client communication while maintaining high model performance. The framework provides tools for defining update contracts, minimizing payloads, and evaluating end-to-end performance in federated settings.
source.title: NVIDIA FLARE Enables Efficient Federated Multimodal AI Workflows

source.summary: NVIDIA has developed SkillEvaluator, an open-source tool to measure how skills affect AI agent performance. The tool evaluates skills through static checks and real-world task runs, with results showing improvements in Correctness, Discoverability, Effectiveness, and Efficiency. Skills are verified through three tiers of evaluation, ensuring safety, distinctiveness, and live performance. The tool helps developers understand the impact of skills on agent behavior and efficiency, with examples showing significant reductions in token usage and execution time. NVIDIA publishes verified skills for use with Claude Code, Codex, and Cursor, available through Skills.sh, ClawHub, and Hermes Hub.
source.title: NVIDIA Introduces SkillEvaluator to Assess AI Agent Performance

source.summary: Databricks hosted the inaugural Grounded Reasoning Cup, a live AI competition to assess agents' ability to reason over complex enterprise document collections. Eleven academic teams, supported by industry partners like OpenAI and Google DeepMind, developed agents using the OfficeQA benchmark. On competition day, they applied their systems to the new OfficeQA Pro V2 benchmark. Stanford won with 63.3% accuracy, outperforming the average team by +22 points. The top teams used strategies like document preprocessing, targeted retrieval, and structured tool use. Despite these advances, 18.8% of questions remained unsolved. The competition highlighted the importance of holistic system design over model choice alone, with insights from Stanford, UMass, and Yale teams demonstrating varied approaches to achieving accuracy and speed in grounded reasoning tasks.
source.title: Grounded Reasoning Cup Evaluates AI Agents' Performance on Enterprise Document Tasks

source.summary: Researchers introduce MVICAD2, a method for multi-view independent component analysis that accounts for both temporal delays and dilations in brain activity data. The technique improves upon existing methods by allowing sources to vary across subjects, addressing limitations in modeling individual differences and age-related changes. The model features identifiable sources and uses regularization to enhance performance. Simulations show MVICAD2 outperforms current methods, and results on the Cam-CAN dataset demonstrate its ability to capture how delays and dilations relate to aging.
source.title: New method for analyzing brain activity with delays and dilations

source.summary: Researchers propose a specialized semismooth Newton method to improve the computational efficiency of kernel-based optimal transport estimators. These estimators, known for their statistical efficiency in high-dimensional settings, face challenges due to the high computational cost of the short-step interior-point method. The new method reduces per-iteration cost and achieves global convergence rates of O(1/√k) and local quadratic convergence under regularity conditions. The approach demonstrates significant speedups over existing methods on both synthetic and real datasets.
source.title: Researchers develop efficient semismooth Newton method for kernel-based optimal transport

source.summary: Databricks Feature Store allows data scientists to author features once and use them across both batch and streaming pipelines, achieving sub-second freshness. Traditional batch processing introduces significant lag, making it unsuitable for real-time applications like fraud detection. The Feature Store uses Spark Real-Time Mode (RTM) for continuous stream processing, Lakebase for optimized online storage, and Model Serving for fast retrieval. This infrastructure enables features like a user's transaction sum over the last 10 minutes to be updated in milliseconds. The system handles stateful aggregations with RocksDB, manages fault tolerance through checkpointing, and scales to handle high throughput. It also supports offline training data generation and provides governance through Unity Catalog, making it a comprehensive solution for real-time machine learning.
source.title: Databricks Feature Store enables sub-second freshness for real-time machine learning features

source.summary: Strands Robots, an open-source SDK from AWS, enables a continuous data loop for robot training and deployment by integrating with Hugging Face Storage Buckets. The system allows recording robot demonstrations, training policies on streaming data from the Hub, and deploying the trained model back to hardware. The process involves syncing datasets to a mutable Storage Bucket, which uses Xet-backed object storage for efficient byte-level deduplication. This reduces data transfer costs compared to versioned repositories. The loop is demonstrated through a single agent that records, streams, and deploys data without requiring local copies. The system supports both simulation and physical robots, with the same on-disk format used throughout. The article provides code examples and installation instructions for setting up the environment, including dependencies like LeRobot, datasets, and Hugging Face CLI tools.
source.title: Strands Robots Enable Continuous Data Loop for Robot Training and Deployment

source.summary: A large-scale reproduction challenge of 2,200 ICML 2026 papers revealed significant issues with reproducibility. The initiative, involving 2,962 cloud jobs, found that 51% of papers had at least one verified claim, with 266 fully reproduced and 632 partially reproduced. However, 23% of papers had at least one falsified or contested claim, including 49 papers where all claims were falsified and 242 where independent teams reached opposing verdicts. The challenge highlighted the limitations of AI agents in reproducing complex claims, with some errors stemming from arithmetic mistakes or misinterpretations. Human oversight was crucial, as agents occasionally failed to detect issues due to premature stopping or misreading scale-dependent behavior. The results underscore the need for human involvement in scientific review, as agents alone cannot fully replace the nuanced judgment of human reviewers.
source.title: ICML 2026 Reproduction Challenge Reveals 51% of Papers Verified, 23% Falsified

source.summary: NVIDIA has partnered with major financial institutions including Apollo, BlackRock, and Goldman Sachs to establish financing platforms aimed at mobilizing over $500 billion in third-party capital for AI infrastructure. The initiative seeks to transform AI compute into an investable asset class by offering repeatable platforms, long-term capital, and a broad customer base. NVIDIA's AI factories, which include hardware and software, support a wide range of AI models and can be redeployed across different users and workloads. The company emphasizes that its compute infrastructure improves over time through software updates, extending its economic value. NVIDIA may provide limited residual-value support for up to 25% of opportunities, but the primary financing comes from independent assessments by financial partners. The initiative aims to create an open capital market for AI infrastructure, enabling companies and nations to build productive AI factories that drive innovation and revenue.
source.title: NVIDIA Partners with Financial Firms to Finance AI Infrastructure

source.summary: NVIDIA, Google, and Microsoft are advancing a 800 VDC power architecture to improve AI compute performance and efficiency. Traditional AC power systems face limitations as AI demands grow, with multiple conversions reducing efficiency. The 800 VDC approach uses direct current at higher voltages, reducing conversion stages and increasing power delivery to GPUs. NVIDIA's DSX reference designs guide the transition from existing AC infrastructure to hybrid and fully native 800 VDC facilities. Over 80 companies are building products to this open standard. The hybrid 800 VDC rack allows existing AI facilities to upgrade without major infrastructure changes, while future row power centers and DC power blocks support larger-scale deployments. This open standard ensures interoperability across vendors, enabling a scalable supply chain for AI infrastructure.
source.title: NVIDIA, Google, and Microsoft Develop 800 VDC Architecture for AI Compute Scaling

source.summary: The inaugural Santa Cruz PyTorch Meetup, attended by 45 participants, featured talks on GPU programming, AI applications in chemistry, plant health, and autonomous driving. Organized by Red Hat and UCSC's OSPO, the event highlighted the growing global PyTorch community and demonstrated how local meetups can thrive with a welcoming, low-key approach. Speakers included NVIDIA's Faradawn Yang, Red Hat's Anil Vishnoi, and UCSC researchers showcasing PyTorch's versatility. The meetup emphasized the importance of community engagement and the broad applicability of PyTorch across various fields, encouraging others to start similar initiatives in their areas.
source.title: Santa Cruz PyTorch Meetup Showcases Community and AI Applications

source.summary: Alexander 'Sasha' Rakhlin has been appointed director of the MIT Statistics and Data Science Center (SDSC), succeeding Ankur Moitra. Rakhlin, a Distinguished Professor in Data, Systems, and Society, has been connected to the SDSC since 2016. He emphasizes the importance of interdisciplinary collaboration and the rigorous foundations of data science and AI. Rakhlin, who received his PhD from MIT, aims to deepen interdisciplinary connections and support the SDSC's role in addressing scientific and societal challenges through statistical and mathematical approaches.
source.title: MIT Appoints Alexander Rakhlin as New Director of Statistics and Data Science Center

source.summary: Daniela Rus, director of MIT's CSAIL, has been awarded the 2026 Bavarian Minister-President's High-Tech Prize for her work in robotics, AI, and autonomous systems. The prize, jointly awarded by the Bavarian State Government and Academy of Sciences, recognizes her 30-year research on self-organizing robots, soft robotics, and brain-inspired AI. Rus emphasized collaboration between humans and machines to solve complex problems. Her work includes ingestible robots for medical use and liquid neural networks for efficient autonomous systems. The award highlights her influence in fields ranging from transportation to environmental monitoring.
source.title: MIT's Daniela Rus honored with Bavarian High-Tech Prize for robotics and AI contributions

source.summary: Meta has developed fbtriton, a downstream fork of the upstream Triton infrastructure, to support custom GPU compiler innovations like TLX and autoWS. This fork allows Meta to rapidly develop hardware-specific optimizations while maintaining minimal divergence from the upstream codebase. The system employs continuous cherry-picking to synchronize with upstream changes, using a risk-partitioned agentic bundling approach to manage conflicts and maintain stability. A hierarchical test framework (L1/L2/L3) ensures comprehensive validation of changes, balancing speed and reliability. The approach addresses practical engineering challenges, including infrastructure reliability, operational friction, and context gaps in downstream workloads. While agentic solutions streamline workflows, the core complexities of compiler and hardware remain unchanged, requiring careful oversight to prevent errors and ensure safety.
source.title: Meta's fbtriton Infrastructure Enables Custom GPU Optimizations While Syncing with Upstream Triton

source.summary: Three studies from IBM, UChicago, Qedma, RIKEN, BlueQubit, and Algorithmiq demonstrate quantum advantage with built-in validation, enabling trustworthy quantum computations beyond classical verification. IBM and UChicago used doped Clifford sampling and spacetime codes to certify classically hard quantum computations. Qedma, RIKEN, and BlueQubit observed quantum phenomena beyond classical simulations using validated error-mitigation techniques. Algorithmiq showed how trusted quantum results can emerge by validating the computation process rather than a classical answer. The Quantum Advantage Tracker continues to compare quantum advantage claims against the best classical methods. These papers represent part of ongoing work in the field, with submissions from multiple organizations expected to continue as the community benchmarks quantum and classical performance.
source.title: Three studies show quantum advantage with built-in validation

source.summary: Gemini Robotics 2, a new intelligence layer, enables robots to perform complex tasks through whole-body control, advanced dexterity, and multi-robot collaboration. The system includes three models: Gemini Robotics 2, which converts vision and language into motor control; Gemini Robotics ER 2, which allows robots to understand and plan tasks; and Gemini Robotics On-Device 2, which adapts to new robot bodies quickly. The technology aims to create more versatile and autonomous robots capable of interacting with unpredictable environments.
source.title: Gemini Robotics 2 introduces whole-body intelligence for adaptable robots

source.summary: Amazon is providing substantial, long-term financial support to the Lean Focused Research Organization (FRO) to make mathematical proof accessible for software correctness. Lean, a programming language, enables rigorous verification of AI systems, with applications in AI safety, differential privacy, and distributed protocols. Amazon highlights its use in verifying AI agent policies and AWS systems, emphasizing transparency and trust through open-source development.
source.title: Amazon funds Lean FRO to advance verified AI safety

source.summary: RBI officials note that the West Asia conflict is affecting supply chains and business confidence. U.S. tariffs have added to trade uncertainty, yet the global economy continues to expand with inflationary pressures. The Indian economy shows resilience due to strong macroeconomic fundamentals, with domestic demand remaining robust. Petroleum consumption growth has turned positive, and merchandise trade saw strong growth in July, though the deficit widened. Monsoon activity supported kharif sowing, and CPI inflation rose slightly to 4.45%, driven by food and beverages, while core inflation remained stable. Food and fuel prices increased, with cereals, pulses, and edible oils seeing notable price rises.
source.title: RBI highlights West Asia conflict's impact on business confidence and inflation trends

source.summary: The BJP's sudden acceptance of a caste census marks a significant political shift, driven by the need to adapt to the 'data state' era. Previously opposing caste enumeration as divisive, the party now sees it as a tool for managing social divisions through detailed data. The 2024 election results exposed the limits of its earlier strategy of subsuming caste within Hindu identity. The census, as a governance tool, enables precise targeting of communities for welfare and political mobilization, fragmenting larger groups into manageable constituencies. This transition from constitutional to data-driven governance allows the state to reorganize social identities for administrative and electoral purposes. The article warns that while the census can promote social justice, its use depends on the political intent behind it, raising concerns about its potential to deepen inequality rather than address historical injustices.
source.title: BJP's Caste Census Shift Reflects Data State Governance Strategy

source.summary: Sumit Sarkar, a pioneering historian of modern India, left an indelible mark on the discipline through his method of 'history from below,' which emphasized the social and cultural dimensions of nationalism. His work, such as 'Modern India, 1885-1947,' challenged traditional narratives by incorporating the voices of peasants, workers, and marginalized groups. Sarkar's scholarship was deeply rooted in Marxism but remained open to questioning its assumptions, and he was a committed feminist. His intellectual rigor and modesty influenced generations of students, including Charu Gupta, who recalls his teaching style and the impact of his mentorship. Sarkar's legacy endures in the questions he inspired, encouraging historians to continually interrogate the past and its representations.
source.title: Sumit Sarkar's legacy in reshaping modern Indian history through critical inquiry

source.summary: A study on the shola sky islands in the Western Ghats reveals how land use changes have impacted bird movements. Both forest and grassland species avoid human-dominated landscapes, but forest specialists face fewer movement obstacles in invaded woodlands. The Nilgiri pipit, the only grassland specialist in the study, experienced the most adverse effects from woody invasions and human activities. Between 1973 and 2017, the islands lost 516 sq km of grasslands and 63 sq km of forests. Researchers built 126 models to predict species movement patterns, finding that increased woodland cover fragmented grassland habitats, reducing connectivity for grassland species. The study highlights the need to restore native grasslands in the Shola Sky Islands to preserve biodiversity.
source.title: Land use changes disrupt bird movement in shola sky islands

source.summary: The 2026 Environmental Performance Index (EPI) ranks India among the worst climate performers, sparking debate over fairness and ethical principles in climate rankings. Different indices, such as the Climate Change Performance Index (CCPI), yield conflicting results due to varying ethical frameworks. The EPI focuses on absolute greenhouse gas emissions, while the CCPI emphasizes per capita emissions, reflecting differing views on equity. A 2024 study shows that adjusting the EPI to incorporate fairness-based metrics significantly improves rankings for the Global South. The article argues that no single index is neutral, and policymakers should consider multiple indices to form a principled stance. Thailand's engagement with the EPI led to improved rankings, illustrating the value of constructive responses over rejection. The piece concludes that climate indices should be transparent about their design choices, and countries should use them to inform policy rather than dismiss them outright.
source.title: India's Climate Rankings Differ Across Indices Due to Ethical Premises

source.summary: Capital markets finance teams face increasing complexity in managing balance sheet risks due to market volatility, regulatory changes, and AI-driven workflows. The article highlights how AI tools like Genie One help finance professionals analyze real-time data, track funding and liquidity shifts, and ensure accurate capital and valuation reporting. These tools enable faster decision-making by providing context through ontologies like FIBO, which standardize financial definitions across systems. The article outlines three key challenges: anticipating funding tightening, identifying silent return erosion, and explaining capital numbers on demand. Genie One supports these tasks by integrating governed data and business definitions, allowing finance teams to respond proactively to market changes while maintaining regulatory compliance. The role of AI is to enhance analysis and coordination, not to make decisions, which remain the responsibility of trading desks and risk teams.
source.title: Capital Markets Finance Uses AI to Track Balance Sheet Risks in Real Time

source.summary: Data governance tools are software platforms that help organizations catalog, secure, and audit their data assets, ensuring compliance with regulatory requirements. These tools automate data discovery, apply access controls, track lineage, and generate compliance reports, transforming governance from a static document into an operational reality. They address fragmented data across warehouses, lakes, and SaaS applications by creating a shared, searchable layer over data sources. Key features include data cataloging, lineage tracking, access control, quality monitoring, compliance reporting, and AI governance. The article outlines five categories of data governance tools, emphasizing the need for a comprehensive platform that integrates with existing systems. A data governance framework, combined with the right tooling, ensures scalable and effective data management, with seven criteria for evaluating tools including scalability, integration, usability, and vendor support.
source.title: Data Governance Tools Enable Enterprise Data Management and Compliance

source.summary: Gordon Brown highlights growing global fears of a third world war amid nuclear tensions and rising nationalism. A survey of 36,000 people across 34 countries shows 55% support international cooperation even at the cost of national interests, rejecting 'America first' and similar ideologies. Majorities in every continent oppose populist nationalist leaders. Over 70% of respondents want governments to uphold human rights, address climate change, and fund humanitarian aid. Brown emphasizes that community engagement fosters support for international cooperation. While the US, China, and Russia are unpopular, countries like Canada, Australia, and the UK are seen as potential unifying forces. Brown calls for reforming global institutions to address shared challenges, urging a coordinated effort by cooperation-minded nations to build a more stable and equitable world order.
source.title: Global public favors cooperation over divisive nationalism

source.summary: Nine Entertainment CEO Matt Stanton sees growth in publishing due to new media laws forcing tech platforms to negotiate deals, despite cost reductions. The company expects Google and Meta to pay similar amounts to their 2021 agreement. Nine is also pursuing AI partnerships, including Microsoft's Copilot. The firm is cutting over $160m in costs across newsrooms, with the Sydney Morning Herald and The Age facing redundancies. The Australian Financial Review remains unaffected, while Nine's streaming and broadcast units saw slight revenue declines. Stanton emphasized focusing on growth assets like QMS while divesting smaller, challenged ones.
source.title: Nine CEO highlights publishing growth amid cost-cutting and AI deals

source.summary: Voice AI startup Ringg has raised $10 million from Peak XV Partners, bringing its total Series A funding to $15.5 million. The company, which processes 20 million call attempts monthly, is shifting from simple outbound calling to complex workflows like healthcare appointment booking and fintech onboarding. Ringg's co-founder Siddharth Tripathi noted that while voice calls still make up over 70% of its business, the startup is expanding into chat and WhatsApp, and targeting partnerships with Global Capability Centers in India. The company builds its own speech models but currently uses an orchestration layer to route tasks. Peak XV's Rishen Kapoor highlighted Ringg's technical depth in handling complex enterprise workflows.
source.title: Ringg raises $10 million to expand voice AI beyond basic call automation

source.summary: Meta has released Muse Glimmer, a 30B parameter dense model with a 120K context window, optimized for local agentic workflows on NVIDIA platforms. The model processes 20K tokens per second on a single GPU, designed for reliable, long-context tasks requiring multi-step execution. Unlike chat-focused models, Muse Glimmer uses a dense architecture without routing, ensuring consistent performance for agents managing complex tasks. It fits within a single NVIDIA GPU's VRAM, avoiding external endpoints, and benefits from NVIDIA's Tensor Core acceleration. The model supports deployment on various NVIDIA systems, including GeForce RTX 5090, DGX Spark, DGX Station, and Jetson, enabling secure, on-device inference for applications like code generation and autonomous support. Developers can fine-tune it using NVIDIA's NeMo tools and deploy via open-source inference stacks or prebuilt NIM containers.
source.title: Meta Releases Muse Glimmer for Local Agentic AI Workflows on NVIDIA Hardware

source.summary: Researchers highlight the limitations of vision-language action (VLA) models in robotics, particularly their inability to predict physical dynamics. They propose world action models (WAMs), which are built on video world models and better capture how scenes evolve. WAMs generalize better to unseen environments and require less task-specific data. NVIDIA's Cosmos 3 world model provides a strong foundation for building WAMs, offering diverse physical-world data and supporting deployment across different hardware tiers. The article outlines how post-training can specialize WAMs for specific robots, demonstrating improved performance in tasks like object manipulation. Cosmos 3's open-source release enables faster adaptation and reduces the need for extensive data collection, making WAMs a promising approach for generalist robot policies.
source.title: World Action Models Offer Better Generalization Than Vision-Language Action Models for Robotics

source.summary: DharmaOCR, an OCR model specialized for Brazilian Portuguese, outperformed newer models like Mistral OCR4 and Unlimited-OCR in both extraction accuracy and stability. The model's success stems from a two-stage training process: first, supervised fine-tuning focused on Brazilian Portuguese's vocabulary and document structures, and second, Direct Preference Optimization (DPO) that improved stability by training the model to select coherent outputs. On a Portuguese-specific benchmark, DharmaOCR achieved a score of 0.925, while Mistral OCR4 and Unlimited-OCR scored 0.798 and 0.7587, respectively. The results highlight the structural advantage of domain specialization over broader multilingual models, as the latter distribute training resources across multiple languages, reducing their effectiveness in specific tasks. The article argues that while newer models may eventually surpass DharmaOCR, the fundamental logic of specialization remains unchanged, ensuring that focused systems will continue to outperform generalist ones in targeted domains.
source.title: DharmaOCR Outperforms Multilingual OCR Models in Brazilian Portuguese

source.summary: Hugging Face disclosed a security incident in July 2026 involving unauthorized access to internal datasets and credentials. The breach exploited vulnerabilities in dataset processing pipelines, allowing an autonomous agent framework to execute thousands of actions across sandboxes. The company took steps to close the vulnerabilities, secure affected systems, and improve detection mechanisms. The attack was detected through AI-assisted anomaly detection, and forensic analysis was conducted using an open-weight model to avoid data leakage. The incident highlights the growing threat of AI-driven offensive tools and the need for robust defensive AI capabilities. Hugging Face emphasized the importance of having capable models for forensic analysis and warned of the risks posed by autonomous, AI-powered attacks.
source.title: Hugging Face Discloses Security Breach Involving AI-Driven Attack

source.summary: MIT has appointed Jesse Thaler as the new director of the Laboratory for Nuclear Science, effective August 1. Thaler, a theoretical physicist, will lead the lab as it embraces AI-driven research. He succeeds Bolek Wyslouch and will also oversee the Leinweber Institute. Thaler has been instrumental in advancing AI applications in particle physics and has led the NSF AI Institute for Fundamental Interactions. His leadership at LNS will focus on integrating AI into scientific discovery, with plans to expand research through the Department of Energy's Genesis Mission. Thaler's background includes roles at Harvard, Brown, and UC Berkeley, and he joined MIT in 2010.
source.title: MIT Appoints Jesse Thaler as New Director of Nuclear Science Lab

source.summary: Rachel Sava, a PhD candidate at Harvard-MIT, explores the ethical risks of neural implants in her winning submission for the Envisioning the Future of Computing Prize. She warns that as neural implants become more accessible, they could transition from medical tools to surveillance devices used by corporations and governments. Sava's work, inspired by her internship at IBM and a mentor's experience with brain decoders, highlights the potential for misuse in monitoring mental productivity or policing 'thought crimes'. The prize, organized by MIT's SERC initiative, encourages students to consider societal impacts alongside technological advancements. Sava emphasizes the importance of envisioning a future where technology benefits all while addressing ethical concerns. The competition awarded $10,000 to Sava, with other prizes given to runners-up and honorable mentions.
source.title: PhD Candidate Explores Ethical Risks of Neural Implants in Consumer Markets

source.summary: Google Research presented new AI tools at I/O 2026, emphasizing their role in accelerating scientific discovery and improving healthcare. The company introduced Gemini for Science, a suite of tools including Empirical Research Assistance (ERA) and Co-Scientist, which aid researchers in fields like neuroscience and cosmology. These tools enable rapid hypothesis testing and literature synthesis, with results published in Nature. In healthcare, Google launched the Google Health app and Health Coach, leveraging AI to support users in managing their health through symptom analysis and personalized coaching. The company also highlighted advancements in AI-driven disaster prediction, such as WeatherNext for hurricane forecasting and Groundsource for flash flood prediction. Additionally, Google shared progress on MedGemma and Coral NPU, aiming to democratize access to healthcare technologies and edge AI applications.
source.title: Google Research Unveils AI Tools for Scientific Discovery and Healthcare Innovation

source.summary: Google researchers present a new private analytics solution that combines cryptographic secure aggregation with trusted execution environments (TEEs) to enhance privacy and security in on-device AI systems. The approach allows for anonymized, aggregated insights without exposing individual user data, addressing challenges in understanding system performance across diverse devices. By leveraging a novel cryptographic protocol, the solution enables single-message submissions, reducing reliance on prolonged device connectivity. Integrated with Google's confidential federated analytics system, the method ensures data remains encrypted until the final aggregation stage, with TEE attestation providing verifiable proof of secure execution. This innovation supports tools like Android SafetyCore, improving threat detection while preserving user privacy. The work highlights advancements in secure computation and aims to raise the security bar for private analytics in large-scale systems.
source.title: Google Introduces Zero-Trust Private Analytics for Enhanced On-Device Safety

source.summary: Biologists Omar Abudayyeh and Jonathan Gootenberg are using Co-Scientist to overcome challenges in aging research. The AI tool helps identify genetic factors that reverse cellular aging by analyzing vast scientific literature and generating testable hypotheses. Lab tests validated some of Co-Scientist's recommendations, showing success in shifting cells toward a youthful state. Additionally, Co-Scientist accelerates data analysis, reducing the time needed to interpret results from months to days.
source.title: Biologists use AI to identify genetic factors reversing cellular aging

source.summary: Project Genie, a general-purpose world model, now connects with Google Street View to create realistic virtual environments. Users can base their imaginative worlds on real locations in the U.S., selecting styles like 'Ocean World' or 'B&W film' to reimagine places. The integration allows AI agents and robots to navigate and interact with real-world imagery. Project Genie is available to Google AI Ultra subscribers and is an experimental prototype in Google Labs.
source.title: Project Genie integrates Street View for realistic virtual environments

source.summary: Tim O'Brien argues that measuring AI productivity solely by token volume is a flawed approach that ignores whether work was actually valuable. He compares this error to FinOps blind spots regarding databases, where cost alone does not justify expense without understanding purpose and architecture. The author warns that vendors promoting simple token optimization miss critical questions about model selection, task complexity, and failure consequences. O'Brien notes that a cheap model causing retries can cost more than an expensive one succeeding immediately, and that different tasks require different architectural approaches. He suggests the future of AI financial management lies in connecting consumption to business outcomes rather than just counting tokens.
source.title: Tokens Are Not Dollars: Why AI Cost Metrics Fail to Measure Value

source.summary: The Georgia Public Service Commission approved Georgia Power's contract to supply electricity to OpenAI's new facility in Effingham County. OpenAI will pay for new infrastructure and provide up to 1 GW of flexible demand response. Georgia Power estimates these agreements could generate $950m in annual customer savings starting in 2029. CEO Kim Greene stated that typical residential savings are expected to rise to $180 annually. The utility noted this represents one of the largest single-facility demand response agreements in the US.
source.title: Georgia Power secures regulatory approval for OpenAI electricity supply deal

source.summary: Amazon announced four new power purchase agreements in Sweden, bringing its total carbon-free energy capacity there near 1 gigawatt. The company also expanded its largest-ever German PPA for 600 megawatts from the Gennaker offshore wind farm. These moves support Amazon's growing data center and AI computing needs. The International Energy Agency noted that AI-focused data center electricity demand surged by 50% last year.
source.title: Amazon Signs Four Swedish Wind Deals to Reach 1 GW Capacity

source.summary: The Energy Information Administration reports that U.S. uranium concentrate production reached 2.1 million pounds in 2025, the highest volume since 2017. Exploration and development drilling activities increased significantly compared to the previous year. Nuclear plant purchases of uranium fell to 46.9 million pounds, with foreign sources providing the majority of the material. Domestic uranium accounted for only 7% of total deliveries to U.S. nuclear facilities.
source.title: U.S. uranium production tripled in 2025 to highest level since 2017

source.summary: The article claims an Australian-American billionaire gave Trump a $1 million bribe before his firm received $900 million for a methane terminal stake. The text states the Department of the Interior illegally paid RWE $1.22 billion to cancel wind projects, with most funds going to Stonepeak. The author alleges this spending is wasteful and illegal, noting that states have sued and Democrats oppose the deals. The piece asserts the transaction raises electricity prices while restricting energy supply.
source.title: Private equity firm receives $900M after billionaire allegedly bribed Trump

source.summary: US President Donald Trump stated he does not believe Moscow will attack a NATO nation following his engagement with Russian President Vladimir Putin. Trump told reporters in the Oval Office that Putin is not going to attack NATO territory, though he did not specify when their talks occurred. Meanwhile, the Kremlin dismissed media reports suggesting a potential Russian strike as scare stories. CIA Director John Ratcliffe visited Moscow to urge the Kremlin against escalating tensions with US allies, particularly the Baltic states. Despite these diplomatic efforts, Western leaders remain concerned about Russian aggression and the security environment in the region. Additionally, a senior Pentagon official pressed NATO allies to outline their efforts in taking more responsibility for Europe's defense as the US reviews its force levels on the continent.
source.title: Trump Dismisses NATO Attack Fears After CIA Chief's Moscow Trip

source.summary: The Maine Public Utilities Commission selected Clearway Energy Group to develop an 800 MW wind project and named Avangrid as the preferred developer for the connecting transmission line. The commission stated that the plan utilizes existing corridors and shows strong viability. Massachusetts, Vermont, Connecticut, and Rhode Island will share the line's costs alongside Maine. The MPUC estimates net benefits to Maine of at least $387m–425m over the project's life. Permitting and construction will take years, with a power purchase agreement still to be finalized.
source.title: Maine PUC selects Clearway for 800 MW wind project and Avangrid for transmission

source.summary: BloombergNEF reports that global renewable energy investment reached $327.5 billion in the first half of 2026. Co-located solar-plus-storage projects attracted a record $25 billion, driven by revenue uncertainty in standalone solar markets. The United States led growth in this segment, while global wind investment declined 27% year on year. Europe bucked the trend with record onshore wind investment in Germany, Romania, and Serbia. BloombergNEF expects new installations to fall below 2025 levels in 2026 before growth resumes in 2027.
source.title: BloombergNEF reports $25 billion solar-plus-storage investment in first half of 2026

source.summary: Cmb-Tech has begun operations at a green hydrogen facility in Walvis Bay, Namibia, developed with Ohlthaver & List Group. The site features 5 MW of solar power and 5 MW of electrolyzers, producing hydrogen for dual-fuel trucks and generators. Cmb-Tech plans to scale the project to 250 MW and later 500 MW. Other recent developments include new catalyst research, AI efficiency gains, and China's new hydrogen infrastructure plans.
source.title: Cmb-Tech launches Africa's first PV-driven green hydrogen hub in Namibia

source.summary: The Municipality of Bluewater unanimously rejected Bedrock Energy's proposed compressed air energy storage project in Huron County, Ontario. The 382MW facility planned for 130 acres faced opposition regarding its impact on productive farmland. While the Agricultural Impact Assessment suggested land restoration, the project's 40-50 year lifespan remains significantly longer than typical lithium-ion battery systems. Meanwhile, competitor Hydrostor submitted a similar advanced-CAES project to the same Ontario request for proposal.
source.title: Ontario municipality rejects Bedrock Energy compressed air energy storage project

source.summary: Nomad Power Solutions announced that the US Department of Energy authorised its Vermont Long Duration Energy Storage demonstration project to proceed to phase 3. The approximately US$19 million initiative will deploy up to eight transportable battery units across five sites within Green Mountain Power's service territory. Nomad, now owned by Lixte Biotechnology Holdings, stated the project moves into installation and construction following prior operational use of its systems. The company reported a net loss of US$4.3 million for the six months ended June 2026 and faces substantial doubt regarding its ability to continue as a going concern. Despite these financial challenges, the project aims to demonstrate how transportable lithium iron phosphate batteries can improve grid reliability in rural communities.
source.title: Nomad Power Solutions advances Vermont pilot with US DOE approval

source.summary: Electrek hosts the Wheel-E podcast to discuss recent developments in the electric vehicle sector. The episode covers new e-bikes from Flit and SONDORS, a battery charging cabinet test, and the Qronge e-moto. Additionally, the show examines London police officers riding Sur-Rons and other nontraditional electric vehicles. Listeners can access the live stream on Electrek's YouTube channel.
source.title: Electrek hosts Wheel-E podcast covering new e-bikes and police use of Sur-Rons

source.summary: MARS Energy Group announced the acquisition of Citadel Roofing & Solar, adding over 1,000 employees to its platform. The company stated the deal strengthens its integrated residential roofing and solar presence across California. MARS CEO Manvendra Saxena emphasized that the partnership preserves Citadel's culture and leadership under Dieter Folk. The combined organization aims to expand service offerings and invest in technology while maintaining existing customer relationships.
source.title: MARS Energy Group acquires Northern California contractor Citadel Roofing & Solar

source.summary: Georgia Public Service Commission staff approved a contract between Georgia Power and OpenAI for a 3.2 gigawatt data center in Effingham County without a direct commission vote. Environmental groups criticized the lack of transparency and the secretive process used to finalize the agreement. Sierra Club and Southern Alliance for Clean Energy stated that elected Commissioners must weigh in on future contract decisions to ensure public accountability. The organizations also questioned how Georgia Power calculated costs and what protections exist if the data center leaves or reduces power usage.
source.title: Georgia PSC Staff Approves Secret OpenAI Data Center Contract

source.summary: Waaree Renewable Technologies Limited secured a Letter of Award for a major solar and energy storage project from an Indian thermal power company. The order covers EPC works for a 291 MWp ground-mounted solar PV system integrated with a 280 MWh Battery Energy Storage System. According to the company's regulatory filing dated August 28, 2026, the project is scheduled for completion during Financial Year 2027–28. Waaree Renewable Technologies stated that the promoters and group companies have no interest in the awarding entity, confirming the transaction is not a related-party deal. Heema Shah, Company Secretary, signed the regulatory communication on behalf of the company.
source.title: Waaree Renewable Technologies Secures LOA for 291 MWp Solar PV and 280 MWh BESS Project

source.summary: CNNC reported the hoisting of a 1,000-tonne steel dome at the Xudabao unit 1 nuclear plant. The company stated this step marks near completion of the unit's large steel structure modules. The facility utilizes CAP1000 reactor designs built with modular construction techniques. Ownership involves CNNC, Datang International, and State Development and Investment Corporation.
source.title: CNNC lifts 1,000-tonne steel dome at Xudabao nuclear unit

source.summary: Wood Mackenzie reports Latin America's energy storage capacity is expected to grow from 2.5 GW in 2025 to 34 GW by 2035. Chile leads the region, while Mexico and Brazil plan significant new tenders. Argentina has awarded 1.3 GW of standalone storage, and the Dominican Republic targets 500 MW by 2030. Pamela Morales of Wood Mackenzie stated that comprehensive regulatory frameworks with clear remuneration mechanisms are essential to sustain this growth beyond current policy-driven waves.
source.title: Latin America energy storage capacity projected to reach 34 GW by 2035

source.summary: A Newcleo-led consortium secured nearly EUR1 million to develop the n-Floating project, a floating nuclear power solution. The initiative, funded by Bpifrance, involves Newcleo, Bureau Veritas Marine & Offshore, and ABMI Groupe. Work on the 18-month project has begun to assess the feasibility of housing multiple LFR-AS-200 reactors on a non-self-propelled unit. The partners aim to design and build the solution in France with potential industrial deployment by 2036.
source.title: Newcleo consortium wins funding to develop floating nuclear plant

source.summary: BW Ideol reports that its eight-year-old Floatgen turbine has produced 40 GWh of energy. The company states the project demonstrates the technology's long-term viability. No other details were provided in the source text.
source.title: BW Ideol's Floatgen Turbine Generates 40 GWh After Eight Years

source.summary: Nvidia CEO Jensen Huang stated that securing power for AI data centers can take two to three years. Evercore ISI analyst Nicholas Amicucci suggests this delay creates an opportunity for Bloom Energy Corp. The firm reported its Oracle partnership system became operational in just 55 days. Kalshi traders predict U.S. data center counts will reach 5,300 by the end of 2026.
source.title: Nvidia warns of AI power delays while Bloom Energy sees opportunity
