source.summary: The Alliance for a Green Revolution in Africa (AGRA), backed by the Gates and Rockefeller Foundations, has failed to significantly boost agricultural productivity or reduce hunger in 13 African countries over two decades, according to a report by Timothy A. Wise and Jomo Kwame Sundaram. Despite billions in funding, yield growth has been slow, and undernourishment has risen by 58% since 2006. Smallholder farmers, who often lack access to subsidized inputs, have been left behind, while wealthier landowners benefited more. AGRA shifted focus to food systems and policy reforms in 2022, abandoning its original goals. Critics argue the Green Revolution approach, promoted by private foundations, has been ineffective in Africa compared to more diversified strategies seen in countries like Senegal. Donors have reduced support for AGRA, which now emphasizes commercialization over small-scale farming.
source.title: Gates and Rockefeller Foundations' AGRA Fails to Improve African Agriculture

source.summary: Diego Maradona’s iconic 'Hand of God' soccer ball, from the 1986 World Cup match against England, sold for £2.5 million at auction. The sale, reported by the Independent, highlights the enduring cultural and historical significance of the ball. The article also covers a range of other news, including a 6,500-year-old human tooth pendant discovered in Serbia, the impact of climate change on wheat prices and wine production, and ongoing geopolitical tensions involving China, Israel, and the United States. Additionally, it touches on economic issues, AI developments, and various international conflicts, providing a broad overview of global events as of August 25, 2026.
source.title: Maradona's 'Hand of God' Ball Sells for £2.5m

source.summary: Canada announced retaliatory tariffs of up to 50% on $20 billion in US goods, effective September 8, as part of a trade dispute. The measures target 700 products, with duties ranging from 15% to 50%. The government also unveiled a $7.5 billion support package for affected businesses and workers. Trump responded by threatening to double tariffs on Canadian autos, prompting criticism from Ontario Premier Doug Ford. Economists estimate the tariffs will raise the effective US tariff rate on Canadian exports to 6.9%.
source.title: Canada imposes $20 billion tariffs on US goods, introduces support measures

source.summary: Honda's executive vice president, Noriya Kaihara, stated the company may delay building an eighth North American assembly plant without an extended USMCA trade deal. He noted Honda is nearing full production capacity in the region and needs a new factory. Kaihara emphasized the need for a decision within a year or two, with the plant expected to operate by 2030. The Trump administration is negotiating the future of the USMCA with Canada and Mexico.
source.title: Honda Executive Warns New Plant in North America Depends on USMCA Extension

source.summary: CIA Director John Ratcliffe reportedly arrived in Moscow on an unannounced trip, according to US media outlets. The visit, which has not been confirmed by Washington or Moscow, follows the arrival of a US Air Force aircraft at Moscow's Vnukovo airport. CBS News cited sources familiar with the situation, while Kremlin spokesman Dmitry Peskov stated there was no information about the aircraft or planned meetings. This marks Ratcliffe's first visit to Russia as CIA director and the first such trip in five years, following the last by William Burns in November 2021.
source.title: CIA director visits Moscow on unconfirmed trip, sources report

source.summary: One Nation senator Malcolm Roberts expressed uncertainty about whether gay people should have equal rights during a conference, citing his personal stance and societal examples. Roberts, alongside party leader Pauline Hanson, attended a conservative Christian event where he questioned the moral soundness of James Ashby, a gay party director. While acknowledging prominent gay figures in various fields, Roberts suggested banning gay individuals, a stance criticized by Equality Australia's Anna Brown as incompatible with democratic values. The conference organizer criticized 'loud, screaming activists' for influencing medical policies. Roberts also advocated for an abortion ban and life beginning at conception, contradicting Hanson's position. The party has faced internal contradictions on immigration and other issues, with members like Barnaby Joyce and Cory Bernardi making controversial remarks on homosexuality. Roberts and One Nation did not comment on the report.
source.title: One Nation Senator Expresses Uncertainty on Gay Rights and Contradictory Party Positions

source.summary: The Paris region has introduced retro 'sunflower' pools, evoking nostalgia among residents and visitors. These pools, designed with sunflower motifs, have become a popular attraction. Local authorities stated the initiative aims to blend historical charm with modern recreational spaces. The project has drawn positive reactions from the community. The pools are part of a broader effort to revitalize public spaces with thematic elements.
source.title: Paris Region Introduces Retro Sunflower Pools Sparking Nostalgia

source.summary: Nine years after the 2017 Myanmar military crackdown that displaced hundreds of thousands of Rohingya Muslims, the crisis continues to escalate. Despite ongoing humanitarian efforts, conditions in refugee camps in Bangladesh have deteriorated, with aid shrinking and living conditions worsening. Analysts warn that repatriation is premature as conflict in Rakhine state persists, and more Rohingya continue fleeing into Bangladesh. The U.N. refugee agency reports that 154,000 additional Rohingya have arrived since 2024, with conditions in Rakhine remaining unstable. Rohingya refugees, barred from legal work in Bangladesh, rely heavily on dwindling humanitarian aid, which has been cut multiple times in recent years. With international attention waning and funding shortfalls, refugees face increasing risks of falling into illicit economies or dangerous journeys to Malaysia. Experts call for greater international engagement and support to address the crisis, which has left over a million Rohingya in limbo for nearly a decade.
source.title: Rohingya refugees face worsening crisis as return remains uncertain

source.summary: Samuel Bateman, a polygamous sect leader featured in Netflix's Trust Me: The False Prophet, is set to be sentenced after three girls were found in a poorly ventilated trailer. Bateman, already serving a 50-year federal prison sentence for child sex offenses, faces additional charges from a 2022 traffic stop. Authorities were alerted after seeing small fingers through the trailer's gaps, revealing conditions with a makeshift toilet and no air conditioning. Each count carries a mandatory sentence of four to eight years. Bateman, who claimed the girls had escaped, admitted knowing the girls were trapped but downplayed the conditions. His sect, an offshoot of Warren Jeffs' group, has seen its influence wane, with the towns no longer under court supervision.
source.title: Polygamous leader to face sentencing after girls rescued from trailer

source.summary: US President Donald Trump claimed all mines have been removed or detonated in the Strait of Hormuz, according to his social media post. He warned Iran that any vessel placing new mines would be 'systematically destroyed' under Space Force surveillance. Trump emphasized a 'zero tolerance policy' on mine placement, asserting Washington is monitoring the strategic waterway and other locations with Space Force technology. The statement was made on 25 August 2026.
source.title: Trump announces mine clearance in Strait of Hormuz, threatens Iran with 'zero tolerance'

source.summary: Two unvaccinated people in Pennsylvania have died from measles, according to health officials. Pennsylvania reported 393 cases this year, part of a national surge to the highest level in 35 years. Last year, two unvaccinated children in Texas died during an outbreak affecting over 1,000 people. Vaccination rates in Lancaster County, where the deaths occurred, are 85% for kindergarten-age students, below the 95% needed for herd immunity. Public health officials warn that vaccine hesitancy and recent policy changes may contribute to the spread of measles.
source.title: Two unvaccinated individuals die from measles in Pennsylvania

source.summary: Brazil’s data protection regulator fined ByteDance, TikTok’s parent company, nearly $30 million for alleged mishandling of minors' personal data. The ruling cited failures in protecting children and teenagers' information across both logged-in and guest sessions. The company has 10 days to appeal the decision, which also orders the removal of illegally collected data and a plan to improve protections for minors. The regulator previously recommended suspending Discord live broadcasts following a suicide case linked to the platform. Brazil’s government and Supreme Court have sought to regulate internet use by minors, with similar efforts underway in Australia, Canada, and Indonesia.
source.title: Brazilian Regulator Fines TikTok's Parent Company $30 Million Over Data Privacy Violations Involving Minors

source.summary: The AP has outlined a hypothetical 17-game college football road trip that would allow fans to see every team in its preseason Top 25. The journey begins with the Apple Cup between Washington State and Washington on September 6, followed by games involving SMU, Missouri, Tennessee, and LSU. The schedule includes key matchups like Oklahoma vs. Georgia, Ohio State vs. Iowa, and the Iron Bowl between Auburn and Alabama on November 28. The route prioritizes reasonable travel times between games, with some games scheduled in the early afternoon to allow for overnight travel. The trip concludes with a Thanksgiving showdown between Texas and Texas A&M, followed by the Iron Bowl. The AP's plan highlights major rivalries and potential matchups that could shape the season.
source.title: AP's College Football Top 25 Dream Road Trip Outlines 17 Games

source.summary: Israeli Prime Minister Benjamin Netanyahu accused Iran of attempting to kill one of his sons, though he provided no details about the alleged plot. The claim came during an interview with Channel 14, following reports that a security agency refused to protect a political rival ahead of the October 27 general election. Netanyahu emphasized the need for security measures, citing the heightened tensions since the U.S.-Israeli war on Iran began in February. Israeli media reported that Shin Bet chief David Zini declined to provide security for Gadi Eisenkot, whose party is projected to win the most seats. Netanyahu told Zini that appropriate security should be provided for any prime ministerial candidate.
source.title: Netanyahu Accuses Iran of Attempting to Kill One of His Sons

source.summary: Slovak police have arrested three foreign nationals for planning an arson attack on a drone manufacturing facility, which could have endangered 70 employees. The suspects allegedly prepared a napalm-like mixture and a site plan, leading to the seizure of incendiary substances and tools. Two were detained in Slovakia, while the third was arrested in Germany under a European arrest warrant. Authorities reported no injuries or damage due to their intervention.
source.title: Slovak police arrest three foreigners for planned arson at drone factory

source.summary: A US judge has rejected Ghislaine Maxwell's attempt to overturn her sex trafficking conviction. The court dismissed her appeal, upholding the original verdict. Maxwell was found guilty of conspiring to sexually exploit minors. The ruling marks the final stage in her legal proceedings. The court emphasized the evidence supporting the conviction.
source.title: US judge denies Ghislaine Maxwell's appeal against sex trafficking conviction

source.summary: Sudan's short-stature football team faces war, displacement, and limited resources as it prepares for the 2026 World Cup. Players from different regions, many displaced by conflict, train in Khartoum despite security challenges. Soccer expert Mohammed Abdullah praised their dedication. The team, established in 2020, aims to overcome financial and travel obstacles. Player Ibrahim Abdalla overcame childhood discrimination to pursue football. Sudan missed the first World Cup for short-stature teams due to funding issues. The federation's president, Mohammed Nour Kasha, said the team brings hope to a war-torn country. The conflict has killed 59,000 and displaced 13 million people, making the team's campaign a symbol of resilience.
source.title: Sudan's short-stature football team seeks World Cup amid conflict

source.summary: The World Health Organisation has updated temporary recommendations for member states amid the ongoing Ebola outbreak in the Democratic Republic of Congo. The DRC is classified as the only country at 'very high' risk, with neighboring nations like Burundi and the Central African Republic rated 'high risk'. The WHO chief noted the outbreak is spreading faster than any previous one and remains a public health emergency of international concern. Congolese authorities reported 5514 confirmed cases and 2690 deaths, resulting in a 47.9 percent fatality rate.
source.title: WHO updates Ebola recommendations as DRC outbreak spreads

source.summary: Russian military drones have been accused of targeting Ukrainian civilians in 'human safaris,' a practice described as a war crime by the UN. A video showing a civilian cyclist being killed by a drone, posted and later deleted by the Russian military, sparked outrage. Experts note this is not an isolated incident, with such attacks occurring for two years, particularly in Kherson and other frontline regions. The practice involves using short-range drones to hunt civilians, including pedestrians, cyclists, and vehicles, often with the intent to instill fear and force displacement. The UN's independent commission has condemned these actions as potential crimes against humanity. Analysts suggest the tactics are tolerated by Russian military leadership and may serve as training for drone operators or a means to desensitize troops to civilian casualties. The videos are also used to justify further drone purchases and funding. Despite the controversy, the Russian military continues these operations, with experts warning that the low cost and effectiveness of such tactics could be replicated elsewhere.
source.title: Russian drones target Ukrainian civilians in 'human safaris' across multiple regions

source.summary: A tornado struck a southern French village, injuring dozens and leaving over 1,400 homes without electricity. Local authorities in Pomas reported two people in critical condition. The village is now assessing the aftermath of the storm, which occurred on August 25.
source.title: French village assesses damage after tornado leaves 1,400 homes without power

source.summary: Oracle employees are monitoring Slack member counts and online forums for signs of layoffs after failing to receive expected termination emails at 6 am on September 1. Business Insider reported in mid-August that managers were preparing lists to cut payroll before the fiscal quarter began, citing internal documents suggesting double-digit reductions. The company has declined to comment on these rumors. Staff recall a previous wave in March where roughly 10,000 positions were eliminated without prior manager conversations, affecting teams like Oracle Health and NetSuite. Financial data shows Oracle's headcount fell by 21,000 in the fiscal year ended May 31, while restructuring charges rose to $1.8 billion. Despite strong revenue growth of 17% to $67.4 billion, the stock has dropped more than 20% this year as investors question the company's borrowing strategy for its OpenAI commitment.
source.title: Oracle employees track layoffs after missing 6 am termination emails

source.summary: Tim Cook will step down as Apple CEO on September 1, passing leadership to hardware chief John Ternus. Cook will transition to executive chairman to guide company dealings with policymakers. During his tenure, Apple grew from a $350 billion to over $4.5 trillion company. Analysts note Ternus faces significant challenges in advancing AI and reducing manufacturing dependence on China.
source.title: Tim Cook steps down as Apple CEO, handing leadership to John Ternus

source.summary: John Ternus officially took over as Apple CEO on Tuesday, replacing Tim Cook after nearly 15 years at the top. Bloomberg reports that Apple shares rose about 2,275% since Cook became CEO in August 2011, with a total-return basis gain of 2,736%. Analysts suggest Ternus must combine innovation with operational discipline to maintain growth. The new CEO faces immediate pressure to address artificial intelligence concerns and Apple's high valuation of around 33 times expected earnings. Services revenue now exceeds $109 billion, representing more than a quarter of total sales. Ternus is expected to unveil a foldable iPhone at an upcoming event to demonstrate his leadership strategy.
source.title: John Ternus becomes Apple CEO amid AI concerns and high valuation

source.summary: OpenAI stated that Apple is solely responsible for the current trade secret conflict. The AI company argued that Apple failed to prove any confidential data was stolen by former employees. OpenAI claimed Apple's internal policies make it difficult for staff to separate personal and work information. The lawsuit represents a significant shift from the companies' previous partnership.
source.title: OpenAI Blames Apple for Trade Secret Lawsuit Dispute

source.summary: Sun Pharma became the first Indian drugmaker to sign a Most Favoured Nation pricing agreement with the US government. The deal delays Section 232 tariffs on innovative products for over two years and extends pricing to state Medicaid programs. Alongside eight other manufacturers, Sun Pharma committed to investing $19.6 billion in US manufacturing. The White House noted the agreements cover 89 percent of the branded drug market.
source.title: Sun Pharma signs US MFN pricing deal to avoid tariffs

source.summary: The Indian commerce ministry asked exporters to share concerns about US market access to address tariff uncertainties. Industry officials noted that while order books remain good, buyers are reducing volumes and diversifying sources due to tariff risks. Commerce Minister Piyush Goyal will visit the US in late September to discuss the bilateral trade agreement. The ministry is seeking to conclude the pact quickly to help Indian goods compete against nations like Vietnam and Thailand that face similar tariffs.
source.title: India Commerce Ministry Seeks Exporter Input on US Trade Pact Amid Tariff Uncertainty

source.summary: Jurors in the Lindsay Clancy murder trial told Judge William Sullivan they could not reach a unanimous decision on Tuesday. The judge instructed the jury to continue deliberating rather than declaring a mistrial immediately. Defense attorney Kevin Reddington argues Clancy acted under postpartum psychosis, while prosecutors present evidence of premeditation. A hung jury allows for a retrial, unlike an acquittal which would prevent further prosecution.
source.title: Lindsay Clancy Jury Fails to Reach Verdict in Massachusetts Murder Trial

source.summary: TMC leader Abhishek Banerjee accused the BJP-led West Bengal government of a political vendetta following nearly six hours of police questioning regarding a scuffle over an unauthorized billboard. Banerjee alleged false cases, custodial torture, and procedural lapses while claiming the action was part of a wider attempt to target the Trinamool Congress. Senior minister Agnimitra Paul rejected the charge, stating that the law applies equally to everyone. The confrontation involved Kolkata Municipal Corporation officials and police dismantling a billboard at Banerjee's office, leading to arrests and three FIRs. Banerjee and his lawyer questioned the police procedure, noting that FIR copies were not uploaded online as per Supreme Court directions. He also linked the incident to a recent fire at the Alipore Administrative Building, alleging selective government focus on the TMC.
source.title: Abhishek Banerjee accuses BJP of vendetta after six-hour police questioning

source.summary: Vodafone Idea unveiled a refreshed brand identity featuring a new logo and Bollywood actor Shah Rukh Khan as its brand ambassador. The company stated the move reflects its ambition and optimism during a new phase. CEO Abhijit Kishore announced upcoming strategic launches to enhance customer engagement. The government holds a 49% stake in the debt-ridden telecom operator. Recent reassessment of AGR liabilities has improved the company's financial visibility.
source.title: Vodafone Idea launches new logo and appoints Shah Rukh Khan as brand ambassador

source.summary: The Ministry of Corporate Affairs extended the Companies Compliance Facilitation Scheme, 2026, until September 15 following stakeholder requests. The ministry cited data center disruptions from a June 5 fire as a reason for the initial delay. Under the scheme, companies pay reduced penalties to file financial statements or obtain dormant status. The extension allows firms to complete pending compliances by paying significantly lower fees than usual.
source.title: Government extends corporate compliance relief scheme until September 15

source.summary: Prime Minister Narendra Modi gifted Indian cultural artefacts to leaders in Uzbekistan and Kyrgyzstan during his recent visit. Officials stated the items highlighted India's literary, musical and artisanal heritage while underlining shared traditions. Specific presents included a Mahabharata translation for Kyrgyz President Sadyr Japarov and a santoor for Uzbek President Shavkat Mirziyoyev. Other gifts featured Ladakhi textiles, Kangra tea, Dokra artwork and marble inlay pieces for various dignitaries and family members.
source.title: PM Modi gifts Mahabharata, santoor and crafts to Central Asian leaders

source.summary: Cockroach Janata Party leader Abhijeet Dipke welcomed the Supreme Court's decision to quash all FIRs against protesters involved in the NEET UG paper leak controversy. Dipke stated that the order served true justice for students and families affected by the exam leak and subsequent suicides. He credited the victory to the collective voice of protesters at Jantar Mantar and supporters who shared messages on social media and WhatsApp. Dipke announced that the CJP has called off its planned September 5 protest following the court's intervention under Article 142. The party leader also apologized to the families of deceased students, attributing their loss to government failure rather than the children's actions.
source.title: CJP leader Dipke welcomes Supreme Court order quashing NEET protest FIRs

source.summary: The Ministry of External Affairs reported that 163 Indian nationals were rescued from Nepal floods, with 151 departing China on Tuesday. An Indian tunnel rescue team established a foothold at Chilime hydropower tunnels despite restricted access and marshy conditions. The MEA stated the team used innovative methods to move deeper and will continue efforts to save trapped individuals. India has expanded forensic activities with Nepal to expedite DNA sample processing. The death toll in Nepal and China surpassed 1,000 as rescue operations entered their seventh day. External Affairs Minister S Jaishankar confirmed India sent a consignment of 37.5 tonnes of humanitarian aid, bringing total assistance to 47.5 tonnes.
source.title: India rescues 163 nationals in Nepal floods as death toll exceeds 1,000

source.summary: Delhi Police are reconstructing the route of a sleeper bus where a 16-year-old girl was gang-raped on August 4, using CCTV footage and mobile data. The probe reveals the vehicle had eight traffic challans in July, totaling ₹54,000, including one for operating without a valid permit. Investigators found the travel company failed to verify the background of the accused driver and conductor before hiring them. Police are analyzing forensic evidence from the girl's clothes and the bus interior, which contained curtains that concealed the crime. The bus was reportedly undergoing repairs and being driven for painting when the assault occurred. Authorities have arrested the two men and are comparing DNA samples with evidence recovered from the vehicle.
source.title: Police investigate Noida bus rape case amid eight prior challans and missing background checks

source.summary: Officials report that heavy rain killed at least seven people and triggered landslides across Uttarakhand on Tuesday. The India Meteorological Department issued a red alert for Nainital and Almora while an orange alert covered most other parts of the state. Three deaths occurred in Almora after house walls collapsed, and two Nepalese labourers died in the same district. In Dehradun, a car was swept away by a rain-swollen current, killing two passengers and injuring another. Falling boulders and landslides blocked the Dehradun-Mussoorie highway, disrupting traffic. Rivers swelled significantly, with Haldwani recording 192 mm of rain in 24 hours. Authorities closed schools in several districts and urged residents to avoid disaster-prone areas.
source.title: Heavy rain kills seven and triggers landslides across Uttarakhand

source.summary: Sun Pharmaceutical Industries agreed to supply U.S. state Medicaid programs at Most Favoured Nation pricing. The company also committed to MFN pricing for future innovative medicine launches. Rick Ascroft, North America CEO, stated the deal recognizes Sun Pharma's investment in the U.S. market. The agreement delays Section 232 tariffs on innovative pharmaceutical products for over two years. Sun Pharma will contribute antibiotics to the Strategic Active Pharmaceutical Ingredients Reserve.
source.title: Sun Pharma agrees to MFN pricing for U.S. Medicaid programs

source.summary: The Shri Ram Janmbhoomi Teerth Kshetra Trust has shortlisted three names for its first CEO after reviewing 5,500 applications. A three-member panel, including retired Justice Pramod Kohli, will present these candidates to the trust board for a final decision expected on September 2. The selection process involved rigorous screening, with 16 individuals interviewed after an initial Google Form assessment. Concurrently, the trust announced Jagdish Aafle as its first secretary, noting his background with the RSS and engineering qualifications. The panel expressed confidence in the transparency of the selection and the vision of the shortlisted candidates. Trust treasurer Govind Dev Giri confirmed the board retains the final authority to appoint the CEO from the shortlist.
source.title: Ram Mandir Trust shortlists three candidates for CEO role

source.summary: Jennifer Donnelly reports that social media trends like 'maxxing' repurpose self-improvement concepts to encourage constant optimization of health and lifestyle. The article explains that while these trends can motivate healthy behaviors, they often promote a mindset of self-surveillance and criticism. Donnelly notes that focusing on reaching an idealized maximum can lead to psychological issues such as muscle dysmorphia and orthorexia. The researcher suggests adopting 'moderation-maxxing' instead, which involves checking motivations and practicing self-compassion. This approach allows individuals to pursue growth without the stress of constant comparison or the pressure to achieve perfection in every life aspect.
source.title: Experts warn social media maxxing trends may increase stress and anxiety

source.summary: Inara Foods announced a distribution partnership with the Kalimark Group to reach nearly 100,000 retail outlets in Tamil Nadu. Nawabzada Mohammed Asif Ali stated the company aims to establish Inara Foods as a leading snack brand in the region. Ramesh, Chairman of Kalimark Group, described the collaboration as a significant business opportunity contributing to Tamil Nadu's economic growth. The partnership will distribute products including chikkis, flavoured peanuts, chips, and mixtures.
source.title: Inara Foods partners with Kalimark Group to expand snack distribution in Tamil Nadu

source.summary: The article reports that the death toll from Nepal's recent floods has exceeded 1,000, with approximately 4,000 people still missing. Families in Delhi describe the anguish of being unable to reach affected areas due to sealed borders. Several specific cases illustrate the tragedy: Dinesh Thapa's body was found severed, allowing identification, while his mother remains untraced. A bus carrying 38 passengers, including three family members, was swept away, with only one body recovered. Another engineer, Sudhir Kumar Shah, was part of a team of 60 swept away, with no credible information received since his last call. The article highlights the widespread uncertainty and grief affecting the Nepali diaspora in India.
source.title: Delhi's Nepali community searches for missing relatives after Nepal floods

source.summary: Gautam Adani, chairman of the Adani Group, called for a new credit framework to better evaluate large infrastructure projects in India. Speaking at a conclave hosted by CareEdge Group, he argued that traditional rating models fail to capture the value of modern ecosystem-based projects. Adani stated that India needs wider lenses to assess how different infrastructure assets work together to create economic benefits. He cited the Mundra port and Vizhinjam port as examples of platform infrastructure that generate new demand and capabilities. Adani also linked the future of artificial intelligence to the need for robust physical infrastructure like data centers and power grids. He urged CareEdge to develop a comprehensive framework that recognizes ecosystem multipliers and strategic benefits. Adani emphasized that his proposal seeks dynamic models rather than lower standards for risk assessment.
source.title: Gautam Adani calls for new credit framework to assess India's infrastructure

source.summary: President Donald Trump has personally contacted Apple regarding a request to rename Lake Ontario to Lake America on its mapping service. Interior Secretary Doug Burgum stated that the technology company could soon make the change following the president's direct outreach. Google Maps has already implemented the new name for US users while retaining the original name for Canadian users. The dispute stems from an executive order directing changes in US federal databases, though it does not alter Canada's naming conventions or international usage.
source.title: Trump urges Apple to rename Lake Ontario to Lake America

source.summary: TCS iON expressed deep regret over power failures at a Jaipur examination centre during the NEET-PG and AIIMS CRE exams. The company cited unknown local electrical issues and stated it is working with vendor teams to fix the problem urgently. NBEMS has scheduled a retest for September 5 and formed a three-member committee to probe the incident. TCS iON head Venguswamy Ramaswamy confirmed all possible measures are being taken to prevent recurrence.
source.title: TCS iON regrets Jaipur power failure during NEET-PG exam

source.summary: OpenAI announced that its ChatGPT advertising business has reached a $1 billion annualized revenue run rate. The company expanded its Ads Manager to India, Europe, the Middle East, and North Africa starting Monday. OpenAI stated that small and medium-sized businesses now represent a material share of its ad revenue. The company is using advertising to drive growth ahead of a potential 2027 IPO.
source.title: OpenAI Announces ChatGPT Ads Reach $1 Billion Annualized Revenue

source.summary: OpenClaw released version 2.0, the platform's most extensive update since its debut. The company stated the upgrade was built by 933 contributors and touches every part of the system. New features include streamlined setup, automatic tool detection, and a redesigned browser interface. The update also adds multi-user collaboration tools and deeper cross-platform automation capabilities.
source.title: OpenClaw releases largest update in history with new features

source.summary: Chief Minister N. Chandrababu Naidu will visit Mogalturu on Tuesday to distribute pensions under the NTR Bharosa Pension Scheme. He plans to visit beneficiaries in wards 2, 3, and Ponnapalli before addressing a public meeting. Naidu is scheduled to return to Amaravati by 5:20 pm after attending a party cadre meeting.
source.title: CM Naidu visits Mogalturu to distribute pensions under NTR Bharosa Scheme

source.summary: Chief Minister N. Chandrababu Naidu directed officials to enhance citizen services based on public feedback during a review of the Real Time Governance initiative. He called for extensive publicity on measures to curb crimes against women and ganja use while stressing the need for proper sanitation in urban and rural areas. Naidu also instructed officials to conduct regular reviews at constituency and district levels to identify service lapses and rank officers based on performance. Additionally, he directed departments to provide services online and resolve applications through the Public Grievance Redressal System.
source.title: CM Naidu directs officials to improve citizen services using public feedback

source.summary: The Ramon Magsaysay Awards announced three winners on Monday for their contributions to international law, democracy, and social welfare. Tommy Koh received the honor for his role in adopting the UN Ocean Treaty. Bo Kyi was recognized for his seven-year imprisonment while resisting Myanmar's military. Runa Khan won for her work helping the poorest in Bangladesh through Friendship Bangladesh. The awards body highlighted each recipient's specific achievements in their respective fields.
source.title: Singapore lawyer, Myanmar activist, and Bangladeshi teacher win Ramon Magsaysay Awards

source.summary: John Galliano has withdrawn from a planned 2027 Met Gala exhibition following criticism of his past racist and antisemitic remarks. The designer stated he decided against the show after discussions with museum officials, expressing deep regret for the pain his words caused. Although The Met intended to address his controversial history directly, the backlash led to the cancellation. Galliano emphasized that meaningful atonement requires ongoing conduct rather than institutional recognition.
source.title: John Galliano withdraws from 2027 Met Gala exhibition amid past remarks backlash

source.summary: Karnataka Home Minister Priyank Kharge vowed to retire from politics if any role in Assistant Executive Engineer recruitment irregularities is proven. He accused Union Minister HD Kumaraswamy of spreading false propaganda without documents. Kharge demanded a proper probe to identify responsible officials rather than targeting him politically. He also questioned why Kumaraswamy did not raise similar concerns during the NEET examination issues.
source.title: Priyank Kharge vows to quit politics if recruitment irregularities are proven

source.summary: BLOs report that the ECI's Booth Level Officer app blocks Form-6 submissions for voters lacking Aadhaar, despite guidelines allowing it. Officials claim everyone possesses the card, but BLOs warn this creates barriers for slum dwellers and those without documents. The app's E-sign feature requires OTP authentication linked to Aadhaar, preventing digitization of applications. Additionally, a new declaration form requiring 2002 electoral roll details further complicates re-enrollment for many excluded voters.
source.title: Voters without Aadhaar face exclusion risks during India's Special Intensive Revision

source.summary: The Judicial Infrastructure Advisory Committee submitted an interim report to Chief Justice of India Surya Kant on Monday. Headed by Justice Aravind Kumar, the panel outlined a blueprint to address court infrastructure deficiencies and secure government funding. The committee also recommended measures for computerisation under the e-Courts initiative and expanding citizen-centric services. The group was tasked with identifying gaps affecting justice delivery and improving working conditions for staff.
source.title: Supreme Court panel submits interim roadmap for modernising Indian courts

source.summary: The National Stock Exchange of India reported a record-breaking turnover in its Closing Auction Session on Monday. The exchange said the session handled ₹39,718 crore, which was 42 times higher than the previous day. More than 98,000 unique investors participated in the event. NSE attributed the surge to the MSCI August 2026 Index Review, which required passive investors to realign portfolios. Sriram Krishnan, Chief Business Development Officer at NSE, stated that the successful completion of the first month marks an important milestone for Indian capital markets. The exchange noted that the mechanism brings price discovery closer to global best practices. Cumulative turnover for the first month reached approximately ₹63,000 crore.
source.title: NSE records historic turnover in closing auction session during MSCI review

source.summary: Karnataka food safety authorities launched a statewide crackdown on sweet manufacturers, seizing hundreds of kilograms of expired and mislabelled products. The drive, directed by Health and Family Welfare Minister U T Khader, inspected units across Bengaluru, Mysuru, and other districts under the Food Safety and Standards Act, 2006. Officials found violations including unhygienic conditions, unauthorized artificial colours, and missing mandatory labels. Six units were temporarily closed, and legal proceedings were initiated against several businesses. A major seizure of 400 kg of khova occurred at Balaji Milk Khova in Bengaluru, while expired curd and mislabelled savouries were also confiscated. The department stated that similar inspections will continue with no leniency for violations posing public health risks.
source.title: Karnataka officials seize expired sweets and shut six food units

source.summary: The National Company Law Tribunal approved a repayment plan for Zee Group founder Subhash Chandra that reduces admitted claims from over ₹22,000 crore to ₹6.5 crore. The plan secured support from creditors holding more than 81 per cent of the voting share. Member (Technical) Reena Sinha Puri recommended rejection due to unresolved concerns about the resolution professional's conduct and potential related-party voting. However, Member (Judicial) Nilesh Sharma concluded there was insufficient evidence to disqualify the objecting creditors' claims. The tribunal held that the resolution professional lacked investigative powers under personal insolvency provisions. Several banks, including HDFC Bank and Union Bank of India, intend to challenge the order before the National Company Law Appellate Tribunal.
source.title: Zee founder's repayment plan survives NCLT scrutiny despite creditor objections

source.summary: The Pakistan Cricket Board announced sweeping changes to the Test squad and coaching staff following a 0-2 series deficit against England. Seven players, including Mohammad Rizwan and Imam-ul-Haq, were released while seven replacements were named. Red-ball coaches Sarfaraz Ahmed and Umar Gul were also relieved of their duties. The team will face England at Edgbaston starting September 9.
source.title: Pakistan Cricket Board releases seven players and two coaches after England series defeat

source.summary: The Mumbai Metropolitan Region Transport Authority approved fare increases for taxis and autorickshaws effective September 1. Officials stated that minimum fares will rise to ₹27 for autos and ₹33 for taxis. Per kilometer rates also increased, with drivers required to calibrate meters by November. The revision follows an 18-month gap since the last hike in February 2025.
source.title: Mumbai MMRTA approves fare hikes for taxis and autorickshaws

source.summary: ONGC Chairman Arun Kumar Singh announced plans to invest ₹1 lakh crore in deepwater exploration by 2030. The company intends to drill 87 wells during this period, supported by better technology and government initiatives. Meanwhile, ONGC Videsh Managing Director Rajarshi Gupta stated the firm is negotiating to become the operator for Venezuelan assets. These talks are expected to conclude within the next three months.
source.title: ONGC plans ₹1 lakh crore deepwater investment and Venezuela operatorship talks

source.summary: Social activist Anna Hazare has been admitted to the ICU at Bombay Hospital in Mumbai following acute dehydration and kidney complications. Doctors are currently assessing his condition after he was diagnosed with a viral infection. Hazare, who is 89 years old, was previously treated at a facility near his village in Maharashtra. The report notes that further details regarding his health are awaited.
source.title: Anna Hazare admitted to ICU in Mumbai after kidney issues

source.summary: Milky Mist Dairy Food reported a significant surge in financial performance for the quarter ended June. The company's consolidated net profit jumped 889.8% year-on-year to ₹64.68 crore, while revenue from operations rose 43.6% to ₹973.45 crore. Strong growth in its summer portfolio and paneer sales supported these results. The stock listed at a premium of 17.85% over its issue price following robust investor demand.
source.title: Milky Mist Dairy Food reports strong Q1 profit and revenue growth

source.summary: Union Minister Chirag Paswan received a death threat via an unsigned postal communication on Tuesday, his office said. The message warned he would be killed by hardcore terrorists and included two mobile numbers. Paswan's office wrote to the Union Home Secretary seeking an urgent investigation into the threat's origin and authenticity. Officials also requested a review and potential augmentation of the minister's existing Z-category security arrangements. Further details regarding the source of the threat are awaited.
source.title: Chirag Paswan receives death threat via unsigned postal communication

source.summary: NVIDIA and CrowdStrike announced SafeMind, a new agentic cybersecurity system designed to counter automated attacks. Jensen Huang and George Kurtz stated that defense must evolve as quickly as offense. The system combines CrowdStrike's threat data with NVIDIA Nemotron models in a continuous coevolution loop. CrowdStrike also unveiled Falcon IQ to automate security workflows using over 50 agents. The companies tested SafeMind in a high-fidelity simulation of NVIDIA's infrastructure. Huang noted that AI-enabled attacks rose 89% in the past year. Kurtz emphasized that defenders now possess asymmetric advantages through this collaboration.
source.title: NVIDIA and CrowdStrike Announce SafeMind Agentic Cybersecurity System

source.summary: ZS Associates reports that it built a security-hardened Amazon SageMaker environment to balance developer agility with strict governance in regulated industries. The platform now serves over 1,000 daily active users across more than 200 SageMaker domains. ZS implemented a multi-tenant architecture with isolated volumes and IAM roles to ensure strong isolation and granular cost tracking. The solution runs in internet-free mode by default, using Amazon VPC endpoints for controlled communication with required AWS services. ZS integrated JFrog Artifactory for package management to prevent unauthorized code entry. The firm states that monthly SageMaker spend exceeds $50,000, while Savings Plans save approximately $10,000 per month. Custom implementations include automated backups, secure package installation, and self-service tools to reduce manual compliance overhead. ZS continues exploring features like Model Registry and Pipelines to extend governance controls into production workloads.
source.title: ZS Associates builds secure Amazon SageMaker platform for regulated analytics

source.summary: Boomi introduces Boomi Scribe, an AI-powered agent running on AWS that automates the creation and maintenance of technical documentation for complex enterprise integrations. The solution addresses the persistent technical debt caused by manual documentation efforts, which often lead to inconsistencies and compliance gaps. Boomi Scribe parses integration processes into Directed Acyclic Graphs and utilizes Amazon Bedrock and Claude models to generate accurate, user-friendly documentation automatically. The architecture leverages Amazon SageMaker for intent classification, Amazon S3 for storage, and AWS Lambda to orchestrate the pipeline across Boomi's 33,000 customers. By comparing version changes, the tool provides developers with concrete insights to improve planning and auditing. Boomi reports that the solution reduces time spent on documentation by up to 85 percent while ensuring accuracy across hundreds of daily processes.
source.title: Boomi Scribe automates documentation for enterprise workflows using AWS AI

source.summary: Matt Clifford, the architect of the UK government's AI strategy, has joined US startup Anthropic as managing director for international affairs. Clifford will lead engagement with governments outside the US while remaining chair of government-backed Aria. A not-for-profit campaign group raised concerns about the revolving door between government and industry. MP Chi Onwurah expressed some concern that Clifford is taking his knowledge to a global AI player so soon after leaving government. Anthropic stated it hires people with expertise who understand how government works.
source.title: Matt Clifford joins Anthropic as managing director for international affairs

source.summary: Anthropic released Claude Fable 5.1, which the company says sets a new standard for coding and long-running problem-solving tasks. The model achieved a 52.6% score on the Terminal-Bench-Science 0.1 benchmark. A user tested the model's reasoning capabilities by generating SVGs of a pelican riding a bicycle at five different effort levels. Results showed that low and medium settings skipped reasoning entirely, while max effort produced a detailed image in 13 minutes and 54 seconds. The user then animated the max effort SVG for $1.37, noting minor wheel rotation artifacts in the video conversion. The article highlights how reasoning effort levels significantly impact output quality and cost.
source.title: Anthropic's Claude Fable 5.1 generates animated pelican SVGs

source.summary: OpenAI announced its upcoming Astra model, the first large language model to meet its critical cybersecurity threshold. The company stated the model can autonomously discover and exploit unknown security flaws in computer systems. OpenAI reported that Astra achieved a perfect score on ExploitBench and found two zero-day vulnerabilities during testing. To mitigate risks, the firm is implementing new safety techniques, including restricted access for high-risk accounts and additional monitoring. However, without third-party confirmation, it remains difficult to fully evaluate the model's safety measures before its public release.
source.title: OpenAI unveils Astra model designed to find and exploit computer security flaws

source.summary: Databricks has released the Big Book of AgentOps, a new guide designed to help enterprise teams build and manage reliable AI agents in production. The authors report that this resource codifies essential practices including architecture patterns, evaluation loops, and governance strategies to prevent operational complexity from becoming a liability. The book outlines four specific deployment architectures and highlights common anti-patterns that often stall pilot projects. It also details a seven-phase roadmap for implementation, emphasizing the need for stakeholder alignment and continuous learning. Databricks notes that the guide draws on principles from The DevOps Handbook to address the unique challenges of non-deterministic agent systems. The publication aims to assist engineers, product owners, and security teams in transitioning promising AI pilots into dependable, scalable enterprise solutions.
source.title: Databricks releases Big Book of AgentOps to guide production AI agent deployment

source.summary: Amazon announced the launch of a new Alexa for Shopping feature named Update Me When on Tuesday. The tool sends personalized notifications when new products or events relevant to a user occur. Amazon stated the feature helps anticipate purchases before shoppers ask. Other highlighted AI tools include price tracking and automated buying capabilities.
source.title: Amazon Alexa launches new shopping alert feature called Update Me When

source.summary:
The FDA described its modernization of a federal data platform using Databricks on AWS GovCloud during a Data + AI Summit session. The agency reported that this initiative created a secure, AI-ready foundation to address siloed data and operational overhead. Key points include:

*   The FDA migrated over 5,000 users and 8,000 jobs with zero downtime while refactoring thousands of pipelines.
*   The agency consolidated more than 40 data sources to improve collaboration and strengthen its security posture.
*   According to the FDA, query response times improved by more than 30% and compute costs fell by over 20%.
*   User adoption grew from roughly 500 in 2020 to more than 6,000, with expectations to exceed 10,000 by 2028.

The FDA emphasized that governance is the prerequisite for AI, integrating the platform with its enterprise AI tools to support responsible, human-in-the-loop innovation.
source.title: FDA builds secure AI foundation on Databricks for Government

source.summary: Researchers introduce BenchMIRT, a new method for auditing large language model benchmarks by analyzing individual prompts. The authors report that BenchMIRT applies multidimensional Item Response Theory to separate underlying capabilities like safety and general reasoning. The team trained the tool on results from 100 LLMs across 16 benchmarks and more than 34,000 questions. Analysis revealed that some benchmarks, such as BBQ and WMDP, align more strongly with general reasoning than their intended safety goals. BenchMIRT can also identify the most informative questions, predicting model performance on unseen items 79% of the time. The authors note limitations, including the use of models released by March 2025 and potential risks if informative questions are removed from evaluations.
source.title: Researchers introduce BenchMIRT to audit LLM benchmarks at the prompt level

source.summary: MIT School of Architecture and Planning Dean Hashim Sarkis announced that Walter Torous will serve as executive director of the MIT Center for Real Estate starting July 1, 2026. Justin Steil will act as faculty chair of the Academic Curriculum Council to guide the center's academic and strategic direction. Torous will oversee teaching, fundraising, and staff while continuing to direct the Master of Science in Real Estate Development Program. He plans to expand the curriculum across the Institute and engage over 1,200 alumni to train future leaders in technology and financial markets. Torous, an economist specializing in real estate finance, aims to integrate AI and machine learning into the program to address current market changes.
source.title: Walter Torous named executive director of MIT Center for Real Estate

source.summary: Ai2 researchers introduce BenchMIRT, a new method for auditing large language model benchmarks by analyzing individual prompts. The authors report that BenchMIRT applies multidimensional Item Response Theory to separate underlying capabilities like safety and general reasoning within single evaluations. Analysis of 100 models across 16 benchmarks revealed that some tests, such as BBQ and WMDP, align more strongly with reasoning than their intended safety goals. The tool also identifies the most informative questions, showing that keeping only 10% of items can preserve nearly the same model ranking as the full set. Ai2 states that BenchMIRT correctly predicted model performance on held-out questions 79% of the time, outperforming simpler approaches. The authors note limitations regarding models released after March 2025 and warn that question-level detail could allow unsafe models to pass trimmed evaluations.
source.title: Ai2 introduces BenchMIRT to audit LLM benchmarks at the prompt level

source.summary: Paint.NET author Rick Brewster announced a new internal rewrite of Direct2D for WINE compatibility. The code, located in PaintDotNet.Windows.Direct2D1.Managed.dll, was generated by Claude without thorough review. Brewster noted the 180,000 lines of code were written in a "vibe coded" style. He admitted to babysitting the AI to fix resource management and architecture issues.
source.title: Paint.NET author Rick Brewster credits Claude for rewriting Direct2D

source.summary: Approximately 2,000 University of Sydney staff walked off the job on Wednesday to protest artificial intelligence usage and job security concerns. The National Tertiary Education Union reported that zero percent of arts and social sciences faculty trust the university to act in their best interests. Union leaders stated management has repeatedly refused to enforce appropriate AI protections, while the university maintains industrial action is premature. The strike disrupted classes, with most moving online or being cancelled. Broader grievances include growing class sizes, reduced student satisfaction, and new restrictions on protest following the Gaza encampment. Despite police presence, picket lines maintained a jovial atmosphere as staff and students demonstrated solidarity.
source.title: University of Sydney staff strike over AI protections and job security

source.summary: Shopify COO Jess Hertz discussed the company's growth strategy during an interview on Rapid Response. She noted that nearly 90% of quarterly revenue comes from merchants on the platform for over a year. Hertz described Sidekick as an AI-powered commerce agent helping merchants sell more. She also highlighted the Catalog product layer designed to make products discoverable by AI. The interview covered how these tools increase conversion rates compared to using scraped data.
source.title: Shopify COO Jess Hertz explains the company's AI strategy and infrastructure

source.summary: Consumer group Which? created a fake listing for 10 Downing Street on Booking.com, which remained active for two months. The platform removed the bogus property only after Which? researchers successfully booked a stay and left a review. Booking.com stated its fraud controls were not triggered because the listing was not fully live. Which? criticized the site's AI systems as unfit for purpose and called for stricter enforcement under the Online Safety Act.
source.title: Consumer group exposes fake 10 Downing Street listing on Booking.com

source.summary: Pyka and other companies are racing to bring autonomous fixed-wing aircraft into commercial service, initially for crop spraying and cargo delivery. Pyka's electric planes, which can fly for about 35 minutes, are already operating in Brazil and recently received US authorization for limited agricultural use. While eVTOLs capture much attention, these self-flying planes aim to eventually carry passengers. Experts note that aircraft face stricter safety standards than cars, slowing deployment despite military interest helping propel the technology. Companies differ in their approaches, with some retrofitting existing planes while others build from scratch, and varying strategies regarding AI usage and air traffic control communication.
source.title: Pyka and rivals race to deploy self-flying planes for cargo and farming

source.summary: The government of Bangladesh announced a new incentive tariff of $0.086 per kilowatt-hour for surplus electricity from eligible rooftop solar systems. The Power Division stated the rate includes a 20% profit margin and an 11.25% premium over a benchmark generation cost of $0.065/kWh. Consumers installing systems by February 28, 2027, will receive payments for three years to help reach a 5 GW net-metering target. Mostafa Al Mahmud of the Bangladesh Sustainable and Renewable Energy Association welcomed the move as a commitment to renewable energy expansion.
source.title: Bangladesh sets $0.086/kWh tariff for rooftop solar surplus power

source.summary: Ørsted announced the completion of major construction works for its 920 MW Greater Changhua offshore wind farms in Taiwan. The project is expected to enter full commercial operation in late Q3 2026. Ørsted Group President and CEO Rasmus Errboe stated the milestone supports the company's global construction programme. The facility will supply electricity to approximately two million households annually.
source.title: Ørsted Completes Major Construction on 920 MW Taiwan Offshore Wind Project

source.summary: US colleges are introducing three-year bachelor's degree programs that require fewer credits, potentially saving students up to $20,000. These programs, now available in 26 states, allow students to graduate with 90 credit hours instead of the traditional 120. The shift is driven by rising tuition costs and the desire for students to enter the workforce sooner. Programs are common in countries like the UK and India but are relatively new in the US. Critics argue the change could reduce academic rigor and raise concerns about employer recognition. Some fields, like engineering and teacher education, face challenges in compressing requirements. Ohio is exploring similar programs, with plans to offer two 90-credit degrees by 2028.
source.title: US colleges offer three-year bachelor's degrees to cut costs and graduation time

source.summary: The Indian Meteorological Department (IMD) reported a glacier lake outburst from the Tibetan side, causing rapid water surges that threaten the Gandak river and surrounding areas. The agency activated emergency SMS alerts for riverbanks in Rasuwa, Nuwakot, Dhading, Gorkha, and Chitwan, warning of a rapidly advancing flood wave expected to converge at the Marshyangdi confluence. The flood, suspected to be a Glacial Lake Outburst Flood (GLOF), caused widespread destruction in northern Rasuwa and resulted in casualties, with nearly 500 people, including 133 Indians, missing. Prime Minister Narendra Modi expressed condolences to Nepal's PM and pledged India's support for humanitarian aid and rescue efforts. The Embassy of India provided emergency contact numbers for affected Indian nationals.
source.title: IMD warns of glacier lake outburst and flood risks in Nepal

source.summary: Vanguard Group has agreed to acquire Altruist, a wealth management technology company, for about $4 billion, according to a Wall Street Journal report. The deal, expected to close later this year, aims to enhance Vanguard's presence in financial advice and independent advisory services. Altruist provides tools for account management and portfolio services to financial advisers, competing with Schwab and Fidelity. Vanguard's CEO, Salim Ramji, emphasized the opportunity to support advisers in serving clients more effectively. The acquisition follows Vanguard's recent expansion into wealth management, including the 2021 purchase of Just Invest. Altruist will continue operating as a standalone business, retaining its leadership and brand.
source.title: Vanguard Acquires Altruist for $4 Billion to Expand Wealth Management Services

source.summary: Teenagers in North-East Delhi are joining gangs and acquiring weapons before starting school, according to a report. The article describes how these underage offenders, supplied with knives and homemade pistols by older gang members, engage in criminal activities. Legal experts note that the Juvenile Justice Act limits their maximum sentence to three years, incentivizing larger gangs to recruit minors. The report highlights the systemic issues contributing to youth involvement in crime, with sources indicating that some gangsters actively recruit underage members for their low legal risk.
source.title: Delhi's Teen Gangs: Armed Youth and Legal Loopholes

source.summary: Three men from Telangana were killed in a car accident near Palm Bay, Florida, after their vehicle crashed into a tree and caught fire. Rahul, a 26-year-old from Nizamabad, was hospitalized but later died. His father, an assistant sub-inspector, stated the accident occurred around 9:49 am on Interstate 95. The other two victims, identified as his flatmates from Telangana, died at the scene. The Florida Highway Patrol reported the crash, and the Telugu Association of North America is assisting with repatriation efforts.
source.title: Three Telangana men killed in Florida car crash near Palm Bay

source.summary: Bharat Electronics Ltd. (BEL) announced a ₹730 crore order for various defense equipment, including communication systems and cybersecurity solutions. This follows recent contracts worth ₹541 crore and ₹847 crore, contributing to a 5% stock rebound in August. BEL's revenue rose 25.3% YoY to ₹5,533 crore, though net profit declined sequentially. The stock has gained 1,275% over seven years, with strong annual returns in each year.
source.title: Bharat Electronics secures ₹730 crore order, boosts investor confidence

source.summary: The Union government has confirmed that the 2027 Census will include caste enumeration, but concerns persist over its design. The pre-test rehearsal indicated potential issues, with the open-ended caste question remaining despite past failures. The 2011 Socio-Economic Caste Census (SECC) failed due to similar issues, including the absence of predefined categories for 'Other Backward Classes' and 'General' groups, leading to over 4.6 million distinct responses. The 2027 Census is repeating these mistakes by not including these categories and using open-ended data collection. Experts warn that without structural changes, such as updated lists for OBC and General categories, and improved enumerator training, the census risks repeating the SECC's failure. Public oversight and lessons from past mistakes are urged to ensure a successful caste enumeration.
source.title: Census 2027's Caste Enumeration Faces Same Structural Failures as SECC

source.summary: The Tamil Nadu government, led by the Tamilaga Vettri Kazhagam (TVK), canceled the Parandur greenfield airport project, fulfilling an election promise. Chief Minister C. Joseph Vijay announced the cancellation after visiting the site ahead of the 2026 Assembly election. The government plans to build a new international airport near Chennai, with alternative locations to be identified. Farmers in affected villages expressed gratitude, but concerns remain about land repurposing and legal challenges. The land acquired under the Tamil Nadu Acquisition of Land for Industrial Purposes Act, 1997, may be used for industrial projects, though legal ambiguities persist. Political parties, including the Tamil Nadu Congress Committee, support the decision but demand clarity on the future of the land and compensation. The cancellation has sparked debate over Tamil Nadu's development and the need for a second airport to address Chennai's growing air traffic demands.
source.title: Tamil Nadu cancels Parandur airport project, faces land repurposing challenges

source.summary: A viral video falsely claims Jawaharlal Nehru stated he opposed India's independence fight. The video, however, is cropped and mislabeled. In the full 1964 interview, Nehru discusses Muhammad Ali Jinnah's opposition to independence, not his own. The original clip shows Nehru saying Jinnah 'opposed it,' refuting the misleading claim. The Quint verified this by analyzing the video's context and full version.
source.title: Nehru's Interview Clarifies He Spoke About Jinnah's Opposition, Not His Own

source.summary: The article introduces the COMPASS framework, a unified approach for training cross-embodiment robot navigation policies using residual reinforcement learning. It leverages expert demonstrations from a single embodiment to enable scalable mobility across different robots and environments. The framework reuses pre-trained navigation behavior from the NVIDIA X-Mobility policy, training a residual specialist policy that corrects base actions for specific robots and scenes. The workflow includes agent-driven development, with a coding agent handling validation, asset preparation, training, and diagnostics. Human approval gates control scene acceptance and checkpoint promotion. The tutorial demonstrates the process using Boston Dynamics' Spot robot, with examples involving built-in scenes, generated SAGE-10K scenes, and reconstructed environments via NVIDIA Omniverse NuRec. The COMPASS framework is packaged as repository skills, supporting tools like Codex and Claude Code for automation, and requires specific hardware and software configurations for deployment.
source.title: COMPASS Framework Enables Cross-Embodiment Robot Navigation via Residual RL

source.summary: Google Research introduces GlucoFM, a self-supervised foundation model for continuous glucose monitoring. The model separates slow glycemic trends from short-term deviations using a dual-stream design, enhancing performance in diabetes risk assessment and other metabolic predictions. Evaluated across four cohorts and seven tasks, GlucoFM outperformed existing models like GluFormer, achieving higher PR-AUC and lower MAE in postprandial glucose forecasting. The model's ability to handle missing data and adapt with limited labeled examples highlights its efficiency. Researchers suggest further work on larger, more diverse datasets and multi-day modeling to improve long-term metabolic insights.
source.title: GlucoFM: Dual-stream model improves glucose prediction across metabolic tasks

source.summary: A new study highlights the risks of relying on majority votes from LLM judges, arguing that agreement may stem from shared biases rather than independent analysis. The paper introduces a method using Ising models to assess correlations between judges' outputs, adjusting aggregate scores to account for dependence. Testing on tasks like relevance classification and toxicity detection showed improvements of 9-14% over traditional weighted majority voting. The approach treats judge panels as networks, identifying redundant agreement and complementary perspectives. Key findings include the importance of evaluating judge diversity, inspecting agreement patterns, and reporting uncertainty with dependence in mind. The method works without human labels, learning from evaluation logs to infer true labels and judge reliability.
source.title: LLM judges' agreement may reflect shared biases, not independent evidence

source.summary: Alibaba released the Qwen3.8-Flash-Next model, a 176B parameter multimodal MoE model, for developers to experiment with. It features a 262,144-token context window, extendable to 1M tokens. The model uses a hybrid architecture combining Gated DeltaNet and Qwen Sparse Attention to address context length challenges. NVIDIA provides support through SGLang, vLLM, and TensorRT LLM on the GB300 NVL72 platform. Benchmarks show Qwen3.8-Flash-Next achieves up to 7.6x speedup in prefill tasks. The model runs on local NVIDIA hardware and can be fine-tuned using NVIDIA NeMo AutoModel for domain-specific applications.
source.title: Alibaba Introduces Qwen3.8-Flash-Next 176B Model for Agentic Coding on NVIDIA GB300 NVL72

source.summary: Google has introduced Gemini 3.5 Transcribe, a new speech-to-text model designed for intelligent voice interactions. This model improves upon previous versions by handling background noise, complex jargon, and disfluency cleanup, converting raw audio into accurate, formatted text. Available through the Gemini API in Google AI Studio and the Gemini Enterprise Agent Platform, it offers two main APIs: real-time streaming for interactive voice apps and pre-recorded audio processing with speaker attribution and timestamps. The model achieves a 4.0% Word Error Rate for streaming and 2.6% for non-streaming use-cases, with support for 85 languages and multi-speaker identification. It also enables function calling for complex tasks and integrates with various Google products like Gboard, Antigravity, and the Gemini app, enhancing voice-driven workflows and dictation capabilities.
source.title: Google Launches Gemini 3.5 Transcribe for Enhanced Speech-to-Text Capabilities

source.summary: Thai researchers modified the Dolma toolkit to develop a 47-billion-token Thai pretraining corpus called Mangosteen. They addressed gaps in existing Thai datasets by incorporating books, research papers, and YouTube subtitles while filtering out unsuitable content. The team adapted Dolma's pipeline for Thai language specifics, such as adjusting deduplication methods and quality filters. Their work resulted in a dataset that outperformed larger, less curated collections in Thai cultural knowledge tests. The project highlights how open-source tools can enable local customization of AI systems.
source.title: Thai researchers adapt Dolma to create tailored language model dataset

source.summary: Researchers propose an integrated enlarge-and-prune pipeline for generative language models, combining model expansion, pruning, and recovery under a single learning rate schedule. The method addresses knowledge loss during pruning by redistributing model capacity among surviving neurons. Experiments show compressing 2.8B models to 1.3B with up to 2T tokens in pretraining improves token efficiency and pruned model performance. The approach includes an iterative structured pruning method for gradual parameter removal.
source.title: IDEA Prune: Integrated Enlarge-and-Prune Pipeline for Efficient Language Model Training

source.summary: Researchers introduce PROOF-Gen, a method that recovers successful trajectories from failed tool-calling attempts by optimizing per-scenario prompts. The approach analyzes execution traces and feedback to generate corrective guidance, which is then used to train models without task-specific scaffolding. On τ 2-bench, PROOF-Gen recovers 93% of failed scenarios, significantly improving performance metrics for Qwen3-4B-Instruct-2507 and Gemma 4 E4B-it. Deployed pipelines show increased goal completion and response quality, with positive transfer across different locales.
source.title: PROOF-Gen improves tool-calling models by optimizing failed generation scenarios

source.summary: The article explores advanced usage patterns of the MCP (Multi-Client Protocol) framework, emphasizing its ability to connect multiple servers and clients for complex AI workflows. It highlights scenarios where MCP enables cross-app tasks, such as filing expense receipts through Gmail and Benepass, and integrating multiple interfaces like Slack, Linear, and Claude.ai. The text discusses challenges with local servers and advocates for remote deployment, using tools like mcp-auth-wrapper to convert local servers into remote, multitenant ones. It also addresses configuration friction, suggesting solutions like install-mcp and mcp-aggregator to streamline setup and authentication. The article concludes by demonstrating how MCP can be embedded into SaaS applications and even games, showcasing its versatility and potential for both individuals and enterprises.
source.title: MCP Patterns Enable Multi-Server Integration for AI Workflows

source.summary: Google's Gemini app introduces multiple branded AI features like Spark and Daily Brief, complicating user experience by requiring task-specific mode switching. The article argues this branding undermines the app's promise of simplicity, as features like Daily Brief offer unclear, potentially intrusive updates. Spark, while useful as an AI agent, is unnecessarily branded. The piece criticizes the broader AI industry for exposing internal architecture to users, contrasting with Apple's approach to Siri and text-based AI services, which prioritize simplicity and intuitive interfaces.
source.title: Google's Gemini app faces branding confusion in AI features

source.summary: OpenAI has experienced a wave of executive departures, including key roles like COO and CRO, as the company prepares for an IPO. The firm, known for its advanced models like GPT-5.6, faces challenges with growing losses despite rising revenue. Executives cite reorganization and health issues for their exits, with some, like Chris Malone, leaving due to restructuring. Greg Brockman, OpenAI's president, is reasserting leadership, overseeing infrastructure and product teams. The company filed for an IPO in June, though the timeline is delayed to 2027, raising questions about its financial health compared to rivals like Anthropic. Brockman's growing influence may help streamline operations ahead of the IPO.
source.title: OpenAI's Leadership Changes Amid IPO Plans and Internal Reorganization
