source.summary: Google Research and Google Cloud have introduced an agentic RAG framework designed to handle complex, multi-source enterprise queries more effectively than traditional RAG systems. The new system breaks down queries into specialized roles, allowing agents to iteratively search for context and ensure sufficient information before generating responses. Unlike standard RAG, which may stop at incomplete data, the agentic RAG includes a Sufficient Context Agent that identifies gaps and directs further searches. This framework improves accuracy on factuality datasets by up to 34% and performs well in cross-corpus scenarios, achieving 90.1% accuracy in testing. The system is now available as a public preview in the Gemini Enterprise Agent Platform.
source.title: Google Introduces Agentic RAG Framework for Complex Query Handling

source.summary: Promptimus is a system that automatically optimizes well-developed prompts for large language models (LLMs), improving performance without requiring manual engineering. The method is model-agnostic, allowing it to reoptimize prompts for different target models. It uses performance metrics and a four-step iteration loop to identify failure points and make targeted refinements. Promptimus includes an edit mode for preserving complex, structured prompts while making specific changes. The system was tested across 20 benchmarks, achieving the best results on 16 of them. It also improved performance on enterprise tasks like code generation and multimodal understanding, with gains ranging from 3.18% to 90.27%. The approach is sample-efficient, requiring only 20–50 examples, and is available through Amazon Bedrock for enterprise use.
source.title: Promptimus Enhances Existing LLM Prompts Without Manual Engineering

source.summary: Ai2, in partnership with the National Science Foundation (NSF) and NVIDIA, has launched the Open Multimodal AI Infrastructure for Science (NSF OMAI), a fully open AI infrastructure project. The initiative, funded with $152 million, aims to create an ecosystem where researchers can access, reuse, and build upon shared AI models, tools, and training data. By deploying NVIDIA Blackwell Ultra-powered systems, Ai2 is enabling a more collaborative approach to AI research, emphasizing openness and reuse to maximize the impact of computational resources. The project's goal is to foster innovation and U.S. leadership in AI by supporting a broader research community. Recent research highlights the benefits of open infrastructure, showing that shared work can lead to more efficient use of computational resources and greater scientific progress. Ai2's efforts include developing open-source models like Molmo 2 and Olmo Hybrid, which are designed to be adaptable and reusable for various scientific applications.
source.title: Ai2 launches open AI infrastructure with NSF OMAI to boost research collaboration

source.summary: Amazon's logistics team faces the challenge of optimizing its middle-mile network, which connects fulfillment centers to customers, under conditions of uncertainty. The network must adapt to daily variations in demand and travel times, as well as larger disruptions like weather events or facility outages. Engineers use advanced computational tools to model and manage these uncertainties, employing techniques like mixed-integer optimization and Monte Carlo simulations. A key innovation is the use of graph attention networks to capture spatial and demand correlations between facilities and destinations. These models generate realistic demand scenarios and stress-test network designs, ensuring flexibility and reliability. By focusing on small efficiency gains, Amazon aims to maintain reliable delivery promises even during peak periods or unexpected disruptions.
source.title: Amazon Optimizes Middle-Mile Network for Uncertainty

source.summary: The company has open-sourced MolmoAct 2, a robotics foundation model, along with its training data and evaluation rollouts, enabling researchers to adapt and extend the model. MolmoAct 2 outperforms proprietary models on industry benchmarks, handles real-world tasks without fine-tuning, and runs 37x faster than its predecessor. The release includes the MolmoAct 2-Bimanual YAM dataset, the largest open-source bimanual robotics dataset, and an open-source tokenizer. The model's architecture was reimagined with a specialized embodied-reasoning variant, Molmo 2-ER, which improves performance on embodied-reasoning benchmarks. MolmoAct 2 also features an adaptive-depth mechanism for efficient 3D reasoning and is evaluated across simulation, adaptation, and real-world tasks, achieving high success rates. The model is designed for deployment in real-world environments, supporting natural-language instructions and visual guidance, with a reference hardware setup provided for researchers. Pilots with research partners, including Stanford's Cong Lab, show potential for accelerating scientific discovery through automated lab tasks.
source.title: MolmoAct 2 Open-Sourced for Robotics Research and Real-World Deployment

source.summary: NIST scientists and collaborators have developed integrated photonics chips capable of generating light across a wide range of wavelengths. These chips, created by depositing specialized materials onto silicon wafers, use nonlinear materials like tantalum pentoxide to transform single laser colors into a full spectrum of visible and infrared light. The technology could significantly advance quantum computing, optical atomic clocks, and artificial intelligence by enabling compact, efficient light processing. The researchers demonstrated the ability to fit 10,000 photonic circuits on a single wafer, each producing a unique color. While not yet ready for mass production, the technique offers a path for scaling up the technology, with collaboration from a startup company working to commercialize the innovation.
source.title: NIST Scientists Develop Photonics Chips That Generate Light in Any Color

source.summary: Researchers at the National Institute of Standards and Technology (NIST) have developed a new photonic chip packaging method that can withstand extreme environments. The technique, called hydroxide catalysis bonding (HCB), uses a sodium hydroxide solution to create a stable, inorganic bond between optical fibers and photonic chips. This method ensures precise alignment and efficient light coupling, allowing photonic circuits to function in harsh conditions like cryogenic temperatures, intense radiation, and high vacuum. NIST tested the packaging by exposing it to extreme conditions, confirming its resilience. While the current process takes several days, the team believes it can be scaled for manufacturing with further development.
source.title: NIST Creates Robust Photonic Chip Packaging for Extreme Conditions

source.summary: Mistral Small 4, the latest release in the Mistral Small family, integrates the capabilities of Magistral, Pixtral, and Devstral into a single model. The model supports text and image inputs, offering versatile applications for chat, coding, and complex reasoning. It features a 256k context window, configurable reasoning effort, and a 119B parameter architecture. Mistral Small 4 is released under Apache 2.0 and optimized for both latency and throughput, achieving 40% faster completion times and 3x higher request rates than its predecessor. The model outperforms GPT-OSS 120B and Qwen models in benchmarks, generating shorter outputs with comparable accuracy. It is available on multiple platforms and optimized for NVIDIA hardware, with enterprise deployment options and open-source flexibility.
source.title: Mistral Small 4 Unifies Reasoning, Coding, and Multimodal Capabilities

source.summary: Mistral AI and NVIDIA have joined forces as founding members of the NVIDIA Nemotron Coalition to co-develop open-source AI models. The partnership combines Mistral's model architecture and platform with NVIDIA's compute resources and tools. Mistral will contribute training techniques and multimodal capabilities, while leveraging NVIDIA's infrastructure to scale model training. The coalition's first initiative is a base model trained on NVIDIA DGX Cloud, which will underpin the upcoming NVIDIA Nemotron 4 family. The collaboration aims to advance open, frontier-level foundation models, promote transparency, and enable developers to build AI applications on a shared, open foundation.
source.title: Mistral AI and NVIDIA collaborate on open-source AI model development

source.summary: EarthGrid's tunnel boring machine, capable of melting through granite at 27,000C, successfully tested in California, offering a new method for underground infrastructure. The machine, which uses plasma torches to create a vortex for debris removal, could enable faster and safer tunneling for power, fiber optic, and pipeline projects. Engineers note rising demand for underground infrastructure due to vulnerabilities exposed by conflicts like Ukraine's war with Russia. While the machine over-bored slightly during testing, adjustments are planned for commercial deployment by next year. Experts highlight the growing trend of 'data bunker boom' with underground data centers, such as Trentino DataMine in Italy, offering natural protection and cooling. Subsea internet cables are also increasingly buried to reduce damage from anchors. Despite advancements, challenges like gas release and flooding remain, with tunneling costs still high compared to above-ground alternatives. In the UK, while some projects like London Power Tunnels use underground infrastructure, cost-effectiveness often favors above-ground solutions with redundancy.
source.title: EarthGrid's tunnel boring machine tests underground infrastructure solutions

source.summary: A developer has enhanced their markdown-svg-renderer tool to allow sharing of Markdown transcripts with SVG documents. The tool converts SVG into rendered visuals and offers tabs for PNG, JPEG, and MP4 formats. The MP4 tab uses FFMPEG compiled to WebAssembly to convert animated SVG into video, enabling sharing on platforms that do not support SVG animation natively. The tool allows users to paste Markdown or URLs to rendered content, with examples provided.
source.title: Markdown SVG tool enables animated SVG sharing via MP4 conversion

source.summary: The article reviews the Qwen 3.8 27B, a 27B parameter vision-capable LLM from Alibaba's Qwen research lab. The model defaults to 'xhigh' reasoning effort, leading to excessive overthinking and significantly slowing performance, especially on consumer hardware. The author tested the model on a MacBook Pro and an NVIDIA DGX Spark, noting that the default setting uses up context tokens quickly and results in long processing times. While the model produces high-quality outputs, such as detailed SVGs and accurate bounding boxes, the default reasoning level is deemed impractical. The author recommends using lower reasoning settings for better efficiency. The model also shows promise in coding agent tasks, though its speed remains a concern compared to hosted API models. The article highlights potential optimizations like Multi-Token Prediction to improve inference performance.
source.title: Qwen 3.8 27B Model Defaults to Overthinking, Slows Performance

source.summary: Leading U.S. AI firms OpenAI and Anthropic are lowering prices to retain cost-sensitive customers shifting to cheaper Chinese alternatives. OpenAI reduced GPT-5.6 Luna prices by 80%, while Anthropic introduced Claude Opus 5 at half the cost of Fable 5. Prices for U.S. models dropped nearly 25% since mid-July, according to Silicon Data. The shift reflects growing competition from open-source Chinese models and pressure from rising AI costs. Companies like DoorDash and Airbnb are testing Chinese models to cut expenses. U.S. firms also transition to usage-based billing, while planning IPOs at trillion-dollar valuations.
source.title: OpenAI and Anthropic cut prices to compete with Chinese AI firms

source.summary: The article explores the concept of intent debt in software development, distinguishing it from technical and cognitive debt. It argues that intent debt arises from the absence or erosion of externalized rationale, goals, and constraints that explain why a system is designed a certain way. Unlike technical debt, which can be addressed by AI agents, intent debt cannot be resolved by machines because it requires human input. The article highlights how agents exacerbate intent debt by failing to understand unexternalized intent, leading to costly misunderstandings. It emphasizes the need to document intent as a first-class artifact to ensure systems remain aligned with their original purpose, especially in an era where AI plays an increasing role in software development.
source.title: Intent Debt: The Unwritten Reason Behind Software Systems

source.summary: Flock, a police-tech company, is introducing new rules to address concerns about surveillance and officer abuse. The changes include requiring officers to enter a criminal case number before conducting searches and expanding an automatic auditing system to monitor suspicious activity. These measures aim to prevent unauthorized use of Flock's license plate reader network, which has been linked to 46 cases of alleged stalking by officers. The company also recommends shorter data retention periods and limits on cross-departmental searches. Despite these steps, critics argue the changes are insufficient and call for greater transparency and independent oversight. The backlash against Flock includes lost contracts, legislative bans on license plate readers, and criticism from civil liberties groups like the ACLU. Flock's CEO attributes the backlash to misinformation, while critics accuse the company of misleading city officials about its technology's capabilities.
source.title: Flock Implements New Safeguards Amid Surveillance Backlash

source.summary: A 2026 survey of over 700 professionals reveals that data work, not data collection, determines success in visual and physical AI. The report highlights that 78% of teams see value from these technologies, yet 74% believe the field is underinvested. Teams that successfully deploy AI invest nearly three times more in data work than those that struggle. Annotation is costly and inefficient, as teams often label excessive data, leading to significant waste before production. The study emphasizes that data curation is more important than pursuing larger models for achieving production success.
source.title: Data Curation Critical for Success in Visual and Physical AI

source.summary: An author who wrote a textbook on reinforcement learning from human feedback discusses the current state of AI writing capabilities. While AI models have made significant strides in tasks like coding and mathematics, they still struggle with long-form, non-fiction writing. The author notes that models like GPT-4.5 and Claude have not improved as much in writing quality as in other domains, suggesting that writing requires a different kind of intelligence. The author used AI tools extensively during the writing process, including for editing and formatting, but acknowledges the limitations of AI in capturing the depth and nuance of human expression. The author expresses optimism about AI's potential in scientific work but emphasizes the importance of human oversight in critical writing tasks. The piece highlights the challenges of using AI for non-fiction writing, where the ability to organize and present complex ideas coherently remains a significant hurdle for current models.
source.title: Author reflects on AI's limitations in non-fiction writing despite progress in other areas

source.summary: An author has published a textbook titled 'Reinforcement Learning from Human Feedback: Aligning and Post-training LLMs' through Manning. The book aims to explain post-training techniques for large language models (LLMs) in simple terms, covering topics like rejection sampling, outcome reward models, and character training. It includes a 12-hour course, code examples, and model comparisons. The author notes that while the title is somewhat outdated, the content is fresh and includes a section on on-policy distillation. The book is targeted at readers with a bachelor's degree in computer science and is intended to help them understand the intuition behind RL algorithms, system design challenges, historical context, distillation techniques, and practical post-training challenges.
source.title: Author publishes post-training textbook on RL and LLM alignment

source.summary: A team of researchers evaluated whether frontier AI agents could conduct open-ended AI research by having them draft papers based on questions posed by human researchers. The agents' resulting papers were rejected by the original authors, highlighting several limitations. The agents lacked judgment, awareness of available resources, creativity in responding to feedback, and the ability to backtrack. They also failed to follow explicit instructions. The study, called 'shadow evaluations,' aims to test agents on novel tasks and involves collaboration with experts. While the findings suggest challenges in achieving recursive self-improvement through AI agents, the researchers acknowledge limitations in their methodology and plan to address them by increasing sample size and testing with new models. The study also raises questions about potential bottlenecks in AI progress, such as compute limits and data collection needs, and their impact on the pace of innovation.
source.title: Researchers find frontier AI agents struggle with open-ended research tasks

source.summary: The author, a Princeton researcher, discusses the implications of AI's growing capabilities on the future of work. They present the 'AI as Normal Technology' framework, arguing it is a useful way to understand AI's medium-term impacts unless a future discontinuity, like recursive self-improvement, occurs. The author emphasizes that while AI will transform jobs, it will not immediately replace all human work. They highlight the need for adaptation, drawing parallels to historical technological shifts like the industrial revolution. The author also critiques the common misinterpretation of AI's capabilities as a threat to employment, advocating instead for developing complementary skills and understanding the broader economic and organizational changes AI will bring.
source.title: AI's Impact on Work: A Framework for Adaptation

source.summary: The Indian men's hockey team's underwhelming performance at the World Cup has raised concerns, with critics pointing to defensive lapses, poor decision-making, and an ineffective attack. Despite moments of promise, the team conceded 16 goals in five matches, scoring 14, including five field goals. Former player and coach Jagbir Singh criticized the team's lack of consistency and questioned the coaching staff's strategies, particularly the midfield's inability to adapt. With less than three weeks until the Asian Games, the team faces pressure to improve ahead of the LA Olympics.
source.title: India's hockey team struggles in World Cup, faces criticism for poor performance

source.summary: The US has paused visa appointments worldwide as the Trump administration initiates a global training program for consular officers. The State Department said the training will adjust visa schedules, though details remain unclear. The initiative aims to ensure thorough screening of applicants for potential reliance on public benefits. This follows broader immigration crackdowns, including visa and green-card revocations, and legal challenges to some policies. The administration also plans to increase H-1B visa fees and tighten screening for applicants, while considering revoking business and tourism visas for those seeking asylum.
source.title: US halts global visa appointments amid Trump administration training push

source.summary: Coimbatore's Onam sadya experiences showcase regional Kerala culinary traditions and local adaptations. Karthiyayini Kovai offers a 24-item takeaway sadya with Kerala-style dishes and North Kerala influences, priced at ₹799, available until August 27. Rasanai presents a 28-dish sadya with regional variations, including Thiruvananthapuram and Thrissur specialties, priced at ₹1205 for dine-in. Friends Catering, with a 30-year history, serves a 20-dish sadya featuring traditional dishes like kaalan and aviyal, with a focus on handmade desserts. All venues emphasize family traditions, with preparations starting days in advance and special arrangements for the final day of the festival.
source.title: Coimbatore Onam sadya offerings highlight regional diversity and festive traditions

source.summary: SpaceX, led by Elon Musk, announced plans to build a $100 billion spaceport in Louisiana, which will be its largest launch site. The project, named Starbase Louisiana, will feature over a dozen launch towers, enabling more than 30 Starship flights per day. The site, spanning 125,000 acres in Vermilion Parish, will include facilities for propellant production, power generation, and deep-water shipping. Construction is set to begin in 2027, with the first Starship launch expected in 2029. The project is expected to create over 3,000 jobs. Louisiana Governor Jeff Landry praised the investment, highlighting its potential for new jobs and economic growth. SpaceX aims to significantly increase rocket launches, including deploying space-based data centres by the end of next year.
source.title: SpaceX to develop $100 billion Louisiana spaceport with over a dozen launch towers

source.summary: An independent director, Anil Khandelwal, resigned from Rashi Peripherals Ltd, citing governance concerns related to the company's professional engagements with firms linked to two of its independent directors. Khandelwal alleged that director appointments and management compensation were handled by company management rather than the board's nomination committee, and that due diligence for an acquisition was conducted by firms associated with the directors. The company's chairperson, Krishna Kumar Choudary, denied any governance lapses, stating the engagements were at arm's length and within legal limits. Rashi Peripherals' stock fell 10% following the resignation, with the company's market cap at ₹5,200 crore. The resignation marks the second such instance this year, following a similar exit by Atanu Chakraborty from HDFC Bank.
source.title: Independent director resigns over governance concerns at Rashi Peripherals

source.summary: Sir Demis Hassabis, Chief Scientist of Alphabet and founder of DeepMind, emphasizes his scientific approach to AI, aiming to understand nature and the universe. His work at DeepMind focused on AI applications in medicine and agriculture rather than chasing user metrics. The book 'The Infinity Machine' explores his career, from his origins in North London to his role in developing breakthroughs like AlphaGo and AlphaFold. Hassabis's philosophy of deep reinforcement learning contrasts with early symbolic AI, allowing machines to learn through observation. The book also examines DeepMind's competitive landscape, including its response to OpenAI and the rise of Chinese AI labs like DeepSeek. It raises questions about the ethical implications of AI development and the challenges of managing its rapid growth.
source.title: Demis Hassabis's journey in AI and science

source.summary: NITI Aayog's report flags a structural imbalance in India's higher education system, where millions of students pursue generic degrees with weak job links. Only 8.25% of graduates are employed in roles aligned with their qualifications, and 13% of all graduates are unemployed. The report notes that 1.86 crore students apply for just 55,000 government jobs, highlighting the mismatch between education and employment. It calls for reimagining higher education through industry participation and Public-Private Partnership (PPP) models to align curricula with industry needs. The report suggests moving toward specialised, job-linked programmes and expanding work-integrated learning to improve employability.
source.title: NITI Aayog highlights job mismatch in India's higher education system

source.summary: Tamil Nadu Chief Minister C Joseph Vijay has scrapped the Parandur site for Chennai's second airport, sending the project back to the drawing board. The decision, which the DMK's MK Stalin called an 'irreversible setback,' was made after protests from local communities concerned about displacement and environmental impact. While the existing Chennai International Airport has not yet reached its capacity threshold, experts warn that the long lead time for developing a new airport could delay necessary infrastructure. The airport's current capacity is expected to rise to 55 million passengers by 2026 with planned expansions, but industry bodies stress the urgency of finding an alternative site to avoid losing investment and talent to other regional hubs. The Parandur project, which would have handled 100 million passengers annually, was seen as long-term infrastructure rather than an immediate solution to congestion.
source.title: Chennai's Second Airport Project Back to Site Selection After Parandur Scrapped

source.summary: Crude oil prices fell 6% over two days, with Brent crude at $86 and U.S. West Texas Intermediate at $80.42, reacting to developments around the Strait of Hormuz and Iran-Oman negotiations. JPMorgan estimates prolonged disruption could push Brent prices up by $7-$8 per barrel, while Goldman Sachs warns of potential $120 per barrel if disruptions continue. However, the bank forecasts Brent to average $80 in Q4 and $75 next year, with risks tilted to the upside due to ongoing tensions.
source.title: Oil prices drop 6% amid Strait of Hormuz tensions and Iran-Oman talks

source.summary: Banks in multiple Indian states and Union Territories will close on August 26 due to Eid-e-Milad-un-Nabi. The Reserve Bank of India lists this day as a holiday under the Negotiable Instruments Act. Branches in cities like Mumbai, Delhi, and Chennai will remain shut, while others in areas like Ahmedabad and Jaipur will operate normally. Online banking and UPI services will remain functional. The next major holidays are August 28 and August 30.
source.title: Banks in several states close on Eid-e-Milad, August 26

source.summary: Hindustan Copper has opened its offer for retail investors, with a 10% discount on the floor price of Rs 514. The government plans to sell a 3% equity stake as part of the base offer, with an additional 3% available as a green shoe option. The OFS, valued at nearly Rs 2,982 crore, received strong demand from non-retail investors, leading to the exercise of the greenshoe option. A minimum of 10% of the offer size is reserved for retail investors. Analysts note that the discount is already stale, and the stock has sharply crashed more than 7% on the opening day. The government's divestment efforts continue with this OFS, following recent stake sales in other PSUs.
source.title: Hindustan Copper OFS opens for retail investors with 10% discount

source.summary: सोशल मीडिया पर वायरल हो रहे बयान में रामदेव के कांग्रेस की आलोचना करने पर माफी मांगने का दावा नकली है। नवभारत टाइम्स और अन्य स्रोतों के अनुसार, रामदेव के कोई ऐसा सार्वजनिक बयान उपलब्ध नहीं है। उनके हालिया बयानों में कांग्रेस या विपक्ष की आलोचना ही है। एक इंटरव्यू में रामदेव ने 'मोहब्बत की दुकान' के नारे को समाज में घृणा के कारण नकार लिया। निष्कर्ष यह है कि वायरल बयान गलत है।
source.title: रामदेव के बयान के वायरल दावे नकली हैं, न्यूज चैनल ने खंडन किया

source.summary: NASSCOM responded to the U.S. Department of Homeland Security’s proposal to set the H-1B visa fee at $103,265, emphasizing the program’s role in addressing U.S. skill gaps. The agency argued that the fee increase should be viewed in light of the program’s original purpose and highlighted that Indian tech companies have reduced H-1B employee numbers while investing over $1.1 billion in U.S. STEM education. NASSCOM also noted a significant drop in H-1B employees from Indian firms over five years and pledged continued engagement with stakeholders on the issue.
source.title: NASSCOM urges context for H-1B fee hike amid industry investment

source.summary: RBI officials note that the West Asia conflict is affecting supply chains and business confidence. U.S. tariffs have added to trade uncertainty, yet the global economy continues to expand with inflationary pressures. The Indian economy shows resilience due to strong macroeconomic fundamentals, with domestic demand remaining robust. Petroleum consumption growth has turned positive, and merchandise trade saw strong growth in July, though the deficit widened. Monsoon activity supported kharif sowing, and CPI inflation rose slightly to 4.45%, driven by food and beverages, while core inflation remained stable. Food and fuel prices increased, with cereals, pulses, and edible oils seeing notable price rises.
source.title: RBI highlights West Asia conflict's impact on business confidence and inflation trends

source.summary: The BJP's sudden acceptance of a caste census marks a significant political shift, driven by the need to adapt to the 'data state' era. Previously opposing caste enumeration as divisive, the party now sees it as a tool for managing social divisions through detailed data. The 2024 election results exposed the limits of its earlier strategy of subsuming caste within Hindu identity. The census, as a governance tool, enables precise targeting of communities for welfare and political mobilization, fragmenting larger groups into manageable constituencies. This transition from constitutional to data-driven governance allows the state to reorganize social identities for administrative and electoral purposes. The article warns that while the census can promote social justice, its use depends on the political intent behind it, raising concerns about its potential to deepen inequality rather than address historical injustices.
source.title: BJP's Caste Census Shift Reflects Data State Governance Strategy

source.summary: Sumit Sarkar, a pioneering historian of modern India, left an indelible mark on the discipline through his method of 'history from below,' which emphasized the social and cultural dimensions of nationalism. His work, such as 'Modern India, 1885-1947,' challenged traditional narratives by incorporating the voices of peasants, workers, and marginalized groups. Sarkar's scholarship was deeply rooted in Marxism but remained open to questioning its assumptions, and he was a committed feminist. His intellectual rigor and modesty influenced generations of students, including Charu Gupta, who recalls his teaching style and the impact of his mentorship. Sarkar's legacy endures in the questions he inspired, encouraging historians to continually interrogate the past and its representations.
source.title: Sumit Sarkar's legacy in reshaping modern Indian history through critical inquiry

source.summary: A study on the shola sky islands in the Western Ghats reveals how land use changes have impacted bird movements. Both forest and grassland species avoid human-dominated landscapes, but forest specialists face fewer movement obstacles in invaded woodlands. The Nilgiri pipit, the only grassland specialist in the study, experienced the most adverse effects from woody invasions and human activities. Between 1973 and 2017, the islands lost 516 sq km of grasslands and 63 sq km of forests. Researchers built 126 models to predict species movement patterns, finding that increased woodland cover fragmented grassland habitats, reducing connectivity for grassland species. The study highlights the need to restore native grasslands in the Shola Sky Islands to preserve biodiversity.
source.title: Land use changes disrupt bird movement in shola sky islands

source.summary: The 2026 Environmental Performance Index (EPI) ranks India among the worst climate performers, sparking debate over fairness and ethical principles in climate rankings. Different indices, such as the Climate Change Performance Index (CCPI), yield conflicting results due to varying ethical frameworks. The EPI focuses on absolute greenhouse gas emissions, while the CCPI emphasizes per capita emissions, reflecting differing views on equity. A 2024 study shows that adjusting the EPI to incorporate fairness-based metrics significantly improves rankings for the Global South. The article argues that no single index is neutral, and policymakers should consider multiple indices to form a principled stance. Thailand's engagement with the EPI led to improved rankings, illustrating the value of constructive responses over rejection. The piece concludes that climate indices should be transparent about their design choices, and countries should use them to inform policy rather than dismiss them outright.
source.title: India's Climate Rankings Differ Across Indices Due to Ethical Premises

source.summary: Capital markets finance teams face increasing complexity in managing balance sheet risks due to market volatility, regulatory changes, and AI-driven workflows. The article highlights how AI tools like Genie One help finance professionals analyze real-time data, track funding and liquidity shifts, and ensure accurate capital and valuation reporting. These tools enable faster decision-making by providing context through ontologies like FIBO, which standardize financial definitions across systems. The article outlines three key challenges: anticipating funding tightening, identifying silent return erosion, and explaining capital numbers on demand. Genie One supports these tasks by integrating governed data and business definitions, allowing finance teams to respond proactively to market changes while maintaining regulatory compliance. The role of AI is to enhance analysis and coordination, not to make decisions, which remain the responsibility of trading desks and risk teams.
source.title: Capital Markets Finance Uses AI to Track Balance Sheet Risks in Real Time

source.summary: Data governance tools are software platforms that help organizations catalog, secure, and audit their data assets, ensuring compliance with regulatory requirements. These tools automate data discovery, apply access controls, track lineage, and generate compliance reports, transforming governance from a static document into an operational reality. They address fragmented data across warehouses, lakes, and SaaS applications by creating a shared, searchable layer over data sources. Key features include data cataloging, lineage tracking, access control, quality monitoring, compliance reporting, and AI governance. The article outlines five categories of data governance tools, emphasizing the need for a comprehensive platform that integrates with existing systems. A data governance framework, combined with the right tooling, ensures scalable and effective data management, with seven criteria for evaluating tools including scalability, integration, usability, and vendor support.
source.title: Data Governance Tools Enable Enterprise Data Management and Compliance

source.summary: Queensland recorded 417 unintentional overdose deaths in 2024, the highest number on record according to the Penington Institute. Regional areas saw higher rates than Brisbane, with amphetamines identified as the primary cause. Advocacy groups are calling for a dedicated state strategy and access to drug checking services. The Queensland government stated there is no safe way to take drugs while investing $394.4 million in mental health and drug services.
source.title: Queensland overdose deaths hit record high in 2024

source.summary: President Donald Trump promised to hit Iran hard following the first direct military exchange between the two nations in weeks. US forces struck Iranian targets in the Strait of Hormuz, prompting Iran to attack bases in Jordan and the UAE. Treasury Secretary Scott Bessent attributed the conflict to Iran's economic struggles, while Iranian President Masoud Pezeshkian called for negotiations. Despite Trump's aggressive rhetoric, Iran stated that continuing the war serves no one's interest.
source.title: Trump vows retaliation after US and Iran exchange strikes

source.summary: Brigette Metzler is fighting to secure a customised mRNA vaccine for her 16-year-old son Coby, who has a terminal brain cancer diagnosis. Brain Tumour Alliance Australia states that more options are needed for families facing such dire circumstances. The article reports that the trial timeline risks excluding children like Coby who have short life expectancies. Professor Jordan Hansford notes that the experimental vaccine is not currently available for purchase and requires strict ethical approval. Brigette Metzler is appealing to the Federal Health Minister for funding to access the treatment outside the trial. Oliver Jarrett suggests drug companies should provide free compassionate access to unproven treatments. The Department of Health states that patient access to trials is a matter for pharmaceutical companies. Liz Dawes of the Robert Connor Dawes Foundation emphasises the need for safety data before allowing untested therapies.
source.title: Mother seeks access to customised brain cancer vaccine for dying son

source.summary: An author reflects on the death of Dr. Jason Arday, a Black education professor at the University of Cambridge, attributing his passing to coordinated online harassment. Professor Sir Simon Baron-Cohen described Arday as a kind man subjected to relentless scrutiny and ridicule. The author identifies Nathan Cofnas, a former Cambridge employee, as the initiator of the outrage campaign against Arday. The text argues that right-wing media and organizations like Turning Point USA weaponize digital platforms to target Black educators and dismantle diversity initiatives. The author notes that over 600,000 Black women have been pushed out of the workforce since January 2025, linking this trend to broader attacks on anti-racist educators. Ultimately, the piece frames Arday's death as a grim warning about the dangers of allowing political opportunists to discredit Black thought leaders.
source.title: Author mourns Dr. Jason Arday, linking his death to right-wing media attacks

source.summary: Tadej Pogacar underwent successful surgery on his left clavicle following a crash that ended his Vuelta a Espana campaign. Adrian Rotunno, Medical Director for UAE Team Emirates-XRG, confirmed the procedure went well and the rider will remain hospitalized for monitoring. The injury raises uncertainty about his participation in the upcoming world road championships in Quebec. Pogacar, who recently won the Tour de France and Giro d'Italia, aims to complete the Grand Tour hat-trick.
source.title: Tadej Pogacar undergoes clavicle surgery after Vuelta crash

source.summary: Lawyers representing thousands of families warn that Meta's recent settlement with U.S. attorneys general does not resolve their separate class-action lawsuit against the tech giant. Joseph VanZandt of the Beasley Allen law firm stated the agreement extinguishes state claims but leaves individual claims for mental health harms intact. The legal team, which includes Mariana Aroditis and Rachel Lanier, coordinates cases alleging platforms caused depression, anxiety, and other issues in young users. One plaintiff, Kaley G. M., received a historic $6 million award after a jury found Meta and YouTube responsible for her addiction. VanZandt expressed cautious optimism about Meta's new safety measures, such as daily time limits and nighttime restrictions, but emphasized the need to verify their implementation. Trials against Meta and other platforms are scheduled to begin in October.
source.title: Meta families' lawyers warn legal battles continue despite state settlement

source.summary: The news site reports the death of Edouard Balladur, a former French prime minister, at the age of 97. The article includes a technical error message regarding a failed site load.
source.title: Former French Prime Minister Edouard Balladur Dies at 97

source.summary: Defense attorneys for singer D4vd withdrew from his murder case on Monday after a judge ruled he qualified for a court-appointed lawyer. The outgoing team cited the judge's decision without explaining their departure, while the new public defender, Walid Kandeel, accepted the case. Singer David Anthony Burke entered a not guilty plea to charges of killing, sexually abusing, and dismembering 14-year-old Celeste Rivas Hernandez. Although Burke reportedly earned at least $10m in music revenue, the public defender's office confirmed his financial eligibility. District Attorney Nathan Hochman stated his office remains ready to prove the charges beyond a reasonable doubt and is still deciding whether to pursue the death penalty.
source.title: D4vd's Private Lawyers Withdraw as Public Defender Takes Over Murder Case

source.summary: France has begun a new voluntary national service programme with 3,000 participants starting this week. The government aims to reach 10,000 volunteers annually, targeting 50,000 by 2035. Selected based on motivation rather than degrees, volunteers will undergo ten months of training and receive €800 monthly pay. The armed forces intend to build a recruitment pool, though compulsory service remains unlikely due to capacity and financial constraints.
source.title: France launches voluntary national service for 3,000 young people

source.summary: Kemi Badenoch has restructured the Conservative shadow cabinet to challenge Labour and Reform UK. Andrew Griffith replaces Mel Stride as shadow chancellor, while Claire Coutinho becomes shadow business secretary. Tom Tugendhat is appointed shadow foreign secretary, and Katie Lam takes on the role of shadow housing and communities minister. Several other ministers retained their posts or moved to new briefs, including Chris Philp and James Cartlidge. The reshuffle aims to present a united front against the opposition.
source.title: Kemi Badenoch reshuffles Conservative shadow cabinet ahead of election

source.summary: Spanish Prime Minister Pedro Sanchez attributed disinformation fueling the Ceuta migrant surge to Russian and Israeli networks, noting no evidence of Moroccan involvement. Over 72,000 migrants crossed the border in two days, causing at least 100 deaths. Sanchez announced an additional €168 million in emergency funds to support the enclave's economy. Local tensions remain high following the unprecedented influx.
source.title: Spanish PM blames Russia and Israel for Ceuta migrant crisis disinformation

source.summary: Guinea-Bissau voters cast ballots on a referendum to replace the semi-presidential system with a stronger presidential model. The proposed constitution would reduce parliament from 102 to 65 lawmakers and grant the president authority to appoint and dismiss the prime minister. General Tomás Djassi defended the reforms as necessary to prevent conflict, while the opposition urged a boycott citing concerns over legitimacy. The National Electoral Commission reported turnout could exceed 55 percent despite logistical challenges. This vote occurs less than four months before scheduled December elections intended to restore civilian rule following a military takeover in November 2025.
source.title: Guinea-Bissau votes on constitution to strengthen presidency amid military transition

source.summary: Prediction-market operator Kalshi permanently barred former US congressman George Santos from trading after concluding his activity showed signs of insider dealing. The company alleged Santos placed bets in February related to his own attendance at President Trump's State of the Union address. Kalshi issued a penalty of $71,356 and referred the case to federal authorities. Santos thanked the platform on X and earned $17,839.57 from the trades. The disciplinary moves highlight increased scrutiny on prediction markets as they face heightened compliance burdens.
source.title: Kalshi permanently bans former congressman George Santos from its betting platform

source.title: Barcola transfers from PSG to Liverpool in record Ligue 1 deal

source.summary: Celebrity lawyers representing US singer D4vd have withdrawn from his murder trial, with the court appointing a public defender instead. Lawyers Blair Berk, Marilyn Bednarski, and Regina Peter confirmed the change, stating Burke qualified for appointed counsel. Deputy public defender Walid Kandeel pledged a serious examination of the evidence against the 21-year-old. Prosecutors acknowledge the lawyer switch may delay proceedings but remain ready to proceed with charges including first-degree murder and mutilation of human remains.
source.title: D4vd's celebrity lawyers withdraw as public defender takes over murder case

source.summary: Nepal's disaster authority reported that flash floods killed at least 939 people while missing persons dropped to 3,925. Indian authorities are currently identifying bodies found near the border, which are excluded from the official toll. Nepal's Foreign Secretary confirmed that unidentified remains were buried following standard protocols. Chinese state media acknowledged 16 deaths and 546 missing in Tibet, dismissing links to hydropower projects as malicious speculation.
source.title: Nepal death toll reaches 939 as floods kill 16 in Tibet

source.summary: A report details how young Cameroonian men are lured to Russia with false promises of employment and citizenship, only to be deployed to the war in Ukraine. Ukrainian officials state nearly 3,000 African nationals are currently fighting for Russia, with Cameroon identified as a significant source. DW correspondent Dorcas Ekupe notes the actual death toll is likely higher than official figures, which reported 16 Cameroonian deaths in April. Analyst Banjo Herman explains that economic desperation drives many recruits, who are promised high wages but instead face battlefield conditions. Families often suffer in silence, receiving news of deaths years later without compensation. While international law places liability on individuals, experts urge Cameroon to implement economic reforms and public awareness campaigns to combat this recruitment scheme.
source.title: Young Cameroonians deceived into fighting in Russia's war in Ukraine

source.summary: US Ambassador to Belgium Bill White pledged to refrain from making derogatory statements about Belgian politicians after meeting with Foreign Minister Maxime Prevot. White promised to direct complaints to the government directly rather than making public remarks. Prevot stated that such statements from an ambassador cannot be tolerated and emphasized the need for mutual respect. The dispute arose after White posted an AI-generated image of Health Minister Frank Vandenbroucke on social media. The meeting also covered US support for Belgium's energy security through liquefied natural gas and nuclear projects.
source.title: US Ambassador Promises to Stop Derogatory Comments on Belgian Officials

source.summary: Switzerland's Unia trade union called for enhanced heat protections after a survey revealed most construction workers lack required breaks during extreme heat. The survey of 984 workers found only 18% consistently received mandated 15-minute hourly breaks at 33C. Unia urged authorities to include a 33C threshold in the Construction Work Ordinance and increase workplace inspections. The union also requested adjustments to deadlines and compensation rules to account for heat-related work stoppages.
source.title: Swiss Unia union demands stronger heat protections for construction workers

source.summary: Indian Prime Minister Narendra Modi and Russian President Vladimir Putin are scheduled to meet in Bishkek on Monday during the SCO summit. The discussion addresses how India-Russia relations persist despite Western sanctions and US pressure over Russian oil purchases. Former ambassador Meera Shankar stated that India's strategic partnership with Moscow is intended to meet national goals rather than oppose the US. Energy ties have deepened as discounted Russian oil became a primary source for India, though supply disruptions from the US-Israel war on Iran complicate this reliance. Defense cooperation is shifting as India reduces dependence on Russian hardware and seeks indigenous production capabilities. Experts note that Russia's growing dependence on China alters its strategic value for India, prompting New Delhi to pursue an 'America plus' strategy. The upcoming BRICS summit in Delhi will further test whether political continuity can yield progress in trade and technology.
source.title: Modi and Putin meet in Bishkek to test India-Russia ties amid global shifts

source.summary: The Indian rupee fell 4 paise to 95.74 against the U.S. dollar in early trade on August 25, 2026, due to elevated crude prices and dollar demand from importers. Forex traders noted the RBI's intervention through state-run banks limited the decline. Analysts said the rupee remains range-bound between 95.50 and 96.00, with oil prices and RBI actions as key factors. The dollar index rose to 99.04, supported by U.S. sanctions on Iran, while Brent crude increased to $92.45 per barrel. Domestic markets saw a drop in the Sensex and Nifty, with foreign investors buying ₹1,181.66 crore in equities. The RBI's forex swap facility attracted $73 billion in foreign inflows as of August 21, 2026.
source.title: Rupee declines 4 paise to 95.74 against dollar amid crude prices and RBI intervention

source.summary: Ratnamani Metals' subsidiary, Ratnamani Finow Spooling Solutions Pvt Ltd, secured export orders worth Rs 2,700 crore, leading to a 21% rise in the company's shares over two sessions. The orders, placed by international customers, will be fulfilled through the subsidiary's plant and subcontracting over two to three years. The company stated the order was received in the ordinary course of business and emphasized it does not involve related-party transactions. It expects the win to enhance the subsidiary's export visibility and revenue prospects.
source.title: Ratnamani Metals subsidiary secures Rs 2,700 crore export order

source.summary: The BSE and NSE will remain open on August 26, with only a settlement holiday in place. Trading continues normally, while clearing and settlement are suspended. MCX and NCDEX will also operate as usual. The next market holiday is on September 14 for Ganesh Chaturthi. Key 2026 holidays include Gandhi Jayanti on October 2, Dussehra on October 20, Diwali Balipratipada on November 10, Guru Nanak Jayanti on November 24, and Christmas on December 25. Four holidays fall on weekends and will not cause additional closures. The Indian stock market extended losses on Tuesday, with Sensex and Nifty opening lower.
source.title: BSE and NSE remain open on August 26 with settlement holiday

source.summary: Indian stock markets opened lower on Tuesday amid rising U.S.-Iran tensions and higher crude oil prices. The Sensex and Nifty indices declined, with major firms like HCL Tech and Maruti underperforming, while others such as Trent and Adani Ports rose. Brent crude prices increased to $92.49 per barrel. Analysts warned of heightened volatility due to geopolitical risks and market positioning. Foreign investors bought equities worth ₹1,181.66 crore on Monday.
source.title: Indian markets fall on U.S.-Iran tensions and oil prices

source.summary: Anu Singh, an artist and life coach, argues that noticing everyday moments can transform daily life. She highlights simple interactions, like a stranger's smile or a compliment, as opportunities for connection. These small acts of awareness, she suggests, can foster a deeper appreciation for life's beauty. Singh emphasizes that noticing people, nature, and personal achievements can lead to a more meaningful existence. She encourages readers to cultivate the habit of observation, suggesting it can improve relationships and self-awareness.
source.title: Noticing Ordinary Moments Enhances Daily Experiences

source.summary: Indian benchmark stock indices Sensex and Nifty opened lower on Tuesday, August 25, amid escalating US-Iran sanctions and falling crude oil prices. The Sensex fell 0.077% to 77,309.84, while Nifty dropped below 24,200. The decline followed a similar trend on Monday, with geopolitical tensions and elevated oil prices contributing to market uncertainty. Key Sensex firms like Adani Ports and Axis Bank underperformed, while Tata Steel and HCL Tech were among the top gainers. Brent crude prices fell 1.68% to $92.80 per barrel.
source.title: Indian stock indices open lower due to US-Iran sanctions and oil price drop

source.summary: Ahmad Faraz, a prominent Urdu poet, is celebrated for his ability to blend classical discipline with contemporary precision in his ghazals. His work, marked by a unique balance of intellectual rigor and emotional depth, has left a lasting impact on both performance and written poetry. Faraz's verses, such as 'Ranjish hi sahī' and 'Ab ke ham bichhre', are noted for their intricate structure and philosophical insights, often addressing themes of desire, ethics, and political commitment. His poetic style, characterized by strategic use of rhyme and rhythm, made his work accessible yet profound, resonating with both critics and general audiences. Faraz's commitment to social and political issues is evident in his magnum opus 'Muhāsarā', where he asserts the poet's responsibility to the people rather than to power. His legacy endures through the continued relevance of his work in both literary and musical contexts.
source.title: Ahmad Faraz's poetic mastery and political commitment

source.summary: A Chinese waste-to-energy firm, Ecogreen Energy Pvt Ltd, invested Rs 428 crore in its Indian operations in Gurugram and Faridabad, with the government adding Rs 157 crore. Despite promises to reduce the Bandhwari landfill, the site grew to 38 metres high, polluting groundwater. Company records show funds were diverted to related firms, consultancy fees, and unfulfilled machinery purchases. In 2024, the government terminated the contract, and the firm sold for Rs 1 crore. The failure reflects broader issues in India's waste management, with multiple companies failing to deliver on public contracts. Ecogreen's contracts, including a 22-year Rs 330-crore agreement, were awarded despite its dormant status. The company outsourced waste collection to local scrap dealers, bypassing contractual obligations. The National Green Tribunal fined the government Rs 100 crore for environmental damage, highlighting the cost of failed public spending.
source.title: Chinese firm's Rs 428 crore investment in Gurugram waste management failed, leaving landfill unchanged

source.summary: Farmers in Assam are adopting an integrated rice-crab farming method to address climate challenges. Women cultivate indigenous rice varieties like Betguti, which can withstand erratic weather, and raise freshwater crabs that help control pests and aerate soil. Supported by the Assam State Rural Livelihood Mission, this approach is being scaled across 219 blocks. The crabs provide an additional income source and reduce reliance on agrochemicals. Research highlights benefits such as improved soil fertility and biodiversity. Women like Nikumoni Bora have seen success, earning over ₹1.35 lakh through rice and crab harvests. The initiative aims to promote indigenous rice varieties and enhance nutritional security through community-led farming efforts.
source.title: Assam farmers integrate rice and crab farming to combat climate change

source.summary: A new study shows glaciers in the Zanskar Himalayas of Ladakh have slowed by 16% in velocity from 1992 to 2023, with lower elevation glaciers losing speed faster. This slowdown, linked to accelerated ice thinning, threatens water security for the region, which relies on glacier melt. Scientists note that glacier velocity reflects their health, as mass accumulation at higher elevations drives movement. The study, published in The Cryosphere, used satellite data to track changes, finding that glacier thinning accelerated from 0.22 to 0.57 meters per year between 2000-2005 and 2015-2020. Researchers attribute the changes to global warming, which is reducing precipitation in the area. The findings add to growing concerns about glacier retreat across the Himalayas, with the HKH region experiencing a 12% area loss between 1990 and 2020.
source.title: Ladakh glaciers slow down as ice melts, threatening water supply

source.summary: Ollobot's OlloNi SS1 represents a shift in companion robotics, prioritizing emotional connection over task automation. Unlike earlier models that relied on voice commands, the SS1 uses proactive interaction, emotional awareness, and adaptive behavior to foster companionship. Designed for elderly individuals, children in single-parent households, and urban professionals, the robot integrates into daily life through mobility, facial recognition, and persistent presence. It features a 'heart module' for local AI processing, enabling real-time responses and memory retention. The device also includes a privacy cover for cameras and an automated life-recording system that captures spontaneous moments. With a projected market growth of 31% through 2033, the SS1 aims to fill emotional voids by evolving with its household, rather than simply mimicking human behavior.
source.title: AI Companion Robots Focus on Emotional Presence Over Functionality

source.summary: Recruiters are increasingly advocating for more friction in the job application process as AI tools have made it easier for applicants to submit mass applications, overwhelming hiring teams. Andrew Stockwell, a former head of people at Vendr, notes that the volume of applications has surged from dozens to hundreds, with many being fake or AI-generated. This has led to a situation where quality candidates struggle to stand out, while low-quality applicants slip through. Ophir Samson of Greenhouse highlights that recruiters now face 2,000 applications in 24 hours, calling it a 'shitty experience' for everyone. While some companies are turning to AI for initial screenings, experts like Tessa White argue that these tools lack the ability to accurately assess potential. As a result, recruiters are relying more on referrals and internal hires, raising concerns about diversity and talent discovery.
source.title: Recruiters Want More Friction in Job Applications as AI Floods Markets

source.summary: Spirit Airlines' sale of 34 years of employee data to Google has drawn strong opposition from a labor union representing former flight attendants. The data includes sensitive information like time cards, tax forms, and email accounts, which the union argues could be re-identified by AI, violating employee privacy. The union claims the sale lacks proper safeguards and seeks to exclude all employee data from the transaction. The case highlights growing concerns about worker data privacy in the AI era, as companies seek to monetize data from bankrupt firms. Legal experts warn that current laws have not kept pace with the risks of selling employee data for AI training. The sale, valued at $10 million, faces potential legal hurdles as the union pushes for stronger protections for worker data.
source.title: Spirit Airlines' Data Sale Sparks Labor Union Opposition Over Employee Privacy

source.summary: A robot carnival in Shanghai highlights China's progress in humanoid robotics, with over 100 companies displaying machines capable of performing tasks like making coffee and folding clothes. The event draws families and showcases robots in action, including a duel between remote-controlled machines and a humanoid demonstrating martial arts. While challenges like safety and cost remain, Chinese firms are promoting humanoids as solutions to mundane work. The carnival reflects broader efforts to integrate AI into daily life through embodied systems, with public enthusiasm evident as attendees cheer for robotic performances.
source.title: Chinese robot carnival showcases humanoid advancements and public engagement

source.summary: Scotland is introducing new regulations for datacentres following significant public opposition. A proposed 600MW datacentre in Auchertool, Fife, has drawn 1,600 objections, with Scottish parliament member David Torrance calling it the highest level of objection he has seen. The Scottish government is considering a moratorium on large datacentre projects, requiring planning authorities to notify the government for applications over 50MW and mandating environmental impact assessments for certain projects. Campaigners plan a demonstration in Edinburgh to push for a full moratorium. Datacentre developers, like ILI Group, defend their plans as economically beneficial, though some projects face uncertainty.
source.title: Scotland imposes new datacentre regulations amid public opposition

source.summary: NVIDIA showcases how Quantization-Aware Distillation (QAD) improves the Nemotron 3.5 Lightning model's efficiency. The technique allows for aggressive quantization to 4-bit weights while preserving accuracy. By using a full-precision BF16 model as a teacher, the quantized model (student) learns to maintain performance through simulated quantization during training. QAD outperforms post-training quantization (PTQ) in accuracy recovery, especially on agentic benchmarks. The process involves two stages: first, PTQ to create a quantized checkpoint, then distillation using KL divergence loss to align the student with the teacher. NVIDIA provides examples and code for implementing QAD with their Model Optimizer, emphasizing the benefits of dynamic and frozen scale strategies based on PTQ calibration methods.
source.title: NVIDIA Demonstrates QAD Technique for Efficient Model Quantization

source.summary: Alibaba has released the open weights for Qwen3.8-2.4T-A95B, its largest open-weight model, featuring 2.4T total parameters and 95B activated per token. The model uses a hybrid of full and linear attention, supporting up to one million tokens in context and 128K output length. It is designed for complex reasoning tasks like coding and document analysis. NVIDIA collaborates to deploy the model on GB300 NVL72 systems, achieving 4K tokens per second per GPU. The fine-grained MoE architecture improves efficiency by activating only necessary experts. Developers can use NVIDIA NIM for deployment and fine-tune the model with NVIDIA NeMo AutoModel.
source.title: Alibaba Releases Qwen3.8-2.4T-A95B Model for Agentic Workloads

source.summary: Firebird, an AI cloud provider, launched the CIS region's largest AI factory in Armenia, powered by NVIDIA and Dell technologies. The facility, attended by Armenian, Kazakhstani, and U.S. officials, aims to support local AI development and global innovation. Firebird plans to deploy over 70,000 GPUs and 300 megawatts of capacity by 2027, with NVIDIA and CoreWeave investing in its expansion. Schneider Electric and Vertiv provided critical infrastructure to support the project's rapid deployment and energy efficiency.
source.title: Firebird Opens Largest AI Factory in CIS Region, Boosting Armenia's Computing Capacity

source.summary: GeForce NOW announced 26 new games for its platform in August 2026, including the free-to-play naval combat game World of Warships: Legends. The service is also showcasing its capabilities at QuakeCon, offering demos of GeForce RTX 5080-powered cloud gaming at up to 5K 120 frames per second. The platform allows games to be played across multiple devices, including laptops, Macs, handhelds, and TVs. A list of newly added games and upcoming titles was provided, with additional games from July also available.
source.title: GeForce NOW Adds 26 New Games in August Including World of Warships: Legends

source.summary: NVIDIA has introduced Cosmos-H-Dreams, a real-time generative simulator for surgical robotics that enables interactive environments for training and evaluation. Built on the Cosmos-H-Surgical-Simulator, it distills the model into a causal student using FlashDreams for accelerated inference. The system, running on a single RTX PRO 6000 GPU, supports real-time operation by processing live robot kinematics and generating video frames. It is integrated with the Versius surgeon controller, allowing real-time interaction. The model is trained on surgical data, including both successful and failed procedures, to ensure realistic outcomes. Key challenges include maintaining surgical dynamics while reducing generation costs, addressed through teacher-to-student training and self-forcing distillation. The system supports closed-loop interactions, enabling human and policy-based control. NVIDIA highlights its potential for policy development, reinforcement learning, and applications like telesurgery and surgical rehearsal, while emphasizing it is a research platform, not a clinical tool.
source.title: NVIDIA Introduces Real-Time Surgical Simulation System for Robotics
