source.summary: AMD reports a 30% productivity boost from AI in software development, surpassing its initial 25% target. The company attributes this to AI-generated code now comprising up to 80% of some codebases. AI agents are now integrated into every stage of the software development lifecycle, from code analysis to testing and release. AMD envisions a future where collaborative AI agent swarms can independently identify and develop solutions, guided by human-defined goals rather than human assumptions. The company is working to create continuous learning loops that improve AI performance through feedback and iteration, with a notable example being the resolution of Radeon Software eXperience (RSX) issues, which increased from 6% to 75% resolved by AI agents. AMD emphasizes AI as a tool to enhance productivity and enable engineers to focus on higher-value tasks, rather than reducing workforce size.
source.title: From AI Copilots to Agent Swarms

source.summary: Tesla will hold a ceremonial inauguration for its new Semi factory in Nevada on September 24, 2026, despite having already begun volume production in April 2026. The facility, part of a $3.6 billion expansion, is designed to produce 50,000 electric trucks annually. Tesla announced the event through its Semi account, emphasizing the plant's vertical integration with the nearby Gigafactory Nevada. The company is building two Semi variants with ranges of 325 and 500 miles, using an 800-kW three-motor powertrain. Analysts estimate deliveries in 2026 will fall short of the plant's capacity. The event coincides with Tesla's push into Europe and aims to reset expectations for production ramp-up and cost of ownership.
source.title: Tesla to hold Semi factory inauguration ceremony in Nevada next month

source.summary: The Trump administration's economic sanctions against Iran are targeting key trade partners, including China, Iraq, Turkey, India, and the UAE, by restricting access to the U.S. financial system. China remains the largest importer of Iranian oil, with flows reduced but still significant, despite efforts to circumvent U.S. sanctions. Iraq relies heavily on Iranian gas for electricity, and sanctions could lead to power grid failures. Turkey faces rising energy costs and supply disruptions, while India's trade with Iran has declined sharply. The UAE has suspended dealings with Iran, reducing its exposure to U.S. sanctions. The administration's strategy aims to pressure Iran's trading partners into compliance, with major banks still a potential target.
source.title: Trump's Economic Sanctions Target Iran's Key Trade Partners

source.summary: U.S. oil firms like ExxonMobil and ConocoPhillips are delaying their return to Venezuela's oil industry despite the country's vast reserves, as negotiations with PDVSA face hurdles. Smaller U.S. companies such as Hunt Oil and Pacific Coast Energy have signed agreements with PDVSA to develop Venezuela's oil fields, but major firms are cautious due to uncertain fiscal terms and political instability. The Wall Street Journal reported that U.S. firms are seeking favorable terms for the Orinoco Belt, while PDVSA cannot guarantee stability. Pacific Coast Energy faces legal challenges from the Cisneros family, who claim their assets were illegally transferred. These complications highlight the risks for Big Oil returning to Venezuela, which has a history of nationalizing assets.
source.title: U.S. Oil Firms Hesitant to Return to Venezuela Amid Negotiation Delays

source.summary: Tesla has discontinued its solar roof product, which failed to gain significant market traction despite initial hype. The company, which once aimed to install 1,000 solar roofs weekly, only managed 3,000 installations by 2022. The product's high cost, slow installation, and performance issues contributed to its failure. Tesla now focuses on standard solar panels, launching a new 300 MW manufacturing line at its Buffalo factory. The company also plans a $10.1 billion solar cell factory in Texas, aiming to boost domestic production amid rising tariffs on imported solar products. Analysts suggest Tesla's shift reflects a lesson from the solar roof's shortcomings: simplicity and economies of scale are key in the solar market.
source.title: Tesla Abandons Solar Roof, Focuses on Standard Panels

source.summary: The Port of San Diego has approved Skycharger's solar + electric semi truck project on a 4.8-acre site near the National City Marine Terminal. The Environmental Impact Report was certified, and a Coastal Development Permit was issued, allowing the project to proceed. The facility will include 70 charging ports and a 1,719-kW solar array with battery storage. Skycharger also plans a Trucking as a Service program to help operators transition to zero-emissions vehicles with flexible leasing options. The project supports the Port's Maritime Clean Air Strategy to reduce diesel pollution.
source.title: Port of San Diego approves Skycharger's solar-powered truck hub for fleet electrification

source.summary: Clean energy investments in Appalachia have declined significantly, impacting employment and manufacturing output. According to the Keystone Research Center and ReImagine Appalachia, private construction spending in manufacturing fell from $249 billion in November 2024 to $170 billion in June 2026. The decline followed a peak in 2022 driven by federal policies like the Inflation Reduction Act. Clean energy manufacturing investments in Appalachia dropped 26% from their Q4 2023 peak. While consumer spending on clean energy and electric vehicles increased in 2026, experts warn that reversing federal policy is needed to revive manufacturing in the region.
source.title: Clean energy investments in Appalachia decline, affecting jobs and manufacturing

source.summary: Commercial crude oil inventories in the U.S. increased by 2.0 million barrels to 411.7 million barrels for the week ending July 17, 2026, 6% below the previous five-year average. Gasoline and distillate inventories also rose, while propane/propylene inventories surged 34% above the five-year average. U.S. refineries operated at 96.1% capacity, processing 17.1 million barrels per day. Crude oil imports rose slightly, but the four-week average was 11% lower than a year ago. Total product demand averaged 20.4 million barrels per day, with increases in gasoline, distillate, and jet fuel demand offset by declines in residual fuel oil and other products.
source.title: U.S. crude oil inventories rise by 2 million barrels, below five-year average

source.summary: On July 3, 2026, New York imported 52 gigawatthours of electricity from Canada, the highest since January 2025, partly via the newly operational Champlain Hudson Power Express (CHPE) transmission line. A heatwave drove demand up, with a peak load of 31,097 MW. Canadian imports met 9% of demand, with Hydro-Québec supplying 1,400 MW/hour. The CHPE line, capable of 1,250 MW, was fully utilized. The New York State Energy Research and Development Authority expects CHPE to meet up to 20% of New York City’s power demand. However, the line faced an outage in June and was offline for repairs on July 4.
source.title: New York imports significant electricity from Canada via new transmission line during heatwave

source.summary: Aarhus University researchers used virtual reality to explore how citizens perceive agrivoltaics compared to conventional solar parks. The study, published in Environmental Science & Policy, involved 102 participants viewing three solar configurations from different viewpoints. Findings showed that as participants gained a better understanding of agrivoltaics' dual food-energy function, they evaluated them more favorably. Agrivoltaics scored higher on compatibility with agriculture and innovativeness than conventional solar parks. However, acceptance intentions were similar across all installation types, suggesting that experiential engagement can reduce unfamiliarity. The research highlights the importance of visual and functional clarity in shaping public perception and recommends using VR or visualizations to support informed discussions about agrivoltaics. The study also notes that scale and local context matter, and tools like VR should facilitate dialogue rather than replace formal consultation processes.
source.title: Virtual reality helps citizens understand agrivoltaics and boosts acceptance

source.summary: India added 3 GW of open-access solar capacity in Q2 2026, the highest quarterly addition on record, according to Mercom India. Open-access solar allows C&I consumers to procure power from off-site projects. Rajasthan accounted for 25% of the additions, while cumulative capacity reached 36 GW. The growth was influenced by regulatory deadlines and market changes, with project economics affected by transmission constraints and evolving regulations.
source.title: India's Q2 2026 sees 3 GW open-access solar added

source.summary: ACWA has signed three Storage Services Agreements with Saudi Power Procurement Company for 1.5 GW/6 GWh battery energy storage systems at Haden, Muwayh, and AlKahfah. The projects, each with 500 MW capacity and 2,000 MWh storage, will supply power for 15 years. ACWA stated the facilities will store renewable energy and discharge during peak demand, supporting grid reliability. The projects align with Saudi Arabia’s Vision 2030 goals and expand ACWA’s energy storage portfolio. The tender treated energy storage as a standalone service, offering a replicable procurement model.
source.title: ACWA Secures 1.5 GW BESS Projects in Saudi Arabia

source.summary: ACWA Power has signed agreements with the Saudi Power Procurement Company to develop three battery energy storage projects totaling 6,000 MWh in Saudi Arabia. The projects, located in Haden, Muwayh, and AlKahfah, will each have 500 MW power capacity and 2,000 MWh storage capacity. The facilities, operating under 15-year agreements, aim to support the national grid by storing electricity during low demand and releasing it during peak times. Omar Al Hassan, CEO of ACWA Power in Saudi Arabia, highlighted the importance of energy storage in the Kingdom’s power system development. The projects are part of Saudi Arabia’s efforts to integrate renewable energy sources and align with Vision 2030 goals.
source.title: ACWA Power Develops 6,000 MWh Battery Storage Projects in Saudi Arabia

source.summary: The article explores the factors influencing EV owners' decisions to trade in their vehicles. A Tesla Model 3 owner, after seven years of use, is trading it in for a Model Y due to aging, difficulty accessing the vehicle, and the desire for Tesla's FSD (Supervised) technology. The owner notes that while battery degradation is minimal, maintenance costs and depreciation are concerns. Other EV drivers, such as a BYD Atto 3 owner and Neil Warner, share their perspectives, highlighting considerations like battery technology, creature comforts, and warranty periods. The article emphasizes that modern EVs last longer and require less maintenance than traditional vehicles, but personal factors like convenience and technological upgrades often drive trade-in decisions. The piece concludes with insights from multiple EV owners, illustrating the evolving criteria for vehicle replacement in the electric vehicle era.
source.title: EV Owners Discuss Reasons for Trading In Vehicles

source.summary: Over 100 organizations and businesses are urging EU President Ursula von der Leyen to commission an independent, science-based roadmap to end Europe's reliance on fossil fuels. The letter highlights that the EU's continued dependence has led to higher energy costs and exacerbated the climate crisis, with the June heatwave alone estimated to claim at least 14,000 lives. The report should focus on quantifying the economic burden of fossil fuels, charting a competitive exit through renewables and energy efficiency, aligning finance with the phase-out, ensuring a just transition, and leveraging natural solutions for climate action. The initiative aims to make this fossil fuel crisis Europe's last, with the report to be announced in von der Leyen's upcoming State of the Union address.
source.title: EU Urges Commission of Independent Report to End Fossil Fuel Dependence

source.summary: Bruce Power has received approval from the Canadian Nuclear Safety Commission to operate a hot cell facility, a key milestone in its production of medical isotopes. The facility, completed in July, enables Target Carrier Removal, a critical step in producing Lu-177 for cancer treatment. The company, which has produced medical isotopes since 1986, plans to expand its isotope production capacity with additional equipment at Bruce unit 6. Bruce Power's Chief Operating Officer highlighted the approval as a step toward strengthening Ontario's isotope supply chain and Canada's global leadership in medical isotope innovation.
source.title: Bruce Power receives approval to operate hot cell facility for isotope processing

source.summary: SunShare and CSolPower have completed two community solar gardens in New Mexico. The 6-MW Juniper Sol project in Santa Fe incorporates agrivoltaic practices and serves 2,000 families, half of whom are income-qualified. The 4.5-MW Rockhound Sol project in Deming also supports community energy needs. SunShare’s CEO highlighted the projects’ role in meeting growing electricity demand and advancing renewable energy. The company also announced $7 million in donations to three organizations.
source.title: SunShare completes two solar gardens in New Mexico

source.summary: BRICS countries, including China, India, and Russia, have rejected the EU's Carbon Border Adjustment Mechanism (CBAM), calling it a punitive and protectionist measure. The joint statement from the BRICS Environment and Climate Ministers’ Meeting, held in New Delhi, expressed concern that CBAM undermines global climate efforts, particularly for developing nations. The mechanism, which took effect on January 1, requires EU importers to pay carbon prices on certain goods from non-EU countries. India, with 90% of its CBAM-covered exports being iron and steel, faces significant exposure. Analysis shows high-emission steel producers reduced EU exports during the reporting phase, while lower-emission firms maintained their volumes. The CBAM certificate submission deadline for 2026 is May 31, 2027.
source.title: BRICS Nations Condemn EU's CBAM as Unfair and Punitive

source.summary: Atomic Canyon introduced NIVA, an AI tool designed to help nuclear professionals access and apply industry knowledge. NIVA features two assistants: a Knowledge Assistant that draws from regulatory and technical documents, and an Operating Experience Assistant that uses context to surface relevant operational insights. The tool runs on Atomic Canyon's Neutron AI platform and leverages FERMI, an AI model trained on over 53 million pages of nuclear data. The company highlighted its recent deployment at Diablo Canyon nuclear plant and partnerships with Constellation Energy and NVIDIA, aiming to scale AI use across the US nuclear fleet.
source.title: Atomic Canyon launches NIVA to aid nuclear professionals with AI-driven knowledge access

source.summary: Danske Commodities will optimise a 20MW/40MWh battery energy storage system (BESS) added to BeGreen's 48MW solar PV plant in Denmark. The project, located in Norddjurs Municipality, is part of an extended partnership. Danske will operate the entire plant, acting as the balancing responsible party for solar and balancing service provider for the BESS. The hybrid project is nearing full operations, with commissioning underway. The BESS is expected to enhance the value of solar energy produced. Danske also manages Denmark's largest BESS, the 200MWh Kvosted project, for IPP European Energy.
source.title: Danske Commodities to optimise co-located BESS with BeGreen's solar plant in Denmark

source.summary: U.S. petroleum exports reached a record 13.6 million barrels per day in April, driven by increased global demand due to disruptions through the Strait of Hormuz. Crude oil exports averaged 5.6 million b/d, up 21% from December 2023. Propane and distillate fuel oil also saw record or near-record levels. Finished petroleum products exports remained high despite average motor gasoline exports. Weekly estimates show crude, distillate fuel, jet fuel, and propane exports stayed above five-year seasonal highs in May and June.
source.title: U.S. petroleum exports hit record 13.6 million barrels per day in April

source.summary: Safegrid, part of G&W Electric Company, will showcase its Intelligent Grid System at T&D World Live 2026. The solution uses field sensors and data analytics to detect and predict faults in distribution and transmission networks. It identifies abnormal patterns indicating equipment issues, enabling proactive maintenance. The system also provides accurate fault location using GPS time-synchronized measurements. Utilities are using it to address challenges like failing cable terminations and vegetation-related faults. The demonstration highlights a shift from reactive to proactive grid management, aiming to improve reliability and reduce outage duration.
source.title: Safegrid Demonstrates Predictive Fault Intelligence for Grid Management

source.summary: R.M. Young Company and Western Weather Group are offering a free Wind Monitor at T&D World Live. Attendees can visit Booth 419 to answer a weather-related trivia question for a chance to win the $1,249.00 device. The companies, who have partnered for over 20 years, are co-exhibiting for the first time, showcasing their weather instrumentation and expertise. Visitors can also learn about their collaborative solutions for utility and weather-monitoring professionals. Advance reservations are recommended for one-on-one meetings with the teams.
source.title: R.M. Young and Western Weather Group Offer Free Wind Monitor at T&D World Live

source.summary: BMW is launching two new electric models in China, including the long-wheelbase Neue Klasse iX3 electric SUV, priced between 269,900 and 339,900 yuan. The company began pre-sales at the 2026 Chengdu Motor Show, with deliveries set for November. The iX3, which has seen 100,000 orders in Europe since 2025, faces stiff competition in China, where local electric vehicles offer high value for money. BMW aims to reverse declining sales in the world's largest auto market, though success remains uncertain due to intense competition.
source.title: BMW Introduces China-Exclusive Electric SUV to Boost Sales

source.summary: Sage Geosystems has launched its first next-generation geothermal plant in Texas, marking a significant milestone for the sector. The 3-megawatt pilot plant, operational since April 2026, has performed reliably after over 120 days of grid-connected operations. The company said the results will inform its upcoming collaboration with Ormat Technologies in Nevada, a precursor to its deal with Meta for 150 MW of geothermal power. Sage’s enhanced geothermal system involves drilling into hot rocks and fracturing them to create water pockets for power generation, differing from traditional geothermal methods. The plant has shown promising water retention, with less than 10% loss, which could improve efficiency for future projects. Sage plans to begin drilling at Ormat’s Nevada plant later this year, aiming to scale up and develop 150 MW of next-gen geothermal power by 2028.
source.title: Sage Geosystems launches first next-gen geothermal plant in Texas

source.summary: Qcells' Georgia factory, which produces solar panel components, faces challenges from fluctuating U.S. solar policies. The plant, which began full production in June, represents a major step toward domestic solar manufacturing. China has dominated the global market, but the U.S. seeks to reduce reliance on foreign imports. The Trump administration's new tariffs and import restrictions aim to boost domestic production, while the Biden-era Inflation Reduction Act offered tax incentives. Policy changes have created uncertainty for companies like Qcells, which invested billions in its facility. Analysts note that while the U.S. solar industry may eventually shift to domestic production, short-term policy instability and limited supply could increase costs for developers. Despite these challenges, solar remains a cost-effective energy source, with experts predicting continued growth in solar deployment.
source.title: Qcells' Georgia factory navigates U.S. solar policy shifts

source.summary: The US has warned that its sanctions on Iran will significantly impact its economy, but experts argue the measures may have limited effectiveness. Iran's major trading partners, including China, Turkey, Pakistan, and Armenia, have complex relationships with the US and face economic risks from sanctions. China, Iran's largest buyer, has rejected the sanctions, while Turkey and Pakistan, both bordering Iran, struggle with economic pressures. Armenia, despite sanctions against Russia, continues trade with Iran. Experts suggest the US's ability to enforce sanctions is questionable, with some noting that the measures may disproportionately affect civilians rather than economies. Global markets have shown limited reaction to the sanctions threat.
source.title: US sanctions on Iran face challenges from key trading partners

source.summary: Levi Strauss & Co. reported a cybersecurity breach on Aug. 7, with unauthorized access to three employees' computers via social engineering. The company said corporate information was accessed and exfiltrated, though it does not expect material operational impact. The incident underscores vulnerabilities in complex supply chains, as major brands like Nike and Adidas have also faced similar breaches. Experts warn that third-party relationships are increasingly exploited by bad actors, urging stronger verification protocols and access controls across the supply chain.
source.title: Levi's Cybersecurity Breach Highlights Risks in Apparel Industry Supply Chains

source.summary: An investor continues to add to their Oracle position, citing the company's $638 billion contracted backlog and forward P/E of 18 as undervalued compared to Microsoft and Amazon. The investor highlights Oracle's multicloud growth and contracted revenue visibility, despite its $124.7 billion debt and negative free cash flow. The analysis contrasts Oracle's PEG of 0.83 with Microsoft's 1.57 and Amazon's 1.39, suggesting the company offers a discounted alternative. The investor acknowledges risks, including potential execution friction and dilution, but believes the asymmetry in enterprise software presents a compelling opportunity.
source.title: Oracle's Contract Backlog and Valuation Attract Investor Despite Financial Risks

source.summary: China's Foreign Ministry spokesperson Lin Jian criticized US sanctions on Iran, stating Beijing will safeguard its interests. The comments come as the US expands penalties on Iranian entities, including those in China. Analysts suggest US sanctions on Chinese companies are unlikely due to diplomatic and legal challenges. China remains a key buyer of Iranian oil, and Iran has long evaded sanctions through international financial networks. The US Treasury Secretary warned Chinese banks could be targeted, but analysts doubt the feasibility of such measures.
source.title: China rejects US sanctions on Iran, vows to protect its interests

source.summary: The US Treasury Department has sanctioned 60 entities and individuals across multiple countries, targeting networks that support Iran's nuclear and missile programs, cyber operations, and oil revenue generation. The sanctions, announced by Treasury Secretary Scott Bessent, aim to cut Iran's economic lifelines and isolate it from the global economy. Entities targeted include Iranian government ministries, Chinese logistics firms, Hong Kong-based companies, and others in Singapore, Malaysia, and the UK. Iran has rejected the sanctions, with officials claiming the measures will fail. The US has spared some Chinese financial institutions, possibly to avoid provoking retaliation. Analysts suggest Iran is well-prepared to circumvent sanctions, and other nations like China have criticized the US actions as unilateral and disruptive to international cooperation.
source.title: US sanctions 60 entities linked to Iran's nuclear and oil networks

source.summary: A study finds that local synthetic opioid overdose deaths significantly increase buprenorphine prescribing, with treatment volumes rising by 5-17% of pre-treatment levels. The effect emerges within one to two quarters and is most pronounced in areas with existing buprenorphine infrastructure, Medicaid patients, and advanced practice providers. The findings suggest provider behavior, rather than patient demand, drives the increase, though the study cannot separate these factors. Local mortality data appears to act as a determinant of treatment volume, comparable in magnitude to legislative interventions, but only where prescribing capacity exists.
source.title: Local synthetic opioid overdose deaths influence buprenorphine prescribing

source.summary: Serena Goldberg and Costas Meghir examine how childcare affects female labor supply and child development in low and middle income countries. They present a household model showing how improved childcare availability can influence mothers' employment and earnings. The study reviews literature indicating childcare may increase women's employment but faces barriers like limited opportunities or social norms. Child development outcomes are mixed, depending on context and care quality.
source.title: Childcare's Impact on Women's Employment and Child Development in Low and Middle Income Countries

source.summary: A Venetian island with a Napoleonic fort and lush gardens is for sale. Crevan, built in 1806 as a military outpost, has been restored as residential properties. The island, slightly smaller than a football pitch, features a converted fort into a villa, manicured gardens, and a private mooring. It is listed by luxury real estate agencies, with the asking price undisclosed. Crevan competes with other Venetian islands, including Isola Santa Cristina, which is priced at €24m.
source.title: Venetian island with Napoleonic fort listed for sale

source.summary: The article explores the scientific evidence supporting creatine as a supplement. It features insights from science editor Ian Sample and Dr. Justin Roberts, a professor of nutritional physiology. The discussion covers creatine's role in enhancing fitness and muscle building, as well as its reported cognitive benefits. The article questions the validity of these claims and examines the underlying research.
source.title: Experts discuss creatine's scientific basis and benefits

source.summary: Average earnings in Jersey rose by 1.2% in real terms in June 2026, according to Statistics Jersey, after adjusting for 2.8% inflation. This marks a slowdown from the five-year average of 5.6% and the long-term average of 4.2%. The private sector saw a 0.9% real-term increase over 12 years, while the public sector grew by 2.9% but fell by 3% over 25 years. Statistics Jersey noted the survey was compulsory for employers for the fourth year. Matthew Gill, a statistician, said real-term earnings had not changed much since 2001, with inflation affecting daily costs like petrol. Heidi Gibaut of Law At Work highlighted the challenge of balancing inflation with fair wages.
source.title: Jersey earnings growth outpaced inflation by 1.2% in real terms

source.summary: The article explores alternatives to the traditional hereditary system for selecting members of the House of Lords. It argues that merit-based selection may not ensure independence from politics. Instead, it proposes a system where bondholders, particularly pension funds, hold seats proportional to their holdings, emphasizing long-term financial stability. The author suggests this approach could align with national prosperity, though acknowledges potential fiscal conservatism. The idea also includes a mix of equity ownership, such as Trills, to balance economic interests.
source.title: Proposing a Bondholder-Based House of Lords for Stability

source.summary: The Federal Reserve announced five task forces to review and improve monetary policy practices. Led by external experts, these groups will examine communication strategies, balance sheet policies, data quality, productivity impacts, and inflation frameworks. Each task force will operate independently, providing feedback to the Federal Open Market Committee. The goal is to enhance the Fed's ability to achieve its dual mandate of price stability and maximum employment.
source.title: Federal Reserve Establishes Task Forces to Review Monetary Policy Practices

source.summary: The Federal Reserve Board has imposed a written agreement on TS Banking Group, Inc. and TS Contrarian Bancshares, Inc., both based in Treynor, Iowa. The enforcement action, dated July 6, 2026, was announced by the Board. The agreement outlines specific conditions the institutions must adhere to. The Board did not provide further details on the nature of the enforcement action. Additional enforcement actions can be accessed through the provided link.
source.title: Federal Reserve imposes written agreement on TS Banking Group and TS Contrarian Bancshares

source.summary: Morgan Stanley Research notes that institutional investors increased their exposure to technology after a strong Q2 rally. However, this buying did not close the positioning gap in the largest tech names. The report highlights that while there was a rise in tech holdings, the gap in ownership for major companies persists.
source.title: Institutional investors boost tech exposure but gap remains in mega-cap stocks

source.summary: Calculated Risk, a financial blog, is ending its daily updates after 21 years. The author will transition to a weekly economic newsletter with three sections: a schedule of upcoming data, a review of previous data, and commentary on current topics. The Real Estate Newsletter will continue with 4 to 6 weekly updates. The author thanked readers for their support and expressed hope that the blog was useful and informative.
source.title: Calculated Risk Ends Daily Blog, Introduces Weekly Newsletter

source.summary: The U.S. hotel industry reported a 4.4% year-over-year increase in occupancy rate to 50.5%, according to CoStar’s data through January 3, 2026. Average daily rates rose 3.4% to $175.47, while revenue per available room (RevPAR) increased by 7.9% to $88.65. The data shows a seasonal pattern, with the red line representing 2026 performance, the blue line as the median, and the dashed light blue line for 2025. The report notes that early-year comparisons are challenging due to weak travel demand in January, and the 4-week average is expected to rise seasonally in the coming months.
source.title: Hotel Occupancy Rate Rose 4.4% Year-over-year in Early 2026

source.summary: Japan's Finance Ministry plans to allocate a record $230 billion for debt-servicing in the next fiscal year, according to documents. This represents a 17% increase from the current year's allocation, driven by higher interest rates and bond yields. The ministry used a provisional rate of 3.8%, the highest in nearly three decades. Rising borrowing costs are linked to concerns over Prime Minister Sanae Takaichi's fiscal policies, including a planned sales tax cut. The overall budget request is expected to exceed ¥130 trillion for the first time, with ministries aiming to include more spending in the initial package.
source.title: Japan's Debt-Servicing Costs to Reach $230 Billion Record Next Year

source.summary: South Korea scrambled fighter jets after multiple Russian military aircraft entered its air defense identification zone over the East Sea, according to the country's defense ministry. The ministry stated the Russian planes did not violate South Korean airspace but failed to notify Seoul before entering the zone. This marks the second such incursion in weeks, following a similar event in late June involving Chinese and Russian aircraft. South Korea protested the incidents, demanding preventive measures, amid strained relations with Russia due to sanctions and military cooperation with North Korea.
source.title: South Korea scrambles jets as Russian planes enter its air defense zone

source.summary: The Japanese Red Cross has raised concerns about the health of evacuees in Kumamoto Prefecture, nearly a month after a 7.0 magnitude earthquake. Officials noted potential health deterioration due to prolonged shelter life, including risks of aspiration pneumonia and heart failure. The organization highlighted improved relief efforts compared to past disasters, with faster delivery of supplies and quicker medical response. JRCS doctor Shinsaku Ueda emphasized the need for evacuees, especially the elderly, to maintain physical activity and proper nutrition to mitigate health risks.
source.title: Japanese Red Cross warns of evacuees' health risks in Kumamoto

source.summary: US President Donald Trump has submitted a civilian nuclear cooperation agreement with Saudi Arabia to Congress for review, according to an administration official. The classified pact aims to bolster Saudi Arabia's nuclear program but is contingent on the kingdom normalizing relations with Israel. The agreement, signed last month, requires Saudi Arabia to join the Abraham Accords, raising concerns about its implementation. Congress has 90 days to review the deal, which could take effect without approval if not rejected. The deal, expected to last 30 years, involves US firms in developing the program.
source.title: Trump submits Saudi nuclear deal to Congress with Israel condition

source.summary: Senior Seaman Michael Coccon Johen, a Malaysian navy special forces member, spent 15 hours adrift in the South China Sea after a parachute training exercise went wrong. The incident occurred during a free-fall drill when sudden weather changes disrupted visibility, causing the team to land in the sea instead of on an island. Johen, the last of six personnel to be rescued, remained calm and waited for naval assistance, though high waves prevented immediate recovery. The accident happened during the second jump at 4:30 pm, with the team 10 km from the island. The navy's safety vessels could not reach them due to dangerous sea conditions.
source.title: Malaysian Commando Adrift in South China Sea After Parachute Drill

source.summary: The Longhaul Festival, launched by TEG Live in early 2027, has been cancelled just a month after its announcement. The festival, which featured Kacey Musgraves and Kane Brown, was set to take place in Melbourne, Sydney, and Brisbane. A TEG spokesperson expressed disappointment, stating the decision was made to provide certainty to fans and artists. The cancellation follows TEG's decision to cut its country music touring department, citing cost-cutting measures. Ticketek has confirmed all tickets will be refunded. The festival's cancellation joins a trend of declining music events in Australia, with several other festivals also facing cancellations or reduced operations.
source.title: Longhaul Festival Cancellation Marks Another Blow to Australian Music Events

source.summary: US President Donald Trump has submitted a 30-year nuclear cooperation agreement with Saudi Arabia to Congress for review, according to The Wall Street Journal. The agreement, announced last month, allows US companies to lead Saudi Arabia's nuclear infrastructure development while excluding foreign competitors. It has drawn controversy due to concerns that it could enable Saudi Arabia to enrich uranium domestically. The deal was formally transmitted to Congress on Monday, requiring a joint resolution and two-thirds majority in both chambers to block it.
source.title: Trump submits Saudi nuclear agreement to Congress for review

source.summary: Danni Smith, an Indigenous Voice to Parliament member in South Australia, had assault charges dropped after pleading guilty to disturbing the peace. The magistrate ruled the incident was a one-off and not trifling, issuing a good behaviour bond instead of a conviction. Smith, who represents the South East and Riverland regions, faced domestic violence-related aggravated assault charges but maintained her innocence throughout the court process. The altercation occurred after she visited her parents' home following personal loss, with no physical contact made during the argument.
source.title: Indigenous Voice to Parliament member's assault charges dismissed

source.summary: Ten Japanese players are registered with Premier League clubs, marking a record high. Clubs are drawn to their skill, cost-effectiveness, and low risk. Zion Suzuki's move to Aston Villa and Takehiro Tomiyasu's return to Crystal Palace highlight this trend. FIFA agent Joel Pannick notes increased confidence in Japanese players' adaptation and integration. Japanese players like Wataru Endo and Kaoru Mitoma are already established in the league. Pannick attributes the success to improved language skills and a more tactical Premier League style, which suits Japanese players' playing style. The league's shift toward coordinated play has made it easier for Japanese players to thrive.
source.title: Ten Japanese players in Premier League set new record

source.summary: Dolly Parton, a legendary country music singer and songwriter, passed away at age 80 in Nashville, her family announced. Known for her heartfelt lyrics and business acumen, Parton sold over 100 million records and won 11 Grammy awards, including a Lifetime Achievement Award. Her music, including classics like 'Jolene' and 'I Will Always Love You,' resonated globally, and she became one of the best-selling female artists of all time. Parton was also a philanthropist, donating $1 million to vaccine research and launching literacy programs. Her ability to connect with people and her distinctive image, shaped by her signature look and vibrant personality, made her a cultural icon. Despite her fame, she remained grounded, emphasizing her work as a songwriter and her commitment to her roots.
source.title: Dolly Parton's Legacy Lives On Through Music and Philanthropy

source.summary: Hundreds gathered at a police station in Porepunkah to honor two officers killed by Dezi Freeman one year ago, with a minute's silence and heartfelt tributes. The incident occurred on 26 August 2025 when officers attempted to serve a warrant at Freeman's remote property, resulting in two deaths and one serious injury. Family members of the slain officer, Neal Thompson, expressed their grief, highlighting his dedication to his job. Meanwhile, Australian Prime Minister Anthony Albanese's department confirmed that four Japanese melons gifted by Prime Minister Sanae Takaichi were valued at $200 each, below the $750 threshold for declaration. The gifts sparked controversy after Albanese's comments on a podcast. Other news included a federal MP stepping aside from a special envoy role due to legal issues, inflation data showing a slight decrease, and reflections on Australia's immigration policies following the Tampa affair.
source.title: Australia news live: Hundreds pay tribute to police killed by Dezi Freeman on one-year anniversary; value of Japan’s melon gifts to Albanese revealed

source.summary: SpaceX announced plans to build a $100 billion rocket launch complex in southern Louisiana, named Starbase Louisiana, covering 125,000 acres on Pecan Island. The site, which will support Starship and AI satellite missions, is expected to handle thousands of launches annually once operational. Construction is set to begin next year, with the first Starship launch planned for 2029. The project includes methane production, power generation, and deep-water shipping capabilities. SpaceX emphasized environmental restoration efforts, including protecting migratory bird habitats. The site cleared legal hurdles after a settlement with ExxonMobil, allowing the project to proceed. The initiative is part of SpaceX's broader expansion in the southern U.S., including data centers and Starlink facilities.
source.title: SpaceX to develop $100 billion launch site in Louisiana for Starship missions

source.summary: U.S. President Trump has submitted a classified civil nuclear agreement with Saudi Arabia to Congress for review, as required by the Atomic Energy Act. The pact, signed by U.S. Energy Secretary Chris Wright and his Saudi counterpart, includes a condition that Saudi Arabia normalize relations with Israel through the Abraham Accords. The agreement's implementation hinges on this condition, raising concerns about its viability. Congress has 90 days to review the deal, which could take effect without approval. The deal, expected to last 30 years, involves U.S. firms in developing Saudi's civilian nuclear program. Critics warn it could enable Saudi uranium enrichment and nuclear proliferation. The Saudi Embassy did not comment, while Israeli Prime Minister Benjamin Netanyahu opposes Palestinian statehood, a prerequisite for Saudi normalization with Israel.
source.title: Trump's Saudi nuclear deal faces congressional review amid Israel ties condition

source.summary: Golf Channel postponed the premiere of 'Big Break x Good Good' by a week due to a sponsor's request to remove branding, following backlash against a video showing a man shoving a woman. The video, an ad for Callaway, was deleted after drawing criticism for depicting violence against women. Good Good apologized, and Callaway expressed disappointment, with its CEO acknowledging approval of the video. The PGA Tour also voiced concerns, while the sponsor's identity was reported as Golf Galaxy.
source.title: Golf Channel postpones ‘Big Break’ premiere after sponsor pulls out over Good Good Golf video

source.summary: Minnesota Vikings wide receiver Jeshaun Jones received a three-game suspension from the NFL for violating the league's substance abuse policy. The NFL did not specify the nature of the violation. Jones, who spent the past two years on the practice squad, was promoted to the active roster and played in the 2025 season's final game. He remains eligible for the remaining preseason games but will miss the first three regular-season games. His suspension begins on Sunday, with reinstatement possible on Sept. 28. Jones faces competition for roster spots with established players like Justin Jefferson and Jordan Addison.
source.title: Vikings WR Jeshaun Jones Suspended for 3 Games Over Substance Abuse Violation

source.summary: A tornado devastated Pomas, with residents describing the destruction as 'like bombs were dropped on our heads'. The article notes technical issues preventing full loading, suggesting potential browser or network problems.
source.title: Tornado strikes Pomas, residents describe devastation

source.summary: The article examines the historical significance of the Suez Canal, tracing its origins as a colonial project and its eventual decline. It highlights how the canal, once a symbol of European imperial power, has faced challenges and transformations over time. The piece explores the political and economic factors that contributed to its rise and fall. The Suez Canal's role in global trade is discussed, alongside its impact on regional geopolitics. The article suggests that the canal's legacy is complex, reflecting both the ambitions and limitations of colonial rule.
source.title: Suez Canal's colonial legacy and its decline

source.summary: Typhoon Narra triggered record floodwaters in Guangxi, China, leading to the evacuation of over 54,000 people. In Chongzuo, water levels surpassed 2008 highs, submerging homes and reaching rooftops. Authorities ordered business closures and warned against returning to high-risk areas. Meanwhile, Typhoon Saudel approached Japan and Taiwan, causing separate flooding and casualties. In Taiwan, a tropical depression led to one death and four missing in Tainan and Kaohsiung, where rainfall exceeded that of Typhoon Morakot in 2009.
source.title: Typhoon Narra causes record floods in Guangxi, China, prompting evacuations

source.summary: Flash floods killed roughly 160 people and left hundreds missing after a glacier collapse triggered a landslide in Nepal. Initial analysis suggests warming temperatures destabilized the ice, causing a massive piece to fall and pulverize into water. Experts note that retreating glaciers increase risks of catastrophic glacial lake outburst floods globally. While conclusive statements on the cause remain premature, satellite imagery indicates a 2,000-foot-wide ice section fell nearly 4,000 feet. The event registered as a magnitude 5.2 seismic event, highlighting the growing danger of climate change in mountainous regions.
source.title: Rising temperatures likely contributed to Nepal's deadly flash floods

source.summary: Alabama Power has partnered with over 80 municipalities across the state to provide subscription-based surveillance services from companies like Flock Safety. The utility markets automated license plate readers and cameras as a convenient public safety tool, leveraging its existing power poles for installation and electricity. Critics argue this arrangement obscures costs and accountability, embedding private surveillance infrastructure within public utility bills. While law enforcement agencies praise the technology for solving crimes, residents and legal scholars express concern over data privacy and potential misuse. Records show millions of data searches by local governments, yet transparency regarding contracts and data sharing remains limited. Birmingham recently approved a multi-million dollar contract to expand its camera network, bypassing competitive bidding under a public safety exception. Despite company claims that they do not access customer data, questions persist about how sensitive location information is managed and shared among third parties.
source.title: Alabama Power Partners With Surveillance Firms To Expand City Monitoring

source.summary: The Invest in Tomorrow Coalition, a super PAC financed by solar entrepreneurs and Silicon Valley venture capitalists, spent $1 million supporting Darline Graham's victory over Rep. Ralph Norman in South Carolina. Tom Matzzie, the group's chair, stated the PAC aims to demonstrate that the clean energy industry can be politically lethal to opponents. The group targeted Republicans who opposed clean energy subsidies, using ads devoid of environmental messaging to attack candidates' loyalty to President Trump. Matzzie explained the strategy focuses on accountability rather than advocacy, aiming to create chatter among members of Congress. Edward Maibach of George Mason University noted that political action by clean energy companies is critical to counter the fossil fuel industry's influence. The PAC has also spent heavily in Tennessee and Texas, with Chris Larsen contributing $5 million to the group. While primarily targeting Republicans, Matzzie indicated Democrats opposing clean energy would not be exempt from future efforts.
source.title: Clean Energy Super PAC Targets Conservatives Against Renewable Initiatives

source.summary: Sumitomo Mitsui Banking Corporation reached financial close on a 210 MW hybrid renewable energy project developed by JSW Energy in Maharashtra. This transaction marks SMBC's first project finance deal with JSW Group's renewable platform and JSW Energy's first facility via External Commercial Borrowing. SMBC served as the mandated lead arranger and sole structuring bank for the wind and solar initiative. The financing expands SMBC's portfolio in India's renewable energy sector and supports the country's growing electricity demand.
source.title: SMBC reaches financial close on JSW Energy 210 MW hybrid project

source.summary: The Solar Energy Corporation of India Limited issued a Request for Empanelment to select cybersecurity auditing organizations for the nation's renewable energy sector. This initiative aims to ensure independent audits of IT and Operational Technology systems used in renewable projects. SECI, acting as the Sectoral Computer Emergency Response Team, plans to support entities in meeting Central Electricity Authority regulations. The initial empanelment period is set for two years, with potential extensions based on satisfactory performance. Applicants must pay a non-refundable bid processing fee of ₹5,000, except for Micro and Small Enterprises. Selected agencies will be deployed across five geographic zones to conduct regular security assessments.
source.title: SECI invites cybersecurity auditors to strengthen renewable energy sector security

source.summary: The New Brunswick government granted conditional approval for a 500-megawatt natural gas plant operated by U.S.-based ProEnergy. Officials state the facility is essential to prevent rolling blackouts within two years. The project requires meeting 45 specific conditions regarding environmental monitoring and emergency management. Environment Minister Gilles LePage emphasized that ProEnergy must adhere to these requirements or face project shutdown. While the plant will primarily burn natural gas, it can switch to diesel if needed. Critics, including Green Party legislator Megan Mitton and Environmental Defence, argue the approval is irresponsible and risks energy security. The facility is scheduled to begin operation by 2028, with Nova Scotia already agreeing to purchase 100 megawatts of its output.
source.title: New Brunswick approves 500-MW gas plant with strict conditions

source.summary: CleanTechnica reports that the vast majority of vehicles receiving 'park outside' safety warnings in the US have internal combustion engines rather than electric powertrains. The Washington Post analysis indicates that conventional gas and diesel cars account for most recalls due to 'key-off' fires caused by always-on electronics. Sean Kane of Safety Research and Strategies explains that growing electronic systems in modern vehicles contribute to these risks. While EV battery fires receive significant attention, data shows conventional vehicles experience roughly 1,500 fires per 100,000 sold compared to about 25 for electric vehicles. Adam Barowy of the Fire Safety Research Institute notes that better data collection is beginning to clarify these statistics. The article concludes that fear of EV fires often overshadows the higher fire risk associated with traditional gasoline and diesel cars.
source.title: Most US 'Park Outside' Warnings Apply to Internal Combustion Engine Vehicles

source.summary: CleanTechnica reports that fully electric vehicle registrations in Europe jumped 51% year over year in July, reaching 288,000 units. This growth was driven by new affordable models and high fuel prices, pushing the year-to-date BEV market share to 23%. While electrification is advanced in Northern Europe, adoption remains low in Southern and Central regions. Tesla faced a 36% decline in sales due to a lack of stock, allowing competitors like Skoda and BMW to lead the monthly rankings. The article notes that while Volkswagen Group leads by automotive group, BYD is gaining ground at the expense of Stellantis. CleanTechnica highlights that the B and C segments remain the primary laggards for full electrification.
source.title: European EV sales surge as Tesla struggles amid rising Chinese competition

source.summary: Nevada officials filed the first lawsuit challenging the federal government's new management plan for the Colorado River. The state argues the plan illegally forces unacceptable water reductions on its urban population center. Nevada claims the federal decision failed to consider economic impacts or creative alternatives to drastic cuts. While the state previously advocated for compromise, it now seeks legal intervention after negotiations failed. Experts note this action does not necessarily end future collaboration among basin states. The suit casts uncertainty over near-term water operations but may not prevent long-term agreements.
source.title: Nevada Sues Federal Government Over Colorado River Water Cuts

source.summary: Sony Music Publishing and Warner Chappell sued Anthropic in the Northern District of California, alleging the company engaged in illegal torrenting to train its Claude AI model. The lawsuit claims a brazen campaign of intellectual property theft involving thousands of copyrighted works. This action follows a separate $1.5 billion ruling in the Bartz v. Anthropic case regarding similar practices. The new suit is broader, accusing the lab of flagrant piracy to obtain millions of books containing lyrics and sheet music.
source.title: Music publishers sue Anthropic over alleged copyright theft for AI training

source.summary: Former Kansas City Fed President Tom Hoenig told Semafor that the Federal Reserve has been too quiet regarding the Treasury Department's campaign to lower yields by purchasing long-term debt. Hoenig, now with the Mercatus Center, noted that the Fed avoids mentioning Treasury actions to maintain independence, though coordination could raise concerns under the Trump administration. Treasury Secretary Scott Bessent plans to double government bond purchases, a move that risks clashing with Fed Chair Kevin Warsh's strategy to shrink the central bank's balance sheet. Hoenig warned Warsh that raising interest rates next month will require extensive explanations to the Treasury to avoid market disturbance. Additionally, Hoenig predicted President Trump's attempt to remove Fed Governor Lisa Cook would fail and urged Congress to rein in spending before a fiscal crisis occurs.
source.title: The Fed ‘has been a little too quiet’ on Treasury, former Fed official says

source.summary: An investor argues that holding Nvidia stock remains justified despite a high price-to-sales ratio of 17. The author points to the company's rapid revenue growth and dominant position in artificial intelligence as key reasons. Nvidia recently reported a second quarter with revenue up 106% year over year to $96 billion. The company also announced a $12.9 billion acquisition of AI specialist Hugging Face. CEO Jensen Huang stated that AI has reached an inflection point with accelerating demand.
source.title: Author Defends Nvidia Stock Despite High Valuation Citing Growth

source.summary: Tim Cook maintains formal leadership and advisory positions at various external institutions alongside his duties as Apple's chief executive. The article notes that these commitments include board and trustee roles across corporate, educational, and athletic organizations. These positions remain an active component of his professional scope.
source.title: Tim Cook holds leadership roles beyond Apple

source.summary: OpenAI announced it will end its contract to provide AI models to Cursor, a coding platform owned by Elon Musk. The company stated the shutdown is scheduled for November 12, 2026. This decision follows a notification sent to SpaceX regarding the termination of the agreement. The move intensifies the ongoing conflict between OpenAI CEO Sam Altman and Musk.
source.title: OpenAI plans to cut off Cursor from its AI models by November 12

source.summary: Time Magazine released its 2026 list of 100 most influential people in artificial intelligence without including Nvidia CEO Jensen Huang. The publication noted his absence despite his company leading the AI sector. The article highlights this notable omission from the annual ranking.
source.title: Nvidia CEO Jensen Huang excluded from Time's 2026 AI influencers list

source.summary: A federal judge ruled that the Trump administration violated constitutional rights by deporting international students for criticizing Israel's war on Gaza. District Judge Noel Wise criticized the State Department and DHS for punishing protected speech. The decision centered on visa revocations targeting students like Mahmoud Khalil who advocated for Palestine. Lawyers hailed the ruling as a victory for First Amendment rights against government retaliation.
source.title: US judge rules against Trump deportation of pro-Palestinian students

source.summary: The provided text lists several unrelated news items. Roger Myerson has launched a new Substack publication. The Wall Street Journal reports on puffin tourism in Maine and the business acumen of Dolly Parton. Additionally, a description of the Global Economics Lab at Harvard is included, noting its non-partisan research focus.
source.title: Roger Myerson launches Substack; WSJ covers Maine tourism and Dolly Parton

source.summary: Dana Peterson, Chief Economist at The Conference Board, told Semafor that consumer sentiment among Republicans and independents is starting to fade before the midterm elections. She noted that while Democrats remain the least optimistic, independents are recently moving in a negative direction alongside Republicans. Peterson attributed this shift to concerns about elevated inflation, interest rates, and issues like oil prices, food costs, and global conflict. She predicted Federal Reserve Chair Kevin Warsh would not support an interest-rate hike at the next meeting, citing risks of demand destruction. Additionally, Peterson expressed concern that coordination between the Treasury and the Fed could jeopardize the central bank's independence, especially amid President Trump's attempts to fire Fed Governor Lisa Cook.
source.title: Economist says GOP consumer sentiment fading ahead of midterms

source.summary: The United Nations announced that 13 people, including six children and seven women, were released after being kidnapped in Kenscoff, Haiti. UNICEF representatives stated this event highlights the ongoing crisis affecting the country's youth. The abduction occurred during a larger attack on August 23 where armed gangs killed at least 47 people and displaced thousands. UN officials described the incident as a stark reminder of the scale of violence threatening children across Haiti. The country faces severe instability due to political turmoil, natural disasters, and the expansion of armed groups. A general election is scheduled for December, but security forces remain stretched as gangs continue to challenge state authority. The Haitian government pledged to deploy reinforcements to restore order in the affected area.
source.title: Haitian gangs release 13 captives after mass kidnapping in Kenscoff

source.summary: Three friends launched a crowdfunding campaign to save their Cheltenham crafting shop from rising costs. The business moved locations earlier this year, causing overheads to double. Founders Siobhan Westmacott, Samantha Potter, and Zarina Ismail work other jobs and contribute personal funds to the business. The fundraiser aims to cover a core restock order and fill shelf gaps. The shop hosts community crafting sessions and supports local charities.
source.title: Friends launch fundraiser to keep independent crafting shop open

source.summary: The North American Electric Reliability Corporation issued a Level 3 Essential Action Alert requiring immediate utility responses to power fluctuations caused by AI data centres. Thomas Sisto of XL Batteries stated that individual campuses now draw gigawatts of power, creating swings from zero to 100% in milliseconds that traditional grids cannot absorb. Dr. Hooman Ghaffarzadeh of Wärtsilä Energy Storage explained that unlike predictable industrial loads, these dynamic demands occur every 10 milliseconds without reliable forecast profiles. Matthew Williams of IONATE noted that current monitoring lags are too slow to catch such disturbances, necessitating a layered approach using fast transformers and battery storage. Industry experts anticipate these alerts will evolve into formal interconnection requirements similar to those for renewable energy. Sisto emphasized that storage must be designed to manage daily load smoothing rather than just backup power to bridge the gap until transmission upgrades are complete.
source.title: NERC issues Level 3 alert for AI data centre grid risks

source.summary: TEPCO officially entered Unit 6 of the Kashiwazaki-Kariwa Nuclear Power Station into commercial operation in April after completing safety inspections. The restart marks the first time this facility has operated commercially since the 2011 Fukushima disaster. Japan now has 15 operating nuclear plants with a combined capacity of about 33 GW. Officials state the goal is to have nuclear power supply at least 20% of the nation's electricity by 2030. The U.S. Energy Information Administration estimates the restart could displace about 1.3 million tons of LNG annually. TEPCO implemented extensive upgrades, including new seawalls and watertight doors, to prevent flooding. Industry analysts note these measures address lessons learned from the Fukushima accident.
source.title: TEPCO Restarts Kashiwazaki-Kariwa Unit 6 Reactor in Japan

source.summary: Korea Hydro & Nuclear Power (KHNP) announced that Saeul 3 reached criticality on April 12, 2026, marking a major milestone for the 1,400-MW APR1400 reactor. The unit, originally Shin Kori Unit 5, experienced a nine-year interruption due to national policy shifts and regulatory reviews. KHNP expects commercial operation by October 2026, with the plant supplying 37% of Ulsan's electricity demand. The reactor includes enhanced safety features, such as aircraft-impact-resistant structures and expanded spent-fuel storage. Despite minor issues like a smoke incident and turbine concerns, the project continues toward its target of meeting South Korea's growing data-center power needs.
source.title: Saeul 3 Reactor Achieves Criticality After Nine-Year Construction Delay

source.summary: A University of Exeter research group reviewed literature on vehicle-integrated photovoltaics, arguing battery preservation is the primary value rather than range extension. The team found standard solar ratings fail to capture real-world driving conditions like urban shading and vibrations. They concluded that dynamic testing standards are needed to properly assess these systems. The review suggests VIPV reduces grid-charging frequency and slows battery degradation through trickle charging.
source.title: Exeter researchers say vehicle-integrated PV protects EV batteries more than extending range

source.summary: The article notes that two months remain before the OEEC 2026 event. Readers are advised to secure their tickets now. The text provides a call to action for ticket buyers.
source.title: Organizers urge fans to purchase tickets for OEEC 2026 event in two months

source.summary: A massive Ukrainian drone attack set fire to Russia's Ust-Luga oil export terminal overnight. Leningrad region governor Alexander Drozdenko stated that 52 drones were shot down and the fire was extinguished with no casualties. The port, a key export outlet for Russian oil, has been targeted multiple times since 2022 to disrupt fuel supplies and export revenues. Ukraine continues its campaign to cripple Russian energy infrastructure, contributing to a domestic fuel crisis.
source.title: Ukraine strikes Russian Ust-Luga oil port, causing fire and damage

source.summary: ONE Nuclear Energy signed a binding letter of intent with Louisiana landowners to develop Project Cayman. The site will host a 2.88GW natural gas plant, a 700MW battery system, and a data centre. CEO Richard Taylor stated the project aims to support regional economic growth and grid reliability. Community engagement meetings are scheduled between September and December 2026.
source.title: ONE Nuclear secures Louisiana site for 2.88GW Project Cayman

source.summary: Odyssey Energy Solutions announced the closing of a $74 million fundraising round to expand its platform for financing distributed energy projects. The company, founded in 2017, raised $27 million in equity and $47 million in debt to deepen its presence in markets like Nigeria, India, and Latin America. Odyssey acts as a middleman, placing equipment orders on behalf of local installers and allowing them to pay off costs over time after their clients pay. CEO Emily McAteer stated that distributed energy is leapfrogging centralized grids, particularly in the Global South where reliability is low. The company now facilitates over $3.6 billion in financing across more than 50 countries. Odyssey plans to use the new capital to expand into financing batteries for electric two- and three-wheelers. The firm also acquired Ferntech in 2021 to gain data on project performance, which helps underwrite credit risk for lenders. Meanwhile, California lawmakers passed the Home Energy Choice Act, requiring utilities to offer incentives for home electrification instead of replacing gas service lines. Governor Gavin Newsom has until September 30 to sign or veto the bill. Separately, Chemours filed for priority review of a new coolant, Opteon 2P50, for data centers. Environmental groups oppose the chemical, a PFAS, arguing it poses health risks and that the EPA's fast-track review is inappropriate.
source.title: Odyssey Energy raises $74 million to expand small-scale solar financing

source.summary: Ørsted announced that its 920 MW offshore wind project in Taiwan has entered the final commissioning phase. The company stated this milestone marks the project's transition toward full operational status. No specific completion date was provided in the initial report.
source.title: Ørsted begins final commissioning of 920 MW Taiwan offshore wind project

source.summary: GenusPlus Group received formal approval to start building the North West Transmission Developments Stage 1 project for TasNetworks. The contract, valued at approximately A$750m, includes upgrading Tasmania's transmission infrastructure to support renewable energy growth. Construction is scheduled to finish by 2029, involving a new dual-circuit 220kV line and new switching stations. Genus managing director David Riches stated the company is committed to employing local people and engaging Tasmanian businesses throughout the work.
source.title: Genus begins construction on TasNetworks $537m Tasmanian transmission project

source.summary: Ørsted announced the completion of main construction on the 920 MW Greater Changhua 2b and 4 offshore wind farms in Taiwan. The projects are expected to enter full commercial operation in late Q3 2026 after remaining commissioning work. Ørsted developed the project with Cathay Life Insurance and various suppliers. The development adds to Taiwan's offshore wind sector and increases Ørsted's market presence. Patrick Harnett, Ørsted's chief construction officer, called the delivery a major achievement. The financing structure highlights the role of Taiwanese institutional capital, with Cathay Life holding stakes in the projects. Thirty financial institutions supported the project's financing. A corporate power purchase agreement links the development to Taiwan's semiconductor industry. Group CEO Rasmus Errboe stated the completion is a significant milestone in Ørsted's strategy. Construction included suction bucket jacket foundations and local operations capability development at the Port of Taichung.
source.title: Ørsted completes 920 MW Greater Changhua offshore wind build in Taiwan

source.summary: Researchers published a study in Communications Earth & Environment arguing that limiting global warming to well-below 2C requires stringent methane emissions cuts alongside net-zero CO2 targets. The authors report that even under ambitious national net-zero goals, failing to reduce methane leads to peak warming exceeding 1.85C. Their analysis indicates that to reach 1.7C under a 2050 net-zero CO2 scenario, methane must fall by at least 69% by 2050. Conversely, current policies project a 20% methane increase by 2050, which would push peak warming above 2C even if CO2 reaches net-zero. The study suggests that cutting methane by one-third could reduce peak warming by 0.15C, with 0.05C achievable at no net cost. The authors conclude that decoupling methane from CO2 metrics is necessary to refine existing climate targets.
source.title: Study shows methane cuts are crucial to limit warming below 2C

source.summary: Inside Climate News reports that the Trump administration's EPA is enforcing environmental laws less effectively than its own performance metrics suggest. The analysis reveals a sharp decline in civil lawsuits against major polluters and a strategic shift toward low-cost administrative orders. Former EPA administrator Christine Todd Whitman stated that the agency has removed enforcement officers, while Inside Climate News data shows the workforce lost more than a quarter of its staff. Legal expert Laura Thoms noted that remaining attorneys require explicit political approval to proceed with cases. The agency has also dismissed lawsuits against political allies, such as the Denka chemical company, and dropped complaints against major donors like the GEO Group. Consequently, the median cost to offenders has dropped to a new low, with most actions now being minor compliance orders regarding lead pipes rather than significant penalties. Critics argue this approach allows violators to profit while undermining the agency's core mission of protecting public health.
source.title: Analysis Shows Trump EPA Enforcement Is Weaker Than Reported

source.summary: A new report from the nonprofit Plastic Pollution Coalition documents how the plastics industry has inserted its agenda into classrooms across the U.S. through lesson plans, worksheets, and mobile programs. Industry interests provide these resources for free or cheap, often highlighting plastic necessity while downplaying environmental and health risks. Madison Dennis of the Plastic Pollution Coalition stated that this information obfuscates the true impacts of plastic pollution. The report cites cases where trade groups like the Society of Plastics Engineers and Dow Chemical Company initiatives promote industry talking points under the guise of STEM education. Experts argue these materials prioritize ideological perspectives over scientific accuracy and good pedagogy. The Plastic Pollution Coalition is calling for stricter school policies against industry-sponsored learning materials.
source.title: Plastic industry inserts agenda into U.S. school curricula

source.summary: The Trump administration has agreed to pay nearly $4 billion to energy firms to abandon offshore wind leases, a move coastal states are now challenging in court. California became the eighth state to sue, arguing the practice jeopardizes state investments and jobs. The Department of the Interior returned $120 million to Golden State Wind in exchange for fossil fuel investments, a deal California Attorney General Rob Bonta calls "blatantly unlawful." Critics question the Interior Bureau of Ocean Energy Management's legal authority to refund lease funds and claim improper use of the federal Judgment Fund. Meanwhile, New York and six other states continue a separate legal challenge over a $795 million agreement with TotalEnergies. These actions represent a significant shift in federal energy policy that opponents say undermines clean energy development.
source.title: Trump administration offshore wind buyouts face legal challenges from coastal states

source.summary: The Invest in Tomorrow Coalition, a super PAC founded by Tom Matzzie, Chris Larsen, and Michael Brune, is spending up to $30 million to influence Republican primary elections. The group focuses on defeating candidates who opposed the Inflation Reduction Act, such as Rep. Andy Ogles and Rep. Ralph Norman. Matzzie stated the strategy aims to make politicians fear antagonizing the clean energy industry. While the PAC has succeeded in several primaries, experts note its impact on future legislation remains uncertain. Steve McBee of Amped advocates for coalition building rather than creating enemies. The clean energy sector continues to seek greater political influence despite recent legislative setbacks.
source.title: Invest in Tomorrow Coalition super PAC targets Republican foes of clean energy

source.summary: Independent research indicates that Rot-Guard total barrier systems can extend the service life of wood poles by 20 years. The system bonds to and seals the pole surface to prevent moisture entry and biological decay. Field studies in Uganda showed poles with the barrier remained free from fungal decay and termite attacks over eight years. UK Building Research Establishment tests confirmed protected poles stayed dry and decay-free after ten years of service.
source.title: Rot-Guard total barrier system extends wood pole life by 20 years

source.summary: A voltage dip in Virginia disconnected 1,500 megawatts from 60 facilities, prompting NERC to issue a Level 3 Alert for dynamic fault recording. FERC now requires regional operators to evaluate Grid Enhancing Technologies like Dynamic Line Rating. EGM states its Meta-Alert platform can locate faults within 300 feet and compress response times to roughly one hour.
source.title: AI Data Centers Create New Grid Risks as Utilities Adopt Monitoring Tech

source.summary: AI's erratic power consumption is damaging data centre equipment and threatening grid stability. Experts warn these fluctuations could cause blackouts and harm household appliances. A 2026 U.S. Department of Energy report calls for better monitoring of the issue.
source.title: AI Power Fluctuations Damage Data Centres and Risk Household Grids

source.summary: Adamant describes connecting Canada's fragmented electricity grids as a critical nation-building initiative. The authors report that provinces currently trade more power with the United States than with one another, creating isolated energy islands. A new east-west transmission network would lower costs, create tens of thousands of jobs, and reduce reliance on American markets. The Canadian Climate Institute identifies this project as essential for economic resilience and Indigenous reconciliation. Federal recommendations include a $20 billion investment package and prioritizing Canadian steel and aluminum content. A March 2026 Leger poll found 76% of Canadians support upgrading the grid to reduce energy exports.
source.title: Adamant calls east-west transmission lines Canada's top nation-building project
