source.summary: U.S. Sen. Darline Graham has won the Republican nomination in South Carolina's special Senate election, replacing her late brother Lindsey Graham. She defeated Rep. Ralph Norman in a runoff primary, gaining support from President Trump, who endorsed her campaign and campaigned with her. Graham, a political newcomer, emphasized her alignment with Trump's policies and her focus on domestic issues. Norman, a more experienced candidate, criticized Graham's lack of expertise in foreign policy during a debate. Graham will face Democratic nominee Annie Andrews in November. Trump's backing appears to be a strategic move to secure a Senate ally, as no Democrat has won a South Carolina Senate seat in decades.
source.title: Darline Graham secures South Carolina GOP Senate nomination

source.summary: Oswaldo Pirela, a San Diego Padres minor league catching coordinator, was released on bond after being detained by ICE at El Paso International Airport. His family disputes the government's claim that he overstayed his visa, stating he applied for asylum and obtained work permits. The Padres confirmed his release and will not comment further. Pirela's family emphasizes his lawful presence and contributions to the U.S., calling for due process. DHS has not responded to requests for comment.
source.title: San Diego Padres coach released after ICE detention

source.summary: Hundreds of Egyptian Sufi Muslims gathered in Cairo on Tuesday to celebrate the birth of Prophet Mohammed. Participants held banners and chanted religious hymns during a procession from the Sidi Saleh Al-Jaafari Mosque to the shrine of Al-Hussein. Saber Abd El Raouf, a Sufi shiekh, described the event as renewing faith within hearts. Hassan Abd El Nazeem, another Sufi member, explained the celebration involved chanting praises and reciting supplications for the Prophet's birthday.
source.title: Sufi Muslims in Cairo Celebrate Prophet's Birth with Procession and Chants

source.summary: The United States has launched 'Operation Economic Outcast' to isolate Iran by urging countries to cut economic ties, warning of retaliation. Treasury Secretary Scott Bessent emphasized that all entities must face sanctions, offering Iran two paths: global isolation or rejoining the global economy. The campaign follows US-Israeli strikes on Iran six months prior, with the regional conflict now at a stalemate.
source.title: US urges nations to sever economic ties with Iran amid sanctions campaign

source.summary: Interpol coordinated Operation Jackal IV, arresting 58 individuals linked to West African cybercrime groups across 22 countries. The operation focused on romance and investment scams, identifying 263 suspects. It also examined trends like sextortion targeting minors and money laundering. Interpol emphasized international cooperation in disrupting financial flows. In South Africa, 39 arrests were made, with $2.67m seized. The operation is part of a series targeting networks like Black Axe, which engages in global criminal activities.
source.title: Interpol arrests 58 in global operation targeting West African cybercrime networks

source.summary: The UN condemned the Israeli raid on the Qalandia Training Center, a UNRWA vocational school in occupied East Jerusalem. UN spokesperson Stephane Dujarric called the entry unlawful and expressed concern over the disruption of education for Palestinian youth. The raid marked the fifth unauthorized entry since May, following other breaches of UN premises. UN Secretary-General Antonio Guterres urged Israel to cease interference and restore the facility. The center, operational for over 70 years, provides vocational training to hundreds of students annually.
source.title: UN Condemns Israeli Raid on Qalandia Training Center

source.summary: The USS Abraham Lincoln, which spent over 250 days at sea without a port call, is set to make a brief stop in Thailand in early September. Thailand’s Navy described the visit as routine, providing rest and logistical support for the nearly 5,000 crew members. The ship left San Diego in November 2025 and had only one stop in Guam during its deployment. Concerns about living conditions, including cold showers and supply shortages, have been raised by family members and media outlets. Two Democratic senators requested an independent review of conditions aboard the ship and others involved in the Iran conflict. Defense Secretary Pete Hegseth acknowledged the deployment’s difficulty but praised the crew’s performance. Meanwhile, a crew member’s father faces deportation after being detained by immigration agents in Key West.
source.title: USS Abraham Lincoln ends 250-day deployment with Thailand stop

source.summary: A large immigration raid at a bonded warehouse in New Jersey detained 46 workers, including María Eugenia García’s daughter Killy Tatiana, who was arrested during an immigration operation in October 2025. The raid, involving multiple federal agencies, disrupted the lives of over 50 people and their families, with many workers holding pending asylum applications or valid work permits. The Trump administration’s aggressive immigration policies, including daily arrest quotas and widespread raids, have intensified the crackdown on undocumented workers. Advocates argue these operations violate constitutional rights, as law enforcement lacked warrants for entry into the warehouse. Killy Tatiana was deported to Colombia, where she now lives under voluntary departure, while her mother struggles with the emotional toll of separation. The case highlights the broader impact of immigration enforcement on families and communities, with legal challenges ongoing as activists seek transparency and accountability.
source.title: Immigration raid in New Jersey separates 46 workers from families

source.summary: Nigeria's President Bola Tinubu has ordered a manhunt for kidnappers who attacked four villages in Niger state, killing over 40 people. The attackers, dressed in military-style clothing, abducted up to 500 people, though this has not been verified. A video released by the kidnappers showed some of the captives, identified by a local youth leader. Authorities suspect the attackers are bandits, not jihadists, and have not received ransom demands. The attack highlights growing insecurity in the region, with local officials warning of increasing jihadist activity.
source.title: Nigeria's president orders manhunt after kidnappers release victim video

source.summary: Elon Musk's Starlink has begun offering satellite internet in Vietnam, a country with strict online controls. The service, operated through a local subsidiary, is available on a controlled trial basis with 600,000 subscribers allowed until 2030. Vietnam's government approved the trial in 2025 to avoid US trade penalties, but Starlink's high cost may limit its impact, especially in rural areas where average income is lower than its service price. Analysts suggest its primary benefit may be for institutions rather than individuals. Despite potential connectivity improvements, Starlink must comply with Vietnam's censorship laws, and experts believe it will not challenge the country's digital sovereignty. The service operates through licensed domestic infrastructure, ensuring it remains within the government's regulatory framework.
source.title: Starlink's Vietnam Trial Faces Censorship and Cost Challenges

source.summary: US Treasury Secretary Scott Bessent announced new sanctions targeting Iran's shadow economy, focusing on digital assets, gold, and shipping networks. The measures aim to disrupt money laundering and pressurize foreign intermediaries. The US has sanctioned 60 entities and individuals but avoided major Chinese banks. Iran's economy faces severe inflation, with food prices rising 128% year-on-year, and many transactions now conducted in US dollars. Iranian businesses struggle with rising costs and disrupted supply chains, with over 70% of employees laid off at one company. Sanctions also affect Iranian entrepreneurs abroad, creating uncertainty for those operating in Dubai. Analysts suggest the measures may intensify inflationary expectations and deepen economic polarization without fundamentally altering Iran's behavior. The sanctions could strengthen informal economic networks, leading to a more uncontrolled underground economy.
source.title: US sanctions target Iran's shadow economy networks

source.summary: The Israeli Defense Forces (IDF) issued an evacuation order for certain Tehran neighborhoods ahead of planned strikes. The announcement was made by IDF Spokesperson Avichay Adraee in Arabic. The situation is described as a developing story with further updates expected.
source.title: IDF Orders Evacuation of Tehran Areas Before Strikes

source.summary: The Defense Ministry's Border Crossings Authority will conduct an exercise on Sunday between 11 a.m. and 1:30 p.m. at the Tarkumiya Crossing on Highway 35, according to a statement from the ministry. The exercise may involve gunshots and explosions, with high movement of emergency and rescue vehicles expected. The ministry warned that the activity could cause traffic disruptions.
source.title: Defense Ministry Conducts Exercise on Highway 35

source.summary: Chennai, once known as Madras, has undergone significant transformation from a colonial trading hub to a diversified global business destination. The city's industrial development began in the late 19th century with initiatives like the Madras Chamber of Commerce and Industry, which aimed to stimulate technical education and industrial growth. Early industries such as cotton piece goods and indigo laid the foundation for later manufacturing, including the establishment of mills and factories like Binny’s Buckingham Mill and Simpson’s coach building. The automotive sector took root in the mid-20th century with companies like Ashok Leyland and TVS Motor Company. In recent decades, Chennai has embraced the IT revolution, becoming a hub for multinational corporations and startups, with over 5,134 startups and a growing focus on deep tech and innovation. The city is also expanding into new sectors like electric vehicles, animation, and space technology, with plans to create 200,000 jobs by 2030. Experts predict continued growth in GCCs, NBFCs, and new-age startups, positioning Chennai as a key player in India's evolving economic landscape.
source.title: Chennai's Evolution from Madras: A Century of Industrial and Technological Transformation

source.summary: A speeding bus collided with a stationary lorry near Suryapet in Telangana on August 26, 2026, killing six passengers and injuring twelve. The accident occurred at around 5 a.m. with the bus carrying 42 people traveling from Hyderabad to Eluru. Two injured are in critical condition. Chief Minister Revanth Reddy expressed shock and directed officials to provide medical care, while other ministers and local leaders also extended condolences and instructed emergency response measures. Further details remain pending.
source.title: Speeding bus collision with lorry kills six, injures twelve in Telangana

source.summary: Asaduddin Owaisi accused the RSS and BJP of opposing Dr. BR Ambedkar's Constitution and favoring the Manusmriti. During an Eid speech in Hyderabad, he highlighted historical tensions between Hindu nationalist groups and the Constitution, citing an RSS publication that criticized the 1949 Constitution. Owaisi also contrasted the stance of Hindutva ideologue VD Savarkar with Muslim freedom fighters like Allama Fazl-e-Haq Khairabadi. He emphasized the role of Muslim figures in India's independence struggle, noting Maulvi Alauddin as the first prisoner sent to the Andaman Islands. The debate over Manusmriti intensified amid political clashes between BJP and Congress, with Rahul Gandhi criticizing the text's patriarchal views.
source.title: Owaisi criticizes RSS and BJP over Manusmriti opposition to Ambedkar's Constitution

source.summary: Analysts warn that the Hindustan Copper OFS may not attract retail investors despite a 10% discount. The stock fell 7.04% to ₹533.20, with the OFS floor set at ₹514. Siddarth Bhamre notes the discount is not enough to justify investment, as valuations may not offer significant upside. Retail bids will open on Wednesday after the non-retail portion was oversubscribed. Gaikar highlights limited upside and risks of copper price declines, advising against chasing short-term gains.
source.title: Analysts caution retail investors on Hindustan Copper OFS due to limited upside

source.summary: Mid- and small-cap stocks have outperformed blue-chip stocks, with the average advance-to-decline ratio reaching its highest level in four months. This indicates broader market participation, as retail investors favor these segments. In August, mid- and small-cap schemes received 56% of equity flows, compared to 40% in July, while large-cap funds saw outflows. The Nifty Midcap 100 and Nifty Smallcap 100 have risen 22% and 31% since April, outperforming the Nifty 50's 15% gain. Analysts attribute this to strong earnings growth and value opportunities in smaller stocks.
source.title: Mid- and small-cap stocks outperform blue-chips as market breadth expands

source.summary: New York City Mayor Zohran Mamdani opposes a planned event featuring RSS chief Mohan Bhagwat at Madison Square Garden, stating the city may lack legal authority to cancel the private gathering. The event, part of the RSS's centenary outreach, is expected to draw 5,000 Indian diaspora members. Mamdani criticized the RSS's exclusionary vision, aligning with his family's values of pluralism and secularism. Protests against the event have been organized by interfaith groups. The AHEAD Forum promotes the event as a message of global unity.
source.title: New York Mayor Opposes RSS Leader's Event, Questions Legal Authority

source.summary: Global brands have faced backlash for culturally insensitive campaigns, impacting their sales and reputations. Target's Halloween costume was criticized for resembling a racist caricature, leading to its removal. Starbucks faced a sales decline in South Korea over a campaign referencing the Gwangju Uprising. American Eagle's ad campaign drew racial criticism, though the company claimed it expanded its customer base. Anheuser-Busch InBev's Bud Light saw a sales drop after a social media promotion with a transgender influencer. Balenciaga and Gucci faced backlash for designs evoking blackface imagery. H&M and Pepsi faced criticism for ads perceived as racist, while Unilever's Dove and Zara also encountered controversies over their marketing choices.
source.title: Global brands face backlash over culturally insensitive campaigns

source.summary: Europe's solar power generation outperformed other energy sources during the summer's extreme heat and drought, according to Ember. As heat waves and droughts strained traditional power systems, solar panels produced 17% more energy than usual, helping meet cooling demand. Wind and thermal power plants faced reduced output due to cooling system limitations. France's nuclear plants lost 18% of capacity due to warm river water, while UK gas plants cut 2.5 gigawatts. Solar paired with batteries provided evening power when solar output declined. Experts highlight the need for storage solutions as cooling demand grows, with France planning $10 billion in upgrades. Solar and battery installations grew significantly in 2025, with experts calling for regulatory changes to enhance grid flexibility.
source.title: Europe's Solar Power Surpasses Other Sources Amid Heat and Drought

source.summary: Global LNG trade volumes reached a record 56.3 billion cubic feet per day in 2025, up 5.4% from the previous year, according to the GIIGNL. U.S. exports rose 26% to 15.1 Bcf/d, the largest increase among all countries. The U.S. accounted for 26% of global exports, up from 21% in 2024. Qatar and Australia also saw growth, with Qatar's exports rising 3% to 10.6 Bcf/d. However, the closure of the Strait of Hormuz in 2026 disrupted 20% of global LNG supplies. European imports increased by 29% as pipeline gas supplies declined, while Asian imports fell 4% due to reduced Chinese demand.
source.title: U.S. LNG exports surge to record 15.1 Bcf/d in 2025, driving global trade growth

source.summary: The United States produced 13.6 million barrels per day of crude oil in 2025, according to International Energy Statistics, setting a new record. This output, 40% higher than Russia and Saudi Arabia's combined average, was driven by improved shale basin productivity. The Permian Basin saw a 4% increase to 6.6 million b/d, contributing 48% of U.S. production. Despite lower WTI prices, output grew, with forecasts suggesting further increases to 14.2 million b/d by 2027. Russia and Saudi Arabia saw minimal growth, with Saudi production rising to 9.6 million b/d.
source.title: U.S. crude oil production surpasses global rivals in 2025

source.summary: Hitachi Energy unveiled new SF6-free switchgear at CIGRE 2026, including EconiQ 300-kV GIS and 245-kV DTB circuit breakers. The company highlighted its commitment to reducing SF6 use, which has high global warming potential. Over 4,000 EconiQ units have been ordered by customers in 40 countries. Utilities in North America and Europe, including Hydro One and TenneT Germany, have placed orders for the equipment. The expanded portfolio supports grid modernization and accommodates increasing renewable energy integration.
source.title: Hitachi Energy Launches SF6-Free Switchgear for Grid Modernization

source.summary: The U.S. Trade and Development Agency (USTDA) will host a delegation of power sector officials from Angola, Botswana, Mozambique, and Zambia in the U.S. to explore partnerships for modernizing Southern Africa's transmission and distribution systems. The group, comprising about 15 government and private-sector representatives, will visit Denver and Austin, meeting with U.S. companies and utilities to discuss grid security and AI-enabled control systems. USTDA highlighted the potential of advanced technologies to enhance grid stability and efficiency, driven by rising electricity demand from mining and urbanization. A public business briefing in Denver will connect U.S. firms with the delegation to showcase solutions.
source.title: U.S. Delegation to Explore Grid Modernization Partnerships in Southern Africa

source.summary: The Can-Am Pulse 2026 is a compact electric motorcycle designed for city commuting, offering agile handling and a comfortable ride. The reviewer tested it over 570 km of mixed city and highway riding, including in rain and heat, and found it to be confident in braking and with a well-tuned traction control system. The bike features a 6.6kW onboard charger and 50-minute Level 2 top-up time, which are competitive. However, it has some drawbacks, including a constantly running cooling fan in hot weather, Apple CarPlay restrictions, and no DC fast-charging option. The Pulse shares its battery pack with the Outlander Electric and Origin, using NMC cells, and has a 5-year/50,000km battery warranty. While it performs well for daily commuting, its range drops significantly on highways, and the reviewer suggests DC fast-charging would enhance its utility. The bike scores 51.5 out of 85 in overall performance, with strengths in electric performance and ergonomics, but weaknesses in engineering and value.
source.title: Can-Am Pulse 2026 Review: Performance and Features Evaluated

source.summary: Fuyao Glass, a major automotive glass supplier, has launched a semitransparent solar glass product that can generate electricity from a car's roof. While the glass produces around 150W per square meter, this is less efficient than standard solar panels, which generate about 200W per square meter. The technology is not intended to power entire vehicles but could offset the energy needs of car electronics, such as air conditioning and internet connectivity. Fuyao's product could be used in both electric and gas-powered vehicles, though its impact on vehicle range is limited. The company claims the glass could provide 720W at peak for BYD EVs, though this has not been confirmed. The article notes that solar-powered cars are unlikely to replace traditional vehicles due to physical limitations, suggesting that solar glass may offer more practical benefits for vehicle electronics rather than full propulsion.
source.title: Fuyao Glass Introduces Solar Roof Glass for Vehicles, Limited Power Output

source.summary: Lynk & Co, as official car partner in Sweden for the CEV Trendyol EuroVolley 2026 Women, provided mobility support during the tournament in Gothenburg. The company deployed a fleet of 08 vehicles with championship branding to transport teams and officials. At Scandinavium, Lynk & Co showcased its 08 plug-in hybrid and 02 all-electric models through on-site displays and activations. Patric Holm, VP Market Area Sweden, highlighted the partnership's role in enhancing the event experience and engaging fans. The 08 offers up to 200 km of electric range, while the 02 features updates like Onyx Black color and enhanced in-car technology for MY27.
source.title: Lynk & Co supports EuroVolley 2026 Women with mobility and brand activations in Gothenburg

source.summary: David Ball, a retired civil engineer, has owned his Genesis GV70 Electrified for four years and shares his experience with CleanTechnica readers. The car, built on a multi-fuel platform and a Hyundai sub-brand, appealed to him and his wife due to its conventional dashboard layout and long range. They opted for an electric vehicle over hybrids to avoid double maintenance costs. The Genesis offered sufficient range and space for their travel needs, though it cost AU$138,000, more than the Tesla Model Y and BMW i4. David appreciates the car's adaptive features, one-pedal driving, and safety innovations. He uses solar power to charge the vehicle and has spent around $1,500 on fast charging for trips to Melbourne. The Genesis also provides 5 years of free concierge service, which he finds exceptional. David, who is environmentally conscious, sees the car as a step toward reducing fossil fuel reliance.
source.title: Retired Engineer Shares Four-Year Experience with Genesis GV70 Electric Vehicle

source.summary: A new facility in Cumbria, UK, combines immersive technology and robotics to enhance nuclear decommissioning planning. Developed by AtkinsRéalis, Sellafield Ltd, and Igloo Vision Ltd, the RAICo1 facility allows engineers to visualize and test operational scenarios remotely, reducing time spent in hazardous environments by up to 40%. The 360-degree environment supports collaborative planning and decision-making, integrating digital twins, live data, and robotic systems. The project builds on previous immersive facilities and aims to improve safety and efficiency in decommissioning complex nuclear sites.
source.title: RAICo1 facility enables remote nuclear decommissioning planning through immersive tech and robotics

source.summary: A passive reactor cavity water injection tank, a key component of the reactor cavity cooling system, was installed at Zhangzhou 4. The tank, with a total height of 22 metres, was assembled from three modules weighing 132.8 tonnes each, lifted by a 2000-tonne crawler crane. Zhangzhou 4 is the fourth Hualong One unit at the site, following the commercial operation of units 1 and 2. The project, owned by CNNC-Guodian Zhangzhou Energy Company, plans to build two more Hualong One units, aiming for a six-unit plant that would generate over 60 billion kilowatt-hours of clean energy annually.
source.title: Zhangzhou 4 Reactor Gets Passive Safety Module

source.summary: Energy storage company EVO Power USA and Ranial Systems are forming a partnership to provide energy management services to commercial and industrial customers. The collaboration combines EVO’s battery systems with Ranial’s AI software to optimize energy use and reduce costs. A pilot project at Sunrise Toyota in New York, supported by Sprocket Power, demonstrated a 55% reduction in energy costs using the integrated system. EVO has completed over 125 global deployments, many operational for more than five years. EVO’s CEO emphasized the strategic value of Ranial’s technology in creating a smart energy platform.
source.title: EVO Power and Ranial partner to offer nationwide energy management services

source.summary: Inox Clean Energy, part of the INOXGFL Group, acquired Vena Energy India for $626.7m, expanding its renewable portfolio. The deal, finalized within two months, includes 1GW of operational assets and a 12GW development pipeline. Vena Energy India, owned by BlackRock’s GIP, manages 1.7GW of solar and wind capacity. Inox Clean Energy's combined operational portfolio is expected to reach 4GW, with BESS projects exceeding 2.5GWh. The acquisition also includes a 640MW wind-solar hybrid portfolio in Maharashtra.
source.title: Inox Clean Energy acquires Vena Energy India's renewable assets for $627m

source.summary: LG Energy Solution has begun operations at a new battery manufacturing plant in Lansing, Michigan, contributing to its goal of producing 80% of its energy storage systems (ESS) in North America by year-end. The facility will manufacture lithium-iron phosphate (LFP) cells for ESS and nickel-manganese-cobalt (NMC) cells for Toyota's electric vehicles. The Lansing plant, which received over $2 billion in investment since 2022, is expected to employ 1,700 workers at full capacity. LGES now operates two Michigan facilities and plans to achieve 50 GWh of LFP cell capacity in North America by 2026.
source.title: LGES opens second Michigan battery manufacturing plant, now makes 80% of ESS in North America

source.summary: China's National Development and Reform Commission and National Energy Administration released the 15th five-year plan for coal, covering 2026-2030, as the country approaches its carbon peak target by 2030. The plan emphasizes coal's role as a foundational energy source but also outlines a 'green and low-carbon transition' and aims to peak coal consumption during the period. It does not set a specific year for peaking, though state-affiliated organizations suggest 2027. Analysts note the plan reflects a broader trend of reinforcing coal's role due to Middle East conflicts, while also encouraging diversification into clean energy and chemicals. The plan includes targets for modernizing coal production, increasing the share of high-quality coal, and developing coalbed methane to reduce emissions. It also calls for centralized management of coal production and maintaining reserve capacity to ensure energy security.
source.title: China's 15th Five-Year Coal Plan Outlines Peaking Goals and Green Transition

source.summary: A study by Arnold, Richards, Singh, and Whaley explores how deregulation affects cardiac care markets. The research focuses on Medicare's expansion of non-hospital treatment options and its influence on market dynamics. It finds that market entry leads to business stealing among low-cost settings, increasing Medicare spending by about $2.5 million. The study highlights how federal policies interact with state regulations and market behaviors, creating externalities for other procedures and payers. Vertical integration by hospitals and physicians mitigates these effects.
source.title: Study examines deregulation's impact on cardiac care markets

source.summary: A study by Bordo and Bastidon uses a non-linear dynamic model to analyze currency dominance. The model incorporates regime switches based on five shock categories, including democracy and conflicts. Calibration shows democracy's role in regime changes. Stress tests suggest the US dollar's dominance remains largely unaffected, with no other currency emerging as a major force.
source.title: Study Shows US Dollar Dominance Resists Shocks in Non-Linear Model

source.summary: An article predicts Nintendo's stock could outperform the 'Magnificent Seven' in the second half of 2026. Despite concerns over memory chip shortages impacting its Switch 2 sales, Nintendo reported $900 million in operating income last quarter. The company raised Switch 2 prices by $50, and its current market cap of $64 billion suggests potential undervaluation if earnings growth continues. Analysts highlight Nintendo's conservative profit forecasts and its strong historical performance as factors supporting its stock's potential rebound.
source.title: Nintendo's Stock May Outperform AI Leaders as Switch 2 Sales Grow

source.summary: Microsoft's AI initiatives are driving significant growth in its cloud services, with Azure and Copilot contributing to a 40% year-over-year revenue increase. The company reported a $37 billion annual AI revenue run rate, up 123% from the previous year, fueled by AI integration into Microsoft 365 and enterprise software. Microsoft plans $175 billion in capital expenditure for 2026, focusing on data centers and infrastructure, supported by strong revenue and backlog growth.
source.title: Microsoft's AI Growth Drives Cloud Revenue Expansion

source.summary: The life insurance market, now a multibillion-dollar industry, originated during the AIDS crisis in the 1980s. Frank Sierawski, diagnosed with cancer, discovered life settlements—a practice where individuals sell their life insurance policies to investors for a fraction of their value. This concept, initially a desperate solution for AIDS patients like Scott Page and his partner Greg, allowed families to access funds for medical expenses and end-of-life care. The Supreme Court's 1911 ruling enabled the sale of life insurance policies, creating a legal foundation for the market. As the AIDS crisis eased, the industry expanded to include elderly, wealthy individuals, evolving into a financial asset. Investors now buy policies expecting payouts, with companies ensuring long-term returns by managing large portfolios of policies.
source.title: Life insurance market emerged from AIDS crisis and evolved into financial asset

source.summary: Ukrainian President Volodymyr Zelenskyy stated that the United States provided Kyiv with information regarding recent meetings in Moscow. Zelenskyy expressed appreciation for the alignment of steps and the realistic vision America is advancing. The Kremlin confirmed CIA Director John Ratcliffe visited Moscow for security service contacts. US President Donald Trump characterized the visit as semi-routine and stated Russia will not attack NATO territory.
source.title: Zelenskyy confirms US shared intelligence on Moscow meetings with Ukraine

source.summary: Serbia recently called on Russia for firefighting aid after wildfires burned over 3,500 hectares in the Deliblato Sands Special Nature Reserve. Interior Ministry official Luka Causic stated that no aircraft of that capacity was available within the European Union. President Aleksandar Vucic visited the site to emphasize that European equipment was less capable than Serbian resources. Political scientist Vuk Vuksanovic suggests Vucic is managing relations with both Moscow and Kyiv to avoid alienating either side before the October election. Vuksanovic noted that Vucic aims to present himself as a friend to Ukraine and Israel to prevent Western opposition. However, the EU expects Serbia to align its policies with the bloc, while Moscow does not fully trust Vucic. Vucic must now decide whether to maintain this delicate balance or face pressure to choose a side.
source.title: Serbia balances EU and Russia ties ahead of October election

source.summary: Rescuers in Nepal and China continue searching for thousands missing after deadly floods swept through the Himalayan region. Latest figures show the number of missing people has risen to nearly 3,000, with 633 bodies recovered so far. Nepal's disaster authority added 933 hydropower workers to the missing list, which already includes trekkers and pilgrims. Reports indicate some deceased individuals may have been swept downstream as far as India.
source.title: Missing persons in Nepal and China floods reach nearly 3,000

source.summary: The U.S. Department of Justice filed a federal civil forfeiture action against a ranch in Hemet, California, owned by Juan Carlos Valencia González, the newly appointed leader of the Jalisco New Generation Cartel. The property, purchased in 2011 for $250,000 under the name González, is now valued at approximately $695,000. A DEA source stated the land is currently managed by the capo's maternal uncle, José María González Valencia. Following sanctions imposed by the Office of Foreign Assets Control, the uncle reportedly ordered a tenant to vacate the premises. The tenant, who rents the property for $1,500 a month, fears the government will seize the land before he can remove his belongings. The DOJ alleges the property is connected to the cartel leader, whose rise followed the death of his stepfather, El Mencho.
source.title: US seeks to seize California ranch owned by new CJNG leader

source.summary: New York City Mayor Zohran Mamdani appointed Anthony Shorris and Lina Khan to lead the city's Economic Development Corporation to address the challenge of delivering both economic redistribution and growth. While Mamdani has made progress on redistribution promises like rent freezes and free bus use, he faces structural limits from state governments and skeptical bond markets. The article notes that progressive leaders across Europe have similarly struggled to convince voters they can deliver economic dynamism alongside social justice. Harvard economist Dani Rodrik suggests a 'productivism' framework focusing on service-sector job creation rather than manufacturing. Mamdani's team includes Shorris, a business community veteran, and Khan, who previously challenged corporate power at the FTC. However, the administration must also collaborate with large firms in finance and technology to generate jobs at scale. Without showing progress on this front, critics may use the upcoming midterm elections to attack the progressive agenda. The article concludes that Mamdani's appointments suggest an understanding of these complex economic-policy challenges.
source.title: NYC Mayor Mamdani Appoints Leaders to Balance Redistribution and Growth

source.summary: UN Secretary-General Antonio Guterres called on nuclear-armed nations to uphold testing moratoria and formalize global bans. He stated that nuclear tests shatter trust and fuel an arms race. The appeal followed Russia's announcement of a nuclear-capable ICBM training launch. Guterres urged bringing the Comprehensive Nuclear-Test-Ban Treaty into full effect. The treaty remains inactive because nine Annex 2 states, including the US and Russia, have not ratified it.
source.title: UN chief urges nuclear powers to maintain test bans after Russian missile launch

source.summary: Independent scientific studies conducted by Source International, RAID, AfreWatch, and University of Lubumbashi professors found widespread pollution in the Lualaba mining area of the Democratic Republic of the Congo. Researchers reported that nearly 98 percent of hourly fine-particle measurements at the Galaxy School exceeded World Health Organization safety thresholds. The studies detected high concentrations of heavy metals in water sources near major industrial sites operated by CMOC, Zijin Mining, and Glencore. Community leaders and environmental advocates argue that local populations are suffering severe health consequences while the country drives the global green energy transition. The Initiative for Good Governance and Human Rights criticized the Congolese state for failing to protect citizens from mining giants. Scientists emphasize that the next crucial step is an epidemiological investigation to establish direct causal links between pollution and reported health issues like miscarriages and respiratory problems.
source.title: The devastating impact of copper and cobalt mining pollution in Lualaba, DRC

source.summary: Haiti's Centre Department, historically peaceful, now faces severe gang violence forcing mass displacement. Armed groups led by Jeff Larose and Wilson Joseph attacked Mirebalais and Saut d'Eau in April 2025, destroying infrastructure and killing residents. Reports from the IOM, BINUH, and OCHA indicate approximately 147,000 people have fled their homes. Many displaced families previously lived in overcrowded school shelters with poor sanitation. On June 5, the IOM launched a relocation program moving over 350 families to a new transit center with improved facilities. Despite these efforts, gangs continue to operate in parts of the region, extorting civilians and committing atrocities. Local self-defense groups, the Haitian National Police, and the Armed Forces of Haiti currently hold key areas to prevent total gang takeover.
source.title: Haiti gang violence displaces thousands in Centre Department as relocation begins

source.summary: Yashoda Hospitals HITEC City branch reported performing over 400 kidney transplant surgeries since launching its program. The hospital highlighted this milestone at the Kidney Symposium 2026, which Union Minister G. Kishan Reddy inaugurated. Medical professionals discussed advances in transplantation and the need for increased organ donation awareness. Managing Director G. Surender Rao noted improved outcomes through advanced technology and experienced specialists.
source.title: Yashoda Hospitals Hyderabad completes 400 kidney transplants

source.summary: A postcard collection titled 'Madras: Arches, Alleys & Icons' featuring illustrations by the late Pavithra Srinivasan was launched at Higginbothams Book Store. The set highlights iconic Chennai landmarks like the Big Mosque and the Armenian Church. Organizers include the Postcrossing Welfare Society of India and the Madras Literary Society. Proceeds from sales support a foundation providing school fees for poor children. Srinivasan's father revealed plans for a future book on Royapuram and trams.
source.title: Postcard collection featuring late artist Pavithra Srinivasan's Madras illustrations launches

source.summary: The government notified the Legal Metrology (Indian Standard Time) Rules, 2026, making IST mandatory for all legal and commercial activities in India from March 2027. Violations will attract penalties under the Legal Metrology Act. The rules require entities to use only IST for official purposes, with limited exceptions for scientific research and navigation. CSIR-National Physical Laboratory will maintain India's primary time scale, while Regional Reference Standards Laboratories and ISRO's NavIC will disseminate official time. The notification aims to enhance cyber resilience and ensure accurate time synchronization for digital infrastructure.
source.title: India mandates Indian Standard Time for all entities from March 2027

source.summary: RSS chief Mohan Bhagwat addressed crowds at Madison Square Garden in New York, emphasizing inclusiveness and societal change. He stated that a Hindu who wants India without Muslims would not remain Hindu. Bhagwat argued that public opinion drives lasting change rather than political power. He added that Hindu thought requires accepting different paths to the same truth.
source.title: RSS chief Bhagwat rejects exclusion of Muslims in Hindu thought

source.summary: HDFC Bank announced that MD and CEO Sashidhar Jagdishan will not seek reappointment and will retire on October 26, 2026. The bank stated the Board appreciated his leadership during the 2023 merger with HDFC Ltd. Jagdishan faces recent criticism over stock underperformance and allegations of governance violations, which the bank denied. He previously faced fines for business overreach regarding deposit arrangements with MSRDC. The bank plans to fast-track the selection of his successor.
source.title: HDFC Bank CEO Jagdishan steps down after tenure ends in October 2026

source.summary: Amazon is requesting bids from selected third-party sellers to access its sub-Same Day delivery service. The company states that eligible orders can arrive in as little as two hours across 2,300 metropolitan areas. Amazon reports that products using this service see 12% higher sales on average compared to regular FBA. Sellers must weigh potential sales boosts against the costs of securing faster delivery. The company has not publicly detailed specific bid amounts for participation.
source.title: Amazon asks US sellers to bid for sub-Same Day delivery access

source.summary: Tamil Nadu Health Minister K.G. Arunraj announced the phased implementation of the NalamAI WhatsApp chatbot service across all state government hospitals. Speaking at a neurologists' conference, he detailed staffing increases at the Hosur district hospital and expanded insurance coverage under the Chief Minister's scheme. The minister also highlighted new dengue prevention measures and plans for a new ESI hospital in Hosur.
source.title: Tamil Nadu Health Minister announces NalamAI chatbot rollout in all government hospitals

source.summary: Google, Amazon, Microsoft, Meta, and OpenAI are developing custom AI chips to reduce reliance on Nvidia's GPUs. Despite these efforts, Nvidia's revenue more than doubled to $96.2 billion in the July quarter. The company targets a 70% revenue increase by 2028 as overall AI demand outpaces the shift to custom hardware. Nvidia CEO Jensen Huang noted a deepening partnership with Amazon Web Services, which plans to buy 2 million more Nvidia GPUs. While competitors innovate, Nvidia is expanding its ecosystem and pushing its standalone CPU business, which aims to generate $20 billion this year. However, rising memory chip costs may lower Nvidia's profit margin from 75% to 71–72% by January. Consequently, the company expects to raise prices next year, creating uncertainty about customer acceptance.
source.title: Google and Amazon build AI chips, yet Nvidia revenue surges

source.summary: Infosys stated its subsidiary CEO Lax Gopisetty was unreachable during Nepal floods on August 26. The company confirmed he was visiting personally and remains in contact with his family. India's Ministry of External Affairs reported 287 Indian nationals and 128 persons of Indian origin remain missing. Four individuals were rescued from a hydropower project in Rasuwa district.
source.title: Infosys CEO unreachable in Nepal floods as hundreds go missing

source.summary: Paul Black, a veteran portfolio manager, outlines three principles for identifying businesses capable of generating long-term wealth. He advises investors to prioritize companies where competitive advantages are strengthening rather than merely existing. Black emphasizes evaluating corporate culture by speaking with employees and suppliers to understand operational alignment. He also recommends focusing on the direction of Return on Invested Capital rather than its absolute level. The article notes that Black suggests avoiding short-term market noise and maintaining patience to allow compounding to occur over five to 15 years. His framework argues that owning structurally stronger businesses provides better downside protection during difficult economic periods.
source.title: Paul Black outlines three rules for identifying long-term wealth creators

source.summary: Infosys stated that its CEO Lax Gopisetty is unreachable following devastating floods in Nepal where he was visiting personally. The company confirmed it is working with agencies to locate him while remaining in contact with his family. Infosys expressed deep sadness over the disaster, which has killed 626 people and left thousands unaccounted for. The firm is providing support to the family during this difficult time.
source.title: Infosys says CEO Lax Gopisetty unreachable after Nepal floods

source.summary: Silver prices have recovered from a recent correction driven by renewed buying interest and optimism regarding demand from sectors like solar energy and electric vehicles. The author notes that a strong rally in gold has provided a significant tailwind, as investors seek relatively cheaper precious metal alternatives. Additionally, a weaker U.S. dollar has boosted affordability for global buyers, supported by expectations of accommodative Federal Reserve policy. Industrial demand remains structurally strong due to limited mine production growth and tight supply-demand balances. While short-term volatility persists due to economic uncertainty, the long-term outlook appears constructive as industrial applications drive sustained demand growth.
source.title: Silver rebounds as gold rallies and dollar weakens amid industrial demand

source.summary: STARFlow2 combines language models and normalizing flows to enable continuous, single-pass multimodal generation. The model uses a Pretzel architecture that interleaves a frozen vision-language model with a TARFlow stream, operating under the same causal mask. This design preserves pretrained understanding, allows high-fidelity image generation, and supports cache-friendly interleaved output. Experiments show strong performance in image generation and multimodal understanding. The work highlights autoregressive flows as a foundation for unified modeling.
source.title: STARFlow2 integrates language models and flows for unified multimodal generation

source.summary: Experts suggest Australian datacentres may rush for approvals before new federal regulations on power costs, water use, and location take effect. The rules, aimed at curbing power price increases and environmental impact, will not apply to projects approved before their implementation. Aemo reports 225 datacentres in development, with electricity demand expected to rise significantly by 2036. Developers, like Goodman Group on Project Mars, face community pushback and regulatory uncertainty. Advocates call for a moratorium on approvals until regulations are in place, citing environmental and amenity concerns.
source.title: Australian datacentres seek approval before new regulations on power and water use

source.summary: Gamma, a presentation startup, acquired Lica, an Accel-backed design firm, to enhance its design research lab. Lica, founded in 2023 and backed by Accel, focused on creating marketing videos for e-commerce sites. The founders, familiar with Gamma's CEO, saw alignment in their vision for visual communication. Gamma plans to explore new communication formats through the acquisition, aiming to create fluid, multimodal presentations. Lica's co-founders emphasized personalizing AI models for different audiences. The acquisition follows trends of consolidation in the AI presentation space.
source.title: Gamma acquires Lica to expand design research capabilities

source.summary: OpenAI's Jalapeño chip, unveiled at the Hot Chips conference, demonstrated superior performance in inference tasks, achieving higher tokens per user and throughput per kilowatt compared to current state-of-the-art processors. Richard Ho, OpenAI's head of hardware, noted the chip's efficiency in handling AI workloads with lower latency. Developed in collaboration with Broadcom, Jalapeño is designed to minimize data movement and communication delays during inference processing. The chip is expected to deploy in small volumes by late 2026, with broader rollout planned for 2027. OpenAI aims to make Jalapeño a multigenerational platform, integrating AI products, models, chips, and memory development.
source.title: OpenAI's Jalapeño chip outperforms state-of-the-art systems in inference benchmarks

source.summary: Apple has released updated versions of the Mac mini and Mac Studio, along with new M6 and M5 Ultra chips, emphasizing improvements for local AI inference and software development. The updates focus on enhancing performance for tasks like distributed AI inference using MLX, leveraging Thunderbolt 5 and unified memory architecture. The popularity of these devices for running large language models grew after macOS 26.2 introduced low-latency communication features. Developers and researchers now use these machines as an alternative to specialized hardware with Nvidia GPUs.
source.title: Apple updates Mac mini and Mac Studio for enhanced local AI development

source.summary: Perplexity has introduced Portable Computer, a new local AI agent that runs AI models directly on the user's device, offering faster performance, improved security, and lower costs compared to cloud-based solutions. The agent allows users to keep their data and work on their machine, with the option to connect to external services like Google Drive and Slack when needed. However, it requires high-end hardware, including Nvidia RTX GPUs with at least 24GB of VRAM, and is currently available only to paid subscribers on Linux systems, with a Windows version promised for September. The agent supports multiple models, including Qwen 3.8 27B and PPLX 27B, with plans to add Nvidia's Nemotron 3.5 Lightning. Perplexity emphasizes that local AI avoids data breaches and eliminates cloud-related costs, though the current hardware requirements may limit accessibility.
source.title: Perplexity Launches Local AI Agent for Enhanced Performance and Security

source.summary: Linus Torvalds, a Finnish graduate student, introduced Linux in 1991 as a hobby project, initially intending to name it 'Freax'—a blend of 'free,' 'freak,' and 'x.' However, his friend Ari Lemmke disliked the name, leading to the adoption of 'Linux.' The project started with a Usenet post on August 25, 1991, and quickly gained traction through collaborative development. Torvalds emphasized that Linux's growth was gradual and unexpected, with early contributors like Theodore Ts'o helping expand its reach. The shift to the GNU Public License version 2 in 1992 was pivotal, enabling Linux's widespread adoption. Torvalds remains actively involved, viewing Linux as a significant cultural and technical milestone in software development.
source.title: Linus Torvalds' Linux began as a hobby, nearly named Freax

source.summary: Mathematicians Bruce Schneier and Kasra Rafi argue that while AI has produced notable mathematical results, it currently lacks the ability to develop substantial new conceptual frameworks. They note AI models have disproven conjectures and found novel applications of existing techniques, but these achievements do not equate to true mathematical creativity. The authors emphasize that AI excels at recombining existing ideas but struggles with deep, sustained theory-building. They acknowledge AI's growing capabilities but caution that significant conceptual innovation remains beyond its current reach, though they remain optimistic about future developments.
source.title: Mathematicians Discuss AI's Role in Their Field

source.summary: In early 2026, a series of vulnerabilities and a landmark incident shifted AI security from theoretical concerns to real infrastructure compromises. A CyberArk survey revealed that 91% of organizations maintain always-on privileged access, creating an environment where AI agents operate with broad permissions and minimal oversight. Three separate disclosures showed that sanctioned agents inherit permissions from their host environments, leading to potential exploitation. Meanwhile, unsanctioned 'shadow AI' tools, used by 45% of employees, compounded the risk by accessing internal data and executing commands without oversight. The Sysdig Threat Research Team documented the first end-to-end AI-agent-driven ransomware attack, exploiting known vulnerabilities and persistent credentials. The incident highlighted the need for just-in-time access controls, better discovery of nonhuman identities, and stronger governance frameworks. The OWASP Top 10 for Agentic Applications now includes these risks, urging organizations to treat agent access as an identity lifecycle issue with the same rigor as human access management.
source.title: AI Agents Exploit Persistent Privileges in 2026 Cybersecurity Breach

source.summary: NVIDIA provides a framework for implementing full-stack observability in AI infrastructure to detect and resolve silent failures. The article explains how to map AI components to telemetry tools, select the right monitoring stack, and create a unified triage dashboard. It highlights the importance of focusing on key metrics and avoiding alert fatigue by prioritizing signals that directly inform remediation actions. The framework emphasizes a step-by-step approach, starting with essential tools like DCGM, NVSM, and UFM, and expanding coverage as needed. NVIDIA also recommends a two-layer monitoring system for efficient troubleshooting and root-cause analysis.
source.title: NVIDIA Outlines Observability Strategy for AI Infrastructure

source.summary: NVIDIA has introduced open world models, such as Cosmos 3, to advance physical AI by enabling developers to generate training data, simulate environments, and specialize models for robotics, autonomous vehicles, and vision AI. These models, available under the Linux Foundation’s OpenMDW 1.1 license, allow teams to post-train on their own data and hardware. Cosmos 3, built on a mixture-of-transformers architecture, combines vision reasoning, world generation, and action prediction, offering variants for different use cases. NVIDIA’s physical AI stack includes tools like Isaac GR00T, Alpamayo, and Metropolis, while the NVIDIA Cosmos Coalition fosters collaboration across industries to develop open world models for various applications.
source.title: NVIDIA Introduces Open World Models for Physical AI Applications

source.summary: MIT undergraduates participated in the JARVIS Challenge, a four-week competition to design and build a small gas turbine jet engine using AI as a primary engineering tool. The challenge aimed to explore whether AI could accelerate the design-build-test cycle for complex physical systems. Teams used AI for tasks like summarizing textbooks, creating designs, and sourcing vendors, but faced limitations in areas requiring physical understanding and vendor coordination. While AI aided in initial design phases, human expertise and hands-on experience proved critical for successful engine testing. The competition highlighted that AI can enhance engineering productivity, but human judgment and fundamental knowledge remain essential for safety-critical systems. The winning team, 811 Crew, relied more on traditional engineering principles and teamwork, demonstrating that a balance between AI use and human expertise is key to effective engineering outcomes.
source.title: MIT Students Test AI's Role in Jet Engine Design Through JARVIS Challenge

source.summary: MIT's Cybersecurity Clinic, launched in 2019, trains students to conduct free vulnerability assessments for municipalities and healthcare organizations. The program, led by Jungwoo Chun and Lawrence Susskind, combines technical training with social science insights, emphasizing 'defensive social engineering' to address human factors in cybersecurity. Students analyze clients' systems, recommend protective measures, and help build organizational capacity. The clinic has completed over 40 assessments, with recommendations including software patching, multi-factor authentication, and ransomware response plans. The course also offers open online modules, and has inspired similar programs at universities nationwide. Susskind notes that simple, low-cost measures can prevent most cyberattacks, and the clinic continues to follow up with clients for at least two years after each engagement.
source.title: MIT students provide free cybersecurity assessments to local governments

source.summary: Cleveland Clinic, RIKEN, and IBM conducted a 12,635-atom protein simulation, setting a new milestone in quantum chemistry. The simulation methods are now available open source via Qiskit Community.
source.title: Cleveland Clinic and IBM Advance Quantum Chemistry Simulations

source.summary: Researchers at the University of California San Diego, with Google's support, are developing a low-carbon computing platform using retired smartphones. The project involves extracting motherboards from discarded phones and redeploying them as a general-purpose computing platform. This initiative aims to reduce the environmental impact of computing by avoiding the need for new hardware. The team plans to build a datacenter using 2,000 Pixel smartphones, providing low-cost cloud computing for students and researchers. The project will test the reliability of consumer-grade hardware under sustained use and is expected to launch in Fall 2026. The researchers note that smartphones, despite their smaller size, can perform similarly to servers in single-threaded tasks, making them suitable for certain computing applications.
source.title: UC San Diego researchers deploy 2,000 retired phones as low-carbon computing cluster

source.summary: Google Research introduces a new framework for auditing machine unlearning, addressing challenges in verifying whether AI models have effectively 'forgotten' specific data. The method, called Regularized f-Divergence Kernel Tests, enhances sensitivity and accuracy in detecting distributional shifts between models. Traditional two-sample testing often produces false positives due to retraining variations or residual data footprints. The new approach uses f-divergences to measure distance between data distributions, allowing auditors to detect subtle, localized shifts that standard tests miss. It also reduces the need for manual tuning and large sample sizes. The framework was tested on synthetic data and high-energy physics datasets, outperforming existing methods in detecting privacy violations with fewer samples. The research highlights the limitations of current unlearning techniques and proposes a relative three-sample test to more accurately assess compliance with privacy standards.
source.title: New framework improves auditing of machine unlearning

source.summary: Google DeepMind, alongside Schmidt Sciences and other organizations, is launching a $10M research funding call to address safety risks in multi-agent AI systems. The initiative focuses on understanding and mitigating risks from large-scale interactions between AI agents. Key areas include developing testbeds, studying agent networks, strengthening infrastructure protocols, and creating oversight methods. The call invites global researchers to submit proposals by August 8, 2026, with results expected in Autumn 2026.
source.title: Google DeepMind Launches $10M Research Initiative for Multi-Agent AI Safety

source.summary: Google has released Gemini 3.5 Live Translate, an audio model that enables real-time speech-to-speech translation across 70+ languages. The model generates smooth, natural-sounding translations that preserve the speaker's intonation, pacing, and pitch, without requiring the speaker to finish before responding. It is rolling out via Google products, including Google Meet, Google Translate on Android and iOS, and the Gemini Live API for developers. The model supports multilingual inputs and handles noisy environments, with partners like Grab testing its capabilities for real-time communication. Google also introduced a 'listening mode' in the Translate app, allowing users to hear translations through their phone's earpiece. All audio output is watermarked with SynthID to help detect AI-generated content.
source.title: Google Launches Gemini 3.5 Live Translate for Real-Time Speech-to-Speech Translation

source.summary: Researchers propose a method to enhance large language models' reasoning capabilities by training them on diverse reasoning traces. The approach, presented at ICLR, introduces global forking tokens to prompt different reasoning modes during post-training. Set-supervised fine-tuning (SSFT) pairs each reasoning trace with a dedicated token, encouraging distinct behaviors and avoiding mode collapse. Reinforcement learning, specifically global forking policy optimization (GFPO), helps models select the most effective reasoning mode for each question. This combination improves single-shot accuracy and reasoning diversity, outperforming standard pipelines. The method maintains strong accuracy while increasing the likelihood of correct answers through diverse strategies.
source.title: New method trains LLMs to use diverse reasoning strategies for better decision-making

source.summary: Researchers present a framework at ICLR that connects architectural design choices to scaling laws, enabling efficient large language model (LLM) operation without compromising accuracy. The study builds on the Chinchilla scaling law, which relates model loss to parameters and training data. The new approach incorporates three architectural factors: hidden size, MLP-to-attention ratio, and grouped-query attention (GQA). Each factor influences inference throughput differently, with optimal points for accuracy. The researchers developed two model families, Panda (maximizing accuracy) and Surefire (optimizing accuracy-efficiency tradeoff), through extensive experimentation with over 200 models. Results show Surefire models achieve up to 47% higher throughput than LLaMA-3.2 on H200 GPUs, while maintaining similar accuracy. The framework is applicable across different hardware and serving systems, allowing cost-effective exploration of model architectures before full-scale training.
source.title: Researchers develop framework to optimize LLM efficiency without sacrificing accuracy

source.summary: Mumbai opposition parties warned against de-reserving the Alexandra Theatre for residential use, fearing it would set a dangerous precedent. Congress and Shiv Sena (UBT) members argued that cancelling the reservation for a closed cinema could open floodgates for similar claims regarding other theatres. They demanded public disclosure of all 119 cinema reservations under DP-2034 and a comprehensive White Paper on public reservation amendments. While a civic official noted the theatre has been unused since 2007, the proposal remains on hold pending further committee review.
source.title: Mumbai Opposition Warns Against De-Reserving Byculla's Alexandra Theatre

source.summary: Onion prices in Bhopal have surged from Rs 20 to Rs 50-60 per kg, with traders warning rates could hit Rs 80 per kg. Wholesale traders attribute the spike to low market arrivals and damaged stored stock. Farmers report a 40% to 50% production drop due to adverse weather and panic selling during the monsoon. New crop arrivals from Nashik are not expected until October.
source.title: Rising Onion Prices in Bhopal May Reach Rs 80 Per Kg

source.summary: Weeve provides free tools to help users avoid sharing private information with artificial intelligence assistants. The Dutch startup offers a service that removes identifying details from text before AI processing. Weeve also provides free transcription in 25 languages and a local-first AI note taker for Mac. These features allow users to analyze documents securely without leaking personal data to public databases.
source.title: Weeve offers free privacy tools for safe AI data use

source.summary: Tencent introduced Hy4 Preview, a new open-weight text-only large language model. The model features 770 billion total parameters and a 1 million token context window. It offers two reasoning effort levels: high and no_think. The release represents a significant increase in size compared to the previous Hy3 model.
source.title: Tencent launches Hy4 Preview, a massive 770B parameter open-weight LLM

source.summary: A journalist attending Gamescom for the sixth time reports on major game reveals at the Cologne event. CD Projekt Red announced a new expansion for The Witcher 3, Songs of the Past, which includes a free upgrade for the original game. Creative Assembly showcased Alien: Isolation 2, featuring a new protagonist and larger open spaces. Playground Games revealed a 2027 reboot of Fable with a cast of over 100 actors representing various UK accents. Additionally, the event highlighted a remaster of Tomb Raider: Legacy of Atlantis and the Scottish setting of Silent Hill Townfall. The Games Done Quick charity marathon also raised millions for various causes.
source.title: Gamescom 2024 Highlights Witcher 3 Expansion, Alien Sequel, and Fable Reboot

source.summary: Vijay Pande, formerly of a16z, co-founded VZVC with Zach Werner to pursue a concentrated investment strategy. The firm plans to make approximately five investments annually instead of the dozens typical of larger funds. Pande explained that biology differs from text because biological data cannot be scraped from the internet, creating unique challenges for AI models. He noted that while AI improves drug discovery, clinical trials remain expensive and animal models often fail to predict human responses. Pande emphasized the need for high-integrity founders who prioritize long-term collaboration over competition. The new firm relies on AI agents for operations rather than hiring associates.
source.title: Vijay Pande launches small firm VZVC to make five concentrated biotech bets

source.summary: AI-generated videos are increasingly replacing human performers in China's entertainment sector. The China Netcasting Services Association reports that 95% of short dramas published in Q1 2026 were AI-generated. Production costs have dropped significantly, with one minute of AI video costing between $90 and $120. Tsinghua University professor Shen Yang told the Financial Times that some performers are forced to provide their likeness before losing their jobs. Lawyers note a rise in AI-related labor disputes over the past few years.
source.title: AI Videos Displace Actors and Livestreamers in China's Entertainment Industry

source.summary: The Centre for Research on Energy and Clean Air reports that the conflict between the United States, Israel, and Iran increased global energy import costs by $330 billion between March and August. The European Union suffered the most financial pain, paying an extra $78 billion due to its reliance on foreign oil and gas. China and India followed as the next largest affected importers, paying additional $35 billion and $22 billion respectively. While crude oil accounted for the largest share of extra costs, liquefied natural gas prices in Asia remain 75% higher than pre-war expectations. The International Energy Agency estimates that hostilities have knocked out 9.6 million barrels of daily refining capacity in the Middle East. Low-carbon energy sources like wind and solar provided a partial offset by saving importers $36 billion during the period.
source.title: Iran War Adds $330 Billion to Global Energy Import Bill

source.summary: The US Justice Department and Pentagon are preparing to use dormant prize law to seize and sell Iranian oil captured during a blockade. Bloomberg reports that Houston is being considered a venue for these cases due to its petrochemical infrastructure. US Attorney Aaron Reitz stated the department is reviving this ancient maritime legal system. The move aims to generate revenue and tighten economic pressure on Iran while avoiding the delays of civil forfeiture. However, legal experts warn of uncertainties regarding modern international law and the lack of contemporary experience administering such cases.
source.title: US Justice Department revives 18th-century prize law to seize Iranian oil

source.summary: Robot.com has unveiled the R-dog, a delivery robot featuring a furry tail and red cap designed to navigate stairs and engage passersby. The company states the robot will run advertisements and use cameras for sentiment analysis while collecting engagement data. Robot.com claims the design aims to make automation more approachable, though it remains unclear how the device handles multiple deliveries. The article notes the robot's makers address privacy concerns through limited data retention and user opt-out options.
source.title: Robot.com unveils R-dog delivery robot with ads and facial recognition

source.summary: Illinois Governor JB Pritzker signed SB 3484 into law, creating a legal pathway for high-speed electric bikes on public roads starting January 1, 2027. The legislation treats electric motor-driven cycles with speeds up to 40 mph as motor vehicles, requiring registration, titling, insurance, and a valid driver's license. However, the law mandates that these vehicles must comply with federal motor vehicle safety standards and possess a legitimate vehicle identification number. Most current high-powered e-bikes lack the necessary manufacturer certifications and documentation to meet these requirements. Consequently, while the state offers a regulatory framework for these devices, the majority of existing models cannot be legally registered or operated on public roads under the new rules.
source.title: Illinois legalizes 40 mph e-bikes but requires motorcycle registration

source.summary: Poland's electricity transition is accelerating, with coal's share of generation dropping from 72.5% in 2021 to 52.7% in 2025. Renewables reached 31.4% of generation in 2025, surpassing coal for the first time in June. Gas generation also grew significantly, contributing 24.4 TWh in 2025 alongside wind and solar. Despite falling generation, Poland maintains high-emitting coal capacity through a special derogation in its capacity market auctions. The International Energy Agency expects renewables to overtake coal annually by 2028. Poland faces a dual challenge of reducing energy mix reliance while building the grid infrastructure needed to replace coal's reliability functions.
source.title: Poland rapidly reduces coal use while retaining high-emitting capacity for reliability

source.summary: A dairy farm in Kerman, California, is operating a new biogas project that converts methane waste into hydrogen fuel. The California Air Resources Board assigned the project the lowest carbon-intensity rating in the state's history, sparking debate among environmental groups. Critics argue the project prioritizes climate metrics over local water and air pollution caused by dairy waste lagoons. While regulators highlight the project's potential to displace fossil fuels, environmental advocates contend that carbon credits incentivize herd expansion and mask ongoing contamination issues. The facility, Bar 20, has faced previous citations for runoff and groundwater monitoring failures. CARB officials maintain the low rating reflects the capture of methane that would otherwise enter the atmosphere, though they note the approval is provisional. The project supplies hydrogen to refueling stations via truck, despite broader market challenges for hydrogen fuel. Experts warn that energy losses during conversion reduce the total fuel yield compared to direct biogas use. This case illustrates the tension between state climate goals and local environmental justice concerns surrounding industrial agriculture.
source.title: California Dairy Farm Gets Record-Low Carbon Rating for Biogas-to-Hydrogen Project

source.summary: Pennsylvania continues to spend millions subsidizing waste coal burning despite the state's renewable energy generation ranking 42nd nationally. The Alternative Energy Portfolio Standards (AEPS) regulation mandates utilities purchase specific fuel sources, with waste coal currently providing about 3 percent of the state's energy compared to 4 percent from renewables. Critics argue these subsidies hinder climate progress, noting that burning waste coal produces significantly more greenhouse gas emissions than traditional coal plants. Although House Bill 501 aims to reduce waste coal's role and increase renewable requirements, the proposal has stalled in the Democrat-controlled State House. Political opposition comes from both Republicans and a faction of Democrats representing coal regions who fear plant closures. Industry representatives warn that altering subsidies could force specialized plants into precarious 'peaking' modes, potentially ending cleanup operations. Meanwhile, costs for the program have risen sharply since 2020 border restrictions required in-state waste coal. Environmental advocates suggest creating a separate state program to manage waste coal, but lawmakers remain divided on the best path forward.
source.title: Pennsylvania Subsidizes Coal Waste While Renewables Lag Behind

source.summary: CleanTechnica reports that global pure electric vehicle registrations reached 1.8 million units in July, representing a 16% year-over-year increase. While battery electric vehicles (BEVs) grew significantly, plugin hybrid sales declined by 11%, causing the overall plugin market to rise only 7%. BEVs accounted for 71% of all plugin sales in July, marking the highest share since 2022. The Tesla Model 3 saw deliveries crash 44% year-over-year to 19,000 units, falling to 11th place globally, whereas the Tesla Model Y remained the top-selling model despite a 9% drop. BYD's Song secured second place, aided by exports and a new generation, while a group of small EVs from Geely and BYD filled the third through seventh spots. Leapmotor achieved record sales, doubling its output year-over-year to reach six-digit levels and surpassing Hyundai-Kia to take sixth place among manufacturers. Toyota also set a new record with 50,415 registrations, edging closer to Volkswagen in the legacy OEM rankings. The article notes that excluding China and the USA, EV sales jumped 50% year-over-year in July.
source.title: Global EV sales surge in July as Tesla Model 3 drops and Leapmotor rises

source.summary: Reports indicate Apple might delay the regular iPhone 18 until March 2027, focusing the September event on Pro models. Consequently, buyers in India are considering whether to purchase the current iPhone 17 now or wait for potential price drops after the upcoming launch event.
source.title: Reports suggest regular iPhone 18 may launch in March 2027

source.summary: Apple CEO Tim Cook ends his 15-year tenure on August 31, succeeded by John Ternus. During his leadership, Apple introduced the Apple Watch, AirPods, Apple Silicon, and Vision Pro to diversify its business beyond traditional hardware.
source.title: Tim Cook leaves Apple CEO role after 15 years of expanding product lines

source.summary: Nvidia has reportedly agreed to acquire Hugging Face for US$13 billion, a deal that would significantly expand the chipmaker's influence over open-source AI development. The article notes that Hugging Face previously rejected a US$500 million investment from Nvidia in 2024 to avoid concentration of power. This transaction occurs as OpenAI develops custom chips that could compete with Nvidia's hardware. By owning Hugging Face, Nvidia aims to steer developers toward its processors rather than those from competitors like Google. The startup generates approximately US$150 million in annual revenue, making the purchase price roughly 86 times its annualised revenue. Critics argue this move creates a paradox where a company promoting open models may instead strengthen its own market dominance.
source.title: Nvidia reportedly agrees to buy Hugging Face for US$13 billion

source.summary: Prime Minister Anwar Ibrahim announced the reinstatement of a 300-litre monthly quota for subsidised RON95 transport fuel. This measure is part of broader steps to address rising living costs in Malaysia.
source.title: Malaysian PM reinstates 300-litre monthly RON95 transport fuel limit per citizen

source.summary: The Competition and Markets Authority (CMA) removed requirements for multinational companies to disclose which veterinary practices they own, raising concerns that pet owners could be misled. The CMA found that pet owners pay 16.6% more on average at large vet groups than at independent practices within the £6.3bn market. While new rules propose capping prescriptions at £21, the Progressive Veterinary Association (PVA) has threatened a judicial review after the CMA softened wording to allow corporations to obscure ultimate ownership. The PVA argues this allows large groups to hide behind misleading brand names, whereas the CMA believes recognisable high street names are more useful to consumers. More than 60% of practices are currently owned by six major groups, including private equity investors and Mars Petcare.
source.title: CMA vet ownership rules change risks pet owners being misled by private equity firms
