source.summary: Amrita Tripathi, founder of Say Again Press, introduces a new book series targeting modern leaders with short, accessible leadership guides. The books are designed for quick reading, featuring notes pages and QR codes linking to video content. The initiative aims to promote deep thinking and original thought in an age dominated by AI and short attention spans. The series is available through indie bookstores and online platforms, with a launch event planned in Mumbai.
source.title: Say Again Press Launches Short Leadership Books to Counter AI's Impact

source.summary: India's Directorate General of Civil Aviation (DGCA) is considering expanding drug testing for commercial pilots from 10% to 100% annual random testing, potentially making it the first country with such a policy. Civil aviation minister Ram Mohan Naidu stated that the proposal aims to enhance safety but acknowledges the operational challenges for airlines. The move follows an incident where an Air India pilot tested positive for narcotics, prompting one-time testing of all pilots. Airlines would need to manage increased testing volumes, infrastructure, and crew downtime. While some airlines already conduct higher testing rates, the DGCA is assessing the balance between safety improvements and operational feasibility. The Federation of Indian Pilots supports expanded testing but advocates for a gradual increase and the use of oral-fluid testing alongside urine-based methods.
source.title: India Considers Annual Random Drug Tests for All Airline Pilots

source.summary: The Sensex and Nifty 50 rose on 25 August, driven by a 3% drop in Brent crude prices and eased U.S. sanctions on Iran. The 30-share index gained 0.37% to 77,656, while the Nifty 50 climbed 0.48% to 24,335. Analysts noted the relief in energy costs contributed to the positive close. Midcaps performed well, but smallcaps fell slightly. Key stocks like ICICI Bank and Infosys led the gains, while HDFC Bank and Eternal shares dragged down the benchmark. Analysts highlighted the importance of upcoming U.S. inflation data and Fed Chair Warsh's speech, with mixed views on potential market movements.
source.title: Stock Market Rises on Oil Price Drop and Geopolitical Factors

source.summary: A social media image claiming to show a 1947 letter from Lenin to Mountbatten requesting India's division was debunked. The fact-checker found the image AI-generated through reverse image search and AI detection tools. Analysis showed Lenin died in 1924, making the letter impossible. The text also used modern slang, inconsistent with 1947 language. The image originated from a meme page, further indicating its falsity.
source.title: Fact-check reveals Lenin's letter on India division is AI-generated

source.summary: The ex-mill price of sugar dropped 18% to ₹55 per kg following government measures to allow imports and curb speculation and hoarding, according to Food Secretary Sanjeev Chopra. Prices had previously surged to ₹67/kg due to mills increasing rates, which Chopra attributed to non-fundamental factors. The government's actions, including importing 1 million tonnes of raw sugar and imposing stock limits, have helped stabilize prices. While ex-mill prices are expected to fall further, wholesale and retail prices remain higher at ₹58.29/kg and ₹63.05/kg respectively. The National Federation of Cooperative Sugar Factories noted a ₹2-3/kg gap between ex-mill and wholesale prices, and a ₹7-8/kg gap between ex-mill and retail prices.
source.title: Government intervention lowers sugar ex-mill prices to ₹55/kg, curbing speculation and hoarding

source.summary: Four app-based cab drivers in Mumbai have filed a petition with the Bombay High Court challenging Maharashtra's new rule requiring Marathi language proficiency for auto-rickshaw, taxi, and app-based drivers. The petition argues the regulation exceeds the state's authority under the Motor Vehicles Act and violates constitutional rights. Petitioners claim nearly 9.65 lakh permits and badges have been issued, with many drivers unable to speak Marathi. They seek an immediate stay on the August 12 notification, warning of economic hardship for thousands of drivers. The case is scheduled for urgent consideration on August 26.
source.title: Mumbai drivers challenge Marathi language rule in court, citing livelihood risks

source.summary: Karnataka MP Captain Brijesh Chowta has urged Chief Minister D.K. Shivakumar to support the Railway Ministry's decision to integrate Mangaluru Railway Region under South Western Railway (SWR). Chowta emphasized that the move aligns with Karnataka's developmental needs and allows for more integrated planning of rail networks. He highlighted the importance of the Mangaluru-Hassan-Mysuru axis as a key corridor for both passenger and freight movement. While Kerala's government opposes the decision, Chowta called on Karnataka to publicly endorse the August 21 notification, which he said reflects long-standing regional aspirations.
source.title: Karnataka MP urges CM to support Railway Ministry's decision to integrate Mangaluru under SWR

source.summary: The government initiated an Offer-for-Sale (OFS) for up to 6% in Hindustan Copper, selling 5.80 crore shares at a floor price of ₹514/share. The two-day auction, open to institutional bidders, aims to raise ₹3,000 crore. Retail investors can bid starting Wednesday. Hindustan Copper shares fell 6.37% to ₹537 on BSE on the first day of the sale.
source.title: Government launches OFS for 6% stake in Hindustan Copper at ₹514/share

source.summary: The article explores the public persona of Narendra Modi through the lens of dramaturgical theory, comparing it to the more personal and introspective poetry of V.P. Singh. It argues that Modi's public image, or 'front stage' self, is carefully constructed and lacks the authenticity seen in Singh's work. The piece highlights how Modi's poetry, such as 'A Journey,' reflects a detached, idealized self, in contrast to Singh's candid and emotionally revealing verses. The author suggests that Modi's poetic expression, like his political persona, is more about projecting a polished image than revealing genuine emotion. The article concludes that Modi is not a 'dimagi poet'—a term implying a deep, introspective poet—because his work lacks the vulnerability and self-awareness found in Singh's poetry.
source.title: Modi's Public Persona and Poetic Expression Compared to V.P. Singh

source.summary: The Cockroach Janta Party in India has announced it will resume protests on Teachers' Day after the government failed to fulfill commitments made during a sit-in at Jantar Mantar. The party claims no delegation has been contacted about compensation, police cases have not been withdrawn, and formal talks on examination reform have not occurred. The group, which gained significant online support, warns against diluting or dishonoring the agreement. A 2015 Serbian activist's manual, which outlines a method for achieving political change, highlights the need for enforceable commitments, which the party has not received.
source.title: Cockroach Janta Party Reinstates Protest After Government Fails to Deliver Promises

source.summary: Netweb Technologies raised Rs 1,200 crore through a Qualified Institutional Placement (QIP), leading to a 4% drop in its shares. The company's Board of Directors approved the equity share allotment on August 20, 2026, marking its first capital raise since listing on NSE and BSE in July 2023. The QIP attracted participation from major investors like Goldman Sachs, Nomura, and Edelweiss Mutual Fund. The issue price was Rs 4,790 per share, with proceeds intended for working capital and growth initiatives. The company's chairman, Sanjay Lodha, expressed gratitude for investor confidence in its AI and high-performance computing business. Shares had previously hit a 52-week high of Rs 5,813 per share.
source.title: Netweb Technologies raises Rs 1,200 crore through QIP, shares fall 4%

source.summary: 3P Investment's funds purchased 2.5% of Entero Healthcare through a block deal, valued at Rs 104.99 crore. The acquisition was made from Prasid Uno Family Trust at Rs 1,377.8 per share. Entero Healthcare reported a 38% year-on-year revenue increase to Rs 1,940.5 crore in Q1 2026. The company focuses on MedTech, IVD, and Cardiology/Orthopaedic devices, which it considers high-growth sectors.
source.title: 3P Investment acquires 2.5% stake in Entero Healthcare

source.summary: Godrej Industries Group plans to invest ₹20,000 crore in Haryana, creating nearly 40,000 jobs. The investment, formalized through a Memorandum of Understanding with the state government, builds on existing ₹12,000 crore investments. Godrej Properties Ltd is expected to drive much of the expansion, with plans to invest ₹16,000 crore by FY28. The company also aims to deploy ₹3,500 crore for Grade A+ office infrastructure in Gurugram, generating over 30,000 jobs. Pirojsha Godrej, Chairperson of the group, stated the MoU reflects confidence in Haryana's market and long-term commitment to its development.
source.title: Godrej Industries to invest ₹20,000 crore in Haryana, aiming for 40,000 jobs

source.summary: An exhibition titled 'What Women Carry' explores the personal items women take when leaving home, highlighting their significance in migration and memory. The display includes photographs and handwritten accounts of objects like jewelry, clothing, and heirlooms, connected by red threads to form a narrative of loss and continuity. Organized by the Margins to Access Project, the exhibition features stories of women who fled conflict, violence, or economic hardship, carrying fragments of their past with them. One woman described wearing a necklace as a connection to her homeland, while others carried items with emotional weight, such as a dress from Myanmar or shirts belonging to a deceased husband. The exhibition emphasizes the often-overlooked labor of women in migration, who rebuild domestic life and preserve cultural practices. The organizers argue that displacement is not just about movement but also about carrying memory and maintaining connections to the past.
source.title: Exhibition captures women's personal belongings as symbols of displacement and memory

source.summary: A study published in Environmental Conservation reveals that a majority of ornamental plants sold online in India are alien species, many of which are invasive or naturalised in other countries. Researchers analyzed data from three major online retailers and found 1,371 out of 1,856 species were alien, with 327 classified as invasive elsewhere. The study highlights biosecurity gaps, noting that 57 invasive species already declared harmful in India are still available for purchase. Lead author Kesang Bhutia explains that ornamental plants often escape cultivation and naturalise, posing ecological risks. The online trade, facilitated by e-commerce platforms, increases propagule pressure and geographic spread, bypassing biosecurity checkpoints. The authors suggest implementing risk-assessment protocols, public awareness campaigns, and regulatory measures to mitigate invasion risks. They also propose a screening tool based on 'invasive elsewhere' metrics to prioritise species for further evaluation.
source.title: Online ornamental plant trade in India includes many invasive species

source.summary: IBM has released two new speech recognition models, Granite Speech 5.0 Turbo CTC, which offer high accuracy and unprecedented speed. The models, with 470M parameters, achieve over 12,600 RTFx on an NVIDIA H200 GPU, enabling transcription of more than 3.5 hours of speech in one second. They differ in training data and licensing: one uses a CC-BY-NC-SA-4.0 license with additional data, while the other is Apache 2.0 licensed. Both models perform well on public and far-field speech recognition benchmarks, with the noncommercial model scoring 4.85% WER and the Apache 2.0 model 5.00% WER. The encoder-only design provides faster throughput and a smaller memory footprint compared to previous models, though it sacrifices some capabilities like speech translation. The models use a lower token rate and different tokenizations, with training data including natural and synthetic datasets.
source.title: IBM Releases Fast and Accurate Granite Speech 5.0 Turbo CTC Models

source.summary: NVIDIA introduces CUDA Python 1.0, a unified framework enabling direct access to the full CUDA platform from Python. This release includes libraries like cuda.core, which provides Pythonic interfaces to CUDA runtime, and cuda.bindings, offering low-level C API access. The new system replaces fragmented approaches where developers had to choose between low-level CUDA C++ or higher-level libraries like PyTorch. CUDA Python 1.0 introduces semantic versioning, ensuring API stability and reducing version conflicts. It enables libraries to share resources across the ecosystem, allowing features like green contexts and inter-process memory sharing. The release aims to simplify GPU development by providing a common foundation for all Python-based CUDA applications, reducing the need for custom bindings and improving interoperability between libraries such as CuPy and PyTorch.
source.title: CUDA Python 1.0 Unifies GPU Access for Python Developers

source.summary: NVIDIA has introduced the Jetson Orin Nano 2, a new robotics computer designed to enhance entry-level edge AI capabilities. The device offers twice the inference performance of its predecessor in the same form factor while consuming 40% less power. Over 3 million developers have utilized NVIDIA's robotics stack, with companies like Cognex, Doosan Bobcat, and Matic among the early adopters. The Jetson Orin Nano 2 features 78 trillion operations per second of AI compute, 8GB of memory, and an 8-core Arm CPU, enabling developers to run advanced AI models for real-time applications. Partners are creating carrier boards and reference solutions to support the development of edge AI systems. The module and developer kit are expected to be available in the first half of 2027.
source.title: NVIDIA Launches Jetson Orin Nano 2 for Enhanced Edge AI Performance

source.summary: IBM has released Granite 4.2, a new series of large language models designed for enterprise agentic workflows. The models include native reasoning capabilities, allowing them to plan, evaluate trade-offs, and catch mistakes before execution. Available in 3B, 8B, and 30B parameter sizes, Granite 4.2 supports complex tasks like software engineering and multi-step development. IBM also introduced two new speech models, Granite Speech 5.0 Turbo CTC and 5.0 Turbo CTC NC, optimized for edge devices and high-throughput transcription. These models are smaller and more efficient, with the NC version trained on restricted data. The release includes a new training structure with reinforcement learning and synthetic code training to improve reasoning and coding capabilities.
source.title: IBM Releases Granite 4.2 with Enhanced Reasoning and Speech Models

source.summary: A new method called Quantization-Aware Healing (QAH) allows a 4-bit compressed model to outperform its full-precision bfloat16 version on 7 of 9 benchmarks, according to a paper by Multiverse Computing. The approach distills knowledge directly from the original, pre-compression model rather than from a recovered checkpoint, enabling the 4-bit model to surpass its 16-bit counterpart in accuracy and efficiency. QAH achieves this by using KL divergence on output logits, avoiding the instability of cross-entropy loss. The 4-bit model also uses less memory and compute, making it cheaper to run. The method was tested on a GPT-OSS 120B model compressed to 60B parameters, showing significant gains in long-context reasoning and math tasks. Compared to quantization-aware training (QAT), QAH reaches peak performance faster and maintains stability, reducing deployment risks. The research highlights how compression and quantization can be combined to create more efficient models without sacrificing capabilities.
source.title: Quantization-Aware Healing Enables 4-Bit Model to Outperform Full-Precision Original

source.summary: Ukraine is hosting a meeting with key European backers to demand more air defense systems and pressure on Russia, as attacks have killed more civilians than at any time since the war began. The Coalition of the Willing, led by Britain, France, and Germany, will discuss critical support. Germany's Foreign Minister Johann Wadephul urged the U.S. to involve its lawmakers more in diplomatic efforts. The EU approved an additional €6.1 billion in aid for Ukraine's defense, bringing total support to €24.35 billion. Meanwhile, Russia reported destroying 351 Ukrainian drones overnight and hitting a fuel tanker near Odesa. Zelensky rejected wartime elections, calling them dangerous. Ukraine also targeted Russian logistics sites, including Ozon's warehouses, as part of its ongoing campaign.
source.title: Ukraine seeks air defense as attacks rise, EU approves new aid

source.summary: South Korean President Lee Jae Myung's approval rating hit a record low of 40.2%, according to a Realmeter poll, marking the sixth consecutive week of decline. The drop was attributed to public dissatisfaction with housing policies, political disputes, and security concerns following reduced South Korea-US military exercises. Realmeter also noted declining support among conservative voters and those aged 70 and above. Meanwhile, the ruling Democratic Party of Korea saw its support fall to 41.9%, while the opposition People Power Party gained 37.6%.
source.title: South Korean President's Approval Rating Drops to Record Low Amid Housing and Security Concerns

source.summary: AfD co-leader Alice Weidel proposed that Germany should leave the euro and Schengen Area, close its borders, and implement stricter migration policies if her party enters government. She argued the euro weakened Germany's economy and reduced household wealth. Weidel also called for increased deportations, fewer naturalizations, and the return of Syrians with expired protection status. The AfD is polling at 27% nationally, ahead of the CDU, and is leading in Saxony-Anhalt. Weidel criticized the CDU and SPD for their stance on cooperation and policies, and reaffirmed the party's opposition to a combustion-engine ban and climate change measures.
source.title: AfD Leader Proposes Germany's Exit from Euro and Schengen

source.summary: French presidential candidates frequently emphasize referendums as a key policy tool. The article highlights referendums as a common campaign promise. Candidates use referendums to engage citizens directly. This strategy reflects a broader political trend in France. The focus on referendums underscores their perceived importance in governance.
source.title: French presidential candidates' reliance on referendums

source.summary: Raphaël Glucksmann, a center-left figure, has announced his candidacy for the French presidency. The announcement marks a significant move in French politics, positioning him as a potential contender in the upcoming election. Glucksmann, known for his political activism, aims to leverage his influence to shape the nation's future. His campaign highlights key issues such as economic reform and social justice. The move has drawn attention from political analysts and party leaders, signaling a shift in the electoral landscape.
source.title: Raphaël Glucksmann announces French presidential bid

source.summary: The article explores why people continue harmful behaviors despite knowing they are detrimental. Clinical and forensic psychologist Aleix Hildebrandt argues that these actions are not merely automatic but often result from conscious choices prioritizing immediate relief over long-term well-being. He distinguishes between habits, which are automatic responses, and broader behavioral patterns influenced by emotions, fears, and past experiences. A recent study highlights the limitations in understanding habit formation, noting that habits often emerge from conscious decisions that become automated through repetition. Researchers emphasize that the brain's reward and emotional systems play a significant role, often overriding rational knowledge. Psychiatrist Rosa Molina adds that many so-called 'bad habits' are attempts at emotional regulation, driven by the need for immediate relief from stress or loneliness. The article concludes that understanding the complex interplay between knowledge and behavior is crucial for addressing these recurring patterns.
source.title: Why we repeat harmful behaviors despite knowing they are bad

source.summary: Mexican Governor Ruben Rocha Moya, accused by US prosecutors of conspiring to smuggle drugs, requested a temporary leave of absence from his post. The 77-year-old politician, who returned to office after stepping down in May for an investigation, faces charges of trafficking drugs into the US in exchange for bribes and political support. Rocha denied the allegations, claiming they aim to harm the left-leaning Morena Party. His return to leadership sparked criticism from Mexican President Claudia Sheinbaum, who emphasized the importance of public service over personal ambition.
source.title: Mexican Governor Faces US Drug Charges, Requests Leave of Absence

source.summary: Kazakhstan will hold parliamentary elections on August 23, transforming its legislative body from a two-chamber to a single-chamber system. Experts suggest the ruling party, Adilet, will likely win, consolidating President Tokayev's power and weakening the legacy of former president Nursultan Nazarbayev. The new constitution allows Tokayev to seek another term in 2029 and replaces the two-chamber parliament with a single-chamber assembly. Independent candidates are barred, limiting political choice. European Union officials and experts note a lack of reaction to the political changes, citing pragmatic economic interests. Kazakhstan remains neutral in the Russia-Europe conflict, balancing relations with multiple powers while seeking to avoid over-dependence on any single nation.
source.title: Kazakhstan's parliamentary elections and political consolidation under Tokayev

source.summary: The Trump administration is intensifying economic pressure on Iran to push for negotiations over the Strait of Hormuz, with Treasury Secretary Scott Bessent set to outline new measures. The U.S. has already imposed extensive sanctions, which are expected to deepen Iran's distrust of the U.S. Meanwhile, the Supreme Court will decide whether Trump can continue construction on his ballroom, with the National Trust for Historic Preservation arguing that congressional approval is required. The Trump administration claims the ballroom is essential to an integrated military complex. Investors dumped stocks and bonds after government debt yields reached their highest level in nearly two decades, with the Treasury Department buying back bonds to reassure investors. The U.S. also manages wild horse populations through helicopter captures in Colorado, and new research shows positive experiences from Oregon's psychedelic industry.
source.title: Trump escalates economic pressure on Iran as SCOTUS rules on White House ballroom

source.summary: North Korea rebuffed President Trump's diplomatic outreach, launching short-range ballistic missiles and dismissing the U.S.-South Korea military drills reduction as insufficient. Seoul fears being sidelined in U.S.-North Korea negotiations, worried Trump may prioritize diplomacy over security commitments. Kim Yo Jong, North Korea's leader's sister, criticized the drills as provocative and rejected Trump's claims of communication with Kim Jong Un. Analysts suggest a potential pro forma summit between Trump and Kim, while South Korea seeks China's mediation. The U.S. and South Korea face growing mistrust as Trump's transactional approach risks eroding political trust in the alliance.
source.title: North Korea rejects Trump's diplomatic overture, escalates tensions with South Korea

source.summary: Commerce and Industry Minister Piyush Goyal stated India is negotiating free trade agreements with 8 to 9 more blocs, covering an additional $15 trillion in GDP. These agreements, along with existing ones, would total $70 trillion in market access, aiming to cover 75% of global trade. Goyal emphasized India's role in global value chains and highlighted opportunities in data centres, manufacturing, and AI. The minister is leading a delegation to strengthen India-Japan economic ties.
source.title: India seeks to expand FTAs to cover 75% of global trade

source.summary: Oriental Hotels Limited (OHL) will merge with Indian Hotels Company Limited (IHCL), a Tata Group subsidiary, through a share exchange ratio of 25 IHCL shares for every 117 OHL shares. The merger, expected to complete in the second half of FY28, aims to simplify IHCL's holding structure and unlock OHL's portfolio, including iconic assets like Taj Coromandel and Taj Fisherman’s Cove Resort & Spa. IHCL's CEO highlighted the merger's role in driving long-term value creation and supporting the Accelerate 2030 strategy. The transaction is set to create two new operating subsidiaries and streamline governance.
source.title: Oriental Hotels to merge with Tata Group’s IHCL through share exchange

source.summary: Trinamool Congress MP Mahua Moitra has approached the Supreme Court, alleging that West Bengal's Nadia district administration evicted her from her official constituency accommodation at the Circuit House in violation of a High Court order. Moitra claims local officials, including the Additional District Magistrate and District Magistrate, evicted her at 11 pm despite a protective order. Her counsel emphasized the constitutional implications and called for an independent investigation. The case was mentioned before the Supreme Court's Chief Justice Surya Kant and Justice Joymalya Bagchi. Moitra described the incident, stating she was served dinner in her room at 9:20 pm before being ordered to vacate at 9:47 pm, with a crowd outside chanting 'Jai Shree Ram'.
source.title: MP seeks Supreme Court intervention over midnight eviction from constituency home

source.summary: Indian stock markets opened higher on Monday, August 24, 2026, with the BSE Sensex and NSE Nifty rising due to buying in blue-chip stocks like HDFC Bank and Infosys. The Sensex gained 202.42 points to 77,744.15, while the Nifty rose 55.35 points to 24,309. Analysts noted ongoing geopolitical tensions and rising oil prices as factors limiting risk appetite. Asian markets like South Korea's Kospi and Japan's Nikkei 225 were lower, while U.S. markets closed higher. FIIs sold equities worth ₹542.71 crore on Friday.
source.title: Indian stock markets open higher on blue-chip buying amid global cues

source.summary: Sugar stocks such as Balrampur Chini Mills, Dhampur Sugar Mills, and Uttam Sugar Mills saw significant gains, with Uttam Sugar rising 11% to Rs 359 per share. The surge is attributed to two main factors: increased festive demand from August to November, which boosts confectionery consumption, and global supply concerns. Brazil, the world's largest sugar producer, faces delayed harvests and suspended reporting, while the EU, UK, Thailand, and India also report reduced output. Global deficit estimates range from 1.7 million to 3.3 million tonnes. The Indian government has tightened sugar stockholding limits to 15 days and mandated sales reporting to curb prices ahead of the festive season.
source.title: Sugar stocks rise on festive demand and global supply concerns

source.summary: Motilal Oswal reiterates a buy recommendation for Hexaware Technologies, citing its AI-driven initiatives and growth prospects. The brokerage notes that over 50% of Hexaware's revenue is now AI-infused, with a focus on 'Zero License' and tokenomics as key differentiators. Despite lowering CY26 revenue growth guidance, Motilal Oswal believes the slowdown is due to timing, forecasting 6.4% constant-currency growth in CY26 and 9.7% in CY27. The firm maintains its Rs 720 target price, emphasizing the company's AI strategy and execution momentum.
source.title: Motilal Oswal highlights Hexaware's AI strategy and growth potential

source.summary: Congress MP Karti Chidambaram dismissed claims by TVK supporters that Tamil Nadu Chief Minister Vijay could become Prime Minister, stating that 272 parliamentary seats are needed. He noted Vijay's party, centered around a movie star, could have national ambitions but would need parliamentary support. Tamil Nadu Congress leader Manickam Tagore criticized the ruling party for ministers operating in a 'fan club mode', suggesting they cannot change their mindset. Vijay recently met Union Home Minister Amit Shah at a zonal council meeting, where Shah chaired and Vijay served as vice-chairman.
source.title: Congress MP dismisses Tamil Nadu party's PM ambitions as unrealistic

source.summary: The Supreme Court has imposed interim restrictions on construction and pollution activities near Rajasthan's Jojari river. The court banned building within 100 meters of the river's edge and prohibited hazardous industries within 500 meters of the flood line to protect the damaged ecosystem. These measures are in place until scientific studies determine flood lines and ecological buffer zones. The order was issued in a suo motu case addressing river contamination, with a hearing scheduled for September 22.
source.title: Supreme Court restricts construction and pollution near Jojari river

source.summary: An Air India flight from Delhi with 164 passengers suffered a bird strike while landing at Patna airport on Monday, according to officials. The incident occurred near the aircraft’s right turbine, but no engine damage was found. The flight landed safely at 7:43 am and was cleared for a return flight to Delhi, which was delayed by 79 minutes. Airport authorities activated emergency protocols and deployed fire services as a precaution. Officials noted increased bird activity around the airport, citing a bat found on the runway. The AAI has deployed bird chasers with firearms and firecrackers to deter wildlife, but challenges remain due to nearby meat shops. The incident follows a similar bird strike on August 17, which grounded the aircraft for two days.
source.title: Air India flight experiences bird strike at Patna airport, lands safely

source.summary: The opposition has intensified protests demanding the resignation of a reinstated cabinet minister linked to an alleged welfare fund scam, accusing him of diverting 89 crore rupees through fake accounts. The ruling party defends the minister, stating he is on bail and not convicted, and rejects calls for his resignation, criticizing the opposition for disrupting legislative proceedings. Meanwhile, a Chief Minister criticized the Leader of the Opposition for remarks on Manusmriti and traditional values, accusing him of undermining cultural heritage and constitutional institutions. Regional political tensions also rose as some leaders proposed a southern leader for Prime Minister, while others dismissed the idea as unrealistic.
source.title: Opposition Demands Resignation of Cabinet Minister Amid Alleged Welfare Fund Scam

source.summary: Former Union Minister P. Chidambaram stated that there has been 'no corruption or virtually nil corruption' in Tamil Nadu's Registration department and State power utility following the Tamilaga Vettri Kazhagam's takeover. He cited public feedback from interactions in his home district, noting that corruption in document registration and teacher transfers appears to have been eliminated. Chidambaram also addressed the 2026 Assembly election, emphasizing that the two Dravidian parties held 80% of legislative seats, not political space, and highlighted the role of Gen Z voters. He discussed the need for subsidies, using the free bus travel for women scheme as an example with positive externalities.
source.title: Chidambaram highlights reduced corruption in Tamil Nadu government offices

source.summary: Prime Minister Narendra Modi called Nepal's Prime Minister Balendra Shah to offer humanitarian assistance following severe flash floods in Nepal. The floods, originating at the Nepal-China border, impacted areas like Rasuwa and Chitwan. Modi expressed solidarity with Nepal and stated India's teams are coordinating rescue and relief efforts. The Indian Air Force will deploy two aircraft to deliver relief supplies. The Indian Embassy in Kathmandu is also working with Nepalese authorities to assist affected individuals. Opposition leader Rahul Gandhi and Congress president Mallikarjun Kharge urged India to support Nepal, while Sri Lankan President Anura Kumara Dissanayake extended condolences and solidarity.
source.title: India offers humanitarian aid to Nepal after flash floods

source.summary: The controversy over fish consumption during Sawan, a month of dietary restrictions for many Hindus, has sparked political tensions in Uttar Pradesh. Sanjay Nishad, a Nishad Party leader and UP minister, claimed fish without garlic and onion is vegetarian, a statement that gained attention during the Ram Janmabhoomi movement. A video showing fish being prepared at a Nishad community event in Ayodhya, attended by UP Congress president Ajay Rai, intensified the debate. BJP leaders condemned the event, accusing Rai of hypocrisy, while Rai denied eating fish and challenged the Chief Minister to provide evidence. The Nishad community, historically tied to riverine livelihoods, holds significant electoral influence across key constituencies in Uttar Pradesh. Political analysts note that the community's shifting loyalties, from supporting the Ram movement to aligning with the BJP and later the Samajwadi Party, reflect broader struggles for representation and recognition. As the 2027 elections approach, the Nishad vote remains a critical factor in the contest between the BJP, Congress, and the Samajwadi Party, with each party vying to claim the community's political allegiance.
source.title: Nishad Vote and Fish Controversy Shape Uttar Pradesh 2027 Politics

source.summary: Prime Minister Narendra Modi expressed condolences for the loss of life in Nepal's floods and offered India's assistance for rescue and relief efforts. Modi tweeted that the Indian people stand in solidarity with Nepali citizens during the disaster. The Times of India reported the statement, noting Modi's focus on international relations and precise language in his communications.
source.title: India's PM Modi offers support to Nepal after devastating floods

source.summary: Crisil Ratings analyzed 100 large debt-funded acquisitions, finding two-thirds met expectations by delivering scale expansion, geographic reach, and margin improvements within 1-2 years. The remaining third underperformed due to integration challenges, regulatory delays, and cross-border issues. The firm noted stronger credit conditions, with median net debt-to-Ebitda dropping to 1.3x from 2.4x in 2017. Manish Gupta highlighted that successful deals offset increased leverage through scale and synergies, while weaker outcomes were linked to high leverage, slow integration, and industry downturns. Crisil emphasized disciplined capital allocation and strong execution as key to long-term M&A value creation.
source.title: Crisil Ratings: M&A success hinges on execution, with two-thirds of deals meeting expectations

source.summary: Divam Sharma, Co-Founder and Fund Manager at Green Portfolio, argues that earnings growth, not valuation re-rating, will drive returns over the next 2-3 years. He notes that the Nifty is fairly valued at 20.6x earnings, and returns will depend on earnings growth plus dividends. Sharma believes large caps are more attractive than smallcaps, which trade at a steep valuation premium despite lower earnings growth. However, he acknowledges that pockets of mispricing exist in smallcaps with strong fundamentals and limited analyst coverage. He warns that while smallcap valuations are high, they demand a 71% premium for more volatile earnings. Sharma also highlights that the market is transitioning from a re-rating phase to an earnings-driven phase, with foreign inflows improving as the rupee weakens and oil prices stabilize. He advises investors to focus on businesses where growth expectations are not fully priced in, rather than choosing between large and small caps.
source.title: ETMarkets Smart Talk | Large caps look better for next 24 months, but hidden gems remain in smallcaps: Divam Sharma

source.summary: India's engineering goods exports grew 18% year-on-year to $12.24 billion in July 2026, driven by strong demand in the US and China. Exports to the UAE and Saudi Arabia declined due to regional uncertainties and logistics issues around the Strait of Hormuz. The Engineering Export Promotion Council noted 27 of 34 engineering panels showed growth, while seven sectors declined. External risks, including higher costs and geopolitical tensions, could challenge future growth, according to EEPC India Chairman Pankaj Chadha.
source.title: India's engineering exports rise 18% in July, but West Asia faces risks

source.summary: JSW Group, led by Sajjan Jindal, has paused its plan to build a 50GWh battery cell gigafactory in India due to difficulties in securing a Chinese technology partner, as Beijing restricts technology transfers. The company's director, Parth Jindal, stated that lithium iron phosphate (LFP) technology, crucial for the project, is not available outside China. This decision follows similar delays by Reliance Industries and Amara Raja Energy & Mobility. JSW has focused solely on LFP technology, which is cheaper and more stable than NMC, but lacks the global availability of Chinese expertise. The company has already commissioned battery pack assembly facilities but has not yet secured the necessary technology tie-up. JSW's original plan, outlined in a 2025 presentation, aimed to complete the 50GWh capacity by 2032 in three phases, with a focus on partnerships in Japan, South Korea, and China.
source.title: JSW halts 50GWh battery plant due to Chinese tech restrictions

source.summary: Accenture, in partnership with Greater Chennai Corporation and Farmers for Forests, is supporting the development of a 15-acre Eco Action & Learning Hub in Manali, Chennai, focused on wetland restoration. This is the third such hub in India, following projects in Manchar and Nrityagram. The hub will offer environmental education, community engagement, and activities like guided tours and sustainability workshops. Accenture's Senior Country Managing Director, Ajay Vij, emphasized the importance of education in fostering environmental responsibility.
source.title: Accenture supports 15-acre Eco Action Hub for wetland restoration in Chennai

source.summary: Three Telangana students died in a Florida car crash on Interstate 95 near Palm Bay. The vehicle veered off the highway, hit a tree, and caught fire. One identified victim, N. Rahul, had recently completed his master's degree and was pursuing a PhD at the University of South Florida. The driver and front-seat passenger died at the scene, while Rahul was taken to a hospital. His family has requested assistance from Telangana and Central governments to repatriate his remains, with TANA coordinating the process. Authorities continue investigating the accident.
source.title: Three Telangana students killed in Florida car crash after veering off highway

source.summary: Union Minister Kiren Rijiju addressed criticisms of Prime Minister Narendra Modi's leadership style, stating Modi listens more than anyone he's known and speaks less than five percent during cabinet meetings. He rejected comparisons to Rahul Gandhi, who criticized patriarchal norms, by questioning why opposition leaders focus on Hindu texts rather than issues like triple talaq. Rijiju emphasized the Constitution governs India, not Manusmriti, and defended the government's parliamentary management. Meanwhile, Punjab Congress staged a protest against rising sugar prices, with protesters serving tea without sugar to highlight the burden on households. In Karnataka, actors discussed the Kannada film industry's cultural roots and challenges, including pay disparities for female actors.
source.title: Rijiju decodes PM's 'Dimagi Naxal' jibe, Rahul Gandhi's Manusmriti attack and more

source.summary: Bajaj General Insurance has launched 'My Family Complete', a health insurance plan that includes pets as part of the family. The policy covers both human and pet health, offering sum insured options from ₹5 lakh to ₹5 crore. It provides in-patient hospitalisation, ambulance services, and pet-specific benefits like missing pet reimbursement. CEO Tapan Singhel stated the plan reflects evolving family structures and lifestyles. The policy is valid for up to five years and combines indemnity- and benefit-based payouts. It also covers AYUSH treatments for humans and third-party liability for pets.
source.title: Bajaj General Insurance Introduces Family Health Plan Including Pets

source.summary: The Akhil Bharatiya Vidyarthi Parishad (ABVP) has ended its week-long protest at Pondicherry University following discussions with university officials. A delegation from the university handed over written assurances to ABVP president Surya Saravanan, including plans to install RO plants, improve infrastructure, and open the girls hostel on the Karaikal campus within 15 days. The administration also pledged to request the Puducherry government for more free buses and have wardens dine in hostel messes to assess food quality.
source.title: ABVP halts agitation at Pondicherry University after talks with administration

source.summary: Seven fishermen from Andhra Pradesh's Dr. B.R.Ambedkar Konaseema district, who went missing at sea on August 7, were located near West Bengal's Shankarpur fishing harbour. The group, stranded after a technical snag in their boat engine, survived without food for over three days. Local fishermen found them and facilitated contact with their families. The district administration and Fisheries Department are coordinating with West Bengal authorities for their safe return. The Indian Navy and Coast Guard participated in the search operation since August 17.
source.title: Seven Andhra Pradesh fishermen found safe off West Bengal coast after boat engine failure

source.summary: A flash flood in Nepal, triggered by an ice avalanche from an unstable rock mass near the Nepal-Tibet border, has killed 72 people and left 500 missing, including 133 Indian nationals. The disaster, which struck the Bhote Koshi River region at 9 am local time, caused widespread destruction of infrastructure, including roads, bridges, and hydropower projects in Rasuwa and Dhading districts. Authorities warn of further flooding risks due to a river blockage upstream, urging residents near rivers to evacuate. Rescue teams have recovered 72 bodies and rescued 93 people, with 30 receiving treatment in Kathmandu. The National Disaster Risk Reduction and Management Authority (NDRRMA) and Nepal Police have issued warnings about ongoing dangers, emphasizing the need for caution until the river blockage is fully drained.
source.title: Nepal Flash Floods: Ice Avalanche Triggered Devastating Disaster

source.summary: Meta Platforms agreed to a $16.68 billion settlement to resolve lawsuits from 47 states over teen social media addiction and privacy claims related to the Cambridge Analytica scandal. The settlement includes daily usage limits and restrictions on nighttime access for children. Additionally, $459.3 million will be distributed to California, Illinois, New Mexico, and Washington, D.C. for privacy-related claims. The company also faces ongoing lawsuits over alleged addictive platform features. Meta's stock rose 4% following the announcement, though it remains 28% below its all-time high.
source.title: Meta agrees to $16.68 billion settlement for teen addiction and privacy lawsuits

source.summary: Indian Railways announced plans to quadruple capacity on 11,000 km of high-density routes, which carry 41% of national traffic. Railway minister Ashwini Vaishnaw stated the expansion will create four tracks on seven key corridors, including Delhi-Howrah and Mumbai-Delhi. The upgrade aims to ease congestion and support future traffic growth. The project will complement existing freight corridors and improve connectivity between economic hubs. Vaishnaw highlighted railways' environmental and cost advantages over road transport. Implementation requires significant investment and careful management of current operations.
source.title: Indian Railways to expand 11,000 km high-density routes to four tracks

source.summary: JSW Group has paused its Odisha battery plant project due to the lack of available lithium iron phosphate (LFP) technology outside China. Parth Jindal, JSW Group's director, stated the company is seeking a technology partner for LFP battery cells. JSW has already commissioned cell-to-pack assembly lines but faces challenges in manufacturing battery cells. The group had signed an MoU with Odisha's government in February 2024 for a ₹40,000 crore project including a 50 GWh battery plant.
source.title: JSW Group halts Odisha battery plant due to LFP technology shortage

source.summary: The US Personal Consumption Expenditures (PCE) price index rose to 3.7% year-over-year in July, with service prices contributing to inflationary pressure. Core PCE inflation, which excludes volatile food and energy costs, increased 3.3% annually. While goods prices fell slightly, service prices rose 0.3%, with financial services and housing costs increasing. The Federal Reserve faces a difficult decision on interest rates as inflation remains above its 2% target. The July data, which exceeded Dow Jones forecasts, shows mixed signals, with core inflation matching expectations and personal income rising 0.4%. Financial markets reacted with lower futures and higher Treasury yields, reflecting concerns about inflation and Fed policy. The Fed's next policy meeting is scheduled for September 15-16, with markets pricing in a one-in-three chance of a rate move.
source.title: July US inflation rises to 3.7% as service prices push inflation pressure

source.summary: Billionaire investor Thomas Kaplan of Electrum Group predicts gold prices could rise tenfold, reaching Rs 15 lakh per 10 grams if current trends continue. He views the recent correction as a '1987 moment' within a broader bull market, similar to the 1987 stock market crash. Kaplan, who made gold and silver the foundation of his wealth, believes the long-term outlook for gold and silver remains bullish despite short-term volatility. He cited historical precedents to argue that market corrections are temporary and do not signal the end of the bull run.
source.title: Billionaire investor predicts gold may rise tenfold to Rs 15 lakh per 10 grams

source.summary: African country music stars and fans expressed deep grief following Dolly Parton's death, citing her relatable songs about rural hardship. Organizers in Kenya and Nigeria held vigils and noted the strong connection between her music and their own backgrounds. Former South African President Nelson Mandela was a known admirer of her work, and the Ladysmith Black Mambazo group recalled their positive collaboration with her.
source.title: African musicians and fans mourn Dolly Parton's death

source.summary: Nepal authorities warned residents of possible new flooding on Sunday after water levels rose in the Bhotekoshi River. Rescue crews continue clearing a major highway connecting Kathmandu to severely affected areas. The initial floods killed at least 760 people and left more than 3,000 missing across Nepal and Tibet. Residents in Dhading are returning to ruined homes to salvage items while dealing with thick mud. Nepal's disaster agency reported the death toll climbed to 752 with 2,502 missing, while Chinese authorities reported 16 deaths and 546 missing on their side. Malaysia pledged $1 million in aid and sent a specialized search-and-rescue team to assist with relief efforts. Scientists say the disaster began after a glacial collapse registered as magnitude 5.2.
source.title: Nepal warns of fresh flooding as communities recover from deadly disaster

source.summary: The provided text contains a headline about a Russian strike but includes a technical error message preventing the article body from loading. Consequently, no specific details regarding the event or its context are available to summarize.
source.title: Russian strike kills 38 near Kyiv, raising concerns over Ukrainian sensitive urban sites

source.summary: Zambian opposition leader Brian Mundubile has been charged with treason, his lawyer said. Authorities arrested Mundubile after a raid linked to disputed election results. Seventeen others, including his running mate, also face treason charges. Mundubile previously disputed President Hakainde Hichilema's re-election victory.
source.title: Zambian opposition leader Brian Mundubile charged with treason

source.summary: Greece and Turkey have renewed tensions after Turkey designated two marine parks in disputed Aegean waters. Greece's Foreign Ministry called the move illegal, stating it lacks legal validity outside Turkish territorial waters. Prime Minister Kyriakos Mitsotakis emphasized that areas under Greek sovereignty must be defended according to international law. Greece simultaneously announced its own marine parks in 2025, prompting Turkey to warn against unilateral actions in semi-closed seas. Analysts suggest these environmental designations serve as tactics to assert dominance rather than purely protect nature. Greece fears the parks advance Turkey's "Mavi Vatan" doctrine, which challenges Greek sovereignty and exclusive economic zones. To counter Turkey's military advantage, Greece is investing heavily in defense systems, including a planned "Achilles Shield" air defense network modeled on Israel's Iron Dome. While Mitsotakis maintains a conciliatory tone, upcoming elections may pressure him toward a tougher nationalist stance.
source.title: Greece and Turkey clash over new Aegean marine parks

source.summary: Syoutarou Kobayasi discussed his new film "Lives at Right Angles" in an interview with The Japan Times. The director explained that Japanese medical melodramas often feature flawed human characters rather than idealized figures. He noted that while these stories may move audiences to tears, the emotional impact is earned through realistic storytelling. The film centers on an autistic protagonist and aims to present an unblinkingly realistic portrayal of disability.
source.title: Director Syoutarou Kobayasi discusses realistic film with autistic protagonist

source.summary: Residents in Kisangani are receiving vaccines as the Democratic Republic of Congo begins a campaign to stop its worst Ebola outbreak. Health officials hope the Ervebo vaccine will protect against the Bundibugyo strain, for which no specific treatment exists. Frontline workers were prioritized for the shots, with doctors stating it is their duty to be vaccinated. The country has confirmed over 5,600 cases and 2,700 deaths since mid-May. A total of 70,000 vaccine doses are expected to arrive soon.
source.title: DRC launches Ebola vaccination campaign amid record outbreak

source.summary: Alia al-Hallaq of Al-Rihiya says her nine-year-old son Mohammed was killed by an Israeli army bullet last October. She stated he was shot while running away from patrolling soldiers in the occupied West Bank. The mother continues to identify as a parent of five despite the loss. She often visits his grave and cries while ensuring her remaining children do not see her.
source.title: Palestinian mother describes grief after son killed by Israeli soldiers

source.summary: Australian tennis player Alexei Popyrin is working with mindset coach Emma Murray to address mental health struggles before the US Open. Popyrin, who dropped to world number 139, fears his obsession with rankings ruined his enjoyment of life. He will face Grigor Dimitrov in his first round at Flushing Meadows. Popyrin stated he must change his perspective on tennis as a work in progress.
source.title: Alexei Popyrin seeks mental reset with coach Emma Murray before US Open

source.summary: The Van Gogh Museum published a systematic study revealing that Vincent Van Gogh signed only 133 of his 840 known paintings. Researcher Julia Engelmayer found that the artist's signature frequency correlated with his mental well-being and self-confidence. During periods of hope in Paris and Arles, he signed more often, whereas his time in psychiatric hospitals and subsequent decline in Auvers-sur-Oise saw him sign very few works. The study analyzes letters to his brother Theo and museum records to explain these patterns. Senior researcher Teio Meedendorp noted that the lack of signatures complicates authentication of unsigned pieces. Engelmayer concluded that Van Gogh often signed works only when he felt particularly proud of them.
source.title: Van Gogh Museum study links artist's signatures to mental health

source.summary: Elías Jaua, a former vice president of Venezuela, argues that the country has lost its national independence following the January 3 operation that removed Nicolás Maduro. Speaking through the Center for Studies on Socialist Democracy, Jaua states that Venezuela's sovereignty is compromised because its oil revenues are held in a U.S. Treasury sub-account, effectively placing the nation under American tutelage. He contends that the current interim government led by Delcy Rodríguez is cooperating with the United States out of fear of military action rather than genuine partnership. Jaua asserts that a true national agreement must prioritize the recovery of independence and the full restoration of control over national revenues before any other political negotiations can succeed. He further criticizes the exclusion of various political currents, including opposition leader María Corina Machado, arguing that a pluralistic democracy is essential to prevent future instability. While acknowledging past corruption and management failures within Chavismo, Jaua maintains that the current crisis stems from a lack of political will to manage conflict democratically after Hugo Chávez's death. He calls for state actors to set aside personal ambitions to negotiate a path that allows Venezuelans to determine their own future without foreign intervention.
source.title: Former Venezuelan VP Elías Jaua criticizes current leadership and US occupation

source.summary: Icelandic polling stations closed Saturday evening as nearly 400,000 citizens voted in a referendum on reopening EU membership negotiations. Preliminary results are expected early Sunday, according to RUV. The campaign focused on living costs, security, and fisheries control. A majority 'Yes' vote would mandate the government to resume talks, though final membership requires a second vote. The European Commission maintains Iceland's 2009 application remains legally valid despite previous suspensions.
source.title: Icelanders vote in referendum on reopening EU membership talks

source.summary: Iceland's public broadcaster RUV reported that preliminary referendum results show a narrow majority supporting the reopening of EU membership negotiations. The vote count indicates 50.5% in favor and 49.5% against the proposal. Regional breakdowns reveal strong support in Reykjavik North and significant opposition in the Southern constituency. The campaign focused on cost of living, security, and fisheries control. A majority yes vote would mandate the government to resume talks, though final membership requires a second referendum.
source.title: Iceland referendum initial tally narrowly favors reopening EU accession talks

source.summary: Newer Tamil Nadu companies like Milky Mist and Lalithaa Jewellery are joining the IPO market, with Garuda Aerospace and Sathya Agencies expected to follow. Analysts note that family businesses are shifting from conservative ownership to public listing to resolve succession disputes and increase value. Capital market experts describe this trend as a 'net worth creation effect' driven by seeing peers become millionaires through public offerings. Recent data shows a significant rise in IPO issues and funds raised across India from 2023 to 2025, with 2026 figures already showing strong momentum.
source.title: Tamil Nadu business houses increasingly pursue IPO listings

source.summary: Intel Corporation shares dropped 2.85% on Friday as investors weighed new 14A chip progress against persistent foundry losses. CFO David Zinsner stated that 14A defect density is improving faster than expected, tracking above Intel's target curve. However, Intel Foundry reported a $2.09 billion operating loss in the second quarter despite $5.77 billion in revenue. The company plans high-volume manufacturing of 14A chips in 2028, with risk production starting in late 2027. While customer interest in Intel's foundry services is growing, analysts remain cautious about converting technology progress into sustainable profits. Intel's overall revenue rose 25% to $16.1 billion, supported by strong Data Center and AI performance. MarketBeat reports that 31 of 50 tracked analysts hold a rating on the stock, with an average price target of $107.46.
source.title: Intel stock falls 2.85% despite 14A chip progress and rising foundry losses

source.summary: Assam Chief Minister Himanta Biswa Sarma stated that over 26,500 people were arrested and drugs worth 3,253 crore rupees were seized since 2021. He described the operation as a sustained war against narcotics originating in Myanmar. The CM credited central leadership and improved coordination with Myanmar for the results. Arrest numbers rose steadily from 4,175 in 2021 to 4,901 in 2025.
source.title: Assam CM reports 26,500 arrests and 3,253 crore seized in drug crackdown

source.summary: Prime Minister Narendra Modi and Uzbek President Shavkat Mirziyoyev announced an elevation of bilateral relations to a Comprehensive Strategic Partnership during a joint press meet in New Delhi. The leaders set a target of $5 billion in trade by 2030, building on existing bilateral trade that has already crossed $1 billion. PM Modi stated that Uzbekistan is central to India's engagement with Central Asia and highlighted cooperation in defence, energy, and digital infrastructure. Mirziyoyev noted new areas for collaboration including critical minerals and pharmaceuticals, while both leaders emphasized expanding people-to-people ties through sister-city arrangements and visa-free travel. The visit concluded with Mirziyoyev conferring Uzbekistan's highest state honour on PM Modi.
source.title: PM Modi elevates India-Uzbekistan ties to strategic partnership with $5 billion trade goal

source.summary: Prime Minister Narendra Modi and Uzbekistan President Shavkat Mirziyoyev announced a long-term uranium supply deal during talks in Tashkent. The agreement was reached during delegation-level discussions at the Kuksaroy Presidential Palace on Sunday. Both leaders confirmed the arrangement as part of their bilateral engagement.
source.title: India and Uzbekistan finalize long-term uranium supply agreement

source.summary: Samco CIO Umesh Mehta has positioned the Samco Flexicap Fund with approximately 75% exposure to mid, small, and micro-cap stocks, limiting large-cap holdings. Mehta argues that mega-cap companies are languishing due to lack of valuation support and limited net new buyers. He believes growth is currently concentrated in smaller companies, though he cautions that earnings momentum may not sustain due to supply-chain restrictions. Mehta identifies refining margins, defence, power, and AI ancillaries as attractive sectors, noting that power capital expenditure offers a sizeable, sustainable opportunity. Regarding nuclear power, he suggests investors should wait for lower valuations after the long gestation period rather than buying now. On asset allocation, Mehta recommends increasing gold exposure to 15–20% for moderately aggressive investors, citing geopolitical risks and currency weaponisation as drivers for gold's secular bull market. He also warns that aggressive IPO issuance could drain secondary market liquidity, potentially forcing a correction if foreign institutional investors do not return.
source.title: Samco CIO Umesh Mehta allocates 75% of fund to small and mid caps

source.summary: Subhash Chandra accused Reliance Industries Chairman Mukesh Ambani and RIL-owned media entities of orchestrating a misinformation campaign following the National Company Law Tribunal's approval of his repayment proposal. Reliance Group rejected these allegations as baseless, stating its media brands have never been used to attack anyone. Chandra's current disclosed net worth is approximately ₹31.79 crore, significantly lower than historical figures of around ₹45,888 crore in 2017. Meanwhile, Mukesh Ambani's net worth is estimated at $88 billion, primarily derived from his stake in Reliance Industries. The controversy highlights the stark contrast between the two tycoons' financial standings amid Chandra's insolvency proceedings.
source.title: Subhash Chandra accuses Mukesh Ambani of misinformation over debt claims

source.summary: AI agents require continuous oversight, leading to extended work hours for developers. Sharma, a 27-year-old developer, forgoes regular sleep to monitor agents around the clock. Pezaris, a developer at Proxon, works from 7:30 a.m. to 2 a.m., noting his team operates 30 times faster with agents. However, increased efficiency creates more human work, such as customer support. Pezaris also mentions an 'agent FOMO' effect, where missing out on agent work means missing a week’s worth of tasks. The article highlights the growing reliance on AI agents and their impact on work schedules.
source.title: AI agents demand constant attention, reshaping work hours

source.summary: The U.S. federal debt has reached $40 trillion, with annual interest costs exceeding $1 trillion. The debt has grown due to political decisions and automatic spending increases linked to aging populations. Higher debt levels have pushed up interest rates, affecting mortgages and loans. While the Treasury has taken measures to stabilize bond yields, long-term solutions require congressional action on taxes or spending cuts. Experts warn that the debt should serve as a wake-up call for fiscal responsibility.
source.title: U.S. federal debt hits $40 trillion, raising concerns over interest costs and economic impact

source.summary: The Pakistan Tehreek-e-Insaf (PTI) party has criticized the authorities for failing to conduct a CT Coronary Angiography (CTA) on Imran Khan despite cardiologists' concerns about cardiac risks. Central Secretary Information Sheikh Waqas Akram accused hospital officials of negligence after Khan was transferred to Adiala Jail without the test. The party demanded the procedure be conducted immediately at Shifa International Hospital, citing a Supreme Court order. Akram alleged that the decision to bypass Shifa, where the test was available, was intentional, raising concerns about political interference in medical care. The government formed an inquiry committee to investigate the incident, with Akram calling for full disclosure of Khan's medical records.
source.title: PTI demands immediate cardiac test for Imran Khan at Shifa Hospital

source.summary: The US Treasury Secretary Scott Bessent is set to announce a 'D-Day' package of economic sanctions against Iran, marking the administration's most severe financial offensive against the country. Iran's security chief, Mohsen Rezaei, warned of an 'earthquake-like' retaliation, threatening to block oil exports from the Persian Gulf if the US and its Gulf allies proceed with sanctions. The US has also canceled a joint military exercise with South Korea due to resource limitations from the Iran conflict. Iranian officials dismissed the sanctions as a sign of US desperation, claiming they would fail to weaken Tehran. The sanctions come amid rising global oil prices due to Iran's blockade of the Strait of Hormuz, which has disrupted international oil shipments.
source.title: US to impose 'D-Day' sanctions on Iran as Tehran warns of retaliation

source.summary: A 15-year-old boy pleaded guilty to manslaughter but faces murder charges for fatally stabbing Oscar Hamilton, 16, at a Melbourne shopping centre in 2024. Prosecutors claim the unproven sexual assault allegation against Oscar was the motive, though the jury is not required to assess its truth. The accused, who remains on trial, admitted to the act and expressed infatuation with the girl who accused Oscar. The defense argues the boy did not intend to kill Oscar, focusing on intent rather than motive. The trial continues with witnesses including Oscar's friends and medical experts.
source.title: Teen accused of murdering boy over unproven sexual assault allegation

source.summary: Japanese convenience store chain Lawson will reduce prices on hand-wrapped onigiri rice balls starting Sept. 29, citing expected lower rice costs. The move follows a 28% drop in supermarket rice prices since January, driven by improved supply and private-sector inventories reaching a 13-year high. A spokesperson noted that falling market prices are likely to reduce procurement costs. Last year, rice shortages led to price hikes and government intervention, but supply improvements have since eased pressure on retailers.
source.title: Lawson to lower onigiri prices as rice costs decline

source.summary: The family of Ann Marie Smith, an Adelaide woman who died in 2020 from severe neglect, has shared their grief in victim impact statements during a court case against her former NDIS provider. Amy June Collins, a former co-director of Integrity Care SA, pleaded guilty to reckless conduct under the Work Health and Safety Act. The court heard statements from Smith's brother and uncle, who described her suffering and the preventable nature of her death. Collins' lawyer claimed her actions were not the cause of Smith's death, blaming her carer instead. The case highlights concerns about oversight in disability care, with the family urging stronger protections for vulnerable individuals.
source.title: Family of NDIS client recounts neglect leading to death in court

source.summary: The National Environment Agency (NEA) warned that Singapore may experience haze due to intensified fires in Sumatra and Kalimantan. Air quality remained moderate on Aug 24, with the 24-hour PSI ranging from 68 to 90. NEA noted increased hotspot activity over the weekend, with smoke plumes observed in Kalimantan, southern Sumatra, and Riau. The agency said prevailing winds could bring occasional haze to Singapore. NEA will issue daily advisories if the PSI exceeds 100. The inter-agency haze task force is prepared to implement action plans if air quality worsens. The ASEAN Specialised Meteorological Centre has raised its alert to Level 2, indicating an increasing risk of transboundary haze.
source.title: Singapore warns of possible haze due to increased fires in Sumatra and Kalimantan

source.summary: Las Vegas Raiders running back Ashton Jeanty suffered an apparent injury during Sunday's practice, requiring assistance to leave the field and unable to bear weight on his right leg. The team provided no update, with coach Klint Kubiak set to speak Tuesday. Jeanty, drafted sixth overall, had rushed for 975 yards as a rookie despite a weak offensive line. Rookie Mike Washington Jr. could take over if Jeanty is sidelined. Washington has 15 carries for 119 yards in preseason games.
source.title: Ashton Jeanty injured during Raiders practice, status unclear

source.summary: Norway's King Harald was hospitalized for a bacterial blood infection, receiving antibiotics. His condition is stable, according to the royal palace. The 89-year-old monarch, who has been on sick leave for weeks, has a history of hospitalizations due to hemolytic anemia and fluid retention from cortisone treatment. Crown Prince Haakon has been acting as regent during his absence.
source.title: Norway's King Harald hospitalized for bacterial infection

source.summary: Fabinho is set to sign with Trabzonspor on a free transfer, joining fellow free agent Mohamed Salah. The Turkish Super Lig club shared a photo of the Brazilian midfielder in their kit on a private jet. Fabinho left Liverpool in 2023 for Al Ittihad in Saudi Arabia and is now a free agent. Salah also joined Trabzonspor earlier this month as a free agent. Fabinho posted on Trabzonspor's social media: 'A familiar face is waiting for me in Trabzon.'
source.title: Fabinho to join Trabzonspor on free transfer with Salah

source.summary: British Prime Minister Andy Burnham announced in Kyiv that UK-made components of the SCALP long-range cruise missile will be shared with European manufacturer MBDA, aiding Ukraine's defense against Russia. The move follows Russian strikes that killed three people in Kharkiv and Ukrainian drone attacks on Russian logistics hubs, including Ozon's facilities in Dagestan. Ukraine's President Zelensky warned of Russia's plan to draft 300,000 new troops, while UK officials emphasized that Ukrainian elections are an internal matter. Meanwhile, Russia reported downing 351 Ukrainian drones overnight and hitting a fuel tanker near Odesa.
source.title: UK shares missile component details with Ukraine as attacks continue

source.summary: The 15th edition of Gabon's Festival of Cultures, held in Libreville from August 21 to 23, highlights the country's cultural diversity and aims to preserve traditions. The event, themed 'Reappropriation of our Cultural Values,' brings together representatives from Gabon's nine provinces, artists, and artisans. Young attendees expressed interest in reconnecting with their heritage, emphasizing the importance of preserving traditional practices. The festival also features Senegal as the guest country, showcasing its cultural elements and fostering intercultural dialogue. Organizers stress the role of the event in strengthening national identity and passing on cultural knowledge to future generations.
source.title: Gabon's Festival of Cultures Celebrates Cultural Heritage and Intercultural Exchange

source.summary: Japanese power prices reached their highest level in over three years, driven by increased electricity demand from a heat wave and higher LNG costs. The next-day power price rose 20% to ￥25.18 per kilowatt-hour, according to Japan Electric Power Exchange data. Unusually hot weather, with temperatures expected to reach 35°C in Tokyo and Kansai regions, contributed to the demand surge. LNG prices in Asia have more than doubled since late February due to Middle East supply disruptions, including Iranian attacks on shipping. The Strait of Hormuz, a key LNG route, has seen halted shipments since July, with no immediate reopening expected.
source.title: Japan's power prices hit three-year high due to heat wave and LNG supply issues

source.summary: UK Prime Minister Andy Burnham visited Ukraine's capital Kyiv on Independence Day, accompanied by European leaders. He plans to announce that the UK will allow MBDA, a European defense company, to share declassified information about UK-made components of the Storm Shadow/Scalp missiles. This move aims to help Ukraine develop its own long-range missile capabilities. Burnham also intends to meet with Ukrainian President Zelenskyy and chair the first meeting of the Coalition of the Willing. Ukrainian Foreign Minister Sybiha emphasized the importance of international support for Ukraine's independence.
source.title: UK PM Announces Missile Component Sharing with Ukraine During Independence Day Visit

source.summary: Oil prices declined as investors anticipated U.S. economic sanctions against Iran, part of a broader strategy by President Trump. Asian markets saw mixed performance, with South Korea's Kospi falling after Samsung's $80 billion share buyback. Nvidia and Alibaba face scrutiny over their AI investments, while global stock indices showed varied results. U.S. Treasury Secretary Scott Bessent hinted at further economic pressure on Iran, amid rising concerns over federal debt and inflation.
source.title: Oil falls as Trump pledges economic war on Iran

source.summary: Diego Maradona's football, used in his 1986 World Cup 'Hand of God' goal, sold for £2.5m at Heritage Auctions. The ball, which Maradona famously described as scored 'a little with the head of Maradona and a little with the hand of God,' was expected to fetch around £7.3m. Tunisian referee Ali Bin Nasser, who collected the ball, confirmed it was the only one used in the match. The ball had previously sold for $2.37m in 2022 and was re-auctioned in 2023 without meeting the minimum bid.
source.title: Maradona's 'Hand of God' football sells for £2.5m at auction

source.summary: A landfill collapse in Conakry, Guinea, killed at least 30 people and injured six after heavy rain triggered a landslide. The disaster occurred at the Dar Es Salam waste site, which was scheduled to close on Sunday. Eyewitnesses described the collapse as occurring in stages, with rescuers struggling to reach survivors. Authorities reported that several nearby homes were destroyed, and a search and rescue operation was underway. The incident highlights ongoing challenges with waste management in the area, as residents had been ordered to leave the site but many remained nearby.
source.title: Landfill collapse in Conakry kills at least 30, triggers rescue efforts

source.summary: Chinese authorities are investigating reports of formaldehyde use to preserve cabbages for human consumption. Footage verified by Hebei province officials shows individuals dipping cabbages in a solution before transportation. The practice, which is illegal, was first reported by an environmental blogger. Police have taken legal action, and officials are conducting market checks to restore consumer confidence. Xinfadi market in Beijing confirmed none of the affected vegetables had entered its market. The incident has sparked media attention, with critics condemning the wholesalers' disregard for consumer health. China produces over 30 million tonnes of cabbages annually, with major exports to Vietnam, South Korea, and Russia. The American Cancer Society notes exposure to high levels of formaldehyde may link to cancer, though effects of small amounts are unclear.
source.title: Chinese authorities investigate formaldehyde use in cabbage preservation

source.summary: Paris Saint-Germain drew 2-2 with Rennes in Ligue 1 on the opening day. Ferran Torres, the club's new signing, came on after halftime and scored the equalizing goal. The result ended a challenging start for PSG, who had trailed twice in the match.
source.title: Ferran Torres scores late goal for Paris Saint-Germain draw against Rennes
