source.summary: An opinion piece argues that US tariffs on Canada demonstrate how trade power relies on leverage rather than loyalty. The author states that Washington's actions show trade agreements are conditional on power, not just paper. The text notes the US imports roughly three-quarters of Canada's exports, creating an imbalance that allows market access to be withdrawn at whim. The author claims India previously paid a similar toll in February 2026 by lowering tariffs in exchange for energy and Russia-related adjustments. The piece concludes that New Delhi must diversify trade ties and negotiate provisional agreements with review clauses to avoid structural vulnerability.
source.title: US Tariffs on Canada Warn India About Trade Leverage

source.summary: Scientists from the Nature Conservation Foundation and CSIR-Centre for Cellular and Molecular Biology generated high-quality reference genomes for four Asian hornbill species. The researchers used a hybrid approach combining Illumina and Oxford Nanopore Technology sequencing to assemble the genetic data. These new genomes provide a critical baseline for future evolutionary and population genomics research across Asia and Africa. Analysis using the Pairwise Sequentially Markovian Coalescent method revealed that all four species experienced a dramatic population decline during the Pleistocene due to climatic changes. The study highlights how genomic data can inform conservation decisions by identifying populations with low genetic variation. Meghana Natesh of WWF India noted the importance of these assemblies for understanding population history and adaptive potential.
source.title: Researchers create reference genomes for four Asian hornbill species

source.summary: The article reports on multiple current events across India and abroad. Prime Minister Narendra Modi met with Armenian Prime Minister Nikol Pashinyan in Bishkek to discuss defence cooperation. Political tensions arose in Tamil Nadu between TVK and Congress over the 2029 leadership contest. In Karnataka, Minister Basavaraj Rayareddy faced criticism for remarks on Islam. Meanwhile, Nepal's official death toll from floods reached 903. A Delhi bus rape case and a Surat railway food hygiene scandal also made headlines.
source.title: PM Modi meets Armenian PM; southern India politics; Nepal floods kill 903

source.summary: A Chhattisgarh High Court division bench ruled that denying compassionate jobs to married daughters is discriminatory. The court set aside a previous order rejecting claims by Sheena David and Ankita Mishra, whose fathers died while working for the Chhattisgarh Rajya Gramin Bank. Justice Ramesh Sinha and Justice Ravindra Kumar Agrawal directed the bank to appoint the women to suitable posts within 90 days. The judges held that marital status cannot disqualify a dependent daughter when married sons receive the same benefit. The court found the bank's rejection based on marriage arbitrary and violative of constitutional Articles 14 and 15.
source.title: Chhattisgarh HC Orders Compassionate Jobs for Married Daughters

source.summary: The article reports on several current events, including a rape case in Delhi, SCO summit talks, Nepal floods, and a food hygiene incident. A 16-year-old girl was allegedly gang-raped on a Delhi bus, leading to arrests. At the SCO Summit in Bishkek, Indian and Armenian leaders discussed defence cooperation and regional dynamics. Nepal's flood death toll reached 903, with over 4,000 people missing. A Surat railway tea stall was sealed after a video showed a rat eating food. BJP and Akali Dal student wings formed an alliance for Panjab University elections.
source.title: SCO Summit: India and Armenia discuss defence ties and regional dynamics

source.summary: Three residents of Hindupur, Andhra Pradesh, were killed after being struck by a train near Doddaballapur Railway Station in Bengaluru on Monday. The deceased, identified as Irfan, Rukia, and Rakia, were returning home from a visit when the incident occurred. Yelahanka Railway Police arrived at the scene, shifted the bodies for examination, and registered a case to launch an investigation.
source.title: Three Andhra Pradesh Residents Killed in Bengaluru Train Accident

source.summary: The Supreme Court refused to interfere with the Bombay High Court order cancelling bail for the owners of a Goa nightclub where a fire claimed 25 lives. A bench of Justices Dipankrar Datta and Sheel Nagu upheld the August 18 order and dismissed petitions filed by Saurabh Luthra, Gaurav Luthra, and Ajay Gupta. The court directed the trio to surrender within two weeks and asked the lower court to expedite the trial. Senior advocates for the accused argued the case involved negligence rather than intentional offences, while the prosecution opposed the bail petitions. The High Court had noted the venue operated without adequate fire safety installations and that the accused allegedly knew about the risks of conducting fire displays without proper measures.
source.title: Supreme Court Upholds Bail Cancellation for Goa Nightclub Fire Owners

source.summary: Shares of Balrampur Chini, Shree Renuka Sugars, and other sugar companies rose up to 11% on Monday. The rally followed a sharp increase in domestic and global sugar prices. The government announced fortnightly sale quotas for mills to ensure steady supplies. Analyst Seema Srivastava noted the sector is shifting toward a bio-energy ecosystem. She stated this transition positions companies for structural re-rating and sustained earnings growth.
source.title: Sugar stocks rise 11% as prices climb and government assigns sale quotas

source.summary: LiveMint presents a quote by Robin Williams from the film Dead Poets Society, emphasizing that words and ideas can change the world. The article explains the quote serves as a counter to cynicism regarding the arts and humanities. It notes Williams delivered the line while portraying John Keating in the 1989 drama. The piece also outlines Williams' career, mentioning his roles in Mork & Mindy, Aladdin, and Good Will Hunting. LiveMint describes itself as a credible source for news and analysis across various sectors.
source.title: LiveMint shares Robin Williams quote on power of words and ideas

source.summary: Activist Sonam Wangchuk shared previously unreported details regarding the NEET examination protest at Jantar Mantar in Delhi. Speaking to Prakhar Gupta on the PGX podcast, Wangchuk explained his strategy of testing the Cockroach Janata Party leadership before initiating his 26-day hunger strike. He described a critical moment where he considered ending the fast due to deteriorating health and low morale among protesters. Wangchuk credited the return of young demonstrators after the July 20 violence for restoring confidence within the movement. The article notes that Union ministers JP Nadda and Jitendra Singh eventually met with him to urge an end to the strike. Wangchuk stated that the protest ultimately contributed to the resignation of education minister Dharmendra Pradhan.
source.title: Sonam Wangchuk reveals untold NEET protest stories and leadership tests

source.summary: The controversy surrounding Rahul Gandhi's criticism of the Manusmriti highlights deep divisions within Hindu society. The article argues that while dominant-caste Hindus often defend the text, Dalits and women from marginalized communities do not share this attachment. It suggests that claims of Hindu unity are often constructed through opposition to Muslims rather than genuine emotional solidarity. The piece further examines the Rashtriya Swayamsevak Sangh's ideological reliance on the Manusmriti over the Constitution and its internal caste dynamics. Author Apoorvanand concludes that Gandhi's remarks exposed the reality that political Hindu unity cannot sustain itself without underlying emotional unity among all castes.
source.title: Controversy over Manusmriti reveals lack of Hindu unity

source.summary: Ather Energy shares climbed nearly 4% to reach a lifetime high of ₹1,679 after the company unveiled its new Konarc scooter. The electric two-wheeler maker priced the mass-market model starting at ₹99,999, targeting a wider consumer base beyond its premium portfolio. Hero MotoCorp strengthened its position by acquiring an additional 3.01% stake in Ather Energy from the Government of Singapore for ₹1,758.24 crore. Analysts note the stock has surged 423% from its IPO price, with renewed buying interest and bullish technical indicators. However, some analysts caution that the sharp rally could lead to near-term exhaustion despite the broader uptrend.
source.title: Ather Energy shares hit lifetime high after launching mass-market Konarc scooter

source.summary: At least five people were reportedly killed and several others injured in a massive explosion at a cracker manufacturing unit in Prayagraj on Monday. Rescue operations are underway while senior police officials have rushed to the spot to carry out investigations. Further details are awaited.
source.title: Five dead, several injured in blast at cracker unit in UP

source.summary: Fact-checkers determined a viral video falsely claimed to show a Hindu woman attacked by Islamists in Bangladesh. The video actually depicts a robbery in Feni where a Muslim woman was held hostage. Investigators identified the footage via a reverse image search linking it to Daily Jugantor. Multiple Bangladeshi news outlets reported the incident occurred on August 19, 2026. The woman, identified as Shahena Akhtar, was robbed at her home around 8 AM.
source.title: Fact-checkers debunk viral video falsely claiming Hindu woman attacked in Bangladesh

source.summary: Climate activist Sonam Wangchuk told Hindustan Times that CJP leaders considered ending the Delhi protest following the July 20 police crackdown. He reported that officials asked him to urge protesters to leave, but the message was never posted. Wangchuk credited returning youth for restoring morale after the stage was dismantled. CJP founder Abhijit Dipke announced a new march on September 5 seeking FIR withdrawals and compensation.
source.title: Sonam Wangchuk says CJP leaders wanted to end Delhi protest after crackdown

source.summary: A joint Tamil Nadu and Manipur police team arrested Manik Uddin Laskar and Bhagabati Majhi in Manipur regarding the killing of Hayathun Nisha. The suspects were flown to Chennai for questioning after a 24-day investigation spanning multiple states. Police allege the couple killed Nisha following a dispute, though these claims remain unproven in court. Investigators continue searching for Nisha's missing head while examining potential financial motives.
source.title: Police arrest Tamil Nadu murder suspects in Manipur after 24-day manhunt

source.summary: The article reports that caste divisions threaten the unity of the Gen Z-led Cockroach Janta Party (CJP). The CJP built a cross-caste coalition by demanding education reform and accountability for exam leaks. However, anti-reservation activists are attempting to fracture this alliance by challenging reservation quotas. Ashoka University researcher Sneha Thomas notes that improved government schooling benefits all social groups, yet anti-reservationists seek to protect general category interests. Union Minister J.P. Nadda has met anti-reservationists, while the government refuses to parley with the CJP. Additionally, the government's flawed methodology for the 2026-27 Census risks further alienating general category students. Senior journalist Ajaz Ashraf argues the CJP must navigate these divisive caste waters to maintain its momentum.
source.title: Caste threatens Gen Z unity as anti-reservationists split the Cockroach Janta Party

source.summary: The Supreme Court issued notices to the Centre and Delhi Police regarding a plea against the Cockroach Janata Party's September 5 protest but refused an early hearing. A bench comprising Chief Justice Surya Kant and two other judges stated that maintaining law and order is the responsibility of the police. Retired officer Rajendra Singh filed an application alleging the march lacks requisite permissions and could disrupt the upcoming BRICS Summit. The Court noted that no permission has been sought by the organisers to date. The planned 2.5-km march involves families of NEET aspirants and students alleging the Centre failed to drop cases against July protesters.
source.title: Supreme Court issues notices to Centre and police on CJP Delhi march

source.summary: SpiceJet requested additional time from the Delhi High Court to pay a ₹50 crore instalment owed to Kalanithi Maran. Senior advocate Mukul Rohatgi stated the airline used recent government emergency credit for operations while awaiting a second tranche of ₹349 crore. The court will review compliance on September 21. This dispute stems from a 2015 stake transfer and involves multiple legal proceedings regarding outstanding liabilities and government support measures.
source.title: SpiceJet seeks court extension to pay ₹50 crore debt to Maran

source.summary: Bangladesh State Minister for Foreign Affairs Humaiun Kobir stated that positive dialogue is underway regarding Dhaka joining the Makkah Joint Defence Agreement. The pact, signed by Pakistan, Saudi Arabia, and Türkiye, aims to strengthen collective deterrence in West Asia. Kobir noted Bangladesh sees no risk in joining and views the agreement positively within the broader context of addressing challenges facing the Islamic world. Discussions are ongoing with all parties involved, including bilateral partners. These statements come amid strained ties between India and Bangladesh over the extradition of former Prime Minister Sheikh Hasina.
source.title: Bangladesh says positive dialogue continues on joining Makkah defence pact

source.summary: The San Francisco Municipal Transportation Agency is accepting applications for a new curbside electric vehicle charging program. Residents can use a new map to nominate locations for chargers. The city aims to install 100 stations by 2030. Environment Department director Tyrone Jue stated the network will help residents choose electric vehicles. The program follows a 2025 pilot involving three companies.
source.title: San Francisco launches citywide curbside EV charger program

source.summary: The Centre for Energy Research and Clean Air reported that global energy import bills rose by $330 billion between March and August due to Strait of Hormuz disruptions. In response, Saudi Arabia rerouted exports via the Red Sea and Suez Canal, while the UAE plans to double Fujairah pipeline capacity to 3.6 million barrels daily. TotalEnergies joined ADNOC in expanding this project and exploring a new Iraq-Syria pipeline route. Iraq is evaluating a four-year new pipeline or a three-year repair of an existing line, alongside talks with Turkey. Kuwait seeks to connect to UAE and Saudi ports, while Japan agreed to support regional network expansion. Gulf governments now prioritize port infrastructure as a mission-critical priority to mitigate war-induced economic shocks.
source.title: Iran War Triggers Billions in New Oil Pipeline and Port Investment

source.summary: Voltalia has fully commissioned the 148 MW Bolobedu solar farm in Limpopo, South Africa, to supply Richards Bay Minerals. The facility is expected to generate around 300 GWh annually, avoiding more than 237,000 tonnes of carbon dioxide emissions each year. During construction, the project created employment for about 800 local residents, including women and young people. The project uses a wheeling arrangement to deliver power through Eskom's national grid to the mining customer's operational sites.
source.title: Voltalia commissions 148 MW Bolobedu solar farm in South Africa

source.summary: Waaree Energies Limited announced it secured a Letter of Award from SECI for a 700 MW solar project with 2,800 MWh energy storage in Solapur. The company stated the deal was received on August 27, 2026, and will be developed by its subsidiary Waaree Forever Energies Private Limited. The Power Purchase Agreement covers a 25-year tenure and the firm confirmed no related-party interests exist. This award strengthens Waaree Energies' position in large-scale renewable energy development.
source.title: Waaree Energies Wins SECI Contract for 700 MW Solar and Storage Project

source.summary: Five major Chinese solar manufacturers reported first-half losses due to persistent oversupply and weak prices. Longi, GCL Technology, and Daqo New Energy saw widening net losses, while TCL Zhonghuan and Xinte Energy showed signs of stabilization. The companies cited low capacity utilization and high silver costs as key factors. Strategic shifts toward overseas sales and diversification are underway, though broad profitability recovery remains unmaterialized.
source.title: Five Chinese solar makers report H1 losses amid oversupply

source.summary: JA announces the Journey Ahead: JA Roadshow 2026 to demonstrate its expanding energy ecosystem across Europe. The initiative will highlight battery energy storage systems and various photovoltaic technologies including the DeepBlue 5.0 and HyperGen modules. The tour begins in Poland on September 2 and will visit multiple countries throughout the year. JA aims to position itself as an integrated energy solutions provider by combining generation, storage, and management innovations.
source.title: JA launches 2026 European roadshow to showcase integrated energy solutions

source.summary: Jackery has launched the HomePower 1000 Plus v2, a portable battery designed for home, outdoor, and worksite use. The device features 1.024 kWh of storage and supports up to five 2 kWh expansion packs. It utilizes cell-to-pack construction with LFP cells to achieve a rugged, lightweight design measuring 12.4 inches by 7.9 inches by 9.2 inches. Power output increases to 1800 W continuous and 3600 W peak across four AC outlets. The battery includes a 5-year warranty and offers multiple charging options, including AC and DC inputs. Jackery states the unit can charge to 80% in 36 minutes via AC power. The article notes the MSRP starts at $749, with promotional pricing available. The author tested the unit by running appliances like a window air conditioner and dishwasher.
source.title: Jackery launches expandable HomePower 1000 Plus v2 battery

source.summary: Apple alleges that former senior system electrical engineer Chang Liu accessed a power converter circuit schematic while working at OpenAI. The company claims Liu used this proprietary information to train an AI agent in March 2026. Apple states this new evidence emerged from a MacBook provided to the company on August 21. Consequently, Apple is asking a U.S. federal court to expedite discovery proceedings in its trade secret case against OpenAI, which has sought to dismiss the lawsuit.
source.title: Apple alleges former engineer accessed circuit plans at OpenAI

source.summary: Federal regulators and 22 state attorneys general sued Amazon on Monday, alleging the company secretly overcharged advertisers by manipulating auction bids. The complaint claims Amazon deceived 1.2 million brands and sellers to pocket tens of billions of dollars. Amazon responded by arguing the lawsuit misrepresented its ad auction reality and cherry-picked findings. This marks the third major federal lawsuit against the company in recent years.
source.title: Federal regulators sue Amazon over alleged ad price manipulation

source.summary: The FTC and 22 U.S. states sued Amazon alleging the company illegally raised ad prices without advertiser knowledge. The lawsuit claims Amazon generated over $20 billion in profits at the expense of customers. Amazon denied wrongdoing, stating its policies aim to show relevant ads and that average costs remained flat. The agency seeks tens of billions in damages while Amazon reported a 26% rise in ad sales for the second quarter.
source.title: FTC and 22 states sue Amazon over alleged illegal ad price hikes

source.summary: The authors report that a lack of cross-country labor mobility contributes to higher unemployment in the euro area. Their model suggests increasing mobility to US levels would reduce unemployment volatility by 28% and return over 1 million workers to the workforce.
source.title: Authors report higher labor mobility would reduce euro area unemployment volatility

source.summary: The authors report that their endogenous portfolio choice model shows US convenience yields fall during high sanction risk. Empirical analysis finds elevated geopolitical risk coincides with higher gold prices and 10-year Treasury yields. Official reserve compositions shift toward gold, with less US-aligned countries increasing holdings more.
source.title: Authors model how geopolitical risk shifts official reserves toward gold

source.summary: Union Electronics and IT Minister Ashwini Vaishnaw stated that India's semiconductor manufacturing sector could generate 50,000 to 60,000 direct jobs annually. He outlined the government's focus on building a foundation across chip design, fabrication, packaging, equipment, and materials under Semicon 1.0 and 2.0. Vaishnaw highlighted industry-linked skilling programmes to prepare students and workers for manufacturing environments. He noted that around 85,000 engineers have already been developed, while the sector may require 10 lakh engineers over the next decade.
source.title: Ashwini Vaishnaw Says Semiconductor Push Could Create 50,000–60,000 Direct Jobs Every Year

source.summary: President Donald Trump stated that communities resisting data centers will end up backwards and poor. He urged for data to reign during remarks made on Monday. A Bloomberg columnist noted that tech leaders are financially supporting the Trump administration. Meanwhile, Semafor's Ben Smith wrote that Democrats plan to subpoena Big Tech leaders in 2027.
source.title: Trump warns communities opposing data centers will become poor

source.summary: Japan intends to increase its defense spending to over $55 billion next year to acquire more drones and missiles. The government aims to deploy uncrewed weapons, including a new 3D-printed drone fleet, to counter threats from China, North Korea, and Russia. Beijing has criticized the plan as new militarism, while the budget represents a modest rise compared to South Korea and Taiwan. Officials note the increase may be too incremental to fully satisfy US demands.
source.title: Japan plans record $55 billion defense budget for drones and missiles

source.summary: Authorities confirmed three minors died in a Colombian military air strike targeting cocaine-trafficking rebels. President Abelardo de la Espriella intensified operations against armed groups following the deadliest attack since his inauguration. Human Rights Watch reported a rise in child recruitment, noting social media platforms may have promoted content encouraging minors to join rebel factions. Meta and TikTok stated they prohibit violence-promoting content and removed flagged accounts.
source.title: Three minors killed in Colombian military strike on armed group

source.summary: Brand Finance named Amul the world's strongest dairy brand in 2026. The Indian cooperative scored 93 out of 100 on the Brand Strength Index and received an AAA+ rating, beating global rivals Yili, Vinamilk, and Valio.
source.title: Amul named world's strongest dairy brand in 2026

source.summary: The Jerusalem Daily reports that Israeli forces attacked journalists and a child died in an airstrike. The article also notes Ben-Gvir released an AI video of detainees.
source.title: Israeli forces attack journalists and kill a child in Gaza

source.summary: A reader posted a request for advice regarding a Yerevan bleg. The text contains no further details or sources. No specific information about the bleg was provided in the article.
source.title: Reader requests advice on Yerevan bleg

source.summary: The authors report that Uphold allows users to trade over 250 cryptocurrencies, four precious metals, and dozens of national currencies within a single account. The platform utilizes an anything-to-anything model to facilitate direct asset swaps without intermediate cash conversions. However, the review notes that this wide selection results in higher all-in prices due to spread-based pricing rather than separate commissions. While the service offers real-time proof of reserves and FDIC coverage up to $2.5 million for idle cash, it lacks advanced trading tools and does not support stocks or ETFs. The article highlights that Uphold is licensed in 42 U.S. states but excludes eight others, including New York. Additionally, the platform agreed to a $5 million settlement in April 2026 regarding misleading promotions of a third-party product. The authors conclude that while Uphold simplifies asset management for casual investors, its fee structure and limited regulatory footprint may deter active traders.
source.title: Uphold review 2026: One account for crypto, metals, and cash

source.summary: Algerian President Abdelmadjid Tebboune ordered the restoration of the death penalty for deliberately setting forest fires following a deadly wave of blazes. State television reported that the directive was issued during a high-level meeting attended by senior officials. The justice minister is instructed to submit a penal code amendment by September 15. Any death sentence will only be carried out after all legal appeals are exhausted. Tebboune also ordered immediate compensation for victims and the rapid restoration of essential services.
source.title: Algeria restores death penalty for deliberate forest fires after deadly blazes

source.summary: Belgium's Foreign Minister Maxime Prevot warned US Ambassador Bill White that further public remarks targeting Belgian politicians could escalate bilateral relations. Prevot stated such statements from an ambassador cannot be tolerated and must respect diplomatic customs. White posted an AI-generated image criticizing Health Minister Frank Vandenbroucke regarding alcohol health warnings. The dispute arose after Belgium changed alcohol warning requirements, prompting brewers to campaign against the new wording. White described the subsequent meeting as productive but did not apologize for his comments.
source.title: Belgium warns US ambassador remarks could escalate bilateral ties

source.summary: Swiss police arrested a 43-year-old man following a shooting at a rave in Aarau that killed 22-year-old Maria Spinelli. Authorities confirmed the suspect was apprehended shortly before 01:00 local time on Monday. Police stated the perpetrator likely acted alone while the investigation into the motive continues. Several others were injured, and Italian officials are monitoring the case.
source.title: Swiss police arrest man after rave shooting killed Italian woman

source.summary: The article presents a video tour of Lhasa that examines the city's mix of historic culture and contemporary development. Viewers see modern roads and tunnels alongside visits to the Tibet Museum and the traditional Barkhor Street.
source.title: A video tour explores Lhasa's blend of ancient traditions and modern infrastructure

source.summary: The United States attacked Iranian rocket launchers on an island in the Strait of Hormuz on Sunday, prompting Tehran to retaliate. Iran's Revolutionary Guard Corps reported casualties from the strikes and said its forces attacked U.S. military targets in Jordan. Meanwhile, the UAE stated it dealt with a drone coming from Iran over its waters. Oil prices jumped more than $1 a barrel on Monday as the conflict in West Asia extended into its sixth month.
source.title: UAE claims it intercepted a drone from Iran over its waters

source.summary: Brazilian authorities are processing over 90,000 Cuban refugee applications, surpassing Venezuelan claims as living conditions deteriorate on the island. The Jesuit Service for Migrants and Refugees reports Cubans now account for about 85% of those assisted by the organization. Most migrants travel through Guyana to Boa Vista, where they gain access to healthcare and education while awaiting individual case reviews. Unlike Venezuelans, Cubans do not qualify for expedited processing because Brazil does not classify Cuba as a country with widespread human rights violations. Many arrive with pre-arranged jobs in southern cities like Curitiba, which migrants jokingly call the new Miami. While some seek medical treatment unavailable in Cuba, others find work quickly despite language barriers.
source.title: Cubans surge to top of Brazil asylum claims amid Caribbean crisis

source.summary: The Treasury warns that Australia risks missing out on artificial intelligence economic benefits unless businesses make significant operational changes. Fewer than 10 per cent of Australian businesses report significant AI adoption, with officials noting the feared jobs shock has not yet materialised. Treasurer Jim Chalmers expressed confidence that Australia can maximise economic upside while minimising risks. The Treasury states that realising productivity gains requires investment in organisational capital and workforce skills. Deputy Prime Minister Richard Marles is travelling to the US to meet with major technology companies regarding national security and emerging technologies.
source.title: Australia risks missing AI economic boom due to slow business adoption

source.summary: Indian Prime Minister Narendra Modi and Russian President Vladimir Putin are scheduled to meet in Bishkek on Monday during the SCO summit. The discussion addresses how India-Russia relations endure despite Western sanctions and US pressure regarding Russian oil purchases. Former ambassador Meera Shankar stated that India's strategic partnership with Russia serves national goals rather than opposing the US. Energy ties have deepened as discounted Russian oil became vital after Gulf disruptions, though India aims to diversify sources long-term. Defense cooperation is shifting as India reduces dependence on Russian hardware and seeks indigenous production capabilities. Experts note Russia's growing reliance on China limits its ability to balance Beijing for India. Professor C Raja Mohan describes India's approach as an 'America plus' strategy, prioritizing US partnership while engaging other powers. Professor Rajan Kumar expects Putin to seek assurance of continued engagement from Modi. The upcoming BRICS summit in Delhi will further test whether political continuity translates into trade and defense progress.
source.title: Modi and Putin meet in Bishkek to test India-Russia ties amid global pressure

source.summary: London's Notting Hill Carnival started its 60th anniversary with the traditional J'ouvert parade on Sunday. Organisers expect millions of visitors over the three-day event celebrating Caribbean culture. The festivities featured participants covered in oil and paint dancing through the streets. The event highlights six decades of Caribbean heritage and community in the British capital.
source.title: London's Notting Hill Carnival begins 60th anniversary with J'ouvert parade

source.summary: A jury of nine women and three men continues deliberating in the murder trial of Lindsay Clancy, a 36-year-old former nurse charged with killing her three children in Massachusetts. Her legal team argues she acted under postpartum psychosis, while prosecutors claim she made an intentional decision knowing right from wrong. The jury must choose between five verdicts, ranging from not guilty to first-degree murder. A not guilty verdict is considered unlikely, whereas a finding of not guilty by reason of insanity would likely result in hospital detention rather than prison. Conviction for first-degree murder carries a mandatory life sentence without parole, requiring jurors to view Clancy as a monster. Second-degree murder also carries a life sentence but allows for parole, while manslaughter offers a maximum of 20 years per count. Legal experts note the case hinges on whether Clancy's mental illness prevented her from understanding her actions.
source.title: Jury deliberates options in Lindsay Clancy murder trial

source.summary: Nepal's Independent Power Producers Association criticized the government's initial delay in accepting international aid for flood relief. The disaster has killed 903 people and left 4,247 missing, including 85 Americans. While the finance minister denied rejecting foreign assistance, industry leaders stated Nepal lacks the necessary technology for complex rescues. Consequently, the government eventually approved teams from China, India, and Australia to assist in locating and saving workers trapped in nine blocked hydropower tunnels.
source.title: Nepal private sector pressures government to accept foreign flood rescue help

source.summary: Claire Valdez and Darializa Ávila Chevalier, both Latina candidates endorsed by Mayor Zohran Mamdani, are running for Congress in New York as Democratic Socialists of America members. The Indypendent reports that these fresh faces, coming from backgrounds as community organizers and artists, aim to create a new era of Latino socialist politics. They emphasize abolishing ICE and addressing the high cost of living, drawing on personal experiences with low wages and medical debt. The article notes that the DSA has grown significantly during the Trump era, with over 100,000 members across nearly 200 chapters. While facing criticism from the establishment and some mainstream Democrats, the candidates argue that the Democratic Party must offer humane immigration reform to lead. Diana Moreno, another candidate, states that the party must create a solution to the immigration problem rather than focusing solely on ICE. The group seeks to expand democracy through universal programs like healthcare and childcare, distinguishing their approach from authoritarianism.
source.title: New York Latino socialists seek to lead Democrats on immigration

source.summary: Prime Minister Balendra Shah faces a severe crisis as deadly floods kill over 900 people and leave nearly 4,800 missing in Nepal. Authorities report that rescue efforts have entered a sixth day while hundreds of workers remain trapped in buried tunnels. The administration admitted initial confusion but praised security agencies for helicopter rescues. However, experts criticize the federal government for acting alone without involving local or provincial authorities. Former officials note delays in accepting international help from China and India cost crucial time. Despite these challenges, over 5 billion Nepali rupees have been collected for relief, showing public trust in the new leadership.
source.title: Nepal floods test PM Balen's inexperienced government during deadly disaster

source.summary: The provided text contains a headline stating Spain's Sanchez rules out Morocco's responsibility for the migrant surge, but the article body failed to load due to technical issues.
source.title: Spain's Sanchez rules out Morocco's responsibility for migrant surge

source.summary: The Trump administration announced a new partnership with Venezuela to develop oil reserves, with the U.S. receiving 55% of the estimated 65 billion barrels. An anonymous official stated the deal aims to lower gas prices, though experts remain skeptical. Meanwhile, a new investigation by NPR and Boston University researchers reveals that heat-related deaths in the U.S. are nearly five times higher than official estimates. The study involved fieldwork in Arizona, California, and Washington to understand why these deaths go uncounted. Officials noted the deal could undermine Venezuela's sovereignty, while the heat report highlights the vulnerability of communities in extreme temperatures.
source.title: U.S., Venezuela strike oil deal. And, the staggering hidden toll of U.S. heat deaths

source.summary: Yuko Nishikawa has installed a galaxy of multicolored discs at Tokyo's Trunk(Hotel) Cat Street. The sculptural forms are made from discarded photo studio backgrounds pulped with bookbinding glue. The installation, titled Chromonaut, remains on view until Sept. 8. Nishikawa stated that she is interested in the transformation of materials that already contain a story.
source.title: Yuko Nishikawa creates Chromonaut installation from discarded studio materials

source.summary: A monthlong effort to consolidate Japan's centrist opposition parties has effectively collapsed. Komeito-affiliated lawmakers in the Centrist Reform Alliance decided not to merge after the Constitutional Democratic Party of Japan abandoned its merger plans last week. Leaders of the three parties met Monday evening to discuss future relations. CRA head Junya Ogawa stated their resolve to defend centrist politics has not weakened and proposed creating a new framework for a fresh start.
source.title: Japan centrist opposition merger plan collapses after CDP withdrawal

source.summary: Photojournalist Suman Nepali documented the devastating floods in Nepal on August 27, 2026, describing scenes of destruction and human suffering. The reporter noted that five-year-old Kirti Tamang survived the flood but cannot speak, while another boy, Biswas Tamang, was found with severe bruises. Nepali stated that the tragedy was too large for relief organizations to tackle and noted the absence of young men in villages due to migration. A survivor told the reporter there was no warning before the flood arrived. The article highlights the loss of homes and family members, with Nepali expressing that the event changed his outlook on life. Army trucks and helicopters arrived to deliver supplies while pilgrims continued their journey to a festival.
source.title: Photojournalist Suman Nepali witnesses Nepal floods and survivor trauma

source.summary: India's GDP grew 7.8% in the April-June 2026 quarter, outpacing last year's 6.9% but falling short of the previous quarter's 8.6%. Prime Minister Narendra Modi and Finance Minister Nirmala Sitharaman credited the growth to domestic resilience and government reforms. The manufacturing sector drove expansion with a 9.2% rise, while the primary sector lagged due to mining contraction. Chief Economic Adviser V. Anantha Nageswaran highlighted continued economic resilience supported by high-frequency indicators. However, economists warn that a deficient monsoon and El Niño conditions may slow future growth.
source.title: India GDP grows 7.8% in Q1, led by manufacturing and services

source.summary: A 68-year-old cab driver named R.A. Babu died after a GBA garbage truck allegedly struck his motorcycle in Yeshwantpur on Monday morning. Police stated the truck was being driven at high speed when it hit the two-wheeler from behind. The driver lost control and fell, after which the truck ran over him, causing fatal injuries. Authorities have registered a case and taken the truck driver into custody for further investigation.
source.title: GBA garbage truck driver arrested after killing elderly cab driver in Bengaluru

source.summary: Ireland's grid-scale solar farms generated 1,101 GWh of electricity in 2025, a 51% increase from 2024, according to the Central Statistics Office. Solar surpassed 1 GW generation in April 2026, meeting needs for 500,000 customers. Connected solar capacity is expected to exceed 3.3 GW by 2026. The highest solar generation peak was 1.26 GW on 11 August 2026, contributing a third of national electricity use. Wind accounted for 40% of total generation, with 11,782 GWh produced in 2025. Renewables curtailment wasted enough wind energy to power 667,000 homes in 2026's first half. Gas remained the largest energy source at 47%, while coal generation dropped 52%. The CSO noted its data excludes rooftop solar and other auto producers.
source.title: Ireland's grid-scale solar generation rises 51% in 2025

source.summary: Raafe Khan of Camelot Energy Group outlines the financial and market challenges facing long-duration energy storage (LDES) projects. He highlights the economic disconnect between the cost of extending storage duration and the revenue generated in current market structures, using PJM's capacity pricing and BloombergNEF's cost curves as examples. Khan argues that the market remains dominated by four-hour systems due to poor economic returns for longer durations. He also discusses the role of captive batteries in data centers, emphasizing their value in accelerating interconnection timelines rather than energy arbitrage. Khan identifies structural drivers like solar and wind buildout as key to battery storage growth, while cautioning about unpriced risks in cost decline assumptions. He advocates for capacity market reforms, including multi-year commitments and aligned duration accreditation, to support LDES deployment. Additionally, he notes the evolving role of merchant batteries and the importance of optimization strategies in a competitive market.
source.title: Raafe Khan analyzes financial challenges and market dynamics for long-duration energy storage

source.summary: The Center for Rural Affairs has released a fact sheet to assist farmers and landowners in navigating the leasing process for renewable energy projects. The guide outlines steps from initial developer consultations to decommissioning, emphasizing the importance of clear communication and long-term commitment. Laura Priest, a policy associate, noted that marginal agricultural land can be ideal for such projects, offering predictable income. The document advises landowners to seek professional guidance and ask detailed questions before entering agreements.
source.title: Center for Rural Affairs offers guide on renewable energy land leasing for farmers

source.summary: Core Power and the US Maritime Administration signed a Memorandum of Cooperation to develop nuclear propulsion for commercial shipping. The agreement aims to create a commercial pathway by addressing regulatory, operational, and financial challenges. Core Power emphasizes the need for a complete system that is safe, licensable, and operable at fleet scale. The collaboration follows a Request for Information on system-centric nuclear power approaches. The initiative seeks to position the US as a global maritime power, leveraging its nuclear expertise and allied shipbuilding capacity. The partnership also aligns with the US government's strategy to strengthen maritime dominance and energy security.
source.title: Core Power and US Maritime Administration collaborate on nuclear propulsion for commercial shipping

source.summary: TC Energy has appointed Worley to advance the development of its 1GW/11GWh Ontario Pumped Storage Project. The project, which includes collaboration with EllisDon and AECOM, will follow TC Energy’s Hire and Buy Local Programme. Ontario’s government began pre-development work in January 2025, investing up to CA$285 million. The system will pump water from Georgian Bay to generate low-cost electricity during peak demand. TC Energy initially proposed the project in 2019 with a US$3.25 billion estimate, but construction remained pending provincial approval. Ontario’s energy minister requested further analysis of pumped hydro’s benefits before proceeding.
source.title: TC Energy partners with Worley to develop Ontario's 1GW pumped hydro storage project

source.summary: NTPC Renewable Energy Limited secured 500 MW under SECI’s FDRE-IX tender at ₹6/kWh, securing one-third of the total capacity. POWERGRID invited bids for a 265 MW/530 MWh BESS project in Haryana, aiming to enhance grid flexibility. India’s renewable generation reached 38,497 MU in July 2026, with solar and wind contributing 96.14%. REC transferred Luhri SPV to Terralight for ₹14.13 crore. OREDA invited empanelment for rooftop solar in Odisha, while POWERGRID won a ₹822.91 crore Gujarat RE transmission project. KELTRON sought partners for solar and street light projects across North and East India.
source.title: NTPC REL wins 500 MW renewable tender, POWERGRID expands storage projects

source.summary: Cube Green Energy has appointed Dr Felix Grolman as Executive Chair, effective August 1, 2026, to lead the company's expansion of renewable energy and storage projects across Europe. Grolman, with over 15 years of experience in renewable energy, previously led VSB Group, which was acquired by TotalEnergies. His appointment follows the hiring of Moritz von Plate as CEO in May 2026. The move aligns with European energy policies focused on security and grid resilience. Cube Green Energy currently operates 280 MW of renewable assets and has a 1.8 GW development pipeline. The company aims to leverage its grid infrastructure and technology platform to support further growth in renewable energy and storage solutions across Europe.
source.title: Cube Green Energy Appoints Dr Felix Grolman as Executive Chair to Drive European Renewable Energy Growth

source.summary: Thornova Solar, a U.S.-focused subsidiary of China's Sunova Solar, is establishing a new division called Nextnova to manufacture silicon solar cells in Oklahoma. The facility, located in a former Xerox building in Yukon, will produce p-type cells with an initial capacity of 2 GW, expandable to 6 GW. The company expects mass production to begin in Q1 2027, supporting 300 jobs. Nextnova emphasizes transparent sourcing and scalable production. Thornova currently operates a facility in Kenya and has 2.5 GW of production capacity in Indonesia, using U.S. OEMs for American manufacturing. Details on sales and assembly locations for Nextnova cells were not provided.
source.title: Thornova Solar Establishes Nextnova Division for U.S. Solar Cell Production in Oklahoma

source.summary: Greece added 724 MW of solar power in May, bringing total renewable installations to 18,317 MW, according to DAPEEP. The country aims for a new annual record of 4 GW in renewables, surpassing the 2024 total of 2.73 GW. Despite curtailments and negative wholesale prices, investments continue, with solar producers facing up to 80% income loss. Greece's first standalone energy storage units reached 600 MW, with plans to expand to 1.5 GW by 2027. The nation remains a net exporter of electricity, with a EUR 438 million surplus in the first six months. DAPEEP reported a EUR 53.48 million deficit in the renewable energy account for May, mainly due to older plants receiving subsidies.
source.title: Greece installs 724 MW solar in May amid curtailments and low prices

source.summary: The U.S. Department of Energy's National Reactor Innovation Center (NRIC) has selected 13 new projects across 12 companies for its Nuclear Energy Launch Pad initiative, expanding support for advanced nuclear technologies. These projects span microreactor developers, enrichment startups, fuel fabrication firms, and isotope producers, marking the first major round since the program opened to broader industry applications in late April. The initiative aims to provide federal support for advanced nuclear deployment, including siting, infrastructure, and regulatory pathways. Selected companies include Antares Nuclear, Atlas Atomics, Deployable Energy, Forge Atomics, and others, each with distinct technologies and goals. The DOE emphasized that the program offers a prioritized authorization pathway, not federal funding, and that developers remain responsible for financing their projects. The selections highlight a growing interest in advancing nuclear technologies through federal collaboration and regulatory support.
source.title: DOE Selects 13 Projects for Nuclear Energy Launch Pad Expansion

source.summary: The Victorian government has launched Australia's first offshore wind auction, inviting bids for renewable energy projects. The initiative aims to boost clean energy production and meet climate targets. Bidders must submit proposals by a specified deadline. The auction is part of a broader strategy to transition to sustainable energy sources. The government emphasized the importance of renewable energy in reducing carbon emissions.
source.title: Victoria Government Initiates Australia's First Offshore Wind Auction

source.summary: Glamox Marine Lighting has been selected to supply lighting solutions for the Formosa 4 offshore wind farm in Taiwan. The project aims to enhance visibility and safety in the marine environment. The company's expertise in maritime lighting systems is highlighted as a key factor in the decision. The wind farm is expected to contribute significantly to Taiwan's renewable energy goals. The contract underscores Glamox's role in supporting offshore energy infrastructure.
source.title: Glamox Provides Lighting for Formosa 4 Offshore Wind Farm

source.summary: Avantus, a US-based energy company, has secured a $300 million tax equity commitment from Truist Bank for the Aratina 2 solar and battery storage project in Kern County, California. This follows $525 million in construction financing from CIBC, BBVA, and Santander. The project, set to begin operations by late 2026, will provide 150MW of solar generation and 452MWh of storage, enough to power 75,000 homes annually. Avantus has signed 15-year power purchase agreements with Southern California Edison. The project is the second phase of the Aratina Solar Center, with the first phase already operational. Avantus aims to add 788MW of solar and storage capacity by 2026, with over 24GW in its development pipeline.
source.title: Avantus secures $300m tax equity for Aratina 2 solar storage project

source.summary: ArcLight Capital Partners has invested $1bn to establish Anchor Point Transmission, an independent company focused on US power grid infrastructure. The initiative aims to address growing demand from electrification, manufacturing, and AI computing, requiring significant investment in high-voltage transmission. Anchor Point will partner with utilities to develop new transmission assets, led by Justin Campbell and Michael Deggendorf. ArcLight, with over 70GW of energy assets, emphasized its capability to support utilities in meeting evolving customer needs. The company also recently acquired a 50% stake in a 5.4GW power generation portfolio.
source.title: ArcLight creates $1bn transmission company to support US power grid

source.summary: U.S. petroleum exports reached a record 13.6 million barrels per day in April, driven by increased global demand due to disruptions through the Strait of Hormuz. Crude oil exports averaged 5.6 million b/d, up 21% from December 2023. Propane and distillate fuel oil also saw record or near-record levels. Finished petroleum products exports remained high despite average motor gasoline exports. Weekly estimates show crude, distillate fuel, jet fuel, and propane exports stayed above five-year seasonal highs in May and June.
source.title: U.S. petroleum exports hit record 13.6 million barrels per day in April

source.summary: Safegrid, part of G&W Electric Company, will showcase its Intelligent Grid System at T&D World Live 2026. The solution uses field sensors and data analytics to detect and predict faults in distribution and transmission networks. It identifies abnormal patterns indicating equipment issues, enabling proactive maintenance. The system also provides accurate fault location using GPS time-synchronized measurements. Utilities are using it to address challenges like failing cable terminations and vegetation-related faults. The demonstration highlights a shift from reactive to proactive grid management, aiming to improve reliability and reduce outage duration.
source.title: Safegrid Demonstrates Predictive Fault Intelligence for Grid Management

source.summary: R.M. Young Company and Western Weather Group are offering a free Wind Monitor at T&D World Live. Attendees can visit Booth 419 to answer a weather-related trivia question for a chance to win the $1,249.00 device. The companies, who have partnered for over 20 years, are co-exhibiting for the first time, showcasing their weather instrumentation and expertise. Visitors can also learn about their collaborative solutions for utility and weather-monitoring professionals. Advance reservations are recommended for one-on-one meetings with the teams.
source.title: R.M. Young and Western Weather Group Offer Free Wind Monitor at T&D World Live

source.summary: BMW is launching two new electric models in China, including the long-wheelbase Neue Klasse iX3 electric SUV, priced between 269,900 and 339,900 yuan. The company began pre-sales at the 2026 Chengdu Motor Show, with deliveries set for November. The iX3, which has seen 100,000 orders in Europe since 2025, faces stiff competition in China, where local electric vehicles offer high value for money. BMW aims to reverse declining sales in the world's largest auto market, though success remains uncertain due to intense competition.
source.title: BMW Introduces China-Exclusive Electric SUV to Boost Sales

source.summary: Sage Geosystems has launched its first next-generation geothermal plant in Texas, marking a significant milestone for the sector. The 3-megawatt pilot plant, operational since April 2026, has performed reliably after over 120 days of grid-connected operations. The company said the results will inform its upcoming collaboration with Ormat Technologies in Nevada, a precursor to its deal with Meta for 150 MW of geothermal power. Sage’s enhanced geothermal system involves drilling into hot rocks and fracturing them to create water pockets for power generation, differing from traditional geothermal methods. The plant has shown promising water retention, with less than 10% loss, which could improve efficiency for future projects. Sage plans to begin drilling at Ormat’s Nevada plant later this year, aiming to scale up and develop 150 MW of next-gen geothermal power by 2028.
source.title: Sage Geosystems launches first next-gen geothermal plant in Texas

source.summary: Qcells' Georgia factory, which produces solar panel components, faces challenges from fluctuating U.S. solar policies. The plant, which began full production in June, represents a major step toward domestic solar manufacturing. China has dominated the global market, but the U.S. seeks to reduce reliance on foreign imports. The Trump administration's new tariffs and import restrictions aim to boost domestic production, while the Biden-era Inflation Reduction Act offered tax incentives. Policy changes have created uncertainty for companies like Qcells, which invested billions in its facility. Analysts note that while the U.S. solar industry may eventually shift to domestic production, short-term policy instability and limited supply could increase costs for developers. Despite these challenges, solar remains a cost-effective energy source, with experts predicting continued growth in solar deployment.
source.title: Qcells' Georgia factory navigates U.S. solar policy shifts

source.summary: Siemens has partnered with the Electric Power Group (EPG) to develop an intelligent grid management solution. The alliance combines Siemens' grid automation expertise with EPG's analytics capabilities, focusing on enhancing grid resilience. The technology integrates EPG's synchrophasor and Wide Area Monitoring Systems with Siemens' power automation tools to provide real-time grid visibility. This collaboration addresses challenges posed by the energy transition, including variable renewable generation and dynamic loads. EPG's technology uses high-speed, time-synchronised data to offer precise measurements of grid behaviour. The joint solution is expected to improve grid stability, enable faster fault detection, and enhance situational awareness for operators. Bernd Meyer of Siemens highlighted the importance of the collaboration for a resilient, self-optimising grid. Vikram Budhraja of EPG noted the scalable and interoperable design of the WAMS architecture for global deployment.
source.title: Siemens and EPG alliance aims to improve grid resilience through advanced monitoring technology

source.summary: Faisal Mohd of Envision Energy Australia argues that conventional battery energy storage system (BESS) degradation guarantees, which impose strict operational limits, hinder asset owners from maximizing project value. These guarantees often restrict how batteries can be operated, limiting flexibility when market conditions change. For example, batteries may need to operate at higher states of charge or cycle more frequently to capture revenue opportunities, but doing so could void warranties or accelerate degradation. Recent data shows grid-scale batteries in Australia's National Electricity Market (NEM) capture only 38% of their theoretical maximum revenue. Mohd suggests that current 'flexible' degradation guarantees, which offer limited degradation buckets, do not account for changes in operational parameters like resting SoC or temperature. He advocates for more transparent, flexible guarantees that evolve with asset operation, allowing operators to optimize revenue without compromising long-term performance. Envision Energy's Forecastable Flexible Capacity Guarantee model aims to provide this transparency by linking operating behavior to battery health and efficiency over the project's lifetime.
source.title: Battery storage degradation guarantees limit project value due to rigid operational constraints

source.summary: Cummins has secured its largest battery energy storage system (BESS) order to date for a US data centre, aimed at managing electricity demand fluctuations from AI workloads. The system uses 5 MWh lithium iron phosphate battery blocks and liquid cooling, designed to meet utility requirements for rapid load management and grid stability. Cummins emphasized that the BESS supports data centres alongside diesel and natural gas power systems, positioning it as part of a broader power architecture for AI facilities. The project marks a shift for Cummins beyond traditional power generation, highlighting battery storage as a critical component for modern data centre resilience.
source.title: Cummins supplies largest BESS for US data centre to manage AI workload demand

source.summary: The Port of Corpus Christi has signed a memorandum of cooperation with the US Maritime Administration (MARAD) to explore nuclear maritime technologies, making it the second US port to formalise such a partnership. The initiative aims to advance maritime energy systems through small modular reactors (SMRs), resilient port microgrids, and infrastructure for emerging vessel propulsion concepts. The collaboration also includes a study with UK-based Core Power to assess floating nuclear power plants (FNPPs) and readiness for nuclear-powered commercial ships. The partners will examine technical, environmental, and regulatory requirements for FNPP deployment and safe operations of nuclear vessels. Core Power emphasized the study is a preliminary fact-finding exercise without committing to licensing or construction. The Port of Corpus Christi, as a major energy gateway, seeks to maintain its competitive edge in the evolving global energy marketplace through these efforts.
source.title: Port of Corpus Christi and MARAD partner on nuclear maritime tech exploration

source.summary: PJM Interconnection has proposed a new framework to manage growing data center demand, allowing large loads to enter service without securing full capacity upfront. The plan, called IRAS, would make uncovered load available for reduction during emergencies before using existing demand-response resources. The framework includes a Large Load Registry, a Bring Your Own New Capacity (BYONC) mechanism, and compensation for load reductions. PJM aims to implement the changes by 2027, as data center growth is projected to add 32 GW of demand by 2030. The proposal follows recent capacity shortages and aims to ensure reliability amid rising load and retiring generation. PJM also plans a Reliability Backstop Procurement to cover remaining capacity gaps, with costs allocated to load-serving entities and states.
source.title: PJM Introduces New Framework to Address Data Center Load Growth

source.summary: A study by Jonathan Hall, Jason Hicks, Morris M. Kleiner, and Yun taek Oh examines whether occupational licensing enhances service quality and safety for Uber drivers. Using trip-level data, the researchers compare trips by licensed and unlicensed drivers in New York City, New Jersey, and post-deregulation Houston. They find no consistent evidence that licensing improves consumer outcomes. In Houston, new entrants after deregulation perform similarly to previously licensed drivers in ratings and driving behavior, despite differences in experience and age. The study uses quasi-random assignment and instrumental variable estimates to analyze the impact of licensing.
source.title: Uber Driver Licensing Study Finds No Consistent Improvement in Service Quality or Safety

source.summary: Olivier Wang decomposes stock returns into a Treasury component linked to monetary policy surprises and a payoff component. Risk and returns for stocks increase less with duration compared to matched Treasuries. Stock volatility is reduced by rate insurance, where rates fall in bad times, offsetting payoff risk. Expected stock returns are dampened as rates rise in good times, hedging losses for investors holding net duration, particularly when Ricardian equivalence fails. The framework explains bond premia, negative stock-bond covariance, equity anomalies, and the collapse of the value premium, suggesting fiscal and monetary policy influence bond and equity premia. It also proposes a two-factor model for pricing stocks and bonds together, and explains why long bonds outperform long stocks.
source.title: Stock Returns Decomposed with Rate Insurance Framework

source.summary: Ross Stores increased its 2026 earnings per share forecast to $8.61-$8.77, citing a 13% sales rise to $6.3bn and 47 new store openings. The company reported net income of $851m and operating profits of $1.1bn, with tariff refunds contributing to a 610 basis point margin increase. CEO Jim Conroy highlighted customer traffic and store expansion as key drivers, raising the 2026 new store target to 115 locations. For Q3 and Q4, Ross expects comparable sales growth of 6-7% and 4-5%, respectively, with EPS projections of $1.75-$1.83 and $2.17-$2.26.
source.title: Ross Stores boosts 2026 earnings forecast due to Q2 sales growth and store expansion

source.summary: President Donald Trump sold up to $25 million of Vanguard Dividend Appreciation ETF (VIG) in June 2026, while holding Schwab U.S. Dividend Equity ETF (SCHD). VIG's performance lagged behind SCHD's 30% year-to-date gain. Trump also bought Fidelity National Information Services (FIS), Home Depot (HD), and the Technology Select Sector SPDR ETF (XLK). SCHD outperformed the S&P 500 due to its energy holdings and exclusion of AI mega-caps. The report notes the filing only provides a range for the sale and no rationale for the transaction.
source.title: Trump Just Dumped Over $5 Million Of A Popular Dividend ETF. Here’s What It Means For VIG and SCHD

source.summary: The Netherlands' public broadcaster, AVROTROS, will skip next year's Eurovision Song Contest, citing the event's 'no longer neutral' status due to conflicts over the Gaza war. Director-General Taco Zimmerman stated that international conflicts are undermining the contest's neutrality. The decision follows recent boycotts by several countries over Israel's participation, with five nations pulling out this year. Next year's contest will be held in Burgas, Bulgaria, following Dara's victory. This year's event saw a 35 million viewer drop compared to last year.
source.title: Netherlands broadcaster withdraws from Eurovision over perceived loss of neutrality

source.summary: US Treasury Secretary Scott Bessent warned Iran of an 'economic D-Day' to sever all financial ties, threatening to isolate any nation partnering with the country. Iran dismissed the comments, vowing to shut down oil exports if the conflict continues. The Strait of Hormuz, a critical oil route, has been effectively blocked by Iran since February. Bessent's remarks followed previous US threats, including Trump's April warning of a 'civilisation dying' unless Iran unblocked the strait. The US has imposed tough sanctions on Iran since 2018, after pulling out of the 2015 nuclear deal. Biden's attempts to reinstate the deal failed, and recent sanctions targeted foreign firms doing business with Tehran.
source.title: US Treasury Secretary warns of economic D-Day against Iran

source.summary: Creditors of Thames Water, led by London & Valley Water, have proposed a board overhaul to avoid nationalisation. The plan includes appointing Liz Barber, Clive Selley, and Dame Bernadette Kelly as directors, with Mike McTighe becoming chair. The consortium aims to reassure the government that a commercial deal would bring leadership changes. Critics, including We Own It, accuse the plan of being a 'deckchair shuffle' that ignores public interests. The proposal comes amid concerns over rising water bills and potential government intervention through a special administration regime.
source.title: Creditors propose board overhaul for Thames Water to avoid nationalisation

source.summary: The Trump administration is escalating economic pressure on Iran with 'toughest sanctions in history,' aiming to isolate Tehran through a naval blockade and financial restrictions. Treasury Secretary Scott Bessent warned that any country engaging in trade with Iran will face severe consequences. Iran's Foreign Ministry condemned the measures as an 'erosion of sovereignty,' while Supreme National Security Council secretary Mohsen Rezaei warned of 'seismic' retaliation against nations joining the sanctions. Analysts note that China and Russia, key trading partners of Iran, may resist U.S. pressure due to their limited reliance on the American financial system. Gulf states remain divided on whether to support U.S. sanctions, fearing regional instability if Iran collapses.
source.title: US threatens economic sanctions against Iran, Iran vows retaliation

source.summary: Canadian and US businesses are facing significant challenges due to escalating trade tensions between the two nations. The imposition of 50% tariffs on each other's products has raised concerns among business owners, with many fearing a decline in sales and potential closures. Cindy Baldassi, a Calgary-based jeweler, warns that half her business could be lost due to increased costs. Canadian Prime Minister Mark Carney announced tariffs on US goods starting September 8, while US tariffs on Canadian products took effect immediately. Business owners like Michael Saifer of Lind Furniture and Matteo Sgaramella of Outclass are struggling to navigate the new economic landscape, with small businesses particularly vulnerable. The impact extends beyond trade, affecting companies like Paloma Clothing and Terre Rouge Wines, which face higher costs and reduced market access. Heather Seevers of Northwest Yarns and Mercantile reports a drop in Canadian customers and increased community support efforts to sustain her business amid the trade war.
source.title: Canadian and US businesses brace for trade war fallout

source.summary: A study by Daniel Fernández-Kranz and Sébastien Fontenay finds that childhood exposure to joint custody reforms reduces adult fertility by 7 percent, affecting both men and women equally. The effect is primarily through reduced parenthood and couple formation, with sub-additive impacts within couples. Exposed individuals also tend to assortatively match. The research highlights the development of family preferences during childhood and links the US fertility decline to rising childlessness and declining couple formation.
source.title: Childhood Joint Custody Exposure Linked to Lower Adult Fertility

source.summary: The UK government must decide whether to approve oil and gas drilling at Rosebank and Jackdaw fields, with differing environmental and energy implications. The Conservative government previously granted licenses in 2022 and 2023, but a court ruled their environmental assessments were incomplete, failing to account for emissions from burning the extracted oil and gas. The new energy and climate secretary, Miatta Fahnbulleh, must assess if updated assessments justify approval. Jackdaw, a small gasfield, could contribute to energy security by displacing dirtier LNG imports, while Rosebank, a large oilfield, would generate significant emissions over 25 years, conflicting with net zero targets. The article argues that Rosebank should only be approved if it meets carbon capture and storage (CCS) conditions, a technology already used by Equinor. The government is also urged to accelerate decommissioning of aging fields and publish a net zero transition roadmap to address economic and climate concerns.
source.title: UK Government Faces Decision on Oil Drilling Conditions Amid Climate and Energy Pressures

source.summary: The Federal Reserve Board announced enforcement actions against Elazia Jones, a former employee of Regions Bank, related to check fraud. The action includes a consent prohibition. The board provided details on the enforcement measures taken. Additional actions are available for search. The announcement was released on August 13, 2026.
source.title: Federal Reserve Takes Enforcement Action Against Former Regions Bank Employee Over Check Fraud

source.summary: The Federal Reserve Board has approved Banco Santander, S.A. and Santander Holdings USA, Inc.'s application to acquire Webster Financial Corporation, which would indirectly lead to the acquisition of Webster Bank, National Association. The approval was announced on August 4, 2026. The transaction involves Banco Santander, based in Madrid, Spain, and Santander Holdings USA, based in Boston, Massachusetts. Webster Financial Corporation and Webster Bank are both based in Stamford, Connecticut.
source.title: Federal Reserve approves Santander's acquisition of Webster Financial

source.summary: The Federal Reserve outlined four guiding principles for modernizing financial regulation and supervision, emphasizing material risk prioritization, tailored oversight, transparency, and forward-looking approaches. These principles aim to enhance effectiveness while reducing regulatory burdens. The Fed highlighted reforms to the capital framework, including a risk-based approach and adjustments to global systemically important bank surcharges. It also introduced supervisory operating principles for greater transparency and updated asset thresholds to align with economic growth. The Fed is seeking public feedback on AI adoption practices and plans to publish a consultation report in the fall. The FSB will use these principles to guide international regulatory efforts, promoting flexibility and shared goals of financial stability and innovation.
source.title: Federal Reserve Outlines Principles for Modernizing Financial Regulation

source.summary: Federal Reserve Chair Bowman addressed the Financial Stability Board's (FSB) consultation report on sound practices for responsible AI adoption. The report, set for finalization as a U.S. G-20 deliverable, outlines governance and control measures for financial institutions using AI. Bowman emphasized the importance of understanding specific AI use cases and materiality in determining appropriate risk management strategies. The report promotes proportionality, noting that governance requirements should align with institutional size and complexity. Bowman encouraged feedback to refine the report's guidance, particularly regarding its applicability to institutions of varying risk profiles and the adequacy of its risk management frameworks.
source.title: Federal Reserve Chair Discusses AI Risk Management Practices in FSB Report
