source.summary: Mistral and HUMAIN announced a strategic collaboration to advance sovereign AI in Saudi Arabia and the Middle East. The partnership focuses on AI infrastructure, model development, and deployment, with initial emphasis on cybersecurity and voice technologies. They aim to create Arabic-language frontier models and explore HUMAIN’s data center infrastructure to meet local compute needs. The collaboration, valued in the hundreds of millions of Euros, seeks to provide organizations with control over data, models, and operations, supporting sectors like finance and cybersecurity. The partnership reflects a broader trend of combining local infrastructure with sovereign AI capabilities to enable innovation and operational autonomy.
source.title: Mistral x HUMAIN

source.summary: NVIDIA's Spectrum-X Ethernet is designed to overcome the limitations of traditional Ethernet in handling the synchronized, low-entropy traffic of large-scale AI training. Traditional Ethernet, which relies on static routing and congestion control, struggles with AI workloads due to hash collisions, packet loss, and slow congestion responses. Spectrum-X Ethernet introduces hardware-accelerated networking with Adaptive Routing and a Plane Load Balancer to dynamically manage traffic and isolate congestion. This architecture supports multiplane topologies, allowing massive scaling without the latency and cost issues of traditional multi-tier fabrics. Testing shows Spectrum-X maintains stable performance under congestion and multi-tenant conditions, offering faster failover and better bandwidth utilization compared to standard Ethernet. The system's design ensures predictable low latency and high fabric utilization, crucial for efficient AI training at scale.
source.title: NVIDIA's Spectrum-X Ethernet Addresses AI Networking Challenges

source.summary: NVLink Fusion allows custom XPUs to connect with NVIDIA's established AI infrastructure, enhancing performance and reducing time-to-market for semi-custom AI factories. The solution addresses the complexity of building AI factories by combining custom XPU design with mature infrastructure, including scale-up networking, rack-scale architecture, and a robust supplier ecosystem. Key benefits include improved performance through high-bandwidth, low-latency networking, reduced operational risk via proven technology stacks, and streamlined integration with NVIDIA's MGX architecture. The initiative supports a unified platform for diverse workloads, enabling hyperscalers and AI-native companies to build scalable, efficient AI systems without requiring full infrastructure development from scratch.
source.title: NVLink Fusion Enables Custom XPUs to Integrate with NVIDIA's AI Infrastructure

source.summary: NVIDIA is extending its Vera Rubin NVL72 platform with the full production of Groq 3 LPX, a new inference accelerator designed for agentic AI systems. In tests with Gemma 4 31B, the system achieved 3,400 output tokens per second for long-context use cases, 4x faster than alternatives. Partners like Nebius, CoreWeave, and SpaceXAI are adopting the technology to power agentic applications, with SpaceXAI using Vera Rubin CPUs for CPU-intensive tasks. NVIDIA emphasizes extreme codesign across compute, networking, and inference to optimize performance and throughput for large-scale, low-latency AI workloads. The company also introduced Spectrum-X Multiplane and Scale-In infrastructure to support growing AI factories, highlighting a shift toward integrated, efficient AI infrastructure for the agentic era.
source.title: NVIDIA Expands Vera Rubin with Groq 3 LPX for Agentic AI Inference

source.summary: NVIDIA has introduced BlueField-4, a new DPU (Data Processing Unit) designed to power Scale-In network infrastructure for agentic AI factories. This infrastructure accelerates secure access, data movement, and operations across AI compute systems. Traditional cloud infrastructure, built for predictable workloads, is insufficient for agentic AI, which requires high-bandwidth, multi-tenant networking and security. Scale-In transforms north-south networks into a unified, accelerated domain, using BlueField-4, NVIDIA DOCA, and Spectrum-X Ethernet. BlueField-4 provides host-independent processing, offloading security, storage, and networking tasks from host CPUs. It supports four infrastructure pillars: Scale-Up, Scale-Out, Scale-Across, and Context Memory, each addressing different AI factory needs. NVIDIA claims BlueField-4 offers 4x more memory bandwidth and 2x more network bandwidth than its predecessor, enabling more concurrent services and higher throughput. DOCA microservices and Spectrum-X Ethernet enable programmable, high-performance networking and storage, while BlueField Astra ensures consistent policy enforcement across both Scale-In and Scale-Out networks. The solution aims to provide secure, efficient, and scalable AI infrastructure for enterprise and cloud environments.
source.title: NVIDIA Introduces BlueField-4 for Secure, Scalable AI Infrastructure

source.summary: NIST researchers have developed larger superconducting nanowire single-photon detectors (SNSPDs) to improve photon detection. Traditional SNSPDs, which use nanoscale wires, face limitations in current capacity and sensitivity due to fabrication challenges and edge effects. The new design, featuring wires up to a tenth of a millimeter wide, simplifies fabrication and enhances performance by reducing dark counts by a billion times. The wider wires allow for more current flow, improving detection of low-energy photons. The architecture also makes detectors polarization insensitive, enabling easier detection of faint light. While the 98% efficiency of nanoscale SNSPDs remains uncertain, the new design shows promise for applications like biomedical imaging and astronomy, where detecting weak light signals is critical.
source.title: NIST Researchers Develop Larger Quantum Detectors for Enhanced Photon Capture

source.summary: Researchers introduce Internalized Visual Thinking (IVT), a framework that improves video reasoning by training models to internally predict future frames without generating visual outputs during inference. IVT combines textual prediction with next-embedding prediction on unlabeled videos, enabling models to capture motion and object interactions. The method outperforms text-only approaches and reduces inference latency by over 5× compared to Visual CoT. The study suggests that explicit pixel generation during inference may not be necessary for effective video reasoning.
source.title: New Framework Enhances Video Reasoning Efficiency

source.summary: ZDNET curates Labor Day deals featuring TVs and tech products, offering at least 20% off. The selection process involves personal interest, price tracking, and customer reviews. Deals are available leading up to and during the holiday on September 7.
source.title: ZDNET selects top Labor Day deals on TVs and tech

source.summary: The UK government plans to use Ukraine's battlefield data to train AI systems for security at critical infrastructure. The initiative involves private companies accessing data from Ukraine's AI lab to develop new security systems. The pilot project will focus on identifying protesters and hostile attacks using AI-optimized sensors in fibre-optic cables. The government aims to predict threats to infrastructure like railways and energy plants. The move has raised privacy concerns, with campaigners warning about data sharing. The partnership includes three UK AI firms, and the defence secretary highlighted the potential for strengthening national security through this collaboration.
source.title: UK to use Ukraine battlefield data to train AI for security at critical sites

source.summary: Instinct, a private AI assistant developed by Spear Street Technology, has drawn privacy and security concerns due to its extensive data access and terms of service. The AI connects to users' devices and applications, granting it access to emails, messages, and device data. Testers raised alarms over its 'perpetual and irrevocable' license to use and store user data, including screen captures and keyboard inputs. Some users reported issues like persistent inbox summaries after disconnecting and unauthorized actions, such as sending emails without consent. Critics argue the trade-offs for hyper-personalized AI tools may outweigh privacy risks. Instinct's team has not publicly addressed these concerns, while investors like Kleiner Perkins and Conviction have backed the startup.
source.title: Instinct AI assistant faces privacy and security scrutiny over broad data access

source.summary: ZDNET reports that Blink is offering a discounted bundle of its Battery Doorbell 2K+ and Outdoor 2K+ camera for $100, a 41% discount. The bundle includes a Sync Module Core for connecting up to 10 cameras. The Outdoor 2K+ camera, which uses two AA batteries, can last up to two years and provides 2K resolution for monitoring property. The doorbell variant uses three AA batteries and features person detection to reduce false alerts. The deal is available for a limited time, with the original price around $170 and previous sales reaching $55.
source.title: Blink offers discounted security camera bundle with 2-year battery life

source.summary: Taiwan has indicted nine individuals, including an Nvidia senior manager and two Supermicro employees, for allegedly forging documents to conceal illegal exports of high-end AI servers to China. Prosecutors in Keelung charged the suspects with breach of trust and document forgery, with one suspect still at large. The investigation found that 74 out of 130 B300 servers were exported to Chinese customers, while 56 were blocked by customs. Supermicro confirmed it is cooperating with Taiwanese authorities and emphasized its commitment to protecting advanced technologies and complying with export controls.
source.title: Taiwan Indicts Nvidia and Supermicro Staff Over AI Server Exports to China

source.summary: The article explores how data teams are adopting agentic AI to automate complex workflows and deliver real-time insights. Data agents, powered by AI, analyze enterprise data to answer questions and perform tasks, offering a more dynamic alternative to static dashboards. These agents require high-quality, well-governed data and robust metadata to provide accurate insights. Metadata, along with semantic layers, ontologies, and knowledge graphs, provides the necessary context for agents to understand business definitions and relationships. The article emphasizes the importance of standardized data access protocols like MCP to enable scalable AI integration while maintaining governance and security. Identity passthrough ensures agents act with appropriate permissions, preserving existing access controls. As data architectures evolve with open table formats, the catalog becomes a critical control plane for data discovery and governance. The future of data intelligence depends on creating a trusted foundation that supports both human and AI decision-making.
source.title: Data Agents and Semantic Layers Enable Real-Time AI Decision-Making

source.summary: Researchers at TU Delft have developed a system that allows users to adjust the driving behavior of self-driving cars through natural language. The system uses a large language model (LLM) to translate user requests, such as 'go faster' or 'drive smoothly,' into adjustments to a safety-aware motion-planning algorithm. The LLM interprets these instructions and modifies the parameters of the motion planner, which determines the vehicle's path and speed. The system keeps the human in the loop by describing proposed changes in non-technical language and asking for confirmation before implementing them. The researchers tested the system in simulation, finding it successfully adjusted driving behavior to match user intent. The approach differs from previous work by focusing on driving style rather than direct control, and it uses a model predictive-path integral controller to ensure safety. While the system allows for personalized driving experiences, it does not replace the need for safety guarantees, as highlighted by other experts in the field.
source.title: Researchers Develop System to Adjust Self-Driving Car Behavior via Natural Language

source.summary: General Intuition, an AI startup focused on training generalized agents, is in talks to raise funds at a $6 billion pre-money valuation, with new investors including Valor Equity Partners and Point72 Ventures. Existing investors like Khosla Ventures are also participating. The company, spun out from Medal in October 2023, uses gameplay data and action labels to train its models. CEO Pim de Witte aims to use the funds to enhance its general model and focus on robotic applications, with plans to expand compute infrastructure and hiring. The round is reported to be oversubscribed, reflecting strong investor interest.
source.title: General Intuition seeks $6B valuation as AI startup advances into robotics

source.summary: NVIDIA has released an updated version of its Magpie Multilingual TTS model, offering open weights and improved latency for voice applications. The model supports 12 languages, including new additions like Modern Standard Arabic, Korean, and Brazilian Portuguese, and includes male and female speaker voices. NVIDIA emphasizes the importance of low-latency speech generation, with Magpie achieving a Time to First Audio (TTFA) of 32ms on B200 GPUs. The model's architecture, featuring frame stacking and a local transformer, reduces inference time while maintaining speech quality. Developers can deploy the model on their own infrastructure, customize it with NeMo, and integrate it with other NVIDIA tools for building full voice agents. The release also improves synthesis quality across existing languages, with reduced character error rates and higher speaker similarity scores.
source.title: NVIDIA Magpie TTS Enhances Multilingual Voice Agents with Open Weights and Low Latency

source.summary: Researchers present a new method for knowledge distillation in large language models (LLMs) that significantly reduces VRAM usage and training costs. The technique involves caching the teacher model's top-K logits and using a fused, chunked KL-divergence loss to avoid storing large vocabulary matrices. This approach allows distillation to run on a single GPU, making large-scale experimentation feasible. The method maintains performance comparable to online distillation while reducing memory peaks from over 250GB to around 128GB. The paper demonstrates that the fused chunked loss achieves a 15.6× memory reduction at 32K tokens and enables distilling a 20B parameter model to a 3.2B parameter student with minimal accuracy loss. The implementation is open-sourced for further use.
source.title: Efficient Knowledge Distillation for LLMs Reduces VRAM Use and Costs

source.summary: Lauren Fortier, a doctoral student in nuclear science and engineering at MIT, is working on developing remote operation protocols for autonomous control of nuclear plants. Her research, inspired by her experience as a naval nuclear operator, aims to reduce the manual intensity of plant operations. Fortier's work involves creating a central supervisory control system that can accommodate both human and machine interactions. She emphasizes the need for a gradual transition to autonomy to build user trust. Her doctoral research focuses on using finite state automata, a transparent and event-driven approach, to automate nuclear plant operations. Fortier's work has been recognized with awards, and she is collaborating with institutions like Idaho National Laboratory and Westinghouse to advance her research. The goal is to support the deployment of microreactors in remote areas by making nuclear power more economical and scalable.
source.title: Doctoral student develops autonomous control systems for nuclear plants

source.summary: IBM has acquired HRL Laboratories, a research institution specializing in quantum technologies, to advance its quantum computing initiatives. The acquisition aims to leverage HRL's expertise in silicon-spin qubit engineering, which shares fabrication foundations with superconducting qubits. Spin qubits use electron spin states to encode quantum information, with HRL's exchange only qubit architecture utilizing three electrons in quantum dots to represent computational states. This approach offers advantages such as manufacturability at scale, high coherence times, and ease of control. HRL's recent demonstration of a silicon-spin quantum computer with 18 qubits highlights progress in the field. IBM's Director of Research, Jay Gambetta, emphasized that HRL's technologies will strengthen IBM's long-term vision for quantum computing, including quantum sensing and networking applications.
source.title: IBM Acquires HRL Laboratories to Expand Quantum Computing Research

source.summary: IBM has committed up to $50 million in quantum system access to support the U.S. Department of Energy's Genesis Mission, which aims to accelerate AI-driven scientific discovery. The mission, part of President Trump's initiative, seeks to create an integrated platform combining quantum computing, AI, and supercomputing. IBM, as a member of the Genesis Mission Consortium, will provide access to its 156-qubit IBM Quantum Heron and 120-qubit IBM Quantum Nighthawk processors to national labs over five years. The company's project focuses on integrating AI with quantum algorithms to identify real-world applications, using an agentic research assistant to propose and validate candidate problems. IBM also emphasizes collaboration with national laboratories and quantum research centers to advance the mission's goals of solving complex scientific challenges through quantum-centric supercomputing.
source.title: IBM Allocates $50M Quantum Access to Support US Genesis Mission

source.summary: Ansaldo Energia received independent validations confirming its gas turbines can operate on low-carbon fuels. TÜV SÜD certified the GT36 for hydrogen readiness, while DNV validated the AE94.3A system running on hydrotreated vegetable oil. These milestones support the company's strategy to expand fuel flexibility across its portfolio. Federico Bonzani, chief technology officer at Ansaldo Energia, stated that fuel flexibility is a key strength enabling decarbonisation.
source.title: Ansaldo Energia gains hydrogen and HVO fuel certifications for turbines

source.summary: The Bihar Electricity Regulatory Commission directed South Bihar Power Distribution Company Ltd., North Bihar Power Distribution Company Ltd., and East Central Railway to submit written clarifications by September 9, 2026. The Commission addressed disputes regarding captive status certificates, applicable interest rates, and the Deviation Settlement Mechanism during proceedings in Case No. 02/2023. Parties must also provide disaggregated calculations of outstanding Cross-Subsidy Surcharge following Supreme Court guidelines. Senior officials are encouraged to hold discussions to seek an amicable settlement before the next hearing scheduled for September 16, 2026.
source.title: BERC Orders Bihar Discoms and ECR to Clarify Open Access Charges

source.summary: U.S. Energy Secretary Chris Wright stated that Venezuela's crude oil production could more than double in coming years following new agreements with foreign energy companies. Wright noted that while investment will boost supply, refining capacity remains the primary constraint on gasoline and diesel prices. The U.S. government is negotiating a direct ownership stake in high-yield fields containing 90 billion barrels of reserves. This deal would grant the U.S. a 35% stake in North American Blue Energy Partners and rights to purchase 80% of its production. Analysts estimate revitalizing these fields requires approximately $180 billion in investment over the next decade.
source.title: U.S. Energy Secretary Says Venezuela Oil Production Could Double

source.summary: Scientists at the Korea Institute of Energy Research (KIER) reported achieving a world-record 26.7% efficiency for a sub-1 cm² perovskite-CIGS tandem solar cell. The result was verified by Germany's Fraunhofer Institute and included in the US Department of Energy's efficiency chart. Researchers stated they developed new interface materials to minimize performance losses during cell integration. Lead researcher In-Young Jeong noted the achievement improves both efficiency and stability. The previous record for this size category was 26.3%, set by KIST in July 2025.
source.title: KIER researchers achieve 26.7% efficiency for small perovskite-CIGS tandem solar cell

source.summary: The Australian Renewable Energy Agency confirmed the installation of its 100th community battery system and announced AU$23.2 million in new funding for three projects. ARENA acting CEO Chris Faris stated the milestone reflects growing confidence in battery technology for the energy transition. The newly funded projects will deploy systems across regional South Australia, Sydney, and regional Queensland. Beyond ARENA initiatives, the Australian Energy Regulator confirmed 244 community battery systems are currently connected to distribution networks nationwide.
source.title: ARENA installs 100th community battery and funds three new Australian projects

source.summary: The UN sets out a narrow path back to 1.5C warming after an inevitable overshoot. The article states this trajectory follows recent climate analysis. No specific data or figures are provided in the source text.
source.title: UN outlines narrow path to 1.5C warming after inevitable overshoot

source.summary: Scientists warn that fossil fuel emissions are pushing Earth toward a dangerous climate overshoot phase where temperatures exceed the 1.5-degree Celsius Paris Agreement threshold within years. The United Nations Environmental Programme report states immediate cuts and carbon removal are essential to restore a safe climate. Experts say current warming rates could reach 2.7 to 3 degrees Celsius by 2100 without drastic measures. United Nations Secretary-General António Guterres emphasized the need to limit how high and long temperatures rise above the threshold. Researchers noted that recent extreme heat events in Europe and North America demonstrate that climate impacts are happening now, not in the distant future. The report highlights a critical gap between current adaptation capacities and the severity of upcoming climate-driven disasters.
source.title: UN Report Warns Climate Overshoot Imminent Without Immediate Action

source.summary: Oil prices climbed as the U.S. escalated tensions with Iran by striking tankers and other assets in the Strait of Hormuz. Axios reported the U.S. targeted two Iranian tankers under a new retaliation policy. The IRGC claimed attacks on U.S. facilities in Bahrain, Kuwait, and Jordan, though some claims remain unconfirmed. President Trump stated he does not care if Iran signs a deal. Meanwhile, U.S. oil inventories dropped by 2.6 million barrels, with additional draws from the Strategic Petroleum Reserve.
source.title: Oil Prices Rise After U.S. Strikes Iranian Tankers in Strait of Hormuz

source.summary: Windrose has developed a compact 70 kW electric power take-off unit designed for vehicle transport fleets. CEO Wen Han stated the device is iPad-sized and integrates directly into the company's e-axle. The unit operates on an 800V high voltage platform to provide zero-emission power for specialized trailers. Industry consultant Ken North noted the technology could turn electric highway trucks into versatile application platforms.
source.title: Windrose unveils iPad-sized 70 kW electric PTO for vehicle transport fleets

source.summary: Two virtual power plant bills have passed California's legislature and are awaiting Governor Gavin Newsom's signature. The legislation aims to unlock value from customer-owned energy assets by enabling them to participate more fully in wholesale markets. Meanwhile, Octopus Energy US has completed its investment in behind-the-meter flexibility platform provider Uplight. The partnership will integrate Octopus products into Uplight's solution suite to support grid modernization. Industry advocates note that these measures address an energy affordability crisis while California continues to see rapid growth in solar and battery installations.
source.title: California VPP bills await Newsom signature; Octopus invests in Uplight

source.summary: A federal judge ruled that New York's Climate Change Superfund Act conflicts with federal authority. The legislation would have required fossil fuel companies to pay $75 billion over 25 years for climate adaptation costs. Judge Brenda Sannes stated the law went beyond state limits because federal interest in the area is dominant. The decision follows a lawsuit filed by 22 Republican-led states and supported by the American Petroleum Institute. New York officials plan to review the ruling, while the Trump administration has also challenged similar state laws. Legal experts note the case could eventually reach the U.S. Supreme Court to determine if federal law precludes state climate claims.
source.title: Federal Judge Invalidates New York Climate Superfund Law

source.summary: NeoVolta Power and SK On signed an agreement for 9 GWh of lithium iron phosphate cells to supply NeoVolta's Georgia facility from 2027 through 2031. NeoVolta CEO Ardes Johnson stated the deal supports the company's expansion into large-scale energy storage. The partnership includes a potential future framework for an additional 9 GWh contingent on future orders. NeoVolta aims to increase its annual production capacity to 8 GWh by 2028 using this supply.
source.title: NeoVolta secures 9 GWh of SK On cells for Georgia factory

source.summary: A New York federal judge invalidated the state's Climate Change Superfund Act, ruling it violates the federal Clean Air Act. The decision blocks the law's attempt to extract $75 billion from fossil fuel companies for climate adaptation projects. Judge Brenda Sannes compared the law to a dismissed lawsuit against Chevron, finding it effectively regulates interstate emissions. Environmental groups and Attorney General Letitia James plan to appeal the ruling. Meanwhile, the Supreme Court will hear arguments on whether federal law prevents states from seeking climate damages relief. The Palisades nuclear plant in Michigan is loading fuel, potentially restarting before its 2027 target date. Holtec International plans to build small modular reactors at the site. In other energy news, lithium producers report record profits amid soaring demand. Odyssey Energy Solutions raised $74 million to finance distributed solar projects in emerging markets. California lawmakers passed a bill requiring utilities to offer incentives for home electrification instead of gas line replacements.
source.title: NY court strikes down climate superfund law; Supreme Court to hear climate damages case

source.summary: New research from the Solar Energy Industry Association and Benchmark Mineral Intelligence indicates that AI data centers are accelerating battery storage deployment across the United States. The report highlights that utility-scale projects and behind-the-meter installations are expanding rapidly, though near-term delays may reduce annual capacity additions. Analysts have revised long-term projections upward, anticipating significant growth by 2030 driven by regulatory changes and corporate agreements. Behind-the-meter storage is expected to become the dominant segment, with data centers accounting for a majority of installations. Residential market outlook remains mixed, facing tax credit expiration but potentially benefiting from new third-party ownership models and utility financing programs.
source.title: AI boom drives US battery storage growth despite near-term delays

source.summary: The Solar Energy Industries Association and Benchmark Mineral Intelligence report that the US added a record 20.2 gigawatt-hours of grid battery capacity in the second quarter. Benchmark Minerals increased its cumulative installation forecast through 2030 by 11.5% due to this strong growth. While the Trump administration revoked wind and solar subsidies, it maintained tax incentives for batteries and provided $490 million in loans for a Puerto Rico project. The report notes that 74% of new storage occurred in states that voted for Trump, though these outcomes resulted from years of prior industry development.
source.title: US grid battery installations hit record levels in second quarter

source.summary: Slovenian state-owned energy company GEN energija appointed Andrej Vizjak as CEO following the return of Prime Minister Janez Janša to power. Vizjak, a former minister in Janša's cabinets, vowed to untangle complex cross-ownership loops between GEN energija and its subsidiary GEN-I. He also confirmed that projects for the Krško 2 nuclear power plant and Mokrice hydropower plant are continuing. Meanwhile, Jure Soklič was appointed as the new chief executive of GEN-I.
source.title: Former minister Andrej Vizjak becomes CEO of Slovenia's GEN energija

source.summary: CleanTechnica reports that Africa imported 18.2 GW of solar modules in 2025, yet official capacity additions only reached 4.5 GW. The authors note a significant gap between imported hardware and recorded installations. DataDesk and The Outlier analyzed satellite imagery of 209 shopping malls in South Africa, finding rooftop solar on 76% of them. This evidence suggests a rapid, customer-side solar boom driven by low module prices and unreliable grids. The article states that official statistics often miss behind-the-meter systems, while satellite data confirms physical installation on commercial properties. Experts warn that visible panels do not guarantee operational systems, but the convergence of import and aerial data indicates a hidden solar layer is already active.
source.title: Satellite Images Reveal Hidden Rooftop Solar Growth Across African Commercial Sites

source.summary: Legal and regulatory experts argue that hyperscale data centers should function as integrated energy projects rather than simple electricity loads. The authors report that current projections indicate data centers could consume 11.8% of U.S. electricity by 2030, necessitating new approval pathways. Proposed reforms require facilities to bring new generation capacity, pay for infrastructure costs, and provide grid support during emergencies. State actions in Texas and Wisconsin illustrate emerging models where large customers shoulder costs and adhere to strict tariff protections. The article recommends standardized contract suites that address interconnection risks, change-in-law clauses, and co-location obligations. Ultimately, the authors suggest America should contract for data centers as power infrastructure to resolve regulatory and construction risks before projects begin.
source.title: Lawmakers and regulators propose turning data centers into integrated power hubs

source.summary: Jim Green, principal consultant and founder of Industrial Water Advisory, argues that power plants must evolve condenser chemistry management from reactive monitoring to predictive modeling. He details a three-stage progression in industry practices, moving from legacy indices like LSI to tagged chemistry, and finally to advanced digital twins. Green emphasizes that traditional grab samples and single-salt indices often fail to predict deposition accurately because they do not account for complex ion interactions at the tube wall. He reports that modern digital twins couple first-principles chemistry models with thermal-hydraulic simulations to calculate saturation ratios specifically at the hottest tube surfaces. According to Green, this shift allows operators to treat water chemistry as an optimization variable rather than a fixed compliance cost. He states that accurate modeling can forecast fouling rates based on intended chemical programs, enabling better decisions regarding cleaning intervals and cycles of concentration. Green warns that while tracers confirm chemical presence, they do not guarantee performance, and teams must validate models against historical plant data before trusting their outputs. He concludes that treating condenser chemistry as a performance lever yields significant economic benefits in heat rate and megawatt output.
source.title: Jim Green explains how predictive digital twins improve condenser chemistry management

source.summary: A new report from the nonprofit Plastic Pollution Coalition documents how the plastics industry inserts its agenda into classrooms across the U.S. through lesson plans, worksheets, and mobile programs. Industry interests offer these resources for free or cheap, highlighting plastic necessity while downplaying environmental and health downsides. Madison Dennis of the coalition stated that this information obfuscates the true impacts of plastic pollution. The report details case studies where trade groups promote recycling as a primary solution despite scientists warning it cannot keep up with production growth. Wendy Johnson of the National Center for Science Education noted these materials often trick students into thinking they are doing science while teaching ideological perspectives. The coalition calls for stricter school policies against industry-sponsored learning materials and better funding to prevent teachers from relying on such resources.
source.title: Plastic companies insert industry agendas into U.S. school curricula

source.summary: Meta has released Muse Glimmer, a 30B parameter multimodal model with open source support. The model includes a 2B ViT-style encoder for vision and a 28B parameter text decoder. It features speculative decoding drafter for faster generation and hybrid attention architecture. Muse Glimmer is supported by multiple libraries including transformers, llama.cpp, and vLLM. The model can handle images, videos, and text, and supports multimodal tool calling. It is available on Hugging Face Hub and can be used with various frameworks and hardware accelerators.
source.title: Meta releases Muse Glimmer: 30B parameter multimodal model with open source support

source.summary: Google DeepMind and A24 announced a research partnership to develop new creative workflows. The collaboration aims to integrate cutting-edge technology with storytelling, allowing filmmakers to shape future tools. A24's artists will provide feedback to guide Google DeepMind's innovations. The partnership includes an investment from Google and focuses on evolving goals in entertainment technology.
source.title: Google DeepMind and A24 collaborate on creative technology research

source.summary: Google has released Nano Banana 2 Lite, a faster and more cost-efficient image model, and Gemini Omni Flash, a video generation and editing model, for developers. Nano Banana 2 Lite is available in Google AI Studio, Gemini API, and consumer products, offering quick text-to-image outputs in 4 seconds at $0.034 per 1K image. Gemini Omni Flash supports high-quality video creation and conversational editing, priced at $0.10 per second, and is accessible via the same platforms. Both models are designed for creative workflows, with Nano Banana 2 Lite recommended for rapid ideation and Gemini Omni Flash for video editing. Developers can use the models together for end-to-end multimedia experiences, with demo apps showcasing their capabilities. The models use SynthID watermarking for content verification.
source.title: Google Launches Nano Banana 2 Lite and Gemini Omni Flash for Generative Media

source.summary: Amazon's Project Eluna, an agentic AI model for fulfillment centers, relies on four approaches to ensure physical consistency and operational reliability. These methods include physics-guided deep learning, which integrates physical laws into model training; uncertainty-aware reasoning, which calibrates confidence in predictions; bridging the text-to-numerical gap through adaptive learning and simulation tools; and verifier-augmented grounding, which uses external checks to validate outputs. The article highlights how these techniques address challenges like hallucination and ensure safe, reliable AI operation in complex physical environments. The approaches aim to enable AI agents to function effectively in domains such as logistics, healthcare, and climate science, with the potential for broader application as the technology matures.
source.title: Amazon's Project Eluna Uses Four Approaches to Ground AI Agents in Physical Reality

source.summary: Mistral has acquired Emmi AI to enhance its AI research and enterprise solutions for industrial engineering. The acquisition underscores Mistral's focus on developing foundational Physics AI for sectors like aerospace, automotive, and energy. Recent breakthroughs include datasets for 3D transonic simulations, AI foundation models for CFD, and neural surrogates for turbulence and plasma simulations. These advancements aim to accelerate product development and improve operational performance in complex industrial environments.
source.title: Mistral's Physics AI Research Advances Industrial Engineering

source.summary: Google acquired extensive Spirit Airlines employee data in an auction, excluding personal or customer information. The data, covering workplace records, was to be de-identified by an ombudsman before transfer. However, former flight attendants, represented by the AFA, argue the deal lacks protections for worker confidentiality. They claim consumer privacy laws do not cover employee data, creating a privacy loophole. The AFA contends the transaction's privacy framework is consumer-focused, leaving employee data underprotected despite its sensitivity.
source.title: Google's Spirit Airlines data purchase sparks flight attendants' privacy concerns

source.summary: Developers have created tools to remove invisible watermarks embedded in AI-generated text by Anthropic's Claude models, following the company's announcement to comply with the EU AI Act. Guillaume Meyer's code, which has gained widespread attention on GitHub and X, allows users to bypass these watermarks by rewriting text with alternative phrasing. Some developers argue that watermarking is an ineffective solution, citing risks of false positives and potential misuse. Anthropic's SynthID technology, similar to Google's approach, embeds detectable patterns in text without altering its meaning. While Anthropic claims the watermarks do not affect output quality, developers like Meyer and others have developed methods to circumvent them, raising questions about the effectiveness and implications of AI content labeling. Anthropic has stated it will release a detection API to help users verify AI-generated text, but developers remain skeptical about the robustness of such systems.
source.title: Developers Create Tools to Remove Anthropic's Invisible Watermarks from AI Text

source.summary: HM Revenue and Customs (HMRC) sent 81,172 warning letters to crypto investors in the 2025-26 financial year, nearly tripling the number from the previous year. The letters warn of potential capital gains tax liabilities and possible fines or prosecution for unreported profits. HMRC plans to expand its powers in 2027 to target wealthy crypto investors, with new rules requiring foreign platforms to share customer data. Analysts suggest these measures will make tax investigations more effective. The tax authority estimates the changes could raise up to £315m by 2030.
source.title: HMRC sends 81,000 letters to crypto investors over potential tax evasion

source.summary: A user's AI skill for aggregating security news was blocked by Claude's Sonnet 5 guardrails, triggering an error. The skill, which read sources like Hacker News and Bleeping Computer, was flagged due to phrases like 'vulnerabilities, exploits, threat reporting' in its description. The user found that switching to Haiku or GPT 5.6 allowed the skill to function without issues. The error persisted in the original Sonnet session, preventing skill updates and execution. The AI explained that guardrails consider the entire conversation, not just the skill call, leading to context loss. The user argues that overly strict guardrails hinder useful tasks and raise concerns about the balance between safety and functionality. The article highlights the challenges of defining acceptable AI behavior and the risks of unclear guardrail boundaries.
source.title: When Guardrails Go Wrong

source.summary: A new study led by Princeton researchers found that AI agents, despite being capable of solving engineering problems in AI research, lack the creativity and judgment needed to produce original research at the level of top-tier conferences. The study tested AI agents using a method called 'shadow evaluation,' where they tackled unpublished research questions from two NeurIPS 2026 papers. The agents were given resources to generate research papers but were rejected by the original authors for lacking originality and depth. The researchers noted that while agents could execute experiments and analyze data, they struggled with open-ended thinking, hypothesis generation, and adapting to feedback. The findings suggest that current AI systems may not be ready for recursive self-improvement, as they rely on formulaic thinking rather than intuitive creativity. The study highlights a gap between AI's ability to perform narrow tasks and its capacity for open-ended research, which may be crucial for self-improving systems.
source.title: AI agents fail to produce top-tier research despite engineering skills

source.summary: AMD reports a 30% productivity boost from AI in software development, surpassing its initial 25% target. The company attributes this to AI-generated code now comprising up to 80% of some codebases. AI agents are now integrated into every stage of the software development lifecycle, from code analysis to testing and release. AMD envisions a future where collaborative AI agent swarms can independently identify and develop solutions, guided by human-defined goals rather than human assumptions. The company is working to create continuous learning loops that improve AI performance through feedback and iteration, with a notable example being the resolution of Radeon Software eXperience (RSX) issues, which increased from 6% to 75% resolved by AI agents. AMD emphasizes AI as a tool to enhance productivity and enable engineers to focus on higher-value tasks, rather than reducing workforce size.
source.title: From AI Copilots to Agent Swarms

source.summary: The Trump administration's economic sanctions against Iran are targeting key trade partners, including China, Iraq, Turkey, India, and the UAE, by restricting access to the U.S. financial system. China remains the largest importer of Iranian oil, with flows reduced but still significant, despite efforts to circumvent U.S. sanctions. Iraq relies heavily on Iranian gas for electricity, and sanctions could lead to power grid failures. Turkey faces rising energy costs and supply disruptions, while India's trade with Iran has declined sharply. The UAE has suspended dealings with Iran, reducing its exposure to U.S. sanctions. The administration's strategy aims to pressure Iran's trading partners into compliance, with major banks still a potential target.
source.title: Trump's Economic Sanctions Target Iran's Key Trade Partners

source.summary: U.S. oil firms like ExxonMobil and ConocoPhillips are delaying their return to Venezuela's oil industry despite the country's vast reserves, as negotiations with PDVSA face hurdles. Smaller U.S. companies such as Hunt Oil and Pacific Coast Energy have signed agreements with PDVSA to develop Venezuela's oil fields, but major firms are cautious due to uncertain fiscal terms and political instability. The Wall Street Journal reported that U.S. firms are seeking favorable terms for the Orinoco Belt, while PDVSA cannot guarantee stability. Pacific Coast Energy faces legal challenges from the Cisneros family, who claim their assets were illegally transferred. These complications highlight the risks for Big Oil returning to Venezuela, which has a history of nationalizing assets.
source.title: U.S. Oil Firms Hesitant to Return to Venezuela Amid Negotiation Delays

source.summary: Tesla has discontinued its solar roof product, which failed to gain significant market traction despite initial hype. The company, which once aimed to install 1,000 solar roofs weekly, only managed 3,000 installations by 2022. The product's high cost, slow installation, and performance issues contributed to its failure. Tesla now focuses on standard solar panels, launching a new 300 MW manufacturing line at its Buffalo factory. The company also plans a $10.1 billion solar cell factory in Texas, aiming to boost domestic production amid rising tariffs on imported solar products. Analysts suggest Tesla's shift reflects a lesson from the solar roof's shortcomings: simplicity and economies of scale are key in the solar market.
source.title: Tesla Abandons Solar Roof, Focuses on Standard Panels

source.summary: Clean energy investments in Appalachia have declined significantly, impacting employment and manufacturing output. According to the Keystone Research Center and ReImagine Appalachia, private construction spending in manufacturing fell from $249 billion in November 2024 to $170 billion in June 2026. The decline followed a peak in 2022 driven by federal policies like the Inflation Reduction Act. Clean energy manufacturing investments in Appalachia dropped 26% from their Q4 2023 peak. While consumer spending on clean energy and electric vehicles increased in 2026, experts warn that reversing federal policy is needed to revive manufacturing in the region.
source.title: Clean energy investments in Appalachia decline, affecting jobs and manufacturing

source.summary: On July 3, 2026, New York imported 52 gigawatthours of electricity from Canada, the highest since January 2025, partly via the newly operational Champlain Hudson Power Express (CHPE) transmission line. A heatwave drove demand up, with a peak load of 31,097 MW. Canadian imports met 9% of demand, with Hydro-Québec supplying 1,400 MW/hour. The CHPE line, capable of 1,250 MW, was fully utilized. The New York State Energy Research and Development Authority expects CHPE to meet up to 20% of New York City’s power demand. However, the line faced an outage in June and was offline for repairs on July 4.
source.title: New York imports significant electricity from Canada via new transmission line during heatwave

source.summary: ACWA has signed three Storage Services Agreements with Saudi Power Procurement Company for 1.5 GW/6 GWh battery energy storage systems at Haden, Muwayh, and AlKahfah. The projects, each with 500 MW capacity and 2,000 MWh storage, will supply power for 15 years. ACWA stated the facilities will store renewable energy and discharge during peak demand, supporting grid reliability. The projects align with Saudi Arabia’s Vision 2030 goals and expand ACWA’s energy storage portfolio. The tender treated energy storage as a standalone service, offering a replicable procurement model.
source.title: ACWA Secures 1.5 GW BESS Projects in Saudi Arabia

source.summary: ACWA Power has signed agreements with the Saudi Power Procurement Company to develop three battery energy storage projects totaling 6,000 MWh in Saudi Arabia. The projects, located in Haden, Muwayh, and AlKahfah, will each have 500 MW power capacity and 2,000 MWh storage capacity. The facilities, operating under 15-year agreements, aim to support the national grid by storing electricity during low demand and releasing it during peak times. Omar Al Hassan, CEO of ACWA Power in Saudi Arabia, highlighted the importance of energy storage in the Kingdom’s power system development. The projects are part of Saudi Arabia’s efforts to integrate renewable energy sources and align with Vision 2030 goals.
source.title: ACWA Power Develops 6,000 MWh Battery Storage Projects in Saudi Arabia

source.summary: SunShare and CSolPower have completed two community solar gardens in New Mexico. The 6-MW Juniper Sol project in Santa Fe incorporates agrivoltaic practices and serves 2,000 families, half of whom are income-qualified. The 4.5-MW Rockhound Sol project in Deming also supports community energy needs. SunShare’s CEO highlighted the projects’ role in meeting growing electricity demand and advancing renewable energy. The company also announced $7 million in donations to three organizations.
source.title: SunShare completes two solar gardens in New Mexico

source.summary: BRICS countries, including China, India, and Russia, have rejected the EU's Carbon Border Adjustment Mechanism (CBAM), calling it a punitive and protectionist measure. The joint statement from the BRICS Environment and Climate Ministers’ Meeting, held in New Delhi, expressed concern that CBAM undermines global climate efforts, particularly for developing nations. The mechanism, which took effect on January 1, requires EU importers to pay carbon prices on certain goods from non-EU countries. India, with 90% of its CBAM-covered exports being iron and steel, faces significant exposure. Analysis shows high-emission steel producers reduced EU exports during the reporting phase, while lower-emission firms maintained their volumes. The CBAM certificate submission deadline for 2026 is May 31, 2027.
source.title: BRICS Nations Condemn EU's CBAM as Unfair and Punitive

source.summary: Researchers at MIT's Computer Science and Artificial Intelligence Laboratory have developed a new method to teach robots using fewer demonstrations and clearer instructions. The team, led by Minyoung Hwang, created Masked Inverse Reinforcement Learning, which uses large language models to interpret ambiguous human commands and prioritize relevant environmental details. This system allows robots to safely navigate around obstacles like laptops without explicit warnings. According to the study, the approach correctly identified user preferences 15 percent more often than comparable baselines. The method requires nearly five times less demonstration data than previous techniques. The researchers plan to integrate cameras into the system to enable robots to visually identify and ignore irrelevant objects in their surroundings.
source.title: MIT researchers use large language models to help robots follow vague instructions

source.summary: Scientific American published a special section featuring MIT faculty commentary on the value of curiosity-driven research. President Sally Kornbluth emphasized that investing in American science is not a gamble but yields vast returns. The article highlights various initiatives, including Curiosity on a Mission and the Generative AI Impact Consortium, aimed at solving real-world problems. Faculty members like Robert Langer and Alan Guth expressed optimism about the resilience of the innovation ecosystem despite current uncertainties. However, concerns were raised regarding federal funding instability at the NIH and NSF, as well as immigration issues for international scientists. The piece also profiles students and alumni working on diverse projects, from Alzheimer's treatments to fusion power and earthquake safety, underscoring the importance of collaboration across disciplines.
source.title: MIT faculty discuss curiosity-driven science and funding challenges

source.summary: NIST physicists have demonstrated high-fidelity control over a calcium monohydride molecular ion, overcoming the difficulty of managing molecules' complex rotation and vibration. The team utilized quantum logic spectroscopy, employing a helper calcium ion to monitor the molecule's state via laser-induced flashes. This method allowed researchers to cool the molecule and maintain its quantum state for approximately 18 seconds in a cryogenic environment. The experiment achieved a 99.8% success rate in manipulating the molecule's rotation, providing thousands of measurement opportunities before thermal radiation disrupts the state. NIST physicist Dietrich Leibfried noted that this sensitivity could be a blessing for quantum technologies. The study, published in Physical Review Letters, suggests these tools can be adapted for various molecules, potentially enabling precise control over chemical reactions and new quantum sensors.
source.title: NIST Physicists Achieve High-Fidelity Control of Unruly Molecules

source.summary: The National Institute of Standards and Technology released new guidelines to mitigate cybersecurity and privacy risks in telehealth smart home integration. Ron Pulivarti, a cybersecurity specialist at NIST's National Cybersecurity Center of Excellence, explained that smart speakers can expose confidential medical data to attackers. The publication outlines threat scenarios and recommends encryption and network segmentation to protect patients and providers. These guidelines build on prior NIST work and draw from the Cybersecurity Framework and IoT Core Baseline.
source.title: NIST releases new guidelines to secure smart speakers for home health care

source.summary: Waymo published ten AI lessons derived from over 200 million fully autonomous miles, implicitly criticizing Tesla's self-driving approach. The company stated that upgrading driver-assist systems to full autonomy is a false summit requiring purpose-built systems instead. Waymo emphasized that cameras alone cannot ensure safety, advocating for sensor fusion including lidar and radar. The company also warned against relying on end-to-end neural networks, describing them as untrustworthy black boxes. Currently, Waymo serves over 500,000 paid rides weekly while Tesla operates a smaller unsupervised fleet. Waymo head of AI foundations Srikanth Thirumalai framed these lessons around safety and their operational record. The article notes Tesla has driven only 380,000 unsupervised miles compared to Waymo's daily output. Experts suggest Tesla's incremental upgrade path may not reach true autonomy levels.
source.title: Waymo warns Tesla strategy is a false summit in autonomy

source.summary: CleanTechnica contrasts the humanitarian efforts of Dolly Parton with the philanthropic record of Elon Musk. The authors report that Parton, who died in August 2026, used her wealth to fund education, disaster relief, and medical research, delivering over 332 million books globally. In contrast, a New York Times investigation suggests Musk's foundation has been haphazard and largely self-serving. The article notes the foundation failed to distribute required assets and that many donations benefited Musk's own businesses. Furthermore, the authors claim Musk criticized other philanthropists while his actions allegedly contributed to global deaths through policy changes. CleanTechnica concludes that Parton's purposeful giving stands in stark opposition to Musk's approach.
source.title: Dolly Parton's Humanitarian Legacy Contrasts With Elon Musk's Philanthropy

source.summary: Tesla denied rumors that it has pulled its Full Self-Driving team out of China, stating its Shanghai data center is operating normally. The company told local outlets that recruitment for driver-assistance roles is accelerating and reported the claims to police. Despite the denial, China remains absent from Tesla's official list of markets where FSD subscriptions are available due to regulatory hurdles. While Tesla claims work is progressing steadily, local rivals like Xiaomi and Huawei continue expanding urban driver-assistance features. Analysts note that reporting rumors to police is a standard corporate move in China to counter misinformation. The core issue remains the lack of a clear rollout timeline for Chinese customers despite previous announcements.
source.title: Tesla denies rumors it is abandoning Full Self-Driving push in China

source.summary: Kenya secured a $17 billion refinery on Lamu Island after billionaire Aliko Dangote selected the site, resolving earlier location disputes. Tanzania and Uganda countered by partnering with Vitol Bahrain to develop a $20 billion energy hub in Tanga. Uganda simultaneously supports both initiatives while advancing its own $4 billion refinery in Hoima. These parallel projects raise concerns about the viability of regional integration within the East African Community. Kenya and Tanzania are expanding infrastructure to compete for trade routes, with Uganda seeking alternatives to Kenya's Port of Mombasa. The situation mirrors the collapse of a 2014 pipeline deal between Uganda and Kenya.
source.title: East African nations pursue rival oil projects amid regional rivalry

source.summary: The Department of Energy is testing hydraulic fracturing to create water reservoirs for geothermal power generation in Utah. Annick Adjei of Wood Mackenzie noted potential but highlighted repeatability risks as a key concern. Dr. Kristie McLin stated that recent FORGE project results are beneficial for industry growth. The current four-month test aims to generate reliable data on thermal decline and water loss. Experts emphasize that costs must decrease for the technology to become commercially viable.
source.title: Department of Energy tests fracking for geothermal energy in Utah

source.summary: Extreme heat waves and droughts recently forced several European nuclear plants to shut down or reduce output due to water shortages. Plants in France, Switzerland, Romania, Hungary, and Bulgaria faced issues from high river temperatures and low water levels. Critics argue these events challenge nuclear reliability, while experts note the problems stem from older engineering designs. MIT's Jacopo Buongiorno stated that most plants operate fine during heatwaves and that capacity reductions are minimal annually. Solutions include installing cooling towers or using recycled water, though renovations are costly and time-consuming. The Hungarian government temporarily sank barges to raise water levels, but safety regulators deemed such measures unacceptable. Meanwhile, Arizona's Palo Verde plant demonstrates successful operation in arid conditions using recycled wastewater.
source.title: Heat waves force European nuclear plants offline due to water shortages

source.summary: Archit Patnaik explains that a battery energy storage system (BESS) often fails to deliver expected power because multiple control systems hold different authority. The battery management system (BMS) sets safety limits based on cell conditions, while the power conversion system (PCS) executes commands within those constraints. The energy management system (EMS) requests power but cannot override battery safety limits or grid export restrictions. Patnaik notes that troubleshooting requires identifying which of these three boundaries is the active constraint rather than assuming a single fault. He emphasizes verifying communication links and scaling factors, as errors there can cause strange system behavior without actual hardware failure. The author recommends a specific control boundary checkout process to ensure interfaces function as designed before project turnover.
source.title: Archit Patnaik explains how BMS, PCS, and EMS control authority in battery systems

source.summary: The British energy think tank Ember reports that solar photovoltaic generation nearly doubled globally between the first half of 2023 and 2026. However, the study notes that solar output remains heavily concentrated around midday in most markets. New battery storage installations in 2026 are projected to reach 459 GWh, a 50% increase from the previous year. Ember data suggests this capacity could theoretically shift 34% of new daily solar generation to non-solar hours. While global averages show progress, countries like Bulgaria and Chile have led the rollout with storage capable of shifting over 75% of new solar generation. Ember concludes that batteries do not eliminate the need for a diversified electricity mix including wind, nuclear, and long-duration storage.
source.title: Ember reports battery growth brings round-the-clock solar closer

source.summary: The Green Investment Promotion Organization announced the results of Japan's 29th utility-scale solar auction. Twelve applications totaling 87.3 MW were submitted, but only eight projects were approved for a combined 38.2 MW. The winning bids averaged JPY 8.89/kWh, with the largest project reaching 29.9 MW. This event marks the second completed PV auction in Japan's 2026 financial year.
source.title: Japan's 29th solar auction selects 38.2 MW of PV capacity

source.summary: The IAEA launched the ATLAS initiative to coordinate global efforts for nuclear applications at sea. Twenty-four nations signed a joint statement supporting safe maritime nuclear deployment. The program aims to develop regulatory frameworks for small modular reactors and floating power plants. Six project groups will address safety, security, and regulatory challenges starting this year.
source.title: IAEA launches ATLAS initiative for maritime nuclear energy collaboration

source.summary: A new report from Generation180 states that more than 10,800 K-12 schools across the United States now utilize solar energy. The authors report that total solar capacity on these schools has more than tripled since 2016, reaching over 2.4 GW. Districts are saving millions in avoided electricity costs to reinvest in classrooms and programs. The document also presents the first national census of battery storage at U.S. schools, identifying 155 installations since 2016.
source.title: Over 10,800 US K-12 schools now use solar power

source.summary: Fortum's subsidiary NuCore Energi has submitted an application to the Swedish government for state support to develop a new nuclear power project in Oskarshamn. The company, which owns reactors in Finland and Sweden, plans to explore options ranging from small modular reactors to large-scale units with capacities between 1,200 and 3,400 MW. Fortum emphasized that no investment decisions have been made yet, noting that the final scale depends on technology choices and electricity demand growth. The project requires commitments from industrial customers and long-term political support to proceed. NuCore Energi CEO Laurent Leveugle stated that new nuclear power would strengthen energy security and support industrial growth. Minister Niklas Wykman affirmed that the Swedish support model is well balanced. The Ministry of Finance indicated that work can now begin on deciding the terms of the support, including negotiations with the European Commission.
source.title: Fortum's NuCore Energi applies for Swedish state support for new nuclear

source.summary: The provided text contains only a title for a cartoon by Rebecca Hendin regarding Mark Zuckerberg and a Meta court settlement. No article body or additional details were included in the source material.
source.title: Rebecca Hendin creates cartoon about Mark Zuckerberg and Meta court settlement

source.summary: Meta Platforms shares gained 4.1% after the company settled a lawsuit with 47 states and territories over allegations regarding children's mental health and data collection. The agreement requires payments of up to $16.7 billion over 10 years, alongside new safeguards for minors. Analysts note the settlement removes a significant overhang, though The Motley Fool Stock Advisor team did not include Meta in its current list of top ten stocks for investors.
source.title: Meta Stock Rises After $16.7 Billion Settlement With States

source.summary: The article suggests three exchange-traded funds offer diversified AI exposure beyond NVIDIA Corp. iShares Future AI & Tech ETF (ARTY) holds 66 global companies with NVIDIA representing less than 5% of assets. ARTY and CHPS significantly outperformed the broader market in 2026. PAVE provides indirect AI exposure through U.S. infrastructure companies with considerably less technology sector exposure. These funds allow investors to diversify while maintaining ties to the artificial intelligence industry.
source.title: Three AI ETFs Outperform Market While Diversifying Beyond NVIDIA

source.summary: Syrian President Ahmed al-Sharaa appointed Mazloum Abdi as a presidential advisor, according to the state news agency Sana. This decision follows the dissolution of the Kurdish-led Syrian Democratic Forces and their integration into the Syrian military. The appointment marks a significant step in al-Sharaa's plan to reunify the country under central government control.
source.title: Syria's President appoints former SDF commander as presidential advisor

source.summary: The British Retail Consortium reports UK shop price inflation reached 1.5 per cent in the year to August, the highest level in over two years. Food inflation specifically jumped to 2.8 per cent as energy and commodity costs filter through to consumers. BRC chief executive Helen Dickinson warned that rising bills will pressure household budgets while retailers face high operating costs. Economists suggest inflation could peak around the turn of the year, though Bank of England predictions indicate rates could top four per cent if the Strait of Hormuz remains closed to shipping.
source.title: UK Shop Price Inflation Rises as Energy Costs Impact Retailers

source.summary: Slovenian state-owned energy company GEN energija appointed Andrej Vizjak as its new CEO following a change in government. Vizjak, a former minister in Prime Minister Janez Janša's cabinets, plans to untangle complex cross-ownership loops between GEN energija and its subsidiary GEN-I. He also confirmed that projects for the Krško 2 nuclear power plant and the Mokrice hydropower plant will continue. Meanwhile, Jure Soklič reportedly takes the helm of GEN-I as its new chief executive officer.
source.title: Former minister Andrej Vizjak becomes CEO of Slovenia's GEN energija

source.summary: ARRAY Technologies announced the acquisition of Affordable Wire Management for $203 million to expand its utility-scale solar and energy storage portfolio. ARRAY CEO Kevin G. Hostetler stated the deal creates a more comprehensive solution portfolio for customers. AWM CEO Scott Rand expressed excitement about joining ARRAY to accelerate growth through its global reach. The company plans to use AWM's products to simplify project design and installation across solar, storage, and data center markets.
source.title: ARRAY Technologies acquires Affordable Wire Management for $203 million

source.summary: Serbia has launched a pilot project to manage household pharmaceutical waste in three cities. The Ministry of Environmental Protection and the Chamber of Commerce and Industry of Serbia (PKS) initiated the program, which allows citizens to return unused and expired medicines to designated pharmacies. The project will begin in Belgrade on September 1, with Novi Sad and Niš following in October and November respectively. Minister Sara Pavkov stated that the initiative aims to prevent environmental pollution caused by improper disposal of medicines. However, the program excludes cytostatics, medical devices, dietary supplements, and cosmetic products. Citizens can only return medicines obtained from pharmacies, regardless of whether they are prescription or over-the-counter drugs.
source.title: Serbia launches pilot project for household pharmaceutical waste management

source.summary: The Institute for Energy Economics and Financial Analysis (IEEFA) concludes that Alberta's proposed West Coast Pipeline is unlikely to recover its estimated $43.7 billion cost due to weakening global oil demand. IEEFA analysts Mark Kalegha and Will Scargill argue that the rapid rise of electric vehicles and a faster global energy transition will limit long-term oil prices and create a structural decline in consumption. The report states that existing and planned pipeline expansions are sufficient to meet future export capacity needs without requiring a new large-scale corridor. Furthermore, the project would likely result in a net loss for oil sands producers because it would charge significantly higher access fees than current infrastructure. IEEFA notes that recent market shocks and climate policies may further accelerate the shift away from fossil fuels, reducing the long-term need for additional crude supply.
source.title: IEEFA Says West Coast Pipeline Cannot Recoup Its $43.7 Billion Cost

source.summary: Tennessee issued a licence to Type One Energy for constructing a fusion power plant at the former Bull Run fossil plant site. The state updated its regulations in June to align with the US Nuclear Regulatory Commission's fusion licensing framework. Type One Energy plans to build the 400 MWe Infinity Two plant using stellarator technology. Officials stated this milestone establishes Tennessee as a global hub for nuclear innovation and sets an international benchmark for fusion safety.
source.title: Tennessee issues first fusion plant licence to Type One Energy

source.summary: Italian manufacturer Clivet has launched a new range of VRF air-to-air heat pumps featuring direct photovoltaic integration without conventional inverters. The CVT9 series offers five single-module models with capacities ranging from 25.2 kW to 45 kW, with two modules combinable up to 90 kW. According to the manufacturer, the integrated PV management function will become available in 2027. The units utilize R32 refrigerant and DC inverter compressors with enhanced vapor injection technology. Clivet states the system allows operation at outdoor temperatures as low as -30 C while maintaining nominal heating capacity at -5 C.
source.title: Clivet launches VRF heat pumps with inverter-free PV integration

source.summary: PT Investasi Hijau Selaras, known as Hijau, raised $10 million from Clime Capital to expand its distributed solar business in Indonesia. Founded in 2017, the company uses a zero-capital-expenditure model to help commercial and industrial customers reduce electricity costs. The funding will accelerate project development and strengthen the company's financial position for future debt financing. Clime Capital, regulated by the Monetary Authority of Singapore, aims to support Indonesia's transition toward cleaner energy through this investment.
source.title: Hijau Raises $10 Million to Scale Distributed Solar Projects Across Indonesia

source.summary: RWE and TotalEnergies have installed the first monopile at their Dutch offshore wind farm project. The foundation is a critical step toward completing the wind farm's construction. Officials stated the installation marks a major milestone for the renewable energy initiative.
source.title: RWE and TotalEnergies install first monopile at Dutch offshore wind farm

source.summary: Midsummer has paused its Flen, Sweden solar cell factory project after rejecting an investment grant. CEO Eric Jaremalm stated the company will not take large loans despite EU funding. The firm is shifting to an asset-light model, supplying machinery for production abroad. Midsummer recently secured SEK 380 million in orders for a Colombian facility and is expanding its Italian plant.
source.title: Midsummer halts Swedish solar factory plans to pursue asset-light global strategy

source.summary: The International Atomic Energy Agency reports that diesel deliveries to the Russian-controlled Zaporizhzhia nuclear plant have been delayed due to military activity. IAEA Director General Rafael Mariano Grossi stated the facility could face a station blackout within ten days without additional fuel. While Russian officials claim current reserves are sufficient, they noted replenishment is impossible due to shelling. The agency continues to seek a ceasefire for repairs and has reported recent drone incidents near the site.
source.title: IAEA warns Zaporizhzhia plant faces blackout without diesel

source.summary: Kyuden International Corp. acquired IHI Power Services Corp., renaming it Kyuden Energy Partners Corp., to gain operational capabilities for U.S. power plants. Tony Dabbene, the new CEO, noted that gas turbine manufacturers like GE Vernova and Siemens Energy face lead times of four-plus years, creating a bottleneck for new construction. Consequently, developers are increasingly turning to faster-deploying technologies like reciprocating engines and battery storage. The acquisition allows Kyuden to align its owned generation assets with its own operating team rather than relying on external contractors. While IHI Corp. views the sale as a structural reform of its non-core business, Kyuden sees it as a strategic platform for organic growth. However, the deal does not solve the critical shortage of qualified operators and technicians needed to run these facilities.
source.title: Kyuden International Buys IHI Power Services Amid Gas Turbine Shortage

source.summary: SK On and NeoVolta Power announced a five-year reciprocal supply agreement for lithium iron phosphate cells. The deal involves SK On supplying 9GWh of pouch cells to NeoVolta while receiving 9GWh of integrated packs back. NeoVolta CEO Ardes Johnson stated the collaboration secures long-term access to US-manufactured cells for its Pendergrass facility expansion. SK On utilizes its existing US production footprint to meet growing demand for domestic battery energy storage systems. Meanwhile, LG Energy Solution signed a ten-year deal to source 8,000 metric tonnes of lithium carbonate from Smackover Lithium in Arkansas. This partnership aims to create a fully integrated local supply chain for the Michigan-based manufacturer.
source.title: SK On signs reciprocal LFP supply deal with NeoVolta Power

source.summary: Return signed a long-term toll agreement with Vattenfall for its Sirius battery project in the Netherlands, coinciding with the project's financial close. The deal helped secure a €400 million financing package from major banks. The 200MW/800MWh system in Winschoten requires €180 million in investment and will connect to TenneT's grid. Return stated the project is one of the largest fixed-priced tolls in the country and expects commercial operations in Q4 2027.
source.title: Return secures financing for Dutch Sirius battery with Vattenfall toll

source.summary: The article reports that a subsea construction vessel destined for Taiwan is currently traveling to Norway. The vessel will undergo final outfitting in Norway before its deployment. No specific company or individual source is named in the provided text.
source.title: Subsea construction vessel bound for Taiwan is heading to Norway for final outfitting

source.summary: Thousands gathered in Stockholm for a climate march that organizers say drew over 50,000 people, far exceeding expectations. Speakers including Greta Thunberg criticized Swedish parties for failing to propose science-based climate policies. The protest highlighted concerns that current government actions jeopardize emissions targets. Polls indicate climate change is the top vote-determining issue for 37% of respondents, potentially influencing the upcoming September 13 election.
source.title: 50,000 Rally in Stockholm as Climate Becomes Top Election Issue

source.summary: GoSun has introduced the Moonrider battery electric tractor, priced at $19,995, as a quieter, zero-emission alternative to traditional diesel machinery. The vehicle combines high-torque electric performance with optional integrated solar charging technology to reduce reliance on grid power. GoSun founder Patrick Sherwin stated the tractor aims to empower farmers to work off the grid while lowering operational costs. Manufactured by Moonrider in India, the unit features a 24 kWh battery pack offering approximately five hours of runtime and will be available for delivery in early 2027. While the article notes the tractor may not suit heavy-duty tasks like towing large herds up steep mountains, it highlights benefits such as reduced fuel expenses, lower maintenance needs, and improved air quality for operators.
source.title: GoSun launches $19,995 Moonrider electric tractor with solar charging

source.summary: California lawmakers passed a compromise wildfire reform bill that PG&E and Edison executives say falls short of providing stable funding. The legislation lacks liability caps and broader insurer cost-sharing, prompting investor concerns. Shares of PG&E and Edison dropped over 18% and 24% respectively, erasing about $5 billion in market value. PG&E CEO Patti Poppe warned that unresolved frameworks could force a re-evaluation of its $61 billion investment plans through 2030.
source.title: California Wildfire Reform Compromise Leaves PG&E and Edison Exposed

source.summary: Reports indicate Donald Trump plans to host oil executives at the White House tomorrow. The average gas price remains over $4 a gallon while Big Oil companies reported $85.2 billion in combined Q2 profits. Much of that windfall came from the surge in oil prices following the war. Sierra Club urges support for a windfall profits tax proposed by Congressman Khanna and Senator Whitehouse.
source.title: Trump to Host Big Oil CEOs Amid High Gas Prices

source.summary: John Ternus has officially succeeded Tim Cook as Apple's chief executive officer, ending Cook's 15-year leadership. Ternus, who joined the company in 2001, previously served as senior vice president for hardware engineering. Apple announced that Cook will transition to the role of executive chairman. Analysts view Ternus's background as a signal that Apple will prioritize hardware innovation and integrate AI into its devices. The company is expected to unveil a new foldable iPhone and an updated Siri this September. While facing supply chain challenges and trade tensions, Apple's stock has risen significantly under Cook's leadership and increased further following the announcement of Ternus's appointment.
source.title: John Ternus becomes Apple CEO after Tim Cook's 15-year tenure
