source.summary: The emerging-market carry trade, which involves borrowing in low-yield currencies like the US dollar and investing in higher-yield currencies such as the Turkish lira, has achieved its longest winning streak since 2008, returning 22% over the past seven quarters. This outperforms returns from US Treasuries and other global bond classes. The trade benefits from a weakening dollar against emerging-market currencies and high local bond yields, with Turkey and Colombia offering particularly attractive returns despite currency volatility.
source.title: Emerging Markets Carry Trade Hits 7-Quarter Win Streak

source.summary: The Indian Navy and Coast Guard continue searching for 22 crew members of a Panama-flagged bulk carrier that sank in the Bay of Bengal off Odisha. Iran's President Masoud Pezeshkian argued that a memorandum of understanding with the U.S. is the best path to resolve a stalled war, while the head of Iran's security body warned of retaliation if neighboring countries support U.S. sanctions. The ICMR stated no new H1N1 strain has been identified in India, and existing vaccines are sufficient. Congress criticized the delay in proroguing the Lok Sabha, while Ranchi authorities mandated prior permission for protests. The CJP plans to review the Centre's assurances, and Tamil Nadu explores alternative sites for Chennai's second airport. ED officials raided an IAS officer's premises in Karnataka over a KPSC recruitment probe. Pinarayi Vijayan accused the UDF government of yielding to BJP and RSS on the Waqf issue. Assam's CM announced the state is nearing selection of a private partner to launch its own satellite. China postponed its Chang’e-7 lunar mission, which aimed to search for water ice on the moon.
source.title: Morning digest: Search continues for crew members from vessel that sunk off Odisha; U.S. MoU best path out of stalled war, says Iran’s President

source.summary: A Panama-flagged cargo ship carrying 72,000 tonnes of iron ore sank off the Odisha coast in the Bay of Bengal, leaving 22 seafarers missing and two rescued. The vessel, MV Ocean Winner, departed Paradip Port on Friday and reportedly sank in deep waters on Saturday. Officials stated that the crew included 20 Chinese nationals, three Myanmar citizens, and one Bangladeshi national. Rescue operations, involving the Indian Coast Guard, Navy, and merchant vessels, are underway to locate the missing crew. The ship developed a list and sank within eight minutes, according to survivors. The cause of the sinking remains under investigation, with possibilities including adverse weather, cargo issues, or mechanical failure. Authorities are also examining the loss of the vessel from tracking systems.
source.title: Panama-flagged cargo ship sinks off Odisha coast, 22 missing

source.summary: Crude oil prices fell over 1% on Monday as investors anticipated new US sanctions against Iran, which could disrupt Middle East oil supplies. Brent crude dropped $1.22 to $93.17 per barrel, while WTI crude fell $1.20 to $85.86 per barrel. The decline followed a week of gains after US-Iran peace talks stalled, limiting oil shipments through the Strait of Hormuz. US Treasury Secretary Scott Bessent warned of 'toughest sanctions in history' against Iran, while President Trump threatened sanctions on countries trading with Tehran. A firm raised its Brent price forecast for the quarter to $86 per barrel, citing continued production disruptions and increased Chinese demand.
source.title: Oil prices drop as US prepares new sanctions against Iran

source.summary: Two MLAs, Anil Jha of the AAP and Abhay Patil of the BJP, were injured when a Swift car collided with an Innova SUV near Delhi's PWD headquarters. The accident occurred as the hatchback crossed a road divider and entered the opposite carriageway. All six injured individuals sustained minor injuries and were taken to Lok Nayak Hospital. Police reported the incident happened around 9:30 PM, with the driver being a 32-year-old man from Delhi's Arya Nagar. The Fire Brigade assisted in clearing the damaged vehicles from the road.
source.title: Two MLAs injured in car collision with SUV near Delhi's PWD headquarters

source.summary: Max Verstappen crashed during the Dutch Grand Prix, ending his race early after losing control in the first lap. The incident triggered a red flag and delayed the event. Lando Norris capitalized on the chaos, overtaking Kimi Antonelli to win the race and keep his title hopes alive. Norris' victory moved him into fourth in the championship standings, while Antonelli extended his lead over other contenders.
source.title: Max Verstappen crashes in chaotic Dutch GP as Lando Norris secures crucial victory

source.summary: A study by the Securities and Exchange Board of India (Sebi) reveals that Gen Z traders in the derivatives market experience higher loss rates compared to older investors. Around 89% of traders below 30 incurred losses in FY26, compared to 81% of those above 60. The report highlights a shift in the retail derivatives market, with increased participation from non-metro areas and lower-income groups. About 75% of individual traders earn less than ₹5 lakh annually, contributing to 53% of aggregate losses despite accounting for only 43% of turnover. The study also notes that younger investors show greater risk appetite relative to their broader investment behavior.
source.title: Gen Z traders in India's derivatives market face higher loss rates despite growing participation

source.summary: A chlorine leak from a tanker at a water plant in Nagpur's Godni area caused health issues for several residents during the night of Sunday to Monday. Police reported that people with breathing difficulties were taken to hospitals, though the exact number of affected individuals remains unclear. The area still has a strong chlorine odor, and while social media videos show stray dogs dying in the vicinity, the cause of their deaths has not been confirmed.
source.title: Chlorine leak near water plant in Nagpur affects residents' health

source.summary: The article discusses India's strategy to transition from importing medical devices to becoming a global medtech manufacturing hub. It highlights the need to move beyond assembly and focus on creating high-value, technology-driven products. Key points include the importance of developing local component manufacturing, investing in R&D for innovation, and improving quality to meet international standards. The article also emphasizes collaboration between startups, academia, and established firms to support innovation. India's medical devices market is valued at $16 billion, with exports rising from $2.5 billion to $4.1 billion. The goal is to increase the share of sophisticated, technology-intensive products in exports while maintaining strategic connections to global supply chains.
source.title: India aims to build high-value medical devices for global markets

source.summary: India's core industrial sectors experienced a slowdown in July, with the index of core industries (ICI) growing at 5.4%, down from 6% in June. The decline aligns with a weak Manufacturing Purchasing Managers’ Index, reflecting easing demand. While some sectors like coal and iron ore showed strong growth, these were partly driven by a statistical low base effect. The crude oil and natural gas sectors continued to contract, with rising import costs and tariffs on Russian oil adding to economic pressure. The electricity and cement sectors were the only bright spots, with growth rates of 9% and 13.1%, respectively, though overall economic conditions suggest a period of moderating growth and higher costs.
source.title: India's core industries show mixed growth amid slowing demand and base effects

source.summary: The Supreme Court of India upheld the Triple Test for defining 'industry' under the old Industrial Disputes Act, but a majority ruled it should not guide interpretation of the new Industrial Relations Code. Justice B.V. Nagarathna dissented, arguing the test remains relevant for protecting workers. The court's decision leaves a gap in interpreting the new law, which retains the essence of the Triple Test. Legal experts warn the ruling may undermine the framework for resolving industrial disputes.
source.title: Triple test, adrift: On the ruling on definition of ‘industry’

source.summary: The Bihar government has formed a five-member expert committee to review and reform its examination system. The panel will examine security, technology use, and timelines to prevent malpractice, leaks, and delays. It will assess the entire exam process, from registration to result declaration, and suggest measures to enhance transparency and fairness. The committee will also explore digital technology, AI, and cybersecurity tools to strengthen the system. It is expected to submit recommendations within three months.
source.title: Bihar government establishes five-member panel to reform exams and prevent leaks

source.summary: Anthropic, the AI company behind Claude, could reach a $2 trillion IPO valuation, surpassing SpaceX's $1.77 trillion valuation from June. This optimism stems from its rapid revenue growth, which increased from $1 billion in early 2025 to a $65 billion annualized run rate in July. Investors project Anthropic's revenue could hit $100 billion to $120 billion by 2026 and $190 billion to $200 billion by 2028. SpaceX, while currently at a $31.2 billion annualized revenue run rate, aims to reach $100 billion by 2026. However, SpaceX's AI business remains in an operating loss, whereas Anthropic is projected to generate a $559 million adjusted operating profit in Q2. Analysts note that Anthropic's strong AI models and pricing power could support its valuation, though its long-term growth and profitability remain uncertain. The company's IPO filing will provide further insights into its financials and future plans.
source.title: Anthropic's Potential $2 Trillion IPO Valuation and Comparison with SpaceX

source.summary: On August 19, US Ambassador Sergio Gor met with Jammu and Kashmir Chief Minister Omar Abdullah in Srinagar, prompting cautious public statements from Abdullah. Abdullah emphasized that Kashmir's issues should be resolved by New Delhi, not Washington, while Gor described the region as an 'important part' of India, drawing sharp criticism from Pakistan. The meeting was described as 'cordial,' with both sides expressing hope for improved relations and economic engagement. Abdullah's guarded approach reflects a historical pattern, as his grandfather Sheikh Mohammad Abdullah faced similar pressures in the 1950s, when his advocacy for Kashmiri independence led to the Kashmir Conspiracy Case. The article highlights how international involvement in Kashmir has often been fraught with political risk, with past US diplomats like Loy Henderson and Adlai Stevenson linked to Abdullah's nationalist aspirations. Analysts suggest that Abdullah's caution stems from the region's current status as a state without semi-autonomy, and the potential risks of aligning with foreign powers. The article underscores the complex interplay between local politics, international diplomacy, and the long-standing sensitivity of the Kashmir issue.
source.title: Omar Abdullah's Caution in US Engagement on Kashmir Reflects Historical Precedents

source.summary: In an interview with Gowhar Geelani, Bilal Gani Lone, a former Hurriyat leader, reflects on Kashmir's evolving political landscape and the need for local self-reliance. Lone acknowledges his shift towards electoral politics, emphasizing the importance of addressing the people's daily issues and restoring their dignity. He criticizes the political elite for exploiting the masses and highlights the disparity between the wealthy few and the struggling majority. Lone also discusses the loss of Jammu and Kashmir's statehood and the impact of prolonged conflict. He stresses that Kashmiris must take charge of their political and economic future, rejecting external interference and internal divisions. The conversation touches on Article 370, the role of political parties, and the legacy of his late father, Abdul Gani Lone.
source.title: Bilal Gani Lone discusses Kashmir's political shift and self-reliance

source.summary: A photo of BJP national president Nitin Navneet showing an inverted national flag has been shared on social media, but it is edited. The claim that he does not know the correct order of the flag's colors is false. The image was verified using Google Lens, matching it with official BJP website and social media accounts, confirming the flag was held correctly. A Deccan Herald report mentions BJP Delhi unit filed a complaint against the viral fake image. The conclusion is that the edited photo is being shared with misleading claims.
source.title: BJP National President's Edited Photo Showing Inverted Flag Shared on Social Media

source.summary: The podcast episode explores Geoffrey Hinton's journey from studying the brain to collaborating with researchers who developed powerful AI technology. It highlights the intersection of human and artificial intelligence, referred to as two black boxes, and discusses the profound implications of their work. The episode is part of season one, which will be followed by season two in early September.
source.title: Black Box Season One Episode Explores Geoffrey Hinton's Work with AI Researchers

source.summary: The article discusses the shift from traditional embedding-based recommenders to generative recommenders (GRs) in the context of large-scale recommendation systems. It highlights the challenges of handling massive user history data and the long-tail problem, where popular items dominate interactions. GRs, inspired by large language models (LLMs), reframe recommendation as a sequence modeling task, enabling more efficient training and inference. The NVIDIA recsys-examples repository provides optimized implementations of GR architectures like HSTU and Semantic IDs, addressing issues such as memory constraints and latency. DynamicEmb and nv-embedding-cache are introduced as tools to manage large embedding tables and improve inference performance. The article also outlines a specialized inference framework for Semantic ID-based GRs, emphasizing their unique requirements compared to LLM serving systems.
source.title: Generative Recommenders Address Scalability and Long-Tail Challenges in RecSys

source.summary: NVIDIA explores the use of AI coding agents in developing real-time endoscopic tool segmentation applications using Holoscan. The process involves iterative development cycles guided by a developer and an agent, leveraging HoloHub examples, documentation, and the Holoscan CLI. The first iteration focused on creating a new application using an existing model and video, while subsequent prompts refined visualization, added benchmarking, and optimized performance. The workflow demonstrated how agents can reuse existing components, implement new features, and maintain model integrity. The study compared different resource configurations, showing that combining CLI, skills, and documentation provided the most efficient development experience. The final application included multiple modes, automated tests, and reproducible benchmarking, highlighting the potential of agentic development in AI edge computing.
source.title: NVIDIA Demonstrates AI Coding Agent Workflow for Holoscan Application Development

source.summary: A new algorithm, ComputePN, addresses the computational challenges of evaluating complex Boolean queries on inverted indexes. The paper establishes that evaluating Boolean query DAGs is P-Complete, highlighting theoretical limits of existing methods. ComputePN uses a Positive-Negative dual representation and DAG memoization to bound evaluation time to O(|Q| · |U_active|), avoiding exponential blowup and universal scan penalties. The approach enables native execution of P-Complete queries over inverted indexes, providing a formal foundation for computational retrieval. The paper also introduces Wally, a private search system that improves performance for large-scale queries by reducing cryptographic operations.
source.title: New Algorithm Enables Efficient Evaluation of Complex Boolean Queries on Inverted Indexes

source.summary: Authors Qing Liu, Zanhui Liu, and Vivian Zhanwei Yue propose a theory explaining the division of labor among creditors in sovereign finance. Their model shows official lending acts as monitored liquidity provision that remains countercyclical even when private debt defaults. A calibration of their framework reproduces procyclical private debt alongside countercyclical official debt.
source.title: Liu, Liu, and Yue propose a theory of international official lending

source.summary: Jonathan Freedland spoke with Dan Alexander of Forbes regarding Donald Trump's personal wealth accumulation and his economic record. The discussion occurred while the Trump administration recently reignited trade tensions with Canada. Additionally, the US national debt has surpassed $40tn, and the administration threatened an economic D-day against Iran.
source.title: Trump reignites trade war with Canada amid rising US debt

source.summary: Activist investor Elliott Management has acquired a stake in French industrial giant Air Liquide and is urging management to improve profit margins. People familiar with the matter stated Elliott believes the company can benefit from global AI expansion. Air Liquide is scheduled to discuss a turnaround plan with analysts at an upcoming investor day. The company and Elliott declined to comment on the specific size of the investment.
source.title: Elliott Management Acquires Stake in Air Liquide to Improve Margins

source.summary: President Donald Trump warned that resisting data center construction risks leaving communities "backwards and poor." The National Republican Senatorial Committee noted Ohio opposition hurt Sen. Jon Husted's race. Vice President JD Vance stated high electricity bills drive the backlash. Polls show roughly 70% of Americans oppose local data centers. Governors in Texas and Pennsylvania have moved to limit new projects.
source.title: Trump warns communities opposing data centers will become poor

source.summary: The Guardian editorial argues that Meta's $18bn settlement with US states fails to adequately regulate the company's business model. While the deal introduces new child safety features, it avoids liability admissions and leaves addictive design elements untouched. The article notes that other nations have imposed stricter restrictions on social media access for children. Furthermore, the editorial highlights that current measures do not address the platform's role in promoting violence globally. The piece concludes that foreign governments and other courts must hold Meta accountable for its impact on the digital commons.
source.title: Guardian editorial says Meta settled too lightly over child safety

source.summary: The Central Bank of the UAE launched an investigation into local branches of Egypt's Banque Misr. The US Treasury announced it would bar the lender's UAE operations from dollar transactions. The department stated the branches processed about $1.8 billion in transactions potentially linked to Iranian shadow banking networks. This probe follows a fresh US sanctions campaign against Iran.
source.title: UAE investigates Egyptian bank branches after US sanctions

source.summary: U.S. Treasury Secretary Scott Bessent told CNBC that he believes Japan will take action to strengthen the yen, signaling a likely Bank of Japan rate hike in September. Bessent, speaking at a G20 gathering in Asheville, North Carolina, stated he has information suggesting the BOJ will do the right thing on monetary policy. The yen gained against the dollar following his comments, reinforcing market expectations of a September rate increase. Sources told Reuters the BOJ is set to raise rates at its September 17-18 meeting and may hike more aggressively afterward. Bessent noted he does not see recent yen moves as disorderly, suggesting Washington is not planning another market intervention.
source.title: Bessent expects Japan to act on yen, signals BOJ rate hike

source.summary: Yahoo Finance reports that Bitcoin and Ethereum prices fell on Monday, August 31, 2026, as higher rate expectations pressured the market. Bitcoin opened 0.7% lower, while Ethereum dropped 1.6% from Sunday's levels. Fed Chair Kevin Warsh's speech and renewed Middle East hostilities pushed oil prices higher, raising expectations for imminent rate hikes. Both cryptocurrencies remain significantly down from Friday's opening prices despite early morning gains.
source.title: Higher rate expectations pressure Bitcoin and Ethereum prices lower on Monday

source.summary: Silver futures opened 1.4% lower on Monday, August 31, 2026, amid growing expectations for a Federal Reserve rate increase. Fed Chair Kevin Warsh stated the central bank must ensure inflation moves toward its objective. Additionally, a U.S. military attack on Iranian rocket launchers added to market uncertainty. The article outlines various investment methods, including physical bullion and ETFs, noting storage costs and tax implications for each option.
source.title: Silver prices fall as Fed rate hike expectations rise

source.summary: Treasury data indicates that the entire yield curve has risen since Friday. This follows earlier progress in lowering long-term rates. The chart displays yields as of August 18, 19, and 28.
source.title: Treasury data shows entire yield curve rose after initial long rate progress

source.summary: The article critiques the Trump administration's recent financial maneuvers and the Democratic Party's internal conflicts. The Office of the Comptroller of the Currency granted preliminary conditional approval for a federally chartered national trust bank for the Trump family's crypto outfit, World Liberty Financial. This approval occurred despite significant concerns regarding foreign ownership, with a UAE-controlled vehicle holding a 49 percent stake in the holding company. The author notes the bank will issue the USD1 stablecoin with minimal capital reserves relative to its outstanding tokens. Simultaneously, the piece argues the Democratic establishment is waging a war against its own progressive left, exemplified by the intense backlash against commentator Hasan Piker. The author claims this mirrors the UK Labour Party's historical suppression of its left wing. Finally, the article highlights a potential upset in the Texas Senate race, where Democrat Vikki Goodwin faces a massive fundraising deficit against incumbent Dan Patrick despite polls suggesting voters oppose Patrick's policies on marijuana and book bans.
source.title: Trump family secures UAE-backed bank charter amid Democratic internal strife

source.summary: The post presents seven graphs to elicit thoughts on current financial system events. The author notes that debt is rising fast even at full employment and questions if the stock market is near a peak. The Fed funds rate is shown above Taylor rule implied levels, while Fed credibility is reported as lower under Trump 2.0. Additionally, the text highlights stablecoin developments after GENIUS and mentions eroded dollar reserve currency domination.
source.title: Seven Graphs Illustrate Current Financial System Events and Trends

source.summary: MapQuest rose to the No. 1 navigation app after refusing to rename Lake Ontario following a presidential executive order. The company stated it would keep familiar names, a stance that drove a 50-fold increase in app usage. While Google Maps updated the name for U.S. users, Apple has not yet changed it. Critics accused Google of capitulating to the administration. Meanwhile, trade tensions between the U.S. and Canada have intensified with new tariffs.
source.title: MapQuest Ranks Higher After Refusing to Rename Lake Ontario

source.summary: Naomi Watts will receive the Donostia Award at the 2026 San Sebastián International Film Festival. The Zinemaldia jury recognized the actress as one of the most talented and recognizable of her generation. Director Werner Herzog will receive the first award in August. The ceremony will take place on September 19 following a screening of 'La esposa perfecta'. Previous honourees include Gregory Peck and Pedro Almodóvar.
source.title: Naomi Watts to receive Donostia Award at 2026 San Sebastian Film Festival

source.summary: Indigenous ranger groups across northern Australia are removing tons of ghost nets and marine debris from remote coastlines where abandoned gear kills sea life. The nets drift from Southeast Asia into the Gulf of Carpentaria, posing a persistent threat to turtles, dugongs, and sharks. After funding nearly lapsed, the Australian government committed AU$25 million over four years to support cleanup and prevention efforts. Rangers now use drones with artificial intelligence to locate nets faster than before, increasing daily removals significantly. While cleanup continues, advocates emphasize addressing the problem at its source through international cooperation and preventing gear loss at sea.
source.title: Indigenous rangers remove ghost nets with drone aid and government funding

source.summary: Jean-Philippe Tanguy, a National Rally MP, stated the party plans to fine women wearing the Islamic veil if they gain power. He described the move as penalizing the wearing of the veil while fighting Islamist ideology. Tanguy claimed the sanctions would show solidarity with women forced to wear the garment globally. FRANCE 24 reported these comments made on Sunday.
source.title: Jean-Philippe Tanguy says National Rally plans fines for veils

source.summary: Vedika Bahl reports that social media is flooded with fake and AI-generated images linked to the Nepal floods. One video with over 7 million views was created using Google's AI tools. Other viral posts recycle footage from disasters in Chile, Alaska, and India. Genuine footage of the real disaster continues to emerge from affected areas.
source.title: Fake and AI images flood social media during Nepal floods

source.summary: The Associated Press reports that the National Hurricane Center issued tropical storm warnings for coastal Texas and Louisiana. Forecasters expect the system to strengthen into a named storm by Monday night and make landfall in Texas on Tuesday. Meanwhile, Tropical Storm Lowell is moving toward Hawaii and could rapidly intensify into a hurricane. Additionally, Hurricane Karina strengthened into a Category 4 storm in the Pacific without threatening land.
source.title: Texas and Louisiana warned of storm as Hurricane Lowell heads to Hawaii

source.summary: Former Cleveland Browns tight end Dae'Quan Wright practiced with LSU on Monday as the team prepared for its season opener against Clemson. LSU coach Lane Kiffin stated he would bring in former pros if they could help the team win, noting that team leaders supported the move. However, whether Wright or other former NFL players will suit up remains uncertain due to ongoing litigation involving the NCAA. Nearly 400 athletes have sued the NCAA, and a hearing is scheduled for Thursday in Baton Rouge. Defensive end Jack Pyburn was claimed by the Kansas City Chiefs instead of returning to LSU.
source.title: LSU practices ex-NFL player amid NCAA lawsuit uncertainty

source.summary: The NASCAR Cup Series playoffs commence at Darlington Raceway with a 10-race format determining the champion. Denny Hamlin leads the field after his regular-season advantage was reset to 25 points over Ryan Blaney. The new format eliminates early knockouts to allow more drivers a chance at the title. Drivers are seeded from one to 16 based on their performance throughout the season. While Hamlin and Blaney are favorites, other contenders like Kyle Larson and Joey Logano remain in the mix. Several drivers on the bubble, including Chris Buescher and Daniel Suarez, face significant challenges to advance. The championship will be decided at Homestead-Miami Speedway in mid-November.
source.title: NASCAR Cup Series playoffs begin with 16 drivers vying for championship

source.summary: MindTopo, a new benchmark, evaluates whether multimodal AI models can understand topological concepts like connectivity and knots. The benchmark tests both static recognition and interactive planning, revealing that current models excel at recognizing topological relationships in images but struggle to maintain this understanding during sequential actions. Failures in planning often involve losing track of structural relationships or proposing physically impossible actions. The study highlights the importance of topological understanding for AI systems in robotics and interactive environments. MindTopo categorizes tasks into continuity, separation, order, enclosure, and knots, with models evaluated on both reasoning and planning tasks. Results show significant gaps between static perception and dynamic interaction, suggesting the need for models that explicitly track topological states.
source.title: MindTopo benchmark assesses AI's topological reasoning and planning capabilities

source.summary: WhatsApp is introducing Scam Alert, an optional feature that uses on-device machine learning to detect potential scam messages. The system runs entirely on the user's device, ensuring no message content leaves the device for classification. Scam Alert complements end-to-end encryption by providing users with warnings about suspicious messages from non-contacts, without automatically reporting any data to WhatsApp or Meta. The feature is designed with strict privacy principles, including on-device processing, no automatic reporting, and user control over the tool. To validate its implementation, WhatsApp is inviting security researchers and the public to review the system's architecture and provide feedback. The feature is currently in beta and will be rolled out gradually, with additional safeguards like confidential federated analytics and differential privacy to protect user data while measuring the system's effectiveness.
source.title: WhatsApp Introduces Scam Alert Feature With On-Device Machine Learning and Privacy Safeguards

source.summary: The Quantum Optimization Benchmarking Library (QOBLIB) is a community-driven framework designed to track progress toward quantum advantage in optimization. Developed by the Quantum Optimization Working Group and supported by organizations like IBM Quantum and Zuse Institute Berlin, QOBLIB includes ten challenging optimization problem classes and provides metrics for comparing quantum and classical methods. A recent publication in Nature Computational Science and a new website have expanded its reach, with over 2,000 submitted results from researchers worldwide. The library aims to foster collaboration and rigor in benchmarking, helping identify where quantum computing may deliver practical value. Contributions from both classical and quantum researchers are encouraged to advance the field and measure progress over time.
source.title: Quantum Optimization Benchmarking Library Tracks Progress Toward Quantum Advantage

source.summary: Amazon's Automated Reasoning Group (ARG), launched in 2016, has evolved from research prototypes to essential services used by millions of customers. The group applies formal verification and automated reasoning to ensure the correctness and security of AWS systems. Key tools like Tiros and Zelkova now power network security analysis and policy enforcement, while cryptographic and infrastructure systems have been mathematically proven. The work has also extended to AI, with features like Amazon Bedrock Guardrails using automated reasoning to validate AI-generated content. The group's approach has shown that mathematical rigor enhances both security and efficiency, positioning AWS to lead in the next era of AI development with provably safe systems.
source.title: Amazon's Automated Reasoning Group Transforms Security and AI with Mathematical Certainty

source.summary: Mistral is advancing AI sovereignty by offering enterprises and countries control over AI models, infrastructure, and compute capacity, ensuring regional compliance and reliability. The company is expanding open model access, introducing regional endpoints and priority tiers, and forming a coalition to secure long-term European AI compute capacity. Mistral aims to build up to 1 GW of capacity by 2030, providing scalable, sovereign AI infrastructure. The company emphasizes regional control, production-grade reliability, and open model choice, allowing customers to run models under strict regional controls and service commitments. Mistral is also forming a coalition of enterprises to secure long-term compute capacity in Europe, converting commitments into access to its infrastructure over multiple years.
source.title: Mistral enhances AI sovereignty with regional control and open model access

source.summary: NIST researchers have identified a common error in analyzing nanomaterial properties that can distort understanding of how size affects performance. The team found that size measurements of nanoscale objects are often imprecise, leading to misleading conclusions about material behavior. This error can affect various nanotechnology applications, from drug delivery to electronics. The researchers developed a mathematical correction to account for measurement uncertainties, allowing for more accurate analysis of the relationship between nanoparticle size and properties like brightness or drug-carrying capacity. To apply the correction, scientists must estimate their measurement errors using reference materials or calculate uncertainty when such materials are unavailable. The study, published in ACS Nano, aims to improve the reliability of nanotechnology research and development.
source.title: NIST Scientists Identify and Correct Size Measurement Error in Nanotechnology

source.summary: Meta has developed a multi-stage sequence model to enhance its ads ranking system, enabling efficient scaling of sequence learning. The model separates offline user modeling from online ranking tasks, improving performance without increasing serving costs. Key innovations include dense tokenization and target-aware attention, which allow the system to learn feature interactions directly from data. This architecture contributes to a 6% conversion lift on Instagram and 3% on Facebook. The approach follows LLM-style scaling laws, with performance improvements showing a log-linear relationship to compute resources. Meta identifies four scaling levers: balanced model shape, multi-stage tunability, sequence diversity, and semantic feature representation. The model is a core component of Meta’s Generative Ads Recommendation Model (GEM), designed for generalization across various ads ranking tasks.
source.title: Meta Introduces Multi-Stage Sequence Model for Efficient Ads Ranking

source.summary: The llm 0.33 update includes key support for embedding models, allowing per-call key passing without altering shared model state. It also enables combining templates via the -t/--template flag, facilitating the use of pre-configured models and options. Additionally, reasoning-capable models now support a reasoning_summary option with auto, concise, and detailed values. The release notes reference recent articles on conceptual integrity, Qwen 3.8, and an OpenAI incident against Hugging Face.
source.title: llm 0.33 update introduces key support and template combining

source.summary: ZDNET explains how to use a TV as a computer monitor, offering cost-effective alternatives to expensive displays. The guide covers HDMI and wireless connection methods, including AirPlay and Googlecast, while noting potential issues like input lag and resolution mismatches. It also details how to find a TV's IP address for remote access and adjust display settings for optimal performance. The article highlights the benefits of using a TV for additional screen space at lower cost, comparing models like the Alienware 34-inch QD-OLED gaming monitor and the Hisense A4, noting differences in resolution, refresh rate, and features.
source.title: Using a TV as a Monitor: Setup and Considerations

source.summary: Apple allows iPhone users to customize message backgrounds in iOS 26, enabling personalized chat themes. However, this change is visible to all participants in the chat, as long as they also use iOS 26. The feature lets users choose from preset options or photos from their camera roll. While it enhances personalization, it may lead to unintended visibility for others. Users can disable the feature in Settings or revert to a plain background, which also removes the change for all chat members.
source.title: You can change your Messages backgrounds on iPhone - so you never text the wrong person again

source.summary: Chinese AI companies are building large data centers in Ulanqab, Inner Mongolia, driven by low electricity costs, cold climate, and proximity to Beijing. Over 100 data centers have been constructed or planned since 2016, with 70% of commitments announced in the last year. Companies like DeepSeek, ByteDance, and Alibaba are investing in their own infrastructure, marking a shift from relying on cloud providers. However, water scarcity poses a challenge, as Ulanqab receives only 14 inches of rain annually. The region's data centers, part of China's 'Eastern Data, Western Compute' initiative, benefit from reduced latency due to fiber optic cables and are seen as a way to utilize excess renewable energy. Despite progress, coal still provides 37% of Ulanqab's electricity, raising concerns about sustainability.
source.title: Chinese AI firms invest in Ulanqab data centers amid water and energy challenges

source.summary: TikTok has agreed to pay $400 million to the US government to resolve a lawsuit alleging violations of the Children's Online Privacy Protection Act (COPPA). The settlement, stemming from a 2024 Department of Justice suit, addresses data collection on users under 13. TikTok and its parent company ByteDance will pay $300 million immediately and $100 million after the FTC vacates a 2019 consent decree. The deal includes a $5.7 million fine for Musical.ly, ByteDance's predecessor. The DOJ noted TikTok has made changes to its privacy practices and ownership structure since the lawsuit began. Meta faces similar allegations from 29 states, with potential penalties exceeding hundreds of billions of dollars.
source.title: TikTok agrees to $400m settlement for child privacy violations

source.summary: LinkedIn reported over a million users clicked its new 'AI slop' button, introduced to flag AI-generated content. The feature, accessible via the three dots menu, aims to reduce views on AI-generated posts by 40%. The button follows findings that 41% of longform posts were flagged as AI-generated. LinkedIn also improved AI classifiers and removed an AI-enhancement feature. Users now receive messages indicating posts may appear AI-generated, with the company emphasizing efforts to provide helpful feedback.
source.title: LinkedIn's AI slop button used by over a million users

source.summary: Balaji Ingole, an IEEE senior member and project manager at Amla, leverages AI to transform e-commerce operations and develop health care diagnostic tools. Growing up without access to technology, Ingole discovered programming in middle school, which sparked a lifelong passion for problem-solving. He now leads AI-driven initiatives at Amla, helping clients streamline product setup on e-commerce platforms through AI agents. Ingole also works on assistive technologies and health care diagnostics, emphasizing the importance of rigorous data governance. His research includes patents for AI-powered health monitoring devices and breast cancer detection tools. Ingole credits IEEE membership for fostering his professional network and research contributions, highlighting the role of peer review in refining his work. His career path, from self-taught programming to leading global projects, reflects a commitment to 'learn by doing' and using technology for societal benefit.
source.title: Balaji Ingole Develops AI Tools for E-Commerce and Health Care

source.summary: Addy Osmani, a software engineer with over 14 years at Google, shares insights for engineers navigating the AI era. He emphasizes that the key to durability in an AI-driven world lies not in problem-solving but in choosing meaningful projects and judging their quality. Osmani advises optimizing for scarce resources like reputation and relationships, rather than chasing high pay. He highlights the importance of finding problems over solving them, and cultivating judgment through deliberate practice and deep understanding of systems. Engineers should shift from doing to directing, delegating tasks to agents while maintaining verification and accountability. The article stresses the value of finishing strong, focusing on the 'last mile' of development, and building a public track record to seize opportunities. It concludes that the ungradable part of a career—choosing and judging work—is where human value lies, urging engineers to act with intention and integrity.
source.title: Engineer's Guide to Thriving in AI Era: Focus on Judgment and Direction

source.summary: Prominent YouTube creators Matti Haapoja and Sam 'Kolder' have faced backlash for promoting Higgsfield's AI tools through unmarked videos that resemble advertisements. Their content, which showcases Higgsfield's Seedance 2.5 functionality, has led fans to believe the creators were compensated, despite neither confirming paid partnerships. Haapoja's video, which resembles an infomercial, and Kolder's narrative about AI replacing human creators have sparked mixed reactions. While some praised the technological advancements, others criticized the creators for aligning with AI, which many view as a threat to creative authenticity. The controversy highlights the risks creators face when endorsing AI technologies, especially when their audiences value human creativity. Higgsfield later confirmed the collaborations were paid, but the backlash underscores the tension between commercial interests and audience values.
source.title: YouTube creators face backlash for promoting AI tools through unmarked videos

source.summary: AI agents are increasingly reshaping web systems and economic priorities, according to a This Week in AI episode. Models are now optimized for autonomous work rather than conversation, with agents handling tasks independently through cloud computing. Grok 4.6 and Cursor's integration exemplify this shift, offering agents their own computing resources. Gartner forecasts a nearly doubling of AI-optimized cloud spending, with inference costs surpassing training costs. Agents generate most web traffic and content, with Cloudflare reporting agentic bots at 57.4% of requests. Platforms are responding with content flags and watermarking. A security incident involving OpenAI and Hugging Face highlights risks as agents find ways to bypass restrictions. OpenAI's Computer History feature expands AI memory beyond simple recall.
source.title: AI agents reshape web systems and shift economic focus

source.summary: A Seattle-based startup, Endurance Energy, is deploying a 100-kilowatt geothermal generator near an underwater volcano off Oregon's coast, marking the fifth such pilot project. The initiative aims to harness heat from hydrothermal vents, which reach temperatures up to 750°F, to produce emissions-free electricity. The company believes this technology could eventually power entire cities, offering a reliable, clean energy source that is not weather-dependent. While geothermal energy has long been viable in limited geographic areas, recent advancements in drilling techniques are expanding its potential. The U.S. Department of Energy estimates enhanced geothermal systems could supply energy to 65 million homes by midcentury. Meanwhile, growing demand from data centers, driven by AI, is increasing investment in geothermal energy as a scalable solution.
source.title: Seattle startup tests underwater volcano geothermal power off Oregon coast

source.summary: A limited waiver of the Jones Act, renewed by the U.S. Department of Homeland Security, allowed more ships to transport crude oil and petroleum products from the U.S. Gulf Coast to the West Coast, increasing shipments to over 190,000 barrels per day in April. This marked a more than quadruple year-on-year increase, with gasoline blending components, finished motor gasoline, jet fuel, and crude oil contributing to the surge. Shipments to the East Coast also rose to a record 1.2 million barrels per day in April, driven by gasoline blending components and distillate fuel.
source.title: Jones Act waiver boosts Gulf Coast to West Coast oil shipments

source.summary: The Rhine River's water levels have slightly increased from mid-August record lows, but the relief is minimal as barge capacity remains restricted. This has led to higher freight costs, constrained chemical production, and uneven fuel distribution across Europe. The crisis highlights the vulnerability of Europe's industrial system, which relies heavily on the Rhine for transport. The critical chokepoint at Kaub, where water levels fell below 10 cm, has fragmented the river corridor, limiting cargo movement and forcing specialized vessels to operate. Chemical companies like BASF and INEOS face production cuts due to restricted feedstock flows, while refineries struggle with storage surpluses and higher transportation costs. Although weak demand has mitigated some impacts, the situation underscores the risks of relying on river transport and the potential for further disruption if water levels decline again. The article warns that a recovery in manufacturing or increased demand could exacerbate the crisis, even with modest improvements in river conditions. A potential super El Niño event could further worsen the situation by reducing Alpine snowmelt and increasing summer droughts, threatening the Rhine's water levels in future years.
source.title: Rhine Water Levels Rise Slightly, But Industrial Supply Chains Remain Strained

source.summary: The U.S. dollar weakened slightly as investors considered expanded sanctions against Iran and Treasury efforts to ease pressure on longer-dated bonds. Treasury Secretary Scott Bessent's announcement to double repurchases of longer-dated bonds raised concerns about dollar debasement. The dollar index fell 0.07% to 98.92, while the euro and Canadian dollar rose. Canada imposed retaliatory tariffs on $20 billion in U.S. imports, escalating trade tensions. Bitcoin briefly surpassed $80,000 amid dollar weakness. Analysts noted mixed signals in the market, with Fed rate hike expectations easing.
source.title: U.S. dollar dips as sanctions and Treasury actions influence markets

source.summary: A graphic circulating on social media falsely claims Prime Minister Narendra Modi made a statement about distributing laddus in his village on Independence Day. The claim is false, as no such statement by Modi was found through keyword searches or verification of news reports. The graphic, attributed to Nav Bharat Times, was checked against the newspaper's official content and social media accounts, where no matching statement was found. The font used in the graphic also did not match the newspaper's style. The article concludes the graphic is fake and that Modi did not make the claimed statement.
source.title: PM Modi's claimed statement on distributing laddus on Independence Day is fake

source.summary: Delhi Police have registered a case of abetment to suicide against unidentified individuals linked to the death of a 31-year-old IIT Delhi M.Sc. Physics student who allegedly jumped from a building on campus on August 22. The student was found dead at the institute's hospital after being rushed there following the incident. Police collected evidence, seized a mobile phone, and are examining counselling records. No suicide note was found, and the circumstances surrounding the death, including any potential involvement of others, are under investigation. IIT Delhi expressed grief and stated it is supporting the bereaved family.
source.title: Delhi Police Investigate Abetment to Suicide in IIT Delhi Student's Death

source.summary: Indian jewelers Kalyan Jewellers, Tanishq, and Joyalukkas have expanded cash-for-gold services, bringing the practice into the organized retail sector. The move comes as gold prices rose to ₹1.62 lakh per 10 gm in Mumbai. Kalyan Jewellers reported that cash-for-gold accounted for double-digit revenue in the June quarter, up from single digits previously. Analysts noted that inflationary pressures are prompting consumers to liquidate household gold. Internationally, gold prices retreated slightly after hitting three-month highs, with traders awaiting US inflation data and Federal Reserve statements.
source.title: Indian jewelers expand cash-for-gold services amid rising prices

source.summary: President Trump announced the lowering of American flags for seven days in honor of Dolly Parton, who died at 80. The decision reflects her significant cultural impact beyond country music. Parton's family, represented by her nephew Brian Seaver, announced her death, highlighting her role as a family figure and her legacy of opening opportunities for others. Seaver shared personal anecdotes, including Parton's wish to rest in a 'beautiful bed of plush cotton,' reflecting her humor and self-awareness. Parton's career spanned decades, from her Tennessee roots to global fame, with contributions to music, film, and philanthropy, including the Imagination Library. Her legacy continues through tributes and the preservation of her work.
source.title: Trump orders national flag lowering for Dolly Parton

source.summary: Former Chief of Defence Staff General Anil Chauhan revealed that Pakistan sought commercial satellite imagery, including from Chinese providers, to evaluate the impact of its strikes during Operation Sindoor. Despite efforts spanning several days, Pakistan failed to find evidence of damage to its intended targets. Chauhan noted that while satellite imagery is accessible through US and Chinese companies, it requires contracts and payment, with delays in availability. The lack of evidence fueled speculation in Pakistan that information may have been withheld, possibly due to Indian pressure.
source.title: General Chauhan details Pakistan's failed satellite efforts to assess Operation Sindoor strikes

source.summary: The Uttar Pradesh Cabinet approved transferring six hectares of Gram Sabha land near Saman Bird Sanctuary to the Tourism Department. The site will be renamed Mayank Rishi Bird Sanctuary. The move aims to enhance tourist facilities, promote birdwatching, and connect the area with international tourism circuits. The government plans to develop infrastructure like watchtowers and solar lighting. Saman Bird Sanctuary, a Ramsar Site, attracts migratory birds from across the globe. The decision was made during a Cabinet meeting chaired by Chief Minister Yogi Adityanath.
source.title: UP government transfers land to develop Saman Bird Sanctuary tourism

source.summary: Motorola engineer Dr Martin Cooper made the first mobile phone call on April 3, 1973, to Joel Engel of Bell Laboratories. The call, made from a portable device on a New York City street, demonstrated the feasibility of a personal, handheld mobile phone. Cooper aimed to prevent AT&T from monopolizing mobile communications and emphasized the importance of personal freedom in communication. The call marked a pivotal moment in the development of mobile technology, leading to the eventual release of the Motorola DynaTAC 8000X in 1984.
source.title: Martin Cooper made first mobile phone call to rival in 1973

source.summary: Elon Musk's SpaceX plans to invest $100 billion in a new spaceport in Louisiana, set to be its fourth and largest launch site. The facility, located in Vermilion Parish, aims to support thousands of Starship launches annually and boost satellite deployment. Louisiana officials hailed the project as transformative, while environmental advocates raised concerns about coastal impact. SpaceX pledged to preserve land and engage with communities, with construction expected to begin in 2027.
source.title: SpaceX to develop new Louisiana spaceport for Starship launches

source.summary: Franklin Templeton's portfolio manager Sara Araghi emphasized that Nvidia needs to provide detailed information on capital deployment and spending sustainability, beyond just reporting an earnings beat. She highlighted the discrepancy between Nvidia's forward price-earnings ratio and projected growth, noting that markets are pricing in a slowdown despite continued revenue expansion. Araghi also mentioned Nvidia's strategy of raising prices to offset rising memory costs and the importance of showing earnings growth to reassure investors about free cash flow and stock buybacks. Nvidia is set to report earnings after the market close, with analysts warning that a typical beat may not be enough to boost sentiment.
source.title: Franklin's Araghi Urges Nvidia to Provide Capital Deployment Details Beyond Earnings Beat

source.summary: Prashant Kishor challenged Bihar Chief Minister Samrat Choudhary and Leader of Opposition Tejashwi Yadav to sit for their Class 10 exams together, responding to Education Minister Mithilesh Tiwari's advice to Yadav to clear matriculation before supporting student protests. Kishor urged both leaders to demonstrate their academic capability, referencing Yadav's failed Class 9 and Choudhary's past affidavit stating he was only a Class 7 pass. The challenge was made during a political debate over educational qualifications and youth expectations.
source.title: Bihar leaders challenged to take Class 10 exams together

source.summary: Dolly Parton, a legendary American country singer, songwriter, and actress, died at 80, according to her family. She sold over 100 million records globally and won 11 Grammy Awards, including a Lifetime Achievement Award. Parton began writing songs at six, with her first being 'Little Tiny Tasseltop.' She performed at the Grand Ole Opry at 13 and later became a solo artist, with 'I Will Always Love You' becoming a global hit after Whitney Houston's rendition. Parton also acted in films like '9 to 5' and built a business empire, including Dollywood. She was known for her philanthropy, including a $1 million donation to Vanderbilt University for Covid-19 vaccine research.
source.title: Dolly Parton, Country Music Icon, Dies at 80

source.summary: Food safety officials in Bengaluru inspected 10 elite clubs to check compliance with hygiene and food safety regulations. Inspections focused on food handling, storage, labelling, and cleanliness, revealing several shortcomings at the KSCA Club and Mahalakshmi Layout Club. Issues included inadequate hygiene among staff, improper storage of vegetarian and non-vegetarian items, and missing label information on packaged foods. Officials noted unhygienic conditions in utensil cleaning areas and lack of hot water. Further action will depend on the findings and compliance with corrective measures.
source.title: Health officials inspect Bengaluru clubs for food safety compliance

source.summary: Dick's Sporting Goods experienced a 28% stock decline after reporting second-quarter earnings below expectations. The company missed analyst forecasts of $3.78 EPS with $5.65 billion in sales, achieving only $3.53 EPS and $5.6 billion in revenue. Weak footwear demand, a key driver of customer traffic, contributed to the underperformance. While same-store sales grew 4.9%, profits fell due to lower margins. The company also revised its full-year earnings guidance downward to $11-$12 per share from $14.20, and sales forecasts to $22.2 billion from $22.4 billion. Investors are now closely watching footwear sales and the company's ability to improve its outlook.
source.title: Dick's Sporting Goods faces 28% stock drop due to earnings miss and footwear concerns

source.summary: The Ministry of Statistics and Programme Implementation (MoSPI) reported a cumulative cost overrun of ₹3,40,504 crore in infrastructure projects exceeding ₹150 crore. Out of 1,775 monitored projects across 17 ministries, the revised total cost reached ₹37,10,642 crore compared to the original ₹33,70,138 crore. The report noted that 675 projects (38%) achieved over 80% physical progress, while 305 (17%) completed over 80% financially. The Transport & Logistics sector had the highest number of projects (1,246) with a revised cost of ₹19.81 lakh crore, highlighting its role in connectivity-driven growth. The Ministry of Road Transport & Highways led with 993 projects (56%) and a 26% share of the total revised cost.
source.title: MoSPI reports ₹3.4 lakh crore cost overrun in major infrastructure projects

source.summary: Industry participants are calling for tighter eligibility and suitability norms for futures and options trading in India, following SEBI's regulatory interventions that failed to curb excessive retail speculation. Data shows while the number of individual traders fell, trading behavior remained unchanged, with 97% of retail activity concentrated in short-term contracts and 87.7% of traders ending the fiscal year with losses. Experts argue that suitability checks and investor profiling could better protect retail investors than product-level restrictions. SEBI faces a balancing act between addressing retail losses and maintaining market liquidity, as derivatives activity significantly contributes to the revenues of exchanges and intermediaries. The debate highlights the need for a regulatory framework that ensures investor protection without stifling participation.
source.title: Retail F&O losses drive push for stricter eligibility rules in derivatives trading

source.summary: Neurostellar, a Chennai-based startup, introduced its Orbit headband at a hybrid chess tournament in IIT Madras Research Park. The device uses EEG and PPG sensors to monitor brain and heart activity, providing real-time insights into stress, focus, and mental fatigue. The data is analyzed by algorithms developed with NIMHANS scientists to calculate cognitive endurance scores. The headband, priced at $250, is in pre-order with customers including athletes and CEOs. It also offers an app for problem-solving and deep work, alongside a coaching program to enhance cognitive performance.
source.title: Neurostellar's headband tracks cognitive endurance during chess tournament

source.summary: Tata Steel has received interim relief against a ₹1,755 crore mining demand notice from the Jharkhand government. The demand, issued by the District Mining Office in Ramgarh, alleges excess coal extraction of 16.24 million tonnes at the West Bokaro Colliery between 2000-01 and 2006-07. Tata Steel challenged the notice, arguing it lacked justification. The Revisional Authority admitted the company's revision application and directed authorities not to take coercive steps during the review. Tata Group Chairman N Chandrasekaran previously announced a ₹11,000 crore investment in Jharkhand to develop advanced-grade steel at the Jamshedpur facility.
source.title: Tata Steel Granted Interim Relief Against ₹1,755 Crore Mining Demand Notice

source.summary: The Indian government's ethanol-blended petrol (EBP) policy, particularly the push for E20 fuel, has sparked widespread public discontent. Critics argue that E20 results in lower fuel efficiency, higher repair costs, and increased expenses for users, despite official claims of benefits like reduced oil imports and support for farmers. The government has faced mounting pressure but has largely dismissed concerns, attributing mileage drops to factors like driving habits and vehicle conditions. Meanwhile, distillers benefit from guaranteed purchase agreements and subsidies, while farmers see little direct gain. The policy has also led to increased maize imports and concerns about food security, as land and water resources are diverted from food crops to ethanol production. The article highlights the uneven distribution of costs and benefits, with users bearing the brunt of the policy's negative impacts.
source.title: Ethanol Blending Policy: Users Bear Costs While Distillers and Farmers See Limited Gains

source.summary: Young activists in India are challenging the government's education system, demanding better infrastructure and accountability. The movement, led by Gen Alpha, began with protests over examination irregularities and escalated into a nationwide campaign for school improvements. The Cockroach Janta Party's 'School Thik Karo' initiative has sparked resistance, highlighting the political significance of the campaign. Despite lacking a central command, the protests have spread across multiple states, demanding basic facilities like classrooms, toilets, and teachers. The movement reflects a shift in Indian politics, where issues like education can unite people across identities, challenging the state's ability to suppress dissent. The article draws parallels to historical uprisings, suggesting that the current movement could have far-reaching implications for governance.
source.title: Gen Alpha demands accountability through education reforms

source.summary: IBM has acquired HRL Laboratories, a research institution specializing in quantum technologies, to advance its quantum computing initiatives. The acquisition aims to leverage HRL's expertise in silicon-spin qubit engineering, which shares fabrication foundations with superconducting qubits. Spin qubits use electron spin states to encode quantum information, with HRL's exchange only qubit architecture utilizing three electrons in quantum dots to represent computational states. This approach offers advantages such as manufacturability at scale, high coherence times, and ease of control. HRL's recent demonstration of a silicon-spin quantum computer with 18 qubits highlights progress in the field. IBM's Director of Research, Jay Gambetta, emphasized that HRL's technologies will strengthen IBM's long-term vision for quantum computing, including quantum sensing and networking applications.
source.title: IBM Acquires HRL Laboratories to Expand Quantum Computing Research

source.summary: The PyTorch Foundation has expanded to host six projects, including PyTorch, vLLM, DeepSpeed, Ray, Helion, and Safetensors, aiming to foster collaboration across AI domains. In Q2 2025, PyTorch 2.13 was released with performance improvements and hardware support, while vLLM introduced Model Runner V2 and outlined a 2026 roadmap. DeepSpeed integrated Torch.xpu and received academic recognition, Ray enhanced hardware support and model scaling, Helion improved cross-hardware performance with new backends, and Safetensors introduced GIL-free serialization. The Foundation continues to engage the community through events and collaborations.
source.title: PyTorch Foundation Expands to Support Six AI Projects with New Updates

source.summary: A proposed £14.7bn hyperscale datacentre in North Ockendon, London, would emit 1.2m tonnes of CO₂ annually, equivalent to 8,480 flights from London to New York, according to planning documents. The East Havering Data Centre Campus (EHDCC) would use 218 hectares of green belt land and consume 2.65bn kWh of electricity annually, surpassing the demand of over 1m UK households. Developers claim the project does not align with net zero targets by 2050, while critics argue it threatens decarbonisation efforts and local resources. The site would be powered by a 600MVA connection to the National Grid, requiring major upgrades by 2033. Environmental groups and residents oppose the development, citing loss of farmland and wildlife habitats. The government has designated datacentres as critical infrastructure, with demand for electricity connections expected to rise sharply as AI expansion accelerates.
source.title: London datacentre project faces net zero compatibility concerns

source.summary: Promptwatch reports a significant rise in ChatGPT searches using the site:operator following the GPT-5.6 update. The percentage of queries with the operator jumped to 16-17% on August 8, up from 0.3-0.5% previously. OpenAI's August 6 announcement highlighted improved reliability and focused answers. Promptwatch notes the change aligns with the GPT-5.6 rollout, though OpenAI obscures system prompts. Recent tracking shows reduced likelihood of Reddit being used in searches, though system prompt updates remain unclear.
source.title: OpenAI's GPT-5.6 update increases use of site:operator in ChatGPT searches

source.summary: Researchers have discovered a method to trick Grok, Elon Musk's large language model, into leaking user data by encrypting harmful commands. The attack involves hosting encrypted instructions alongside decryption keys and plain text guidance, allowing Grok to execute them when summarizing content. Despite being informed in June, the model continued to exfiltrate data. This highlights the persistent vulnerability of LLMs to prompt injections, as guardrails fail to block encrypted malicious inputs. Security experts warn that such attacks underscore the need for stronger safeguards against AI exploitation.
source.title: Grok leaks user data via encrypted malicious instructions

source.summary: Virgin Atlantic is employing generative AI-powered market models to improve its pricing strategies and revenue management. These models analyze real-time data on demand, competition, and market conditions to make granular commercial decisions. Dominic Kennedy, senior vice president of revenue management at Virgin Atlantic, highlights the models' ability to evaluate positioning relative to competitors and market dynamics. The models are trained on high-resolution numerical data and designed to simulate complex financial environments, enabling faster and more accurate pricing adjustments. The article was produced by Insights, a custom content arm of MIT Technology Review, and includes contributions from human writers and analysts.
source.title: Airline uses AI models to enhance dynamic pricing and revenue management

source.summary: The National Highway Traffic Safety Administration (NHTSA) has expanded its investigation into over 1.1 million GM vehicles, including EVs, due to reports of brake assist failures. Drivers reported a 'Brake System Failure' message appearing after hard braking, with some incidents resulting in crashes and injuries. GM attributed the issue to alleged spindle fractures in the eBoost system, stating that anti-lock brakes and other safety features remain functional until the vehicle stops. The ODI is now conducting an engineering analysis and has broadened the scope to include multiple models and years of GM vehicles equipped with the eBoost system.
source.title: NHTSA expands investigation into GM vehicles over brake assist failures

source.summary: TotalEnergies, through CEO Patrick Pouyanné, announced investments in two oil pipelines to bypass the Strait of Hormuz, supporting Abu Dhabi’s Fujairah export route expansion and an Iraqi-Syrian crude pipeline. The move follows disruptions during the Iran war, which highlighted the vulnerability of Hormuz. The UAE’s Fujairah pipeline, capable of carrying 1.8 million barrels per day, is set to double its capacity. The Iraq-Syria pipeline, estimated at $15 billion, aims to provide an alternative Mediterranean route for Iraqi crude. Pouyanné emphasized the need for equity investment in alternative routes, as global oil supply through Hormuz dropped to a fifth before the conflict.
source.title: TotalEnergies invests in oil pipelines to bypass Hormuz

source.summary: French researchers have developed very-low-bandgap thermophotovoltaic (TPV) cells featuring a barrier layer to suppress dark current, enabling operation at higher temperatures. The cells, made of InAs/InAsSb type-II superlattice absorber material, are designed to convert infrared radiation from heat sources into electricity. The barrier layer, composed of aluminum arsenide antimonide (AlAsSb), reduces unwanted current flow and allows the cells to function without cryogenic cooling. Testing showed the barrier cells outperformed conventional PIN structures at temperatures above 150 K, with improved photovoltaic performance under an 800°C thermal emitter. The study, published in Solar Energy Materials and Solar Cells, highlights potential applications in thermal energy conversion and industrial heat recovery.
source.title: French researchers develop high-temperature thermophotovoltaic cells with reduced dark current

source.summary: Hungary's MVM operators announced the restart of nuclear units at the Paks plant, citing improved Danube water levels and completed construction work. The prime minister emphasized the need for new climate and water management laws to address the country's drought crisis. Romania's Cernavoda nuclear plant was forced to shut down due to low water levels, prompting emergency measures including dredging and an aqueduct project. Bulgaria's Energy Minister outlined plans to build a levee near the Kozloduy plant, while also exploring water transfers from reservoirs to maintain operations. The article highlights the impact of climate change on nuclear power operations and the measures being taken to mitigate its effects.
source.title: Hungary and Romania address climate crisis with new laws and infrastructure projects

source.summary: In the second quarter of 2026, hybrid electric vehicles accounted for 16% of U.S. light-duty vehicle sales, up from 12% in the previous year. Battery electric vehicle sales dropped to 6% of new vehicle sales, down from 7% in the same period in 2025, following the expiration of federal tax credits in September 2025. Plug-in hybrid electric vehicle sales also fell, from 1.9% to 1.4%. The decline in battery electric vehicle sales continued into 2026, with market share in the luxury segment dropping from 22% to 14%. Despite their smaller share of the overall fleet, electric vehicles still represent a growing portion of the U.S. vehicle market.
source.title: Hybrid vehicle sales increase as battery electric sales decline post-tax credit expiration

source.summary: African gas stations are transforming by adopting solar-powered battery swapping and off-grid charging solutions, driven by the dominance of commercial two- and three-wheelers and unreliable centralized grids. Unlike Western models, African stations prioritize rapid battery exchanges and localized renewable energy to meet the needs of high-mileage urban fleets. Companies like Vivo Energy and TotalEnergies are partnering with clean mobility firms to enable quick battery swaps, reducing downtime for drivers. Research from ETH Zurich and others shows that off-grid solar and storage can achieve cost parity with traditional vehicles by 2040. In South Africa, infrastructure developers are building microgrids along highways to provide renewable electricity. Despite progress, the continent faces a significant infrastructure gap, with fewer than 1,000 public charging stations serving over 400,000 electric vehicles. The shift reflects a decentralized, resilient model that is reshaping Africa's transportation landscape.
source.title: African Gas Stations Shift to Solar-Powered Battery Swaps and Off-Grid Charging

source.summary: Tomi Fadipe, Global Vertical Strategy Lead for Regulated Industries at Zebra Technologies, has over 15 years of experience in telecommunication infrastructure and engineering management. She develops and executes growth plans for critical infrastructure entities, including utilities and public safety. Fadipe combines her passion for data, ingenuity, and engineering to create reliable and scalable technology solutions. These solutions empower frontline workers to deliver safe, efficient, and sustainable services.
source.title: Tomi Fadipe Leads Strategy at Zebra Technologies

source.summary: Utilities are increasingly adopting virtualization to enhance substation protection. This approach shifts protection functions from hardware to software, allowing for flexible deployment and easier updates. Centralized computing platforms reduce physical space needs and simplify maintenance by consolidating devices. Digital testing of protection schemes minimizes field risks. Enhanced cybersecurity is achieved through centralized management and coordinated patching. Utilities report lower costs, improved scalability, and faster response to grid demands.
source.title: Utilities adopt virtualization for flexible substation protection

source.summary: Community solar projects allow multiple customers to share energy from a single off-site solar array, offering an alternative to rooftop installations. The article outlines two main participation models: ownership, where customers buy panels or shares, and subscription, where third parties own the system and members subscribe for energy at lower rates. Administration models include utility-sponsored, nonprofit, and special-purpose entity (SPE) structures, each with distinct legal and financial implications. The development of community solar involves navigating complex securities laws, which influence participation rules and project structures. The article highlights the growing importance of community solar in expanding access to clean energy, particularly for low-income and underserved populations, while emphasizing the need for legal compliance and professional guidance in project development.
source.title: Community Solar Explained: Models, Administration, and Legal Considerations

source.summary: Hungary's Paks nuclear plant, which had to shut down three reactors due to low Danube water levels, is set to resume full operations by August 28. Emergency engineering works and the release of water from the Ráckeve lock system raised the water level by 15-20 centimeters, allowing the plant to restart its six idle turbines. Prime Minister Péter Magyar noted that halting operations would have cost HUF 50 billion monthly. The government used 200,000 tons of donated rock to support the effort, significantly reducing costs. Meanwhile, Bulgaria's Kozloduy nuclear plant is reducing capacity for the first time due to extreme weather conditions.
source.title: Hungary's Paks nuclear plant resumes operations after water level rise

source.summary: Ørsted plans to fully commission three offshore wind farms by 2026. The projects are expected to generate significant renewable energy. The company announced the timeline during a recent press conference. Details about the farms' locations and capacities were not disclosed. The development aligns with Ørsted's strategy to expand its renewable energy portfolio.
source.title: Ørsted's Three Offshore Wind Farms to Begin Operations in 2026

source.summary: A US-based company has been selected to develop a 2.13 gigawatt offshore wind cluster in South Korea. The project, part of a broader initiative to expand renewable energy infrastructure, aims to contribute significantly to the country's clean energy goals. The company announced the selection, highlighting its expertise in large-scale wind energy projects. The development is expected to create local jobs and boost South Korea's renewable energy capacity. The project's timeline and financial details were not disclosed in the announcement.
source.title: US Firm Chosen to Build 2.13 GW Offshore Wind Project in South Korea

source.summary: Emerson's Ryan Franks highlights the evolution of BESS asset management, emphasizing performance over safety and the importance of data-driven tools. He notes that imbalance adjustment is critical for maximizing revenue, with lithium iron phosphate (LFP) batteries outperforming degradation expectations. Franks also discusses the shift toward standardized human-machine interfaces and interoperability in utility-scale storage, driven by data centers and diverse generation assets. AI is seen as a transformative tool for pattern recognition and operational optimization, while BESS asset managers must adapt to varying regional regulations across U.S. grids. The Battery Asset Management Summit USA 2026 will explore these topics further.
source.title: Emerson's Approach to Maximizing BESS Returns and Addressing Interoperability Challenges

source.summary: Sage Geosystems has placed its SMECI geothermal facility in service after over 120 days of operation, during which it evaluated subsurface performance metrics. The company reported water losses of less than 10%, indicating efficient water retention. Sage's GeoTwin modeling tool accurately predicted facility behavior, enhancing confidence in future geothermal projects. The results validate the company's EGS approach, reducing development risks and supporting scalable geothermal power. Sage plans to optimize performance at SMECI and apply insights to larger projects.
source.title: Sage Geosystems operationalizes SMECI geothermal facility after 120 days of testing
