source.summary: The Securities and Exchange Board of India (SEBI) has introduced an Information Technology Resilience Index (ITRI) to evaluate the IT systems of market infrastructure institutions (MIIs). The index assesses MIIs across nine parameters, with availability and security each carrying 20% weightage. MIIs must calculate the index every six months and submit comparative analyses to their governing bodies. SEBI also requires the development of an Early Warning System to detect potential performance issues. The framework, currently in beta, aims for full implementation by February 28, 2027.
source.title: SEBI launches IT Resilience Index for market infrastructure institutions

source.summary: Apar Gupta, a digital rights activist, highlights the political control over social media in India, particularly affecting Gen Z activists. He notes the lack of transparency and legal basis for digital censorship and surveillance, emphasizing that the state must pass laws for such activities. Gupta criticizes the government's use of IT Rules and executive notifications to control content, which lack parliamentary authority. He also discusses the impact of social media on elections, noting how opposition parties connect better with young voters through authentic engagement. Gupta stresses the need for institutional capacity and evidence-based approaches to understand social media's role, rather than paternalistic regulation.
source.title: Apar Gupta discusses political control of social media and digital rights in India

source.summary: The article reports on a series of violent attacks by goons linked to the BJP and other groups against workers of the Cockroach Janta Party (CJP) and students in various Indian states. In Rajasthan, goons attacked CJP workers, smashing their vehicles and beating them, while the state education minister defended the violence, claiming it was due to disruptions in education. In West Bengal, goons allegedly affiliated with the ABVP attacked Jadavpur University, prompting BJP leaders to threaten violence. The state chief minister, Suvendu Adhikari, instead called for nationalism and threatened to eliminate the 'tukde-tukde gang'. Similar attacks occurred in Pune and Uttar Pradesh, with goons targeting CJP workers, students, and even police officers. The article criticizes the BJP and its allies for erasing the distinction between the people and goons, suggesting a broader 'Dimagi goondaism' that produces street-level violence. It highlights how laws against cow slaughter, 'love jihad', and anti-conversion are enforced by goons, while BJP leaders and RSS functionaries remain in positions of power, shaping public discourse without participating in the violence.
source.title: BJP-linked goons attack CJP workers and students across India

source.summary: The western hoolock gibbon, India's only ape, is critically endangered due to habitat loss and hunting. Found in northeastern India and neighboring regions, the species relies on contiguous forests for survival. An estimated 3,000 remain, with 2,600 in India. Conservationists warn that habitat fragmentation creates 'habitat islands,' leading to inbreeding and reduced reproductive fitness. The species is protected under India's Wildlife Act, but illegal pet trade and deforestation continue to threaten its survival.
source.title: Western hoolock gibbon faces extinction due to habitat loss and hunting

source.summary: Researchers in Kaziranga National Park and Tiger Reserve identified at least 55 greater hog badgers using camera trap data from the 2026 All India Tiger Estimation. The study, conducted by Kaziranga Tiger Cell and partners, found the species occupies nearly half the surveyed area, suggesting it may be more widespread than previously thought. The assessment used a Royle-Nichols model to account for detection probabilities, noting the actual population could be higher due to low survey effectiveness. Greater hog badgers, listed as vulnerable, are elusive nocturnal mammals that play a key role in ecosystem health through soil disturbance and nutrient cycling. Their presence indicates a pristine environment, and their behavior during Kaziranga’s annual floods remains an area for further study.
source.title: Kaziranga study reveals 55 greater hog badgers through camera traps

source.summary: SpaceXAI will deploy NVIDIA Vera CPUs to accelerate its agentic AI applications and expand its AI infrastructure. The CPUs are designed to handle CPU-intensive tasks like tool use and data processing, enabling faster AI agent performance. SpaceXAI plans to extend this technology to space with its first Starmind satellite, using an optimized NVIDIA Vera Rubin NVL72 system. NVIDIA's Ian Buck highlighted Vera's role in enabling real-time AI actions, while SpaceXAI's Mike Nicolls emphasized its efficiency in combining CPU and GPU performance. The Vera Rubin platform is optimized for massive AI scale, offering high bandwidth and energy efficiency. This collaboration aims to bring accelerated computing from Earth to orbital environments, maintaining a unified architecture across different computing domains.
source.title: SpaceXAI Deploys NVIDIA Vera CPUs to Power Agentic AI and Expand to Orbital Computing

source.summary: The article discusses the growing issue of 'loudcasting'—the practice of playing phone content aloud in public spaces—on transportation networks in the UK. It traces the evolution of this behavior from 'sodcasting' in the 2000s to its current form, driven by 5G technology and social media. The author argues that while loudcasting was once a form of public expression by teenagers, the current version is more antisocial and individualistic, often involving adults. The piece critiques the effectiveness of punitive measures like fines, citing France's approach as an example, and advocates for 'nudge messaging' as a more humane and effective strategy. Transport for London's campaigns are highlighted as successful models of this approach. The author suggests that social consensus and gentle persuasion can help reduce loudcasting without resorting to harsh penalties.
source.title: British authorities tackle loudcasting with nudging strategies

source.summary: Google has integrated AI Overviews into its search bar, providing summarized responses above traditional links. This change has altered user browsing habits, with many relying on AI summaries instead of visiting websites directly. Media companies are suing Google, claiming AI-driven traffic shifts harm their ad revenue. Google asserts that overall traffic remains stable, countering claims of decline. The company continues to expand its AI features, positioning them as a major upgrade to the search experience.
source.title: Google's AI Overviews Shift User Behavior and Spark Legal Challenges

source.summary: Australia's music charts will exclude songs primarily or wholly created by AI, effective this week. The Australian Recording Industry Association (ARIA) stated the rule aims to promote human artistry amid growing concerns over AI-generated content. The decision follows controversy over a DJ's AI-assisted cover of Madonna's song, which initially topped charts before AI credits were added. ARIA allows limited AI use for mastering and production but requires human involvement in songwriting and performance. Artists must declare AI use, and chart positions may be adjusted if AI dominance is later found. The move aligns with global efforts to regulate AI in music, including similar actions in Sweden and upcoming guidelines in Latin America and other regions.
source.title: Australia bans AI-generated music from charts to preserve human artistry

source.summary: NVIDIA's ALCHEMI Toolkit, combined with AI coding agents, streamlines materials simulation by reducing computational barriers. The toolkit provides PyTorch-native building blocks for GPU-accelerated workflows, while AI agents generate code from natural-language prompts. However, the agents require specific API patterns to function correctly, which are provided through 'skills' and reference files. The article outlines a workflow where researchers define simulations with precise prompts, leading to reliable code generation and validation on NVIDIA H200 GPUs. Key findings include the importance of prompt specificity in achieving structured code and reusability, as well as the necessity of validation against independent references. The study also highlights the limitations of MLIP models and the need for scientific judgment in ensuring physically meaningful simulations.
source.title: NVIDIA ALCHEMI Toolkit and AI agents enable accurate materials simulation through structured prompts

source.summary: NVIDIA's cuML and cuVS 25.06 now support multi-GPU UMAP, enabling faster processing of massive datasets. The new feature distributes the all-neighbors kNN graph construction across multiple GPUs, significantly reducing training time while maintaining embedding quality. This approach partitions data into clusters and computes local kNN graphs, which are then merged into a global graph. Key hyperparameters, knn_n_clusters and knn_overlap_factor, control the trade-off between speed, memory, and accuracy. The method allows UMAP to handle datasets with tens to hundreds of millions of vectors in minutes, rather than hours or days. Benchmarks show up to 74x speedup on the 106M vector MIRACL dataset using eight H100 GPUs, completing the task in 8 minutes. The technique preserves neighborhood relationships, ensuring high-quality visualizations at scale. This advancement enhances applications like topic modeling and single-cell analysis by enabling faster iteration and exploration.
source.title: NVIDIA Introduces Multi-GPU UMAP for Faster Large-Scale Data Analysis

source.summary: NVIDIA has partnered with Apollo, BlackRock, Blackstone, Brookfield, Goldman Sachs, and KKR to establish AI compute infrastructure financing platforms. The initiative aims to mobilize over $500 billion in third-party capital to support AI infrastructure development. The collaboration involves leading financial institutions with significant assets under management, ranging from $1.05 trillion to over $1.3 trillion. NVIDIA emphasized its strategic partnerships and the potential benefits of the financial platforms, though the article noted that these statements are forward-looking and subject to risks and uncertainties. The partnership is expected to drive growth in AI infrastructure, though the exact terms and timing of the agreements remain to be finalized.
source.title: NVIDIA Partners With Apollo, BlackRock, Blackstone, Brookfield, Goldman Sachs and KKR to Establish AI Compute Infrastructure Financing Platforms to Mobilize Over $500 Billion of Third-Party Capital

source.summary: Baseten has integrated with Hugging Face Hub as an Inference Provider, enabling serverless model inference. The integration allows developers to use a wide range of AI models, including popular open-weight LLMs like DeepSeek V4 Flash, through Baseten's platform. Users can set API keys, order providers by preference, and choose between custom key and routed by HF modes for billing. Baseten is available via Hugging Face SDKs for Python and JavaScript, with examples provided for using DeepSeek V4 Flash. PRO users receive $2 in monthly inference credits, while free users have a limited quota.
source.title: Baseten integrates with Hugging Face for serverless model inference

source.summary: The article explores how enterprise AI is encountering challenges similar to those faced by the aviation industry, particularly around GPU utilization. Just as airlines' success depends on aircraft utilization, AI companies' performance hinges on how effectively they use their GPU resources. GPUs, like aircraft, incur costs continuously but generate revenue only during compute tasks. The article highlights that while owning more GPUs provides capacity, it's the efficient use of existing hardware that determines competitive advantage. As AI scales, the scarcity of GPUs has shifted from being a hardware issue to a strategic one, with companies like Anthropic and Meta making multi-gigawatt commitments across multiple vendors. The article further explains that the economics of AI production differ significantly from proof-of-concept stages, with cost scaling linearly with token usage. Enterprises are increasingly acquiring GPUs to reduce variable costs, but this introduces new challenges in managing idle capacity and optimizing workload distribution. The article concludes by introducing the emerging discipline of GPU Management, which focuses on continuous, real-time allocation of GPU resources to maximize ROI, moving beyond one-time provisioning decisions.
source.title: Enterprise AI Faces GPU Utilization Challenges as Hardware Scarcity Persists

source.summary: Bailey Flanigan, now a faculty member at MIT, traces her career path to a lifelong curiosity that led her through diverse fields like medicine, public health, and economics. Her early interests in creative problem-solving and social inequality shaped her academic trajectory, leading to a focus on using computational tools to enhance democratic participation. Flanigan's work includes developing algorithms for fair citizen assemblies, addressing representation gaps in decision-making processes. Her research, now deployed on panelot.org, aims to make political processes more transparent and legitimate. Flanigan credits mentors and persistent encouragement for her academic growth, emphasizing the importance of interdisciplinary approaches in tackling complex societal challenges.
source.title: Bailey Flanigan's interdisciplinary journey shapes research on democratic participation

source.summary: Researchers from MIT and other institutions have developed a system called GIFT that enhances vision-language models' ability to convert 2D designs into accurate 3D CAD models. The system uses data augmentation to improve model performance by learning from its own mistakes, generating better training data without requiring human intervention. GIFT outperforms existing methods, producing more accurate CAD programs with significantly less computational cost. The framework allows engineers to set compute budgets and let the system refine models autonomously. The research, presented at the International Conference on Machine Learning, aims to streamline rapid prototyping and improve design efficiency in engineering applications.
source.title: MIT researchers develop AI system to improve 2D-to-3D CAD conversion

source.summary: IBM has outlined three key metrics—programmable qubits, qubit operations, and maximum circuits per second—to evaluate the performance of quantum computers. Programmable qubits measure scale by indicating how many qubits users can directly control. Qubit operations, or 'QuOps,' assess quality by measuring the number of complex operations a system can reliably execute. Maximum circuits per second, or circuit throughput, measures speed and computational efficiency. These metrics apply across various quantum computing hardware modalities, including superconducting and trapped-ion systems. IBM emphasizes that while the framework for evaluation remains consistent, future benchmarks may shift as quantum computers advance, with T-gate counts potentially replacing two-qubit operations as the primary measure of computational capability. The metrics aim to provide a clear understanding of quantum hardware's scale, quality, and speed, helping users compare systems and track progress toward more advanced quantum computing capabilities.
source.title: IBM outlines three metrics to evaluate quantum computer performance

source.summary: Qiskit SDK v2.5 introduces new compiler features, expanded C API capabilities, and significant transpiler performance improvements. The C API now supports classical control flow inspection, closing a gap in C-Python parity. A new multi-representation compiler framework enables custom pipelines for fault-tolerant quantum computing workflows. The Qiskit Runtime Service is renamed to IBM Quantum Compute Service to clarify the distinction between the open-source SDK and IBM's managed service. The v1.x series has reached end-of-life, with users advised to upgrade to v2.x for continued support. Key updates include dedicated pass managers for Pauli-based computation and Clifford+T representations, along with speedups from LightSabre improvements and multithreading enhancements.
source.title: Qiskit v2.5 introduces compiler enhancements, C API improvements, and platform renaming

source.summary: Google Cloud researchers propose linear elastic caching, a method that dynamically adjusts cache size to minimize costs while maintaining performance. The approach frames cache eviction as a ski rental problem, using lightweight machine learning to balance memory usage and cache misses. Traditional fixed-size caching leads to either underutilized memory or poor performance, but linear elastic caching treats memory as a variable cost. By assigning time-to-live (TTL) values to cached data based on access patterns, the system optimizes cache size in real-time. Tests on Google's Spanner database showed a 0.5% increase in cache misses, which had minimal impact on I/O costs. The method outperformed fixed-size caches across various workloads, offering significant cost savings as memory prices rise relative to cache miss costs. The technique was presented at CIDR 2025 and involves collaboration with Tamas Sarlos and Ravi Kumar.
source.title: Google introduces linear elastic caching to reduce cloud memory costs

source.summary: A study by Google Research explores how reasoning improves fact recall in large language models (LLMs) even for simple questions. The research identifies two mechanisms: a computational buffer effect, where generated reasoning tokens allow models to refine internal states, and factual priming, where related facts are generated to prime correct answers. Experiments with models like Gemini-2.5 and Qwen3-32B show that reasoning significantly boosts recall on single-hop factual questions, even when no complex steps are needed. The study also highlights risks, such as hallucination in intermediate facts, and proposes strategies to improve reliability through verification and training adjustments. The findings suggest reasoning plays a broader role in exposing internal memory and expanding knowledge boundaries.
source.title: Reasoning Enhances Fact Recall in Language Models Through Computational Buffer and Factual Priming

source.summary: A flash flood in Nepal's Rasuwa district, near the Tibet border, washed away villages and damaged roads, bridges, and hydroelectric projects, according to authorities. District Administrator Narendra Pariyar warned of potential casualties but noted no immediate loss estimates. The flood, possibly linked to glacier lake drainage, disrupted electricity supply. Prime Minister Balendra Shah ordered rescue efforts and evacuation of riverbank residents, recalling last year's flood that killed nine and destroyed a key bridge.
source.title: Flash flood in Nepal destroys villages and infrastructure near Tibet border

source.summary: CIA director John Ratcliffe's secret visit to Russia prompted Ukraine to resume attacks on Russian targets after agreeing not to strike major cities during his trip. The US requested Ukraine to avoid attacks on Moscow, St. Petersburg, and northern Russia while Ratcliffe was in the country, a request revealed after his departure. Ukraine launched strikes on Wednesday, with Russia reporting the downing of 426 drones overnight. The visit, Ratcliffe's first to Moscow since 2025, remains shrouded in mystery, with no official explanation provided by either the US or Russian governments. Meanwhile, other developments include the release of a US citizen from Russian custody, drone attacks on Russian infrastructure, and discussions on mobilizing women for Ukraine's war effort.
source.title: CIA director's secret Russia visit prompts Ukraine to resume strikes

source.summary: Mediacorp has been awarded the Singapore Environmental Achievement Award 2026 for leadership and advocacy, alongside OCBC. The award, presented by the Singapore Environment Council (SEC), highlights organizations making significant contributions to environmental stewardship. SEC emphasized that companies addressing environmental challenges with their operational capabilities and influence drive meaningful change. Minister Grace Fu stressed the importance of viewing climate risk as a business risk and sustainability as an opportunity. Mediacorp's initiatives include renewable energy use, carbon accounting, and sustainable procurement, while its content aims to raise public awareness about sustainability issues. Mediacorp's editor-in-chief, Walter Fernandez, highlighted the company's role in making complex environmental topics accessible through journalism and documentaries. The awards also recognized other multinational corporations and SMEs for their sustainability efforts.
source.title: Mediacorp Recognized for Environmental Leadership and Advocacy

source.summary: Singapore reported a 14.4 per cent decrease in scam cases and a 17.9 per cent drop in losses during the first half of 2026, according to the Singapore Police Force (SPF). Scam losses totaled S$410.6 million, with cryptocurrency accounting for S$65.5 million. Despite the decline, scams remain the dominant crime type, making up 91.5 per cent of all reported cases. E-commerce scams rose 19.3 per cent, driven by pre-order fraud involving Pokemon trading cards. Investment scams caused the highest financial damage, with losses of S$169.8 million. Government officials impersonation scams saw a 31.7 per cent drop in losses. Business email compromise and social media impersonation scams increased sharply, with losses rising 193.1 per cent and 71.3 per cent respectively. Phishing and job scams also saw declines. Most victims transferred money themselves, and over S$97 million was recovered through proactive measures.
source.title: Singapore sees decline in scam cases and losses, but new trends emerge

source.summary: Bangkok has been named the world's best city for nightlife in 2026 by Time Out, based on a survey of over 24,000 residents across 150 cities. The ranking considers affordability, vibrancy, diversity, and safety after dark. Berlin and New York City secured second and third places, respectively. Bangkok residents rated their nightlife as good or amazing, with 73% giving high marks. Berlin had a 78% approval rate, praised for its clubbing scene. New York was noted for its evolving nightlife options. Other top cities include Melbourne, São Paulo, Medellín, Johannesburg, Brighton, and Amsterdam.
source.title: Bangkok tops global nightlife ranking, with Berlin and New York in top three

source.summary: Northern Territory MLA Tanzil Rahman has challenged the government's voluntary assisted dying (VAD) bill during parliamentary debate, criticizing its safeguards and proposing amendments to remove them. Rahman, who chaired a parliamentary inquiry into VAD, accused colleagues of mischaracterizing the debate and called the bill's 12-month prognosis period for eligibility 'subjective'. He plans to move amendments to eliminate the 12-month limit and a 'doctor gag' clause, which restricts medical professionals from initiating VAD discussions. Deputy Chief Minister Gerard Maley criticized Rahman's comments, defending the 12-month timeframe and calling his arguments 'clearly wrong'. The amendments face an uphill battle in a conscience vote, with only six MLAs supporting changes. The NT was the first Australian jurisdiction to legalise VAD in 1995, but the laws were overturned by the Commonwealth in 1997.
source.title: Northern Territory MLA challenges VAD bill safeguards in parliamentary debate

source.summary: Crown Prince Akishino and Crown Princess Kiko returned to Tokyo after a two-week official visit to Paraguay. Their trip, the prince's first to the South American nation in two decades, included meetings with Paraguayan President Santiago Pena and a ceremony commemorating the 90th anniversary of Japanese immigration. The couple also visited historical sites and communities of Japanese descent, expressing hope for continued ties between Japan and Paraguay.
source.title: Crown Prince and Princess Conclude Official Visit to Paraguay

source.summary: Guinea-Bissau will hold a referendum on August 30 to approve a new constitution that expands presidential authority, including the power to appoint and dismiss officials, dissolve parliament, and reduce legislative seats. The reforms, introduced after a military coup, aim to reshape the political system ahead of December elections. Critics warn the changes could concentrate too much power in the presidency, while supporters argue they may strengthen institutions. The constitution also requires presidential candidates to have lived in the country for five years.
source.title: Guinea-Bissau votes on constitution to expand presidential powers

source.summary: The Reserve Bank of Australia faces growing pressure to raise interest rates for the fourth time this year, as July inflation exceeded expectations. Annual inflation rose to 3.5%, surpassing the forecast 3.3%, with underlying inflation remaining at 3.6%. Economists warn that without policy action, inflation may persist, with some predicting a rate hike as early as September. The decision to keep rates at 4.35% was unanimous, but board members acknowledged the need for further action. Rising construction costs and restaurant prices contributed to the inflationary pressures.
source.title: Reserve Bank faces pressure for fourth rate hike amid higher-than-expected inflation

source.summary: Canada has announced targeted retaliatory measures against US tariffs, aiming to address trade tensions. The government emphasized strategic actions to protect its economic interests. The response includes tariffs on specific US goods. Officials stated the measures are proportional and aimed at restoring fair trade practices. The move follows ongoing disputes over trade policies.
source.title: Canada announces targeted retaliation against US tariffs

source.summary: Japan's Environment Ministry plans to end subsidies for conventional solar panels starting in fiscal 2027, citing falling global prices. Installation costs will still qualify for aid, but new purchases will not. The ministry aims to shift focus to perovskite solar cells, which can be sourced domestically, and seeks ¥28 billion for related efforts in 2027. Critics argue the current subsidies offer limited benefits to domestic industries, as China controls 80% of the global solar panel market. Japan hopes perovskite cells will generate 20 gigawatts of power by 2040, equivalent to 40 nuclear reactors.
source.title: Japan to phase out solar panel subsidies, focus on perovskite cells

source.summary: A fire at the Amur Gas Chemical Complex in Russia's far eastern region killed seven people and left nine Chinese workers missing. The incident occurred on August 25, 2026, and was extinguished by emergency services. The plant, a joint venture between Sibur and Sinopec, had not yet begun operations. The Investigative Committee is investigating potential breaches of industrial safety regulations. The complex, set to produce 2.3 million metric tons of polyethylene and 400,000 tons of polypropylene annually, relied on foreign labor, including Chinese workers, for its construction.
source.title: Fire at Russian gas complex kills seven, leaves nine Chinese workers missing

source.summary: Cameroonian midfielder Carlos Baleba has joined Manchester United from Brighton for approximately 75 million euros. The transfer marks a significant move in the Premier League. Other sports highlights include Olympique Lyonnais facing Fenerbahçe in a Champions League qualification match, Tadej Pogacar's dominance in the Vuelta a España, and Klay Thompson's official presentation with the Miami Heat.
source.title: Cameroon Midfielder Transfers to Manchester United

source.summary: The USS Abraham Lincoln, after a 250-day deployment supporting U.S. operations against Iran, is set to stop in Thailand for rest and recovery, according to Thai officials. The carrier's extended time at sea has raised concerns about crew mental health and supply shortages. The Royal Thai Navy confirmed the stopover, noting no military exercises will occur, though details like the port and arrival date remain undisclosed due to security reasons. The U.S. embassy and Navy have not commented on the visit.
source.title: USS Abraham Lincoln to stop in Thailand after 250-day deployment

source.summary: The UK's energy price cap has reached its highest level in three years, with bills increasing by 4% from October. This follows a 13% rise in July due to global market volatility. Ofgem estimates the average annual cost for a typical household at £1,723, up from £1,663 in the previous quarter. Citizens Advice highlights the impact on living standards, with households facing an extra £350 annually compared to 2024. Fixed-rate deal users are largely unaffected. Energy Secretary Miatta Fahnbulleh notes government efforts to reduce costs, including VAT removal and a £150 bill cut. Calls grow for windfall taxes on energy companies and banks, with critics arguing that renewables investments are driving up costs. Ofgem's calculations assume lower energy use due to affordability concerns, while unit rates and standing charges also rise.
source.title: UK energy price cap hits three-year high as bills rise 4%

source.summary: Iran stated that the Strait of Hormuz remains closed unless the United States ends the war, despite ongoing discussions with Oman about a temporary transit corridor. The US has imposed sanctions to pressure Iran, with Treasury Secretary Scott Bessent warning of economic consequences. Omani Foreign Minister Badr Albusaidi expressed hope for a soon-to-be-announced shipping corridor. US President Donald Trump claimed all mines in the strait's international waters have been removed, with Iran notified that new mines would be destroyed.
source.title: Iran insists Hormuz remains closed despite Oman talks on transit corridor

source.summary: A violent gang attack in Kenscoff, Haiti, killed at least 47 people and kidnapped over 50 others, according to the United Nations. The attack, one of the largest mass kidnappings in recent years, occurred as gangs threatened to execute hostages if authorities killed any gang members. Gang leader Izo 2, also known as 'Didi', issued a video threat against Haiti's police director. The attack has raised concerns about security in the country, with experts suggesting it may be a message to the government and police ahead of upcoming elections. The U.N. condemned the violence, noting that 22 victims were executed in a church compound. The attack has displaced thousands and contributed to a surge in kidnappings, with the U.N. reporting a 40% increase in such incidents from April to June.
source.title: Haiti gang attack kills 47, kidnaps over 50 in violent assault

source.summary: The next Atlantic tropical storm will be named Dolly, a coincidence unrelated to Dolly Parton's recent death. Storm names are assigned by the World Meteorological Organization, following a six-year cycle with alternating male and female names. This season has seen storms Arthur, Bertha, and Cristobal. Forecasters expect a new storm to form near the Cabo Verde Islands, potentially becoming Dolly. The National Hurricane Center noted a below-average hurricane season due to El Nino, predicting eight to 14 named storms. Names are chosen for clarity and familiarity, with some retired due to sensitivity, such as Melissa, a Category 5 hurricane that devastated the Caribbean.
source.title: Next Atlantic storm named Dolly, coinciding with Parton's death

source.summary: Manchester United has signed 22-year-old Cameroon midfielder Carlos Baleba from Brighton in a deal worth up to £70 million, as manager Michael Carrick rebuilds the midfield. Baleba, who impressed in the Premier League last season, has agreed to a five-year contract with an option for a sixth season. The transfer follows the departures of Casemiro and the injury to Manuel Ugarte, prompting United to strengthen their midfield. The club had previously signed Youri Tielemans and Andrey Santos this summer. Baleba expressed his excitement about joining the club, calling it a dream come true.
source.title: Manchester United signs Cameroon midfielder Carlos Baleba for £70m

source.summary: China warned the US that its sanctions on Iran could disrupt the global financial system, urging Washington not to interfere with its cooperation with Tehran. The YPG terror group announced its dissolution after integrating forces into the Syrian army. Canada announced counter-tariffs of 15%-50% on $27.6 billion in US imports starting Sept. 8. Real Betis won 1-0 against Valencia with a late goal from Pablo Garcia.
source.title: Morning Briefing: Aug. 26, 2026

source.summary: The Bombay High Court vacated suspension orders for five restaurants at the Mumbai Cricket Association premises, allowing them to reopen. The bench slammed the Maharashtra FDA for refusing to lift the ban despite an 88% compliance rating found during a fresh inspection. Justice Ravindra Ghuge and Justice Gautam Ankhad warned of contempt action against officials who ignored earlier court directions to take a pragmatic approach. The court questioned why the department acted with undue haste and failed to analyze the legal position properly.
source.title: Bombay High Court clears five Mumbai eateries after slaming FDA

source.summary: BlackRock Inc. reduced the minimum transaction size for swapping Bitcoin for ETF shares to $1 million, making it easier for investors to move crypto wealth into mainstream finance. Robbie Mitchnick, head of digital assets at BlackRock, stated that the firm has facilitated over $5 billion in such conversions since regulators allowed in-kind creations. Matt Hougan of Bitwise noted that while the process remains bespoke, it is becoming more standardized and efficient. Morgan Stanley reported that in-kind conversions now account for 5% to 7% of its spot Bitcoin ETF holdings. Grayscale Investments saw rapid adoption, with in-kind processing rising to 62% for Bitcoin creations by June. Industry experts suggest that as more intermediaries build capacity, minimum thresholds may fall further.
source.title: BlackRock lowers Bitcoin ETF swap minimums to $1 million

source.summary: ETMarkets.com lists five liquid funds with low expense ratios and strong six-month returns. Parag Parikh Liquid Fund led with a 3.34% return and 0.10% expense ratio.
source.title: Five low-cost mutual funds delivered strong six-month returns

source.summary: Zee founder Subhash Chandra accused Reliance chairman Mukesh Ambani and TV18 of disseminating misinformation regarding his insolvency proceedings. Chandra disputed the Rs 22,000-crore figure, stating his liability as a personal guarantor was only Rs 3,992 crore. He alleged that TV18 published false narratives about his debt settlement and claimed Ambani orchestrated a 2019 share-price crash that fell Zee's value by 40 percent. Reliance Industries denied the allegations, stating its media brands would never attack anyone. The dispute arises after the National Company Law Tribunal approved a repayment plan reducing admitted claims by nearly 99.97 percent. Canara Bank has challenged this order before the appellate tribunal. Meanwhile, Chandra indicated plans to invest in startups using funds from his family.
source.title: Subhash Chandra accuses Mukesh Ambani and TV18 of spreading misinformation

source.summary: Goldman Sachs partner Chris Churchman warned that outsourcing reasoning to AI models could cause cognitive atrophy among financial leaders. Speaking on the firm's Exchanges podcast, Churchman stated that delegating fundamental problem-solving threatens the development of core human reasoning skills. He noted that while AI boosts immediate profitability, it risks hollowing out the foundational skills junior staff need to become senior decision-makers. Churchman emphasized that systems must ensure staff make final judgment calls during high-stakes scenarios rather than acting as passive monitors. The executive highlighted concerns that automating entry-level tasks might prevent future traders from fully grasping risk management.
source.title: Goldman Sachs executive warns banks risk losing reasoning skills by relying on AI models

source.summary: NL subscribers share letters on current events and platform issues. Rinchen argues doctors should join trans discussions while criticizing Navatrilova's stance on school sports. Dhruv questions NL's engagement with the CJP protest and Delhi air pollution. Ryan and Shreejeta request YouTube podcast links for subscribers. Shreejata suggests Instagram's neglect by the BJP contributed to recent protests.
source.title: Readers discuss CJP protests, trans representation, and Instagram's role in anti-incumbency

source.summary: OpenAI announced it will terminate its partnership with Cursor following SpaceX's acquisition of the coding tool. The company cited trust issues and a lack of confidence that SpaceX would use the technology within OpenAI's terms of service. OpenAI provided 76 days of notice, setting a shutoff date of November 12, 2026. The decision references past instances where Elon Musk's companies violated OpenAI contracts. Cursor co-founder Michael Truell, now an executive at SpaceX, stated they were in talks to resolve the issue. The move impacts developers relying on OpenAI models through Cursor.
source.title: OpenAI ends partnership with Cursor after SpaceX acquisition

source.summary: A 27-year-old TCS engineer died after a reversing JCB struck his motorcycle near Gurgaon's Rapid Metro station. The machine's driver fled the scene, and police have seized the vehicle. The father alleged the night work lacked proper safety indicators. Authorities are investigating the incident.
source.title: TCS Engineer Dies After JCB Driver Flees Accident in Gurgaon

source.summary: Federal Reserve Chair Kevin Warsh is advocating for a 'quieter Fed' following criticism regarding the central bank's lack of communication. Speaking at the Jackson Hole Symposium, Warsh stated he prefers avoiding early pronouncements on future policy decisions, arguing that transparency is not a virtue in itself. He believes a more purposeful communication style allows the Fed to better meet its objectives and hold itself accountable for results. Warsh noted that forward guidance has overstayed its welcome and risks creating ambiguity. He also acknowledged that US inflation remains too high, hinting that the central bank may need to act to bring it down to the 2% target.
source.title: Fed Chair Kevin Warsh advocates for a quieter central bank amid criticism

source.summary: Andreessen Horowitz announced the creation of a $1.1 billion Machine Age Fund to invest in AI infrastructure. The firm stated the capital will support chips, memory, networking, and data centers. a16z noted that compute density has risen 28-fold while power needs are increasing. The venture capitalist described this as a once-in-a-generation opportunity to redesign systems. Hardware startups now represent over 20 percent of the firm's deal flow.
source.title: Andreessen Horowitz launches $1.1 billion Machine Age Fund for AI hardware

source.summary: Visa announced enhancements to its cybersecurity portfolio to help organizations identify and resolve vulnerabilities more effectively. The company unveiled the next evolution of the Visa Vulnerability Agentic Harness, an open-source framework designed to reduce the time between discovering and fixing attack paths. Visa also expanded its consulting practice with new advisory services to help clients assess risk and prioritize remediation efforts. Key features of the updated framework include closed-loop remediation, flexible model choices, and greater visibility into security workflows. Prateek Sanghi, Head of Visa Consulting & Analytics for Asia Pacific, stated that the real challenge is determining which risks matter most and remediating them before attackers can exploit them. The company noted that since the framework's release in June 2026, it has been downloaded by tens of thousands of developers worldwide.
source.title: Visa launches AI tools to speed up cybersecurity vulnerability fixes

source.summary: Chief Minister N. Rangasamy announced a ₹50 increase in LPG subsidies for ration card holders in Puducherry. The government also plans financial aid for fishing community students and will clear pending pension applications. During the budget discussion, the CM outlined revenue sources and employment initiatives. Additionally, he wrote to the External Affairs Minister regarding three missing tourists in Nepal.
source.title: Puducherry CM announces LPG subsidy hike and budget details

source.summary: The death toll from Nepal's flash floods reached 626, with over 2,400 people still missing. An ice-rock avalanche triggered by a glacial collapse caused widespread destruction across central Nepal. More than 11,000 security personnel and an Indian rescue team are conducting search operations. The NDRRMA warned of potential further flooding as river levels rise. The Mugling-Kathmandu highway resumed operations on Saturday.
source.title: Nepal flash floods kill 626; 2,400 remain missing as rescue continues

source.summary: Kerala Health Minister K Muraleedharan stated that police action against Congress leader Anil Kumar was warranted after he allegedly blocked Chief Minister V D Satheesan's convoy. The incident occurred on Friday evening when workers demanded the CM attend an unapproved event in Chempazhanthy. Muraleedharan condemned the blocking and abusive language as inappropriate for political culture. Home Minister Ramesh Chennithala added that law would take its course regarding the matter.
source.title: Kerala minister supports arrest of Congress leader who blocked CM convoy

source.summary: The author argues that India's new closing auction mechanism lacks critical safeguards present in mature markets like the US and Hong Kong. On August 27, the Sensex dropped nearly 3% during the final auction window before recovering, causing significant losses for derivatives traders and index funds. While the author acknowledges the auction concentrates liquidity, they warn that allowing order cancellations until the end creates a vulnerability to manipulation. The author suggests freezing cancellations in the final window and deepening market-making participation to protect investors. Although surveillance systems detected recent manipulation, the author believes better market design is needed to prevent it. The author concludes that while these changes cost nothing, they are essential to protect millions of investors relying on closing prices for mutual funds and derivatives.
source.title: India's new stock auction lacks safeguards used in mature markets

source.summary: A political party is holding a high-level strategy meeting in the national capital to plan a massive youth and Gen Z outreach drive. Top leaders and a young team are discussing ways to bridge communication gaps and engage young voters on social media and campuses. The new leadership team, with an average age of forty-five, aims to align political strategy with youth aspirations before upcoming state assembly elections. The nationwide outreach program is expected to launch in mid-September.
source.title: Political Party Plans Massive Youth Outreach Ahead of Elections

source.summary: The Greater Bengaluru civic body fined 10 food outlets at Nexus Mall for breaching solid waste management norms. Officials found that establishments failed to separate wet and dry waste and used banned single-use plastic. Fines ranged from ₹5,000 to ₹25,000, with Chaska Bun receiving the highest penalty. The Greater Bengaluru civic body stated that similar checks will continue at commercial establishments across the city. Meanwhile, food safety officials issued notices to canteens in five medical college hostels after finding expired food products and labelling irregularities.
source.title: Bengaluru civic body fines 10 food outlets for waste violations

source.summary: Amritesh Mukherjee reviews Deepa Anappara's novel The Last of Earth, noting its focus on colonial mapping in Tibet. The author reports the book details an Englishman and an Indian surveyor charting the Tsangpo river. Mukherjee states the story exposes the undocumented cost of conquest by highlighting native bearers. He writes the novel critiques imperialists for erasing the names of those who performed the real work.
source.title: Review highlights Deepa Anappara's novel on colonial mapping in Tibet

source.summary: Singapore Airlines (SIA) reaffirmed its long-term commitment to Air India, holding a 25.1% stake, while stating it will evaluate additional capital requests under its disciplined framework. SIA highlighted India's projected growth as the world's third-largest economy by 2030 and the aviation market's expected tripling by 2044. The carrier noted challenges including airspace closures and the AI171 accident but emphasized tangible progress in customer experience and fleet renewal. SIA described its investment as aligned with a multi-hub strategy to enable direct participation in the Indian market.
source.title: Singapore Airlines reaffirms long-term commitment to Air India despite losses

source.summary: Market expectations for a US Federal Reserve rate hike have surged following comments from Chairman Kevin Warsh at the Jackson Hole symposium. Traders now price a 57% chance of a September hike, rising to nearly 90% for December. Warsh stated the Fed must be confident inflation is moving toward 2% or it has work to do. Goldman Sachs maintains its base case for no rate change in September but acknowledges a hike is possible if August inflation data proves hotter. The brokerage notes underlying inflation remains elevated, with 54% of goods and services seeing price increases above 3%. Analyst Mark Hackett observed that Warsh's consistent hawkish stance has not softened market expectations.
source.title: Fed Rate Hike Bets Rise After Warsh Speech, Goldman Sachs Holds Neutral

source.summary: A new study challenges the common belief that invasive alien species (IAS) have the greatest impact in wealthy Global North countries. Published in Science, the research uses two global datasets to analyze impact severity, defined by the IUCN’s Environmental Impact Classification for Alien Taxa (EICAT). The study finds higher average impact severity in the Global South due to weak governance and limited management capacity. It highlights India as a high-income developing economy with significant impact severity, contrasting with the Global North's stronger policies. The research underscores the need for more attention to the Global South's challenges with invasive species.
source.title: Study reveals higher invasive species impact severity in Global South

source.summary: OpenAI has lost its head of data centers, Chris Malone, who left the company last week, according to the Wall Street Journal. Malone, who joined OpenAI in March 2023 after stints at Google and Meta, oversaw the Stargate Project, a $500 million U.S. data center initiative. OpenAI cited a reorganization as the reason for his departure, stating it has a strong data center team in place. This exit adds to a string of over a dozen executive departures in 2026, including the recent exits of chief revenue officer Denise Dresser and former COO Brad Lightcap. The company is also facing departures in its safety and ethics teams, raising questions about its stability as it prepares for an IPO delayed to 2027.
source.title: OpenAI's Data Center Chief Departs Amid Leadership Turnover

source.summary: ARIA, the UK's research and development funding agency, is focusing on unlocking new scientific and technological advancements. The agency's new leader discusses their work and initiatives. The episode also highlights technology supporting disabled racing drivers in achieving their goals, alongside a discussion on the pros and cons of AI-generated complaints. The program is presented by Chris Vallance and produced by Tom Quinn.
source.title: ARIA's new leader discusses R&D focus and tech aiding disabled racers

source.summary: Google Research introduces PHRM, a system that passively measures heart rate and resting heart rate using smartphone cameras during everyday use. The system leverages deep learning and facial video captured after face unlock events to estimate heart rate with a mean absolute percentage error under 10%, meeting industry standards across skin tones. PHRM also estimates daily resting heart rate with an accuracy comparable to wearables, achieving a mean absolute error under 5 beats per minute. The study, published in Nature, includes the largest and most diverse dataset of smartphone videos for research and a pre-trained model for accessibility. The system addresses challenges in detecting photoplethysmography (PPG) signals in darker skin tones, improving inclusivity and accuracy. PHRM's performance was validated through both controlled laboratory settings and real-world 'free-living' studies, demonstrating its effectiveness across diverse populations. The research highlights the potential of smartphones to democratize heart health monitoring, offering wearable-like insights through ubiquitous devices.
source.title: Google Research Introduces Smartphone-Based Heart Rate Monitoring System for Passive Health Tracking

source.summary: Interim CEO Peter Clark of Ai2 emphasizes the institute's commitment to long-term, high-impact AI research and open science. He highlights the importance of maintaining focus on foundational research despite the rapid pace of AI development. Clark notes that projects like ELMo, Olmo, and Molmo demonstrate the potential of open models to drive scientific progress. He also discusses initiatives such as AutoDiscovery and OlmoEarth, which apply AI to real-world challenges in oncology and environmental science. Ai2 is prioritizing areas like AI for scientific discovery, embodied AI, and AI for the planet. Clark stresses the value of open models in enabling broader scientific understanding and collaboration, as seen in the NSF OMAI project. The institute aims to build a future where AI is both transparent and impactful, inviting participation from those interested in advancing science through open innovation.
source.title: Ai2's Interim CEO Discusses Long-Term AI Research and Open Science Commitment

source.summary: AstaBench, an open benchmark for evaluating AI agents' scientific research capabilities, has released updated results showing improved performance on coding, reasoning, and data analysis tasks. The benchmark tested models like GPT-5.5 and Claude Opus 4.7, with the latter achieving the highest score at 58.0%. However, end-to-end discovery remains challenging, with GPT-5.5 scoring 52.9% and struggling with complex workflows. The benchmark also gained industry adoption, with organizations like the UK AI Security Institute and General Reasoning integrating AstaBench into their evaluation frameworks. The results highlight uneven progress across categories and rising costs, emphasizing the need for continued development in full scientific workflows.
source.title: AstaBench benchmarks AI agents' scientific research capabilities with new results and industry adoption

source.summary: The National Institute of Standards and Technology (NIST) has released a new annotated fingerprint dataset and open-source software to aid forensic scientists. The dataset, part of NIST Technical Note 2367, includes 10,000 fingerprints from 200 volunteers, with annotations detailing print quality. These annotations help train both human examiners and AI systems to evaluate fingerprint quality. NIST also released OpenLQM, a modified version of the LQMetric software, which assesses fingerprint quality and is now open-source. The tools aim to improve accuracy and efficiency in forensic analysis. NIST computer scientist Greg Fiumara noted that the resources will enhance education and algorithm training for fingerprint identification.
source.title: NIST Releases Annotated Fingerprint Dataset and Open-Source Software for Forensic Use

source.summary: The National Institute of Standards and Technology (NIST) has submitted its annual report to Congress detailing progress on the National Construction Safety Team (NCST) Act activities for fiscal year 2025. The report highlights the completion of most technical work on the Champlain Towers South collapse investigation, including material testing, full-scale replica tests, and data analysis. It also covers NIST's work on Hurricane Maria's impact on Puerto Rico and actions taken to implement recommendations from the Joplin tornado investigation. The NCST Advisory Committee noted the investigation's thoroughness and expects its methodologies to improve building safety practices. The team plans to present its next findings in June 2026.
source.title: NIST Completes Major Technical Work on Champlain Towers South Collapse Investigation

source.summary: Leanstral, an open-source code agent for Lean 4, aims to enhance formal verification by generating code and proving its correctness. The project, developed by researchers, introduces a model with 6B active parameters, optimized for proof engineering tasks. It is released under an Apache 2.0 license, available through Mistral Vibe and a free API. Leanstral outperforms existing open-source models and competitors like the Claude suite in efficiency and performance, achieving higher scores with lower computational cost. The model was tested on real-world scenarios, including diagnosing issues in Lean 4 code and translating programs from Rocq to Lean. The team emphasizes its accessibility, offering zero-setup integration and the ability to run the model locally.
source.title: Leanstral: Open-Source Code Agent for Formal Verification

source.summary: An autonomous agent was developed to address the issue of insufficient test coverage in large Rails monoliths. The agent reads source files, generates or improves RSpec tests, validates them against style rules and coverage targets, and runs within a CI/CD pipeline without human intervention. It operates in parallel across multiple files, handling different file types like models, controllers, and helpers with specialized instructions. The agent uses Vibe, a coding assistant, with custom tools like RuboCop and SimpleCov to ensure test quality and execution. By enforcing a strict self-review process and using LLM-as-a-judge metrics, the agent improved test quality scores from 0.68 to 0.74. The experiment showed that the agent successfully generated tests for uncovered files and improved existing ones, achieving 100% coverage. However, challenges like syntax errors and versioning issues highlight the need for ongoing refinement.
source.title: Autonomous agent improves Rails test coverage by generating and refining RSpec tests

source.summary: Instagram has refreshed its logo, with Adam Mosseri describing it as 'leaner and more modern' while referencing its original design. The update comes after 10 years without a change, a period the article notes as unusually long in the fast-paced tech industry. The author critiques the redesign, suggesting it reflects algorithmic data exploitation and influencer culture rather than simplicity. The article also humorously questions the new name 'Instagzam' as a possible typo.
source.title: Instagram updates logo with AI-driven design changes

source.summary: A study in Pakistan found that judges using a custom AI tool called JudgeGPT, combined with training, resolved 6.3% more cases without a drop in judgment quality. The tool, developed by economist Sultan Mehmood and collaborators, integrates OpenAI's GPT-4 with a database of Pakistani legal texts. It was tested with 1,559 judges, with those receiving comprehensive training showing the most significant improvements. The tool helps with legal research and drafting, reducing time spent on case law searches and document summaries. However, the study acknowledges limitations, including the lack of direct human evaluation of judgment quality and the risk of over-reliance on AI. Researchers emphasize the importance of training to ensure proper use of the technology, while noting that efficiency gains may not fully address broader concerns about justice quality.
source.title: Pakistan's Judges Report 6.3% Productivity Boost with JudgeGPT AI Tool

source.summary: Major oil companies are increasing their investments in nuclear fusion, signaling a shift from traditional energy sources. Eni S.p.A. plans to deploy a commercial fusion power plant in Europe by the early 2040s, supported by its $1 billion agreement with Commonwealth Fusion Systems. The company is also developing fuel systems for fusion reactors, leveraging its experience in hydrocarbon processing. Commonwealth Fusion Systems raised $1 billion in July, bringing its total funding to $4 billion, with plans for a 400-MW plant in Virginia. Other oil giants like Equinor, Chevron, Shell, and Cenovus are also backing various fusion technologies, with some aiming to build commercial power plants by the mid-2030s. Eni is developing a tritium fuel-cycle facility to support future fusion reactors, as tritium is essential but difficult to obtain. The article notes that commercial reactors will need closed-loop systems to recycle tritium, a challenge that Eni is addressing through its joint venture with the UK Atomic Energy Authority.
source.title: Big Oil Companies Invest in Nuclear Fusion Development

source.summary: BYD is set to release a larger version of its Seagull electric hatchback, named the Great Seagull, by the end of 2026. The new model, which will be sold alongside the current Seagull, features a longer wheelbase and a more powerful 95 kW electric motor. It is expected to include BYD's new Blade Battery 2.0 and Flash Charging technology. The current Seagull offers two battery options with ranges up to 405 km. BYD has not yet disclosed pricing for the Great Seagull, but it is anticipated to be slightly higher than the current model's starting price of 69,900 yuan. The new variant was approved for sale by China's MIIT and will feature advanced safety features like a LiDAR sensor.
source.title: BYD to Launch Larger Great Seagull Electric Hatch by End of 2026

source.summary: Maine's utility regulators have selected an 800-megawatt wind farm and a 1.2-gigawatt transmission line proposal, marking a significant step toward clean energy development. The projects, proposed by Clearway Energy and Avangrid, aim to supply power to New England and reduce oil reliance. The wind farm could lower oil use by 10% in winter, with expected $400 million in net benefits for consumers and over 2,500 construction jobs. The transmission line, shared among six New England states, represents unprecedented regional cooperation. While the projects face challenges including financing and public opposition, advocates see them as a model for future clean energy efforts. The federal environment for wind development remains uncertain due to policy changes under former President Trump.
source.title: Maine selects wind farm and transmission plan for clean energy expansion

source.summary: The U.S. is increasing its oil influence in Iraq, aiming to secure a strategic position as the country plans to boost production to 8-10 million barrels per day within six years. Iraq's vast oil reserves, geographic centrality, and role in the Shia Crescent make it a key asset for global powers. Russia and China previously held significant influence through infrastructure deals and control over key regions, but the U.S. has moved to counter this through sanctions and new oil field acquisitions. ConocoPhillips has acquired a 42% stake in BP's Kirkuk oil fields, targeting production of up to 450,000 barrels per day. Chevron is developing the West Qurna 2 field and the Nasiriyah oilfield, supported by projects like the Common Seawater Supply Project. These moves are part of a broader geopolitical strategy to challenge Russian and Chinese influence in the region.
source.title: U.S. Expands Oil Influence in Iraq Amid Global Power Rivalry

source.summary: Dreame, a Chinese company known for robot vacuums, has canceled its plans for a rocket-powered electric hypercar and all other car-related initiatives. The company, which announced its entry into the luxury electric vehicle market last year, unveiled a hypercar at CES and even planned an SUV to compete with the Rolls Royce Cullinan. However, its ambitions were deemed impractical, with the rocket boosters requiring recharging and the project appearing more as a marketing and fundraising effort than a serious manufacturing endeavor. CarNewsChina reports that Dreame is exiting the car business, having laid off nearly 1,000 employees in the department. The decision follows a trend of high-profile electric car project cancellations by companies not traditionally in the automotive industry, including Apple’s Project Titan and Sony/Honda’s joint venture. Analysts suggest Dreame’s project was overly ambitious and lacked sufficient detail, leading to its premature cancellation.
source.title: Dreame Abandons Rocket-Powered Hypercar and Car Division

source.summary: Larsen & Toubro has secured an order for three battery energy storage system projects in the Middle East, totaling 6 GWh of storage capacity. The projects, for an unnamed client, will use four-hour battery systems to shift electricity from surplus to peak-demand periods. L&T will also deliver grid infrastructure, including substations and underground cables. The contracts highlight the company's expanding role in energy storage, reflecting growing Middle Eastern investments in renewable generation and grid infrastructure. The company did not disclose the client, locations, contract value, or completion dates.
source.title: L&T wins 6 GWh battery storage projects in Middle East

source.summary: A study by researchers Jiyoung Eum and Gyeong-Seok Choi reveals that residential solar adoption in South Korea can trigger rebound effects under the country's tiered electricity tariffs. The research shows households that move to lower tariff tiers after installing solar panels offset 11-22% of expected energy savings. Net metering amplifies this rebound effect, with high-consumption households seeing their offset double. The findings suggest policymakers should account for tier transitions and net-metering in evaluating solar programs. The study highlights the need for adjusted policy frameworks to address these rebound effects in energy and emissions savings calculations.
source.title: South Korean residential solar adoption may lead to energy rebound effects under tiered tariffs

source.summary: A new circular-economy roadmap by Axfoundation, KTH Royal Institute of Technology, and industry partners predicts Sweden's decommissioned solar panels could rise from 17 MT in 2021 to 150,000 MT by 2060. RISE Research Institutes of Sweden estimates this growth depends on solar deployment speed and repowering rates, with scenarios ranging from 40,000 MT to 150,000 MT by 2060. The roadmap highlights the need for circular solutions, including dedicated recycling infrastructure requiring 10,000 MT annual inflow. It warns that current panel waste is often mixed with general e-waste, limiting reuse opportunities. The report outlines five priority areas, including circular design, safer handling, and improved material recovery. It also notes that only six of 12 European countries met the 85% recovery target in 2021, under the EU's WEEE Directive.
source.title: Sweden's solar panel waste could reach 150,000 metric tons by 2060

source.summary: A new documentary titled La superviviente examines the case of Alicia Esteve Head, who fabricated a story about surviving the September 11 attacks. The film reveals that the woman known as Tania Head never entered the World Trade Center but instead constructed a compelling narrative of loss and resilience. Directors Kike Maíllo and Markos Goikolea used actress Hannah Becker to portray the impostor while protecting the real woman's identity. The filmmakers argue that the deception succeeded because society desperately needed a story of survival during the aftermath of the tragedy. Alicia Head turned down financial aid for victims despite securing benefits for her association, seeking emotional validation rather than monetary gain. The documentary compares her actions to other historical impostors and highlights how audiences are willing to believe narratives that offer hope.
source.title: Documentary explores Barcelona woman who lied about surviving 9/11

source.summary: The provided text contains an error message regarding a failed site load rather than a news article. Consequently, no summary of a debate or candidates can be generated from the available source material.
source.title: French presidential candidates clash in first debate

source.summary: Bharat Petroleum Chairman Sanjay Khanna stated that the company faces no logistical challenges if a lower ethanol blend is introduced alongside E20 petrol. The firm clarified that reports suggesting a proposal to replace the 20% ethanol variant with a 10% blend are incorrect. Director Vetsa Ramkrishna Gupta reported that crude requirements for September are secured and October supplies are about 50-55% complete. Khanna also warned that a ban on Russian oil could create significant pressure given that Russian crude forms 35-40% of Indian OMCs' oil basket.
source.title: Bharat Petroleum chief says no logistical issues with lower ethanol blend

source.summary: The Kerala government issued technical sanction for the first phase of the KSRTC bus terminal at Karikkamury. An official stated the Public Works Department will invite tenders in early September for the ₹13-crore project. The initial single-storey structure will be completed in approximately a year. Private buses will not be permitted in the new terminal. MP Hibi Eden emphasized preventing waterlogging and ensuring structural stability.
source.title: Kerala government sanctions first phase of KSRTC bus terminal at Karikkamury

source.summary: Atomic Energy Commission chairperson A K Mohanty and US Energy Secretary Chris Wright discussed strengthening Indo-US nuclear ties in Washington. Insiders noted the talks support India's goal of 100 GW capacity by 2047. The SHANTI Act passed in December 2025 allows private sector participation. American firms expressed interest in setting up plants in India. The meeting preceded the launch of the ATLAS initiative by the IAEA.
source.title: India and US officials discuss nuclear energy cooperation in Washington

source.summary: J&K Congress president Tariq Hamid Karra stated the party declined an invitation from the National Conference to join the Omar Abdullah government. Karra explained that Congress maintains a principled stand against joining the ministry until J&K's statehood is restored. The party affirmed it remains an ally of the NC government but will not compromise on constitutional rights. Congress leaders indicated continued support for the NC administration while reserving the right to raise issues like inflation and power tariffs.
source.title: Congress rejects NC invitation to join Omar Abdullah government in J&K

source.summary: Meta has agreed to an $18 billion settlement regarding teen safety on Facebook and Instagram, but the full amount depends on rival platforms adopting similar rules. The deal, announced Wednesday, imposes strict usage limits and safety measures on Meta's apps while requiring state funds for youth wellness programs. Approximately $5.3 billion of the settlement is contingent on TikTok and YouTube agreeing to comparable restrictions and paying their own settlements. Meta argues that without industry-wide standards, teenagers will simply migrate to less-regulated platforms. Currently, TikTok and YouTube have not publicly committed to the proposed framework, though both face separate legal challenges regarding children's privacy.
source.title: Meta's $18 billion teen safety settlement requires TikTok and YouTube to follow suit

source.summary: Police in northeast Delhi arrested a 17-year-old boy for displaying an illegal firearm in an Instagram video. Officers seized a countrymade pistol from the teenager's possession during a raid on Wednesday. Authorities registered a case under Section 25 of the Arms Act on August 26. Officials stated that further investigation is currently underway.
source.title: Police Apprehend Teen for Illegal Firearm in Instagram Video

source.summary: Nvidia is reportedly planning a $13 billion deal to acquire Hugging Face, a major platform for open-weight artificial intelligence models. The news emerged alongside Nvidia's report of doubled quarterly revenue and a 7% share price increase. Hugging Face previously rejected a $500 million Nvidia investment due to concerns over investor control. The proposed acquisition creates a contradiction as Nvidia would gain significant influence over the open AI ecosystem it aims to support. Nvidia seeks to maintain its dominance against competitors like OpenAI and Google by securing access to millions of developers. The deal represents a high multiple of Hugging Face's $150 million annual revenue, suggesting Nvidia values the company's developer network more than current earnings. Critics worry the move could undermine open-source AI principles and increase concentration of power in the industry.
source.title: Nvidia reportedly plans $13 billion acquisition of open AI platform Hugging Face

source.summary: Moneycontrol reported that Tata Consultancy Services reduced variable pay for mid and senior employees to 60-70% in Q1, while junior staff received full payouts. The company faces margin pressure despite AI investments. TCS did not comment on the report. Meanwhile, TCS stock fell sharply as top Indian firms saw market value declines. CEO K Krithivasan plans to create 5,900-8,900 forward-deployed engineers representing 1-1.5% of the workforce.
source.title: TCS cuts variable pay for mid and senior staff while juniors get full bonus

source.summary: NVIDIA reported second-quarter revenue of $96.2 billion, more than doubling from the previous period, while adjusted profit reached $2.22 per share. The company expects revenue to grow by 70% in 2028, though investors are questioning the sustainability of this pace. CFO Colette Kress stated that demand acceleration continues even at the company's current scale, with customer forecasts indicating growth could double next year. However, experts warn that rising costs, particularly for memory chips, are squeezing profit margins. Viram Shah of Vested Finance predicts margins will fall from 75% to between 71% and 72% by January due to supply constraints. To protect profitability, NVIDIA may need to raise prices next year, a move that could face resistance from customers.
source.title: NVIDIA reports record revenue but faces margin pressure from rising costs

source.summary: The Reserve Bank of India reports that manufacturing operating profit growth reached 21.3% in Q1 2026-27. Sales growth for listed private non-financial companies accelerated to 19.4% year-on-year. Raw material expenses for manufacturers rose 27.5% due to global supply chain disruptions. Staff costs increased across manufacturing, IT, and services sectors. Operating profit margins improved sequentially across all major sectors analyzed.
source.title: RBI reports manufacturing operating profit growth improved to 21.3% in Q1

source.summary: The Federation of Indian MSMEs (FISME) cautions that the Reserve Bank of India's proposal to ban revolving credit from NBFCs may increase borrowing costs for micro, small and medium enterprises. FISME argues that a blanket ban on flexible credit products would create operational inefficiencies and push businesses toward less regulated lenders. The organization urges the regulator to adopt a targeted approach that preserves legitimate working capital tools while addressing risks like loan evergreening. Anil Bhardwaj, Secretary General of FISME, stated that business working capital differs fundamentally from consumer revolving credit and requires distinct regulation. FISME has submitted feedback proposing safeguards such as fixed limits and annual renewals to balance regulatory concerns with business needs.
source.title: FISME warns RBI NBFC credit curbs could raise MSME borrowing costs

source.summary: Tata Motors announced a rebranding strategy where Tata.Cars becomes the primary customer-facing identity while Tata Motors Passenger Vehicles remains the legal entity. CEO Shailesh Chandra stated the move reflects growing Indian confidence and a unified expression of the portfolio. The automaker also unveiled Tata.ev for its electric vehicle range. In July 2026, the company reported total sales of 63,760 units, marking a 59% year-on-year increase.
source.title: Tata Motors rebrands passenger vehicles as Tata.Cars to align with Indian aspirations

source.summary: US stocks opened higher on Thursday, driven by strong earnings from major technology companies. The Nasdaq Composite rose 0.8%, the S&P 500 gained 0.4%, and the Dow Jones Industrial Average increased 35 points. Nvidia was the primary driver, with shares jumping 7% after the chipmaker beat expectations and provided a strong revenue outlook. UBS remains confident in the wider AI growth story, though it warns of potential volatility. Other semiconductor stocks like Broadcom and Marvell Technology also moved higher. Investors are closely watching the Federal Reserve's Jackson Hole symposium and recent jobless claims data. Additionally, reports suggest the Trump administration is considering new tariffs on semiconductors and related products.
source.title: US stocks rise as Nvidia leads gains while investors watch Fed signals

source.summary: Wall Street indices rose on Thursday, driven by a technology rally following Nvidia's strong earnings forecast. The S&P 500 gained 0.7%, the Dow Jones Industrial Average climbed 0.3%, and the Nasdaq Composite increased 1.4%. Nvidia shares jumped 7.3% after reporting quarterly revenue of $96.2 billion, more than double the previous year's level. Salesforce shares soared 20.7% after the company stated artificial intelligence contributed to a record quarter, while CrowdStrike stock jumped 14.5% following better-than-expected earnings. Federal Reserve Chair Kevin Warsh is scheduled to speak at the Jackson Hole gathering on Friday. Treasury yields remained steady at 4.66% for the 10-year benchmark. Other market movements included HP shares dropping 9% and Moderna stock declining 4.6% due to a bond sale announcement.
source.title: Nvidia earnings boost Wall Street as Salesforce and CrowdStrike stocks surge

source.summary: Abhiruchi Bhatti shared a video of her grandmother, Nani, conversing with ChatGPT while believing the AI was a real person. Bhatti stated she lacked the heart to correct the misunderstanding. The clip sparked divided reactions online, with some praising the innocence while others criticized the video as a mockery of the elderly. Sounak Mukhopadhyay reported on the viral social media exchange.
source.title: Grandma chats with ChatGPT believing it is a human

source.summary: The Reserve Bank of India reported that aggregate sales growth for listed non-government non-financial companies accelerated to 19.4% year-on-year in the first quarter of FY27. Manufacturing emerged as a primary driver, with private sector sales expanding 21.4%, led by the automobile, petroleum, and electrical machinery industries. Operating profit growth jumped to 21.3% for manufacturing firms, while debt-servicing capacity improved across sectors. The RBI noted that elevated input costs and global supply-chain disruptions remain key factors for companies to monitor as they seek to sustain margins.
source.title: RBI data shows India Inc sales growth rose to 19.4% in Q1 FY27

source.summary: Anthropic instructed San Francisco employees to work remotely on Monday and Tuesday following a warning from security contractor Allied Universal about a possible guard strike. The Service Employees International Union stated no strike vote has been called or threatened. Anthropic is not part of ongoing wage negotiations between the union and Allied Universal but faces operational disruption if guards stop working. The company declined to comment on the instruction while Allied Universal emphasized a focus on safe operations. This precaution aligns with recent security threats against AI industry staff and Anthropic's upcoming initial public offering.
source.title: Anthropic orders San Francisco staff to work from home amid potential security strike
