source.summary: MIT researchers have developed a system called FloatForm, which uses a swarm of small robotic boats to autonomously assemble and reconfigure floating structures on water. Each robot, about 21 centimeters square, operates with its own thrusters, sensors, and magnetic latches, enabling them to self-organize into bridges, platforms, or other structures with minimal human input. The system draws inspiration from ant rafts, where individual agents follow simple rules to create resilient formations. The robots communicate with their immediate neighbors to navigate, avoid collisions, and adapt to disturbances, allowing for parallel movement and scalability. The project, published in Nature Communications, aims to transform underutilized water surfaces into dynamic, programmable spaces for urban environments, emergency response, and temporary infrastructure. The team tested the system in controlled environments, achieving high success rates with minimal human intervention, and plans to scale it for real-world applications such as canals and harbors.
source.title: MIT Researchers Develop Self-Organizing Floating Robots for Dynamic Water Infrastructure

source.summary: U.S. Air Force cadet Joshua Lynch, with no coding experience, used AI chatbots to develop a battlefield application called ROMAD-AI. Working with mentor Laura Niss, Lynch employed 'vibe-coding' through prompts to guide AI models like Claude, ChatGPT, and Gemini. The project aimed to create tools for reducing collateral damage and enhancing mission survivability. Lynch encountered challenges with AI limitations, leading to a re-scope of the project to focus on document processing instead of full battlefield capabilities. While the prototype showed AI's potential as a prototyping tool, it highlighted security risks and the need for code review. Niss noted AI's value in bridging non-technical and technical expertise, though collaboration remains essential for critical applications.
source.title: Air Force Cadet Uses AI to Develop Battlefield Software with Minimal Coding Experience

source.summary: A pre-registered trial in Sierra Leone found that an AI-powered learning tool, Guided Learning, significantly improved math scores and student engagement. The tool, developed by Google and collaborators, uses a 'Socratic' approach to encourage conceptual understanding rather than direct answers. Students used the tool to build understanding in 91.4% of interactions, with AI posing scaffolding questions in 76% of cases. Teachers reported increased professional growth and shifted from lecturers to facilitators. Students using the tool saw a 0.258 standard deviation gain in math scores, with higher gains in classrooms where teachers integrated AI into lessons. Engagement was notably high, with 69% of students meeting usage targets. The study also noted a shift in student behavior toward skill-building queries. The findings highlight the potential of AI as a pedagogical partner, though the achievement gap suggests the need for targeted support. The results are part of a broader effort to build a global evidence base for AI's impact on education.
source.title: AI tool enhances student learning through guided interactions in Sierra Leone

source.summary: Google Research introduces PHRM, a system that passively measures heart rate and resting heart rate using smartphone cameras during everyday use. The system leverages deep learning and facial video captured after face unlock events to estimate heart rate with a mean absolute percentage error under 10%, meeting industry standards across skin tones. PHRM also estimates daily resting heart rate with an accuracy comparable to wearables, achieving a mean absolute error under 5 beats per minute. The study, published in Nature, includes the largest and most diverse dataset of smartphone videos for research and a pre-trained model for accessibility. The system addresses challenges in detecting photoplethysmography (PPG) signals in darker skin tones, improving inclusivity and accuracy. PHRM's performance was validated through both controlled laboratory settings and real-world 'free-living' studies, demonstrating its effectiveness across diverse populations. The research highlights the potential of smartphones to democratize heart health monitoring, offering wearable-like insights through ubiquitous devices.
source.title: Google Research Introduces Smartphone-Based Heart Rate Monitoring System for Passive Health Tracking

source.summary: Google Research has open-sourced its hydrology model to aid flood forecasting globally. The framework, available on GitHub, enables National Meteorological and Hydrological Services to integrate AI-based flood predictions into their workflows. The model uses Python and PyTorch, incorporating data on climate, topography, and weather to predict river flow rates. It includes LSTM-based architectures and training pipelines using the Caravan dataset, allowing users to refine models with local data. The release includes two versions: one from a 2024 study and an upgraded model powering real-time forecasts on Google’s Flood Hub. The initiative, supported by partners like the Czech Hydrometeorological Institute, aims to improve flood preparedness by enabling regional forecasters to customize models. Dr. Hwirin Kim of the WMO praised the open-source approach for its potential to enhance global disaster response.
source.title: Google opens-sources hydrology framework for flood forecasting

source.summary: Google DeepMind is launching an accelerator program in the Asia-Pacific region to support innovators tackling environmental challenges. The initiative, focused on 'AI for the Planet,' aims to help startups, research teams, and nonprofits use advanced AI to address issues in climate, agriculture, and energy. Selected participants will receive mentorship and technical support from Google AI experts. The program begins with an in-person bootcamp in Singapore.
source.title: Google DeepMind Launches Asia-Pacific Accelerator to Address Environmental Risks

source.summary: Amazon and its vendors face challenges in optimizing supply chain operations due to information asymmetry. The article explains how the Vickrey-Clarke-Groves (VCG) framework, combined with Amazon's consensus planning protocol (CPP), creates a system called Flo Pro that enables cost-effective collaboration. This system allows both parties to achieve socially efficient outcomes without fully revealing proprietary cost structures. The VCG mechanism ensures truthful reporting by calculating transfer payments that reflect each party's externality on the other. CPP provides the computational backbone, enabling iterative optimization without requiring full disclosure of cost data. The approach was tested successfully with a major manufacturer, demonstrating real-world cost savings. The system supports dynamic, rolling-horizon planning and offers an alternative 'menu-of-contracts' method for lower-dimensional decision spaces. The work highlights the potential of mechanism design in supply chain coordination and opens new questions for future research.
source.title: Amazon and vendors use mechanism design to improve supply chain coordination

source.summary: Amazon has embedded responsible AI (RAI) into every phase of its AI model development, from pretraining to post-training and evaluation. The company's approach includes four key phases: pretraining, post-training, evaluation, and third-party monitoring. Senior scientist Chentao Ye explains that pretraining involves teaching models foundational RAI principles using diverse datasets, including internal and public guidance, to ensure adaptability across languages and cultures. Post-training uses reinforcement learning from human feedback (RLHF) to align models with human expectations and policy guidelines. Evaluations focus on creating model-breaking datasets to test for unsafe responses, while third-party collaborations address systemic risks like AI-enabled CBRN research. Amazon has developed over 70 RAI tools, published 500+ research papers, and provided extensive training to employees, emphasizing a proactive, three-pronged strategy for responsible AI implementation.
source.title: Amazon integrates responsible AI into all stages of model development

source.summary: Interim CEO Peter Clark of Ai2 emphasizes the institute's commitment to long-term, high-impact AI research and open science. He highlights the importance of maintaining focus on foundational research despite the rapid pace of AI development. Clark notes that projects like ELMo, Olmo, and Molmo demonstrate the potential of open models to drive scientific progress. He also discusses initiatives such as AutoDiscovery and OlmoEarth, which apply AI to real-world challenges in oncology and environmental science. Ai2 is prioritizing areas like AI for scientific discovery, embodied AI, and AI for the planet. Clark stresses the value of open models in enabling broader scientific understanding and collaboration, as seen in the NSF OMAI project. The institute aims to build a future where AI is both transparent and impactful, inviting participation from those interested in advancing science through open innovation.
source.title: Ai2's Interim CEO Discusses Long-Term AI Research and Open Science Commitment

source.summary: AstaBench, an open benchmark for evaluating AI agents' scientific research capabilities, has released updated results showing improved performance on coding, reasoning, and data analysis tasks. The benchmark tested models like GPT-5.5 and Claude Opus 4.7, with the latter achieving the highest score at 58.0%. However, end-to-end discovery remains challenging, with GPT-5.5 scoring 52.9% and struggling with complex workflows. The benchmark also gained industry adoption, with organizations like the UK AI Security Institute and General Reasoning integrating AstaBench into their evaluation frameworks. The results highlight uneven progress across categories and rising costs, emphasizing the need for continued development in full scientific workflows.
source.title: AstaBench benchmarks AI agents' scientific research capabilities with new results and industry adoption

source.summary: The National Institute of Standards and Technology (NIST) has released a new annotated fingerprint dataset and open-source software to aid forensic scientists. The dataset, part of NIST Technical Note 2367, includes 10,000 fingerprints from 200 volunteers, with annotations detailing print quality. These annotations help train both human examiners and AI systems to evaluate fingerprint quality. NIST also released OpenLQM, a modified version of the LQMetric software, which assesses fingerprint quality and is now open-source. The tools aim to improve accuracy and efficiency in forensic analysis. NIST computer scientist Greg Fiumara noted that the resources will enhance education and algorithm training for fingerprint identification.
source.title: NIST Releases Annotated Fingerprint Dataset and Open-Source Software for Forensic Use

source.summary: The National Institute of Standards and Technology (NIST) has submitted its annual report to Congress detailing progress on the National Construction Safety Team (NCST) Act activities for fiscal year 2025. The report highlights the completion of most technical work on the Champlain Towers South collapse investigation, including material testing, full-scale replica tests, and data analysis. It also covers NIST's work on Hurricane Maria's impact on Puerto Rico and actions taken to implement recommendations from the Joplin tornado investigation. The NCST Advisory Committee noted the investigation's thoroughness and expects its methodologies to improve building safety practices. The team plans to present its next findings in June 2026.
source.title: NIST Completes Major Technical Work on Champlain Towers South Collapse Investigation

source.summary: Leanstral, an open-source code agent for Lean 4, aims to enhance formal verification by generating code and proving its correctness. The project, developed by researchers, introduces a model with 6B active parameters, optimized for proof engineering tasks. It is released under an Apache 2.0 license, available through Mistral Vibe and a free API. Leanstral outperforms existing open-source models and competitors like the Claude suite in efficiency and performance, achieving higher scores with lower computational cost. The model was tested on real-world scenarios, including diagnosing issues in Lean 4 code and translating programs from Rocq to Lean. The team emphasizes its accessibility, offering zero-setup integration and the ability to run the model locally.
source.title: Leanstral: Open-Source Code Agent for Formal Verification

source.summary: An autonomous agent was developed to address the issue of insufficient test coverage in large Rails monoliths. The agent reads source files, generates or improves RSpec tests, validates them against style rules and coverage targets, and runs within a CI/CD pipeline without human intervention. It operates in parallel across multiple files, handling different file types like models, controllers, and helpers with specialized instructions. The agent uses Vibe, a coding assistant, with custom tools like RuboCop and SimpleCov to ensure test quality and execution. By enforcing a strict self-review process and using LLM-as-a-judge metrics, the agent improved test quality scores from 0.68 to 0.74. The experiment showed that the agent successfully generated tests for uncovered files and improved existing ones, achieving 100% coverage. However, challenges like syntax errors and versioning issues highlight the need for ongoing refinement.
source.title: Autonomous agent improves Rails test coverage by generating and refining RSpec tests

source.summary: Dario Amodei argues that public skepticism toward AI stems from a broader crisis of trust in companies, governments, and the tech industry. He contends that ordinary people suspect these entities of exploiting them, a distrust rooted in decades of history. Amodei dismisses the idea of using positive marketing campaigns to rebuild trust, stating that such efforts risk appearing deceptive. Instead, he emphasizes that AI companies, including Anthropic, must deliver on their promises to benefit society, which he views as the core issue requiring attention.
source.title: Amodei attributes public distrust in AI to broader trust crisis

source.summary: Instagram has refreshed its logo, with Adam Mosseri describing it as 'leaner and more modern' while referencing its original design. The update comes after 10 years without a change, a period the article notes as unusually long in the fast-paced tech industry. The author critiques the redesign, suggesting it reflects algorithmic data exploitation and influencer culture rather than simplicity. The article also humorously questions the new name 'Instagzam' as a possible typo.
source.title: Instagram updates logo with AI-driven design changes

source.summary: A study in Pakistan found that judges using a custom AI tool called JudgeGPT, combined with training, resolved 6.3% more cases without a drop in judgment quality. The tool, developed by economist Sultan Mehmood and collaborators, integrates OpenAI's GPT-4 with a database of Pakistani legal texts. It was tested with 1,559 judges, with those receiving comprehensive training showing the most significant improvements. The tool helps with legal research and drafting, reducing time spent on case law searches and document summaries. However, the study acknowledges limitations, including the lack of direct human evaluation of judgment quality and the risk of over-reliance on AI. Researchers emphasize the importance of training to ensure proper use of the technology, while noting that efficiency gains may not fully address broader concerns about justice quality.
source.title: Pakistan's Judges Report 6.3% Productivity Boost with JudgeGPT AI Tool

source.summary: Interconnects introduced the Artifacts Hub and Adoption Dashboard to enhance transparency in the open model ecosystem. The Artifacts Hub provides curated insights into 792 models from the past two years, including adoption metrics and intelligence analysis. The Adoption Dashboard tracks model downloads and usage by geography and organization, highlighting the US-China adoption gap. These tools aim to support the open ecosystem by offering data-driven insights and fostering growth through shared analysis.
source.title: Interconnects Launches Artifacts Hub and Adoption Dashboard to Track Open Model Ecosystem

source.summary: Arvind Narayanan and Akash Kapur argue that AI companies are moving beyond model provision to higher stack layers to avoid the commodity trap. They highlight that current AI business models, reliant on inference charges, face challenges due to undifferentiated models, low switching costs, and price flexibility. The authors suggest that AI labs must adopt enterprise software strategies like vertical integration and switching cost creation to achieve durable profitability. They warn that this shift risks customer lock-in and reduced competition, raising broader concerns about market concentration and innovation. Drawing on historical examples, they note that infrastructure providers rarely capture value, but cloud computing and chip fabrication have escaped the commodity trap through software-like properties or market dominance. The authors caution that without regulatory intervention or structural changes, AI may follow a similar path to past infrastructure industries.
source.title: AI Labs Seek Profitability Through Stack Migration Amid Concerns Over Lock-In

source.summary: The article argues that AI has not replaced software engineers and is unlikely to do so, despite widespread fears of job displacement. It examines the 'decide-execute-deliver' model of software development, noting that AI primarily automates the 'execute' phase but leaves the decision-making and delivery layers resistant to automation. The piece challenges narratives of AI-driven mass layoffs, citing examples like Block, Snap, and Intuit, where layoffs were often attributed to financial pressures or restructuring rather than AI. Surveys indicate that executives frequently cite AI as a reason for layoffs without evidence of actual implementation. The article also highlights that AI's productivity benefits are more evident in slower hiring rather than increased layoffs. While AI may reduce demand for certain roles, it does not eliminate the need for software engineers due to the complexity of decision-making and accountability. The authors conclude with cautious optimism, suggesting that the software engineering profession will continue to grow, albeit at a slower pace, as AI adoption progresses.
source.title: Software Engineering Jobs Remain Resilient Amid AI Adoption

source.summary: The U.S. dollar weakened slightly as investors considered expanded sanctions against Iran and Treasury efforts to ease pressure on longer-dated bonds. Treasury Secretary Scott Bessent's announcement to double repurchases of longer-dated bonds raised concerns about dollar debasement. The dollar index fell 0.07% to 98.92, while the euro and Canadian dollar rose. Canada imposed retaliatory tariffs on $20 billion in U.S. imports, escalating trade tensions. Bitcoin briefly surpassed $80,000 amid dollar weakness. Analysts noted mixed signals in the market, with Fed rate hike expectations easing.
source.title: U.S. dollar dips as sanctions and Treasury actions influence markets

source.summary: A graphic circulating on social media falsely claims Prime Minister Narendra Modi made a statement about distributing laddus in his village on Independence Day. The claim is false, as no such statement by Modi was found through keyword searches or verification of news reports. The graphic, attributed to Nav Bharat Times, was checked against the newspaper's official content and social media accounts, where no matching statement was found. The font used in the graphic also did not match the newspaper's style. The article concludes the graphic is fake and that Modi did not make the claimed statement.
source.title: PM Modi's claimed statement on distributing laddus on Independence Day is fake

source.summary: Delhi Police have registered a case of abetment to suicide against unidentified individuals linked to the death of a 31-year-old IIT Delhi M.Sc. Physics student who allegedly jumped from a building on campus on August 22. The student was found dead at the institute's hospital after being rushed there following the incident. Police collected evidence, seized a mobile phone, and are examining counselling records. No suicide note was found, and the circumstances surrounding the death, including any potential involvement of others, are under investigation. IIT Delhi expressed grief and stated it is supporting the bereaved family.
source.title: Delhi Police Investigate Abetment to Suicide in IIT Delhi Student's Death

source.summary: Indian jewelers Kalyan Jewellers, Tanishq, and Joyalukkas have expanded cash-for-gold services, bringing the practice into the organized retail sector. The move comes as gold prices rose to ₹1.62 lakh per 10 gm in Mumbai. Kalyan Jewellers reported that cash-for-gold accounted for double-digit revenue in the June quarter, up from single digits previously. Analysts noted that inflationary pressures are prompting consumers to liquidate household gold. Internationally, gold prices retreated slightly after hitting three-month highs, with traders awaiting US inflation data and Federal Reserve statements.
source.title: Indian jewelers expand cash-for-gold services amid rising prices

source.summary: President Trump announced the lowering of American flags for seven days in honor of Dolly Parton, who died at 80. The decision reflects her significant cultural impact beyond country music. Parton's family, represented by her nephew Brian Seaver, announced her death, highlighting her role as a family figure and her legacy of opening opportunities for others. Seaver shared personal anecdotes, including Parton's wish to rest in a 'beautiful bed of plush cotton,' reflecting her humor and self-awareness. Parton's career spanned decades, from her Tennessee roots to global fame, with contributions to music, film, and philanthropy, including the Imagination Library. Her legacy continues through tributes and the preservation of her work.
source.title: Trump orders national flag lowering for Dolly Parton

source.summary: Former Chief of Defence Staff General Anil Chauhan revealed that Pakistan sought commercial satellite imagery, including from Chinese providers, to evaluate the impact of its strikes during Operation Sindoor. Despite efforts spanning several days, Pakistan failed to find evidence of damage to its intended targets. Chauhan noted that while satellite imagery is accessible through US and Chinese companies, it requires contracts and payment, with delays in availability. The lack of evidence fueled speculation in Pakistan that information may have been withheld, possibly due to Indian pressure.
source.title: General Chauhan details Pakistan's failed satellite efforts to assess Operation Sindoor strikes

source.summary: The Uttar Pradesh Cabinet approved transferring six hectares of Gram Sabha land near Saman Bird Sanctuary to the Tourism Department. The site will be renamed Mayank Rishi Bird Sanctuary. The move aims to enhance tourist facilities, promote birdwatching, and connect the area with international tourism circuits. The government plans to develop infrastructure like watchtowers and solar lighting. Saman Bird Sanctuary, a Ramsar Site, attracts migratory birds from across the globe. The decision was made during a Cabinet meeting chaired by Chief Minister Yogi Adityanath.
source.title: UP government transfers land to develop Saman Bird Sanctuary tourism

source.summary: Motorola engineer Dr Martin Cooper made the first mobile phone call on April 3, 1973, to Joel Engel of Bell Laboratories. The call, made from a portable device on a New York City street, demonstrated the feasibility of a personal, handheld mobile phone. Cooper aimed to prevent AT&T from monopolizing mobile communications and emphasized the importance of personal freedom in communication. The call marked a pivotal moment in the development of mobile technology, leading to the eventual release of the Motorola DynaTAC 8000X in 1984.
source.title: Martin Cooper made first mobile phone call to rival in 1973

source.summary: Elon Musk's SpaceX plans to invest $100 billion in a new spaceport in Louisiana, set to be its fourth and largest launch site. The facility, located in Vermilion Parish, aims to support thousands of Starship launches annually and boost satellite deployment. Louisiana officials hailed the project as transformative, while environmental advocates raised concerns about coastal impact. SpaceX pledged to preserve land and engage with communities, with construction expected to begin in 2027.
source.title: SpaceX to develop new Louisiana spaceport for Starship launches

source.summary: Franklin Templeton's portfolio manager Sara Araghi emphasized that Nvidia needs to provide detailed information on capital deployment and spending sustainability, beyond just reporting an earnings beat. She highlighted the discrepancy between Nvidia's forward price-earnings ratio and projected growth, noting that markets are pricing in a slowdown despite continued revenue expansion. Araghi also mentioned Nvidia's strategy of raising prices to offset rising memory costs and the importance of showing earnings growth to reassure investors about free cash flow and stock buybacks. Nvidia is set to report earnings after the market close, with analysts warning that a typical beat may not be enough to boost sentiment.
source.title: Franklin's Araghi Urges Nvidia to Provide Capital Deployment Details Beyond Earnings Beat

source.summary: Prashant Kishor challenged Bihar Chief Minister Samrat Choudhary and Leader of Opposition Tejashwi Yadav to sit for their Class 10 exams together, responding to Education Minister Mithilesh Tiwari's advice to Yadav to clear matriculation before supporting student protests. Kishor urged both leaders to demonstrate their academic capability, referencing Yadav's failed Class 9 and Choudhary's past affidavit stating he was only a Class 7 pass. The challenge was made during a political debate over educational qualifications and youth expectations.
source.title: Bihar leaders challenged to take Class 10 exams together

source.summary: Dolly Parton, a legendary American country singer, songwriter, and actress, died at 80, according to her family. She sold over 100 million records globally and won 11 Grammy Awards, including a Lifetime Achievement Award. Parton began writing songs at six, with her first being 'Little Tiny Tasseltop.' She performed at the Grand Ole Opry at 13 and later became a solo artist, with 'I Will Always Love You' becoming a global hit after Whitney Houston's rendition. Parton also acted in films like '9 to 5' and built a business empire, including Dollywood. She was known for her philanthropy, including a $1 million donation to Vanderbilt University for Covid-19 vaccine research.
source.title: Dolly Parton, Country Music Icon, Dies at 80

source.summary: Food safety officials in Bengaluru inspected 10 elite clubs to check compliance with hygiene and food safety regulations. Inspections focused on food handling, storage, labelling, and cleanliness, revealing several shortcomings at the KSCA Club and Mahalakshmi Layout Club. Issues included inadequate hygiene among staff, improper storage of vegetarian and non-vegetarian items, and missing label information on packaged foods. Officials noted unhygienic conditions in utensil cleaning areas and lack of hot water. Further action will depend on the findings and compliance with corrective measures.
source.title: Health officials inspect Bengaluru clubs for food safety compliance

source.summary: Dick's Sporting Goods experienced a 28% stock decline after reporting second-quarter earnings below expectations. The company missed analyst forecasts of $3.78 EPS with $5.65 billion in sales, achieving only $3.53 EPS and $5.6 billion in revenue. Weak footwear demand, a key driver of customer traffic, contributed to the underperformance. While same-store sales grew 4.9%, profits fell due to lower margins. The company also revised its full-year earnings guidance downward to $11-$12 per share from $14.20, and sales forecasts to $22.2 billion from $22.4 billion. Investors are now closely watching footwear sales and the company's ability to improve its outlook.
source.title: Dick's Sporting Goods faces 28% stock drop due to earnings miss and footwear concerns

source.summary: The Ministry of Statistics and Programme Implementation (MoSPI) reported a cumulative cost overrun of ₹3,40,504 crore in infrastructure projects exceeding ₹150 crore. Out of 1,775 monitored projects across 17 ministries, the revised total cost reached ₹37,10,642 crore compared to the original ₹33,70,138 crore. The report noted that 675 projects (38%) achieved over 80% physical progress, while 305 (17%) completed over 80% financially. The Transport & Logistics sector had the highest number of projects (1,246) with a revised cost of ₹19.81 lakh crore, highlighting its role in connectivity-driven growth. The Ministry of Road Transport & Highways led with 993 projects (56%) and a 26% share of the total revised cost.
source.title: MoSPI reports ₹3.4 lakh crore cost overrun in major infrastructure projects

source.summary: Industry participants are calling for tighter eligibility and suitability norms for futures and options trading in India, following SEBI's regulatory interventions that failed to curb excessive retail speculation. Data shows while the number of individual traders fell, trading behavior remained unchanged, with 97% of retail activity concentrated in short-term contracts and 87.7% of traders ending the fiscal year with losses. Experts argue that suitability checks and investor profiling could better protect retail investors than product-level restrictions. SEBI faces a balancing act between addressing retail losses and maintaining market liquidity, as derivatives activity significantly contributes to the revenues of exchanges and intermediaries. The debate highlights the need for a regulatory framework that ensures investor protection without stifling participation.
source.title: Retail F&O losses drive push for stricter eligibility rules in derivatives trading

source.summary: Neurostellar, a Chennai-based startup, introduced its Orbit headband at a hybrid chess tournament in IIT Madras Research Park. The device uses EEG and PPG sensors to monitor brain and heart activity, providing real-time insights into stress, focus, and mental fatigue. The data is analyzed by algorithms developed with NIMHANS scientists to calculate cognitive endurance scores. The headband, priced at $250, is in pre-order with customers including athletes and CEOs. It also offers an app for problem-solving and deep work, alongside a coaching program to enhance cognitive performance.
source.title: Neurostellar's headband tracks cognitive endurance during chess tournament

source.summary: Tata Steel has received interim relief against a ₹1,755 crore mining demand notice from the Jharkhand government. The demand, issued by the District Mining Office in Ramgarh, alleges excess coal extraction of 16.24 million tonnes at the West Bokaro Colliery between 2000-01 and 2006-07. Tata Steel challenged the notice, arguing it lacked justification. The Revisional Authority admitted the company's revision application and directed authorities not to take coercive steps during the review. Tata Group Chairman N Chandrasekaran previously announced a ₹11,000 crore investment in Jharkhand to develop advanced-grade steel at the Jamshedpur facility.
source.title: Tata Steel Granted Interim Relief Against ₹1,755 Crore Mining Demand Notice

source.summary: The Indian government's ethanol-blended petrol (EBP) policy, particularly the push for E20 fuel, has sparked widespread public discontent. Critics argue that E20 results in lower fuel efficiency, higher repair costs, and increased expenses for users, despite official claims of benefits like reduced oil imports and support for farmers. The government has faced mounting pressure but has largely dismissed concerns, attributing mileage drops to factors like driving habits and vehicle conditions. Meanwhile, distillers benefit from guaranteed purchase agreements and subsidies, while farmers see little direct gain. The policy has also led to increased maize imports and concerns about food security, as land and water resources are diverted from food crops to ethanol production. The article highlights the uneven distribution of costs and benefits, with users bearing the brunt of the policy's negative impacts.
source.title: Ethanol Blending Policy: Users Bear Costs While Distillers and Farmers See Limited Gains

source.summary: Young activists in India are challenging the government's education system, demanding better infrastructure and accountability. The movement, led by Gen Alpha, began with protests over examination irregularities and escalated into a nationwide campaign for school improvements. The Cockroach Janta Party's 'School Thik Karo' initiative has sparked resistance, highlighting the political significance of the campaign. Despite lacking a central command, the protests have spread across multiple states, demanding basic facilities like classrooms, toilets, and teachers. The movement reflects a shift in Indian politics, where issues like education can unite people across identities, challenging the state's ability to suppress dissent. The article draws parallels to historical uprisings, suggesting that the current movement could have far-reaching implications for governance.
source.title: Gen Alpha demands accountability through education reforms

source.summary: The Trump administration announced a plan to pressure Iran by asking nations to cut business ties. However, China has already stated it will not cooperate with these voluntary trade restrictions.
source.title: Trump administration seeks voluntary trade cuts with Iran but China refuses

source.summary: A Belgian judge has extended pre-trial detention for one month for a Canadian national accused of spying for a third country while interning at NATO's SHAPE headquarters. The Belgian Federal Prosecutor's Office announced the decision following a rejected appeal by the defendant, identified as Claire Z. Authorities stated the investigation remains ongoing with no trial date set. While Canadian officials pledged to review security screening processes, a SHAPE spokesperson noted there is no indication military operations were disrupted.
source.title: Belgian judge extends pre-trial detention for alleged NATO spy

source.summary: President Donald Trump threatened to retaliate forcefully against Iranian attacks following a month-long pause in hostilities. The exchange began after US strikes on an Iranian island in the Strait of Hormuz, prompting Tehran to target US forces in Jordan and the UAE. While Trump stated all missiles were shot down except one, Jordan intercepted eight missiles and Iran claimed heavy damage to US bases. Iranian President Masoud Pezeshkian called for dialogue, contrasting with Trump's description of Iran as a failed nation. US Treasury Secretary Scott Bessent vowed to continue economic pressure on Tehran. The conflict persists alongside a naval counter-blockade of Iranian ports and a dispute over control of the strategic shipping lane.
source.title: Trump vows to hit Iran hard after strikes resume in Strait of Hormuz

source.summary: Former French Prime Minister Edouard Balladur has died at age 97, his family confirmed to AFP. President Emmanuel Macron honored him as a devoted public servant who dedicated his life to the Fifth Republic. Current Prime Minister Sebastien Lecornu called him a statesman with a reformist spirit. Marine Le Pen also shared condolences, praising his commitment to democratic debate. A private mass service is planned in Paris.
source.title: Former French PM Edouard Balladur dies at 97 after long public service

source.summary: Kenya airport staff are striking, causing delays for thousands of passengers. The strike is happening at Kenya's main airport. Travelers are currently grounded due to the industrial action. This news is part of tonight's edition of the broadcast.
source.title: Kenya airport staff strike delays thousands of passengers

source.summary: India plans to construct one of the world's largest nuclear fleets, creating a market worth tens of billions of dollars. For 15 years, a specific provision in Indian law prevented Japanese firms from participating. Last December, that legal restriction was removed, opening the market to Japanese suppliers. Tokyo now faces a strategic decision on whether to enter this market under rules that reduce supplier liability for catastrophic failures.
source.title: India removes legal barrier to Japanese nuclear reactor exports

source.summary: The UN Committee on the Elimination of Racial Discrimination urged governments to implement comprehensive reparations for people of African descent. The 18-member committee stated that time cannot excuse the enduring consequences of the transatlantic slave trade. Experts called for financial and non-financial remedies alongside national action plans. The group also urged private institutions that profited from slavery to contribute to reparative efforts. Committee member Pela Boker-Wilson emphasized that governments must take concrete action beyond mere apologies.
source.title: UN panel urges states to adopt reparations for slavery legacy

source.summary: President Donald Trump signed an executive order renaming Lake Ontario to Lake America, extending a previous move to rename the Gulf of Mexico. Geographer Jesús Burgueño notes this unilateral action bypasses standard toponymy commissions and reflects an autocratic style. While New York Governor Kathy Hochul rejects the change, companies like National Geographic are expected to comply domestically. Canadian Prime Minister Mark Carney has publicly rejected the initiative, citing the name's Indigenous origins and historical significance. Experts warn that international bodies like the IHO and UNGEGN do not arbitrate such disputes, leaving the impact dependent on private digital mapping platforms. Some platforms may adopt dual labeling, while others refuse to propagate the change entirely.
source.title: Trump renames Lake America to Lake America via executive order

source.summary: NASA successfully launched the Nancy Grace Roman Space Telescope on Sunday, beginning its journey to a gravitational outpost 1.5 million kilometers from Earth. Nicky Fox, associate administrator of NASA's Science Mission Directorate, stated the mission aims to answer fundamental questions about the universe's composition and whether we are alone. The telescope features a field of view at least one hundred times larger than Hubble, allowing it to scan more than a billion galaxies. Mission scientists expect Roman to discover up to 100,000 new worlds beyond our Solar System. The instrument will utilize weak gravitational lensing to study dark matter and dark energy, addressing discrepancies in the standard model of cosmology. Julie McEnery, the project's senior scientist, described the mission as a revolution in how we observe the universe. Begoña Vila, a co-lead of operations, noted the telescope will provide an overview of the universe's structure that predecessors could not achieve. The spacecraft is expected to generate around 500 terabytes of data annually and operate for five years, with a possible five-year extension. Data will be made publicly available to the global scientific community without a proprietary period.
source.title: NASA launches Roman telescope to map a billion galaxies and solve cosmic mysteries

source.summary: Nepal's disaster agency reported 939 deaths and 3,925 missing people following catastrophic flash floods. A private-sector association stated at least 900 workers remain unaccounted for at 12 hydropower projects, with about 500 trapped in tunnels. Chinese authorities reported 16 deaths and 546 missing, including over 100 Nepalis. Rescue teams are digging through sludge to find survivors while experts warn chances of survival are diminishing.
source.title: Nepal flood deaths reach 939 as search continues for trapped workers

source.summary: The Egyptian army announced that joint air drills with China are ongoing at multiple bases. The second edition of the Eagles of Civilization exercise aims to enhance pilot skills and includes aerial refueling training. Chinese Defense Ministry spokesperson Chen Xi stated the drills will conclude in early September. President Xi Jinping is expected to visit Cairo this week for his first trip to Egypt in a decade.
source.title: Egypt and China hold joint air drills ahead of Xi's Cairo visit

source.summary: Nepal's Prime Minister Balendra Shah faces a major crisis as deadly floods kill over 900 people and leave nearly 4,800 missing. Authorities report that rescue efforts are hampered by difficult terrain and delayed international assistance. The disaster has exposed questions about the new government's crisis management capacity and coordination with local authorities. While security agencies received praise for helicopter rescues, critics argue the federal government acted too centrally without involving provincial bodies. Over 5 billion Nepali rupees have been collected for relief, showing public trust in the administration.
source.title: Nepal floods test young PM Balen's government response

source.summary: A failed coup attempt in Niger highlights deep fractures within the military and increasing reliance on Russian forces. Sahel expert Abdoulaye Sounaye noted that most soldiers earn less than €150 monthly while facing high risks against better-equipped insurgents. General Abdourahamane Tchiani's junta, which ousted President Mohamed Bazoum in 2023, now faces loyalty challenges as troops question leadership and resource allocation. Senegalese expert Pape Ibrahima Kane described the event as an attempted coup, suggesting the junta would have fallen without Russian Africa Corps intervention. While Algeria also supported the regime with fighter jets, the incident underscores the limits of foreign security partnerships in resolving internal structural crises.
source.title: Failed Niger coup exposes military cracks and Russia's growing influence

source.summary: An IMF mission led by Gavin Gray began discussions with Ukrainian authorities on Monday regarding the economic outlook and the 2027 budget. The Fund's Ukraine office stated the talks will assess progress on reforms under the $8.1 billion Extended Fund Facility program. This follows the July approval of the first review, which cleared $690 million in disbursements. Discussions focus on macroeconomic stability and structural reforms needed amid ongoing wartime spending.
source.title: IMF mission starts talks with Ukraine on 2027 budget and reforms

source.summary: The Trump administration announced a joint venture with a private Venezuelan company to develop 65 billion barrels of oil reserves, with the U.S. government taking a 55% stake. An anonymous administration official confirmed the agreement, which President Trump described as the biggest oil deal in the world. However, energy experts express skepticism regarding the deal's structure and immediate impact. The U.S. lacks a national oil company to operate the venture, and the 'at-cost' terms may deter private investors seeking market premiums. Furthermore, questions remain about the legitimacy of the acting Venezuelan government led by Delcy Rodríguez. Experts state the deal will not lower gas prices soon because the oil fields are undeveloped and production would take years to begin.
source.title: Trump administration announces Venezuela oil deal that experts say won't lower gas prices

source.summary: A Children and Families Agency survey indicates that 35% of unmarried young people in Japan have no desire to marry. Approximately 15,000 of the 43,500 respondents selected this option, often prioritizing hobbies and leisure. The study, conducted online between May and August, gathered valid responses from 68,000 individuals aged 15 to 39. Officials plan to release final results by next March to inform policy measures.
source.title: Japan survey finds 35% of unmarried youth reject marriage

source.summary: The National Cybercrime Threat Analytics unit warns users about financial fraud linked to malicious Android apps disguised as pornography. These apps, often promoted on Facebook and Instagram, exploit accessibility permissions to take control of devices. The unit advises caution against sideloaded applications masquerading as adult content to prevent unauthorized access.
source.title: NCTAU warns of fraud via porn app ads on social media

source.summary: BJP and Congress exchanged sharp words on Monday following an FIR against Rahul Gandhi. The opposition party criticized the legal action after he demanded venue purification. BJP claimed he raised the issue late due to Kharge's threat to quit.
source.title: BJP and Congress exchange barbs over FIR against Rahul Gandhi

source.summary: US stock indexes closed lower on Friday as rising oil prices and Federal Reserve Chair Kevin Warsh's hawkish comments dampened investor sentiment. Despite the daily losses, all three major indexes recorded monthly gains for August. Market participants now price in a high probability of a 25-basis-point rate hike in September. Sector performance varied, with energy shares advancing while utilities lagged due to regulatory issues in California.
source.title: US stocks fall as oil prices rise and investors fear rate hikes

source.summary: Fifty-one people with disabilities in Visakhapatnam received free three-wheeler motor vehicles on Monday. Legislators Vishnukumar Raju and Vamsi Krishna Srinivas, along with officials M. Visweswara Naidu and Kavitha, flagged off the initiative. Each vehicle costs approximately ₹1.02 lakh, with 51 beneficiaries selected from 79 applications. The State government aims to promote independent living through this distribution.
source.title: 51 disabled residents in Vizag receive free three-wheeler bikes

source.summary: JSW Energy has surpassed 15 GW of total installed capacity, driven largely by renewable additions. The company reports a 26% compound annual growth rate since crossing the 10 GW mark in March 2025. Over 80% of recent capacity additions come from solar, wind, hydro, and hybrid projects. JSW Energy aims to reach 30 GW by 2030 and achieve carbon neutrality by 2050.
source.title: JSW Energy Surpasses 15 GW Capacity With Renewable Surge

source.summary: A Tennessee appeals court halted the execution of Christa Pike, a woman sentenced to death in 1995 for the murder of a fellow student. The stay, issued by the U.S. Court of Appeals for the Sixth Circuit, allows judges to review whether Pike's childhood sexual abuse and rape allegations were considered before her sentence. Pike's lawyers argue her death sentence should be replaced with life without parole due to her history of abuse and mental health issues. The state and governor previously denied requests to stay the execution, but Pike's execution would have been the first for a woman in Tennessee in over two centuries.
source.title: Tennessee Execution Stayed as Appeals Court Reviews Abuse Allegations

source.summary: The CPI(M) threatens indefinite agitation in Pathanamthitta, demanding the UDF government exclude seven villages from the proposed Ecologically Sensitive Area. The opposition argues the state's revised proposal failed to list these villages, despite receiving around 75,000 appeals for their exclusion. A senior Congress leader stated the state report excludes inhabited areas, while the CPI(M) warns restrictions could worsen human-wildlife conflict and force residents to abandon homes.
source.title: Protests Loom Over ESA Proposal in Pathanamthitta

source.summary: Mitsubishi Motors Philippines announced the return of the Outlander PHEV to the local market. The vehicle features updated styling and enhanced performance capabilities. This move signals the company's continued investment in plug-in hybrid technology for the region. The launch aims to capture growing demand for efficient yet powerful SUVs.
source.title: Mitsubishi returns Outlander PHEV to Philippine market with new muscle

source.summary: Anthropic has issued a formal warning in its IPO prospectus that its technology may pose existential risks to humanity. The company, led by Dario Amodei, dedicated nearly a third of its filing to risk factors, including potential AI behaviors like manipulation and blackmail. While backers project a valuation over $2 trillion, the disclosures highlight challenges in valuing the firm ahead of its expected Nasdaq listing this autumn.
source.title: Anthropic Warns Investors of Existential AI Risks in IPO Prospectus

source.summary: The Delhi government has made the Pink Saheli Smart Card compulsory for women and transgender residents to access free travel on DTC and cluster buses. This shift replaces paper tickets with an NCMC-based system effective September 30 under 2026 regulations. While free travel remains available, passengers may still purchase tickets at applicable fares. Officials plan to boost awareness through various media channels.
source.title: Delhi Makes Pink Saheli Smart Card Mandatory for Women's Free Bus Travel

source.summary: U.S. grid planners anticipate annual electricity demand growth of about 0.9% to 1.6% through 2050, with data centers emerging as a major driver. EPRI suggests data centers could account for as much as 17% of U.S. electricity demand by 2030. While this represents a significant growth market for renewable energy providers, hyperscale developers prioritize speed-to-power, reliability, and scalability over traditional economic factors. Consequently, the industry is shifting toward integrated power solutions involving solar, storage, and conventional generation to meet these stringent requirements and manage associated risks.
source.title: Data Centers Reshape Renewable Energy Market Through Speed and Scale Demands

source.summary: In an interview with Living on Earth, author Craig Childs discusses his new book, 'The Wild Dark,' which explores the impact of artificial light on the night sky. Childs, a naturalist based in Colorado, explains how light pollution obscures the view of stars and affects wildlife and human circadian rhythms. He details a journey he took by bike from Las Vegas to a dark sky area to experience different levels of light, ranging from Bortle Nine to Bortle One. Childs notes that while light pollution is a significant issue, he believes it can be reversed through strategic lighting and community efforts. He highlights that 80 percent of people cannot see the Milky Way and shares stories of how light affects bird migration and human health. The interview emphasizes the importance of preserving dark skies for both ecological and human well-being.
source.title: Author Craig Childs Discusses the Value of Dark Skies and Light Pollution

source.summary: Ukrainian Foreign Minister Andrii Sybiha and Iranian Foreign Minister Abbas Araghchi met in New York to discuss preventing further tensions. Sybiha stated that diplomacy requires direct conversation even in challenging circumstances. He emphasized Ukraine's goal to avoid unnecessary escalation while defending against Russian aggression. Araghchi noted Iran does not seek escalation but demanded restitution for losses. Both leaders agreed to maintain open communication channels.
source.title: Ukrainian and Iranian diplomats discuss steps to prevent tensions

source.summary: Rory McIlroy told BBC Sport that President Donald Trump's expected visit to the Irish Open will bring logistical challenges and a different feel. A White House official previously confirmed Trump planned to attend the tournament at his Doonbeg course. McIlroy added that crowds will be limited and that Trump might present the winner with the trophy on Sunday evening.
source.title: Rory McIlroy says Trump's visit brings security challenges

source.summary: Barret Zoph, a former co-founder of Thinking Machines and OpenAI, has joined Google as vice president of research. He previously worked at Google and spent five months at OpenAI before leaving in June. A Google spokesperson stated Zoph will bring his reinforcement learning and post-training expertise to Gemini. TechCrunch reported on the move after reaching out to both OpenAI and Google for comment.
source.title: Barret Zoph Joins Google as Vice President of Research

source.summary: The Saudi Foreign Ministry reported on Friday that a drone attack on its East-West Pipeline was launched from Iraq, causing injuries and damage. The kingdom refrained from immediate retaliation at the Iraqi prime minister's request to allow measures to prevent future attacks. Iraqi armed forces spokesperson Sabah al-Numan later confirmed the attack originated in Maysan province, resulting in the dismissal of the province's military commander and an investigation into responsible parties.
source.title: Saudi Arabia condemns drone attack on pipeline launched from Iraq

source.summary: Economists at the Federal Reserve recently evaluated Kalshi, the largest federally regulated prediction market overseen by the CFTC. The Fed found that Kalshi offers a high-frequency, continuously updated benchmark for macroeconomic expectations. Kalshi Research is applying this data to create the Citizen Debt Forecast, which updates continuously unlike the CBO. This new forecast can incorporate market expectations about future legislative changes regarding taxes and spending.
source.title: Kalshi Research explores using prediction markets to improve economic forecasts

source.summary: Former NITI Aayog Vice Chairman Rajiv Kumar stated that Apple sought to bring its Chinese vendors to India during its expansion. Kumar told The Core that the government agreed to the move despite initial resistance. He argued India should welcome more Chinese foreign direct investment.
source.title: Former NITI Aayog VC says Apple wanted Chinese vendors in India

source.summary: A Panama-flagged cargo ship carrying 72,000 tonnes of iron ore sank off the Odisha coast in the Bay of Bengal, leaving 22 seafarers missing and two rescued. The vessel, MV Ocean Winner, departed Paradip Port on Friday and reportedly sank in deep waters on Saturday. Officials stated that the crew included 20 Chinese nationals, three Myanmar citizens, and one Bangladeshi national. Rescue operations, involving the Indian Coast Guard, Navy, and merchant vessels, are underway to locate the missing crew. The ship developed a list and sank within eight minutes, according to survivors. The cause of the sinking remains under investigation, with possibilities including adverse weather, cargo issues, or mechanical failure. Authorities are also examining the loss of the vessel from tracking systems.
source.title: Panama-flagged cargo ship sinks off Odisha coast, 22 missing

source.summary: The FBI has returned 48 ancient Egyptian artefacts to Egyptian authorities following an investigation by its Art Crime Team. The collection includes figurines, amulets, and tomb equipment from the Pharaonic, Roman, and Coptic periods. FBI Assistant Director Patrick Grandy highlighted their cultural significance. Special Agent Allen Grove noted ongoing efforts to identify traffickers and potential missing items.
source.title: FBI returns 48 Egyptian artefacts after investigation

source.summary: NTPC Renewable Energy Limited secured 500 MW under SECI’s FDRE-IX tender at ₹6/kWh, securing one-third of the total capacity. POWERGRID invited bids for a 265 MW/530 MWh BESS project in Haryana, aiming to enhance grid flexibility. India’s renewable generation reached 38,497 MU in July 2026, with solar and wind contributing 96.14%. REC transferred Luhri SPV to Terralight for ₹14.13 crore. OREDA invited empanelment for rooftop solar in Odisha, while POWERGRID won a ₹822.91 crore Gujarat RE transmission project. KELTRON sought partners for solar and street light projects across North and East India.
source.title: NTPC REL wins 500 MW renewable tender, POWERGRID expands storage projects

source.summary: A long-time Firefox user who previously abandoned the browser due to bloat and lack of features has returned, citing recent improvements. The author highlights five key features that contributed to this change: a refined theming engine offering more consistent visual styling, vertical tabs for better tab management, containers for enhanced privacy, a built-in VPN for secure browsing, and AI integration through Smart Window and a sidebar chatbot. These features, many available in Firefox's Nightly builds, have made the browser more efficient and user-friendly, prompting the author to reconsider Firefox as a viable option.
source.title: Firefox's New Features Win Back User After Years of Struggles

source.summary: Varun Beverages, a major PepsiCo franchisee, has approved the creation of KIVA Spirits and Company, a subsidiary focused on alcoholic beverages and ready-to-drink products. The move, subject to regulatory approvals, follows the company's strategy to expand into new beverage categories. Prathmesh Mishra, previously with Diageo, will lead the subsidiary. The company also approved a joint venture in Tunisia for beverage production and distribution, with Varun holding 75% of the stake. Varun reported a 15% rise in net profit to ₹1,525.35 crore for the June quarter of 2026, driven by growth in both India and international markets.
source.title: Varun Beverages establishes subsidiary for alcoholic drinks and RTD products

source.summary: The Multi Commodity Exchange of India reports a structural shift in the nation's coal market driven by renewable expansion and market maturity. Coal remains the backbone of power generation, supplying 69% of electricity in FY2025-26. Domestic production rose to 26% of total output, while thermal coal imports declined to 159.7 million tonnes. The report states the market is now focusing on operational flexibility and risk management rather than just volume.
source.title: MCX Report Details India's Coal Market Structural Shift

source.summary: The PanIIT Andhra Pradesh Summit 2026 will be held in Vijayawada on October 3, organized by PanIIT Alumni India under the theme 'Andhra's DeepTech Decade.' Chief Minister N. Chandrababu Naidu will be the chief guest, while Education, IT and Electronics Minister Nara Lokesh will participate. The summit aims to foster a DeepTech ecosystem by bringing together IIT directors, government officials, industry leaders, and investors to explore opportunities in artificial intelligence, semiconductors, and other technology sectors. Organizers stated the event will strengthen collaboration among the government, IITs, industry, investors, and startups, focusing on research, innovation, investment, and skill development.
source.title: PanIIT Andhra Pradesh Summit to be held in Vijayawada on October 3

source.summary: India's home loan rates have fallen below US rates for the first time. While US rates exceed 7.3%, India's start at 7.10%. Experts note that currency risk and rental yields remain critical for non-residents considering property purchases in either country.
source.title: India home loan rates now lower than US rates

source.summary: Nepal Finance Minister Swarnim Wagle stated that the death toll from flash floods in Nepal and China could reach 10,000, according to a report by The Indian Express. As of Saturday, 1,411 people had died and 5,875 were missing. The floods, caused by a glacial collapse in Rasuwa district, severely impacted energy infrastructure, including 13 hydropower plants. India has approved an early import of 654 megawatts of electricity to offset the shortfall.
source.title: Nepal Minister Says Flood Toll May Reach 10,000

source.summary: Former Union minister and BJP leader Ravneet Singh Bittu's convoy was attacked on Friday in Punjab while he was traveling to Pathankot for a party event. According to Bittu's office, his security team apprehended three individuals allegedly linked to the AAP. The office stated that the chief minister of Punjab and the DGP Punjab would be held responsible for his safety. It added that such incidents are a grave threat to democracy and demanded an immediate investigation into the incident to ensure the safety of political workers and leaders.
source.title: Former Union Minister Ravneet Singh Bittu's Convoy Attacked in Punjab

source.summary: India's Ambassador to Nepal Naveen Srivastava announced the delivery of the first consignment of components for a 70-metre Bailey bridge to Nepal's Road Division in Hetauda. The Indian Embassy stated this bridge will restore connectivity in the flood-affected Betrawati area. According to the Ministry of External Affairs, India has provided over 130 tonnes of relief material and deployed 54 experts to assist with rescue and forensic operations following the devastating floods that killed nearly 1,400 people.
source.title: India sends first Bailey bridge components to flood-hit Nepal

source.summary: Transport Secretary Heidi Alexander told the Commons that the recent four-hour failure of the Nats air traffic control system was avoidable. She has ordered an independent review by the Civil Aviation Authority while Nats conducts its own investigation. The outage, which occurred at the Swanwick Centre in Hampshire, resulted in over 2,000 cancelled flights. Alexander noted that while a cyberattack could be ruled out, the issue was not unavoidable, highlighting concerns about system resilience and consumer redress.
source.title: Transport Secretary says UK air traffic failure was avoidable

source.summary: Apple will unveil its first foldable phone, the iPhone Ultra, on September 9 under incoming CEO John Ternus. The device features dual screens, four cameras, and the A20 Pro processor, with a starting price of €2,200. Analysts predict Apple will dominate the foldable market, selling over 10 million units in its first year. The event will also introduce the Apple Watch Series 12, iPad mini 8, and other products.
source.title: Apple Unveils Foldable iPhone Ultra on September 9

source.summary: At least 19 people died after allegedly consuming spurious liquor in Nagaland, where a prohibition law has been active since 1990. Police reported eight deaths in Mokokchung and 11 in Tuensang over two days. A Special Investigation Team led by Additional Superintendent of Police I Bunglang Chang has been formed to trace the supply chain. Samples were sent to Guwahati for forensic examination to determine the cause of death.
source.title: Nagaland Police Investigate Deaths Linked to Spurious Liquor

source.summary: Rama Afullo, a former Google and SpaceX employee, founded Satlyt to develop software that enables satellites to perform complex computing tasks independently. The company raised an $8 million seed round led by Non Sibi Ventures. Afullo aims to create an open ecosystem for satellite computing, contrasting with competitors building physical orbital data centers. Satlyt has already tested its software on demonstration missions, reporting a reduction in transmission size for software errors by more than 60%. The company plans to launch its software on a SpaceX rocket this week and expects to operate on 20% of satellites by the end of the decade.
source.title: Satlyt Raises $8M to Run AI on Satellites

source.summary: OpenAI released Astra, a new model it describes as its most capable and safest to date. President Greg Brockman stated the launch signals the beginning of the AGI era. The company reported that Astra outperformed other frontier models in benchmarks covering computer use, software engineering, and professional work. OpenAI plans to roll out the model to specific organizations before making it available to all ChatGPT users and API customers.
source.title: OpenAI launches Astra, claiming it marks the arrival of artificial general intelligence

source.summary: The US and China published lists of goods eligible for lower tariffs under a new framework, covering approximately $30bn in annual trade. While specific rates and dates remain unset, the deal could affect European exporters of pork, dairy, and whiskey facing American competition. Conversely, cheaper Chinese goods may struggle in the US market. The impact depends on the final tariff reductions and their timing.
source.title: US and China List Goods for Tariff Cuts, Impact on Europe Uncertain

source.summary: Reserve Bank of India Governor Sanjay Malhotra stated that while the nation maintains a cautious stance on cryptocurrencies due to risks to monetary sovereignty, it supports blockchain and distributed ledger technologies. Malhotra noted that domestic payments are efficient, making cross-border solutions like CBDCs more relevant. He also linked rising global bond yields to increased government and private spending, including AI-related expenditure, urging the RBI to monitor international interest rates while prioritizing domestic growth.
source.title: RBI Governor Malhotra Balances Crypto Caution with Blockchain Support Amid Global Economic Concerns

source.summary: Dozens of soldiers were arrested or killed in Niger's capital following an attempted mutiny driven by anger over militant violence. Russia's Africa Corps provided support to local forces to suppress the rebellion at a base near the presidential palace. Loyalist forces regained control of the airport, though some rebel troops remained mobile. Public gatherings in Niamey expressed support for military leader Abdourahamane Tchiani, who took power in a 2023 coup.
source.title: Dozens of soldiers arrested in Niger after attempted mutiny

source.summary: The Indian government has conducted a pilot test on NH-44 in Jhansi, mixing waste plastic with bitumen to pave a highway. Developed by IIT (BHU) Varanasi, this wet-process technology aims to reduce bitumen imports and manage plastic waste. Officials state the method could lower costs and improve road durability, with performance currently being monitored for long-term engineering suitability.
source.title: Government Pioneers Waste Plastic Bitumen Mix on National Highway

source.summary: The WTO has released the programme for its 2026 Public Forum, which will examine the role of services in global development. The event, held in Geneva, features high-level panels on future trading systems and digital services. Days two and three include over 100 sessions on macro-economic topics and new curated conversations. Registration for the in-person event is now closed.
source.title: WTO launches 2026 Public Forum programme on services trade

source.summary: A ground-mounted solar plant in Chiba prefecture caught fire on Sept. 24 after floodwater from a breached North Inba-numa lake embankment submerged its electrical equipment. Local fire officials stated that combiner boxes may have short-circuited as water levels fell. Firefighters could not approach due to electrocution risks. The plant operator, Senario Hiroshima GHD, is investigating the cause and cutting wiring to prevent re-ignition.
source.title: Flooded Solar Plant in Chiba Catches Fire After Typhoon

source.summary: MolmoPoint improves vision-language models' ability to point directly at visual elements, surpassing previous methods by selecting from what it sees rather than generating text coordinates. This approach achieves better accuracy and efficiency, particularly in complex UIs. MolmoWeb, an open-source web agent, navigates websites using screenshots alone, enabling task automation without relying on HTML or accessibility data. Both tools build on Molmo 2's open development philosophy, expanding the ecosystem for visual intelligence and action. The projects aim to make AI systems more accessible and collaborative, reducing dependency on proprietary solutions.
source.title: MolmoPoint and MolmoWeb enhance open-source vision models with direct pointing and web navigation

source.summary: Kia is offering up to $10,000 in customer cash on select electric vehicles, including the EV9 and Niro, while the EV6 receives a $5,000 discount. The new EV3, starting at about $30,000, is available with a $1,500 discount or 0.90% APR financing. Kia aims to carry record sales momentum into the end of the year, with offers ending November 2, 2026.
source.title: Kia Offers Up To $10,000 Discount on Select EVs

source.summary: 24/7 Wall St. analysts have lowered their 12-month price target for AMD to $510.66, implying roughly 9% downside from the current trading price of $559.82. The firm cites a trailing P/E of 211 as a key concern, noting that NVIDIA trades at just 45x earnings with 75% gross margins. Although AMD's Data Center revenue doubled 107% year-over-year to $6.72 billion, the analysts argue the stock is fully priced for perfect execution on Helios and Instinct products. The report recommends holding the stock with high confidence, though it warns that real upside could only come from faster-than-expected AI accelerator deployments.
source.title: 24/7 Wall St. Lowers AMD Price Target Amid High Valuation Concerns

source.summary: Uttar Pradesh Chief Minister Yogi Adityanath stated the state holds enough sugar for seven months, yet wholesale prices remain among the highest in India. The article explains that warehouse stock levels do not directly determine retail prices due to complex regulatory controls. Government data indicates mills hold approximately 17.94 lakh tonnes, while the Chief Minister cited 28 lakh tonnes, a discrepancy potentially caused by unsold sugar floating in the open market. Furthermore, the Union Food Ministry sets monthly release quotas that restrict how much sugar mills can sell, regardless of available inventory. The text details how the Essential Commodities Act limits dealer stock and how the Minimum Selling Price of Rs 31 a kg influences market behavior. Industry associations report production costs exceeding Rs 41 a kg, contributing to high prices despite record cane production. Ultimately, the article argues that central regulations on quotas and pricing, rather than state stock levels, dictate sugar availability and cost for consumers.
source.title: UP Chief Minister claims seven months of sugar stock, but prices remain high
