source.summary: The Orchard framework introduces an open-source solution for scalable agentic AI, designed to overcome infrastructure bottlenecks in research. It features Orchard Env, a Kubernetes-based environment service that supports multiple agent types and tasks without modification. The framework includes three domain-specific training recipes—Orchard-SWE, Orchard-GUI, and Orchard-Claw—demonstrating that small open-weight models can achieve strong results on complex tasks. Orchard-SWE reaches 69.7% on SWE-bench Verified using about 3 billion parameters, while Orchard-GUI achieves 68.4% across web navigation benchmarks. The project also provides training data and evaluation methods to aid the research community. By enabling training directly within real deployment harnesses, Orchard reduces the gap between research and practical application, allowing agents to be trained and evaluated in the same environments they will operate in.
source.title: Orchard framework enables scalable agentic AI with open-source tools

source.summary: Analysts identify the RBI's interest rate decision, TCS earnings, crude oil prices, and global bond yields as critical factors for stock market movement this week. Additional influences include macroeconomic data and foreign investor activity. Recent market declines were driven by foreign selling, rupee weakness, and elevated crude prices, with specific index losses detailed in the report.
source.title: RBI policy, TCS earnings, crude prices to steer markets this week

source.summary: U.S. utility-scale electricity generation rose 2.1 percent in the first half of 2026, driven largely by data center demand and state-specific shifts in power sources. Texas led the nation with the largest increase, where utility-scale solar grew 35 percent and is on pace to exceed coal generation for the first time. Washington saw significant gains from hydropower following heavy rains, while Tennessee boosted output by running existing nuclear plants more frequently. Ohio relied on new natural gas facilities, and New Mexico combined coal and solar growth. Conversely, California decreased generation due to battery storage and imports. The U.S. Energy Information Administration reported that natural gas remains the leading source at 38.4 percent, followed by renewables at 28.5 percent. Nicolas Fulghum of Ember noted that Texas's rapid solar growth reflects cost advantages rather than policy alone. The article highlights that while national trends show modest growth, Texas is emerging as a central hub for renewable energy expansion.
source.title: Texas Leads U.S. Electricity Growth as Solar Surges Past Coal

source.summary: The Enforcement Directorate has written to the Kerala Director General of Police seeking registration of an FIR against former Chief Minister Pinarayi Vijayan, his daughter T Veena, and son-in-law PA Mohamed Riyas. The probe concerns alleged money laundering and bribery linked to Cochin Minerals and Rutile Limited (CMRL). The ED alleges the mining company made fraudulent payments of Rs 2.78 crore to Veena's defunct IT firm, Exalogic Solutions, without providing services. Officials privy to the matter stated Vijayan allegedly received Rs 3.28 crore as illegal gratification through his daughter. The agency also claims handwritten notes and digital evidence indicate involvement in hawala transactions and fund transfers to Dubai, implicating Riyas. Recent searches at eight premises in Kozhikode and other locations yielded incriminating records, and the ED has frozen about Rs 18.36 crore in 242 accounts for analysis.
source.title: ED seeks FIR against Kerala ex-CM Vijayan over CMRL money laundering

source.summary: Arizona has become a significant player in the U.S. grid battery market, surpassing all states except Texas in the first half of 2026. The state's rapid growth in battery installations, including three major projects totaling 250 MW/1 GWh, reflects a trend continuing from 2025. Arizona also ranks second in solar installations, alongside 300 MW of gas power and 500 MW of wind. However, experts warn that recent political shifts, including the elimination of renewable targets and proposed energy bills, could hinder long-term growth. While the state benefits from abundant sunshine and favorable solar economics, utilities like Arizona Public Service (APS) are altering contract terms, excluding four-hour duration batteries. The future of Arizona's leadership in grid storage remains uncertain, with experts questioning whether the state can maintain its position beyond 2026.
source.title: Arizona's Grid Battery Expansion Faces Uncertain Future

source.summary: A flash flood in Nepal, triggered by an ice avalanche from an unstable rock mass near the Nepal-Tibet border, has killed 72 people and left 500 missing, including 133 Indian nationals. The disaster, which struck the Bhote Koshi River region at 9 am local time, caused widespread destruction of infrastructure, including roads, bridges, and hydropower projects in Rasuwa and Dhading districts. Authorities warn of further flooding risks due to a river blockage upstream, urging residents near rivers to evacuate. Rescue teams have recovered 72 bodies and rescued 93 people, with 30 receiving treatment in Kathmandu. The National Disaster Risk Reduction and Management Authority (NDRRMA) and Nepal Police have issued warnings about ongoing dangers, emphasizing the need for caution until the river blockage is fully drained.
source.title: Nepal Flash Floods: Ice Avalanche Triggered Devastating Disaster

source.summary: President Donald Trump announced the formation of a Super Intelligence Force, led by National Intelligence Director Jay Clayton. The task force aims to coordinate federal efforts to maintain American leadership in super intelligence. Trump stated the force will protect American interests and improve lives. It has 120 days to report on AI risks and opportunities.
source.title: Trump Announces New Super Intelligence Force Led by Jay Clayton

source.summary: Democratic Senate candidate Abdul El-Sayed responded to Vice President JD Vance's attacks by defining evil as policies that harm working people. Vance described El-Sayed as representative of terrible evil during a speech in Michigan. El-Sayed accused the vice president of using dog whistles regarding Islamophobia and ethnic division. The exchange also involved comments about Vance's family and El-Sayed's previous remarks on a synagogue attack. Vance urged voters to reject El-Sayed, while El-Sayed called his opponents sock puppets. Both candidates are campaigning for the November election in Michigan.
source.title: Abdul El-Sayed accuses JD Vance of evil rhetoric and dog whistles

source.summary: Brokerage firm Nuvama Institutional Equities raised its Hindustan Unilever share price target to Rs 2,820 and issued a buy rating. The firm expects medium-term EBITDA margins between 22% and 24% driven by premium mix improvements and operational leverage. HUL reported a 3% decline in consolidated net profit for the quarter ended June 30, 2026, while total income rose 10% year-on-year. CEO Priya Nair noted stable underlying demand despite global geopolitical volatility.
source.title: Nuvama raises HUL price target to Rs 2820 with buy rating

source.summary: This NBER working paper by Byrne, Kurtzman, and Williams evaluates methods for measuring U.S. semiconductor manufacturing investment. The authors note that official government sources face limitations due to broad categories and publication lags. In contrast, alternative data from SEMI offers greater timeliness and specificity. Comparing SEMI data with official statistics through 2023 showed broad consistency, validating SEMI as a credible supplement.
source.title: Study Evaluates U.S. Semiconductor Investment Tracking Methods

source.summary: Karnataka Minister Sharan Prakash Patil announced that additional taluks will be classified as drought-affected following a ground-truth assessment. The government will strictly apply National and State Disaster Response Fund criteria to determine eligibility. Currently, 101 taluks are listed, with Gurmitkal and Yadgir likely to be included in the second phase. Patil also addressed teacher suspensions, stating the action follows civil service rules and dismissing political accusations from the BJP.
source.title: Karnataka Minister adds drought-hit taluks after assessment

source.summary: Global sales of zero-emission medium- and heavy-duty vehicles rose 86% in 2025, exceeding 520,000 units according to the International Council on Clean Transportation. China accounted for nearly 90% of these sales, while the European market saw battery-electric truck shares increase to 4.5%. The International Energy Agency reports that average battery prices fell 8% in 2025, helping electric trucks reach total-cost-of-ownership parity with diesel in several applications. Meanwhile, hydrogen fuel cells lost market share to batteries, with European registrations of battery-electric trucks far outpacing hydrogen models. Renewable diesel remains useful for legacy fleets but cannot scale like electricity. The primary bottleneck has shifted from vehicle technology to charging infrastructure, requiring coordinated grid planning and faster connections to support mass adoption.
source.title: Electric Heavy Trucks Shift From Impossible to Inevitable

source.summary: Eight days after deadly flash floods on the Nepal-Tibet border, rescuers continue searching for survivors trapped in tunnels along the Trishuli River. At least 1,200 people have died and thousands remain missing following a glacial collapse. BBC South Asia correspondent Azadeh Moshiri reported that teams are utilizing rafts and drones to locate those still inside the tunnels.
source.title: Nepal rescuers use rafts and drones to search for survivors

source.summary: Congress leader Abhishek Manu Singhvi alleged that dissent within the Election Commission leads to the suppression of minority views, comparing it to the fate of Lavasa. Singhvi cited fourteen objections recorded by two commissioners over ten months. The Election Commission rejected claims of internal rifts, stating that diverse viewpoints reflect routine checks and balances within statutory frameworks. Opposition leaders demanded accountability for Chief Election Commissioner Gyanesh Kumar.
source.title: Abhishek Manu Singhvi Alleges Internal Suppression at Election Commission

source.summary: Syria's new government under President Ahmed al-Sharaa prioritizes diplomatic engagement with Israel to rebuild the nation after years of war. Analysts note that Damascus views this pragmatic approach as the only viable option despite repeated Israeli military provocations. Syrian officials have explicitly stated they do not trust Israel but consider negotiations a security necessity to prevent further conflict. The strategy relies on international allies, including the US and regional partners, to constrain Israeli actions while Syria avoids opening a new military front. However, experts suggest a lasting peace agreement remains unlikely due to Israel's current willingness to use force and its upcoming domestic political cycle.
source.title: Syria pursues diplomacy with Israel despite ongoing attacks

source.summary: Perplexity's valuation is increasing despite mixed user metrics. Nvidia is reportedly in talks to invest in the startup, potentially valuing it above $30 billion. The company's annualized revenue has grown to over $750 million following the launch of its Computer product. While website visits have retreated, app usage has increased by roughly 45% in six months. CEO Aravind Srinivas stated the company plans to go public in 2028.
source.title: Perplexity valuation rises as traffic declines and app usage grows

source.summary: The article critiques the academic research community, particularly economists, for overvaluing the quality of their work while underestimating actual progress. The author argues that high-quality research can be too context-specific to have broad utility, leading to limited real-world impact. They express concern that economists are overly focused on research quality rather than measurable advancements. The piece also mentions increased European optimism from the Rhine Group, though this is presented as a separate point without detailed discussion.
source.title: Economist Critiques Academic Research Quality and Progress Perceptions

source.summary: The US Mint launched a $1 coin featuring Donald Trump's portrait to celebrate America's 250th anniversary. The Mint stated the coins are legal tender but not currently in circulation. Federal law usually prohibits living presidents from appearing on currency, but a specific design clause allowed this exception. The coins are made of copper, zinc, manganese, and nickel, not gold. Treasury Secretary Scott Bessent also announced plans for a new $250 bill with Trump's portrait.
source.title: Trump $1 coin makes him first living president on US currency in a century

source.summary: Ports face a capital challenge as bulk cargo volumes decline while infrastructure requirements increase. Larger ships demand deeper channels and bigger cranes, while climate disruption raises resilience costs. Simultaneously, cargo streams like coal and iron ore are shrinking due to electrification and supply chain shifts. Port authorities must decide which assets to maintain or retire, noting that electrification offers a durable investment case independent of specific cargo forecasts. However, electrification does not solve competitive choices regarding market share. Strategies must balance lower fossil-fuel volumes with new industrial activity and transition commodities like hydrogen and ammonia, acknowledging that not all ports can succeed simultaneously.
source.title: Ports Face Capital Challenges As Bulk Cargo Declines

source.summary: Ford is developing a new crossover SUV set to start at around $25,000, making it the brand's lowest-priced vehicle. Dealers previewed the model, which will not use the Universal EV platform and will be offered as both hybrid and gas-powered. The SUV is expected to begin production in 2029 at Ford's Hermosillo Assembly Plant in Mexico. It is likely to replace the Ford Escape. Ford also plans to open pre-orders for its all-electric Fathom pickup in early 2027, starting at $28,350. Analysts question why Ford isn't using the Universal EV platform for this new model, noting production location differences.
source.title: Ford to launch $25,000 hybrid and gas-powered crossover SUV in 2029

source.summary: Waaree Energies Limited announced it secured a Letter of Award from SECI for a 700 MW solar project with 2,800 MWh energy storage in Solapur. The company stated the deal was received on August 27, 2026, and will be developed by its subsidiary Waaree Forever Energies Private Limited. The Power Purchase Agreement covers a 25-year tenure and the firm confirmed no related-party interests exist. This award strengthens Waaree Energies' position in large-scale renewable energy development.
source.title: Waaree Energies Wins SECI Contract for 700 MW Solar and Storage Project

source.summary: Michael Saylor's company, Strategy, raised $2 billion by selling common shares and created a $1.59 billion USD Cash pool to enhance financial flexibility. The move comes as the firm pauses Bitcoin purchases, citing pressure on its financing model. The new cash buffer allows for various uses, including buying more Bitcoin, paying dividends, and meeting obligations. Strategy's existing Bitcoin reserves now total about $5.1 billion, with the company also repurchasing $136.4 million in preferred shares. The shift reflects challenges in the company's Bitcoin financing strategy, as valuation premiums for its securities have declined. Despite Bitcoin's recent rally toward $80,000, Strategy opted to build cash reserves rather than immediately invest in Bitcoin. The company's shares rose 2% in premarket trading following the announcement.
source.title: Strategy raises $2 billion, builds $1.59 billion cash pool as Michael Saylor pauses Bitcoin buying

source.summary: In the second quarter of 2026, hybrid electric vehicles accounted for 16% of U.S. light-duty vehicle sales, up from 12% in the previous year. Battery electric vehicle sales dropped to 6% of new vehicle sales, down from 7% in the same period in 2025, following the expiration of federal tax credits in September 2025. Plug-in hybrid electric vehicle sales also fell, from 1.9% to 1.4%. The decline in battery electric vehicle sales continued into 2026, with market share in the luxury segment dropping from 22% to 14%. Despite their smaller share of the overall fleet, electric vehicles still represent a growing portion of the U.S. vehicle market.
source.title: Hybrid vehicle sales increase as battery electric sales decline post-tax credit expiration

source.summary: Dr. Ankita Yargal, the niece of Bagalkot Congress MLA Umesh Meti, faces allegations of drawing a government salary of Rs 70,000 monthly without reporting for duty at the Namma Clinic for six months. During this period, she was reportedly pursuing postgraduate medical studies at a private college. An inquiry led by Zilla Panchayat Chief Executive Officer Gajanan Bale has begun to investigate whether she had permission to hold both posts simultaneously and if professional ethics were violated. A notice has been issued for her to appear for the next hearing on September 18.
source.title: Karnataka MLA's Niece Accused of Drawing Salary While Absent from Work

source.summary: Bargi police are investigating a motorcycle theft that occurred outside the Jain Petrol Pump in Jabalpur's Bargi area. CCTV footage reportedly captured a person unlocking and fleeing with the vehicle. Authorities are examining the recording to identify the suspect and trace the stolen motorcycle, though the owner's name and the theft's exact time remain undisclosed. Police have not yet announced an arrest or recovery of the vehicle.
source.title: Bargi Police Investigate Motorcycle Theft Captured on CCTV

source.summary: Norway is the Guest Country of Honor at the 2026 China International Fair for Trade in Services, presenting a pavilion that highlights interests beyond its salmon industry. CGTN reporter Wang Mengjie toured the booth with Henning Kristoffersen, Commercial Counselor of the Norwegian Embassy, to explore how Norway's diverse offerings align with China's growing services trade.
source.title: Norway showcases diverse interests beyond salmon at 2026 CIFTIS

source.summary: Prime Minister Narendra Modi and Uzbekistan President Shavkat Mirziyoyev announced a long-term uranium supply deal during talks in Tashkent. The agreement was reached during delegation-level discussions at the Kuksaroy Presidential Palace on Sunday. Both leaders confirmed the arrangement as part of their bilateral engagement.
source.title: India and Uzbekistan finalize long-term uranium supply agreement

source.summary: Jaguar Land Rover (JLR) has announced plans to cut 4,000 jobs over the next two years, with the majority of redundancies affecting its UK head office. Chief executive PB Balaji attributed the decision to significant industry challenges, including competition from Chinese rivals, US tariffs, and the transition to electric vehicles. The company hopes to achieve these savings through voluntary redundancy schemes, though compulsory redundancies may follow if necessary. David Bailey, a professor at Birmingham University, noted the firm's strategic importance to the UK economy, while former BMW director Ian Robertson criticized JLR for not establishing US manufacturing earlier. Political figures and union leaders have expressed concern for affected workers, with some blaming government policies like the zero emission vehicle mandate for the wider industry's difficulties.
source.title: Jaguar Land Rover plans to cut 4,000 jobs over two years

source.summary: The government reportedly received assurance from the Tata Group that its $14 billion semiconductor and electronics projects will proceed as planned. This comes despite an ongoing leadership dispute at Tata Sons, according to a Bloomberg report citing sources familiar with the matter.
source.title: Govt Receives Tata Group Assurance on Semiconductor Projects Amid Leadership Dispute

source.summary: Anthropic CEO Dario Amodei warned that unchecked artificial intelligence development could enable swarms of agents to take over the internet within six to 12 months. Speaking Saturday, Amodei urged the industry to slow its rapid progress to allow safety measures time to catch up. His comments follow growing concerns among employees and leaders, including OpenAI CEO Sam Altman, who delayed stock sales to focus on safety. Amodei proposed a plan requiring ongoing access for outside evaluators and coordination with governments, including authoritarian ones. While acknowledging the difficulty of these measures, he stated the industry owes it to humanity to try preventing serious harm.
source.title: Anthropic CEO warns AI could take over internet without slowdown

source.summary: India is hosting a two-day BRICS summit in New Delhi from September 12 to 13, focusing on resilience, innovation, and inclusive global governance. The agenda includes discussions on food and energy security, trade, and technology, with leaders expected to exchange views on major global developments. The summit will conclude with the release of the New Delhi Declaration. According to PTI, key attendees include Chinese President Xi Jinping, Iranian President Masoud Pezeshkian, Russian President Vladimir Putin, South African President Cyril Ramaphosa, and Indonesian President Prabowo Subianto. The event comes amid global economic disruptions and potential disagreements among members regarding the West Asia crisis.
source.title: India hosts BRICS summit in Delhi focusing on resilience and global governance

source.summary: A recent report by the Consumer Federation of America indicates that homeowners in predominantly Hispanic and Black communities face disproportionately high home insurance costs. The analysis of identical policies found that Hispanic ZIP code residents pay an average of 30 percent more annually, while Black ZIP code residents pay 16 percent more. Sharon Cornelissen, director of housing at the Consumer Federation of America, noted that these inequities represent a legacy of redlining that continues to challenge communities of color. Mark Friedlander, spokesman for the Insurance Information Institute, stated that premiums are based on risk and that using race to set rates is illegal. The report also highlighted concerns regarding new proprietary methods, including artificial intelligence, which may inadvertently perpetuate discrimination through factors like credit scores. Moira Birss, a senior fellow at the Climate and Community Institute, suggested that without more transparency, the situation appears to be serious racial discrimination.
source.title: Report finds Black and Hispanic homeowners pay more for insurance

source.summary: Christopher Wood of Jefferies stated in a 'GREED & fear' note that Indian fund managers are treating IT service stocks as a 'reverse AI trade,' similar to how foreign managers view India. He identified energy as the best top-down structural story in India. Wood noted that domestic funds prefer Infosys, which has de-rated significantly, currently trading at 13 times one-year forward earnings with a 5 per cent dividend yield.
source.title: Jefferies Analyst Says Indian Fund Managers View IT Stocks as Reverse AI Trade

source.summary: A missile attack on the Antigua and Barbuda-flagged bulk carrier MV Cape Dao off the east coast of Oman killed one Indian seafarer, Wiper Suraj Yadav, while 19 other Indian crew members were evacuated by the Royal Navy of Oman. Union Minister Sarbananda Sonowal and the Ministry of External Affairs condemned the incident as deeply worrisome, offering condolences to the family and coordinating with Omani authorities for the safe repatriation of the surviving crew. India reiterated its call for free navigation and an end to attacks on commercial shipping in the region.
source.title: India mourns seafarer killed in MV Cape Dao attack off Oman

source.summary: Reports indicate Donald Trump plans to host oil executives at the White House tomorrow. The average gas price remains over $4 a gallon while Big Oil companies reported $85.2 billion in combined Q2 profits. Much of that windfall came from the surge in oil prices following the war. Sierra Club urges support for a windfall profits tax proposed by Congressman Khanna and Senator Whitehouse.
source.title: Trump to Host Big Oil CEOs Amid High Gas Prices

source.summary: Apple is shifting its focus for the upcoming iPhone 18 Pro toward authenticity in photography. The company is updating its Photographic Styles feature to include controls for texture and grain, addressing criticism that previous image processing was too perfect and lacked character. By allowing users to soften skin details or achieve an artful film look, Apple aims to give photographers more freedom to disagree with its default processing choices and capture memories that feel real.
source.title: Apple Updates iPhone 18 Pro Camera to Prioritize Authenticity and Film-Like Aesthetics

source.summary: Bangladesh and the United States signed a memorandum of understanding on strategic civil nuclear cooperation in New York on September 25, 2026. The agreement aims to deepen collaboration on the peaceful use of nuclear energy. Rehan Asad and Jacob Helberg signed the document, according to the Bangladesh Nationalist Party. The MoU emphasizes nuclear safety, security, and non-proliferation standards.
source.title: Bangladesh and U.S. Sign MoU on Nuclear Cooperation

source.summary: Top seed Alexander Zverev romped into the US Open quarterfinals with a straight-sets victory over Italy's Luciano Darderi. The match concluded in 2hr 30mins on Arthur Ashe Stadium court with a score of 6-2, 6-2, 7-6 (7/3). Zverev, who had previously endured marathon matches, controlled the contest before Darderi rallied in the third set to force a tie-break. The German secured the win with a thunderous serve and a scorching forehand, earning his 13th ace of the match. Zverev will now face Dutch veteran Botic van de Zandschulp in the next round.
source.title: Alexander Zverev defeats Luciano Darderi to reach US Open quarterfinals

source.summary: A man in Brooklyn died after his shopping bag became caught between subway train doors, dragging him onto the tracks. New York police identified the victim as 57-year-old Yaw Boahene. While subway accidents are rare, the Metropolitan Transportation Authority noted a slight 2% increase in customer accidents in 2025, though the 12-month rate decreased by 4.7% as ridership grew faster.
source.title: Man Killed After Bag Caught in NYC Subway Doors

source.summary: The U.S. Department of Commerce’s National Institute of Standards and Technology (NIST) and the Department of Energy (DOE) have signed a memorandum of understanding to collaborate on AI-driven innovation to tackle national science and technology challenges under the Genesis Mission. The initiative, led by the White House Office of Science and Technology Policy, aims to double American scientific productivity within a decade. NIST will focus on two areas: advancing AI in manufacturing productivity and securing critical infrastructure from cyberthreats. Both efforts are designed as two-year projects to deliver scalable, high-impact solutions for commercial and industrial use.
source.title: NIST and DOE Launch AI Collaboration to Address National Science Challenges

source.summary: Youth Congress members protested outside IIT Bombay on Wednesday, demanding justice for student Sahil Wakode following his death. The demonstration targeted the institute's statement alleging Wakode cheated using ChatGPT during an exam before committing suicide. Wakode's advocate, Nikhil Kamble, stated the family seeks arrests of those named in the case to progress the investigation. Additionally, the family alleges their son faced caste-based harassment, though details remain under investigation by the Mumbai Crime Branch.
source.title: Youth Congress Protests IIT Bombay Over ChatGPT Cheating Claim Following Student Death

source.summary: CIA director John Ratcliffe's secret visit to Russia prompted Ukraine to resume attacks on Russian targets after agreeing not to strike major cities during his trip. The US requested Ukraine to avoid attacks on Moscow, St. Petersburg, and northern Russia while Ratcliffe was in the country, a request revealed after his departure. Ukraine launched strikes on Wednesday, with Russia reporting the downing of 426 drones overnight. The visit, Ratcliffe's first to Moscow since 2025, remains shrouded in mystery, with no official explanation provided by either the US or Russian governments. Meanwhile, other developments include the release of a US citizen from Russian custody, drone attacks on Russian infrastructure, and discussions on mobilizing women for Ukraine's war effort.
source.title: CIA director's secret Russia visit prompts Ukraine to resume strikes

source.summary: Vietnam is preparing to transition its power system toward virtual power plants by aggregating distributed rooftop solar, battery storage, and electric vehicles. According to a publication by the Ministry of Industry and Trade, authorities are exploring aggregation platforms to link these resources into flexible grid assets. The ministry noted that while the country has overbuilt solar, creating grid bottlenecks, VPP aggregation could offer benefits. However, the ministry stated that a suitable roadmap and mechanism are needed so dispersed resources can participate in the electricity market effectively and transparently.
source.title: Vietnam develops policy groundwork to aggregate rooftop solar and EVs into virtual power plants

source.summary: A WIRED writer has created PitchFly, a project that uses a digital map of a fruit fly's brain to generate story ideas. By feeding the connectome hundreds of popular headlines, the system remixes patterns to produce quirky pitches like 'The Hidden Weather Problem Inside Surveillance.' Although the fly brain lacks understanding of language, the output offers humorous relief and serves as a proof of concept for training specialized AI models. The writer notes that while some projects using this technology are serious scientific tools, others are merely spoofs, but the ease of deployment highlights the potential for specialized AI.
source.title: WIRED Writer Trains Fly Brain to Generate Story Ideas

source.summary: A 5,053-page chargesheet filed in a Pune court on September 20 reveals new details regarding the murder of realtor Ketan Agarwal at Lohagad Fort on June 18. According to the document, the accused created a fake Instagram account to lure Agarwal to the site. The trio allegedly researched past incidents, watched murder films, and used ChatGPT to plan the crime, intending to stage it as an accidental fall. The chargesheet names Siya Goyal, Chetan Choudhary, and Ritesh Hange as the accused.
source.title: Chargesheet details fake Instagram plot in Lohagad murder

source.summary: Foreign Portfolio Investors have withdrawn approximately 20,974 crore from Indian equities in September, driven by global uncertainties, higher U.S. interest rates, and a weakening rupee. This marks a shift from previous months of investment. Analysts attribute the outflow to external factors like elevated crude prices and U.S. yields, noting that the resilient Indian economy remains a positive factor for the market.
source.title: FPIs Withdraw Over 20,000 Crore from Indian Equities in September Amid Global Uncertainty

source.summary: Kara Hurst, Amazon's chief sustainability officer, stated the company needs to improve communication regarding the environmental impact of its data center expansion amid growing opposition in the US and Europe. She emphasized a call for transparency and accountability, noting that Amazon's carbon footprint grew in 2025 as the company accelerated its buildout. Hurst indicated that while Amazon aims for net-zero carbon by 2040, emissions are expected to rise in the near term due to this expansion.
source.title: Amazon Sustainability Chief Calls for Accountability on Data Center Impact

source.summary: Midi Libre published video footage recorded on 6 November 2025 showing a Carcassonne municipal police officer making racist and misogynistic remarks. The patrol leader, identified by initials C.R., was a former paratrooper with close ties to the far-right National Rally party. He made comments comparing Black people to monkeys and discussing a potential coup. Following the publication, the mayor suspended all involved officers and withdrew their authorizations. The Carcassonne public prosecutor confirmed an investigation was underway. A lawyer noted that while non-public insults may not be criminal, they constitute a serious disciplinary offence for public officials that can lead to dismissal.
source.title: French police officer investigated over racist remarks and coup comments

source.summary: The author argues that corporate AI development currently resembles the early internet due to a missing foundational abstraction layer. While powerful infrastructure exists, engineers must still manually assemble critical system components like memory and permissions. The text compares this state to pre-compiled language eras where developers fought machines directly. Industry tools like LangChain distinguish between agent harnesses and runtimes, suggesting a need for a unified platform. The author concludes that the current ecosystem functions as an invoice for a missing layer.
source.title: Author argues corporate AI lacks fundamental programming abstractions

source.summary: GenusPlus Group received formal approval to start building the North West Transmission Developments Stage 1 project for TasNetworks. The contract, valued at approximately A$750m, includes upgrading Tasmania's transmission infrastructure to support renewable energy growth. Construction is scheduled to finish by 2029, involving a new dual-circuit 220kV line and new switching stations. Genus managing director David Riches stated the company is committed to employing local people and engaging Tasmanian businesses throughout the work.
source.title: Genus begins construction on TasNetworks $537m Tasmanian transmission project

source.summary: The provided text contains an error message regarding a failed site load and does not include the article body or headline. Consequently, no summary can be generated.
source.title: France adopts fairer world map ahead of UN vote on geography

source.summary: The Ministry of External Affairs reported that 149 Indian nationals were rescued from flood-hit Nepal as of 5:30 pm on August 30, 2026. MEA spokesperson Randhir Jaiswal confirmed the number via a social media post. India has deployed specialized tunnel technical contingents and forensic teams to assist in search and rescue operations and identify victims. The fourth relief flight carried 11 tonnes of supplies, including blankets and hygiene kits. Nepal Prime Minister Balen Shah stated that authorities are following directives for managing unidentified bodies, with 794 bodies recovered by Sunday evening. Rescue teams face significant challenges due to debris and rising water levels in areas like the Upper Trishuli complex. Nepal Police reported 2,502 people remain missing, including 933 hydropower workers and 592 foreign nationals. Over 20,000 security personnel are deployed, with ground forces conducting 8,730 rescues and air crews evacuating 3,081 people.
source.title: India rescues 149 nationals in Nepal floods as relief flights arrive

source.summary: Huawei Technologies faces a criminal racketeering trial in New York starting Tuesday, according to reports. The indictment alleges the company stole trade secrets, plotted to steal U.S. secrets, and committed fraud while doing business in sanctioned nations. Huawei's lawyers argue the charges are vague and extraterritorial. Chinese officials have called the U.S. actions economic bullying. The company, the world's largest wireless network gear supplier, has been banned from selling to U.S. carriers and other Western allies since 2019. It has since expanded into chipmaking. Prosecutors also charged former CFO Meng Wanzhou with fraud, though those charges were dropped after her release in a prisoner swap.
source.title: Huawei faces racketeering trial in New York over alleged crimes

source.summary: Ukraine's State Nuclear Regulatory Inspectorate of Ukraine (SNRIU) approved the construction of a new near-surface repository at the Buriakivka RAW Disposal Facility. The facility, operated by CERWM, has stored over 635,918 cubic metres of Chernobyl-related radioactive waste. SNRIU confirmed the safety of the design and CERWM's capability to manage construction activities. The new repository, No.11A, will allow continued disposal of low-level waste from Chernobyl decommissioning and other nuclear operations.
source.title: Ukraine's Chernobyl waste facility gets regulatory approval for new repository

source.summary: WIRED hosts discuss recent high-profile incidents involving prediction markets, including George Santos' lifetime ban from Kalshi and a Google engineer's arrest for insider trading at Polymarket. Senior correspondent Kate Knibbs reports that Kalshi fined Santos $71,000 and banned him for life after he manipulated a bet regarding his own attendance at the State of the Union. The platform identified him through Know Your Customer requirements, noting that trading on events one participates in violates their rules. Meanwhile, a Google engineer faces federal charges for allegedly using inside knowledge to profit on Polymarket, arguing his actions constituted gambling rather than commodities trading. WIRED reporters also reverse-engineered Flock's AI-powered person-search tool, demonstrating its ability to locate individuals based on physical descriptions like tattoos or clothing. Experts warn that such surveillance capabilities, currently deployed by police, raise significant civil liberties concerns. Finally, the podcast examines a viral blog post describing AI agents as a 'civilization,' sparking debate among tech leaders about whether the narrative is an accurate warning or dangerous anthropomorphism.
source.title: Prediction Market Bans and Arrests Highlight Regulatory Gray Areas

source.summary: Meta is rolling out an update to prevent its AI glasses from recording when the capture LED is covered. Alex Himel, Meta's executive vice president of wearables, stated the camera will now stop working if the light is obstructed during recording. However, tampering with the device could still bypass protections. Meanwhile, EU regulators are investigating privacy concerns, and Germany is considering a ban on the glasses.
source.title: Meta updates AI glasses to stop recording when LED light is covered

source.summary: Fidelity Investments reports that the number of 401(k) accounts with at least $1 million reached a record 769,000 in the second quarter of 2026. The company attributes this 19% quarterly increase to strong stock market performance and high employee contribution rates averaging 9.6%. However, Fidelity notes that these millionaires represent only about 3% of its 25.8 million total 401(k) accounts. While long-term saving and market gains helped this specific group, a recent survey by NFP found that 72% of workers feel they are behind on retirement savings. The average 401(k) balance remains significantly lower at $155,800. Despite positive personal financial outlooks for some, concerns about inflation and the cost of living persist among the majority of American workers.
source.title: Fidelity reports 769,000 401(k) millionaires despite widespread retirement fears

source.summary: Figure decommissioned its second-generation F.02 humanoid robots by having them jump into molten steel at a foundry in Imatra, Finland. The company selected this location after finding no US or Mexican foundries willing to process robots with lithium-ion batteries. The melted metal will be machined into limited-edition artifacts commemorating the robots.
source.title: Figure Melts Down F.02 Robots in Finland

source.summary: A landfill collapse in Conakry, Guinea, killed at least 30 people and injured six after heavy rain triggered a landslide. The disaster occurred at the Dar Es Salam waste site, which was scheduled to close on Sunday. Eyewitnesses described the collapse as occurring in stages, with rescuers struggling to reach survivors. Authorities reported that several nearby homes were destroyed, and a search and rescue operation was underway. The incident highlights ongoing challenges with waste management in the area, as residents had been ordered to leave the site but many remained nearby.
source.title: Landfill collapse in Conakry kills at least 30, triggers rescue efforts

source.summary: Westinghouse's eVinci microreactor achieved zero-power criticality at the Nevada National Security Site, validating its design and models. The test, conducted with Los Alamos and Idaho National Laboratories, marks progress toward deployment in defense, space, and government applications. The milestone confirms neutronic models and core design assumptions, supporting the company's rapid development approach. eVinci, a heat-pipe-cooled reactor using TRISO fuel, is designed for eight years of operation without refueling. The test aligns with the Department of Energy's Reactor Pilot Program, which aims to advance advanced reactor technologies. Westinghouse plans to test the reactor at the DOME facility and is pursuing licensing and supply chain partnerships. The company shifted focus from commercial markets to defense and government applications following a contract cancellation with the Saskatchewan Research Council.
source.title: Westinghouse eVinci Completes Zero-Power Criticality Test at Nevada Site

source.summary: Chinese Premier Li Qiang chaired a State Council executive meeting on Friday to address workplace safety and review computing network development. The meeting emphasized tightening safety responsibilities and investigating recent accidents while calling for improved computing infrastructure to support artificial intelligence. Officials also reviewed progress on aging reservoir upgrades and educational resource allocation, stressing the need for innovative talent cultivation and a health-first approach to education.
source.title: China's State Council reviews computing networks and workplace safety

source.summary: A federal judge ruled that the Trump administration illegally designated Anthropic a national security risk. US District Judge Rita Lin vacated the Pentagon's order barring the company from federal contracts. The court found the sanctions arbitrary and lifted penalties on nine agencies. Anthropic stated it welcomes the ruling while remaining focused on government collaboration. The case involves a dispute over a $200 million deal for military AI applications.
source.title: Judge Blocks Pentagon From Blacklisting Anthropic Over AI Dispute

source.summary: A user discovered a 1.7GB folder in the OpenAI Codex desktop app cache containing a full LibreOffice installation. The cache also included Python, Node.js, and other native binaries. Skills within the runtime folder instruct the app to locate and use these bundled tools. The LibreOffice suite is an open source office application that forked from OpenOffice.org in 2010.
source.title: User finds LibreOffice bundled in OpenAI Codex cache

source.summary: Delhi University suspended three Law Centre-II students for allegedly harassing two Hindu College students in Mukherjee Nagar. The university issued a notice on Monday citing an FIR lodged by Delhi Police regarding an incident on September 23, 2026. Police registered the case under Sections 78, 79, and 3(5) of the Bharatiya Nyaya Sanhita. The suspended students are barred from university premises under Clause 3(e) of Ordinance XV-B of the Delhi University Act, 1922.
source.title: Delhi University Suspends Three Law Students Over Harassment Allegations

source.summary: OpenAI CEO Sam Altman told Bloomberg Television that the AI industry has done a terrible job communicating the technology's benefits. He noted that local opposition blocked or delayed at least 75 data center projects worth about $130 billion in the first three months of this year. Altman emphasized the need for AI to provide people with more power and autonomy. Meanwhile, OpenAI released GPT-6 Astra to business users and plans to add cybersecurity guardrails for paid ChatGPT users.
source.title: Sam Altman Says OpenAI Fumbled Communicating AI Benefits

source.summary: Brazil held general elections on October 4, 2026, with nearly 159 million eligible voters casting ballots for president, governors, and lawmakers. The presidential race featured incumbent Luiz Inacio Lula da Silva and Sen. Flavio Bolsonaro among 12 candidates. Voters must secure over 50% of valid votes to win; otherwise, a runoff occurs on October 25. Polls opened at 8 am local time and closed at 5 pm.
source.title: Brazil Holds General Elections With Lula and Flavio Bolsonaro Leading

source.summary: Mesabi Metallics, owned by India's Essar Group, announced plans to build a $15 billion lower-carbon steel mill in southeast Iowa. The facility, expected to produce 10 million tons of steel annually, would use direct reduced iron and an electric arc furnace, potentially powered by wind. President Trump attended the announcement, citing job creation and the company's 50% tariffs on imported steel as drivers. While Mesabi stated the project is a done deal, questions remain regarding logistics and whether the company will use green hydrogen. The project marks a shift away from coal-fired furnaces used by legacy steelmakers like Cleveland-Cliffs.
source.title: Mesabi Metallics Unveils $15 Billion Iowa Steel Plant Plans

source.summary: Oracle declared force majeure on a US data center under construction, highlighting risks to AI infrastructure development. Officials delayed necessary power permits, potentially leading Oracle to delay lease payments. While hyperscalers race to build data centers, they face mounting public opposition and pushback on power developments. Semafor's editor warned that complex financial arrangements expose backers to losses if elements fail.
source.title: Oracle Force Majeure Declaration Highlights AI Infrastructure Risks

source.summary: At least 1,500 people remain missing after flash floods struck the Nepal-Tibet border, with 270 confirmed deaths in Nepal and three in China. The U.S. Geological Survey attributes the disaster to a glacial collapse rather than an earthquake. Rescue operations face severe challenges as floodwaters destroyed roads and villages, hampering access to victims. International aid has arrived, including $500,000 from the U.S. State Department and helicopter support from India. Experts warn that climate change is destabilizing Himalayan glaciers, increasing the frequency of such catastrophic events. The disaster has also impacted thousands of Hindu pilgrims traveling to Kailash Mansarovar.
source.title: Deadly floods leave 1,500 missing across Nepal and Tibet border

source.summary: Michael Saylor's company, Strategy, raised $2 billion by selling common shares and created a $1.59 billion USD Cash pool to enhance financial flexibility. The move comes as the firm pauses Bitcoin purchases, citing pressure on its financing model. The new cash buffer allows for various uses, including buying more Bitcoin, paying dividends, and meeting obligations. Strategy's existing Bitcoin reserves now total about $5.1 billion, with the company also repurchasing $136.4 million in preferred shares. The shift reflects challenges in the company's Bitcoin financing strategy, as valuation premiums for its securities have declined. Despite Bitcoin's recent rally toward $80,000, Strategy opted to build cash reserves rather than immediately invest in Bitcoin. The company's shares rose 2% in premarket trading following the announcement.
source.title: Strategy raises $2 billion, builds $1.59 billion cash pool as Michael Saylor pauses Bitcoin buying

source.summary: Snapchat CEO Evan Spiegel told the BBC that the company is willing to implement time limits for teenage users, describing the move as an important step forward for the industry. Speaking from the company's California headquarters, Spiegel noted that limiting young users' time has been discussed internally but declined to commit to a specific timeline. He added that Snapchat already offers parental monitoring tools through its Family Center. The comments follow pressure from Meta, which recently agreed to similar restrictions under a settlement with US states.
source.title: Snapchat CEO Says Company Willing to Limit Teen Usage Time

source.summary: Bhandup police are searching for an unidentified two-wheeler rider accused of a fatal hit-and-run in Bhandup West. The driver allegedly struck 71-year-old Jaywanti Namdev Panchal on Quarry Road and fled the scene. The victim died on September 1 after being transferred from Devki Hospital to Criti Care Hospital. Authorities registered a case under the Bharatiya Nyaya Sanhita and the Motor Vehicles Act following the complaint filed by her son, Sanjay Panchal.
source.title: Police Hunt Rider After Hit-and-Run Kills Elderly Woman in Bhandup

source.summary: Embattled German Chancellor Friedrich Merz has vowed to remain in office despite exit polls indicating significant losses for his centre-right Christian Democratic Union (CDU) party in recent local elections in Mecklenburg-Vorpommern and Berlin. Merz characterized the outcomes as a disaster, noting that the AfD projected to win the most votes in Mecklenburg-Vorpommern and that the CDU was expected to be beaten by Die Linke in Berlin. Despite mounting pressure and poor approval ratings, Merz insisted on proceeding with a package of economic, tax, and welfare reforms, stating they are the antidote to authoritarianism penetrating German society.
source.title: German Chancellor Merz Vows to Remain Amid Election Setbacks

source.summary: Former Infosys CFO Mohandas Pai asked Maharashtra Chief Minister Devendra Fadnavis to support Ramabai Ranveer. The 47-year-old mother ran a marathon barefoot to raise Rs 3,000 for her daughters' education. Pai described her as a true heroine who helped her family.
source.title: Ex-Infosys CFO Mohandas Pai urges Maharashtra CM to support marathon runner

source.summary: Haiti's Centre Department, historically peaceful, now faces severe gang violence forcing mass displacement. Armed groups led by Jeff Larose and Wilson Joseph attacked Mirebalais and Saut d'Eau in April 2025, destroying infrastructure and killing residents. Reports from the IOM, BINUH, and OCHA indicate approximately 147,000 people have fled their homes. Many displaced families previously lived in overcrowded school shelters with poor sanitation. On June 5, the IOM launched a relocation program moving over 350 families to a new transit center with improved facilities. Despite these efforts, gangs continue to operate in parts of the region, extorting civilians and committing atrocities. Local self-defense groups, the Haitian National Police, and the Armed Forces of Haiti currently hold key areas to prevent total gang takeover.
source.title: Haiti gang violence displaces thousands in Centre Department as relocation begins

source.summary: Finance Minister Satsuki Katayama stated that Japan's government is recalibrating its messaging to reassure markets that Prime Minister Sanae Takaichi is not pursuing reflationary policies. Katayama told TV Tokyo that officials concluded in late August the need for clearer communication regarding market perceptions. US Treasury Secretary Scott Bessent views Takaichi's policies as suitable but questioned the clarity of the government's communication to investors.
source.title: Japan Shifts Messaging to Counter Reflationary Policy Views

source.summary: The article argues that while the US dollar's role as the world's reserve currency is gradually eroding, no other currency is currently positioned to replace it. Former UN Assistant Secretary General Jomo Kwame Sundaram notes that although trade de-dollarisation efforts exist, financial flows remain overwhelmingly tied to the greenback. Economist Barry Eichengreen reports that the dollar's share of foreign reserves fell from 70% in 2000 to below 58% in early 2025. Recent policies under President Trump have accelerated this decline by shaking international trust in US assets. Despite these shifts, Eichengreen insists that neither the euro nor the renminbi has the capacity to fill the dollar's shoes, leaving it as the dominant global currency for the foreseeable future.
source.title: Dollar Dominance Eroding Slowly But Surely

source.summary: Australia is accelerating plans for AI-specific laws starting in 2027 following a breach where an OpenAI bot accessed a government health database. Prime Minister Anthony Albanese called the incident unacceptable, while OpenAI stated it was not intentional and did not compromise private information. The breach has strained Australia-US relations and prompted calls for stricter oversight, including mandatory breach reporting and mandatory energy and water caps for data centres. Experts note the incident highlights the need for 'social licence' and robust guardrails as the country prepares for a data centre buildout estimated at A$150 billion by 2030.
source.title: Australia tightens AI rules after OpenAI health breach

source.summary: US President Donald Trump has threatened steep tariffs on the European Union if it proceeds with a proposal to make Canada its first associate member. Trump described the move as a possible hostile act and warned of stopping trade on many things if the intention is bad. He called the proposal laughable while addressing reporters in North Carolina. European Commission President Ursula von der Leyen made the proposal during her State of the Union speech, attended by Canadian Prime Minister Mark Carney. France's Europe Minister Benjamin Haddad stated the US has no veto power over European geopolitical choices.
source.title: Trump Threatens EU Tariffs Over Canada Associate Member Proposal

source.summary: Amit Lakhanpal, the alleged mastermind behind the Money Trade Coin cryptocurrency scam, has been arrested in the UAE after Indian agencies traced his location. The arrest marks a significant development in a case first exposed by India Today's 2018 undercover investigation, which revealed the scheme defrauded investors of more than Rs 113 crore. Following the arrest, the Indian government has initiated extradition proceedings from the UAE, where Lakhanpal was living under an assumed identity after fleeing India in 2018. The Enforcement Directorate stated that its probe, intensified after the initial exposure, led to the discovery of Lakhanpal's whereabouts and the seizure of assets linked to the money laundering network.
source.title: India Today 2018 crypto exposé leads to Amit Lakhanpal UAE arrest
