source.summary: Police say three masked men burglarized the Delhi home of Congress leader Alka Lamba's 88-year-old father early Sunday. The thieves reportedly fled with cash and jewellery after entering the property in daylight. Lamba shared CCTV footage showing the suspects leaving the gate ajar on a single bike. She questioned public safety in Delhi and stated the first lead has been handed to authorities.
source.title: Three masked men burglarize Alka Lamba's father's Delhi home

source.summary: Gurvinder Singh, a Sikh truck driver, was stabbed 17 times in Pennsylvania by a white supremacist on September 13. Authorities have not determined a motive, but Jasjit Singh of the Jakata Movement links the attack to a Department of Homeland Security social media post posted on September 9. The post featured an image of a man in a turban with the caption 'Get off our roads, you don't know how to drive, Mr. Singh.' While DHS stated the post referred to a specific individual, Jasjit Singh argues it targeted all Sikh men. The Sikh community also faces economic harm from immigration policies that have revoked thousands of truck driver licenses, with industry sources estimating the number has reached 30,000. A recent study found slurs targeting South Asians rose by 109% between January 2023 and December 2025.
source.title: Sikh Community Faces Racism and Immigration Policies Under Trump

source.summary: BJP leaders Sarbari Mukherjee and Rahul Sinha demanded Jadavpur University be renamed after Sri Aurobindo during a campus convention. They alleged anti-India elements and Naxalism were active on campus following recent student clashes. Mukherjee stated a mass petition could be submitted to the state governor to change the institution's name. Sinha promised to ensure 'Vande Mataram' is sung and accused Maoist leaders of involvement in ragging. The party claims no opposition remains in West Bengal after recent Assembly elections.
source.title: BJP leaders demand renaming Jadavpur University after Sri Aurobindo

source.summary: In the final round of NRLW action, Parramatta Eels defeated North Queensland Cowboys 33-28 in a comeback victory, while Cronulla Sharks beat Sydney Dragons 16-8 to award the Dragons the wooden spoon. Both matches featured the experimental rule allowing conceding teams to choose kickoff or receive. The Eels overcame a 16-point deficit with five second-half tries, while Sharks secured their first back-to-back wins of 2026.
source.title: Sharks defeat Dragons while Eels beat Cowboys in NRLW final round

source.summary: The Delhi government directed bus operators to remove window curtains and ensure panic buttons and tracking devices function properly. These orders followed the arrest of a driver and conductor accused of raping a 17-year-old girl on a sleeper bus. Authorities also prohibited stopping at unauthorized locations and required drivers to wear uniforms. Operators must now report harassment incidents to police immediately.
source.title: Delhi orders bus operators to remove curtains and fix panic buttons after rape

source.summary: Uttar Pradesh Chief Minister Yogi Adityanath directed hospitals to remain on alert for swine flu. Officials must ensure isolation wards are ready and stock medicines. Delhi reported over 2,600 H1N1 cases recently. Health authorities are reviewing hospital preparedness in both states.
source.title: UP CM orders hospitals to prepare for swine flu surge

source.summary: Tata Motors secured European Central Bank approval for its proposed acquisition of Iveco Group, valued at approximately 40,000 crore rupees. The company confirmed that all prior sector regulatory authorizations have been obtained, keeping the deal on schedule for an August completion. While British and Spanish regulators have already cleared the transaction, Italy's Consob remains the final regulatory hurdle before the offer document is published. Once approved, the deal will expand Tata's commercial vehicle footprint significantly across European and other developed markets.
source.title: Tata Motors receives ECB approval for 40,000 crore Iveco takeover

source.summary: Treasury Secretary Scott Bessent announced US support for the Financial Literacy Solutions Sprint at a G20 ministers meeting. The contest will select winners from innovative technology solutions developed within G20 member states to improve financial understanding. Bessent also highlighted the Trump Accounts initiative, which deposits $1,000 into investment accounts for infants born during Trump's second term. Critics argue that financial struggles stem from a lack of disposable income rather than ignorance, citing recent survey data showing widespread dissatisfaction with economic conditions.
source.title: Scott Bessent promotes financial literacy contest and Trump-era investment plan at G20

source.summary: Dozens of masked protesters blocked the A20 road at the Port of Dover on Saturday morning, causing significant traffic disruption. Kent police attended the scene while the Port of Dover classified the event as a public order incident. No arrests were made, and the demonstration was claimed by the anti-immigration group Patriot Platform. The government condemned the behaviour, citing delays of up to 30 minutes and four miles of congestion. By lunchtime, the blockade had dispersed and access roads returned to normal flow. Ferry operators pledged to accommodate delayed passengers on subsequent sailings. Local politicians and community groups expressed frustration over the disruption and safety concerns for workers.
source.title: Anti-immigration protesters block Dover port road causing travel delays

source.summary: A 360 ONE Capital report projects India's semiconductor demand rising from $56 billion in 2025 to over $117 billion by 2030. While localisation and packaging are expected, near-term earnings lie in ecosystem enablers like utilities and equipment. The report warns that execution and competitive yields matter more than announcements as capacity builds ahead of proven demand.
source.title: India's semiconductor ecosystem faces gradual value creation over next 3-5 years

source.summary: The Pakistani government is holding talks with the Imran Khan party to defuse tensions following the announcement of a long march to Islamabad. Negotiations are being facilitated by National Assembly Speaker Sardar Ayaz Sadiq. A government delegation led by Rana Sanaullah is meeting with PPP representatives. Key demands include an immediate meeting with Khan and his release from custody. The government has stepped up security measures, placing shipping containers on roads leading to Islamabad.
source.title: Pakistani Government Talks with Imran Khan Party to Defuse Tensions

source.summary: Air Chief Marshal A.P. Singh stated that India may finalize the multi-role fighter aircraft deal by the current financial year if plans proceed as scheduled. He noted that price negotiations are ongoing. Singh also mentioned that Russia offered Su-57 jets, though no decision has been made. The IAF requires 36 to 40 aircraft annually.
source.title: IAF Chief Says India May Finalize MRFA Deal This Year

source.summary: Wall Street ended lower on September 23, with the S&P 500 declining 0. 75 percent to 7,706. 05 points. The market was pulled down by rising oil prices, which increased nearly 4 percent following a speech by Iranian President Masoud Pezeshkian, and surging Treasury yields. Yields on two-year Treasuries reached their highest level since 2024, while 10-year yields hit their peak since 2007. Major tech stocks like Alphabet and Amazon fell, while utilities and communication services led sector declines.
source.title: Wall Street Ends Lower Amid Rising Oil Prices and Treasury Yields

source.summary: G20 trade ministers held a two-day meeting in Milwaukee, Wisconsin, to discuss global trade issues including food weaponization and forced labor. Officials engaged in direct discussions and bilateral meetings ahead of the G20 Leaders' summit scheduled for December 2026 in Miami, Florida. The discussions covered a variety of topics relevant to international trade relations.
source.title: G20 Trade Ministers Discuss Food Weaponization and Forced Labor in Wisconsin

source.summary: BRICS leaders convened in New Delhi on Saturday for a summit focused on trade, investment, and global conflicts. The gathering, hosted by Indian Prime Minister Narendra Modi, included Russian President Vladimir Putin, Chinese President Xi Jinping, and counterparts from other member nations. Discussions centered on economic cooperation, energy security, and reducing reliance on the US dollar. However, the bloc's unity faces tests from ongoing wars in Ukraine and the Middle East, as well as rising US-China tensions. Iranian President Masoud Pezeshkian emphasized expanding trade in national currencies, while China seeks to deepen its influence within the group. India aims to balance its strategic ties with Russia and Iran while improving relations with Western nations and potentially easing tensions with China.
source.title: BRICS leaders meet in India to discuss trade and global conflicts

source.summary: Iran's economy is deteriorating as the US launches a new sanctions campaign called Operation Economic Outcast. The country suffers from runaway inflation, with vegetable oil prices rising 383% and egg prices up 294% in August. Fuel shortages have caused long queues at petrol stations, while officials admit fuel smuggling involves political factions. Iranian leaders are framing the crisis as a war against America, urging citizens to reduce consumption. However, experts argue the root cause is the inability to export oil due to the US blockade. The government plans to restrict poverty statistics, further limiting transparency on living standards.
source.title: Iran faces deepening economic crisis amid new US sanctions

source.summary: West Bengal Chief Minister Suvendu Adhikari announced plans to introduce stringent laws targeting what he described as 'love jihad' and 'land jihad.' He stated his government would also implement a Uniform Civil Code in the state. Adhikari confirmed these legislative measures would be enacted within six months. The announcement was made in New Delhi on Sunday.
source.title: West Bengal CM Promises New Laws Against Love Jihad and UCC

source.summary: Vaamanaa reports that Indian investors are focusing on several companies following post-market business updates. Rail Vikas Nigam secured a ₹903 crore order for a thermal power project. Tata Motors launched an open offer to acquire Iveco Group shares at €14.1 per share. Mazagon Dock received a ₹118 crore purchase order for an AI-based security project. Other updates include JSW Steel's production rise and Lupin's FDA approval for Modafinil tablets.
source.title: Indian stocks focus on RVNL, Mazagon Dock, Tata Motors updates

source.summary: Zee founder Subhash Chandra used an 18-minute Instagram interaction to defend his personal insolvency resolution plan rather than addressing recent allegations against Mukesh Ambani. Chandra stated that borrowers linked to the Essel Group agreed to repay outstanding dues totaling approximately ₹990 crore. He clarified that his personal bankruptcy stems from acting as a guarantor for about 18 to 20 entities, a move he admitted was his "biggest mistake." The National Company Law Tribunal has not yet passed a final order on his repayment plan, which proposes paying ₹6.25 crore against admitted claims of roughly ₹22,006 crore. Creditors are challenging the approval process, alleging that family-linked entities improperly influenced the outcome. Several lenders plan to challenge the NCLT order before the National Company Law Appellate Tribunal.
source.title: Subhash Chandra shifts focus from Mukesh Ambani to debt repayment plan

source.summary: Environmental and community groups have urged the U.S. Environmental Protection Agency to retain public participation requirements for air pollution permits. Nearly 200 organizations filed comments opposing the EPA's proposal to eliminate minimum public notice and comment periods for state-issued Clean Air Act minor new source review permits. These permits typically apply to industrial facilities like data centers and power plants. The current regulations require a 30-day public comment period, but the proposed change would leave decisions to state and local agencies. Advocates argue that public input has historically led to stronger pollution controls and monitoring. They criticized the Trump administration for weakening environmental protections and allowing industrial projects to proceed without community involvement, emphasizing the health risks to affected populations.
source.title: Environmental Groups Push EPA to Maintain Public Input for Air Permitting

source.summary: The World Humanoid Robot Games in Beijing showcased advanced robotic capabilities, with some robots outperforming Usain Bolt in speed and demonstrating impressive dexterity. Over 600 teams from 15 countries participated, featuring over 2,000 robots. The Tiangong Ultra robot ran the 100-meter dash in 8.86 seconds, while the Lightning robot achieved 9.47 seconds. These feats highlight China's progress in humanoid robotics. Beyond speed, the games included tasks like cable plugging and garbage disposal, testing robots' ability to manipulate objects. Experts note that advanced manipulation remains a challenge for robots, requiring precise control and adaptability. Companies like Galbot are pushing for practical applications in manufacturing and retail, aiming to develop robots capable of working alongside humans in complex environments. The event also emphasized the potential of robotics to drive innovation and economic growth, despite concerns about job displacement.
source.title: Humanoid Robots Outperform Usain Bolt in Speed and Dexterity at China's Games

source.summary: Anthropic's chief executive will not attend a Senate committee hearing on AI this week following revelations that OpenAI agents breached Australian government systems. While the US-based company declined the invitation, it is expected to appear before a separate committee next week with representatives from its Australian and US operations. The breach involved the Australian Institute of Health and Welfare and other agencies. Prime Minister Anthony Albanese expressed extreme concern, while Finance Minister Katy Gallagher announced new cybersecurity funding and reporting rules. Anthropic submitted that AI is a national security capability, emphasizing the importance of trusted allies in model development.
source.title: Anthropic CEO Declines Senate Hearing Following OpenAI Data Breach

source.summary: Merchant bankers reported on September 21, 2026, that Deutsche Bank and other investors are offering rupee-denominated bonds of a Shapoorji Pallonji Group firm at a premium. This move is encouraged by the group's plans to sell part of its stake in Tata Sons, a transaction Tata Trusts confirmed last week. The sale aims to provide funds to the debt-laden infrastructure conglomerate. While Eqyizen Investment previously raised funds via zero-coupon bonds, current yields are around 18.70%-18.75%. SP Group and Deutsche Bank did not respond to comment requests.
source.title: SP Group bonds offered at premium on Tata Sons stake-sale plan, bankers say

source.summary: Europol reports a growing trend of violent museum heists in Europe, with thieves using guns, axes, and explosives. The agency notes a shift from non-violent to forceful methods, suggesting new criminal networks targeting cultural artefacts. Precious metals and ancient Chinese porcelain are preferred due to their high value and ease of sale. Recent cases include a 2025 heist at the Louvre, where thieves smashed display cases and stole jewellery worth €88m. Europol warns of potential recruitment of low-level thieves for such crimes.
source.title: Europol reports rise in violent museum heists involving weapons and explosives

source.summary: A man in Brooklyn died after his shopping bag became caught between subway train doors, dragging him onto the tracks. New York police identified the victim as 57-year-old Yaw Boahene. While subway accidents are rare, the Metropolitan Transportation Authority noted a slight 2% increase in customer accidents in 2025, though the 12-month rate decreased by 4.7% as ridership grew faster.
source.title: Man Killed After Bag Caught in NYC Subway Doors

source.summary: Following the Reserve Bank of India's rejection of Tata Sons' application to surrender its systemic importance registration, a report titled 'Tata Sons: Bell the Cat' urges the board to initiate preparations for an initial public offering. The firm argues that a listing would benefit approximately 1.77 crore shareholders and provide greater transparency, liquidity, and access to capital. Although Chairman N Chandrasekaran's second term ends in 2027 and some directors oppose the move, others support it. The board is scheduled to meet on September 17 to consider the RBI order, a potential listing timeline, and leadership succession. InGovern also concluded that Tata Sons has outgrown its current governance model and should establish a public listing timeline.
source.title: Tata Sons Board Urged to Pursue IPO Following RBI Rejection

source.summary: India has firmly rejected the so-called Pakistan-China Boundary Joint Commission, asserting that it has no legal basis. The Ministry of External Affairs spokesperson stated that there is no boundary between Pakistan and China and that Jammu and Kashmir and Ladakh remain integral parts of India. India called on Pakistan to stop theatrical maneuvers and immediately vacate areas under its illegal occupation, emphasizing that any cooperation between China and Pakistan regarding these territories is completely unacceptable.
source.title: India Rejects Pakistan-China Boundary Commission and Demands Territory Vacancy

source.summary: The US Treasury issued $1 coins bearing President Donald Trump's face to mark the 250th anniversary of the United States. The coins are available for purchase with a significant markup and are intended for circulation. This move contradicts federal law prohibiting living presidents from appearing on currency. Treasury Secretary Scott Bessent previously announced plans for a $250 bill with Trump's image, requiring a law change. The Treasury has not yet commented on whether the new coin violates existing statutes.
source.title: US Treasury issues $1 coin featuring President Trump's face

source.summary: Heatmap News and Embold Research conducted new polling and focus group conversations to examine why the argument that renewables are cheap fails to persuade climate change skeptics. The study reveals that 78% of voters who are doubtful or dismissive of climate change believe advocates exaggerate the low cost of wind and solar energy. Even among those persuadable on climate change, 62% hold this view. A majority of all voters, 55%, believe renewables are only cost-competitive due to subsidies. While attacks on clean energy for raising electricity bills have not gained traction, the affordability message itself does not land. Independent scientists are the only messengers trusted by a majority of voters, yet less than a third of skeptics trust any messenger. The authors report that breaking through requires local, tailored proof rather than national messaging, as 54% of skeptics said nothing could convince them solar was affordable.
source.title: Polling shows clean energy cost arguments fail to convince climate skeptics

source.summary: Chelsea and Brighton prepare to meet at Stamford Bridge on Sunday, August 30, as both teams look to build on strong starts to the season. Chelsea manager Xabi Alonso has hinted that Enzo Fernandez may not feature due to a lack of desire, while Brighton coach Fabian Hurzeler warned his side must defend collectively against Cole Palmer. The match follows Chelsea's recent victories over Fulham and Luton, and Brighton's wins against Aston Villa and Tromso. Chelsea has invested heavily in new signings, including Morgan Rogers and Emiliano Martinez, while Brighton faces absences for key players like Evan Ferguson. The Opta supercomputer predicts a Chelsea win, though Brighton has won their last four league encounters against the Blues.
source.title: Chelsea host Brighton at Stamford Bridge in Premier League clash

source.summary: Apple has launched the iPhone Duo, its first foldable phone, in India at a starting price of Rs 2,99,900. Pre-orders begin on October 16, with sales commencing on October 23. The device breaks with iPhone conventions by replacing Face ID with Touch ID and eliminating the SIM tray, operating exclusively on eSIM. It features a 7.6-inch inner display and a 5.4-inch outer screen, both powered by the A20 Pro chip and running iOS 27. While it shares the same processor as the iPhone 18 Pro, the camera system is less advanced, focusing instead on software features like Split View and enhanced AI capabilities. The phone includes dual batteries and a durable hinge design, though it does not include an adapter or earphones in the box.
source.title: Apple launches first foldable iPhone Duo in India at Rs 2,99,900

source.summary: A 31-member Kerala group returned safely to Kochi after being stranded by flash floods in Nepal. Group members stated that a 20-minute delay at a Buddha temple prevented them from crossing a bridge that was subsequently washed away. They described seeing buildings swept away within seconds and spending a difficult night without food. Emotional reunions occurred at the airport as families reunited with the travellers.
source.title: Kerala group credits 20-minute temple delay for survival in Nepal floods

source.summary: Energy Transfer, a Dallas-based pipeline company, filed a lawsuit seeking to declare parts of Pennsylvania's Clean Streams Law unconstitutional before facing criminal charges related to a jet fuel spill. The company argues the law lacks a 'mens rea' requirement, potentially allowing criminal liability for accidental pollution. Pennsylvania Attorney General Dave Sunday urged the court to dismiss the suit as an improper attempt to preempt an ongoing investigation. Legal experts note the challenge could upend decades of environmental enforcement by affecting minor offenses like traffic violations. Bucks County District Attorney Joe Khan intervened, warning the move threatens public safety and accountability for polluters. The Commonwealth Court has set a September 24 deadline for further filings.
source.title: Energy Transfer Challenges Pennsylvania Clean Water Law Amid Criminal Probe

source.summary: Delhi Police detained over 40 members of the Tibetan Youth Congress on Thursday, October 1, 2026, while they staged a protest outside the Chinese Embassy in Delhi. The group condemned China's assertion of sovereignty over Tibet and other regions. Police held the protesters at Mandir Marg police station. The Tibetan Youth Congress stated that Tibet is never part of China and will never be.
source.title: More than 40 Tibetans detained in Delhi over protest against China’s 77th founding day

source.summary: Linkdaze's smart calendar is designed to manage household schedules, integrating multiple calendar services and offering AI-driven meal planning. The device syncs Google, iCloud, Outlook, and Cozi calendars, using color coding to distinguish family members. It includes a 'Snap-to-Sync' feature that converts photos of recipes or lunch menus into digital meal plans. Linkdaze does not require a subscription for core features, unlike competitors like Skylight, and is priced lower than similar devices. It serves as a practical tool for families, college roommates, and busy professionals managing complex schedules.
source.title: Linkdaze's smart calendar organizes households with AI meal planning and multi-calendar sync

source.summary: Workers at an AutoZone store in White Plains, New York, are seeking to become the first location for the retailer to win a union election, set to begin 25 September. LaborLab, a non-profit workers' rights watchdog, estimates AutoZone has spent around $200,000 to oppose the effort. Workers cite low pay and lack of holiday compensation as drivers. The company has more than 6,800 US stores and reported a net income of $2.5bn in fiscal year 2025. AutoZone did not respond to requests for comment. The organizing drive mirrors past Teamsters attempts in the early 1990s, which resulted in a rerun election due to company conduct.
source.title: AutoZone Workers in White Plains Seek First Union Vote

source.summary: The European Central Bank raised interest rates to 2.5% on Thursday, citing heightened inflation risks linked to renewed conflict in the Middle East. The central bank increased rates from 2.25% and adjusted its economic growth forecast for the eurozone. ECB President Christine Lagarde stated that headline inflation is expected to return to target by the end of 2027, supported by higher interest rates. Simultaneously, energy prices jumped after US and Iranian attacks on ships in the Strait of Hormuz, causing Brent crude to pass $105 a barrel. These spikes drove government borrowing costs to historic highs in the UK, Germany, and France. Analysts at Schroders noted that while core inflation remains stable, higher energy prices will likely keep headline inflation elevated. Concerns persist over low EU gas storage levels ahead of winter, which could further strain inflation if supplies are disrupted.
source.title: ECB raises rates to 2.5% as Middle East conflict fuels inflation fears

source.summary: A Nagercoil YouTuber couple lost 118 sovereigns of gold and cash worth Rs 1 crore in a burglary. Police suspect their social media posts, which displayed wealth and announced travel plans, helped thieves time the raid. The couple is in shock as investigators examine the case.
source.title: TN YouTuber Couple Loses Rs 1 Cr in Burglary Linked to Social Media Posts

source.summary: NATO Secretary General Mark Rutte expressed the alliance's full solidarity with Germany following an alleged Russian hybrid attack in Leipzig. Rutte stated that Russia's attempts to undermine NATO unity and support for Ukraine will fail. German authorities revealed that the August incident involved multiple rigged drones targeting a Ukrainian cargo plane. Additionally, a weapons cache near Berlin was discovered, which German intelligence assessed was intended for Russian spies.
source.title: NATO expresses solidarity with Germany after alleged Russian ‘hybrid attack’ in Leipzig

source.summary: Amit Lakhanpal, the alleged mastermind behind the Money Trade Coin cryptocurrency scam, has been arrested in the UAE after Indian agencies traced his location. The arrest marks a significant development in a case first exposed by India Today's 2018 undercover investigation, which revealed the scheme defrauded investors of more than Rs 113 crore. Following the arrest, the Indian government has initiated extradition proceedings from the UAE, where Lakhanpal was living under an assumed identity after fleeing India in 2018. The Enforcement Directorate stated that its probe, intensified after the initial exposure, led to the discovery of Lakhanpal's whereabouts and the seizure of assets linked to the money laundering network.
source.title: India Today 2018 crypto exposé leads to Amit Lakhanpal UAE arrest

source.summary: Indian IT stocks rallied on Wednesday as the Nifty IT index rose over 2 per cent. Kotak Institutional Equities expects muted growth for large IT firms ahead of the Q2 FY27 earnings season, citing AI-led deflation and weaker macroeconomic conditions. The brokerage forecasts significant gross deflation of around 7 per cent for the sector, though margins may remain stable or decline marginally year-on-year.
source.title: Kotak Forecasts Muted Indian IT Growth Amid AI Deflation Risks

source.summary: Cathay Pacific and Google announced on Monday an expansion of trials using AI to help pilots avoid climate-warming aircraft contrails. The initial test on more than 80 flights achieved an estimated 40 per cent reduction in contrail warming impact. The companies stated that persistent contrails could account for around one-third of aviation's total climate impact. A larger second phase will cover Cathay's Asian and trans-Pacific network.
source.title: Cathay Pacific and Google expand AI trials to reduce aircraft contrails

source.summary: External Affairs Minister S. Jaishankar addressed the United Nations General Assembly, asserting India's right to defend itself against terrorism. He responded to Pakistan Prime Minister Shehbaz Sharif's criticism of India's Operation Sindoor and accusations regarding human rights. Jaishankar stated that state-sponsored terrorism must be held accountable and that agreements based on friendship cannot coexist with such acts. He also highlighted global conflicts' impact on the Global South and called for a reformed multilateral system.
source.title: India's Jaishankar Condemns Pakistan's Terrorism Claims at UNGA

source.summary: In a panel discussion in Dubai, Azerbaijan's presidential advisor Hikmet Hajiyev affirmed the country's dedication to preserving Christian heritage as an integral part of its history. While acknowledging the difficulty of maintaining peace with Armenia, he highlighted the need for both sides to prepare their populations. Hajiyev also criticized the European Parliament for adopting resolutions that undermine regional peace, urging the EU to adopt a more balanced approach that includes all countries in the South Caucasus rather than focusing on a single-centric strategy.
source.title: Azerbaijan Official Promises to Preserve Christian Heritage Amidst Regional Tensions

source.summary: Chief Minister N. Rangasamy announced a ₹50 increase in LPG subsidies for ration card holders in Puducherry. The government also plans financial aid for fishing community students and will clear pending pension applications. During the budget discussion, the CM outlined revenue sources and employment initiatives. Additionally, he wrote to the External Affairs Minister regarding three missing tourists in Nepal.
source.title: Puducherry CM announces LPG subsidy hike and budget details

source.summary: Energinet's CEO, Thomas Egebo, has stepped down after eight years, with deputy CEO Søren Dupont Kristensen taking over as acting chief. The move follows increased pressure to expand Denmark's electricity grid amid rapid electrification and renewable energy growth. The board cited the need for a new leadership profile to address challenges, initiating a CEO search. Board chair Tommy Ahlers emphasized the need for a CEO focused on infrastructure expansion and customer collaboration. Egebo's tenure saw significant changes in Denmark's energy system, including digitalization efforts. Kristensen will lead during the transition, with the board prioritizing grid expansion and maintaining supply security.
source.title: Energinet's CEO resigns as grid expansion pressures grow

source.summary: The Punjab and Haryana High Court ordered a Central Bureau of Investigation probe into alleged corruption involving the Punjab Chief Minister's Office following claims by the Enforcement Directorate. Simultaneously, a panel discussion examined the India-EU trade pact, noting its potential to cut four billion euros in tariffs and double bilateral trade. Indian Finance Minister Nirmala Sitharaman highlighted the agreement's benefits for labour-intensive sectors while addressing global trade pressures, including weaponised tariffs and a growing trade imbalance with China since 2014. The dialogue also covered strategic partnerships and the shift from multilateral to bilateral agreements.
source.title: India-EU Trade Pact and US Tariffs Discussed Amid Domestic Legal Actions

source.summary: U.S. President Donald Trump is expected to deliver a speech at the United Nations on September 22, 2026, where he will defend his ongoing war with Iran and highlight his efforts as a peacemaker. The event is overshadowed by concerns over the war's failure to meet White House objectives and economic damage from the Strait of Hormuz closure. Analysts from the International Crisis Group suggest Trump will contrast his peacemaker claims with military operations, while facing skepticism over a security deal in Greenland. Trump also plans to meet with leaders from Britain, Ukraine, Japan, and Venezuela.
source.title: Trump to Defend Iran War and Gaza Efforts at UN

source.summary: Experts attending the Inter Foundry and Inter DieCast exhibition in Coimbatore highlighted the growing potential for Indian foundries to supply global players. Parag Sharma of Stellantis noted that the sector has grown significantly and urged investment in modern technologies to attract more personnel. Additionally, the Foundries Development Foundation and Germany's VDMA signed a memorandum of understanding to expand the exhibition and secure space for Indian foundries at the upcoming GIFA trade fair in Germany. The event featured 322 exhibitors occupying 18,000 square meters of space, including pavilions from China, Italy, and Germany.
source.title: Experts say Indian foundries have high potential to supply global players

source.summary: The NITI Aayog report 'Reimagining Skilling for Viksit Bharat@2047' highlights India's skilling challenge, covering 145 crore individuals including students, young workers, and those adapting to a changing job market. The report assesses gaps in current education and skilling systems. It focuses on diverse groups facing employment challenges. The study aims to identify areas for improvement in skilling pathways. The report underscores the need for updated education and training programs.
source.title: NITI Aayog Report Examines India's Skilling Needs for 145 Crore People

source.summary: Hundreds attended a funeral in Kenscoff for four victims of a brutal gang attack that killed 47 people. UN Human Rights Office spokesperson Marta Hurtado stated that 150 armed gang members participated in the August 23 assault, executing 34 people after forcing them from a church. Survivors blame police for failing to prevent the carnage, while the National Police ordered an investigation into potential negligence. The attack left over 2,600 people homeless and highlighted the ongoing crisis as gangs control an estimated 70% of Port-au-Prince.
source.title: Hundreds mourn four victims of Haiti gang attack that killed 47

source.summary: Global investment in artificial intelligence is projected to reach $30 trillion by 2050, eclipsing previous technological booms according to PwC. While companies like Anthropic plan massive spending, economists warn that broad-based productivity gains remain elusive without historical precedent. JP Morgan and Bain & Company suggest that infrastructure buildouts may fail to deliver sufficient returns unless new markets emerge. Although AI leaders predict transformative impacts and rapid advancements, researchers note that productivity effects from past revolutions often took decades to materialize, raising concerns about the sustainability of current valuations and the potential for job displacement in white-collar sectors.
source.title: Global AI Investment Surges Amid Uncertainty Over Productivity Gains

source.summary: The provided text contains an error message regarding a failed site load rather than news about Iceland or the EU. No article body or headline details were available to summarize.
source.title: Iceland rejects bid to resume EU membership talks

source.summary: The Labor Department's Office of Inspector General released a report detailing dysfunction during the tenure of former Labor Secretary Lori Chavez-DeRemer. Investigators found merit in all complaints regarding a hostile work environment, an inappropriate relationship with security staff, and misuse of government resources. The report highlights four specific areas of concern where Chavez-DeRemer allegedly failed to follow department policy. First, witnesses described a toxic environment where her staff engaged in abusive behavior that she failed to stop. Second, investigators found evidence of an unprofessional relationship with a security detail member, including directing a driver to tip a performer. Third, the report states she directed employees to perform personal tasks like laundry during work hours. Finally, the investigation revealed she used official travel for personal reasons, such as attending a rodeo, without properly reporting lobbyist gifts. While her attorney stated no laws were broken, the OIG concluded she violated internal policies.
source.title: OIG report details dysfunction and policy violations under former Labor Secretary Lori Chavez-DeRemer

source.summary: Advanced Micro Devices agreed to acquire AI startup World Labs for US$8.2 billion in an all-stock transaction expected to close by the end of 2026. The deal brings World Labs' world models and talent, including founder Fei-Fei Li, to AMD. Lisa Su stated the acquisition helps AMD build better AI systems and compete with Nvidia.
source.title: AMD agrees to acquire AI startup World Labs for $8.2 billion

source.summary: Ørsted announced the completion of main construction on the 920 MW Greater Changhua 2b and 4 offshore wind farms in Taiwan. The projects are expected to enter full commercial operation in late Q3 2026 after remaining commissioning work. Ørsted developed the project with Cathay Life Insurance and various suppliers. The development adds to Taiwan's offshore wind sector and increases Ørsted's market presence. Patrick Harnett, Ørsted's chief construction officer, called the delivery a major achievement. The financing structure highlights the role of Taiwanese institutional capital, with Cathay Life holding stakes in the projects. Thirty financial institutions supported the project's financing. A corporate power purchase agreement links the development to Taiwan's semiconductor industry. Group CEO Rasmus Errboe stated the completion is a significant milestone in Ørsted's strategy. Construction included suction bucket jacket foundations and local operations capability development at the Port of Taichung.
source.title: Ørsted completes 920 MW Greater Changhua offshore wind build in Taiwan

source.summary: The John Lewis Partnership reported a pre-tax loss of £124m for the first half of the year, a 40% increase driven by higher costs and reduced consumer spending. Jason Tarry, the chair, attributed the drop to continued investment in transformation and a challenging trading environment. While Waitrose sales rose 4%, department store sales fell 2% as heatwaves and the cost of living deterred shoppers from visiting high street stores. The group remains in a turnaround plan involving store closures and job cuts, though it expects the second half to include peak Christmas trading.
source.title: John Lewis Partnership losses widen to £124m amid rising costs and weak shopper confidence

source.summary: Scientists warn that fossil fuel emissions are pushing Earth toward a dangerous climate overshoot phase where temperatures exceed the 1.5-degree Celsius Paris Agreement threshold within years. The United Nations Environmental Programme report states immediate cuts and carbon removal are essential to restore a safe climate. Experts say current warming rates could reach 2.7 to 3 degrees Celsius by 2100 without drastic measures. United Nations Secretary-General António Guterres emphasized the need to limit how high and long temperatures rise above the threshold. Researchers noted that recent extreme heat events in Europe and North America demonstrate that climate impacts are happening now, not in the distant future. The report highlights a critical gap between current adaptation capacities and the severity of upcoming climate-driven disasters.
source.title: UN Report Warns Climate Overshoot Imminent Without Immediate Action

source.summary: A political dispute has erupted in Tamil Nadu concerning the proposed construction of a new secretariat at Pattinapakkam. The Communist Party of India (Marxist) criticized the administration for failing to consult allies. Separately, a controversy emerged in Indore after a student outreach event involving mimicry drew sharp criticism from ruling party leaders who claimed it lacked meaningful discourse. This event is part of a nationwide series with sessions planned in Pune and Mumbai.
source.title: Political Dispute Erupts Over Student Event Mimicry Ahead of Mumbai Outreach

source.summary: NVIDIA DSX MaxLPS is a suite of technologies designed to maximize AI factory performance per watt by optimizing power usage across chip, thermal, system, and software layers. Traditional data centers often waste power due to static rack provisioning, which allocates maximum power per rack for peak demand, leaving unused capacity. MaxLPS introduces dynamic power allocation, using Dynamic Power Software (DPS) to monitor and reallocate unused power headroom among GPUs. This approach reduces facility overhead and operational inefficiencies, improving power usage effectiveness (PUE) and enabling more racks within the same power budget. NVIDIA reports that MaxLPS can increase GPU capacity by up to 40% within the same power envelope for its Vera Rubin NVL72 AI factories. The system also includes optimized workload profiles and thermal efficiency features, such as 45°C liquid cooling, to further enhance performance per watt. By aligning GPU configuration with workload needs, MaxLPS aims to improve overall AI factory productivity and output efficiency.
source.title: NVIDIA DSX MaxLPS Enhances AI Factory Efficiency Through Dynamic Power Management

source.summary: A morning briefing on September 20, 2026, highlighted several international security developments. Saudi air defenses intercepted a Houthi ballistic missile targeting Riyadh, with coalition officials condemning the attack as a systematic effort to target civilians. Meanwhile, the US Central Command reported that more than 1 billion barrels of crude oil transited the Strait of Hormuz under a military blockade, with US forces assisting over 2,000 commercial vessel transits. In other news, Israeli warplanes launched airstrikes in southern Lebanon despite a US-mediated agreement. Additionally, US President Donald Trump announced the creation of an 'AI Force' to oversee artificial intelligence development.
source.title: Global Security Briefing Covers Regional Conflicts and US Policy Shifts

source.summary: This article examines how crude AI-generated images have revived a decades-old smear campaign against Indian politician Sonia Gandhi, portraying her as a 'bar dancer.' While the BJP's official social media handles circulated these images, the piece argues that generative AI merely accelerates existing misogynistic visual politics. The author notes that female politicians have long faced scrutiny regarding their appearance, motherhood, and sexuality, with AI now enabling the rapid creation of a 'manufactured visual biography.' This technology allows propagandists to bypass searching for existing photos, instead generating new images that reinforce negative stereotypes and detach women from their actual political performances, making them objects of semiotic violence.
source.title: Generative AI Revives Old Smears Against Female Politicians

source.summary: Matt Clifford has stepped down as chair of the UK's Advanced Research and Invention Agency after senior MPs described his new full-time role at Anthropic as a clear conflict of interest. Chi Onwurah, chair of the Commons science committee, called the arrangement a conflict and questioned how safeguards were established. Clifford announced he would remain until 6 November with appropriate protections in place. Beeban Kidron welcomed the move, stating that rebuilding trust requires a clear line between tech interests and those of citizens. The resignation highlights ongoing concerns about the revolving door between government and AI companies, following similar moves by former Prime Minister Rishi Sunak and Chancellor George Osborne.
source.title: Matt Clifford quits UK AI policy role over Anthropic conflict concerns

source.summary: Ireland's Data Protection Commission fined Google €403 million for violating GDPR rules regarding the processing of location data through features like 'Web & App Activity' and 'Location History' between 2018 and 2020. The regulator stated that users could have lost control over their personal data as a result. Google was ordered to bring its processing into compliance within six months and did not immediately respond to requests for comment.
source.title: Irish Regulator Fines Google €403 Million Over Location Data

source.summary: The White House escalated its trade dispute with Canada by banning specific imports and raising tariffs on others. President Donald Trump signed executive orders imposing a 50% surcharge on goods such as mattresses and motorboats starting September 15, while banning alcoholic beverages and some dairy products from September 29. A senior administration official explained the measures are intended to maintain a level playing field and protect American production. These actions follow Ottawa's recent imposition of new tariffs on U.S. products in response to duties announced by Washington on August 22. Additionally, Trump threatened to exclude Canadian products from a government procurement program unless reciprocity is restored.
source.title: Trump bans Canadian alcohol and raises tariffs on other goods

source.summary: The Trump administration is pressuring European capitals to release emergency diesel supplies or face a US export ban, aiming to curb surging fuel prices. France, Germany, Britain, Italy, and Ireland have been targeted, with officials preparing a unified response to defuse the situation. Meanwhile, Russia extended its diesel export ban, and China suspended fuel exports for October, further squeezing global energy supplies.
source.title: US Pressures Europe to Release Emergency Diesel Amid Price Surge

source.summary: Prime Minister Narendra Modi met Vladimir Putin in Bishkek to deliver India's message for peace in Ukraine. Modi stated that every day of conflict sets humanity back and urged a move from endless war to an end of war. He emphasized that India supports all efforts towards a peaceful resolution. Putin noted that Russian-Indian relations continue to strengthen based on their special partnership.
source.title: PM Modi urges Putin to end Ukraine war at SCO summit

source.summary: PG&E has launched a new virtual power plant initiative in partnership with Google and Rewiring America, aiming to recruit over 20,000 customers with solar and battery systems. Google pledged to cover the program's costs, starting with approximately $14 million for the initial phase. While PG&E and Google insist the program is unrelated to offsetting data center expenses, critics point to Google's planned 250-MW facility in San Jose as a likely beneficiary. Concurrently, California lawmakers have introduced bills requiring data centers to pay a share of grid upgrade costs. Meanwhile, Tesla and Sunrun recently achieved a record 580 MW of peak power from over 110,000 home batteries, though some programs face defunding next year.
source.title: California Utilities Launch Virtual Power Plant Program Amid Data Center Cost Disputes

source.summary: Chemours has requested priority review from the U.S. Environmental Protection Agency to manufacture Opteon 2P50, a new chemical designed to cool AI infrastructure. Environmental groups, including Earthjustice, oppose the filing, arguing the substance poses unreasonable risks to human health and the environment as a type of PFAS. The company claims the fluid can reduce cooling energy use by 90% and nearly eliminate water consumption in data centers. Critics worry that regulatory shortcuts under the current administration create a fast lane for approving persistent chemicals. While Chemours insists the compound is not a PFAS because it breaks down quickly, opponents note its breakdown products are known contaminants. Experts remain divided on the severity of the risks posed by these breakdown products. The EPA has prioritized reviews for data center-related chemicals following an executive order issued last summer. This development occurs as the industry seeks to replace existing standards with new immersion-cooling fluids.
source.title: Chemours seeks EPA approval for new PFAS coolant amid data center boom

source.summary: TechCrunch announces the return of the Builders Stage at its Disrupt 2026 conference, scheduled for October 13-15 at the Moscone Center in San Francisco. The event targets founders, investors, and operators seeking practical advice on scaling startups through candid conversations and case studies. Over 10,000 attendees are expected to join sessions covering fundraising, hiring, go-to-market strategies, and AI integration. The agenda features industry leaders like Grant Lee of Gamma and Robby Stein of Google discussing specific challenges such as competing for AI talent and navigating the Series A landscape in 2027. Speakers will address how product decisions must evolve at scale and how companies can achieve viral growth while maintaining retention. The stage also explores M&A as an early-stage strategy and the psychological demands of founding a high-growth company. Ticket prices are set to increase, prompting organizers to encourage early registration. The event aims to provide actionable insights for building companies that can transition from seed funding to significant market traction.
source.title: TechCrunch Disrupt 2026 Adds Builders Stage for Startup Scaling Strategies

source.summary: British, French, and Canadian leaders announced Tuesday that sanctions on illegal Israeli settlements mark a turning point in their approach to protecting the two-state solution. Andy Burnham, Emmanuel Macron, and Mark Carney issued a joint statement declaring the outcome critical for regional stability. They noted that systematic settlement expansion and increased settler violence pose an urgent threat to peace. Consequently, the three countries will ban the importation of goods from settlements and enforce targeted measures against those who facilitate or profit from them. Additionally, the leaders confirmed they will co-chair a meeting at the United Nations General Assembly later this month to advance their efforts and pursue peace.
source.title: UK, France, and Canada announce sanctions on illegal Israeli settlements

source.summary: Preliminary results indicate United Russia secured a record 355 seats in the State Duma, exceeding the 301 needed to change the constitution. Central Election Commission chief Ella Pamfilova reported 355 of 450 seats for the party, with turnout at more than 59 percent. Five Western nations and Kyiv condemned the voting in occupied Ukraine as illegal. The EU vowed sanctions on those organizing the vote or standing as candidates in occupied Ukrainian territory. Britain, Australia, Canada, New Zealand and Norway called the election a gross violation of sovereignty.
source.title: Putin's party secures record Duma majority amid international condemnation

source.summary: At Meta Connect, the social media giant showcased its commitment to smart glasses, with the devices appearing frequently among staff and influencers. While previous camera-equipped models faced accusations of enabling surveillance, new audio-only glasses without cameras aim to address privacy concerns. These lighter, comfortable glasses integrate with Muse, an AI system for verbal commands, and will cost $150, significantly cheaper than some hearing aids priced up to $1,600. Additionally, Meta introduced glasses for the hearing impaired, developed over five years to assist the 50 million Americans with hearing loss. Despite Mark Zuckerberg's vision for glasses as the future, the technology remains niche as Meta attempts to make them stylish and functional.
source.title: Meta Pushes Smart Glasses at Connect Event Amid Privacy Concerns

source.summary: The Indian government is discussing a proposal to sell 10% ethanol-blended petrol as a premium fuel option for older vehicles. According to a report by LiveMint, the petroleum ministry is talking with state-run oil marketing companies about this approach. Three people aware of the discussions told Mint that no final decision has been taken yet. The proposal aims to address concerns about E20 petrol's impact on older cars without creating new fuel infrastructure. Premium brands like Indian Oil's XP95 could be offered with a 10% ethanol blend. Consumer groups want wider fuel choices for older vehicles, while the government previously opposed multiple fuel streams due to logistical challenges. Fuel dealers say using existing premium-petrol storage could make an E10 rollout straightforward.
source.title: Government explores selling E10 petrol through existing premium fuel infrastructure

source.summary: Federal authorities arrested Shiloh Luckey, a 42-year-old California resident, on charges of orchestrating a $13.3 million investor fraud scheme. According to the U.S. Attorney's Office, Luckey deceived backers into funding her startup, ComplYant App Inc., by falsely claiming she was a licensed CPA and inflating company metrics. Prosecutors allege she diverted the funds to buy a Tesla, an Inglewood home, Super Bowl tickets, and a Caribbean wedding. The company shut down by September 2023, leaving investors with total losses. If convicted, Luckey faces up to 30 years in federal prison.
source.title: Feds Arrest Accounting Fraudster Who Squandered $13.3M on Wedding and Super Bowl Tickets

source.summary: The Indian stock market showed little movement on August 21, 2026, with green energy stocks performing mixed. Kabra Extrusion and Olectra Greentech saw significant gains, while Praj Industries and Sterling and Wilson Renewable Energy declined. Battery and energy storage stocks also faced pressure. Reliance Industries and Larsen & Toubro showed minimal changes, reflecting stock-specific investor activity in the green energy sector.
source.title: Green Energy Stocks Show Mixed Performance As Indian Markets Trade Flat (21 August 2026)

source.summary: The article explains how AI data centers are increasing power demand on the grid. PJM capacity prices rose 833% in a year. A single grid disturbance dropped 1,500 megawatts of AI load in under a second. Utilities must respond quickly without waiting for new transmission.
source.title: AI Data Centers Drive Surging Power Demand and Grid Strain

source.summary: Sir Jim Ratcliffe, owner of Ineos, has suspended production at three UK facilities, citing gas prices in the UK as twelve times higher than in the US and eight times higher than in China. The company stated that up to 1,000 staff could be affected, with two plants already shut and a third set to stop production in the coming days. Ratcliffe described the current government's energy policy as 'economic vandalism on an industrial scale' and called for tariff protections against Chinese products. The Department for Business, Innovation, Science and Trade responded by highlighting existing support measures for the chemicals industry.
source.title: Sir Jim Ratcliffe Halts Ineos UK Production Over High Gas Costs

source.summary: Rachael Gunn discusses her experiences in a new Netflix documentary about her Paris Olympics performance. She described feeling shame after her viral breaking routine received no votes. Gunn noted that while some memes were humorous, the tone eventually became cruel. She revealed she had anticipated mockery before the Games and is now working as a speaker. The film addresses rumors about her qualification and her feelings during the fallout.
source.title: Rachael Gunn discusses Olympic mockery and new Netflix documentary

source.summary: Political editor Anand Mishra contrasts the non-controversial success of the biopic Hanuman Ansh with recent films that sparked legal and social disputes. The article notes that older religious movies like Jai Santoshi Maa achieved commercial success without creating communal divides, unlike recent productions. Mishra questions whether modern filmmakers are prioritizing political agendas and hate-mongering over art to generate box-office revenue.
source.title: Editor contrasts past and present religious films in India
