source.summary: President Trump greeted Chinese leader Xi Jinping at Joint Base Andrews, a ceremony described as historic because Xi leads America's primary adversary rather than a close ally. Experts note this signals a shift in power, with China threatening rare earths after Trump imposed tariffs exceeding 140%. While the summit included protocol giveaways like a 21-gun salute, analysts question the substantive results, citing a fragile trade truce and uncertainty over an AI hotline. Critics argue the lavish welcome contrasts with past diplomatic successes.
source.title: Trump Welcomes Xi at Joint Base Andrews Amid Shifting US-China Power Dynamics

source.summary: Canada's solar market is expanding at varying speeds across provinces, driven by distinct local policies and federal grid constraints. Phil McKay of the Canadian Renewable Energy Association notes that while 2026 data is unavailable, anecdotal evidence suggests a strong year for storage-paired systems. Québec and Ontario are leading buildout with new incentives and large-scale procurements, respectively. Other regions are shifting from net-metering to net-billing, sparking debate over solar value. McKay highlights that US tariffs create uncertainty, yet federal commitments to sustainable energy and cross-Canada transmission offer long-term optimism. Meanwhile, grassroots interest in plug-in solar is rising, though safety standards remain in development.
source.title: Canada's solar sector grows unevenly as provinces adopt different policies

source.summary: Singapore possesses a well-established system of national awards recognizing valuable service in fields like public service, business, and arts. However, a proposal by Goy Soong Ngee suggests creating a simple Citizen Contribution Award to recognize ordinary residents whose constructive suggestions lead to tangible improvements. This initiative aims to encourage active participation and shared effort in building a better Singapore without relying on prestigious medals or significant monetary value.
source.title: Proposal to Recognize Citizens for Improvements in Singapore

source.summary: Motilal Oswal outlines the Mobile Phone Manufacturing Scheme (MPMS), which offers incentives of 2.25% to 5.0% over five years. The scheme requires companies to meet sales thresholds, with minimum turnover of Rs 10,000 crore in FY26-27 and incremental sales targets increasing annually. Dixon is noted as a potential beneficiary due to its scale. Incentives apply when at least 25% of components are domestically sourced. Indian brands with Rs 1,000 crore turnover qualify for 5% on incremental sales and 3% on domestic design and R&D. The scheme aims to boost domestic production and exports.
source.title: Motilal Oswal highlights PLI 2.0 incentives for mobile manufacturers

source.summary: Officials said Indonesia escalated efforts to combat wildfires using cloud seeding and water bombing on August 28. Deputy Health Minister Dante Saksono Harbuwono reported that over five million people faced health risks from the haze. The disaster agency BNPB stated it distributed more than four million litres of water and scattered 8,000kg of salt onto clouds. Environmental groups called for immediate action to address the root causes of the recurring fires.
source.title: Indonesia intensifies wildfire fight as haze affects millions

source.summary: A new city-building game, Lego Skylines, is set to release on multiple platforms including Steam and the Nintendo Switch 2, featuring detailed urban planning mechanics. On September 1, John Ternus assumed the role of Apple CEO, succeeding Tim Cook, who will transition to executive chairman. Ternus, who joined Apple in 2001, is now responsible for all company products following a record-breaking financial quarter. Additionally, the Qubo Smart Air Purifier R700 is reviewed as an affordable, high-performance device priced at ₹14,900. The purifier features a five-layer filtration system, an AI mode, and a long filter life of nearly a year, effectively reducing indoor air quality indices in tested environments.
source.title: Lego Skylines launches; John Ternus becomes Apple CEO; Qubo R700 purifier reviewed

source.summary: Retail and consumer goods teams face challenges in aligning decisions across disconnected systems and teams, leading to difficulties in turning analysis into results. A unified application, demonstrated by Databricks, connects performance reviews, demand planning, audience activation, store execution, and campaign measurement in one end-to-end process. The application is built on three foundations: data unification, governance, and intelligence. It enables stakeholders to review performance, plan demand, and measure outcomes using a shared data source, with features like natural language querying and autonomous agents. The workflow supports planning actions, marketing decisions, and store-level execution, creating a closed-loop view that connects campaign activity back to sales and operational outcomes.
source.title: Connecting retail demand planning to campaign and store execution

source.summary: Researchers at TU Delft have developed a system that allows users to adjust the driving behavior of self-driving cars through natural language. The system uses a large language model (LLM) to translate user requests, such as 'go faster' or 'drive smoothly,' into adjustments to a safety-aware motion-planning algorithm. The LLM interprets these instructions and modifies the parameters of the motion planner, which determines the vehicle's path and speed. The system keeps the human in the loop by describing proposed changes in non-technical language and asking for confirmation before implementing them. The researchers tested the system in simulation, finding it successfully adjusted driving behavior to match user intent. The approach differs from previous work by focusing on driving style rather than direct control, and it uses a model predictive-path integral controller to ensure safety. While the system allows for personalized driving experiences, it does not replace the need for safety guarantees, as highlighted by other experts in the field.
source.title: Researchers Develop System to Adjust Self-Driving Car Behavior via Natural Language

source.summary: Vikram Doraiswami, Ambassador of India to China, describes New Delhi's preparation for the fourth BRICS summit, themed Building for Resilience, Innovation, Cooperation and Sustainability. The article notes the group has expanded to include ten partner countries, representing roughly half of humanity and 40% of global GDP. Doraiswami explains India's chairship focused on four pillars: resilience, innovation, cooperation, and sustainability, executed through a whole-of-nation approach hosting nearly 400 meetings across over 30 cities. The author emphasizes that stable India-China cooperation is vital for BRICS credibility, citing recent working-level engagement and shared development goals between the two largest emerging economies.
source.title: India hosts BRICS summit focusing on resilience and innovation

source.summary: Algeria's education ministry announced that English will replace French as the primary foreign language taught in third-year primary schools starting in 2026-2027. This marks a significant shift in the country's linguistic policy, ending French's long-standing dominance in schools. The decision is part of President Abdelmadjid Tebboune's broader linguistic overhaul, which includes transitioning university subjects from French to English. The move comes amid heightened diplomatic tensions with France, following its support for Morocco's Western Sahara claims. Critics argue the reform lacks sufficient resources and planning, particularly in teacher training. Meanwhile, public interest in English-language books is growing, reflecting a broader cultural shift. Despite these changes, French remains widely spoken, with over 15 million Algerians fluent in the language. The reforms also highlight a regional trend of former French colonies reevaluating their linguistic ties to Paris, as seen in Mali, Niger, and Burkina Faso's recent departures from the Francophone organization OIF.
source.title: Algeria shifts from French to English in primary education amid diplomatic tensions

source.summary: A 14-year-old class 9 student in Ghaziabad died after allegedly falling from a 12th-floor balcony while collecting clothes. Police stated the incident occurred around 9 pm on Friday night. The girl, a two-time CBSE gold medallist in rope skipping, was with family members at the time. Her body was sent for an autopsy to determine the exact circumstances, with no indication of foul play reported by the family.
source.title: Ghaziabad student dies after alleged balcony fall

source.summary: China Southern Airlines announced on Saturday, September 12, 2026, that it will resume regular passenger services on the Guangzhou-New Delhi route from September 21, restarting the service after a six-year suspension. The carrier said it will operate more than 100 weekly flights across eight round-trip routes in South Asia. This announcement coincides with Chinese President Xi Jinping's visit to India to attend the BRICS summit and hold talks with Prime Minister Narendra Modi on improving bilateral relations.
source.title: China Southern Airlines resumes Guangzhou-Delhi flights after six-year suspension

source.summary: Organization for Political Ecology Polekol filed criminal complaints against Zlatna Reka Resources and an unidentified executive regarding suspected environmental harm in southwestern Serbia. The group alleges the mining subsidiary failed to implement required environmental protection measures during gold exploration. Polekol requests authorities test water and soil samples for contamination and stop the company's exploration permit. The organization cites unresolved irregularities identified by geological inspections and compares the situation to illegal deforestation by Zijin Mining in eastern Serbia.
source.title: Serbia environmental group files criminal complaint over mining exploration

source.summary: A new short-form video app called Divine has launched, offering six-second looping videos and banning AI-generated content. Founded by Evan Henshaw-Plath, the app aims to reset social media by emphasizing human-created content. Divine uses a decentralized system like Nostr, allowing users to transfer accounts and data between services. It also hosts over two million original Vine videos, which were preserved by the Internet Archive. The app's founder noted that nostalgia for Vine's format could attract users, despite the rise of longer-form content on platforms like TikTok. Divine faces challenges in proving that its approach can be both addictive and meaningful without relying on AI.
source.title: Divine app launches as AI-free short-form video platform

source.summary: The White House is considering using the Defense Production Act to expand U. S. refining capacity, according to Reuters. American refineries are currently operating at 98% capacity, prompting discussions during a meeting between President Donald Trump and refiners. Executives indicated that federal funds would accelerate expansion of existing plants compared to building new facilities. The Defense Production Act allows the president to provide financial assistance for materials and capacity deemed necessary for national defense. This follows a presidential determination in April declaring domestic petroleum production essential to national defense. U. S.
source.title: White House considers Defense Production Act to boost U.S. refining capacity

source.summary: Alex de Minaur advanced to the quarterfinals of the China Open following a three-set victory over qualifier Quentin Halys. The match lasted 2 hours and 47 minutes, with de Minaur winning 3-6, 7-6 (5), 7-5. He will face Andrey Rublev, ranked number 20 in the world, in the next round.
source.title: Alex de Minaur Advances to China Open Quarterfinals

source.summary: Liam Denning writes that Chevron's new investment highlights the gap between political rhetoric and operational reality in Venezuela. The company announced a $7 billion joint venture with Petroindependencia to increase output by 320,000 barrels daily by 2031. Denning notes this measured expansion contrasts with the White House's larger, riskier deal involving controversial figures. The author suggests Chevron's methodical approach may serve as a proof of concept for future capital investment in the region.
source.title: Chevron invests billions in Venezuela despite production challenges

source.summary: Solar Ireland reports Ireland has reached 3 GW of installed solar capacity through utility sites and rooftop installations. CEO Ronan Power noted over 200,000 homes now have solar roofs. Grid-scale farms generated 1.1 GWh in 2025, a 51% increase from 2024. The industry aims for 8 GW by 2030 ahead of the upcoming RESS 6 auction. Minister Darragh O'Brien pledged continued investment to strengthen energy security.
source.title: Ireland reaches 3 GW solar capacity with rooftop and utility growth

source.summary: Yemen's Saudi-backed government forces stated on September 12, 2026, that they struck Iran-allied Houthi fighters in the Red Sea city of Mocha. The Houthis reported Saudi aircraft conducted 129 airstrikes on their controlled areas during the same period. Since July, the UN migration agency reported that 76,000 people have fled the fighting, a number that quadrupled in one week. The agency warned that humanitarian needs are far outpacing what they can deliver.
source.title: Yemeni forces strike Houthi targets in Red Sea city of Mocha

source.summary: ASML is expanding its presence in India to support the Tata Electronics semiconductor fab in Dholera, Gujarat. Allan Wayne, ASML's Chief Strategic Sourcing and Procurement Officer, highlighted the shift towards AI-driven semiconductor needs. He projected the global industry to reach $1.6 trillion by 2030. Meanwhile, India aims to meet 15-25% of its semiconductor demand through domestic fabs by 2032, with targets rising to 35-50% by 2035. ASML currently has no plans for manufacturing in India but emphasizes building a supply chain first.
source.title: ASML Expands India Presence Amid Tata Electronics Fab Growth

source.summary: Uttarakhand officials banned loud sound systems near Badrinath Dham temple and other Chamoli religious sites following objections to the two-day Devbhoomi Cultural Festival 2026 held on September 19 and 20. District Magistrate Gaurav Kumar mandated prior permission for events near such sites, with legal action threatened for violations. While organizers described the festival as a civil-military initiative, religious leaders argued it compromised the area's sanctity.
source.title: Uttarakhand Bans Loud Sound Systems Near Badrinath Temple

source.summary: A Zonal Railway Users Consultative Committee member has appealed for the immediate restoration of direct train services between Visakhapatnam and Narasapur, citing commuter hardships caused by the withdrawal of previous trains. The member highlighted that passenger footfall at Narasapur station more than doubled to over 7.48 lakh, with earnings jumping to ₹18.27 crore between FY 2021-22 and FY 2022-23. While a final decision rests with the Railway Board, the member has urged the South Coast Railway to operate direct special trains during major festive periods.
source.title: ZRUCC member seeks direct train restoration between Visakhapatnam and Narasapur

source.summary: Congress defended Telangana Chief Minister Revanth Reddy against BJP demands for an apology regarding his comparison of Lord Ram and Lord Shiva. Mahesh Kumar Goud stated the remarks targeted the BJP. Reddy previously claimed the BJP represents the rich while Shiva represents the poor. Union minister Sanjay Kumar Bandi and Telangana BJP president N Ramchander Rao criticized the comments as divisive and insulting to the Hindu religion.
source.title: Congress Defends Telangana CM Over Ram-Shiva Remarks Amid BJP Criticism

source.summary: Finance Minister Nirmala Sitharaman arrived in Asheville for the G-20 finance ministerial meeting hosted by U.S. Treasury Secretary Scott Bessent. The gathering focuses on global growth amid conflicts in West Asia and Europe. Sitharaman met with 3M CEO William Brown to discuss deepening India's role in advanced manufacturing and technology. Both leaders agreed on leveraging Indian talent for innovation and supply chain development.
source.title: Finance Minister Nirmala Sitharaman attends G-20 meeting in Asheville

source.summary: The Film Federation of India announced on September 18 that the Marathi film Gondhal has been selected as India's official entry for the 2027 Oscars. Written and directed by Santosh Davakhar, the film is set in rural Maharashtra and follows a traditional ritual centered on a newly-wed couple. Selection committee chairperson P Seshadri noted that Gondhal was chosen from a list of 33 films. This marks the fourth Marathi film to be selected for the Academy Awards.
source.title: Marathi Film Gondhal Selected as India's Oscar Entry

source.summary: Schwartz's, a famous Montreal deli, has permanently stopped serving its long-time US black cherry soda. The shop struggled to maintain supply for eight years as distributors cut production due to rising aluminium costs. Consequently, the venue switched to a locally-made version of the drink. Customers have largely embraced this new local alternative.
source.title: Schwartz's deli swaps US black cherry soda for local alternative

source.summary: Nvidia CEO Jensen Huang declared on social media that artificial general intelligence has arrived after OpenAI unveiled its new Astra model. Huang stated that 400,000 additional graphics processing units will soon go live to support further AI development. OpenAI president Greg Brockman described the launch as a historic turning point, yet industry figures like Gary Marcus and Sam Altman have urged caution regarding the term AGI. The report notes that major development groups remain heavily reliant on Nvidia's processors for their operations.
source.title: Nvidia CEO Jensen Huang declares AGI has arrived after OpenAI launches Astra

source.summary: Legal opinions obtained by Tata Sons support the validity of N. Chandrasekaran's reappointment as chairman for a third five-year term. Former Supreme Court judges Justice B.N. Srikrishna and Justice Uday U. Lalit opined the casting vote exercised by the chairman was valid under the company's Articles of Association. Tata Trusts, which owns about 66% of Tata Sons, challenged the resolution, arguing the Articles require affirmative support from a majority of Trust-nominated directors.
source.title: Legal Opinion Supports N. Chandrasekaran's Reappointment as Tata Sons Chairman

source.summary: India has warned that it will take necessary steps to protect its trade and economic interests following the US House of Representatives passing a sweeping sanctions bill on Russia. The legislation allows the Trump administration to impose tariffs of up to 100% on major Russian oil purchasers, potentially targeting India. The Indian Ministry of External Affairs reaffirmed its commitment to ensuring energy security for its 1.4 billion people through diversified sourcing and evolving market dynamics, while noting that the issue has been discussed at high levels with US interlocutors.
source.title: India warns against US sanctions bill targeting Russian oil buyers

source.summary: China's carbon dioxide emissions fell by 1% in the second quarter of 2026, driven primarily by a sharp decline in oil consumption rather than coal reductions. The National Bureau of Statistics reports that oil use dropped 9% overall, with transport consumption falling 16% amid disruptions to supply from the Strait of Hormuz. Electric vehicles and public transport became key factors in this shift, with EV usage surging to displace significant amounts of fuel. Despite a rebound in coal-fired power generation, total emissions decreased because the reduction in oil use outweighed the increase from coal. The analysis highlights that structural changes in transportation, including increased EV adoption and charging volumes, played a major role in reducing oil demand. However, power sector emissions rose 3.0% in the first half of 2026 due to curtailment of solar and wind output, which forced greater reliance on coal. Government plans released in the quarter signal a higher bar for new coal projects but also allow for increased renewable curtailment limits in some provinces. While emissions remain below their 2023-24 peak, the trend reflects a complex balance between slowing energy demand growth and the continued expansion of clean energy capacity.
source.title: China's CO2 Emissions Fall in Q2 2026 as Oil Use Drops

source.summary: Pankaj, a senior civil servant, published a book recounting his 14-year legal battle against a conspiracy involving fabricated testimony and a non-existent law. The book, titled My Lady in Black, details his two-month imprisonment and the pivotal support of his wife, Sweta, who studied law to defend him. Pankaj describes the experience as cathartic, noting that while he was acquitted, the process exacted a heavy emotional toll.
source.title: Pankaj publishes book about 14-year legal battle for justice

source.summary: Petra Molnar of Tech Policy Press argues that European human rights frameworks fail to regulate the purchase of surveillance and military technology from Israel. The article highlights Greece's recent $3.5 billion agreement with Israel for systems like Achilles Shield and Centaur, noting these tools are used in contexts involving occupation and potential genocide. Molnar points out that while the EU scrutinizes weapons exports, it excludes military procurement from its AI and data protection rules. She contends that European states must apply human rights due diligence to purchasing decisions, not just sales, to prevent contributing to harm.
source.title: Article argues human rights oversight is missing in European defense procurement from Israel

source.summary: According to a Financial Times report, Tencent signed a five-year lease with Oracle for approximately 100,000 advanced AI chips unavailable in China. The deal, estimated at US$7 billion, includes an upfront payment of about 30%. While the report cites people familiar with the matter, Reuters could not immediately verify the information, and neither company responded to requests for comment.
source.title: Tencent leases 100,000 AI chips from Oracle to accelerate expansion

source.summary: The European Central Bank raised interest rates to 2.5% on Thursday, citing heightened inflation risks linked to renewed conflict in the Middle East. The central bank increased rates from 2.25% and adjusted its economic growth forecast for the eurozone. ECB President Christine Lagarde stated that headline inflation is expected to return to target by the end of 2027, supported by higher interest rates. Simultaneously, energy prices jumped after US and Iranian attacks on ships in the Strait of Hormuz, causing Brent crude to pass $105 a barrel. These spikes drove government borrowing costs to historic highs in the UK, Germany, and France. Analysts at Schroders noted that while core inflation remains stable, higher energy prices will likely keep headline inflation elevated. Concerns persist over low EU gas storage levels ahead of winter, which could further strain inflation if supplies are disrupted.
source.title: ECB raises rates to 2.5% as Middle East conflict fuels inflation fears

source.summary: An analyst from 24/7 Wall St. reports that Amazon's stock could rise 33% based on accelerating AWS growth. The firm sets a price target of $340.96, citing a 37% reacceleration in AWS and strong advertising gains. While Wall Street consensus targets $327, the analyst notes significant upside potential driven by AI infrastructure expansion and high-margin business segments.
source.title: Analyst predicts 33% Amazon stock upside as AWS growth accelerates

source.summary: Bloomberg reported that Amazon entered agreements to purchase nearly 200 MW from four Swedish wind farms to support its data centers. Once operational, the company's total wind capacity in Sweden will approach 1 GW, enough to power over 350,000 households annually. Amazon noted that capacity will increase across its sites in Eskilstuna, Katrineholm, and Västerås as demand grows. Separately, Eolus sold three of the farms to Mirova, which now owns the sites and will collaborate on battery storage development.
source.title: Amazon signs long-term deals to buy 200 MW from four Swedish wind farms

source.summary: China's total solar power capacity has now exceeded its coal capacity, marking a significant shift in the nation's energy infrastructure. Bloomberg reported that if all solar panels received sunlight simultaneously, they would generate more electricity than every coal plant operating at once. However, analysts warn that capacity figures do not equate to actual energy production, as coal remains the primary source of power generation during non-peak hours. A McKinsey report indicates that global markets are financing fossil fuels and low-carbon energy simultaneously rather than replacing one with the other. Meanwhile, the United States is experiencing a massive buildout of natural gas plants to support data centers, with nearly 200 gigawatts of projects announced or under construction. Heatmap News reported that tech giants like Amazon and OpenAI are backing these initiatives despite public opposition to data centers. In California, a wildfire liability bill collapsed after legislators could not agree on core insurance issues, leaving utilities vulnerable to bankruptcy. Additionally, Fervo Energy announced a deal to sell 400 megawatts of geothermal power to Google, while the U.S. Department of Energy invested $12 million in space-based solar technology. The article also noted that next-generation nuclear startups are exploring the use of stockpiled plutonium for energy production.
source.title: China's Solar Capacity Surpasses Coal Output in New Milestone

source.summary: YouTube announced a new feature enabling creators to organize vertical clips into microdrama-style series, aiming to capitalize on the genre's rapid growth. Executives stated they are excited about the rise of episodic content, noting that microdramas have already surpassed 6.5 billion views on the platform in the first half of the year. The microdrama industry is estimated to generate $14 billion in revenue in 2026.
source.title: YouTube Launches Microdrama Series Feature Amid Industry Boom

source.summary: A coalition of heritage activists and historians in Udupi has launched a campaign to clean centuries-old inscriptions on stone slabs in Barkur, which have become obscured by algae, moss, and dust. Inaugurated by Dr DV Paramashivamurthy, the initiative involves weekly cleaning sessions starting on Sundays, with 175 college students already registered. Led by Prof T Murugeshi, the team uses water and soft brushes to reveal over 150 inscriptions spanning from the 11th to 17th centuries without damaging them. The project aims to document, publish, and display details of these records in Kannada next to the stones, ensuring public access to the historical narratives they contain while seeking shelter for the structures from weather exposure.
source.title: Historians Launch Sunday Campaign to Clean Barkur Temple Inscriptions

source.summary: China Energy Engineering Corp. announced a 15 GW solar module procurement program for 2026, the largest centralized tender by a Chinese state-owned enterprise this year. Meanwhile, Golden Solar New Energy Technology revised its 2026 fundraising plan, proposing to raise up to CNY 2.39 billion, primarily for an AI computing center in Beijing's Tongzhou district and debt repayment, reflecting financial challenges in the sector.
source.title: Chinese State-Owned Enterprises Launch Solar Procurement and M&A Deals

source.summary: A project named Operation Blue Skies is using AI to reduce contrail emissions, with Google involved. Contrails, formed by aircraft engines, are harmful to the environment. The initiative aims to minimize their generation. The episode also examines three approaches by manufacturers to promote healthy mobile phone use among children and adults, and explains how AI detectors function.
source.title: Google explores AI to reduce contrails' environmental impact

source.summary: NVIDIA reports that NIM optimizations for Nemotron 3 Ultra on 4xB200 hardware deliver up to 2.5x more users at 50 TPS/user compared to a baseline. The company states these gains come from validated configurations including precision tuning, parallel execution, and speculative decoding.
source.title: NVIDIA NIM Optimizations Deliver 2.5x More Users on Nemotron 3 Ultra

source.summary: Five advanced nuclear vendors will construct and operate more than 20 commercial microreactors at U.S. Army installations under the Janus Program. The Army selected BWXT Advanced Technologies, Radiant Industries, General Atomics Electromagnetic Systems, Antares Nuclear, and Westinghouse Government Services to deploy these units by 2028. The Department of War Innovation Unit negotiated fixed-price, milestone-based agreements totaling up to $2.2 billion through fiscal year 2031. These projects serve as anchor deployments intended to prove sustained operation and unlock broader commercial markets. Radiant Industries secured a binding agreement worth up to $750 million to deliver 15 Kaleidos units by 2030. BWXT will deploy a 20-MWe Advanced Nuclear Reactor at Fort Campbell, Kentucky, while other vendors target sites across Georgia, Texas, North Carolina, and New York. The Army declined to disclose an exact breakdown of the aggregate funding, noting that totals may change over time. Selected reactors range in output from 100 kWe to 20 MWe, utilizing various fuel strategies and targeting initial operations as early as 2028.
source.title: Five Companies Build 20 Microreactors for Army Under Janus Program

source.summary: Indian Defence Minister Rajnath Singh visited Colombo for a three-day trip, marking the first visit by an Indian defence chief in 38 years. During the meeting with President Anura Kumara Dissanayake, both leaders reaffirmed their partnership as civilisational twins and discussed regional security. The Ministry of Defence reported that the sides exchanged memorandums of understanding to upgrade six L70 guns for the Sri Lankan Air Force and to formalise youth exchange programmes between their National Cadet Corps. President Dissanayake reiterated Sri Lanka's commitment to not using its territory against India's security interests. Opposition leader Sajith Premadasa also met Singh, describing the relationship as very special and highlighting India's consistent support during crises like Cyclone Ditwah.
source.title: India's Defence Minister Rajnath Singh strengthens defence ties with Sri Lanka

source.summary: New Delhi is hosting the 18th BRICS Summit on September 12 and 13, with Russian Foreign Minister Sergey Lavrov already present and President Vladimir Putin scheduled to land tonight, according to ANI reports. The Ministry of External Affairs welcomed Brazilian Foreign Minister Mauro Vieira, while other leaders including Xi Jinping and Masoud Pezeshkian are expected to attend the two-day event under the theme 'Building for Resilience, Innovation, Cooperation and Sustainability'.
source.title: Delhi prepares for BRICS Summit 2026 as Lavrov and Putin arrive

source.summary: Donald Trump announced plans to appoint an AI tsar and create an AI Force to support the industry. He dismissed safety concerns regarding AI as a hoax and projected the sector could contribute up to 25% of the country's GDP. Trump stated he intends to keep the US leading in AI development against China and the rest of the world.
source.title: Trump Rejects AI Slowdown Calls and Launches New AI Force

source.summary: Delhi Police arrested activist Swatantra Bhardwaj in Bulandshahr and sent him to one-day custody regarding an alleged assault during the CJP agitation. CJP worker Nishu Aazad filed a complaint claiming her father was attacked at Jantar Mantar in July. Police registered an FIR under the SC/ST Act and the POCSO Act following the incident. Bhardwaj initially boasted about cracking the victim's skull but later claimed self-defence. Rahul Gandhi supported Aazad and questioned Prime Minister Narendra Modi and Home Minister Amit Shah regarding the case.
source.title: Delhi Police arrest activist Swatantra Bhardwaj in Bulandshahr over alleged assault

source.summary: Chinese and US delegations held economic and trade consultations in New York on Sunday. The two sides engaged in exchanges regarding important economic and trade issues of common concern. They also discussed the implementation of the consensus reached in previous talks. The meeting focused on maintaining dialogue and addressing shared economic priorities between the nations.
source.title: Chinese and US delegations hold economic and trade consultations in New York

source.summary: The Indian government has lifted the wheat export ban, effective immediately, to support farmers' income as domestic prices remain low. The decision follows earlier exports of 50 lakh tonnes of wheat and 10 lakh tonnes of products. Officials stated that allowing exports will raise domestic prices and encourage better sowing for the next rabi season. The Food Secretary noted that sufficient wheat stock is available to meet demand. India's wheat production hit a record 120.65 million tonnes in the 2025-26 crop year, with the FCI holding nearly 49 million tonnes in buffer stock.
source.title: Government lifts wheat export ban to boost farmers' income amid low domestic prices

source.summary: Huawei Digital Power showcased its latest "grid forming + AI" practices at the 4th International Digital Energy Expo in Shanghai from September 15 to 17, 2026. The company presented solutions for utility, grid-forming energy storage, smart microgrids, and AI data centers, highlighting innovations like the industry's first 1000VAC string inverter and a 11MW smart transformer station. Huawei also announced that its Smart I-V Curve Diagnosis solution passed the L5 certification on September 10, 2026, becoming the first to achieve this level.
source.title: Huawei Digital Power Unveils Grid-Forming and AI Solutions at IDEE 2026

source.summary: Physical Superintelligence launched a new startup with $58 million in funding led by Breakthrough Energy Ventures. Co-founder Matt Pines stated the company deploys AI physicists to solve physics challenges for data center efficiency. The team, named Emmy, uses hard verifiers to prevent AI errors. Early projects include optimizing a Texas data center and planning a probe to Alpha Centauri.
source.title: Physical Superintelligence launches AI physics lab to optimize data centers

source.summary: Lok Janshakti Party (Ram Vilas) filed a complaint at Parliament Police Station against influencer Swatantra Bhardwaj, alleging he falsely used Union minister Chirag Paswan's name. The party requested an FIR after Bhardwaj claimed political backing and alleged police inaction regarding an attack on Nishu Aazad's father. Chirag Paswan stated he takes full responsibility for ensuring justice for the victim's family. Bhardwaj was detained in Bulandshahr, Uttar Pradesh, after allegedly attempting to flee.
source.title: LJP(RV) seeks FIR against influencer for falsely using Chirag Paswan's name

source.summary: State-owned NTPC and EDF Power Solutions India have formed a 50:50 joint venture to develop pumped storage, hydropower, and other renewable energy projects in India and neighboring countries. The agreement was signed on September 25 in the presence of both companies' chairmen. Through this partnership, the entities aim to contribute to India's goal of 100 GW of pumped storage capacity by 2036.
source.title: NTPC and EDF Partner for Renewable Energy Projects in India

source.summary: The National Lok Adalat settled around 22,500 cases across Nellore district on Saturday, involving recoveries of approximately Rs 6 crore, according to the District Legal Services Authority. The event was guided by District Principal Judge Justice A. Narasimha Murthy and DLSA secretary Justice Y. J. Padmasri. Among the settlements, United India Insurance Company handed over a cheque for Rs 74 lakh to the family of a deceased motor accident victim. Additionally, a couple reconciled after approaching the Family Court for divorce. Narasimha Murthy stated that Lok Adalats provide a legally recognised platform to resolve disputes through mutual settlement rather than prolonged litigation.
source.title: National Lok Adalat settles 22,500 cases in Nellore district

source.summary: India has experienced a significant shift in its energy landscape over the last two years, where rapid renewable energy development has halted coal output growth. According to an analysis from the Centre for Research on Energy and Clean Air, coal production remains unchanged despite surging power demand. Since 2024, power sector emissions have stayed roughly flat as renewable energy, mostly solar, meets rising demand. Although India continues adding coal plants, overall carbon dioxide emissions ticked up in the first half of this year due to steel and cement production.
source.title: India's Rapid Solar Expansion Halts Coal Output Growth Amid Rising Power Demand

source.summary: Eight German state premiers from the Christian Democratic Union (CDU) have rallied behind Chancellor Friedrich Merz, rejecting speculation about his political future. They argue that restoring trust requires listening and taking action rather than debating personnel. Merz faces challenges as his approval ratings remain low while the far-right Alternative for Germany (AfD) party surges, particularly after winning a historic victory in Saxony-Anhalt. Despite rumors of a leadership swap, the premiers insist Germany needs a stable government with a parliamentary majority. The premiers, representing states like Bavaria, Berlin, and North Rhine-Westphalia, emphasize the need for stability as the party prepares for upcoming elections.
source.title: Eight German State Premiers Back Chancellor Merz Amid Speculation

source.summary: The United Kingdom has reaffirmed its unwavering support for Kosovo's sovereignty, independence, and territorial integrity following a war crimes verdict against former President Hashim Thaci. British Minister for Europe Lord Wood of Anfield emphasized that the judgment by the Kosovo Specialist Chambers concerns individuals and should not be used to inflame regional tensions. He called on political leaders to promote calm and ensure peaceful reactions, prioritizing people's safety during this significant moment.
source.title: UK Reaffirms Support for Kosovo Sovereignty Following War Crimes Verdict

source.summary: Senior BJP leader Tarun Chugh claimed that AAP MLA Sukhveer Singh Maiserkhana exposed the gap between the AAP government's claims of an education revolution and the reality in Punjab. Maiserkhana had accused the government of ignoring teacher shortages. Chugh highlighted inadequate school facilities and ongoing teacher protests, questioning the government's commitment to education and law and order.
source.title: BJP MP Tarun Chugh Accuses AAP of Education Revolution Failure

source.summary: ThreatDown researchers at Malwarebytes discovered Carbonato, a new botnet malware targeting insecure Docker hosts. The malware exploits unauthenticated Docker APIs to install the Hermes Agent AI framework, enabling operators to execute commands and collect credentials via Telegram. ThreatDown notes the agent interprets tasks and runs commands on victims. Researchers suggest Costa Rica as a possible operator location and recommend disabling exposed Docker APIs to prevent infection.
source.title: New Carbonato Malware Uses AI Agents to Hijack Docker Hosts

source.summary: Visual Capitalist reported that Tesla CEO Elon Musk earned $132.3 billion in 2025, topping a list of America's highest-paid CEOs. Figma CEO Dylan Field ranked second with $864 million, followed by Welltower CEO Shankh Mitra at $821 million and Opendoor CEO Kasra Nejatian at $741 million, according to data from Equilar and The New York Times.
source.title: America's Top CEOs Earned Record Compensation in 2025

source.summary: Two women have accused Saul Adamczewski of physical and emotional abuse, leading to his record label dropping him and tour dates being cancelled. One woman described being violently treated during her pregnancy, including being pushed, assaulted, and financially exploited. Another alleged victim reported multiple incidents of physical violence. Jessica Winter, a musician, claimed Adamczewski threatened her to silence her. Fat Possum, his label, terminated their partnership, and Insecure Men were removed from the label's roster. The band's festival and tour dates were also cancelled.
source.title: Two women accuse Saul Adamczewski of abuse after label drops him

source.summary: The September 2026 Ponder This puzzle asks participants to find a 35-term arithmetic progression within Loesch numbers with the smallest possible end. A bonus is awarded for finding a progression with at least 42 terms, while an extra bonus goes to those finding the longest progression overall.
source.title: Ponder This challenges readers to find short Loesch arithmetic progressions

source.summary: Shanghai Enflame Technology's stock price jumped 180% on its debut, with the IPO 6,000 times oversubscribed according to Nikkei. While Google's TPUs offer cost advantages over Nvidia GPUs, analysts note Nvidia remains central to the AI ecosystem.
source.title: Chinese chip firm Enflame surges 180% in IPO amid Nvidia competition

source.summary: Bosnia-Herzegovina is defined by a complex political structure established by the 1995 Dayton Peace Accords to end a war that killed approximately 100,000 people and displaced 2.2 million. The country divides power among a central government, the Brcko district, and two semi-autonomous entities: the Muslim-Croat Federation and Serb-run Republika Srpska. While the constitution recognizes three constituent peoples, ethnic nationalism often causes gridlock. Current tensions involve Republika Srpska leader Milorad Dodik, who pursues separatist ambitions, and Croatia's push for a third entity. Bosnia-Herzegovina seeks EU membership, but talks depend on reforms, and infrastructure funding for Republika Srpska remains suspended due to its rhetoric.
source.title: Bosnia-Herzegovina's Complex Structure and Separatist Tensions

source.summary: Poland's Energy Regulatory Office (URE) announced on September 22 that it will run seven price-only auctions from November 2 to November 10 for new renewable energy installations. The auctions aim to allocate support for more than 76 TWh of electricity, valued at nearly PLN 25 billion. A significant portion, 64.5 TWh, is reserved for photovoltaic and onshore wind projects, with 53.25 TWh specifically set aside for installations larger than 1 MW competing in a final auction on November 10. Bids will be assessed solely on price, adhering to a 2022 government regulation that caps annual auction volumes through 2027.
source.title: Poland Announces Large-Scale Renewable Energy Auctions for November

source.summary: Iceland's public broadcaster RUV reported that preliminary referendum results show a narrow majority supporting the reopening of EU membership negotiations. The vote count indicates 50.5% in favor and 49.5% against the proposal. Regional breakdowns reveal strong support in Reykjavik North and significant opposition in the Southern constituency. The campaign focused on cost of living, security, and fisheries control. A majority yes vote would mandate the government to resume talks, though final membership requires a second referendum.
source.title: Iceland referendum initial tally narrowly favors reopening EU accession talks

source.summary: The Nicaraguan parliament approved a constitutional amendment extending the terms of President Daniel Ortega and co-president Rosario Murillo until 2028. This move eliminates the November 2026 election and postpones the next vote. The ruling party justified the reforms by invoking the legacy of poet Rubén Darío. The amendment bans opposition figures deemed linked to coup attempts or foreign financing from public office. Opposition lawyer Juan Diego Barberena stated the reform prevents free choice among candidates. The change also extends terms for military and police leaders while granting the Supreme Electoral Council greater powers. Analysts suggest the regime aims to outlast the current US administration. The Organization of American States has paused a meeting to address the situation in Nicaragua.
source.title: Nicaraguan parliament extends Ortega and Murillo terms to 2028

source.summary: Oman plans to significantly expand its renewable energy capacity to support economic diversification and green transition goals. The government introduced new policies to encourage private investment in cleantech industries and achieve net-zero emissions by mid-century. Minister Salim Al Aufi emphasized the strategic importance of these plans for a sustainable low-carbon economy. The country aims to reduce carbon emissions by 33 per cent by 2035 through energy diversification and carbon capture projects. Oman intends to add approximately 5.7 GW of solar and over 2 GW of wind power by the end of the decade. Despite some withdrawals from green hydrogen projects, the nation continues to develop seven hydrogen projects with a combined output of one million tonnes annually by 2030.
source.title: Oman expands renewable energy capacity to diversify economy

source.summary: The UDF government in Kerala is facing political pressure following a series of controversies involving private sponsorship of ministerial perks. Former CPI(M) state secretariat member MB Rajesh questioned why private individuals are funding expensive benefits for ministers, highlighting three specific instances. These include Home Minister Ramesh Chennithala's US trip reportedly sponsored by a friend, Sports Minister OJ Janeesh's foreign travel, and Chief Minister VD Satheesan's privately sponsored chartered flight. While government sources and ministers argue that these arrangements did not burden the state exchequer, the opposition is demanding transparency regarding the sponsors and the propriety of such arrangements for public officials.
source.title: Kerala UDF Government Faces Scrutiny Over Private Sponsorship of Minister Perks

source.summary: A charity in Chancellor John Healey's constituency reports that working families earning just above benefit thresholds are struggling with the cost of living. Leomi White, project coordinator at Activate Rawmarsh, stated that these families receive no help despite working, with some paying £6 daily for breakfast clubs to afford employment. White urged the government to extend support to those living on a financial cliff-edge, noting that current schemes primarily assist those on benefits rather than working households.
source.title: Charity warns working families in Rawmarsh need more government help

source.summary: The NVIDIA OptiX Toolkit provides a GitHub repository containing utilities to help developers diagnose difficult issues in GPU ray tracing applications. The authors report that the toolkit supports consistent checking of OptiX and CUDA API error codes through macros like OTK_ERROR_CHECK. Additionally, the toolkit includes targeted device-side debug printing to isolate specific GPU-side bugs without overwhelming output. An example program, DemandPbrtScene, demonstrates how to use the DebugLocation mechanism for interactive, one-shot debug output. The code is licensed under a BSD 3-clause style license, allowing developers to copy and modify it for their own projects.
source.title: NVIDIA OptiX Toolkit Offers Debugging Utilities for Ray Tracing Applications

source.summary: The Reserve Bank of Australia faces growing pressure to raise interest rates for the fourth time this year, as July inflation exceeded expectations. Annual inflation rose to 3.5%, surpassing the forecast 3.3%, with underlying inflation remaining at 3.6%. Economists warn that without policy action, inflation may persist, with some predicting a rate hike as early as September. The decision to keep rates at 4.35% was unanimous, but board members acknowledged the need for further action. Rising construction costs and restaurant prices contributed to the inflationary pressures.
source.title: Reserve Bank faces pressure for fourth rate hike amid higher-than-expected inflation

source.summary: The Trump administration has agreed to pay nearly $4 billion to energy firms to abandon offshore wind leases, a move coastal states are now challenging in court. California became the eighth state to sue, arguing the practice jeopardizes state investments and jobs. The Department of the Interior returned $120 million to Golden State Wind in exchange for fossil fuel investments, a deal California Attorney General Rob Bonta calls "blatantly unlawful." Critics question the Interior Bureau of Ocean Energy Management's legal authority to refund lease funds and claim improper use of the federal Judgment Fund. Meanwhile, New York and six other states continue a separate legal challenge over a $795 million agreement with TotalEnergies. These actions represent a significant shift in federal energy policy that opponents say undermines clean energy development.
source.title: Trump administration offshore wind buyouts face legal challenges from coastal states

source.summary: Pennsylvania has reported its first measles deaths in 35 years, both occurring in unvaccinated individuals from Lancaster County. Health officials note a historic resurgence of measles in the U.S., with 2,777 confirmed cases in 2026. Dr. Paul Offit emphasized that measles is preventable with two doses of the MMR vaccine. Pennsylvania recorded 393 cases this year, while Maryland reported 31, mostly in unvaccinated residents. Officials warn that vaccine hesitancy, exacerbated by pandemic-related misinformation and a new Trump administration plan, is driving the outbreak.
source.title: Pennsylvania reports measles deaths linked to unvaccinated residents

source.summary: Jacques Moretti, owner of the Swiss bar Le Constellation where a New Year's fire killed 41 people, has been placed in pre-trial detention over alleged domestic abuse against his wife. The couple faces criminal investigation for manslaughter and arson by negligence. The alleged violence occurred in August at their home in Switzerland's Wallis canton, leading to Jessica Moretti's hospitalization. Their lawyers stated the incident is part of a separate private life investigation and emphasized it should not be conflated with the bar fire case.
source.title: Swiss bar owner faces pre-trial detention over alleged domestic abuse

source.summary: The US announced $3.6 million in humanitarian aid for Nepal, including food assistance for 10,000 households. The State Department stated that embassies in Nepal and China are assisting Americans and supporting relief efforts. Devastating floods along the Nepal-China border killed at least 675 people. Nearly 3,000 people remain missing, including 100 Americans and 589 foreign nationals.
source.title: US announces $3.6M humanitarian aid for Nepal floods

source.summary: Time Out magazine compiled a ranking of the world's most beautiful hotels based on visits by its experts. Ashford Castle in Ireland took the number one spot among 33 properties. The hotel features 83 rooms and a spa with a bronze conservatory. Other top European entries include Four Seasons Hotel Firenze and ION Adventure Hotel in Iceland.
source.title: Time Out ranks Ashford Castle in Ireland as the world's most beautiful hotel

source.summary: The world's first artificial energy island is set to begin construction, according to the project's developers. The initiative aims to generate renewable energy through offshore wind turbines. The island will serve as a hub for energy production and distribution. Developers report that all foundational work has been completed. The project is expected to significantly boost clean energy capacity globally.
source.title: World's First Artificial Energy Island Construction Begins

source.summary: The Hindu is releasing a limited commemorative edition for Gandhi Jayanthi, featuring rare archival pages from the October 2, 1969 edition and the 2003 feature, The Mahatma and The Hindu. This special edition traces Gandhiji’s journey from his early years in South Africa to India’s Independence, including archival photographs. The limited edition is available on Zepto across major Indian cities ahead of the festival.
source.title: The Hindu releases limited Gandhi Jayanthi commemorative edition

source.summary: About 20 Chinese rescue workers searched the Gyirong border crossing on Sunday for hundreds of people missing after a mudslide. The disaster followed a glacier collapse on August 26 that destroyed the main land port between China's Tibet and Nepal. Reuters and other agencies visited the site during the first foreign media trip organized by China's foreign ministry.
source.title: Rescue workers search for missing people at destroyed China-Nepal border port
