source.summary: At least 16 people were killed over the past 24 hours as Russia and Ukraine traded deadly drone and missile strikes, authorities from both countries said Saturday. The UN has warned of rising civilian deaths as Kyiv and Moscow ramp up long-range strikes on critical infrastructure. Ukrainian leader Volodymyr Zelensky said Russia was escalating every single day, while US President Donald Trump stated a deal to end the war was going to happen. Residents in Kyiv described the aftermath of a Russian drone attack on an apartment block, noting that everything was burning and the apartment was completely smashed up.
source.title: Russia and Ukraine Trade Deadly Air Strikes Killing at Least 16

source.summary: India's summer monsoon rainfall ended with a nearly 13% deficit, a shortfall classified as a drought. This marks the fourth lowest seasonal rainfall since 2001 and the 13th lowest since 1901. While the northeast monsoon provides significant rain for south Peninsular India, the overall southwest monsoon performance remains critically low.
source.title: India Records 13% Summer Monsoon Deficit Declared Drought

source.summary: Chief Justice of India Surya Kant stated that all parties are treated equally in the Supreme Court following allegations by senior advocate Gaurav Bhatia regarding delays in a defamation case against Rahul Gandhi. Bhatia, appearing for a complainant, claimed the matter was not listed due to the Opposition leader's status and alleged dilatory tactics. Advocate Prasanna S. objected to these submissions, prompting the Bench to advise Bhatia to submit an application for de-tagging the case. The court previously stayed proceedings based on a complaint filed by a retired Border Roads Organisation officer in August 2023.
source.title: CJI says all parties treated equally in Rahul Gandhi defamation case

source.summary: The S&P 500 faces potential crash risks as its Shiller CAPE ratio rises above 41, while inflation fears, Federal Reserve rate hike concerns, and Trump policies add pressure. The Motley Fool reports the CAPE ratio has crossed 35 only twice in 155 years, both times preceding major downturns. President Trump's tariffs could increase inflation, limiting the Federal Reserve's ability to cut rates or forcing them higher. CME Group's FedWatch tool indicates an 87% chance of a rate hike by year-end. US Treasury bond volatility also threatens highly valued stocks. However, the article notes a crash is not guaranteed if strong corporate earnings continue to lower forward price-to-earnings multiples.
source.title: High CAPE ratio, Fed rates and Trump tariffs raise S&P 500 crash risks

source.summary: The article compares relational and non-relational databases, highlighting their core differences and use cases. Relational databases use structured tables with enforced schemas and ACID properties, making them ideal for applications requiring data integrity, such as financial systems and healthcare records. Non-relational databases offer flexible data models and horizontal scalability, suitable for unstructured data and high-volume, distributed workloads like social media and IoT. The choice depends on whether structured data integrity or flexible scalability is prioritized. Relational databases scale vertically, while non-relational systems scale horizontally. The article emphasizes the need to evaluate data structure, consistency, and query patterns when selecting a database, suggesting polyglot persistence as a viable approach for complex applications.
source.title: Relational vs Non-Relational Databases: Trade-offs in Data Storage

source.summary: The UAE prosecutor general stated that a Flydubai co-pilot attempted a terrorist attack on a flight from the UAE to Israel. The co-pilot, identified as an Omani national, attacked the pilot with a crash axe before being subdued by passengers and crew. A reserve pilot took control and landed the aircraft in Saudi Arabia. Investigations are ongoing.
source.title: UAE Prosecutor General Says Flydubai Co-Pilot Attempted Terrorist Attack

source.summary: Finland is conducting its largest civil defense exercise since World War II, involving over 2,000 participants in Kuopio to rehearse responses to potential Russian attacks. The scenario simulates cyberattacks disrupting critical infrastructure and the threat of missile strikes from Russia. Retired Army Colonel Asko Muhonen stated that the exercise relies on the mindset of ordinary citizens ready to take responsibility for national security. Participants practiced using shelters designed to withstand nuclear or biological attacks, though officials note these offer limited protection against sabotage campaigns. The Finnish Security and Intelligence Service reported investigating various observations but found nothing of concern regarding recent drone sightings or GPS jamming. Veterans shared memories of past conflicts with the Soviet Union, highlighting the historical context of Finland's defense strategy. The event underscores the nation's preparedness to protect itself without external aid for at least 72 hours.
source.title: Finland conducts largest civil defense exercise in Europe since WWII

source.summary: Former Prime Minister John Howard spoke at the Australian National University regarding immigration and security, asserting that stopping terrorism cannot be achieved by simply stopping immigration categories. Meanwhile, One Nation leader Barnaby Joyce defended his party's policy allowing superannuation diversion for rent or mortgages, stating it would have a minute impact on inflation. Assistant Treasurer Daniel Mulino countered that unwinding the 12% superannuation guarantee is dangerous, while Independent MP Kate Chaney criticized the government's Major and Local Community Infrastructure Program as pork barrelling. Additionally, Nationals leader Matt Canavan expressed deep scepticism over new digital duty of care rules proposed by the government.
source.title: Former PM John Howard warns against limiting immigration; Barnaby Joyce defends super plan

source.summary: Electrified Thermal Solutions is developing a thermal storage system to help heavy industry electrify while reducing grid strain. The company's Joule Hive Thermal Battery uses specialized firebricks to store heat at temperatures up to 1,800 C. CEO Daniel Stack stated the system operates with greater than 98% efficiency and can beat natural gas costs where prices exceed $34.8 per MWh. The startup commissioned its first 20 MWh commercial system in Texas and has raised $24.3 million in funding.
source.title: Electrified Thermal Solutions develops firebrick batteries for industry

source.summary: Google has launched Gemini 3.7 Flash, an updated version of its Flash series, offering improved performance in coding, web development, and knowledge work. The model shows significant gains in debugging, code accuracy, and production-ready code generation, outperforming its predecessor, Gemini 3.6 Flash, in benchmarks like FrontierCode 1.1 and DeepSWE v1.1. It also excels in web development tasks and complex document processing. Priced at $0.75 per million input tokens and $3.75 per million output tokens, Gemini 3.7 Flash is available through the end of the year. Gemini Spark, a 24/7 AI agent, will use the new model to enhance efficiency in knowledge work and tool use for Google Workspace apps. The update includes safety improvements against misuse in CBRN and cyber domains.
source.title: Google Introduces Gemini 3.7 Flash with Enhanced Coding and Workflow Capabilities

source.summary: ACME Solar Holdings Limited announced the commissioning of a 15 MW/240.752 MWh battery energy storage system in Rajasthan on August 27, 2026. The facility, operated by ACME Suryodaya Private Limited, is located in Jaisalmer district and will achieve commercial operation on August 29, 2026. This addition brings the subsidiary's total commissioned capacity to 300 MW/1,354.224 MWh. The company filed the regulatory disclosure through its Company Secretary, Rajesh Sodhi, to comply with SEBI listing obligations.
source.title: ACME Solar commissions 15 MW battery storage project in Rajasthan

source.summary: Kerala general education minister N Shamsudheen announced that the United Democratic Front (UDF) leadership will decide on implementing the PM SHRI scheme following a request from the Union government. While the scheme aims to upgrade 14,500 schools and benefit 1.8 million students, the UDF holds reservations, viewing it as an ideological project of the BJP-RSS. The minister clarified that the chief minister will convey the final decision after internal discussions.
source.title: Kerala UDF to decide on PM SHRI scheme amid ideological concerns

source.summary: Mistral AI has updated its free generative assistant, le Chat, with several new capabilities currently available in beta. The company announced enhancements including web search with citations, a new Canvas interface for ideation, and improved document understanding powered by the Pixtral Large model. Users can now generate images via a partnership with Black Forest Labs and create automated agents for repetitive workflows. Mistral stated that all these features are offered as a free tier while they work toward premium options. The update aims to provide a fully integrated alternative to existing AI productivity tools.
source.title: Mistral AI adds web search and image generation to le Chat beta

source.summary: Airbound, a Bengaluru-based drone startup, raised $37 million in a Series A round led by Greenoaks, bringing its total funding to nearly $50 million. The investment will support scaling engineering, manufacturing, and market efforts. The company, which previously raised $8.65 million in a seed round, aims to build a drone delivery network across three cities in Andhra Pradesh and eventually operate 10,000 daily flights. Airbound's technology focuses on autonomous aircraft with a payload-to-aircraft weight ratio that challenges conventional designs. The funding reflects growing interest in deeptech companies with proprietary technology in India's startup ecosystem.
source.title: Airbound secures $37 million Series A led by Greenoaks for drone delivery expansion

source.summary: BRICS leaders met in New Delhi on Saturday for a summit addressing trade, investment, and global conflicts, hosted by Indian Prime Minister Narendra Modi. The gathering includes Russian President Vladimir Putin, Chinese President Xi Jinping, and Iranian President Masoud Pezeshkian, among others. The summit aims to discuss economic cooperation, energy, food security, and reducing reliance on the US dollar. However, the bloc faces challenges from ongoing wars in Ukraine and the Middle East, as well as rising US-China tensions, which test the group's ability to find common ground among members with competing geopolitical interests.
source.title: BRICS leaders meet in India amid global conflicts and US tensions

source.summary: Lisa described her upcoming solo EP Press Play as a cinematic project where each song has its own character and Thai elements. Speaking on The Tonight Show, she noted the EP reflects her journey from her roots to her current status. She also confirmed she will remain in Blackpink indefinitely despite a potential break, and is releasing a documentary titled Always Lalisa to inspire fans with her story.
source.title: Lisa Compares Solo EP to Movie and Shares Career Journey

source.summary: Amazon introduced a new agentic artificial intelligence service for third-party sellers on its main e-commerce site to expand automation features for listing and inventory management. Known as 'workflows,' the service runs continuously to handle seller prompts such as rating alerts and pricing monitoring. The optional service is free, and sellers can decide how much personal data they share with Amazon. Amazon's Mary Beth Westmoreland, vice president of worldwide selling experience, confirmed these details.
source.title: Amazon Launches Agentic AI Service for Third-Party Sellers

source.summary: Haier Europe CEO Neil Tunstall discussed the company's strategy to evolve from smart homes to intelligent homes at IFA 2026 in Berlin. Tunstall explained that Haier aims to build connected systems around people rather than individual products to make household tasks more intuitive. The company also emphasized sustainability, noting that efficient use of electricity and water is a major environmental impact area. Haier plans to invest 13 billion over the next five years in AI, robotics, and R&D to accelerate innovation. Tunstall stated the company does not intend to replace humans but will use robots for basic tasks alongside AI. He noted that while some technologies are currently concepts, Haier expects to launch several innovations to the market within the next year.
source.title: Haier CEO outlines intelligent home vision and 13 billion investment plan

source.summary: Patricia and James Poitras have launched a new fellowship program at MIT to support 50 graduate students and postdocs researching psychiatric disorders. The $10 million gift establishes two-year fellowships through the Poitras Center for Psychiatric Disorders Research, expanding the family's existing philanthropy which has exceeded $100 million. Robert Desimone, director of the McGovern Institute, noted the commitment to bold research transforming mental wellness. James Poitras emphasized the need to support young people driving progress, especially as federal funding becomes precarious. Five researchers form the inaugural cohort, with the next application window opening in May 2027. Patricia Poitras stated that investing in the next generation will accelerate discoveries leading to life-changing treatments.
source.title: Poitras Family Launches Fellowship Program at MIT

source.summary: The Federal Reserve Board released minutes from its discount rate meetings on June 8 and June 17, 2026. The documents detail the process used to determine discount rates for depository institutions through the discount window. The Board emphasized that this process differs from the Federal Open Market Committee's approach to setting the federal funds rate target range. The minutes were made public for release on July 14, 2026.
source.title: Federal Reserve Releases Discount Rate Meeting Minutes for June 2026

source.summary: Noida Power Company Limited invited bids on September 9, 2026, to procure 300 MW of round-the-clock renewable energy via a Build-Own-Operate model. The tender allows developers to combine solar, wind, and energy storage systems with a 25-year power purchase agreement subject to regulatory approval. Bidders must submit online bids by October 1, 2026, and meet specific financial qualification requirements including net worth and liquidity criteria. An electronic reverse auction will determine the final tariff after technical bids open on October 5.
source.title: NPCL invites bids for 300 MW round-the-clock renewable energy supply

source.summary: A disturbing TikTok trend featuring women pretending to harm infants has triggered fierce online backlash following the Lindsay Clancy murder trial. Social media users condemned the videos as sick and demented, with many calling the content evil and disgusting. The controversy intensifies an already heated debate surrounding the Massachusetts mother accused of killing her three children in January 2023. While Clancy admits to the killings but pleads not guilty by reason of lack of criminal responsibility, the case remains deeply polarizing. Jurors have yet to reach a unanimous decision after four days of deliberation, leaving the outcome uncertain. The trial continues to spark wider conversations about postpartum psychosis and the limits of criminal responsibility for defendants with severe mental illness.
source.title: TikTok Trend of Mothers Pretending to Harm Babies Sparks Outrage Amid Lindsay Clancy Trial

source.summary: Cameroon's soccer federation president Samuel Eto'o supports FIFA president Gianni Infantino, attributing criticism of the Swiss-Italian leader to the timing of his 2027 re-election. Eto'o told CNN that opposition to Infantino stems from the upcoming election, not his policies. While UEFA, AFC, and CONCACAF consider a no-confidence vote, African body CAF continues to back Infantino. CAF president Patrice Motsepe stated Infantino's future should be decided in 2027. Eto'o praised Infantino for expanding opportunities in football, arguing that the voices against him do not represent the majority of FIFA's 211 members.
source.title: Cameroon's Eto'o defends Infantino amid FIFA election tensions

source.summary: A family alleges they were assaulted by staff at Swarnamoyee Beach Resort in Mandarmani, West Bengal, following a parking dispute. Mohammad Asif stated that employees, security, and the manager attacked them after they parked to inspect a room. Several family members, including women and an elderly person, were reportedly injured. The Mandarmani Coastal Police detained the hotel manager and an employee for questioning. A viral video of the incident has raised concerns about tourist safety in the coastal town.
source.title: Tourists Allegedly Assaulted by Resort Staff in West Bengal Over Parking

source.summary: Recent disturbing claims regarding the capacity of superintelligent AI to destroy the planet have drawn attention from industry figures. Anthropic reported that various actors have used its models to design weapons and create pathogens, while Elon Musk claimed AI could be more dangerous than nuclear weapons. In response, a team of technology reporters from The Guardian is hosting a live Q&A session to address public questions about AI risks, the fairness of current coverage, and whether benefits are being overshadowed by scare stories.
source.title: Media outlets invite public questions on AI safety fears and industry warnings

source.summary: Advanced Micro Devices announced an agreement to acquire Fei-Fei Li's startup, World Labs, in a deal valued at $8.2 billion. The San Francisco-based company, which raised $1 billion earlier this year, develops spatial-intelligence models. Fei-Fei Li will join AMD as executive vice president and chief scientist, reporting to Lisa Su. The transaction is expected to close by the end of 2026.
source.title: AMD Agrees to Acquire Fei-Fei Li's World Labs for $8.2 Billion

source.summary: Tata Sons, the holding company of the Tata Group, is scheduled to hold a board meeting on Thursday to deliberate its next steps after the Reserve Bank of India rejected its request for exemption from mandatory listing requirements. The company's Nomination and Remuneration Committee is expected to recommend that Chairman N Chandrasekaran continue in his role, according to a report by CNBC TV18. The proposal was reportedly added to the board meeting agenda shortly before the meeting.
source.title: Tata Sons Board to Discuss RBI Listing Rejection and Chairman's Future Amid Governance Debate

source.summary: The Delhi High Court criticized Delhi University for providing a vague response regarding additional hostel facilities during hearings on the Satya Niketan building collapse. The court noted a discrepancy between the university's reported 5,698 hostel residents and the 1.3 lakh students attending classes. Solicitor General Tushar Mehta reported that a magisterial inquiry and a high-powered committee have been constituted to examine the incident and student safety measures.
source.title: Delhi High Court Criticizes Delhi University Over Hostel Shortage Response

source.summary: A large-scale reproduction challenge of 2,200 ICML 2026 papers revealed significant issues with reproducibility. The initiative, involving 2,962 cloud jobs, found that 51% of papers had at least one verified claim, with 266 fully reproduced and 632 partially reproduced. However, 23% of papers had at least one falsified or contested claim, including 49 papers where all claims were falsified and 242 where independent teams reached opposing verdicts. The challenge highlighted the limitations of AI agents in reproducing complex claims, with some errors stemming from arithmetic mistakes or misinterpretations. Human oversight was crucial, as agents occasionally failed to detect issues due to premature stopping or misreading scale-dependent behavior. The results underscore the need for human involvement in scientific review, as agents alone cannot fully replace the nuanced judgment of human reviewers.
source.title: ICML 2026 Reproduction Challenge Reveals 51% of Papers Verified, 23% Falsified

source.summary: Zomato has directed restaurant partners to stop serving analogue dairy products, requiring them to replace such items with natural dairy or remove the dishes from their menus. The platform asked partners to verify supplier labels and ingredient declarations to prevent consumer confusion. Analogue paneer mimics traditional dairy in appearance but replaces milk components with non-dairy ingredients like vegetable oils and plant proteins. While not inherently unsafe, these products may differ nutritionally and mislead customers expecting conventional dairy. The Food Safety and Standards Authority of India has also emphasized proper identification of such products to avoid misleading consumers. Maharashtra recently imposed a one-year ban on artificial paneer after samples failed safety standards. Zomato's move highlights the importance of transparency in food labeling and ingredient disclosure.
source.title: Zomato bans analogue paneer to ensure accurate dairy labeling

source.summary: Blueleaf Energy and Universal Peak announced the financial close of a 100MW/400MWh battery storage project in Malaysia on September 1. The joint venture partners signed agreements with Tenaga Nasional Berhad in June, targeting mid-2027 commissioning for the utility-scale battery energy storage system. The project was selected in the inaugural MyBeST tender launched by the Energy Commission in November 2024. Financial terms were not disclosed, though the signing ceremony took place in Singapore with major bank UOB.
source.title: Blueleaf Energy and Universal Peak close financing for Malaysia BESS project

source.summary: The Supreme Court questioned a Greater Noida executive magistrate for issuing a notice to student Akshat Tripathi regarding his participation in the Cockroach Janta Party protest. Chief Justice of India Surya Kant expressed surprise, stating the court had previously ordered that no coercive action be taken against students. The bench directed the lawyer to place the notice on record and seek an explanation from the authority. Senior Advocate Bishwajit Bhattacharyya argued the move constituted contempt of court, even after the notice was withdrawn.
source.title: Supreme Court seeks explanation from Greater Noida magistrate over student protest notice

source.summary: Japan plans to support pipelines bypassing the Strait of Hormuz to reduce reliance on Middle Eastern oil, according to Cabinet Office documents. The strategy aims to enhance supply security by diversifying procurement sources and supporting shipping costs. Prime Minister Sanae Takaichi noted the shift in energy dynamics post-U.S.-Iran conflict. Japan previously sourced over 90% of its crude from the Middle East, forcing refiners to seek alternatives. The plan includes strengthening JOGMEC's risk-financing capabilities and securing insurance for oil shipments.
source.title: Japan Aims to Develop Pipelines Bypassing Hormuz to Diversify Energy Supplies

source.summary: Israeli media reports indicate Greece is set to sign a $3.6 billion agreement Monday for three air defense systems. The Jerusalem Post stated a Greek delegation will finalize the deal in Tel Aviv after nearly three years of talks. The contract includes David's Sling, Spyder, and Barak MX systems to bolster Greece's Achilles Shield network. Israeli firms Rafael and Israel Aerospace Industries are expected to supply the hardware, while Greek companies will receive approximately $820 million in work. The project, reported by Calcalist and Yedioth Ahronoth, involves a command-and-control network using artificial intelligence and will be implemented in stages over roughly 35 months. Kathimerini also reported the deal's value and timing. Neither Greece nor Israel has officially confirmed the agreement as of Sunday evening.
source.title: Greece set to sign $3.6B deal for three Israeli air defense systems

source.summary: IBM Research introduces a new approach to cryptographic agility by proposing an abstraction layer that separates cryptographic decisions from application code. Developers currently manage complex security operations manually, embedding algorithm choices directly into code, which leads to fragile systems and technical debt. The proposed solution, inspired by filesystems and networking abstractions, aims to centralize cryptographic policy and allow runtime enforcement of security decisions. The initiative includes an intent-based API that defines cryptographic scopes, enabling interchangeable algorithms within defined categories. This shift would transform cryptography from a development concern to an operational one, managed by security teams. IBM has released an API specification and a partial reference implementation, inviting the community to test and refine the approach. The work is framed as a necessary evolution in response to post-quantum cryptography (PQC) adoption, which requires significant system rearchitecture. The goal is to create a sustainable framework that reduces developer burden and enables future cryptographic changes without code modifications.
source.title: IBM Research proposes cryptographic abstraction layer to simplify security operations

source.summary: Researchers Almås, Haushofer, and Kjelsrud report that randomised cash transfers in rural Kenya significantly increase food spending and calorie intake among very poor households. The authors note that conventional correlational methods overstate these nutritional responses compared to experimental data. Their analysis indicates that a 10% budget increase raises food spending by about 8.6% and calories by 6.5%, while also improving diet quality through higher spending on meat, fish, and dairy. The study concludes that while transfers improve nutrition, they may not alone escape a poverty trap without substantial productivity gains. Policymakers are advised to rely on experimental estimates rather than correlational ones when designing transfer programmes.
source.title: Kenya study finds cash transfers improve nutrition more than correlational methods suggest

source.summary: U.S. President Donald Trump rejected an Iranian proposal to reopen the Strait of Hormuz within a week. Iran's President Masoud Pezeshkian and Foreign Minister Abbas Araghchi stated the plan involved a ceasefire and meeting U.S. demands regarding sanctions and assets. Trump expressed skepticism about Tehran's willingness to comply and indicated potential renewal of bombing campaigns. The strait remains central to the ongoing stalemate between the two nations.
source.title: Trump Rejects Iran's Proposal to Reopen Hormuz Strait

source.summary: European Commission President Ursula von der Leyen stated that the Leipzig drone attack represents a new escalation on European soil directly attributed to Russia. She vowed to close loopholes exploited by Moscow and cut deeper into Russia's war chest. Following the incident, Germany closed the Russian Consulate in Bonn and terminated a lease in Berlin, while France, Belgium, Portugal, and the Netherlands summoned Russian ambassadors. Political analyst Alexander Astrov noted that Europe must respond to Russia's hybrid actions while remaining within international law. Von der Leyen confirmed Ukraine has requested PAC-3 Patriot air defense systems, which member states are currently reviewing. EU officials also discussed restricting Schengen tourist visas for Russian nationals and proposed sanctions against 1,600 individuals and companies involved in Russia's defense sector.
source.title: EU Vows Tougher Russia Measures After Leipzig Drone Attack

source.summary: A study in Ethiopia examined how community leaders target beneficiaries for social assistance under budget constraints and varying rules. The research found that when budgets were halved, leaders primarily reduced transfer sizes rather than excluding households, maintaining coverage at around 80%. Granting leaders discretion over selection criteria allowed them to better reach poor and conflict-affected households compared to rigid rule-based approaches, though it also increased inclusion errors. The study suggests that while discretion reduces favouritism, it relies on leaders' broader definitions of need, which may include vulnerability factors not captured by standard poverty lines.
source.title: Ethiopian Community Leaders Prioritize Coverage Over Transfer Size During Budget Cuts

source.summary: India is approaching a significant intergenerational wealth transfer estimated at US$1.3-1.5 trillion over the next decade, prompting a shift in investment strategies among High Net-worth Individuals (HNIs). According to a Julius Baer-EY study, family offices are moving from founder-centric decision-making toward formal family constitutions and professional management. Next-generation investors are diversifying portfolios across listed equities, fixed income, private markets, and global assets, with a strategic range suggesting 40-45% allocation to alternatives. However, experts caution that private market returns show substantial dispersion and advise looking beyond headline IRRs to metrics like DPI and TVPI. Additionally, while pre-IPO investing is becoming meaningful, the gap between private and public valuations has narrowed, making it less of a standalone investment thesis. Experts recommend a neutral view on equities, favoring selective exposure to structural growth themes while maintaining global diversification to reduce dependence on a single economy.
source.title: India's Next-Gen HNIs Shift Wealth Strategies Amid Intergenerational Transfer

source.summary: The Bharatiya Janata Party government in West Bengal faces criticism after Chief Minister Suvendu Adhikari hosted religious preacher Dhirendra Krishna Shastri, who advocated against selling non-vegetarian food near Durga Puja pandals. While BJP leader Samik Bhattacharya dismissed the call as a personal opinion and affirmed that Bengalis retain the right to eat meat and fish, the administration has implemented other regulatory changes. These measures include banning DJ music, restricting crane usage during idol immersion, and designating Ashtami as a dry day. Additionally, the government has altered financial support rules for large-scale pujas, requiring local authority applications for state assistance. The controversy highlights tensions between traditional dietary practices and new administrative directives during the festival.
source.title: West Bengal BJP government restricts Durga Puja traditions amid vegetarianism debate

source.summary: The World Health Organisation has updated temporary recommendations for member states amid the ongoing Ebola outbreak in the Democratic Republic of Congo. The DRC is classified as the only country at 'very high' risk, with neighboring nations like Burundi and the Central African Republic rated 'high risk'. The WHO chief noted the outbreak is spreading faster than any previous one and remains a public health emergency of international concern. Congolese authorities reported 5514 confirmed cases and 2690 deaths, resulting in a 47.9 percent fatality rate.
source.title: WHO updates Ebola recommendations as DRC outbreak spreads

source.summary: Former Google engineer Linwei Ding received a sentence of nearly one year in prison for stealing the company's artificial intelligence trade secrets. US District Judge Vince Chhabria described the theft as a systematic effort to steal Google's property. Although Ding was initially convicted of economic espionage, the judge overturned that charge due to insufficient evidence. Prosecutors alleged Ding transferred over 500 confidential files to his personal account and intended to benefit Chinese technology firms. Ding established a new company in China, Zhisuan, which claimed experience with Google's computational platforms. The judge rejected a request for home confinement, ordering Ding to pay over $189,000 in restitution and a $25,000 fine. Ding will also serve two years of supervised release.
source.title: Ex-Google engineer Linwei Ding sentenced to nearly a year for stealing AI trade secrets

source.summary: The European Commission published terms for its second Europe-wide auction to decarbonize industrial process heat, earmarking EUR 1 billion for the Innovation Fund 2026. The auction, launching in December 2026, supports electrified technologies, renewable heat, and nuclear options. It lowers the temperature threshold to 80 degrees Celsius and builds on a pilot that selected 65 proposals. The initiative aims to boost clean energy investment and reduce emissions.
source.title: EU Commission launches EUR 1 billion auction for industrial heat decarbonization

source.summary: President Donald Trump has posted multiple AI-generated images pairing himself with George Washington on Truth Social. Angelo Carusone of Media Matters suggests these posts aim to project Trump as a founder comparable to Washington. A White House spokesperson defended the platform as Trump's authentic voice. The images appear designed to bolster his legacy while facing tough questions about his administration.
source.title: Trump posts AI images with Washington amid political challenges

source.summary: Wheat futures on the Chicago Board of Trade hit their daily limit and reached multi-year highs as Russia's potential escalation of missile strikes on Kyiv raised concerns over Black Sea grain exports. Corn and soybean contracts also reached life-of-contract highs, driven by spillover effects from wheat's surge and poor U.S. corn yield expectations. The USDA reported a sharper-than-expected decline in U.S. corn crop conditions, further supporting prices. China's continued soybean purchases and recovering crude oil prices also contributed to soybean gains.
source.title: Black Sea tensions drive wheat to daily limit, corn hits lifetime highs

source.summary: New research indicates that giraffe populations in South Sudan maintain high genetic diversity and connectivity despite decades of conflict. While numbers have dropped significantly, the White Nile River does not block gene flow. Experts note the area remains relatively stable for wildlife, though political instability remains a concern for long-term conservation.
source.title: Research Shows Giraffes Thrive in South Sudan Despite Conflict

source.summary: WhatsApp has launched a new bill payments feature in India, allowing users to pay for electricity, water, gas, FASTag, insurance, and other bills directly within the app. The feature is currently rolling out gradually and is not yet available to all users. To use it, users must tap the rupee icon on the home screen to access the Bill Payments option. The feature is integrated with the Bharat Connect (BBPS) network, meaning only bills from providers on this network can be paid. Users select their bill category, choose the service provider, and enter their customer number to view and pay the bill amount.
source.title: WhatsApp launches bill payments feature in India for electricity and more

source.summary: OpenAI announced on Tuesday that an unreleased artificial intelligence model solved the Navier-Stokes problem, one of the seven Millennium Prize Problems, in just 88 hours. The company stated it utilized millions of dollars in computing power to demonstrate that the equations describing fluid motion are fatally flawed. However, mathematician Tristan Buckmaster and researcher Levent Alpoge from rival firm Anthropic claim OpenAI only pursued the challenge after discovering their own AI-assisted efforts. While OpenAI denies using the rivals' specific proofs, it acknowledged on X that de-identified data from their products might have helped improve its models. Professor Martin Bridson of the Clay Mathematics Institute emphasized that the evaluation process remains deliberately unhurried and rigorous before any prize is awarded.
source.title: OpenAI claims AI solved Navier-Stokes problem while rivals dispute credit

source.summary: ZDNET compares the Pixel Watch 5 and Pixel Watch 4, highlighting the new model's faster processor and expanded storage for AI features like Raise to Talk and Smart Replies. The Watch 5 also features improved GPS for route tracking, which Google claims outperforms competitors. Battery life remains largely unchanged between the two models, with only a minor increase in the larger 45mm version. While the Watch 5 offers some upgrades, ZDNET suggests the older model may still be a better value, especially for users not requiring the new AI capabilities.
source.title: Pixel Watch 5 offers faster performance and AI features compared to Pixel Watch 4

source.summary: MIT researchers have developed a new method to accurately model metal alloys using machine learning. The team improved simulations by creating training datasets that capture diverse atomic environments in chemically disordered materials. This approach allows for faster and more accurate predictions of material properties compared to traditional brute-force methods. The researchers demonstrated their technique on various metal alloys, showing it could predict phase diagrams that closely match experimental data. Senior author Rodrigo Freitas noted the method could be adapted for other materials like semiconductors. The work aims to make material design more efficient for industries such as aerospace and energy.
source.title: MIT researchers create faster machine-learning models for metal alloys

source.summary: Campaigning for the Nagaon Lok Sabha bypoll in Assam concluded on Sunday, with major parties expressing strong confidence in their prospects. The BJP, led by Chief Minister Himanta Biswa Sarma, predicts a victory margin of 2.5 to 3 lakh votes, despite acknowledging the constituency's Muslim majority. Conversely, Congress state president Gaurav Gogoi claims the party will win again, citing BJP's alleged atrocities against minorities. The AIUDF, led by Badruddin Ajmal, also asserts a high probability of victory, estimating a margin of around 1 million votes. Voting is scheduled for October 6, with results expected on October 9. Sixteen candidates are contesting the election.
source.title: Campaigning Ends for Nagaon LS Bypoll with High Confidence from BJP and Congress

source.summary: Tech companies are exploring space-based AI data centers to solve power and cooling challenges on Earth. Proponents argue that solar energy in orbit is continuous and more powerful than on Earth. Jeff Bezos and Elon Musk have championed the concept, with Google recently launching test units into orbit. However, critics note that the economics remain daunting and some advantages may not hold up under scrutiny.
source.title: Tech Companies Race to Build AI Data Centers in Space

source.summary: Italy's government passed a decree on September 24, 2026, limiting classrooms to 30% of students with limited Italian skills and banning full-face Islamic veils. Premier Giorgia Meloni stated the measures aim to foster integration. The rules affect approximately 1,000 classrooms nationwide and require parliamentary endorsement within 60 days. Critics, including educators and opposition parties, argue the policy lacks resources and consultation, potentially forcing students to travel far. The Education Minister defends the plan as a necessary step for language acquisition and educational support.
source.title: Italy Decrees Limits on Non-Italian Speakers and Veils in Schools

source.summary: Constellation Energy and Amazon.com announced a 20-year power purchase agreement to support the Calvert Cliffs nuclear plant in Maryland. The deal includes over $3 billion in infrastructure investment and 190 megawatts of new capacity coming online between 2030 and 2032. Amazon's commitment aims to support the plant's license renewal and expansion to meet growing demand for dependable power from technology companies.
source.title: Constellation and Amazon Sign 20-Year Deal for Maryland Nuclear Plant

source.summary: Florida officials identified five people killed in Saturday's Amazon cargo plane crash at Miami International Airport, with two others remaining in critical condition. Miami-Dade Sheriff Rosie Cordero-Stutz confirmed the identities of the deceased and noted that both pilots had been released from the hospital. The National Transportation Safety Board continues its investigation into the accident, which occurred after a thunderstorm. NTSB Chair Jennifer Homendy described the scene as 'utter devastation' and indicated that factors such as weather, mechanical conditions, and pilot decisions are under review. Aviation attorney Robert Clifford suggested the crash might stem from a tailwind landing mistake. Amazon stated it would cooperate with federal investigators.
source.title: Florida officials identify five killed in Amazon cargo plane crash

source.summary: Airbus awarded Mahindra Aerostructures a contract to manufacture A320 fuselage skins in Bengaluru. The deal covers eight skins for Section 18 and three for Section 19, with final delivery targeted for 2028. Airbus stated the partnership strengthens India's role in global aerospace manufacturing. Mahindra will expand capabilities through advanced chemical milling and stretch-forming production lines. Airbus currently sources over $1.6 billion annually from India.
source.title: Airbus awards A320 fuselage skin manufacturing contract to Mahindra Aerostructures

source.summary: The Hoesly family in southwest Wisconsin has permanently protected nearly 2,000 acres of floodplain land after decades of farming became unviable due to frequent flooding and a 2016 state tax change. As reported by The Daily Cardinal, the family chose conservation easements and land donations over continued drainage projects. Partners include the Wisconsin Department of Natural Resources and nonprofit groups. The land will be restored to native forest and wetlands, removing levees to reconnect the river. This agreement serves as a model for addressing climate-driven flooding and habitat loss through private-public cooperation.
source.title: Wisconsin farm family protects 2,000 floodplain acres from farming

source.summary: Early results from Brazil's presidential election indicate Senator Flavio Bolsonaro is ahead of President Luiz Inacio Lula da Silva. With 10% of ballots processed, Bolsonaro received 51% of the vote compared to Lula's 40.8%. Final results are expected within hours as electronic voting machines tally the remaining ballots. The election pits Lula's Workers' Party platform against Bolsonaro's right-wing populist movement.
source.title: Early Brazil Election Count Shows Bolsonaro Leading Lula

source.summary: G7 leaders agreed to release 100 million barrels from emergency oil reserves over four months to address surging energy prices, coordinated through the International Energy Agency. Simultaneously, FlyDubai suspended flights to Tel Aviv following a cockpit incident. In France, student protests led to hundreds of school closures and mass arrests. Other headlines include a Russian drone strike in Kyiv, diplomatic rifts between Eritrea and Ethiopia, and a UN forecast that women face disproportionate food insecurity risks. The US unemployment rate rose to 4.2% in September, while Euro area inflation accelerated to 3.8%.
source.title: G7 Releases Oil Reserves Amid Global Tensions and Protests

source.summary: John Crace writes that John Healey's debut as chancellor was a disappointing performance characterized by silence and a lack of conviction. The author notes Healey arrived 15 minutes late and appeared nervous, struggling to project the strength required for the role. Crace argues that Healey's speech offered little new information, merely repeating fiscal discipline and manifesto promises already established by Rachel Reeves. The columnist suggests Healey is better suited for crisis announcements than delivering optimistic messages, which die on his lips. Furthermore, Crace observes that the wider government seemed silenced during the event, with the home secretary notably absent. Ultimately, the article portrays Healey as ill-equipped for the job, leaving the public and markets in a state of uncertainty.
source.title: John Crace criticizes John Healey's unconvincing and boring first speech as chancellor

source.summary: The author argues that rewriting software to eliminate technical debt frequently fails because the old system remains active while the new one is incomplete. They note that developers on the legacy code lack incentive to improve it, while new teams struggle with unknown scope. The result is often two production systems instead of one. The author recommends automated testing and targeted refactors over full replacements.
source.title: Author argues rewriting code often fails due to dual system risks

source.summary: A Centre for Science and Environment report states Delhi had just one 'Good' air quality day during the 92-day monsoon season. Despite heavy rainfall, pollution rebounded within 48 hours. Executive director Anumita Roychowdhury attributes this to dangerously high baseline emissions, warning that nature's washout cannot manage the crisis without year-round action to cut emissions at their source.
source.title: Delhi Recorded Only One Good Air Day During Monsoon

source.summary: Banka Superintendent of Police Amitesh Kumar confirmed that three youths were detained following a viral video showing a minor girl allegedly harassed and assaulted at Mandar Hill. Preliminary investigations indicated the youths took Rs 1,500 from the victim via PhonePe. An FIR was registered under sections of the Bharatiya Nyaya Sanhita and the Information Technology Act. The SP stated further details would be disclosed after a thorough investigation.
source.title: Police Detain Three Youths Over Viral Video Showing Minor Harassment in Banka

source.summary: Manish Chandi, a tribal expert, discusses threats facing isolated communities in the Andaman and Nicobar Islands during an interview with Mongabay. He highlights encroachment by trawlers in North Sentinel Island's buffer waters and a planned development project in Great Nicobar that overlaps with Shompen hunting grounds. Chandi notes that while some tribes like the Sentinelese live in voluntary isolation, others have varying levels of contact. He argues that government misunderstanding and poor law enforcement lead to resource exploitation and increased dependence on external supplies. Litigation regarding the Great Nicobar project is ongoing as of August 2026, with Chandi asserting the project will have severe negative results without tribal consent. He calls for administrative machinery to respect tribal autonomy and shift from curiosity to appreciation.
source.title: Expert Warns of Threats to Isolated Tribes in Andaman Islands

source.summary: A Massachusetts jury is deliberating the first-degree murder charges against Lindsay Clancy, who is accused of killing her three children. Clancy's attorney argues she suffered from postpartum psychosis, while prosecutors claim she made a calculated decision to murder them. The jury must decide between a life sentence without parole, lesser murder charges, or a finding of not guilty by reason of insanity. Closing arguments highlighted conflicting views on Clancy's mental state and her suicide attempt.
source.title: Massachusetts jury deliberates on first-degree murder charges against mother Lindsay Clancy

source.summary: Core Power and the US Maritime Administration signed a Memorandum of Cooperation to develop nuclear propulsion for commercial shipping. The agreement aims to create a commercial pathway by addressing regulatory, operational, and financial challenges. Core Power emphasizes the need for a complete system that is safe, licensable, and operable at fleet scale. The collaboration follows a Request for Information on system-centric nuclear power approaches. The initiative seeks to position the US as a global maritime power, leveraging its nuclear expertise and allied shipbuilding capacity. The partnership also aligns with the US government's strategy to strengthen maritime dominance and energy security.
source.title: Core Power and US Maritime Administration collaborate on nuclear propulsion for commercial shipping

source.summary: This article explores the precarious lives of fisherfolk in Chennai's Kasimedu harbor through the stories of three individuals. Pavadairayan, a 60-year-old basket man, describes the grueling physical labor of transporting fish in the dark for about $5 a day, noting that supervisors can fine workers thousands of rupees if fish go missing. Nandu Kumar, a former smuggler turned fisherman, lost his family to the dangers of the sea before finding stability selling fish with his sons' support. Bhagat Singh, a researcher, highlights the economic instability of the community, where families face poverty from bad catches or illness with no safety nets. Despite these hardships, many younger fishermen return to the sea, drawn by an enduring connection to their heritage.
source.title: Fishermen in Chennai Harbor Face Precarious Working Conditions and Economic Instability

source.summary: Accenture, in partnership with Greater Chennai Corporation and Farmers for Forests, is supporting the development of a 15-acre Eco Action & Learning Hub in Manali, Chennai, focused on wetland restoration. This is the third such hub in India, following projects in Manchar and Nrityagram. The hub will offer environmental education, community engagement, and activities like guided tours and sustainability workshops. Accenture's Senior Country Managing Director, Ajay Vij, emphasized the importance of education in fostering environmental responsibility.
source.title: Accenture supports 15-acre Eco Action Hub for wetland restoration in Chennai

source.summary: U.S. inflation increased 3.7% in July, exceeding expectations, as Wall Street's main indexes closed nearly flat. Investors remained cautious ahead of Nvidia's earnings, which could provide insights into AI demand. The Federal Reserve faces heightened pressure with upcoming data, and the September meeting has a 38.1% chance of a rate hike. The S&P 500 and Nasdaq Composite ended slightly lower, while the Dow Jones fell 0.21%. Nvidia shares declined ahead of its report, and Intuit's stock dropped after a revenue forecast below expectations.
source.title: U.S. inflation rises 3.7% as markets await Nvidia earnings

source.summary: An investor argues that holding Nvidia stock remains justified despite a high price-to-sales ratio of 17. The author points to the company's rapid revenue growth and dominant position in artificial intelligence as key reasons. Nvidia recently reported a second quarter with revenue up 106% year over year to $96 billion. The company also announced a $12.9 billion acquisition of AI specialist Hugging Face. CEO Jensen Huang stated that AI has reached an inflection point with accelerating demand.
source.title: Author Defends Nvidia Stock Despite High Valuation Citing Growth

source.summary: A retired Delhi Police officer filed a plea in the Supreme Court seeking restrictions on the CJP's planned September 5 protest march in New Delhi. The petition requests that no processions occur in security-sensitive areas without prior police permission. Delhi Police noted they received no formal request for the march from India Gate to their headquarters. The filing aims to prevent large-scale mobilizations in zones like the Central Vista without requisite approvals.
source.title: Retired officer files SC plea to curb CJP protest march in Delhi

source.summary: Preparations are underway for the centenary of the Samastha Kerala Jamiyyathul Ulama, scheduled for January 28 to 31, 2027, at Wadi Haramayn. The four-day event will focus on social empowerment, covering children, youth, and senior citizens. Plans include 630 Tasqiya conferences in Kerala, discussions at 130 centres on over 100 social issues, and support from the Sunni Students Federation's 25,000 members.
source.title: Samastha Kerala Jamiyyathul Ulama prepares for 2027 centenary

source.summary: Anthropic CEO Dario Amodei stated the company aims for a positive-sum evolution rather than destroying traditional software firms. This comment addressed Wall Street fears following a market drop dubbed the 'SaaSpocalypse' that erased $1 trillion in value. Salesforce reported strong recovery and deepened AI integration with Anthropic. Meanwhile, Palantir CEO Alex Karp warned enterprises to protect proprietary data when using AI providers.
source.title: Anthropic CEO Dario Amodei reassures investors about enterprise software

source.summary: The article highlights suicide as a major global health crisis affecting millions annually. It notes that World Suicide Prevention Day was established in 2003 by the International Association for Suicide Prevention and the World Health Organization. The 2024–26 theme, 'Changing the Narrative on Suicide,' calls for challenging myths and reducing stigma through open dialogue. It urges governments and institutions to prioritize mental health in public policy.
source.title: World Suicide Prevention Day urges open conversations to end stigma

source.summary: Users of the Apple Watch Series 12 and Ultra 4 report random restarts caused by a Neural Engine timeout. Apple has released watchOS 27.0.1 to address this issue. The update is currently limited to these models. Users can install the patch via the Watch app on their iPhone or directly on the device.
source.title: Apple Releases Update to Fix Random Restarts on Watch Series 12 and Ultra 4

source.summary: East Point Energy, owned by Equinor, began operations at the 100MW/200MWh Citrus Flatts energy storage project in Harlingen, Texas. This facility marks the company's second operational project after the Sunset Ridge site. Equinor stated the projects demonstrate East Point's progression from developer to independent power producer. The company operates five battery energy storage facilities in the US and has begun construction on four additional projects in Virginia. East Point previously withdrew plans for a New York project due to local regulatory bans.
source.title: Equinor subsidiary East Point Energy starts Texas battery storage project

source.summary: The Allahabad High Court directed the Uttar Pradesh Police to provide protection to a Hindu-Muslim lesbian couple whose families threatened their live-in relationship. Justice Gautam Chowdhary noted that as adults, the petitioners have the freedom to live together peacefully. The court affirmed that under Supreme Court law, consenting adults have a fundamental right to choose to live together, and the absence of marital recognition does not justify threatening their physical safety or dignity. The state government argued against same-sex relationships, but the court upheld the couple's rights.
source.title: Allahabad High Court Orders Police Protection for Hindu-Muslim Lesbian Couple

source.summary: Tihana Škrinjarić presents a new framework to assess risks in the UK housing market. Unlike traditional approaches focusing on average price growth, this model estimates a full range of outcomes to identify potential for significant price drops. The analysis highlights regional differences, noting that supply-constrained areas are more sensitive to interest rate changes. By examining around 50 indicators, the model derives a house-price-at-risk measure to capture severity under adverse conditions. Results suggest that unwinding previous overvaluation amplified recent declines, while forward-looking measures help predict future vulnerabilities.
source.title: New Model Assesses UK Housing Market Risks

source.summary: CleanTechnica reports that global pure electric vehicle registrations reached 1.8 million units in July, representing a 16% year-over-year increase. While battery electric vehicles (BEVs) grew significantly, plugin hybrid sales declined by 11%, causing the overall plugin market to rise only 7%. BEVs accounted for 71% of all plugin sales in July, marking the highest share since 2022. The Tesla Model 3 saw deliveries crash 44% year-over-year to 19,000 units, falling to 11th place globally, whereas the Tesla Model Y remained the top-selling model despite a 9% drop. BYD's Song secured second place, aided by exports and a new generation, while a group of small EVs from Geely and BYD filled the third through seventh spots. Leapmotor achieved record sales, doubling its output year-over-year to reach six-digit levels and surpassing Hyundai-Kia to take sixth place among manufacturers. Toyota also set a new record with 50,415 registrations, edging closer to Volkswagen in the legacy OEM rankings. The article notes that excluding China and the USA, EV sales jumped 50% year-over-year in July.
source.title: Global EV sales surge in July as Tesla Model 3 drops and Leapmotor rises
