source.summary: The US and Denmark announced a security deal for Greenland, resolving a diplomatic dispute sparked by President Donald Trump's threat to seize the territory. While exact terms remain uncertain, the agreement appears to allow Denmark to maintain sovereignty while permitting a significant US military presence and banning adversaries from building bases on the island.
source.title: US and Denmark Announce Greenland Security Deal Resolving Trump-Era Dispute

source.summary: In May 2026, solar generated more electricity than coal or wind in the United States for the first time. The Energy Information Administration reports solar produced 47,147 gigawatt-hours versus coal's 45,119. Over the first five months of 2026, utility-scale solar output rose 21.6% while coal generation dropped 10.9%.
source.title: Solar Surpasses Coal and Wind in US Power Generation

source.summary: Prime Minister Narendra Modi gifted Russian President Vladimir Putin a Russian translation of the ancient Tamil classic Thirukkural during their bilateral meeting in New Delhi on Friday. The exchange took place ahead of the Brics Summit, showcasing cultural diplomacy between the two leaders. The Times of India reported the event as part of their coverage of the summit preparations.
source.title: PM Modi gifts Putin Russian Thirukkural translation ahead of Brics summit

source.summary: The New York Times reports that Western export bans have not reduced demand for brand-name SUVs and trucks in Russia. A sophisticated criminal network steals vehicles, hides them in shipping containers, and ships them to Russia, often through the Middle East. Interpol received 4,798 reports of stolen Canadian vehicles found in Russia between February 2024 and July 2026. Pickup trucks like Dodge Rams and Ford F-150s are in particularly high demand. The Royal Canadian Mounted Police states Russia is the top international destination for these reported stolen cars. Interpol figures likely undercount the actual scale of the problem.
source.title: Russia imports stolen Canadian trucks via criminal networks

source.summary: Researchers studying Nepal's Limi Valley report that human encroachment is advancing at an unprecedented pace, threatening the region's high-altitude wildernesses and wildlife. The authors note that thousands of sheep and goats, trailed by free-ranging dogs, have replaced traditional yak herding, causing overgrazing and spreading disease to species like snow leopards and Himalayan wolves. Geraldine Werhahn and Sabita Gurung, writing in an op-ed, state that this fragile ecosystem requires formal legal protection from the Nepalese government. They emphasize that this protection must be led by the stewardship of the local Limi community, who possess the best knowledge to safeguard the land, while also supporting conservation organizations. The article warns that without immediate action, the unique biodiversity of Upper Humla will be irreversibly diminished.
source.title: Nepal's Limi Valley wildlife faces unprecedented human encroachment

source.summary: Jammu and Kashmir Chief Minister Omar Abdullah pushed back at Congress allies regarding the mandatory singing of the full Vande Mataram song at official events. Abdullah stated that a law enacted in July makes all stanzas of the national song compulsory wherever the national anthem is played, calling it a statutory obligation for the entire country. He questioned why Congress would demand Kashmiris be jailed for complying with this rule. Conversely, Congress leaders, including K C Venugopal and Tariq Hamid Karra, expressed disapproval, arguing the unabridged version does not align with India's pluralist ethos. NC spokesperson Sadiq countered by highlighting that Congress-ruled states in Karnataka and Telangana also play the full version during government functions.
source.title: Omar Abdullah challenges Congress over mandatory Vande Mataram singing

source.summary: Ukrainian strikes on Russian oil refineries have intensified a fuel crisis, affecting 30 regions and particularly impacting Moscow and surrounding areas. Gas stations like Gazprom Neft and Tatneft have restricted fuel sales, with locals reporting long queues and economic disruptions. Analysts like Nikolai Korzhenevsky warn of declining fuel quality and production, projecting potential economic collapse if trends continue. Russian authorities propose fuel imports, but critics argue this is unfeasible given geopolitical isolation. Economist Vyacheslav Shiryaev suggests Ukrainian attacks could cripple Russia's economy and hasten the end of the war, citing disruptions to transportation and industry. He warns that fuel shortages could destabilize Vladimir Putin's regime by crippling critical infrastructure and supply chains.
source.title: Ukraine's attacks on Russian fuel infrastructure worsen crisis and threaten war end

source.summary: Samajwadi Party MP Shiv Pal Singh Patel claims Rahul Gandhi was scared to contest Amethi in 2024, contesting Raebareli instead. Patel asserts Congress won UP seats only due to the SP alliance, stating Gandhi would have lost without it. Congress spokesperson Anshu Awasthi urged Patel to rein in such statements, noting his MP status stems from the INDIA bloc.
source.title: SP MP claims Rahul Gandhi feared contesting Amethi alone

source.summary: The Kerala Water Authority is refurbishing the Maradu water treatment plant to increase its capacity from 100 to 120 million litres per day. Funded by the Asian Development Bank, the project involves laying a new 1,000-mm pipeline and changing filter beds to address water shortages in Kochi. Meanwhile, a separate pipeline rupture in Perandoor disrupted supply to hundreds of houses, requiring temporary repairs before a permanent fix can be implemented.
source.title: Kerala Water Authority upgrades Maradu plant to boost Kochi supply

source.summary: The paper examines how firms set wages and how governments should set income taxes, considering worker and firm heterogeneity. It extends the neoclassical model to include discrete firm choice, production complementarities, and strategic interactions. The study finds that worker heterogeneity accounts for 78 percent of labor supply elasticity variation and markdown differences between large and small firms. Higher tax progressivity reduces labor supply elasticity, eroding the tax base and worsening sorting. The research suggests that increases in marginal tax rates lead to earnings declines, and optimal tax progressivity is reduced by one-third, with associated welfare gains dropping by two-thirds.
source.title: Labor Market Power with Worker and Firm Heterogeneity

source.summary: Microsoft has launched a unified Copilot app designed for both consumers and enterprise users, consolidating previous fragmented tools into a single interface. The new release includes tabs for Home, Code, and Autopilot, with features tailored for the Microsoft 365 ecosystem. While the app integrates advanced AI capabilities, the pricing model is described as 'evolving,' combining fixed monthly subscriptions for chat features with usage-based billing for agents like Code and Autopilot. Microsoft executives highlighted improvements in speed and capability, though the final cost structure remains undefined for enterprise customers. A 'Today view' feature is scheduled for private preview in October.
source.title: Microsoft Unveils Unified Copilot App with Evolving Pricing Model

source.summary: Palo Alto Networks acquired Console, an AI startup, for $500 million in cash and stock, sources say. The deal values Console at $157 million, providing a rapid return for investors including CEO Nikesh Arora. Palo Alto Networks plans to integrate Console into its Cortex platform to enhance autonomous security capabilities. This acquisition marks the cybersecurity firm's seventh purchase in 2026.
source.title: Palo Alto Networks Acquires AI Startup Console for $500 Million

source.summary: The article reports that a dispute regarding the Paris Opera's ceiling remains unresolved six decades after its restoration. The text notes the ongoing nature of the conflict without providing specific details about the parties involved or the current status of the disagreement.
source.title: Feud over Paris Opera ceiling continues 60 years after restoration

source.summary: A women's PG facility in Satya Niketan, located 300 metres from a collapsed building, asked all 40 occupants to vacate immediately on Monday. Students reported being told the hostel could be sealed any time and would operate only as long as supplies lasted. Many students have already left for their hometowns, leaving others stranded. The college administration has not shown interest in the situation, and students face uncertainty regarding their paid rent and security deposits while authorities announce a sealing drive against unauthorized structures.
source.title: Satya Niketan PG asks 40 female students to vacate amid sealing drive

source.summary: The UN Environment Programme warns global temperatures will likely surpass 1.5C above pre-industrial levels in the coming years. UNEP Executive Director Inger Andersen stated that rapid emissions cuts could still limit the overshoot and eventually return temperatures below the threshold. The report identifies an 'overshoot, peak and decline' pathway as the best option to minimize warming duration. Even optimistic scenarios project a peak of 1.8C, while other scenarios foresee higher temperatures. The report warns that risks intensify with every fraction of a degree, threatening human health, food security, and ecosystems.
source.title: UN warns global warming likely to exceed 1.5C within next few years

source.summary: The article examines the historical significance of the Suez Canal, tracing its origins as a colonial project and its eventual decline. It highlights how the canal, once a symbol of European imperial power, has faced challenges and transformations over time. The piece explores the political and economic factors that contributed to its rise and fall. The Suez Canal's role in global trade is discussed, alongside its impact on regional geopolitics. The article suggests that the canal's legacy is complex, reflecting both the ambitions and limitations of colonial rule.
source.title: Suez Canal's colonial legacy and its decline

source.summary: A 2026 review of research indicates that consuming lentils, beans, and chickpeas offers several health benefits, though some evidence remains preliminary. The authors report that pulses feed gut microbes, producing short-chain fatty acids that support the digestive lining and immune system. Clinical trials involving over 2,000 adults show pulses reduce post-meal blood sugar spikes, particularly for those with type 2 diabetes, though long-term control data has low certainty. A 2024 analysis of nearly 2,000 people found modest reductions in total and LDL cholesterol. Studies also suggest pulses increase feelings of fullness without necessarily reducing subsequent food intake. Preparation methods like soaking can improve mineral absorption by reducing phytate levels. Lewis CE Mason, a lecturer in microbiology at Kingston University, notes that while human trials support specific effects, more long-term studies are needed to fully understand their impact on gut health.
source.title: Science suggests eating pulses improves gut health and blood sugar

source.summary: The Left Democratic Front alleges that the signature of BJP councillor R. Sugathan was forged in the Thiruvananthapuram Corporation attendance register to falsely show his presence at meetings he missed while in hiding. LDF leader S.P. Deepak claims the forgery occurred on February 26, March 11, and April 27, suggesting the Mayor's knowledge was involved to avoid Sugathan's disqualification.
source.title: LDF Alleges BJP Councillor Signature Forged in Attendance Register

source.summary: Business Today's Tech Gear episode 19 features an unboxing of the Redmi Note 17 Pro Max and a debunking of five myths regarding the iPhone 18 Pro series. The segment also includes a guide to setting up Apple Pay. AI Anchor Sana provides updates on major tech launches and weekly news. Viewers are invited to submit questions for future reviews and to subscribe for more content.
source.title: Tech Gear Episode 19 Covers New Gadgets and iPhone Myths

source.summary: Anna Tims, a consumer champion for the Guardian, hosts a live session to address reader inquiries regarding customer service. She notes that while AI tools can assist with troubleshooting, they often fail to resolve specific complaints, leading to repetitive platitudes. Tims advises customers to remain calm, gather all relevant evidence such as booking references, and utilize public platforms like Twitter to pressure companies into action. She highlights that although legal frameworks like the Consumer Rights Act 2015 exist, regulatory bodies are frequently overstretched. Consequently, she suggests patronizing companies that demonstrate exceptional service and checking for proper contact details before committing to a provider.
source.title: Consumer Champion Anna Tims Discusses Customer Service Issues and Tips

source.summary: A study by researchers at the University of Swansea's GREAT Centre accuses nearly 90% of licensed British gambling websites of violating GDPR rules regarding cookie banners. The research found that 86% of the sites tested failed to comply with strict data protection regulations. Approximately 24% of the 624 gambling websites examined did not provide users the option to disable tracking software, while two-thirds began harvesting data before obtaining consent. The report highlights that operators frequently use 'dark patterns' to nudge users toward accepting data sharing. Ravi Naik of AWO described the findings as evidence of systemic non-compliance and criticized the Information Commissioner's Office for a lack of meaningful enforcement. While the ICO stated it remains committed to monitoring compliance, several major operators declined to comment on the specific allegations.
source.title: Study accuses UK online bookies of widespread GDPR privacy breaches

source.summary: Tesla CEO Elon Musk stated that weather conditions may prevent the October 1st reveal of the Roadster 2.0, pushing the event back two weeks. The article notes Musk's history of delayed promises. Additionally, the EU is delaying a vote on Full Self Driving approval until at least December, and the podcast discusses robotaxi safety.
source.title: Tesla CEO Delays Roadster Reveal Amidst Autonomous Driving Updates

source.summary: First Minister John Swinney plans to reduce Scotland's 14 health boards to just two mainland bodies as part of a public service reform drive. The proposal aims to save money and improve efficiency by cutting management layers, though final decisions await consultation. While mainland boards would merge, island groups like Shetland and Orkney might instead form unitary authorities with local councils. Swinney also outlined other priorities in his upcoming programme, including eradicating child poverty and tackling violence against women. Additionally, the government intends to introduce a price cap on certain supermarket food items to help with cost of living pressures, despite opposition from 23 industry organisations.
source.title: Swinney proposes merging Scotland's 14 health boards into two for efficiency

source.summary: Thai police have arrested former abbot Phra Wachirayan Wi and a female accomplice on suspicion of embezzling 100 million baht from Wat Phutthaisawan monastery. Lead investigator Pattanasak Bupphasuwan stated that donations meant for temple renovations and sacred objects never entered the temple's account. Police seized cash, gold bars, and jewellery worth an estimated 6.04 million baht from the accomplice's home. The monk was defrocked after his arrest, while the 47-year-old woman faces charges of abetting a state official in illegal activities. Authorities believe two or three other people could be involved in the case, which began after an anonymous tip in mid-July.
source.title: Thai police arrest monk and accomplice in $3m embezzlement scandal

source.summary: US Open players are expressing concerns about the tournament's increasingly late match finishes. Alexander Zverev noted that everyone is tired and wants to sleep. Jessica Pegula questioned if finishing at 2 a.m. is right for players. Venus Williams stated the late start was not ideal and noted there is room for improvement. Aryna Sabalenka warned that finishing late messes up a player's schedule.
source.title: US Open players push back against late-night match finishes

source.summary: The article highlights suicide as a major global health crisis affecting millions annually. It notes that World Suicide Prevention Day was established in 2003 by the International Association for Suicide Prevention and the World Health Organization. The 2024–26 theme, 'Changing the Narrative on Suicide,' calls for challenging myths and reducing stigma through open dialogue. It urges governments and institutions to prioritize mental health in public policy.
source.title: World Suicide Prevention Day urges open conversations to end stigma

source.summary: Kerala general education minister N Shamsudheen announced that the United Democratic Front (UDF) leadership will decide on implementing the PM SHRI scheme following a request from the Union government. While the scheme aims to upgrade 14,500 schools and benefit 1.8 million students, the UDF holds reservations, viewing it as an ideological project of the BJP-RSS. The minister clarified that the chief minister will convey the final decision after internal discussions.
source.title: Kerala UDF to decide on PM SHRI scheme amid ideological concerns

source.summary: Annie Jacobsen discusses the persistent threat of bioweapons, arguing that the danger exists independently of artificial intelligence. Drawing on her book 'Biological War: A Scenario' and interviews with experts, she highlights that accidental releases from high-security labs pose a greater risk than deliberate attacks by terrorists. Jacobsen notes that over 3,600 BSL-4 labs worldwide increase the statistical likelihood of accidents. She references historical Soviet programs and current concerns regarding nations like Russia and China. While acknowledging an Anthropic report on AI misuse, Jacobsen emphasizes that genetic engineering alone allows for catastrophic pandemics. She concludes that raising awareness is crucial to addressing these real, existing threats.
source.title: Author Discusses Bioweapon Threats Without AI

source.summary: Fukuoka Prefecture held a conference to address drunken driving, 20 years after a 2006 incident where a drunk driver caused a fatal accident killing three children. The event followed the tragedy, which prompted stricter regulations on drunk driving. Kaori Onuma, mother of the victims, emphasized that adults should ensure the safety of children and prevent lives from being cut short due to impaired driving.
source.title: Fukuoka Prefecture Marks 20 Years Since Tragic Drunken Driving Incident

source.summary: Maharashtra Chief Electoral Officer S. Chockalingam directed Booth Level Officers to verify voter documents sent via WhatsApp during the Special Intensive Revision exercise. Officials stated that households would be visited if necessary. The Election Commission clarified that decisions regarding the revision were made unanimously, countering Opposition allegations of unilateral actions by Chief Election Commissioner Gyanesh Kumar.
source.title: Maharashtra Poll Body Allows WhatsApp Voter Docs

source.summary: South Africa and Malaysia convened 40 states at the UN in New York to strengthen international law enforcement. Co-sponsors Ronald Lamola and Mohamad Hasan stated that law's authority depends on enforcement. Participants proposed a new monitoring mechanism modeled on the 1962 Special Committee against Apartheid, alongside efforts for an arms embargo on Israel and measures to shield the International Criminal Court. The group views the occupied Palestinian territory as an urgent test of the multilateral system and described defending international law as a common responsibility.
source.title: South Africa and Malaysia Lead 40 States in UN Call to Defend International Law

source.summary: A military aircraft reportedly crashed near the US Air Base Spangdahlem in Germany on Tuesday. Local authorities in the Eifel region initially stated that one person was injured. The Eifel District dispatched fire and emergency response teams but declined to comment on further details. The US Air Force did not immediately respond to a request for comment regarding the incident.
source.title: Military Aircraft Crashes Near US Air Base in Spangdahlem, Germany

source.summary: Multiple organizations across the Middle East and globally are expanding renewable energy and battery storage capabilities. Oman PWP issued a request for proposals to study renewable options in the Musandam Governorate. The Kuwait Fund for Arab Economic Development signed a USD 9.6 million loan to finance an 11 MW solar plant in El Salvador. Larsen & Toubro secured a major order for 6 GWh of battery energy storage systems in the Middle East. ACWA Power and KOWEPO signed an MoU to explore renewable opportunities in Uzbekistan, while NHC and EDF Power Solutions partnered on sustainable energy in Saudi Arabia. ACWA Power also signed agreements for 1.5 GW/6 GWh of storage in Saudi Arabia, and Masdar began operations at a 35 MW facility in the UK. Saudi Arabia signed four additional agreements worth SAR 4.35 billion for 2,000 MW of storage capacity.
source.title: Middle East and Global Firms Advance Renewable Energy and Storage Projects

source.summary: Oracle shares rose 3 per cent on Friday following a $26 billion increase in revenue backlog, which alleviated some investor concerns regarding the company's debt-fueled expansion. While Oracle stated that roughly half of its $664 billion backlog will convert to sales within 36 months, Morningstar analyst Luke Yang noted that cash flow improvements are not expected soon. The company reported negative free cash flow of $5.40 billion, surpassing analyst estimates of $9.56 billion according to LSEG data. Despite these figures, Evercore analysts described the results as a solid step forward, though the stock still trades at a lower multiple than Microsoft and Amazon.
source.title: Oracle shares rise as AI backlog growth offsets spending concerns

source.summary: Chief Minister N. Chandrababu Naidu will visit Mogalturu on Tuesday to distribute pensions under the NTR Bharosa Pension Scheme. He plans to visit beneficiaries in wards 2, 3, and Ponnapalli before addressing a public meeting. Naidu is scheduled to return to Amaravati by 5:20 pm after attending a party cadre meeting.
source.title: CM Naidu visits Mogalturu to distribute pensions under NTR Bharosa Scheme

source.summary: Taiwanese TV host Blackie Chen, 49, was admitted to National Taiwan University Hospital on Tuesday after suffering a heart attack. He is currently under observation in the intensive care unit following surgery. Chen has reassured fans that he is safe and expressed gratitude for the professional and prompt treatment he received. He promised to take good care of himself and return to his job as soon as possible.
source.title: Blackie Chen Hospitalized After Heart Attack and Reassures Fans

source.summary: BRICS countries condemned the European Union's Carbon Border Adjustment Mechanisms (CBAMs) as unilateral and discriminatory climate measures during a joint statement in New Delhi. The ministers argued that such policies undermine developing nations' resilience efforts. Concurrently, they urged developed countries to provide new, additional, and predictable adaptation finance, emphasizing the need to meet the 2035 commitment to triple such funding. The statement highlights the tension between trade compliance and climate justice as BRICS nations seek to protect their economies while addressing global climate challenges.
source.title: BRICS Condemns EU Carbon Tax and Calls for Climate Finance

source.summary: A collection of images displays various properties available for purchase across England, Scotland, and Wales. The selection includes a thatched cottage with a green-topped extension and a lodge-style home located in a town described as ideal for food enthusiasts.
source.title: Pictures showcase homes for sale in England, Scotland and Wales

source.summary: Neurovia AI is pitching video compression software to Saudi security agencies. The Abu Dhabi-based firm claims its technology can reduce video file sizes by up to 95%. CEO Khalifa Mohammed Alshehhi stated the algorithm allows threat detection within milliseconds. Neurovia, acquired by Robo.ai for $100 million, plans to launch the software at the LEAP conference in Riyadh. The company has not yet secured a Saudi contract but aims to serve Mecca, Medina, and other government sectors. Neurovia addresses data sovereignty concerns by stating it never holds footage and can configure systems where data remains within the kingdom.
source.title: Neurovia AI pitches video compression software to Saudi security agencies

source.summary: The BRICS summit aimed to diminish Western influence over the global economy, mirroring the Shanghai Cooperation Organization's goals. However, the gathering fell short of a united front against the West, particularly the United States. India, the host nation, acted as a brake on efforts to de-dollarize the economy. The joint statement called for reforms in Western-dominated financial institutions but avoided naming the US or addressing the Russia-Ukraine conflict directly. Kazakh President Tokayev adopted a middle-of-the-road stance, balancing interests of major powers while emphasizing the need for high-level dialogue to reduce nuclear risks and promote regional stability.
source.title: BRICS Leaders Seek to Diminish Western Economic Influence Amid Internal Divisions

source.summary: The Kerala CPI(M) is confronting significant internal dissent following a historic electoral defeat, with the party's vote share dropping to 21.77 per cent. The Central Committee acknowledged leadership failures in candidate selection and noted a widening gap between the party and its rank and file. While General Secretary MA Baby has urged cadres to speak openly about the loss, tensions remain regarding whether the leadership will accept full responsibility. The upcoming State Committee meeting in Kozhikode from September 13 to 15 is expected to test the party's commitment to self-criticism and organizational reform. Members are increasingly questioning decisions on candidate selection and the handling of communal issues, challenging the leadership to address these concerns publicly.
source.title: Kerala CPI(M) faces internal dissent over electoral defeat and leadership accountability

source.summary: Forbes reports that 19 of the 144 US immigrant billionaires in 2026 were born in India, the highest count for any nation. The collective wealth of these foreign-born billionaires reached $2.2 trillion, with Elon Musk, Sergey Brin, and Jensen Huang controlling over 60% of the total. Israel and Taiwan followed with 11 billionaires each, while new entrants from India include founders of Astera Labs and Palantir's CTO.
source.title: India leads US immigrant billionaires with 19, highest for any country

source.summary: Leanstral, an open-source code agent for Lean 4, aims to enhance formal verification by generating code and proving its correctness. The project, developed by researchers, introduces a model with 6B active parameters, optimized for proof engineering tasks. It is released under an Apache 2.0 license, available through Mistral Vibe and a free API. Leanstral outperforms existing open-source models and competitors like the Claude suite in efficiency and performance, achieving higher scores with lower computational cost. The model was tested on real-world scenarios, including diagnosing issues in Lean 4 code and translating programs from Rocq to Lean. The team emphasizes its accessibility, offering zero-setup integration and the ability to run the model locally.
source.title: Leanstral: Open-Source Code Agent for Formal Verification

source.summary: The U.S. Securities and Exchange Commission proposes removing a rule allowing shareholders to petition companies on climate and sustainability issues. Investor groups warn this move blocks a key avenue for pressuring public companies to address climate risks. The SEC argues the change hands power to states and reduces focus on non-financial debates. Data shows shareholder proposals fell 20% from 2025 to 2026, with environmental proposals dropping 32%. The proposal faces public comment until Nov. 20, 2026.
source.title: SEC Plans to Scrap Shareholder Climate Petition Rule

source.summary: Senegalese consumers in Dakar have started an online campaign to protest increasing prices. The movement highlights sharp rises in meat and onion costs alongside fuel and rent hikes. Organizers launched the hashtag #30DaysForTheRightPrice to alert authorities to the situation. FRANCE 24 reports that the campaign aims to protect vulnerable households from these economic pressures.
source.title: Senegalese consumers launch online campaign against rising living costs

source.summary: The article reports that CD rates are currently high, with Marcus by Goldman Sachs offering the highest rate of 4.30% APY on an 18-month certificate of deposit. Several financial institutions provide competitive rates of 4% APY and up, particularly online banks. The Federal Reserve has cut its target rate three times in late 2024 but is unlikely to cut rates again in 2026. Experts suggest locking in current rates before a potential increase later this year. The article outlines steps for opening a CD, including researching rates, choosing an account, preparing documents, completing the application, and funding the account.
source.title: Best CD rates today, Thursday, September 3, 2026: Lock in up to 4.30% APY with an 18-month CD

source.summary: White Oak Armory LLC filed for Chapter 11 bankruptcy in Tennessee, citing a disputed tax debt to the state. The retailer's website showed no firearms or ammunition for sale as of late August. Industry data indicates a broader decline in gun sales, with total units falling 4.1% in 2025 and rifle sales rising while handgun and shotgun sales dropped significantly in 2026.
source.title: White Oak Armory files Chapter 11 bankruptcy amid falling gun sales

source.summary: US Treasury Secretary Scott Bessent announced that Iranian airlines will be globally shut down by September 23. He warned that countries allowing Iranian aircraft to land could face secondary sanctions, including exclusion from the dollar system. The US previously sanctioned 27 Iranian airlines and designated foreign intermediaries, citing support for the Iranian regime and weapon transfers by the IRGC.
source.title: US Treasury sets September 23 shutdown for Iranian airlines with dollar system threats

source.summary: US stock indices closed higher, driven by investor optimism regarding artificial intelligence and hopes for a resolution to the conflict between the US and Iran. Major indices including the S&P 500, Nasdaq Composite, and Dow Jones Industrial Average posted significant gains. Specific market movers included Microsoft and Akamai Technologies, which surged following announcements of new AI capabilities and a major cloud services deal, respectively.
source.title: US Markets Rally on AI Optimism and Geopolitical Hopes

source.summary: Nigeria's traditional combat sport Dambe is expanding beyond local Hausa communities through social media and professional structures. The authors report that online platforms like YouTube have introduced the sport to international audiences, creating new income opportunities for fighters. However, this visibility raises concerns about who defines the sport's future as it enters the mainstream. Cultural practices, such as spiritual rituals and amulets, require interpretation by practitioners rather than outside observers. Modern organizers are introducing safety rules and points systems, which may increase commercial value but risk sidelining community voices. The article argues that meaningful participation from fighters, elders, and cultural practitioners is essential to ensure the sport's evolution respects its roots. Ultimately, the future of Dambe depends on allowing communities to decide how the tradition changes rather than treating them as spectators.
source.title: Nigeria's Dambe evolves globally while communities demand control

source.summary: Indian opener Abhishek Sharma made history by hitting a record 30-ball T20I hundred against Afghanistan in Delhi. Blazing through the innings, he reached his first 50 in just 16 balls and finished with 108 off 34 balls, including 9 fours and 11 sixes. This achievement makes him the fastest to a century by a Test-playing nation batter and the third-quickest overall in T20I format.
source.title: Abhishek Sharma Sets Record Fastest T20I Century in Delhi

source.summary: US Ambassador to Israel Mike Huckabee stated there is no plan to forcibly displace Palestinians from Gaza. This comment follows Israeli ministers proposing voluntary emigration for the territory's two million residents. Defence Minister Israel Katz suggested migration is necessary, claiming 80 percent of Gazans wish to leave. Huckabee emphasized the US supports the right to leave without forced displacement. These remarks occur ahead of Israel's October 27 general election.
source.title: US Ambassador Mike Huckabee denies Israeli plans for forced Gaza displacement

source.summary: Three hikers were rescued from California's Mount Shasta after using Google's AI chatbot Gemini to plan their trip, according to the Chicago Tribune. The Siskiyou County sheriff's office reported that Gemini advised the group to carry insufficient food and water for their extended ascent. The men attempted to descend in the dark, contacted authorities for directions, and spent the night in Mud Creek Canyon before rescue teams arrived. Officials stated that hikers should never rely solely on AI for trip planning and should contact local ranger stations for accurate information.
source.title: Three hikers rescued after relying on Google Gemini for Mount Shasta plans

source.summary: Reliance Jio has completed ten years of commercial operations, marking a decade of serving more than half a billion customers. Akash Ambani, Chairman of Reliance Jio Infocomm Limited, wrote to employees stating that the pride he feels belongs to them. Jio Platforms Ltd filed draft papers on 19 June for an initial public offering estimated at around USD 4 billion. Mukesh Ambani described the IPO as the company's most significant value-creation event of the year. Akash Ambani emphasized that the company's story is written by its people rather than numbers. He noted that Jio has expanded into broadband, digital products, and enterprise technology while accelerating India's transition to 5G. Looking ahead, Ambani stated the company is building original technology in India across connectivity, digital products, enterprise solutions, and AI.
source.title: Akash Ambani credits employees as Jio celebrates 10 years and prepares for IPO

source.summary: Microsoft's AI division published a code of conduct on Monday to address growing safety concerns regarding artificial intelligence. The document centers on the concept of 'Humanist AI,' designed to keep systems firmly under human control rather than allowing autonomous action. The company stated that people matter more than AI. This initiative was partly timed to respond to security worries, citing recent large-scale hacking campaigns facilitated by AI agents as evidence that the industry cannot afford delays. The code applies to Microsoft's in-house MAI models, positioning them as an alternative to OpenAI technology.
source.title: Microsoft Publishes AI Code of Conduct Amid Rising Safety Fears

source.summary: The Australian government announced stricter visa rules requiring most international students to arrive alone and preventing course-hopping to extend stays. Home Affairs Minister Tony Burke framed these changes as part of a broader strategy to lower net overseas migration to 225,000 by 2027-28. Universities Australia called the move worrying, noting students often bring family members for research degrees. The government also aims to reduce student numbers, which surged post-pandemic, while increasing visa refusal rates. International education contributes A$54.7 billion annually, with student fees accounting for $24.3 billion.
source.title: Australia Tightens Visa Rules for International Students

source.summary: An expert argues that Ethiopia's 2022 Pretoria peace deal failed because it was not a comprehensive political settlement. While the agreement halted large-scale fighting, it excluded Tigray from upcoming elections and did not secure the withdrawal of foreign forces. Consequently, fighting has resumed, and an armed alliance has formed to challenge Prime Minister Abiy Ahmed's government. The author warns that without a broader agreement addressing territorial disputes and political representation, the conflict risks expanding into a wider regional confrontation involving Eritrea and Sudan.
source.title: Ethiopia's Peace Deal Unravels as Regional Conflict Escalates

source.summary: Oracle stock fell 4% after the company sent a force majeure notice regarding its New Mexico AI data center. This move allows Oracle to delay campus payments if the facility does not come online as expected in 2028.
source.title: Oracle Stock Drops After Force Majeure Notice on New Mexico AI Data Center

source.summary: Australian Prime Minister Anthony Albanese has intensified focus on Western Australia (WA), promising no changes to its generous GST payments and showcasing the state with federal meetings, new agreements, and the Blue Poles painting. This attention stems from WA's economic significance and its role in securing Labor's 2022 election victory. The RBA remains cautious about inflation, with minutes showing readiness to raise interest rates if price pressures worsen. Meanwhile, home builder Bathla Group collapsed into voluntary administration due to financial pressures. NSW will mandate facial recognition in gaming rooms by 2028, and advocates call for reforms to support sexual assault survivors. A report criticized police for wrongly identifying an Indigenous teen, welcomed by his family.
source.title: Australia news live: PM dubbed ‘WA’s daddy’ over Blue Poles and GST promises; RBA poised to lift interest rates again if needed

source.summary: Nvidia CEO Jensen Huang and other executives privately challenged Anthropic CEO Dario Amodei regarding his public warnings about AI risks during a White House meeting. While industry leaders like Mark Zuckerberg supported a unified approach, Amodei argued for transparency about AI hazards. The confrontation highlighted tensions over development speed, with Nvidia stock falling nearly 3% after Amodei called for slowing AI progress. Anthropic aims to value at roughly $2 trillion in an upcoming IPO.
source.title: Tech Executives Challenge Anthropic CEO on AI Safety Warnings

source.summary: The article reports that wave energy projects in the United States are progressing despite a shift in federal energy policy. The Energy Department announced the official opening of the PacWave South test facility in Oregon, which allows developers to test devices without regulatory delays. Additionally, the National Renewable Energy Laboratory and the University of Hawaii are collecting data from the SURF-WEC converter to address a lack of real-life industry data. While the Trump administration's American Energy Dominance plan excludes solar and offshore wind, it supports marine energy through expanded collaborations with Norway and continued funding for research networks. Officials state that these facilities aim to reduce testing barriers and spur innovation for the sector's future growth.
source.title: US Wave Energy Projects Advance Despite Trump Administration Policy Shifts

source.summary: Airtel has expanded its family postpaid plans, priced at ₹999 and above, by including Apple perks such as iCloud+, Apple TV, and Apple Arcade. This initiative is part of the telecom operator's broader strategy to focus on premiumisation and extract greater value from its customer base. The move aims to improve average revenue per user through differentiated plans and services, rather than implementing broad-based tariff increases.
source.title: Airtel Adds Apple Perks to ₹999 Family Plans

source.summary: Indian investors are expected to monitor several companies on September 4 following post-market business updates. The Nifty and Sensex indices closed lower on Thursday, though smaller caps recovered. UltraTech Cement announced a ₹1,800 crore investment in a new wires and cables venture. Cipla secured a partnership for a biosimilar drug in the US market. Bharat Forge signed an MoU for local defence manufacturing cooperation. Power Grid Corporation won a bid for a renewable energy transmission project. Sterlite Technologies approved a ₹3,000 crore capacity expansion plan. Solex Energy received solar module orders worth ₹74.77 crore. CreditAccess Grameen raised ₹300 crore via debenture placement. Innovision won a contract for toll plaza operations in Andhra Pradesh. Ramco Systems partnered with Safran for helicopter data integration. Welspun Investments approved a ₹1,000 crore investment in Indivara Realty. Diamond Power Infrastructure received a ₹76.06 crore Letter of Acceptance for power cables.
source.title: Indian stocks gain focus on Friday due to corporate announcements and orders

source.summary: Rachael Gunn discusses her experiences in a new Netflix documentary about her Paris Olympics performance. She described feeling shame after her viral breaking routine received no votes. Gunn noted that while some memes were humorous, the tone eventually became cruel. She revealed she had anticipated mockery before the Games and is now working as a speaker. The film addresses rumors about her qualification and her feelings during the fallout.
source.title: Rachael Gunn discusses Olympic mockery and new Netflix documentary

source.summary: A fire at the Amur Gas Chemical Complex in Russia's far eastern region killed seven people and left nine Chinese workers missing. The incident occurred on August 25, 2026, and was extinguished by emergency services. The plant, a joint venture between Sibur and Sinopec, had not yet begun operations. The Investigative Committee is investigating potential breaches of industrial safety regulations. The complex, set to produce 2.3 million metric tons of polyethylene and 400,000 tons of polypropylene annually, relied on foreign labor, including Chinese workers, for its construction.
source.title: Fire at Russian gas complex kills seven, leaves nine Chinese workers missing

source.summary: Flights were disrupted across the US Northeast on Monday after a backup fiber optic cable was severed during construction work at a Philadelphia air traffic control facility. The Federal Aviation Administration temporarily halted some incoming flights at major airports including Newark Liberty, Philadelphia, and Teterboro. FlightAware reported more than 300 flights at Newark and Philadelphia were delayed, representing about 15% of operations. Newark flights faced an average delay of 112 minutes. FAA administrator Brian Bedford stated the repair would take approximately 13 hours. By early afternoon, some flights resumed at LaGuardia and Philadelphia, though significant delays were expected to continue through Monday.
source.title: Flights Disrupted Across US Northeast After Backup Cable Cut During Construction

source.summary: White Oak Armory LLC filed for Chapter 11 bankruptcy in Tennessee, citing a disputed tax debt to the state. The retailer's website showed no firearms or ammunition for sale as of late August. Industry data indicates a broader decline in gun sales, with total units falling 4.1% in 2025 and rifle sales rising while handgun and shotgun sales dropped significantly in 2026.
source.title: White Oak Armory files Chapter 11 bankruptcy amid falling gun sales

source.summary: Temasek, the majority shareholder of Singapore Airlines, supports the carrier's investment in Air India despite growing questions about the loss-making Indian airline. The Singapore carrier holds a 25.1 per cent stake in Air India, which recently requested US$1.5 billion in fresh equity. Temasek stated that transforming Air India involves complex challenges and outcomes shaped by external factors. While opposition lawmakers urged against using Temasek funds, the company views the decision from a long-term perspective. Air India has faced significant losses and operational disruptions since Tata took control in 2022.
source.title: Temasek supports SIA's Air India investment despite financial scrutiny

source.summary: ETMarkets analysis shows FIIs and mutual funds increased holdings in 94 Nifty 500 stocks during the June 2026 quarter. Eight of these stocks gained 15% to 40% in less than three months, with Welspun Living leading at 41%.
source.title: FIIs and Mutual Funds Boost Holdings in Nifty 500 Stocks

source.summary: Iran announced plans to sign an agreement with Oman establishing a new shipping corridor through the Strait of Hormuz under Iranian control. Mohsen Rezaei, secretary of Iran’s Supreme National Security Council, stated that ships entering the restricted zone without coordinating with Tehran would face sanctions. The proposal follows recent escalations in maritime conflict, with traffic through the strait falling to its lowest level since May. Goldman Sachs warned that further attacks on commercial shipping could push crude prices as high as $120 per barrel.
source.title: Iran announces new Hormuz shipping corridor under Tehran control

source.summary: Revolve Renewable Power Corp. announced a $24 million project financing facility with Banco Multiva to support its distributed generation business in Mexico. The company expects to complete an initial drawdown of $7.7 million to refinance existing assets and recycle capital for future growth. CFO Tania Ontiveros described the deal as a significant milestone validating the firm's expansion strategy. Banco Multiva CEO Tamara Caballero noted the agreement reinforces the bank's ability to deliver long-term energy financing solutions. The 14-year facility is structured through Revolve's Mexican subsidiaries and aims to fund new solar projects while retaining ownership of underlying assets. Revolve reported that three projects have completed installation and seventeen are under construction, with an expected operational completion by the end of 2026.
source.title: Revolve Renewable Power Secures $24 Million Financing from Mexico Bank

source.summary: Artificial intelligence emerged as a major theme at the opening of the UN General Assembly, with world leaders warning about risks ranging from autonomous weapons to job disruption. However, little consensus exists on next steps. US President Donald Trump rejected international control efforts, emphasizing competition and rapid development, while leaders like UN Secretary-General Antonio Guterres and Turkish President Recep Tayyip Erdogan called for common rules and safeguards. Guterres warned that humanity is increasingly transferring power to machines, insisting life-and-death decisions must remain under human control. Other leaders, including British Prime Minister Andy Burnham and French President Emmanuel Macron, highlighted the need for transparency, oversight, and international cooperation to prevent dominance by a few powers or companies. The debate underscores the tension between technological advancement and the establishment of global governance frameworks.
source.title: World Leaders Debate AI Governance at UN General Assembly

source.summary: US President Donald Trump stated on Sunday that he has reached a critical turning point in the conflict with Iran, warning of serious consequences if Tehran does not alter its course. Speaking on Fox News, Trump questioned when he might destroy the nation, outlining options ranging from economic collapse to diplomatic resolution. Meanwhile, Iran's central command declared it would retaliate without limitations against any US attack. Iranian Parliament speaker Mohammad Bagher Ghalibaf emphasized the need to pursue both military action and negotiation, describing the country's stance as clear and non-negotiable.
source.title: Trump Issues Ultimatum to Iran Amid Escalating War Threats

source.summary: Scientists are using very high-resolution satellite imagery to identify whale species and locate strandings in remote ocean areas. Researchers note that this technology supplements, rather than replaces, traditional field work which remains necessary for determining causes of death. The British Antarctic Survey and other groups are building global networks to standardize data collection and improve access to satellite information. Experts warn that weather conditions and satellite availability can still limit the effectiveness of remote monitoring efforts. Ultimately, these tools aim to help scientists understand mortality trends and intervene more quickly in future events.
source.title: Scientists use satellites to track whale strandings in remote places from space

source.summary: A Telangana High Court division bench suspended a single judge order relieving IPS officer A.V. Ranganath from his HYDRAA Commissioner post. The bench, comprising Justices P. Sam Koshy and Narsinga Rao Nandikonda, will hear the matter again on November 3. Both the Commissioner and M/s Shanta Sriram Constructions Private Limited were directed to maintain the status quo regarding 40 acres of land in Lothkunta village. The single judge had previously ordered Ranganath's removal for alleged wilful disobedience of court restraining orders.
source.title: Telangana HC suspends order removing HYDRAA Commissioner in contempt case

source.summary: BYD launched its largest UK sales event, offering discounts of up to $3,300 on select electric and plug-in hybrid vehicles. The campaign runs from September 10 to September 21. BYD has registered over 48,000 vehicles in the UK since March 2023, representing 3.48% of the market. The company is expanding its lineup with new models including the Shark pickup and Ti 7 SUV. BYD stated it aims to offer vehicles for every driver with its broad range of electrified options.
source.title: BYD launches biggest UK sales event with discounts on EVs and PHEVs

source.summary: Myanmar's Min Aung Hlaing is visiting Vietnam to discuss normalizing relations with ASEAN and attracting foreign investment. The military-backed leader has increased diplomatic engagement since taking office in April 2021. While defense ties remain strong, bilateral trade has declined significantly. This visit marks his third trip to an ASEAN member state as he seeks to restore his standing in the bloc.
source.title: Myanmar's Min Aung Hlaing visits Vietnam to normalize ASEAN relations

source.summary: Elon Musk congratulated Tesla Australia after electric vehicles outsold internal combustion engine cars for the first time in August. The authors report that 27,000 battery electric vehicles and 10,591 plug-in hybrids were sold out of 109,000 total cars. Tesla Model Y topped the charts with 6,414 units sold, while BYD led the brand battle by a narrow margin. The authors note that every Chinese brand in the top ten saw year-over-year growth, whereas legacy automakers declined. A recent NRMA survey indicates cost is now the primary driver for EV ownership, with electricity priced at 34 cents per kilowatt-hour. Despite concerns about charging infrastructure, the authors argue the network is performing well based on Open Charge Map data.
source.title: Musk Congratulates Tesla Australia After EVs First Outsell ICE Vehicles

source.summary: Telangana Standards Authority for Food and Essential Drugs (TG SAFE) conducted inspections in Hyderabad, seizing 15 tonnes of adulterated and unhygienic food products valued at ₹30 lakh. The operation, involving 15 teams, found pest infestations, fungal-infested vegetables, and violations of packaging and labelling norms. Officials collected 35 food samples for testing and suspended the licence of M/s Burfi Ghar. Twelve improvement notices and four show-cause notices were issued to non-compliant establishments.
source.title: Telangana authorities seize 15 tonnes of adulterated food from Hyderabad units
